docs.name: Recovery Workbench Admin and Access Model v5

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Admin and access model

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench admin and access model
Version | 5
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Standard | NIST role based access control model (ANSI/INCITS 359)

The Recovery Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository and one front end. Access to the Workbench therefore uses what ACE already runs in production: Entra ID sign-in with multi-factor authentication, the bank IAM integration, role based access control, the audit log, the PII log through PII Kafka and the SOC log. The Workbench adds its own roles, permissions, scope rules and masking rules, held as versioned data. No Workbench role loads source data: ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads it only through SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views.

Question | Position in this model | Reason | Status
Who grants access | The application owner's organization. A role owner approves each grant and an access administrator carries it out in the bank IAM. | SCB administers enterprise tools such as Jira centrally, and business applications through their application owner. | Assumed, G1
Who the application owner is | The Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe, for ACE as a whole. Recovery roles are delegated to recovery role owners. The ACE team is the technical custodian. | ACE holds the collection and the recovery modules in one service, so one application owner covers both. | Assumed, G2
Where identity is held | Entra ID. The Workbench holds no password and no local account. | ACE runs Entra ID sign-in with IAM integration in production. | Settled
How a person holds a role | Membership of one Entra ID group per Workbench role per environment, granted through a bank IAM request. The Workbench reads the membership at sign-in. | ACE grants roles through the bank IAM and Entra ID today. | Settled; group names G7
What a role may do | A permission matrix of 53 roles across 14 capability areas, using the letters C, R, U, D and A, held as versioned data. | Every role and permission is a data row with a version, so a change needs no code release. | Settled
Authority levels | Four administration levels decide who may grant access. Six approval levels from the bank approval authority regulation decide who may approve a recovery decision. | Access authority and approval authority are separate. Approval authority follows Regulation กกค.540031. | Assumed, G1 and G4
Partners | No partner reaches the Workbench until the architecture team approves external access. Partners use the existing channels until then. | Access from outside the bank makes the application internet facing, which needs an architecture change with a lead time of one to three months. | Gap G3
Non-human actors | Each runs under its own service identity, holds a role in the same roles table, and is checked and logged the same way as a person. | ACE runs services under managed identities. | Settled

Settled: agreed by the bank or already in production. Assumed: the position the build uses until the bank answers. Gap: an answer needed from the bank, listed with its owner and date in section 11. Each gap is also held in the Recovery Workbench decision log under the ID shown beside it.

Each element of the NIST role based access control model has one name in the Workbench.

NIST element | Meaning | In the Workbench
User | A person or a service identity that acts in the system | A bank employee, a partner user or a service identity, identified by Entra ID
Role | A job function with the permissions it needs | One row in the roles table, for example RW-CASEOWN, case owner
Permission | Approval to perform an operation on an object | A letter C, R, U, D or A in one of 14 capability areas, with a scope and a masking position
Session | The roles a user has active at one time | Created at sign-in. Carries the roles, the scope and the masking position until it ends
User assignment | Which users hold which roles | Entra ID group membership, granted through the bank IAM
Permission assignment | Which roles hold which permissions | The permission matrix version in force
Role hierarchy | One role inheriting the permissions of another | Not used. A person who needs two roles holds both, and the permissions of both apply
Static separation of duty | Role pairs that one user may never hold together | The conflict table in section 6.1
Dynamic separation of duty | Actions one user may not combine in one session or on one record | The maker and checker rules in section 6.2

secs.h: 3.1 Central administration or application owner administration
secs.t:
| Central administration | Application owner administration
Who decides a grant | A central IAM or IT security team, on the request and the line manager's approval | The role owner for the role requested, under the application owner
Who carries out the grant | The central team | The access administrator in the business, or the IAM fulfillment team on the role owner's approval
Who reviews access | The central team runs the review; managers confirm | Role owners recertify their roles; the application owner signs the result
Where SCB uses it today | Enterprise tools, for example Jira licenses | Business applications
What the Workbench builds | Entra ID groups mapped to roles, the permission matrix as data, the access log | The same
Effect on the Epic 1 build | None. Changes who is trained and who signs the access tests | None

Both options grant access in the same place, Entra ID through the bank IAM, so the build does not wait for the answer. The answer changes who holds administration levels 2 and 3 in section 3.2. This model uses application owner administration, because SCB administers business applications that way.

Level | Position | Held by | May | May not
1 | Application owner | Tribe Lead, Collections and Recovery Tribe (assumed, G2) | Approve the roles table and each permission matrix version. Appoint role owners and access administrators. Sign each access review. Accept the remaining access risk | Approve their own access. Load a matrix version
2 | Role owner | The head of the unit whose staff hold the role: case operations, restructuring, legal and litigation, NPA and asset liquidity, debt sale, credit administration and write-off, control functions | Approve or reject each grant of a role they own. Confirm the separation of duty check. Recertify the holders of their roles at each review | Grant a role they do not own. Carry out a grant
3 | Access administrator | Chief Debt Recovery Management Office (assumed, G1) | Carry out approved grants and removals in the bank IAM. Run the review cycle. Follow up leavers | Approve a grant. Hold a role owner position for the same roles
4 | Line manager | The person's manager | Request a role for a team member. Confirm movers and leavers | Approve the request they raised

Four technical positions support the business levels and decide no business grant.

Position | Role code | Held by | Does
Security administrator | RW-SECADM | SCB IT security | Maintains the Entra ID groups and the IAM link. Approves and reviews break-glass use
Platform administrator | RW-PLATADM | ACE team and TechX platform | Runs the environments. Holds no permanent access to case data. Takes break-glass access only under an open incident
Reference data administrator | RW-REFADM | Center of excellence | Loads an approved roles, permission matrix, scope or masking version. Approves none of them
Internal audit | RW-AUDIT | Internal audit | Reads the access log and every version in force on any date. Changes nothing

Action | App owner | Role owner | Access admin | Line manager | Security admin | Platform admin | Ref data admin | Compliance | Audit
Add or change a role in the roles table | A | R | | | | | D | | V
Change the permission matrix | A | R | | | V | | D | | V
Change a masking rule | V | | | | | | D | A | V
Map an Entra ID group to a role | A | | | | D | | | | V
Grant a role to a person | | A | D | R | | | | | V
Move a person between roles | | A | D | R | | | | | V
Remove a leaver | | | D | R | | | | | V
Recertify the holders of a role | A | D | D | | | | | | V
Take break-glass access | | | | | A | R | | | V
Review break-glass use | V | | | | D | | | V | V
Read the access log | V | V | V | | V | | | V | V

A approves. D does the work. R requests. V views. A blank cell means no part in the action. A role owner views the access log for their own roles only.

secs.h: 3.4 If the bank chooses central administration
secs.t:
Level 3 moves from the Chief Debt Recovery Management Office to the bank's central IAM team.

Role owners still approve each grant, because only the unit head can judge who needs a recovery role.

The application owner still signs each access review.

Nothing in the Workbench build changes. Training and the access tests in section 10 move to the central team.

Class | Roles | Signs in to the Workbench | Identity
Bank user | 37 | Yes | Entra ID, bank account
Partner user | 7 | Not until external access is approved (G3) | A partner identity through an external gateway
Customer party | 4 | No. Customers, guarantors, heirs and bidders are parties on a case and reach the bank through the existing channels | None in the Workbench
Non-human actor | 5 | Acts under a service identity | Managed identity
Total | 53

The five non-human actors are the case workflow module, the rules component, the OCR and extraction pipeline, the decision log writer and the agent platform. None of them loads source data; the read path is the ACE views. Every role with its permissions is listed in the Users, roles and permissions workbook.

A role is named for a job, never for a person.

Every role has one role owner and a default scope: own, team, region or all.

No role inherits from another. A person who needs two roles holds both, and the permissions of both apply.

A role, a permission, a scope rule and a masking rule are each a data row with a version and an effective date. A change is a validated load, not a code release.

A capability area with no letter for a role refuses every action in that area.

Masking is applied before data reaches a screen or an agent. A role sees a personal data field unmasked only where its masking rule allows it.

There is one Entra ID group per role per environment. Membership of the group is the only way to hold the role.

A session keeps the versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends. The next session uses the versions then in force.

Part | Values | Held in | Owner
Operation | C create, R read, U update, D delete, A approve | Permission matrix | Application owner
Capability area | Case record; queue and allocation; treatment and offer; litigation; asset and disposal; debt sale; write-off and posting; documents; rules and parameters; reference data; decision log; partner portal; reporting; platform administration | Permission matrix | Application owner
Scope | Own, team, region, all | Scope rules | Role owner
Masking | Masked or unmasked, per personal data field | Masking rules | Compliance
Approval limit | Decision type and amount per approval level | Delegation of authority table | Risk with the product heads

Scope filters the records first and the permission is checked second. A record outside a person's scope is never returned, and the count of records excluded is never shown.

secs.h: 4.4 Roles with real users at each release
secs.t: Epic 1, released on 30 November 2026, delivers the foundation with no business screens. At that release only the administration roles hold real users: security administrator, platform administrator, reference data administrator, center of excellence analyst, data steward, Compliance and internal audit. Each business role has named test users in SIT and UAT. Business roles receive real users from the release that gives them a screen, starting with Epic 2 in December 2026. This position is assumed until the business lead confirms the list (G6).

Step | Who | Action | Where | Record
1 | Line manager | Raises a request naming the person, the role and the reason | Bank IAM | IAM request
2 | Role owner | Approves or rejects, after checking the conflict table in section 6.1 | Bank IAM | IAM approval
3 | Access administrator | Adds the person to the Entra ID group for the role in each environment requested | Bank IAM to Entra ID | Group change
4 | The person | Signs in with multi-factor authentication | Workbench | Sign-in in the access log
5 | Workbench | Resolves the roles, scope and masking. The first screen names the roles and the scope in one line | Workbench | Session in the access log

Event | What happens | Control
Mover | One request removes the previous roles and adds the new ones in the same change. The owners of both the old and the new roles approve. | A mover never holds both sets of roles
Leaver | The line manager or the HR leaver record starts removal from every Workbench group. The open session ends at the next request and no new session can start. | Removal within the leaver response time (G5)
Periodic review | Each role owner recertifies every holder of their roles. A holder who is not recertified is removed. The application owner signs the result. | At the review interval (G5)
No role | A person who signs in with no role is refused with the message: You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The refusal is written to the access log

A platform administrator requests access beyond their role, naming the open incident, the capability area, the scope and the reason in at least 20 characters.

The security administrator approves. A request with no open incident is refused.

The grant ends when its window ends, with no action by anyone. The screen shows that break-glass is active and the time remaining.

Every action under break-glass is marked as break-glass in the access log with the incident reference.

The security administrator reviews the use inside the review window (G5). An unreviewed use goes to the head of SCB IT security and to Compliance.

secs.h: 6.1 Role pairs one person may not hold
secs.t:
Role | May not also hold | Reason
Security administrator | Any business role | The person who maps groups to roles could grant themselves business access
Platform administrator | Any business role | Technical access combined with business access passes around scope and masking
Access administrator | Role owner for the same roles | One person would approve and carry out the same grant
Reference data administrator | Risk and model risk officer | Loading a delegation or rule version and approving it are separate steps
Center of excellence analyst | Risk and model risk officer | Writing a rule and approving it are separate steps
Restructuring officer | Credit approval committee member | Proposing a restructure and approving it are separate steps
Write-off team member | Write-off committee member | Proposing a write-off and approving it are separate steps
Internal audit | Any other role | Audit reads and changes nothing

The role owner checks the table at step 2 of every grant. The Workbench checks it again at sign-in: a session that would hold a conflicting pair is refused, an incident is raised to the security administrator and the refusal is logged.

A person may not approve a decision they proposed or prepared, whatever their approval level.

A person may not approve their own access request or review their own break-glass use.

The person who requests a grant and the person who approves it are two different people.

An agent may recommend. A person approves wherever the autonomy level of the step requires it.

The bank sets approval authority for problem loans and for assets held for sale in Regulation กกค.540031, amended by กกค.690070: chapter 2 for problem loans and chapter 3 for assets held for sale. Chapter 2 does not cover credit cards, unsecured loans or auto loans. Those follow chapter 8 of credit approval regulation รบ.-กส.450032, amended by กกค.690085, or the product regulation. The Workbench covers hire purchase, so both regulations apply.

Level | Problem loans, chapter 2 | Assets held for sale, chapter 3
1 | Board of Directors | Board of Directors
2 | Executive Committee | Executive Committee
3 | Problem Asset Resolution Committee | Management Committee
4 | Head of Recovery, function level | Problem Asset Resolution Committee
5 | Recovery executive, division level | Head of Recovery, function level, or Recovery executive, division level
6 | Recovery executive, department level | No level 6

Problem Asset Resolution Committee is คณะกรรมการแก้ไขสินทรัพย์ที่มีปัญหา. Management Committee is คณะกรรมการจัดการ.

Chapter 2 sets limits for each of these decisions: debt restructuring; partial release of collateral; delay of legal action; the auction price; release of a guarantor; delay of seizure where the bank holds a preferential right; extension of the repayment period; cancellation of legal action; delay or suspension of an auction; write-off; recovery of written-off debt; new credit to a problem loan; transfer of claims to a third party; and release of a Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation guarantee. Chapter 3 sets limits for sale, lease, extension of a sale contract, and legal action on assets held for sale.

secs.h: 7.1 How an approval level attaches to a person
secs.t:
The A letter in the permission matrix says a role may approve. The approval level and the delegation of authority table say which decision and up to what amount.

An approval level belongs to a person in a position. It is held as data with effective dates, and it is not a role. A person who changes position changes level in the same change.

Limits are held in the delegation of authority table exactly as the regulation states them: principal amount, loss as a percentage, and sale price against fair market value. A limit change is a data load approved by Risk.

Committee levels approve by resolution. The Workbench records the decision once, with the resolution reference, the date and the members present.

Each level names a substitute for when the holder is absent, with effective dates (G4).

A decision that no limit covers goes to the next level up, and an incident records the missing limit.

A decision already approved keeps the delegation version it was approved under.

Seven partner roles exist: collection agencies, law firms, valuers, auction vendors, debt buyers and asset management companies, RAMC, and the Legal Execution Department. Opening the Workbench to users outside the bank makes it internet facing. That needs a change approved by the architecture team, with a lead time of one to three months. Law firms are first needed at Epic 5, litigation, in March 2027. A request made in November gives an answer between December 2026 and February 2027, so the request has to be raised in November.

Until external access is approved, partners keep the channels they use today: the LIT lawyer web for law firms, the OA portal for collection agencies, SVAF for valuers, HOME.SCB for asset buyers, and file exchange by SFTP.

Once approved, a partner user holds a partner identity separate from bank identities, signs in with multi-factor authentication, and is limited to the cases placed with their firm. The partner and agency manager requests partner users. The role owner approves. A partner account ends when the firm's contract ends. The permission matrix, masking and access log apply to partner users in the same way as to bank users.
Customers, guarantors, heirs and bidders do not sign in to the Workbench. They act through SCB Easy, LINE OA, branches and the contact center. A data subject request follows the bank's PDPA process.

Each non-human actor has its own managed identity, a role in the roles table and a named owner.

Credentials are held in Key Vault. No identity is shared between actors.

An agent identity holds only the permissions that the autonomy level of its step allows.

Every action by a service identity is checked against the matrix and written to the access log, as for a person.

The read path adds two database identities, and neither is a Workbench role. The ACE view owner owns the recovery.v_ace_* views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables; it is the only recovery identity that reads the public ACE tables, and it writes neither schema. The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only; it has no direct read of a public ACE table and no write on any ACE table or view, so a direct read of a public table fails at the database.

Record | Holds | Read by
Workbench access log, inside the decision log | Sign-ins, refusals, grants and removals, the versions in force, break-glass use, every read of the case store, the document store and the recovery data. Append only | Application owner; role owners for their roles; security administrator; Compliance; internal audit
ACE audit log | Every change made through the service | Security administrator; internal audit
PII log through PII Kafka | Every read of a personal data field | Compliance; internal audit
SOC log | Security events for monitoring | SCB security operations

Retention of each record follows the bank retention schedule, set in the records retention and archiving document.

secs.h: 10. How access is tested before each release
secs.t:
Test | How | Passes when | Signed by
Sign-in | A test user for each role in the release signs in with multi-factor authentication | The session shows the right roles, scope and masking | Role owner
No role | A user with an Entra ID account and no Workbench group signs in | Refused with the message in 5.2; refusal in the access log | Security administrator
Scope | A case owner test user opens a case owned by another team | Nothing is returned; refusal in the access log | Role owner
Masking | Test users of three roles open the same case | Each sees personal data fields masked as the masking rules state | Compliance
Conflict | A test user is placed in two groups listed in 6.1 | The session is refused and an incident is raised | Security administrator
Leaver | A group is removed during an open session | The next request ends the session | Access administrator
Break-glass | One request with an open incident and one without | The first is granted for its window with every action marked; the second is refused | Security administrator
Matrix change | A new matrix version changes one permission | The change applies from its effective date with no code release | Application owner

Test users exist in SIT and UAT only. The application owner accepts the access tests as part of the release sign-off.

ID | Needed from the bank | Owner | By | Position used until answered | If the answer differs
G1 DL01 | Whether access is granted centrally or by the application owner | K. Tee | 28 Oct | Application owner administration, with the Chief Debt Recovery Management Office as access administrator | Level 3 moves to the central IAM team. No build change
G2 DL02 | Who the application owner is | K. Tee with K. Bell | 28 Oct | Tribe Lead, Collections and Recovery Tribe, for ACE as a whole; ACE team as technical custodian | Level 1 and the review sign-off move. No build change
G3 DL03 | Who makes the architecture change for external partner access | K. Book with the architecture team | 29 Oct | Partners stay on their existing channels | Each month of delay moves partner access in the Workbench one release later
G4 DL18 | Which person holds each approval level, and the substitute for each | Risk with the product heads | 30 Nov | The delegation of authority table is loaded with the regulation's levels and limits and no names | Approval routing in Epic 2 cannot pass user acceptance testing
G5 DL38 | The access review interval, the leaver response time and the break-glass review window | SCB IT security | 20 Nov | Review every six months; leaver within the same working day; break-glass reviewed within one working day. Each is a parameter | The parameter values change by data load. No build change
G6 DL39 | Which roles receive real users at each release | Business lead, Collections and Recovery Tribe | 20 Nov | Administration roles at Epic 1; business roles from Epic 2 | The provisioning list for each release changes
G7 DL40 | The Entra ID group names and the IAM entry for the Workbench roles | SCB IT security | 6 Nov | One group per role per environment, named to the bank standard | Group mapping is a data load. No build change

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Pre-Build Rulings v2 |
| Superseded by | Counts superseded by D-RCV-35 (section 0) |
| Scope | The four source conflicts in RWB-E1-001 found by the specification re-run of 10 November 2026, ruled for the initial phase (nothing built); re-based on Physical Schema v5 and D-RCV-35 (section 0) |
| Status | Proposed - best-answer set for the specification gate. The full paste-ready pack (seed table, corrected view SQL, line-by-line edit schedule) is Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Specification Rulings v2.md |

Because nothing is built, the calculus is to fix root causes in the source documents now: deferring a constraint or carrying an overloading forward costs nothing today but compounds once RWB-E1-003 through E1-013 consume the schema.

This version re-bases the best-answer set on Physical Schema v5 and D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5). The copy-table counts it was written against - 44 tables, 533 fields, 108 `sys_objects` and 1,256 `sys_fields` - are superseded. The schema is 92 tables, 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, 122 `sys_objects` and 1,366 `sys_fields`, with no copy or load tables left in it.

The four answers and their reasoning stand. Q4 (= R4 in the Specification Rulings) holds: the 14 definitions are seeded from the Conceptual Data Model v6 Data products tab, and the systems of record become "ACE (ingested from X)" - for example "ACE (ingested from ALS)" for DP01 - because ACE is the store the Workbench reads. Where the later sections still quote the v4 counts, they are the record of the 10 November re-run. The full paste-ready pack is **Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Specification Rulings v2.md**.

| Question | Initial-phase best answer | Beats the minimal answer because |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 - FK vs catalog | D (new option) - make sys_objects.data_product nullable, set the 33 operational rows to NULL, keep the FK | Fixes the real defect (overloaded column) from day one instead of deferring a knowingly-broken reference |
| Q2 - NULL owner_role | 1 - the view takes owner_role from data_product, plus full section-12 alignment of the view in one pass | No consumers exist yet, so align the view to the contract completely, not just one column |
| Q3 - delegation_limit seed | 3, amended | Already the root-cause answer; the real content belongs to RWB-E1-038 |
| Q4 - missing definitions | 1 - definitions from the CDM v6 Data products tab | Already the root-cause answer; the text is one-to-one for all 14 products |

secs.h: 2. Q1 - best: fix the overloading, keep the FK
secs.t:
The evidence supports the model correction better than deferral:

- LDM DF-REF-091 already anticipates it. Its own meaning text reads: "Data product the object belongs to, **DP01 to DP14 or None**". The Mandatory = Yes flag is the inconsistent part.
- Nothing is lost by emptying the 33 rows. For all 33, subject_area already equals data_product (OPS/AGT/RPT) - the subject_area column is the legitimate home for that classification.
- The story's own text survives unchanged. Section 13's "inserts the data_product seed rows before the sys_objects rows" and the FK statement both remain true. The 68-FK count in flow step 2 (and defect-register row 10, which records "68 FKs matching Physical Schema v4") stays accurate - deferring the FK would have silently changed it to 67.
- Every AC holds. AC1 (44 tables), AC3/AC8 (14 catalog rows), AC6 (108/1,256 after the count correction in section 6), and D-RCV-29's completeness counts. D-RCV-29 needs one wording amendment: "data_product empty for the 33 operational entities, which carry OPS/AGT/RPT in subject_area."

Required edits (details in clauses 1.1-1.8 of the Specification Rulings pack):

1. LDM v6 -> v7: DF-REF-091 -> Optional, and the Entities tab drops OPS/AGT/RPT from the Data product column (they stay in Subject area).
2. Physical Schema v4 -> v5: sys_objects.data_product varchar(10) nullable; FK fk_sys_objects_data_product retained as declared.
3. Story section 13: the seed statement becomes "75 sys_objects rows carry a data product; 33 operational entities leave it empty."
4. Migration order unchanged: catalog rows -> sys_objects -> sys_fields.

secs.h: 3. Q2 - best: one full view alignment, not one line
secs.t:
The view takes owner_role from data_product - but do the whole reconciliation in one pass, since nobody consumes the view yet:

```sql
-- align to story section 12 exactly
o.system_of_record AS entity_system_of_record, -- add (missing today)
p.system_of_record AS product_system_of_record, -- add (missing today)
p.owner_role, -- replace f.owner_role
```

One naming decision to make now while it costs nothing: section 12 calls the flags `mandatory` and `personal`; the view exposes `is_mandatory` / `is_personal`. Update section 12 to the view's names (it matches every other physical column); either is fine, but it must be one set, not two.

secs.h: 4. Q3 - best: no placeholder rows, ever
secs.t:
Already the root-cause fix:

- The 24 rows are `decision_code = 'ALL'`, which is not in LOV-DECISION (D1-D9 plus X1-X7). They are a placeholder grid, not a subset of the 95-limit matrix.
- RWB-E1-038 is the content owner: it loads DOA-2026.11 - 218 rows from the 95 matrix limits (109 MORTGAGE + 109 SSME) - with limit_version and regulation_item properly populated.
- Chapter 8 limits (the 12 HIRE_PURCHASE/UNSECURED rows) "load when supplied (DL18)" per the matrix; they cannot be invented for a baseline.

Pre-build extras while editing:

- Delete the 24 stray inserts from Physical Schema v5 entirely - do not just comment them in the migration; the source file is what the next story copies.
- Amend D-RCV-29: remove delegation_limit from the seed list. The story's flow step 3 never mentioned it anyway, so this re-aligns the ruling with the story rather than diverging from it.
- RWB-E1-043's AC2 fixture (24 rows) stays valid as a version-mechanism test, but its rows should carry limit_version/regulation_item values so it is shape-consistent with real loads.
- RWB-E1-038 section 13 says its migration "adds" limit_version/regulation_item - but v4 already declares them. Correct E1-038 to say the columns come from V0001 and the story's migration adds only the lookup index ix_delegation_lookup, which is not yet in the schema file.

secs.h: 5. Q4 - best: seed the definitions, keep NOT NULL
secs.t:
Sourced from the CDM v6 Data products tab (v5 when first ruled); all 14 fit varchar(400) (longest 154 characters, DP02). The mapping is one-to-one for the 14 products - the non-one-to-one case is only on the Subject areas tab, so no composition rule is needed.

Pre-build extras:

- Correct story section 13's DDL outlier to `definition varchar(400) not null` (matching the LDM and the schema).
- Have each product's business owner approve the wording on record.

These four fall out of the same documents and should not be left for the squad to trip over:

| # | Issue | Best fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | AC1 says 413 of 413 fields; AC6 says sys_objects 41 / sys_fields 413 | 413 is actually the S2T mapping total (110 inbound + 303 Workbench). The 44 tables hold 533 business fields (499 on the 41 tables + 7 sys_objects + 17 sys_fields + 10 data_product) and sys_fields holds 1,256. So AC1 -> "533 of 533", AC6 -> "108 / 1,256" |
| 2 | data_product.valid_from is NOT NULL but the section 13 seed table has no date column | Add it; seed with the AC3/AC10 catalog date 2026-11-20 so seed and first load agree |
| 3 | Story says product_code varchar(4); LDM and v4 say varchar(25) | Correct the story (and the duplicated DDL text in RWB-E1-064 section 13 and RWB-E1-016 section 13) to varchar(25) |
| 4 | RWB-E1-064 still claims it creates data_product and adds the four sys_fields columns that v4 already declares | V0001 owns the DDL; E1-064 owns the content load and sys_field_version. Remove the duplicate migration text before it becomes a real tick-order conflict |

> **D-RCV-34 (proposed):** On the specification-gate re-run of 10 November 2026 against Physical Schema v4: (1) sys_objects.data_product is nullable and empty for the 33 operational entities (OPS/AGT/RPT carry them in subject_area); FK fk_sys_objects_data_product is created in V0001. DF-REF-091 becomes Optional. (2) v_data_dictionary takes owner_role from data_product and adds entity_system_of_record and product_system_of_record; section 12 renamed to the view's column names. (3) delegation_limit is not seeded by V0001; the 24 placeholder rows are removed; content is owned by RWB-E1-038 loading DOA-2026.11 (218 rows) through RWB-E1-043, amending D-RCV-29. (4) data_product.definition stays NOT NULL; the 14 definitions are seeded from the CDM v6 Data products tab and repeated in the catalog load. (5) AC1 corrected to 533/533 conformance fields; AC6 corrected to 108/1,256 rows; valid_from seeded 2026-11-20; product_code length corrected to varchar(25).

If the gate prefers the already-ruled artifacts untouched, the minimal deployable set (previous memo) was C / 1 / 3 / 1 - but it leaves a knowingly-broken reference, a stale view contract, duplicate DDL in E1-064 and wrong AC counts, each trivial to avoid today and non-trivial once other stories depend on the migration. Since we are in the initial phase, take the bundle above as a single specification-gate amendment now.

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Specification Rulings v2 |

| Scope | The four source conflicts in RWB-E1-001 found by the specification re-run of 10 November 2026 against Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql, plus the conformance corrections that ride with them; re-based on Physical Schema v5 and D-RCV-35 (section 0) |
| Status | Proposed - for approval at the specification gate before RWB-E1-001 enters build. v2 re-bases the counts and the systems of record on D-RCV-35; the rulings are unchanged |
| Decision owner | Recovery tech lead with the data architect (the same owner that took D-RCV-29) |
| Amends | D-RCV-29 |
| Related | D-RCV-28; D-RCV-35; DL43 (open, needed 2026-11-21); DL41 (ruled); DL18 (open, needed 2026-11-30); Story Defects register v2 rows 10 and 11 |
| Sources examined | Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v6.xlsx; Conceptual Data Model v5.xlsx; Data Ownership and Stewardship v2.xlsx; Reference Data and Lists of Values v3.xlsx; Delegation of Authority Matrix v2.xlsx; Decision Log v8.xlsx; stories RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-038, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-064; Build Notes Epic 1 v4 |

Because RWB-E1-001 has not been built, each ruling fixes the root cause in the source document rather than deferring a defect. Nothing in this pack changes a runtime code decision; every edit is a document, DDL or seed-data change.

This version carries the four rulings into Physical Schema v5 and the ACE read path. The copy-table counts this document was written against - 44 tables, 533 conformance fields, 108 `sys_objects` and 1,256 `sys_fields` - are superseded by D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5). The schema is now 92 tables, 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, 122 `sys_objects` and 1,366 `sys_fields`, and the 20 copy, load and tracker tables have left it.

The rulings R1 to R4 and their reasoning stand. R1, R3 and R4 are applied in Physical Schema v5, and R4 seeds its 14 definitions from the Conceptual Data Model v6. Systems of record are re-worded "ACE (ingested from X)", because ACE is the store the Workbench reads. Where sections 2 and 6 to 10 still quote the v4 counts, they are the record of the 10 November re-run, not the live figures.

| # | Conflict | Ruling | Key effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 33 sys_objects rows carry AGT/OPS/RPT, which the 14-row data_product catalog cannot hold | sys_objects.data_product becomes nullable; the 33 operational rows are seeded with NULL; fk_sys_objects_data_product is created in V0001 | The FK ships on day one; AC1, AC3, AC6, AC8 and D-RCV-29 counts all hold |
| R2 | v_data_dictionary returns owner_role NULL, failing AC2 | The view reads owner_role from data_product, per story section 12; both system_of_record views are added in the same pass | The physical schema was the defect, not the story |
| R3 | All 24 delegation_limit baseline rows violate NOT NULL limit_version and regulation_item | delegation_limit is empty in V0001; the 24 placeholder rows are removed; content is owned by RWB-E1-038 loading DOA-2026.11 through RWB-E1-043 | The migration deploys; the router never sees invented rows |
| R4 | data_product.definition is NOT NULL but no source supplied values | Seed the 14 definitions from the Conceptual Data Model v6 Data products tab; correct the story DDL to not null | No schema change; RWB-E1-016 AC2 and RWB-E1-064 get a populated catalog |

secs.h: 2. Ruling 1 - sys_objects.data_product is nullable; the FK stays

secs.t: Physical Schema v4 line 2639 declares fk_sys_objects_data_product, yet 33 of the 108 sys_objects seed rows carry values (OPS 22, AGT 8, RPT 3) that are outside the 14-row data_product catalog required by AC3 and AC8.

- Physical Schema v4 lines 4183ff seed 108 sys_objects rows: 75 carry DP01 to DP14, 33 carry OPS, AGT or RPT.
- The LDM v6 Entities tab assigns exactly the same 108 entities to the same distribution, so this is deliberate modelling across two documents, not a seed typo.
- For all 33 rows, subject_area equals data_product (OPS/AGT/RPT). The column is carrying two kinds of code: a product code for 75 rows and a subject-area code for 33.
- The Conceptual Data Model v5 defines exactly 14 data products; its Subject areas tab maps OPS, AGT and RPT to the subject areas Loads and operations, Agent runtime and Reporting.
- LOV-DATA-PRODUCT (Reference Data v3) holds exactly 14 values.
- The LDM meaning text of DF-REF-091 already reads "DP01 to DP14 **or None**"; the Mandatory = Yes flag is the inconsistent part.
- Nothing is lost by emptying the 33 rows: subject_area is the legitimate home for that classification.

sys_objects.data_product becomes nullable. V0001 seeds 75 sys_objects rows with a product and the 33 operational rows with NULL. FK fk_sys_objects_data_product is created in V0001, as story section 13 already states, so the constraint ships from day one. This is the model correction; it replaces the smaller deviation of deferring the FK (previous recommendation C) and is cheaper before build than after it.

**Status:** applied in Physical Schema v5. `sys_objects.data_product` is nullable and the 33 operational rows carry NULL; `fk_sys_objects_data_product` is created in V0001.

| # | Document and location | Current | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Physical Schema v4 -> issue v5, sys_objects DDL (lines 1065-1082) | `data_product varchar(10) NOT NULL` | `data_product varchar(10)` (nullable) |
| 1.2 | v5, sys_objects seed block (lines 4183ff) | 33 rows carry `'OPS'`, `'AGT'` or `'RPT'` | Replace the fourth value with `NULL` on those 33 rows; add the comment: `-- Operational entities (loads, agents, reporting) carry no data product; subject_area keeps OPS/AGT/RPT (D-RCV-34).` |
| 1.3 | v5, line 2639 | fk_sys_objects_data_product | Unchanged - the FK is kept and created in V0001 |
| 1.4 | LDM v6 -> issue v7, Fields tab, DF-REF-091 | Mandatory = Yes | Mandatory = No; meaning text gains "; the operational entities of OPS, AGT and RPT carry no product" |
| 1.5 | LDM v7, Entities tab | 33 entity rows show OPS/AGT/RPT in the Data product column | Blank the Data product value on those 33 rows (subject area unchanged) |
| 1.6 | Conceptual Data Model v5 -> optional reissue, Subject areas tab rows 19-21 | "Loads and operations", "Agent runtime", "Reporting" name OPS/AGT/RPT in the Data products column | Remove those three tokens so subjects no longer masquerade as product codes |
| 1.7 | RWB-E1-001 story, section 13, Database paragraph | "Adds a foreign key from sys_objects.data_product to data_product.product_code; the migration inserts the data_product seed rows before the sys_objects rows." | Sentence stays; append: "sys_objects.data_product is nullable: the 75 product entities name DP01 to DP14; the 33 operational entities of OPS, AGT and RPT leave it empty (D-RCV-34)." |
| 1.8 | RWB-E1-001 story, section 11, row DF-REF-091 | "Create and write 108 rows; read" | Annotate: "Create and write 108 rows (75 with a product, 33 empty); read" |

secs.h: 3. Ruling 2 - v_data_dictionary reads owner_role from data_product

secs.t: The view takes `f.owner_role` (line 2543), but all 1,256 sys_fields inserts use a 12-column list that never populates owner_role, so AC2's expected "RW-DATASTEW" returns NULL.

- Story section 12 has always mapped owner_role to data_product - the view differs from the story, not the other way round.
- data_product.owner_role is NOT NULL and is seeded RW-DATASTEW for every product.
- LDM DF-REF-107 (sys_fields.owner_role) is Mandatory = No and is loaded later by RWB-E1-064 as a per-field attribute; it is not the AC2 source.
- The current view also omits product_system_of_record and entity_system_of_record, which section 12 names.

The view is corrected in one pass, since no consumer exists yet: owner_role from data_product, plus the two system-of-record columns, plus the four sys_fields attributes that RWB-E1-064 will need. Section 12 adopts the view's column names (is_mandatory, is_personal) so there is one naming set.

Replace v_data_dictionary in v5 with:

```sql
CREATE VIEW v_data_dictionary AS
SELECT o.object_name AS entity,
 f.field_name AS field,
 f.field_id,
 f.data_type,
 f.physical_type,
 f.is_mandatory,
 f.lov_code,
 f.references_object,
 f.source_system,
 f.source_field,
 f.is_personal,
 f.late_behavior,
 f.interface_id,
 f.description,
 o.data_product,
 o.system_of_record AS entity_system_of_record,
 p.system_of_record AS product_system_of_record,
 p.refresh_cycle,
 p.owner_role,
 p.owner_user_id
FROM sys_fields f
JOIN sys_objects o ON o.object_name = f.object_name
LEFT JOIN data_product p ON p.product_code = o.data_product AND p.is_active
WHERE f.is_active AND o.is_active;
```

| 2.1 | Physical Schema v5, lines 2529-2551 | Replace the view with the block above |
| 2.2 | RWB-E1-001 story, section 12 contract table | Replace with: entity, data_product, entity_system_of_record from sys_objects; field, field_id, data_type, physical_type, is_mandatory, lov_code, references_object, source_system, source_field, is_personal, late_behavior, interface_id, description from sys_fields; product_system_of_record, refresh_cycle, owner_role, owner_user_id from data_product |
| 2.3 | Build Notes Epic 1, step on the view ("The schema file has no definition for that view, so you write it.") | Replace with: "v_data_dictionary is held in Physical Schema v4 lines 2529-2551; copy it with the D-RCV-34 corrections (p.owner_role and the two system_of_record columns)." |

secs.h: 4. Ruling 3 - delegation_limit is empty in the baseline

secs.t: All 24 `INSERT INTO delegation_limit` rows in Physical Schema v4 (lines 6628-6651) omit limit_version and regulation_item, both NOT NULL (lines 883-884), so every row raises a not-null violation and the transaction discards the schema.

| Source | Rows | What it represents |
|---|---:|---|
| Physical Schema v4 seed | 24 | Placeholder grid: decision 'ALL' x levels L1-L6 x 4 product groups |
| Delegation of Authority Matrix v2 | 95 | The real limits, by regulation item, decision and level; no product_group column |
| RWB-E1-038 load DOA-2026.11 | 218 | 95 limits x 2 products (109 MORTGAGE + 109 SSME), with limit_version and regulation_item |
| RWB-E1-043 AC2 fixture | 24 | A version-mechanism test fixture, not the production matrix |

- decision_code 'ALL' is not a value of LOV-DECISION (D1 to D9 with sub-decisions, X1 to X7), so the placeholders are invalid before the two missing columns are even considered.
- Twelve of the 24 rows are HIRE_PURCHASE and UNSECURED; the matrix states chapter 8 limits "load when supplied (DL18)" and lists them as open.
- Matrix "How it applies" rule 11: each limit is a row with a version, valid from and valid to and the approver; a change is a data load approved by Risk.
- The E1-001 story's own flow step 3 never names delegation_limit - only D-RCV-29 does.

delegation_limit is empty in V0001. The 24 placeholder rows are deleted from the schema, not commented out. Content is owned by RWB-E1-038, which loads DOA-2026.11 (95 limits -> 218 rows) through RWB-E1-043, approved by RW-RISK, with limit_version and regulation_item from the matrix; the chapter 8 product-group rows follow when Risk supplies them (DL18). D-RCV-29 is amended to remove delegation_limit from the baseline seed list, which re-aligns the ruling with the story rather than diverging from it.

secs.h: 5. Ruling 4 - the 14 definitions are seeded from the CDM

secs.t: data_product.definition is varchar(400) NOT NULL (Physical Schema v4 line 984; LDM DF-REF-073 Mandatory = Yes). The story section 13 DDL reads `definition varchar(400)` with no not null, and its seed table carries no definition column, so the seed cannot be written against the schema as declared.

- Longest description is 143 characters, well inside varchar(400).
- BRD REQ-RDF-011 requires a catalog entry stating its definition; RWB-E1-016 AC2 returns definition; RWB-E1-064 owns the formal definitions. Leaving the column nullable would push a null into those two stories and need a later migration to restore NOT NULL.

definition stays NOT NULL. V0001 seeds the 14 definitions from the Conceptual Data Model Data products tab (v5 when this ruling was taken, v6 at issue); the catalog load repeats them. The story DDL outlier is corrected to match the LDM and the schema. Each product owner approves its wording at the gate.

5. Reapply in SIT; assert no change (Flyway skips version 1.001).

secs.h: 11. Fallback if the gate refuses the model change
secs.t: If the gate wanted the absolute smallest edit to the already-ruled documents, the minimal set was: drop the FK (previous recommendation C), correct the view, leave delegation_limit to E1-038, and seed the definitions. That is still deployable but ships a knowingly-broken reference, a stale view contract, duplicate DDL in E1-064 and wrong AC counts. Nothing is built yet, so the root-cause set above costs the same and removes all four follow-on defects.

secs.h: Slide 3. The value stream: six stages from day 90 to close
secs.t:
3
Receive the case
D6 entry
Choose the route
D6
Resolve with the customer
D6
Enforce
D7
Realize the asset
D8
Close
D9
Stage | Decision | L1 and L2 | What the stage produces
Receive the case | D6 entry | 06 | One owner, the case history from collections, running deadlines and a deviation screen
Choose the route | D6 | 07.1, 07.2 | An approved route with the expected return of each option and the reasons
Resolve with the customer | D6 | 07.3 to 07.5 | A settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor agreement, booked and reconciled
Enforce | D7 | 08 | A judgment enforced, a settlement before judgment, or proceeds matched to the case
Realize the asset | D8 | 09 | Cash from the asset or the debt: auction, RAMC, buy-back, rental or debt sale
Close | D9 | 10 | The balance written off and posted, recovery after charge-off, the case closed
A case can return to the route decision at any stage: on a cure, a payment, a deviation or an override.

4
Manage: set the rules and read the results
Strategy and treatment policy · Decision rules and limits · Fees and waivers · Performance reporting · Strategy testing · Model and agent monitoring · Data quality · Benefits tracking · Quality assurance · Conduct control · Audit and regulator response · Access and data protection · Capacity planning
Core: the case from day 90 to close
Case takeover · Case valuation · Route decision · Settlement and deed in lieu · Guarantee claims · Guarantor pursuit · Litigation · Judgment enforcement · Asset holding · Asset sale · Debt sale · Write-off · Recovery after charge-off
Support: used across every core stage
Customer care · Deviation handling X1 to X7 · Partner management · Document management and custody · Correspondence · Payments and reconciliation
Across all: at every decision
Decision routing and approval · Decision log · Feedback to models
Before day 90, collections runs detect, contact, promise, escalate and restructure on EFS and ACE. The Workbench takes the case over from collections at 90 days past due.

secs.h: Slide 6. The six capabilities the Workbench commits
secs.t:
6
Capability | What it provides | The gap it closes | First in
One case record | A single record per customer and product, with the accounts linked, from day 90 to close | Cases, accounts and debtors are held in separate files and systems | Epic 1
Stage clock | Days in each state against a service level, with escalation, and a prescription clock that keeps running when a stage pauses | Queues are visible but nothing escalates from them | Epic 1
Interaction ledger | Every contact, offer, promise, payment and hand-over on the case, in order | Contact history is spread across four systems | Epic 1
Document management | Case documents held against the case, indexed, with retention and custody of originals | Documents are kept outside the case and gaps are found late | Epic 1
Next action | An owned, dated action on every case, produced by the routing rules | Each unit receives its part with no owner where value is lost | Epic 2
Model-writable queue | A queue that analytical models write to directly | Daily model decisions arrive in a weekly manual process | Epic 2

secs.h: Slide 7. The nine decisions, and who owns each
secs.t:
7
 | What is decided | Owner | How it is decided | Where it runs
D1 | Act on the signal | Product head with the center of excellence | Agent, within policy | EFS
D2 | Reach the customer | Center of excellence with Compliance | Agent, within policy | EFS
D3 | Promise kept | Center of excellence | Agent, within policy | EFS
D4 | Escalate | Product head with the agency unit | Agent; a person on exception | EFS
D5 | Offer a restructure | Product head with Credit Risk | Agent proposes; a person approves above the limit | EFS and ACE

D8 | How to dispose | Head of NPA and Head of Auto Recovery | Agent runs; a person approves the floor price | Recovery Workbench
D9 | Write off or pursue | Credit Administration with Risk | Agent proposes; the committee approves | Recovery Workbench
Every decision runs on one pattern: information, decide, outcome, act, log. Who approves is set by the bank approval authority regulation and the delegation of authority table.

secs.h: Slide 10. The seven deviations that interrupt a decision
secs.t:
10
 | What has happened | Who decides | Where the case goes next
X1 | Dispute or complaint | Complaint officer | The same decision. The case timers resume
X2 | Vulnerable customer or hardship | Hardship specialist | D5
X3 | Deceased customer | Specialist; Legal for claims against the estate | Closed if insurance settles; otherwise D6
X4 | Fraud | Fraud team | D9, or D2 if fraud is not confirmed
X5 | Bankruptcy or external seizure | Legal | D7, then D9
X6 | Lost contact | Agent, within policy | D2 if found; D4 or D6 if not
X7 | Collateral event | Agent proposes; a person approves the claim | D6
A deviation pauses the stage clock. The prescription clock keeps running, because a court deadline does not wait for a complaint to be resolved.

docs.name: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4

secs.t:
Every move a case makes is one rule. When an event arrives at a case in a given state and the condition holds, the Workbench takes the action, moves the case to the next state, gives it to the named owner and starts the timer. There are 448 rules in ten route sets.
Rules
448
Route sets
10
Rules with a timer
252 of 448
Rules whose next state a person or partner owns
366 of 448

Each route set is one decision table in Decision Model and Notation 1.4.

Column | Kind | Meaning
Rule | Identifier | R, the route set code and a number, for example R-LIT-12
From state | Input | The state the case is in when the event arrives
Event | Input | What happened: a payment, a document, a decision, a date reached, a partner result
Condition | Input | What must hold for the rule to fire. Any means the event alone fires it
Action | Output | What the Workbench does
To state | Output | The state the case moves to
Owner | Output | Who holds the case in the next state. Workbench means no person
Systems | Output | The systems the action reads or writes
Timer | Output | How long the next state may last before it escalates
Hit policy: Unique
In a route set, for one state and one event, at most one condition holds, so one rule fires.

Every rule is a row in a versioned table, with its rule ID, version, valid from, valid to, author, approver and test case ID. A rule change is a validated data load, not a code release. A case keeps the rule version it was decided under, and the decision log records the rule ID and version for every move.

Test | What it decides
Product | Mortgage, hire purchase or SSME. The product decides which routes are open at all.
Days past due and exposure | Which band the case falls in, and therefore who owns it and what they may approve.
Security | Whether the bank holds an asset, a guarantee or nothing.
Hard gates | A death, fraud, bankruptcy, a complaint or a legal hold stops the normal route and sends the case to a deviation owner first.

Route | Chosen when | How it runs
Restructure | The customer can pay, but needs longer terms. | COLLINS proposes, FCR builds the offer.
Settlement | The customer can pay a reduced amount now. | Priced against the payoff floor.
Deed in lieu | The customer will hand over the asset instead of paying. | Valued, consented, transferred at the Land Office.
Guarantee claim | A guarantor or an insurer covers part or all of it. | Claim filed with TCG or the insurer.
Litigation | No engagement, or the amount justifies court. | Notices, then a panel law firm, then judgment.
Asset disposal | The bank already holds the asset. | Listed and run down the price ladder.
Debt sale | The account is worth more sold than worked. | Built into a lot and awarded to a buyer.
Write off | Nothing is left to recover economically. | Proposed monthly, approved, posted.

End | What happens
Cured or settled | The customer pays, a plan runs to term, or a settlement clears.
Realized | An asset sells, a guarantee pays, or the debt is sold.
Written off | Posted and closed, with recovery continuing after charge-off.

Product | Routes open | Where the volume goes
Mortgage | Restructure, settlement, deed in lieu, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale, write off | Deed in lieu and asset disposal carry the volume. The Land Office transfer and the LED auction ladder are the long steps.
Hire purchase | Restructure, settlement, voluntary surrender, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale, write off | Voluntary surrender replaces deed in lieu. The asset moves faster and the auction cycle is shorter.
SSME | Restructure, settlement, guarantee claim, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale, write off | The guarantee claim route matters here because of TCG cover. Deed in lieu applies only where there is property security.
Unsecured | Settlement, litigation, debt sale, write off | No asset, so no disposal and no deed in lieu. Most volume ends in debt sale or write off.
A deviation stops the normal route at any point and returns the case when it clears. The universal rules run in every state.

All products. D5 runs on EFS and ACE until the TDR project is live, then on the Workbench.

Property and vehicles. The asset is on the bank's books by repossession, deed in lieu or a Legal Execution Department hand-over.
Starts when
An asset is taken onto the bank's books and the holding age clock starts
Ends when
Sold, proceeds applied and the case closed with no shortfall; Sold with a residual, handed to debt sale or write-off; Transferred to RAMC or the joint venture; Rented, with the asset still held
Decision
D8.1 to D8.3

72

Officer step: a bank officer acts
Decision point: a rule or an approver chooses
Customer step: the customer acts
Partner step: a partner acts
Exception: reached by an event
End state: the route ends here
A pale line returns the case to an earlier state. A dashed line is a return that needs no rule.

secs.h: The recovery case as a CMMN 1.1 model
secs.t:
Recovery is adaptive case management. The bank wants a milestone reached, such as a case cured, settled, sold or closed, and the officer chooses much of the path. The case holds stages, the stages hold tasks, and sentries decide when a task starts and when the case moves on. Each sentry is one routing rule, so the case model and the business rules are the same 448 rows.
Stages
10
Milestones
30
Tasks
150
Event listeners
53
Sentries
448
Case file items
12

Element | Count | What it is
Case | 1 | The recovery case for one customer and one product, with the accounts linked, from day 90 to close.
Stage | 10 | A route the case can be on. Eight are entered when the route decision selects them; the deviation stage and the universal rules are always available.
Milestone | 30 | A state the case reaches and does not leave. It marks an achievement, not work.
Human task | 90 | Work a bank officer does. The case puts it in a queue or the officer picks it up.
Customer task | 6 | Work the customer, guarantor or heir does. The case waits on them.
Partner task | 22 | Work an outside party does, such as a law firm, agency, buyer or valuer.
Decision task | 22 | A point where a rule or an approver sets the route. The outcome selects the next sentry.
Stage entry | 10 | The task a stage starts from. One per stage.
Event listener | 53 | A task reached by an event rather than chosen, such as a declined approval or a blocked listing.
Sentry | 448 | One entry or exit criterion: the event it listens for, the condition that must hold, and the action it takes. Each sentry is one routing rule.
Case file item | 12 | Data the case holds. Sentries read it to test their conditions.

Kind | Tasks | Meaning
Automatic | 46 | The Workbench starts the task. No person starts it.
Discretionary | 40 | A person chooses whether to start the task. It has more than one way out.
Required | 64 | The case puts the task in a queue for a named owner. The delegation of authority decides who.

Kind | Sentries | Meaning
User sentry | 137 | Fired by a person's action or decision.
Timer sentry | 269 | Carries a time limit; fires when the time is reached if nothing else has.
System sentry | 42 | Fired by the Workbench or another system, with no time limit.

Owner | Sentries
Bank officer | 264
Workbench | 91
Partner | 50
Approver | 31
Customer | 12

The case, its stages, tasks and milestones are rows in the Workbench database, moved by code in the recovery module of ACE. The condition and the action of each sentry are rows in a versioned table. A sentry change is a data load, and a case in flight keeps the version it entered the state under. Timers are stored due dates that the Workbench scheduler checks.

Every case is in one status at a time. The status is one level above the route state and is what queues, service levels and reports read.
Each box is a status. A pale line returns the case to an earlier status.

Status | Meaning | CMMN case state
New | Created at 90 days past due with its history. Not yet given an owner. | Active
Assigned | An owner and a queue are set by the allocation rules. The stage clock starts. | Active
In progress | The owner or the Workbench is working a task on the case. | Active
Waiting customer | An offer, notice or request is with the customer, with a validity timer running. | Active
Waiting partner | An instruction is with a partner, with a service level timer running. | Active
Waiting approval | A recommendation is with the approver set by the delegation of authority. | Active
On hold | A deviation or a legal hold has paused the case. The prescription clock keeps running. | Suspended
Closed | A milestone that closes the case is reached: cured, settled, sold, or written off with recovery ended. | Completed, then Closed

From | Event | To
New | Allocation rule matched | Assigned
Assigned | Owner or Workbench starts the first task | In progress
In progress | Offer or notice sent to the customer | Waiting customer
In progress | Instruction sent to a partner | Waiting partner
In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | Waiting approval
Waiting customer | Customer responds, or the validity timer expires | In progress
Waiting partner | Partner result arrives, or the service level timer expires | In progress
Waiting approval | Approver accepts, changes or rejects, or the approval escalates | In progress
New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | Deviation flagged or legal hold placed | On hold
On hold | Deviation cleared or hold released | The status it paused in
In progress, Waiting customer, Waiting partner | A milestone that closes the case is reached | Closed
On hold | The deviation ends the case, for example insurance settles the debt | Closed

The case is taken over and the route decision selects one of seven stages. A stage can end the case by itself, for example when a plan runs to term or a settlement clears, or pass what is left to write-off. A case can also move between stages, for example from litigation to asset disposal, through the route decision. The two outlined boxes are always available: a deviation can pause any active state, and the universal rules listen on every active state.

Stage | Kind | Entered when | Leaves when | Tasks and milestones | Sentries | Always available
Restructure, TDR | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a restructure, or D5 proposes one | Plan runs to term and the case closes; Plan breaks and the case returns to the route decision; Customer does not sign and the case returns to its prior status in COLLINS; A second break bars a further restructure | 18 | 37 | No
Settlement | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a settlement | Payment clears, the collateral is released and the case closes; The customer does not pay by the deadline and the case returns to the route decision; A payment reverses after release and the case re-opens | 15 | 27 | No
Deed in lieu and voluntary surrender | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a deed in lieu, or the customer offers the asset during a negotiation | The asset is on the books and hands off to the disposal route; The customer rents the asset back and the rental runs; The customer withdraws or the title is not clean and the case returns to the route decision | 20 | 37 | No
Litigation and enforcement, D7 | Enforcement stage | The route decision D6.3 approves litigation, or a broken treatment returns the case to the legal route | Debt satisfied and the case closes; Asset taken onto the books and handed to the disposal route; Judgment unenforceable or enforcement exhausted, and the case goes to write-off; Customer cures or settles, and the case returns to treatment | 38 | 79 | No
Guarantee claim, D6.5 and D6.6 | Recovery stage | A guarantee is detected on the case at takeover and the claim deadline timer starts | The claim is paid and the residual returns to the route decision; The claim is lost on the deadline and the full balance returns to the route decision; The guarantor settles and the case closes | 17 | 32 | No
Asset disposal, D8.1 to D8.3 | Recovery stage | An asset is taken onto the bank's books and the holding age clock starts | Sold, proceeds applied and the case closed with no shortfall; Sold with a residual, handed to debt sale or write-off; Transferred to RAMC or the joint venture; Rented, with the asset still held | 40 | 72 | No
Debt sale, D8.4 | Recovery stage | The monthly debt sale cycle opens, or a residual arrives from the disposal route | Lot awarded, settled, transferred and closed with realized recovery recorded; Lot withdrawn and the accounts returned to the case list; Put-back upheld and the account returned to the bank | 29 | 41 | No
Write off and recover after charge-off, D9 | Closure stage | The monthly eligibility scan runs on the cut-off date, or a residual arrives from another route | Posted, placed, recovered and closed after the retention period; Rejected by the committee and returned to the pursue track; Sold to a buyer as a charged-off population | 27 | 51 | No
Deviations X1 to X7 | Exception stage | The screening agent flags a deviation at entry or on a new document | The deviation clears and the case returns to the state it paused in; The deviation moves the case to a different route; The case ends, where insurance settles the debt | 9 | 22 | Yes
Universal rules, any state | Always on | The case is in any active state on any route | The case returns to the state it was in; The case moves to the route decision; The case closes; The case is canceled or merged | 20 | 50 | Yes

secs.t:
Case and workflow model: stages
10 stages. Element counts are in the Elements tab.
Stage | Kind | Entered when | Leaves when | Tasks and milestones | Sentries | Always available
Restructure, TDR | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a restructure, or D5 proposes one | Plan runs to term and the case closes; Plan breaks and the case returns to the route decision; Customer does not sign and the case returns to its prior status in COLLINS; A second break bars a further restructure | 18 | 37 | No
Settlement | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a settlement | Payment clears, the collateral is released and the case closes; The customer does not pay by the deadline and the case returns to the route decision; A payment reverses after release and the case re-opens | 15 | 27 | No
Deed in lieu and voluntary surrender | Solution stage | The route decision D6 approves a deed in lieu, or the customer offers the asset during a negotiation | The asset is on the books and hands off to the disposal route; The customer rents the asset back and the rental runs; The customer withdraws or the title is not clean and the case returns to the route decision | 20 | 37 | No
Litigation and enforcement, D7 | Enforcement stage | The route decision D6.3 approves litigation, or a broken treatment returns the case to the legal route | Debt satisfied and the case closes; Asset taken onto the books and handed to the disposal route; Judgment unenforceable or enforcement exhausted, and the case goes to write-off; Customer cures or settles, and the case returns to treatment | 38 | 79 | No
Guarantee claim, D6.5 and D6.6 | Recovery stage | A guarantee is detected on the case at takeover and the claim deadline timer starts | The claim is paid and the residual returns to the route decision; The claim is lost on the deadline and the full balance returns to the route decision; The guarantor settles and the case closes | 17 | 32 | No
Asset disposal, D8.1 to D8.3 | Recovery stage | An asset is taken onto the bank's books and the holding age clock starts | Sold, proceeds applied and the case closed with no shortfall; Sold with a residual, handed to debt sale or write-off; Transferred to RAMC or the joint venture; Rented, with the asset still held | 40 | 72 | No
Debt sale, D8.4 | Recovery stage | The monthly debt sale cycle opens, or a residual arrives from the disposal route | Lot awarded, settled, transferred and closed with realized recovery recorded; Lot withdrawn and the accounts returned to the case list; Put-back upheld and the account returned to the bank | 29 | 41 | No
Write off and recover after charge-off, D9 | Closure stage | The monthly eligibility scan runs on the cut-off date, or a residual arrives from another route | Posted, placed, recovered and closed after the retention period; Rejected by the committee and returned to the pursue track; Sold to a buyer as a charged-off population | 27 | 51 | No
Deviations X1 to X7 | Exception stage | The screening agent flags a deviation at entry or on a new document | The deviation clears and the case returns to the state it paused in; The deviation moves the case to a different route; The case ends, where insurance settles the debt | 9 | 22 | Yes
Universal rules, any state | Always on | The case is in any active state on any route | The case returns to the state it was in; The case moves to the route decision; The case closes; The case is canceled or merged | 20 | 50 | Yes

Elements
The CMMN 1.1 elements in the model and how many of each.
Element | Count | What it is
Case | 1 | The recovery case for one customer and one product, with the accounts linked, from day 90 to close.
Stage | 10 | A route the case can be on. Eight are entered when the route decision selects them; the deviation stage and the universal rules are always available.
Milestone | 30 | A state the case reaches and does not leave. It marks an achievement, not work.
Human task | 90 | Work a bank officer does. The case puts it in a queue or the officer picks it up.
Customer task | 6 | Work the customer, guarantor or heir does. The case waits on them.
Partner task | 22 | Work an outside party does, such as a law firm, agency, buyer or valuer.
Decision task | 22 | A point where a rule or an approver sets the route. The outcome selects the next sentry.
Stage entry | 10 | The task a stage starts from. One per stage.
Event listener | 53 | A task reached by an event rather than chosen, such as a declined approval or a blocked listing.
Sentry | 448 | One entry or exit criterion: the event it listens for, the condition that must hold, and the action it takes. Each sentry is one routing rule.
Case file item | 12 | Data the case holds. Sentries read it to test their conditions.
Starts: Automatic | 46 | The Workbench starts the task. No person starts it.
Starts: Discretionary | 40 | A person chooses whether to start the task. It has more than one way out.
Starts: Required | 64 | The case puts the task in a queue for a named owner. The delegation of authority decides who.
User sentry | 137 | Fired by a person's action or decision.
Timer sentry | 269 | Carries a time limit; fires when the time is reached if nothing else has.
System sentry | 42 | Fired by the Workbench or another system, with no time limit.

Case status
Eight statuses and the CMMN case state each maps to.
Status | Meaning | CMMN case state
New | Created at 90 days past due with its history. Not yet given an owner. | Active
Assigned | An owner and a queue are set by the allocation rules. The stage clock starts. | Active
In progress | The owner or the Workbench is working a task on the case. | Active
Waiting customer | An offer, notice or request is with the customer, with a validity timer running. | Active
Waiting partner | An instruction is with a partner, with a service level timer running. | Active
Waiting approval | A recommendation is with the approver set by the delegation of authority. | Active
On hold | A deviation or a legal hold has paused the case. The prescription clock keeps running. | Suspended
Closed | A milestone that closes the case is reached: cured, settled, sold, or written off with recovery ended. | Completed, then Closed

Status transitions
Every move between statuses.
From | Event | To
New | Allocation rule matched | Assigned
Assigned | Owner or Workbench starts the first task | In progress
In progress | Offer or notice sent to the customer | Waiting customer
In progress | Instruction sent to a partner | Waiting partner
In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | Waiting approval
Waiting customer | Customer responds, or the validity timer expires | In progress
Waiting partner | Partner result arrives, or the service level timer expires | In progress
Waiting approval | Approver accepts, changes or rejects, or the approval escalates | In progress
New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | Deviation flagged or legal hold placed | On hold
On hold | Deviation cleared or hold released | The status it paused in
In progress, Waiting customer, Waiting partner | A milestone that closes the case is reached | Closed
On hold | The deviation ends the case, for example insurance settles the debt | Closed

Milestones

R-UNI-32 | Universal rules | Timer sentry | ANY_ACTIVE | AGENT_UNAVAILABLE | the agent or the model does not answer inside the timeout | Fall back to the rule result and continue. Record the fallback on the decision | RESUME_STATE | Milestone | Workbench | 60 seconds
R-UNI-33 | Universal rules | Timer sentry | ANY_ACTIVE | SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE | a system of record is unavailable | Queue the outbound action and retry on the schedule | RETRY_QUEUE | Event listener | Platform team | per interface

Case file items
The data the case holds.
Item | Holds | Comes from
Case record | Identifier, product, customer, state, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date | P3 case and workflow

Collections history | Contact history, promises, the hand-over at 90 days past due | EFS, through COLLINS
Customer and party | The customer, the parties, the other products they hold | Customer profile received through COLLINS
Collateral | Collateral records | CCMS
Valuation | Appraisal values | SVAF
Case and ownership | State, owner, queue, stage clock | The Workbench
Partner and placement | Agency, law firm and partner placements | The Workbench
Tracker content | The Excel and SharePoint trackers, until they are retired | Excel and SharePoint trackers, until retired
Decision history | Why the system acted: inputs, rule, version, output | P7 decision center and log
Interaction ledger | What happened with the customer: channel, time, who, offer, promise, payment | P3 case and workflow, P6 communications
