secs.t:
COLLECTIONS AND RECOVERY TRANSFORMATION
Recovery Workbench: case journeys
Henka Group, 28 October 2026
(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

secs.h: Slide 2. Eight routes from day 90 to close
secs.t:
2
 | Route | Chosen when | How it runs
R1 | Restructure | The customer can pay, but needs longer terms. | COLLINS proposes, FCR builds the offer.
R2 | Settlement | The customer can pay a reduced amount now. | Priced against the payoff floor.
R3 | Deed in lieu | The customer will hand over the asset instead of paying. | Valued, consented, transferred at the Land Office.
R4 | Guarantee claim | A guarantor or an insurer covers part or all of it. | Claim filed with TCG or the insurer.
R5 | Litigation | No engagement, or the amount justifies court. | Notices, then a panel law firm, then judgment.
R6 | Asset disposal | The bank already holds the asset. | Listed and run down the price ladder.
R7 | Debt sale | The account is worth more sold than worked. | Built into a lot and awarded to a buyer.
R8 | Write off | Nothing is left to recover economically. | Proposed monthly, approved, posted.
A case ends | What happens
Cured or settled | The customer pays, a plan runs to term, or a settlement clears
Realized | An asset sells, a guarantee pays, or the debt is sold
Written off | Posted and closed, with recovery continuing after charge-off

3
Test | What it decides
Product | Mortgage, hire purchase or SSME. The product decides which routes are open at all.
Days past due and exposure | Which band the case falls in, and therefore who owns it and what they may approve.
Security | Whether the bank holds an asset, a guarantee or nothing.
Hard gates | A death, fraud, bankruptcy, a complaint or a legal hold stops the normal route and sends the case to a deviation owner first.
The route is recommended with the expected return of each option from COLLINS, and approved within the delegation of authority. A case can return to the route decision at any stage: on a cure, a payment, a deviation or an override.

4
The customer can pay something, over a longer term. What happens?
1 The system proposes it
COLLINS raises a restructure on the case after the route decision approves it.
Workbench
2 It reaches the restructuring officer
Into the FCR queue, with the plan calculated in ACE.
Restructuring officer, FCR
3 The officer builds and sends the offer
Inside the band, with affordability recorded. Exceptions only reach a person.
Restructuring officer
4 The customer decides
Not a routed state. A wait, with a validity timer running on it.
Customer
5 Signed goes to Operations
The signed agreement is booked and the plan starts.
Operations, booking
6 Not signed goes back
The case returns to the route decision.
Case owner
How the case can end
Plan runs to term and the case closes
Plan breaks and the case returns to the route decision
Customer does not sign and the case returns to the route decision
In the routing rules
Steps | 18
Rules | 37
Branch points | 10
Exception events | 5

5
The customer can pay a reduced amount now. What happens?
1 The route decision approves a settlement
The case carries a payoff figure and a floor.
Workbench
2 The officer prices it
Against the floor. Below the floor needs a second signature.
Case owner
3 The offer goes to the customer
A wait, with a validity timer.
Customer
4 Accepted, then paid
In full, or on an agreed installment plan.
Customer
5 Paid in full closes the case
The balance clears and the case closes.
Case owner
6 Not paid returns it
Back to the route decision for another route.
Case owner
How the case can end
Settled in full and the case closes
Not paid and the case returns to the route decision
In the routing rules
Steps | 15
Rules | 27
Branch points | 7
Exception events | 4

6
The customer will hand over the asset instead of paying. What happens?
1 The route decision approves deed in lieu
Mortgage takes deed in lieu, hire purchase takes voluntary surrender.
Workbench
2 The asset is valued and checked
Valuation and a legal check on title and encumbrance.
Valuer, Legal
3 Offer and consent from the customer
The customer agrees to transfer. A wait, with a timer.
Customer
4 Signed, then transferred
Registered at the Land Office, or the vehicle handed over.
Land Office
5 The asset comes onto the books
And the case moves to disposal.
NPA and asset manager
6 Declined returns it
Back to the route decision.
Case owner
How the case can end
The asset transfers and the case moves to disposal
The customer declines and the case returns to the route decision
In the routing rules
Steps | 20
Rules | 37
Branch points | 12
Exception events | 3

7
A guarantor or an insurer covers part or all of it. What happens?
1 A guarantee is identified on the case
TCG cover, credit life, or a personal guarantee.
Workbench
2 The claim is prepared
Against that guarantor's own rules and deadlines.
Guarantee officer
3 Filed with TCG or the insurer
Inside the claim window, which is deadline driven.
TCG, insurer
4 Paid, and subrogation recorded
The balance reduces by the amount paid.
Guarantee officer
5 A shortfall goes back
Whatever is left returns to the route decision.
Case owner
How the case can end
The guarantee clears the balance and the case closes
Part paid, and the shortfall returns to the route decision
Declined, and the case returns to the route decision
In the routing rules
Steps | 17
Rules | 32
Branch points | 12
Exception events | 6

8
There is no engagement, or the amount justifies court. What happens?
1 Notices go out by rule
Demand and recall notices from Legal templates.
Workbench
2 The notice period runs
From proof of delivery, not from the print date.
Customer
3 The pack is assembled
By the legal document agent, against the defect list.
Workbench
4 The officer verifies and approves filing
First time right is the measure that matters here.
Litigation officer
5 A panel firm is instructed
Selected on the scorecard, with the conflict check run.
Panel law firm
6 Filed, then managed to judgment
Court state and hearing dates reported back to the case.
Court
7 Judgment, then enforcement
Or a coded deferral with its reason.
Enforcement owner
How the case can end
Judgment and enforcement convert to cash
A coded deferral, with a reason and a review date
The debt is written off after enforcement is exhausted
In the routing rules
Steps | 38
Rules | 79
Branch points | 27
Exception events | 10

9
The bank holds the asset. How is it turned into cash?
1 The asset comes onto the books
From a deed in lieu, a surrender, or an enforcement seizure.
NPA and asset manager
2 Valued and held
With holding cost, insurance and maintenance tracked against it.
NPA and asset manager
3 The disposal route is approved
One of five routes, approved inside the floor.
Sale officer
4 Listed and run down the ladder
The LED ladder steps at 100, 90, 80 and 70 percent of official value.
Auction vendor
5 Sold, and the proceeds posted
Price achieved recorded against the model and the floor.
Sale officer
6 Any shortfall goes back
To the route decision, usually toward write off.
Case owner
How the case can end
The asset sells and the proceeds are posted
The asset transfers to RAMC
A shortfall returns to the route decision
In the routing rules
Steps | 40
Rules | 72
Branch points | 20
Exception events | 7

10
The account is worth more sold than worked. What happens?
1 Accounts are selected into a lot
By the lot agent, against the sale policy and the 54 percent cap.
Debt sale officer
2 A reserve is set from the model
And approved by the Head of Asset Liquidity.
Head of Asset Liquidity
3 Buyers qualify and view the data room
KYC and license checks first, then access.
Debt buyer
4 Bids come in and the lot is awarded
To the highest qualifying bid above the reserve.
Debt sale officer
5 Data transfers, remittance confirmed
The buyer confirms receipt of the file and the money arrives.
Debt buyer
6 The accounts close as sold
Every open action on them stops.
Debt sale officer
How the case can end
The lot is awarded and the accounts close as sold
No qualifying bid, and the accounts return to the case list
In the routing rules
Steps | 29
Rules | 41
Branch points | 12
Exception events | 7

11
Nothing is left to recover economically. What happens?
1 The monthly scan proposes a population
On both tracks, with the provision carried on each account.
Write-off team
2 The pack goes to the committee
With the provision position and the recovery history.
Write-off team
3 Approved inside the delegation
Anything outside it goes up a level.
Write-off committee
4 Posted, provision released
And completeness published.
Credit Administration
5 Recovery continues after charge-off
By agency placement, or by a post charge-off sale.
Collection agency
6 Recovered or sold, then closed
Whatever comes in is matched back to the written off account.
Credit Administration
How the case can end
Posted and closed
Recovered after charge-off
Sold after charge-off
In the routing rules
Steps | 27
Rules | 51
Branch points | 14
Exception events | 9

12
Something happened that stops the normal route. What happens?
1 A deviation is flagged
X1 to X7: complaint, hardship, death, fraud, bankruptcy, no contact, collateral.
Workbench
2 The stage clock pauses
The prescription clock keeps running.
Workbench
3 It routes to the named owner
Complaint officer, specialist, fraud team or Legal.
Deviation owner
4 Resolved, and the case resumes
In the state it paused in, with the clock restarted.
Case owner
5 Or the outcome changes the route
Back to the route decision, with the segment recomputed.
Case owner
How the case can end
The deviation clears and the case resumes where it paused
The outcome moves the case to a different route
Insurance settles the debt and the case ends
In the routing rules
Steps | 9
Rules | 22
Branch points | 2
Exception events | 0

secs.h: Slide 13. Rules that apply on every route
secs.t:
13
Something happens that is true whatever route the case is on. What happens?
1 An event arrives
A payment, a death, a complaint, a partner failure, a system outage, a sold lot.
Workbench
2 The universal rules fire first
They outrank the route's own rules, so a cure or a hold always wins.
Workbench
3 One of four things happens
The case pauses, is reallocated, returns to the route decision, or closes.
Workbench
4 Paused cases resume
In the state they paused in, with the timers recomputed.
Case owner
5 Or the segment is recomputed
And the gates re-run, which may change the route.
Workbench
How the case can end
The case returns to the state it was in
The case moves to the route decision
The case closes
The case is canceled or merged
In the routing rules
Steps | 20
Rules | 50
Branch points | 2
Exception events | 2

Approval levels
The six levels of chapter 2 and the five of chapter 3.
Chapter | Level | Approver | How the approval is recorded
Chapter 2 | 1 | Board of Directors | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 2 | 2 | Executive Committee | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 2 | 3 | Problem Asset Resolution Committee | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 2 | 4 | Head of Recovery, function level | Approves in the Workbench
Chapter 2 | 5 | Recovery executive, division level | Approves in the Workbench
Chapter 2 | 6 | Recovery executive, department level | Approves in the Workbench
Chapter 3 | 1 | Board of Directors | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 3 | 2 | Executive Committee | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 3 | 3 | Management Committee | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 3 | 4 | Problem Asset Resolution Committee | Committee resolution recorded in the decision log
Chapter 3 | 5 | Head of Recovery, function level, or Recovery executive, division level | Approves in the Workbench

How the matrix is applied
Rules the Workbench applies when it routes an approval.
 | Rule
1 | The limit is set on the borrower's principal outstanding, or on fair market value for assets held for sale
2 | A limit that depends on collateral value needs a fair market value appraisal by an independent valuer within the last year
3 | Where a level has two rows, the approval is within limit if either row is met
4 | A second delay of legal action or of an auction goes one level up
5 | New credit to a problem loan takes the higher of the restructuring authority and the credit authority in the credit approval regulation
6 | A write-off for a director, senior executive, major shareholder or related party goes to the Board
7 | Hire purchase, auto and unsecured loans follow chapter 8 of the credit approval regulation รบ.-กส.450032 as amended by กกค.690085. Those limits load when supplied (DL18)
8 | A decision that no limit covers goes to the next level up, and an incident records the missing limit
9 | A decision keeps the matrix version it was approved under
10 | A person may not approve a decision they proposed or prepared
11 | Each limit is a row in the delegation limit table with a version, valid from and valid to dates and the approver of the change. A change is a data load approved by Risk

What the bank still provides
The matrix is loaded with the regulation's levels and limits now. Names and substitutes are added when the matrix is signed.
Item | From | Decision
Holder of each level by name and position | Risk with the product heads | DL18
Substitute for each holder when absent | Risk with the product heads | DL18
Chapter 8 limits for hire purchase and unsecured loans | Risk | DL18
Signature of the matrix | Risk with the product heads | DL18

Key
What each term means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Term | Principal | The borrower's principal outstanding, the base the regulation uses for chapter 2 limits
Term | Fair market value | The value set by an independent valuer within the last year
Term | Maximum loss | The most the bank may lose on principal, interest recorded as income and other assets under the approval
Value | No limit | The level may approve any amount
Standard | NIST RBAC | The approve right in the permission matrix; the limit in this matrix

docs.name: Recovery Workbench Deviation and Exception Catalog v3

secs.t:
Deviations X1 to X7
Seven deviations. Each pauses the stage clock and never the prescription clock, goes to a named handler, and returns the case or re-routes it.
Code | Deviation | What it is | What raises it | What it suspends | What keeps running | Handler | Assigned by | How the case returns | Service level | Contact stop
X1 | Dispute or complaint | A complaint is logged, or the customer disputes the balance or the security | R-UNI-04 complaint raised; R-UNI-09 debt disputed; screening agent at case entry; any officer | The stage clock; contact with the customer; recovery action on the disputed amount | The prescription clock and every legal period clock | Complaint officer | R-DEV-02 | The same decision resumes when the complaint is resolved (R-DEV-09, R-DEV-18) | 10 working days, then escalation (R-DEV-20) | Yes
X2 | Vulnerable customer or hardship | Hardship or vulnerability is recorded | R-UNI-06 vulnerability identified; screening agent; any officer | The stage clock; collection contact outside the vulnerable customer treatment rules | The prescription clock | Hardship and vulnerability specialist | R-DEV-03 | Routed to the restructure assessment (R-DEV-10), then the route decision (R-DEV-19) | 10 working days, then escalation (R-DEV-20) | Yes, except treatment contact
X3 | Deceased customer | A death is confirmed from the registry or a document | R-UNI-05 customer deceased; document intake | All contact with the customer; every route action | The prescription clock; the estate claim deadline | Hardship and vulnerability specialist, with Legal for the estate claim | R-DEV-03 | Closed if insurance clears the balance (R-DEV-11); otherwise back to the route decision against the estate (R-DEV-12) | 10 working days, then escalation (R-DEV-20) | Yes
X4 | Fraud | Aric or an officer flags fraud | R-UNI-08 fraud flagged; Aric referral | The case and every route action | The prescription clock | Fraud investigator | R-DEV-04 | Fraud confirmed: to write-off with recovery under the fraud case (R-DEV-13). Not confirmed: back to the route decision (R-DEV-14) | 10 working days, then escalation (R-DEV-20) | Yes
X5 | Bankruptcy or external seizure | A bankruptcy filing or a seizure by another creditor is notified | R-UNI-07 bankruptcy notified | Enforcement and every collection action against the debtor | The prescription clock; the claim deadline with the official receiver or the Legal Execution Department | Legal counsel | R-DEV-05 | Claim filed, then litigation and write-off after the receiver reports (R-DEV-15) | The filing deadline | Yes
X6 | Lost contact | No contact point reaches the customer | Screening agent; failed contact attempts; returned notices | The stage clock | The prescription clock; statutory notices to the last known address | Case owner, with the agent tracing within policy | R-DEV-06 | Contact restored: back to the paused state (R-DEV-16, R-UNI-12). Trace exhausted: escalation or the route decision (R-DEV-17) | 30 days for the trace (R-DEV-17) | No
X7 | Collateral event | The collateral is damaged, destroyed, seized or lost | Screening agent; insurer or valuer report; any officer | The stage clock; disposal of the collateral | The prescription clock; the insurance claim deadline | Case owner, with the agent within policy; a person approves an insurance claim | R-DEV-06 | The same decision resumes (R-DEV-09, R-DEV-18) | 10 working days, then escalation (R-DEV-20) | No

How a deviation is raised
The universal rules that raise a deviation from any active state, and the rule that pauses the case.
Rule | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Timer
R-DEV-01 | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | deviation_code in (X1..X7) | Pause the stage clock, keep the prescription clock running, route to the named owner | DEV_FLAGGED | Workbench | same day
R-UNI-04 | COMPLAINT_RAISED | a complaint is logged against the case | Raise X1, pause the stage clock, apply the contact stop | HELD_DEVIATION | Complaint officer | same day
R-UNI-05 | CUSTOMER_DECEASED | a death is confirmed from the registry or a document | Raise X3, stop all contact, hold the case for the specialist and Legal | HELD_DEVIATION | Specialist, Legal | same day
R-UNI-06 | VULNERABILITY_IDENTIFIED | hardship or vulnerability is recorded | Raise X2, apply the vulnerable customer treatment rules | HELD_DEVIATION | Specialist | same day
R-UNI-07 | BANKRUPTCY_NOTIFIED | a filing or an external seizure is notified | Raise X5, stop enforcement, start the claim deadline clock | HELD_DEVIATION | Legal | deadline driven
R-UNI-08 | FRAUD_FLAGGED | Aric or an officer flags fraud | Raise X4, hold the case, refer to the fraud team | HELD_DEVIATION | Fraud team | same day
R-UNI-09 | DEBT_DISPUTED | the customer disputes the balance or the security | Raise X1, pause recovery action on the disputed amount | HELD_DEVIATION | Complaint officer | same day

How a deviation is handled and cleared
22 rules in the deviation route set.
Rule | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Timer
R-DEV-01 | ANY_STATE | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | deviation_code in (X1..X7) | Pause the stage clock, keep the prescription clock running, route to the named owner | DEV_FLAGGED | Workbench | same day
R-DEV-02 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X1 | Assign to the complaint officer | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Complaint officer | None
R-DEV-03 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X2,X3) | Assign to the specialist; Legal joins X3 for the estate claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Specialist, Legal | None
R-DEV-04 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X4 | Assign to the fraud team and refer to Aric | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Fraud team | None
R-DEV-05 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X5 | Assign to Legal; file with the official receiver or the LED before the deadline | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Legal | deadline driven
R-DEV-06 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X6,X7) | Agent handles within policy; a person approves an insurance claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Agent, case owner | None
R-DEV-07 | DEV_FLAGGED | FLAG_REJECTED | owner marks the flag as not a deviation | Clear the flag, record the reason, resume the clock | DEV_REJECTED | Workbench | None
R-DEV-08 | DEV_REJECTED | CLOCK_RESUMED | Any | Return the case to the state it paused in | RESUMED | Previous owner | None
R-DEV-09 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | deviation_code in (X1,X7) | Record the outcome; the same decision resumes | DEV_RESOLVED | Case owner | None
R-DEV-10 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | deviation_code = X2 | Route to the restructure assessment | DEV_REROUTE | Restructuring officer | None
R-DEV-11 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | INSURANCE_SETTLED | deviation_code = X3 and insurance clears the balance | Close the case | CASE_ENDED | Workbench | None
R-DEV-12 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | ESTATE_CONFIRMED | deviation_code = X3 and insurance does not clear | Return to the route decision against the estate | DEV_REROUTE | Case owner | None
R-DEV-13 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | FRAUD_CONFIRMED | deviation_code = X4 and fraud confirmed | Route to write-off; recovery continues under the fraud case | DEV_REROUTE | Write-off team | None
R-DEV-14 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | FRAUD_NOT_CONFIRMED | deviation_code = X4 and fraud not confirmed | Return to the collections decision | DEV_REROUTE | Case owner | None
R-DEV-15 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | BANKRUPTCY_FILED | deviation_code = X5 | Route to litigation, then to write-off after the receiver reports | DEV_REROUTE | Legal, litigation officer | None
R-DEV-16 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | CONTACT_RESTORED | deviation_code = X6 and a contact point is verified | Close X6 and return to the paused state | DEV_RESOLVED | Case owner | None
R-DEV-17 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | CONTACT_NOT_FOUND | deviation_code = X6 and skip trace exhausted | Route to escalation or to the route decision | DEV_REROUTE | Case owner | 30 days
R-DEV-18 | DEV_RESOLVED | CLOCK_RESUMED | Any | Resume the stage clock and return the case | RESUMED | Previous owner | None
R-DEV-19 | DEV_REROUTE | ROUTE_REOPENED | Any | Recompute the segment and re-run the hard gates | ROUTE_D6 | Case owner | None
R-DEV-20 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | SLA_BREACHED | time in DEV_WITH_OWNER exceeds the deviation service level | Escalate to the team manager and report the breach | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Team manager | 10 working days
R-DEV-21 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code is not one of X1 to X7, or no owner is set for the code | Assign to the case owner's team manager and log the unmapped code | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Team manager | same day
R-DEV-22 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | otherwise, the outcome does not name a next step | Return the case to the route decision and record that the outcome was not mapped | DEV_REROUTE | Case owner | 2 working days

Holds that are not deviations
Events that stop part or all of the normal route without raising X1 to X7.
Rule | Event | Condition | Action | Owner | Timer

Key
What each term means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Term | Deviation | An event that stops the normal route: X1 to X7. The case goes to a named handler
Term | Exception event | A step in a route set reached when something goes wrong in that route, such as a rejected filing or a missed deadline
Term | Stage clock | Time in the current state. Paused while a deviation is open
Term | Prescription clock | Time to the earliest date a legal claim expires. Never paused
Term | Contact stop | No one contacts the customer while it is in force. Statutory notices still go
Standard | CMMN 1.1 | A deviation is an event listener that pauses the stage and starts the handling tasks

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Partner operating model

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench partner operating model
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Henka word rules

Partner | How many | Owner | How work is placed
Collection agencies | 73 | Partner and agency manager | Placement share set by measured return on a matched population
Law firms | 11 to 12 | Head of Litigation | By rule from the panel scorecard (R-LIT-23)
Valuers | Panel | Head of NPA | Appraisal orders through SVAF by rotation and region
Vehicle auction vendors | 4 | Head of Auto Recovery | By distance and the scorecard
Property brokers | Panel | Head of NPA | Fixed-term instruction on the portal
Debt buyers and AMCs | 35 | Head of Asset Liquidity | Lots offered to eligible buyers; award by price against the reserve
RAMC | 1 | Head of Asset Liquidity | Secured pools transferred on agreed terms

Step | What happens | Who
Select | Panel criteria, due diligence, security review, conduct check | Partner and agency manager with Procurement
Contract | Fees, service levels, data protection terms, audit rights, exit terms | Partner and agency manager with Legal
Place | Work placed by rule; shares and caps as reference data | Rules component
Instruct | Instruction with documents and due date through the partner portal | Case owner; Workbench
Track | Partner results, documents and service level clocks | Workbench; partner
Pay | Invoice against completed instructions; fee checked against the schedule | Partner and agency manager; Finance
Measure | Monthly scorecard; quarterly review | Partner and agency manager
Exit | Recall open work, secure documents and cash, end access (R-UNI-26, R-UNI-28) | Partner and agency manager

Partner | Paid by | Measured on
Collection agencies | Fee on cash collected | Cash collected, cost per baht, conduct breaches, complaints
Law firms | Fee schedule per legal step | Time to file, time to judgment, recovery, court fees recovered
Valuers | Fee per appraisal | Turnaround, value against the sale price, outlier rate
Vehicle auction vendors | Commission on sale | Sell rate, price against the model, days to sell
Property brokers | Commission on sale | Days to sell, price against the floor
Debt buyers and AMCs | Purchase price | Price against the reserve, put-backs, complaints after transfer
RAMC | Transfer price from the governed template | Transfer time, pool performance

Scorecards are monthly; a partner below the panel threshold for two months receives fewer placements, and a conduct breach suspends placement (R-UNI-29).

Partners reach the partner portal through the external gateway once external access is approved (DL03).

Each partner user has a separate identity with multi-factor authentication and sees only the firm's work.

Until then partners use their current channels and bank staff record results.

Every partner upload is scanned for malware before it reaches the document hub.
Partners receive only the data their instruction needs, under a contract with data protection terms. Debt buyers receive a masked tape before award (CTL-31).

Collection agencies | E6
Law firms | E5
Valuers | E4
Vehicle auction vendors | E4

Recovery Workbench process architecture: L1 processes
19 L1 processes in four layers. Counts are calculated from the L2 and L3 tabs. Modes are defined on the Key tab.
L1 | Layer | L1 process | Definition | Decision | Runs on | L2 | L3 | A | A+H | H | M | P | A or A+H
01 | Core | Detect and act on signals | Watch every performing and early-arrears account and decide whether, when and how to act before or at the first missed payment. | D1 | EFS
02 | Core | Contact the customer | Reach the customer through the right channel at the right time, within contact limits and customer standards, and record the outcome. | D2 | EFS
03 | Core | Manage promises | Record each promise to pay, track it to the payment and move the case on when the promise is broken. | D3 | EFS
04 | Core | Escalate | Raise the intensity of collection by senior phone contact, field visits or outside agencies when lighter treatment has failed. | D4 | EFS
05 | Core | Restructure | Assess affordability, offer and book a restructure plan, and monitor it until the customer pays as agreed or the plan fails. | D5 | EFS and ACE, then the Workbench after TDR go-live
06 | Core | Take over and own the case | Take the case from collections at 90 days past due, with its history, and give it one owner and a running set of deadlines. | D6 entry | Recovery Workbench
07 | Core | Route, settle and claim | Value the case, decide the route, and resolve it with the customer by settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor pursuit. | D6 | Recovery Workbench
08 | Core | Litigate and enforce | Take the case through notices, filing, judgment and enforcement until the debt is paid, settled or proven unrecoverable. | D7 | Recovery Workbench
09 | Core | Dispose assets and sell debt | Take assets onto the books, hold them, and turn them into cash by auction or other routes, or sell the debt. | D8 | Recovery Workbench
10 | Core | Write off and recover after charge-off | Write off the balance that cannot be recovered, post it, and keep recovering after charge-off until the case closes. | D9 | Recovery Workbench
11 | Support | Handle customer care and deviations | Answer customer contacts and handle the seven deviations that interrupt a decision, then return the case to the right decision. | X1 to X7 | EFS and Recovery Workbench
12 | Support | Manage partners | Select, instruct, measure, pay and govern the partners who work cases for the bank, and end the contract when needed. | All | Recovery Workbench and partner portals
13 | Support | Manage documents and correspondence | Read and file inbound documents, send letters and notices with proof of delivery, and keep documents and originals under control. | All | Recovery Workbench document hub
14 | Manage | Set strategy, policy and decision rules | Set the segments, treatment policy, decision rules, limits, fees and the reference data every decision reads. | All | Recovery Workbench reference data
15 | Manage | Manage performance, data and AI | Report results, test strategies, monitor agents and models, keep data correct and feed what is learned back to policy. | All | Recovery Workbench, data lake, Power BI
16 | Manage | Manage risk, control and compliance | Run quality assurance, conduct control, model and agent risk, audit response, access control, incidents and data subject rights. | All | Recovery Workbench
17 | Across all | Run the decision center | Route every recommendation to the person with the authority to decide it, record one log entry per decision, and feed results back. | D1 to D9 | Recovery Workbench decision service
18 | Manage | Plan capacity and allocate work | Forecast inflow, plan staff and partner capacity, and build and allocate the work lists that collectors and partners work from. | D2, D4 | Capacity model, dialer, field application, partner portal
19 | Support | Manage payments and reconciliation | Receive payments from every channel, apply them to the right account and case, and reconcile cash to the case and the core. | D3, D5, D6 | Core banking, EFS, Recovery Workbench
 | Total

Numbering | L2 | A sub-process inside one L1, numbered L1.n, for example 7.3.
Numbering | L3 | A process inside one L2, numbered with the L1 as two digits, for example 07.3.1. The items under an L2 are always called L3 processes.
Layer | Core | The case moves through these processes in order. 01 to 05 run on EFS before day 90; 06 to 10 run on the Workbench.
Layer | Support | Run across every core process when they are needed.
Layer | Manage | Set the rules every process runs by, and read the results.
Layer | Across all | Runs at every decision point in every core process.
Mode | A Automated | A rule, engine or agent completes the step. No person is involved; the result is in the log.
Mode | A+H AI assisted | An agent or engine prepares, recommends or drafts. A person decides, approves or completes.
Mode | H Human | A bank employee carries out the step. The Workbench prepares the task and records the result.
Mode | M Manual | A physical or legal act done outside any system, such as a title transfer. The Workbench records that it happened.
Mode | P Partner | A partner carries out the step: an agency, law firm, valuer, auction house, broker or court officer.
Decision pattern | Information | Gather and check the facts the decision needs.
Decision pattern | Decide | Apply a rule, a model or an agent to choose an option.
Decision pattern | Outcome | Make the choice final, or route it to the person with the authority to approve it.
Decision pattern | Act | Carry out the choice in the Workbench, another system or through a partner.
Decision pattern | Log | Record the decision, the action and the result once, in the decision log.
Decision | D1 to D9 | The nine decisions a case passes through: act on the signal, reach the customer, promise kept, escalate, offer a restructure, which route, next legal step, how to dispose, write off or pursue.
Decision | X1 to X7 | The seven deviations that interrupt a decision: dispute or complaint, vulnerable customer or hardship, deceased customer, fraud, bankruptcy or external seizure, lost contact, collateral event.
Systems | RW | The Recovery Workbench.
Systems | Portal | The partner portal.

L1 | Process | What it covers | Decision | L2 | L3
01 | Detect and act on signals | Watch every performing and early-arrears account and decide whether, when and how to act before or at the first missed payment. | D1 | 2 | 6
02 | Contact the customer | Reach the customer through the right channel at the right time, within contact limits and customer standards, and record the outcome. | D2 | 6 | 15
03 | Manage promises | Record each promise to pay, track it to the payment and move the case on when the promise is broken. | D3 | 3 | 6
04 | Escalate | Raise the intensity of collection by senior phone contact, field visits or outside agencies when lighter treatment has failed. | D4 | 4 | 10
05 | Restructure | Assess affordability, offer and book a restructure plan, and monitor it until the customer pays as agreed or the plan fails. | D5 | 5 | 15
06 | Take over and own the case | Take the case from collections at 90 days past due, with its history, and give it one owner and a running set of deadlines. | D6 entry | 1 | 3
07 | Route, settle and claim | Value the case, decide the route, and resolve it with the customer by settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor pursuit. | D6 | 5 | 17
08 | Litigate and enforce | Take the case through notices, filing, judgment and enforcement until the debt is paid, settled or proven unrecoverable. | D7 | 4 | 16
09 | Dispose assets and sell debt | Take assets onto the books, hold them, and turn them into cash by auction or other routes, or sell the debt. | D8 | 7 | 28
10 | Write off and recover after charge-off | Write off the balance that cannot be recovered, post it, and keep recovering after charge-off until the case closes. | D9 | 3 | 9

Product heads
Mortgage, Hire Purchase, SSME
Own cures, realized recovery and cost to collect for their product. Approve above set limits.
Shared operations
Collections and recovery for all products
Carry out the work: case ownership, restructuring, legal, NPA, debt sale, write-off and partner management. Approve within set limits.
Center of excellence
Strategy, analytics, testing, QA, rules
Set strategy, rules and limits as data. Propose rule and agent changes to the strategy and model committee.
Platform
EFS, ACE and the Workbench, COLLINS, agents, data
Run the systems and data the work depends on. Approve system and agent releases.

One owner from day 90 to close | A case owner holds the case through every route, with specialists working tasks on it
Limits held as data | Who may approve what is the delegation of authority table, checked by the Workbench

secs.h: Slide 10. Spans and layers in the target model
secs.t:
10
Design rule | What it means
Teams are sized from caseload | A team's size is the caseload cap per role times the cases in its queues. The caps are DL23
Leaders lead people | A team manager coaches, rebalances queues and handles escalations. Allocation is done by rules
Limits belong to roles, not layers | An officer approves within the limit set for the role. Higher amounts go to the approval level, not up the line
Specialists work tasks on the case | Restructuring, legal, NPA and debt sale officers work their tasks on the owner's case. The case does not move between teams
One queue per team and role | Each queue belongs to one team and one role, with an overflow queue and a service level per state (DL22)
Layers from the head of recovery | Function head, unit head, team manager, officer: four layers for every recovery team, proposed

11
Area | Today | Target
Ownership | The case moves between units, with hand-overs by email and file | One owner from day 90 to close; specialists work tasks on the case
Allocation | Managers allocate from spreadsheets | Rules allocate; managers rebalance and handle exceptions
Preparing decisions | Officers gather data from several systems and write account plans | The Workbench gathers the facts, the expected return by route and a recommendation
Approvals | By email and paper, with limits checked by hand | Routed to the approval level, limit checked by the Workbench, logged once
Documents | Prepared, checked and couriered by document services | Generated, read and indexed by the document hub; people review the exceptions
Appraisals | Each appraisal checked by an officer | Rule check, the agent flags outliers, an officer accepts
Partners | Managed by email and spreadsheet | Instructions, results and fees in the partner portal, scored each month
Measures | Assembled by hand for each report | Read from the decision log per decision

Separation of duty
Role pairs one person may not hold. Checked by the role owner at each grant and by the Workbench at each sign-in. A person may not approve a decision they proposed or prepared.
Role | May not also hold | Reason
Security administrator | Any business role | The person who maps groups to roles could grant themselves business access
Platform administrator | Any business role | Technical access combined with business access passes around scope and masking
Access administrator position | Role owner for the same roles | One person would approve and carry out the same grant
Reference data administrator | Risk and model risk officer | Loading a delegation or rule version and approving it are separate steps
Center of excellence analyst | Risk and model risk officer | Writing a rule and approving it are separate steps
Restructuring officer | Credit approval committee member | Proposing a restructure and approving it are separate steps
Write-off team member | Write-off committee member | Proposing a write-off and approving it are separate steps
Internal audit | Any other role | Audit reads and changes nothing

Request, grant, review and removal
Who does what at each step. The review interval, the leaver response time and the break-glass window are DL38.
Event | Step | Who | Action | Where
Joiner | 1 | Line manager | Raises a request naming the person, the role and the reason | Bank IAM
Joiner | 2 | Role owner | Approves or rejects, after checking the separation of duty table | Bank IAM
Joiner | 3 | Access administrator | Adds the person to the Entra ID group for the role in each environment requested | Bank IAM to Entra ID
Joiner | 4 | The person | Signs in with multi-factor authentication | Workbench
Joiner | 5 | Workbench | Resolves the roles, scope and masking and writes the session to the access log | Workbench
Mover | 1 | Line manager | One request removes the previous roles and adds the new ones in the same change | Bank IAM
Mover | 2 | Role owners | The owners of the old and the new roles approve. A mover never holds both sets | Bank IAM
Leaver | 1 | Line manager or HR leaver record | Starts removal from every Workbench group | Bank IAM
Leaver | 2 | Workbench | Ends the open session at the next request and refuses a new one | Workbench
Review | 1 | Role owner | Recertifies every holder of the role at each review. A holder not recertified is removed | Bank IAM
Review | 2 | Application owner | Signs the review result | Bank IAM
Break-glass | 1 | Platform administrator | Requests access beyond the role, naming the open incident, the area, the scope and the reason | Bank IAM
Break-glass | 2 | Security administrator | Approves. A request with no open incident is refused | Bank IAM
Break-glass | 3 | Workbench | Marks every action under break-glass in the access log. The grant ends when its window ends | Workbench
Break-glass | 4 | Security administrator | Reviews the use inside the review window. An unreviewed use goes to the head of SCB IT security and to Compliance | Bank IAM

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Business requirements, Epic 1

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench business requirements, Epic 1
Version | 4
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Release | 30 November 2026
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, until the SCB X requirement template is adopted (DL13)
Change | Version 4 applies D-RCV-35 and ADR-010, which supersedes ADR-005. Section 3.1 states the four-tier read model, the 30 views, the dictionary, reconciliation and freshness position; section 3.2 is outbound only. Section 4 marks the removed requirements and re-words the data requirements, section 7 records DL43, and the requirement and role counts follow. RWB-E1-069 and RWB-ACE-001 are added; removed requirements keep their keys. Other sections are unchanged.

Epic 1, Foundation 1, releases on 30 November 2026.

One case list for every account at 90 days past due or more, reconciled to the core bank. Documents found by case. The decision log store. A read-only case record view. Allocation, assignment and transfer by rule, with timers and prescription dates, and no workflow screens.

Measure | Value
Requirements at development detail | 61
Must | 51
Program requirements this epic meets | 75

Who | Requirements that serve them
A product owner | 8
A case owner | 8
A litigation officer | 8
A team manager | 7
A developer | 6
A document hub owner | 6
An AI product owner | 5
A data product owner | 4
A center of excellence analyst | 2
The Tribe lead | 1
The case workflow module | 1
A head of recovery | 1
A security reviewer | 1
An operations engineer | 1
A business analyst | 1
The ACE team lead | 1
Each requirement is one backlog story. The requirement states what the Workbench does, the benefit states what changes for the user, and the scenarios are the acceptance criteria in the story.

P1 is the read-only data position of the recovery module. ACE ingests every source and holds it; the Workbench reads it through the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views and holds only Workbench-owned data: the case, its decisions, reference data and the extension tables (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). Links to ACE records use business keys, with no foreign key into ACE.

The read model has four tiers. Tier 1 is 22 ACE tables that exist today; the recovery data in them is read through 16 Section A views, and the Workbench never alters them. Tier 2 is 14 ACE tables and 12 columns the ACE team adds under RWB-ACE-001 for 80 source fields; the new tables are read through 14 Section B views and the new columns extend v_ace_account, v_ace_customer and v_ace_efs_action. Tier 3 is 4 Workbench extension tables keyed by ACE business keys. Tier 4 is 88 retained Workbench tables. The recovery schema is 92 tables; with the 30 views the dictionary holds 122 sys_objects and 1,366 sys_fields.

P1 delivers the recovery tables, the extension tables, the two view migrations, the data dictionary, the daily reconciliation of the case list to v_ace_account (REC-01 to REC-05) and the freshness stamp read from the ACE batch record (ace_batch_run through v_ace_batch_status). Section A ships with RWB-E1-069; Section B waits on the ACE additions in RWB-ACE-001 (DL43). The 20 copy, load and tracker tables leave the recovery schema. Source content is read through the views, Workbench-only facts sit in the extension tables, and the trackers are retired through the Cutover plan. A requirement for an inbound load, a data quality check on load or a tracker is removed. It keeps its key and names its later home.

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-001 | Recovery tables for the 14 data products | The recovery schema in the ACE database for the 14 data products: 92 tables, being 88 retained Workbench tables and 4 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys, with a data dictionary and one system of record, read path and owner per product. Source data is read through the 30 ACE views and is never copied. | A data product owner | Every product has one source and one read path | Must | 3
RWB-E1-002 | Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue | One case list with case ID, account, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, balance and days past due for every 90 days past due or more account, read from the ACE account view (v_ace_account) each day after the ACE batch completes, and available in Power BI | A team manager | Every team works from one list | Must | 3
RWB-E1-003 | ALS daily extract load | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1). ACE ingests ALS, and the Workbench reads v_ace_account and v_ace_payment. Later home: ACE ingestion | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-004 | EFS extract load | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1). ACE ingests EFS, and the Workbench reads v_ace_efs_action and v_ace_efs_assignment. Later home: ACE ingestion | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-005 | Excel and SharePoint inventory | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). Excel and SharePoint trackers leave system scope. Later home: the Cutover plan | A program manager | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-006 | Data quality rules v1 | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1). Data quality checks on source data run in ACE ingestion. The daily gate moves into RWB-E1-015. Later home: ACE ingestion checks | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-009 | CCMS and SVAF loads | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1). ACE ingests CCMS and SVAF through RWB-ACE-001, and the Workbench reads v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail and v_ace_valuation. Later home: ACE ingestion | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-010 | Excel and SharePoint loads | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). No tracker is loaded. Later home: the Cutover plan | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-011 | Reconciliation and data quality report | A daily reconciliation of the case list to the ACE account view (v_ace_account), with the variance and the results of reconciliation rules REC-01 to REC-05 in one Power BI report | A team manager | Everyone sees whether today's list can be trusted | Must | 2
RWB-E1-012 | Retire local copies | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). Each team retires its tracker through the Cutover plan. Later home: the Cutover plan | A program manager | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-014 | Decision log copy to the data lake | The decision log copied to the data lake each night and a retention rule per data product and table | A center of excellence analyst | Reporting reads the log without touching the live log and nothing is kept longer than its rule | Should | 2
RWB-E1-015 | Freshness stamp per data product | Every data product row to carry the business date and load time of its ACE batch, taken from the ACE batch record (ace_batch_run, read through v_ace_batch_status), exposed to every consumer and shown on the case record view. The case list waits for a completed ACE batch and shows the last completed business date | A data product owner | Every decision input states how old it is and stale facts are visible | Must | 3
RWB-E1-016 | Access control per data product and catalog entries | Read access to each data product granted by role through the read-only views, PDPA fields tagged, every read logged, and a catalog entry per product with owner, system of record (ACE, ingested from the named source), freshness and fields | A data product owner | Personal data is read only by the roles that need it and every product is findable | Must | 3
RWB-E1-017 | Retention and archive rule for the data store | A retention rule per data product and table, held as reference data, applied by a job that archives rows past their rule and logs the action | A data product owner | The store holds what the policy allows and nothing older | Should | 3
RWB-E1-064 | Data dictionary for the 14 data products | Every field in the 14 data products typed, sourced and owned. The dictionary covers the Workbench tables, the 4 extension tables and the 30 ACE views: 122 objects and 1,366 fields | A business analyst | A data contract can be agreed with the ACE team for every field the Workbench reads | Must | 3
RWB-E1-065 | Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data | A sandbox database holding the ACE schema, the ACE views and synthetic recovery data | A developer | I can build and test before the ACE additions and the real data are available | Must | 3
RWB-E1-066 | Interaction ledger store and writer | Every contact, letter, promise, payment and hand-over on the case written to one ledger when it is recorded | A case owner | The history of the case is never assembled after the fact | Must | 4
RWB-E1-067 | Every Workbench action into the interaction ledger | Every action the Workbench takes on my case written to the ledger when it is taken | A case owner | I can read the history without assembling it from four systems | Must | 3
RWB-E1-068 | Interaction ledger read interface | To read a case's ledger in one ordered sequence | A case owner | I can see what has happened to it before I decide anything | Must | 3
RWB-E1-069 | Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule | The 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views: 16 over ACE tables that exist today (Section A) and 14 over the ACE additions (Section B, when RWB-ACE-001 lands). The 4 extension tables. SELECT on the views for the recovery service identity and nothing else. A test that fails the build on a direct read of a public table, a write to ACE or a foreign key into ACE | A developer | Source data has one copy and one read path, and a wrong read fails the build | Must | -
RWB-ACE-001 | ACE DB additions for the Recovery Workbench | Not built by the Workbench. The ACE team adds 14 tables and 12 columns to the ACE database for the 80 source fields ACE does not hold, with the ACE batch record ace_batch_run, all filled by ACE ingestion. The Section B views and the features that need them stay behind their flags until it lands (DL43) | The ACE team lead | The recovery module reads one copy of source data and no recovery load is built | Must | 8

P2 is outbound only. It sends files and events and receives no source file: every inbound source lands in ACE through ACE ingestion and is read through the P1 views (D-RCV-35, U1; ADR-010).

P2 covers one adapter pattern for the WIN registered-mail notice file, the data lake and Power BI extract, the decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the data lake, the debt buyer tape and the GL write-off event. It uses the ACE logging path to the SOC, and the transport used by the partner portal and the document hub. It also covers feature flags and the run books for Workbench jobs. No inbound file feed, file-load adapter, inbound run record or inbound sign-off remains.

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-007 | Outbound integration adapters for files and events | One adapter pattern for every outbound file and event: the WIN registered-mail notice file, the data lake and Power BI extract, the decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the data lake, the debt buyer tape and the GL write-off event, plus the transport used by the partner portal and the document hub, with checks, logging, retry and an exception queue. SOC and audit events leave through the ACE logging path, and no inbound file load runs in the Workbench. | A developer | Every outbound channel follows one pattern and no inbound source file enters the Workbench | Must | 3
RWB-E1-047 | Feature flags for module release with a removal date | A feature flag service with flags defined as data (name, owner, environments, removal date) and read by every service at run time | A developer | A feature can be released dark and switched on without a deployment | Should | 3
RWB-E1-051 | Legacy feed jobs on ADF and Control-M | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1). No ADF or Control-M job carries recovery source data; ACE ingestion does. Later home: ACE ingestion | A data product owner | - | Removed | -
RWB-E1-056 | Run books and monitoring for every Epic 1 job | A run book for every Workbench scheduled job and service (purpose, schedule, owner, failure signs, restart steps, escalation) and monitoring for each. Source loads are ACE jobs and sit in the ACE run books | An operations engineer | Any Epic 1 job can be restarted by the operations team without the developer | Must | 3

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-018 | Case ID issuance and case record v1 | Every 90 days past due or more account on one recovery case with a case ID (RW-YYYY-NNNNNN) issued at creation and never reused, a stage, a status and linked accounts, created by rule when an account reaches 90 days past due and is not excluded | A product owner | Every team, letter and document refers to one ID | Must | 6
RWB-E1-019 | Roles, teams and queues as data | Roles, teams, queues, queue membership and capacity held as versioned reference data loaded from the Excel template | A product owner | The organization changes without a code release | Must | 3
RWB-E1-020 | Allocation and assignment engine v1 | Each new case placed in a queue and assigned to a person by the allocation and assignment rule tables | A team manager | Nobody allocates cases by hand | Must | 4
RWB-E1-021 | Transfer rules and engine v1 | Cases moved between queues and roles by the transfer rule table on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed or manual request with a reason | A team manager | Hand-offs run without email | Must | 5
RWB-E1-023 | Case record view v1, read only | One screen per case with case ID, accounts, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, contact history and documents, read from the data products | A case owner | I stop searching files | Must | 3
RWB-E1-028 | Service levels, timers, escalation and prescription dates | A service level per queue and status, a timer engine, warning and escalation to the next role by rule, and prescription dates from the legal periods table | A team manager | No case waits past its limit unseen | Must | 3
RWB-E1-029 | Rule load, validation and rollback | An Excel template for the five rule tables, validation on load (schema, overlaps, unreachable rows, missing default, 50 test cases), load with a version, rollback by one call and a change log | A product owner | A rule change goes from template to production without a code release | Must | 4
RWB-E1-030 | Daily rebalancing and queue measures | A daily job that moves unassigned and over-capacity cases by the assignment rules, with queue counts, ageing and service level breaches in Power BI | A team manager | Queues stay balanced and visible | Must | 3
RWB-E1-031 | Queue and owner on the case list with filters | The queue and owner columns on the case list with filters by queue, team and status and an export | A team manager | I see my queues without a new screen | Must | 2
RWB-E1-035 | Case record view v1.1 with documents and history timeline | A timeline on the case record view with contacts, documents, assignments, transfers and status changes in time order | A case owner | I see what happened to the case without asking | Should | 2
RWB-E1-042 | Central configuration service and parameter catalog | Every environment setting and business parameter read from one configuration service, listed in a parameter catalog with name, type, default, owner, environment and where it is used | A developer | No value is hard-coded and every parameter has an owner | Must | 3
RWB-E1-043 | Reference data service with versioned tables | Products, regions, exposure bands, roles, teams, queues, service levels, document types, templates, delegation of authority, legal periods and holidays held as versioned reference data with valid from, valid to, author and approver | A product owner | Business values change by a data release and not by code | Must | 3
RWB-E1-044 | Database migrations versioned with parameterized schema names | Every schema change applied by a versioned migration (Flyway or Liquibase), one migration per story, forward-only in PROD, with schema names taken from parameters | A developer | The database in every environment is the sum of known migrations and nothing else | Must | 3
RWB-E1-045 | Multi-product parameters for Mortgage, HP and SSME | Every product-specific value (entry rule, exclusion list, service levels, templates, exposure bands) keyed by product in the reference data | A product owner | A new product or a product change needs no code change | Must | 3
RWB-E1-048 | Rule change audit report | The parameter change and rule change checklists (request, impact, test cases, approver, load, verify, rollback plan) in the Engineering Standards and followed for every change | A product owner | A configuration change is as controlled as a code change | Should | 2

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-022 | Sign-on with SSO, MFA and the first roles | To sign in with Entra ID SSO and see only the screens my role allows, with roles case owner, team lead, admin and read only | A case owner | Access is controlled from day one | Must | 3
RWB-E1-037 | Role to permission matrix as data and PDPA field masking by role | The mapping of roles to screens, actions, data products and PDPA fields held as a versioned table, applied by every screen and API, with masking by role | A product owner | A change of rights is a data change and personal data shows only to roles that need it | Must | 3
RWB-E1-038 | Delegation of authority table as reference data | The delegation of authority (who may approve what, by decision, amount band, product and exposure) held as a versioned table that the approval router reads | A head of recovery | Approval limits change by a data load and every approval can be checked against the limit that applied | Must | 3
RWB-E1-039 | Access log into the decision log and break-glass admin | Every read of a case record and every export written to the decision log store, and a break-glass admin role granted for a limited time with approval and full logging | A security reviewer | Every access can be audited and emergency access is controlled | Must | 3

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-024 | Document store and index | Every scanned document stored against its case with type, date, source and extracted fields, in a Blob store with a write-once container for legal types, searchable by case ID, type and date | A litigation officer | Documents are found by case | Must | 3
RWB-E1-025 | Document types and fields agreed | The first six document types (demand letter, court notice, appraisal report, title deed, settlement agreement, guarantor notice) with their key fields agreed with Legal and NPA and held as reference data | A product owner | The OCR pipeline has a target | Must | 2
RWB-E1-026 | Attach and search screen | To upload, see and search documents from the case record view | A case owner | The case file is complete | Must | 3
RWB-E1-032 | Automatic attach from the OCR intake | Documents from the OCR intake attached to their case automatically when the case ID or account number is read, with unmatched documents sent to the review queue | A case owner | No document is filed by hand | Must | 3
RWB-E1-033 | Search across cases | A search across all cases by document type, date range, extracted field and free text, with results limited to the cases my role may see | A litigation officer | A document is found in seconds without opening cases one by one | Should | 3
RWB-E1-040 | Document checklist per case type as reference data | The required documents per case type and route held as a reference table that the case record view and the review queue read | A litigation officer | A missing document shows on the case without a person checking a list | Should | 3
RWB-E1-041 | Retention classes and virus scan on intake | Every uploaded or scanned file checked for malware before storage, and a retention class per document type that the store applies | A document hub owner | The store holds only safe files and keeps each for the time the policy sets | Must | 3
RWB-E1-049 | OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub | Inbound scans read by the OCR service and output as text plus layout | A document hub owner | Extraction can start | Must | 3
RWB-E1-050 | Document classification | Each scanned document classified into one of the six types with a confidence score | A document hub owner | It is attached to the right checklist | Must | 2
RWB-E1-053 | Field extraction for the six types into the index | The key fields of each of the six types extracted and written to the document index with a confidence per field | A document hub owner | Documents are searchable by their content | Must | 2
RWB-E1-054 | Review queue for low-confidence documents | A queue of documents with low classification or extraction confidence, each correctable in one screen, with the correction fed back to the labeled set | A litigation officer | No document is attached wrongly and the models improve | Must | 2
RWB-E1-057 | Intake from branches, mailroom, partner SFTP and email | Scans from branch scanners and the mailroom, partner files by SFTP and attachments from the recovery mailboxes to enter the same OCR intake with the source recorded | A document hub owner | Every document path ends in the document hub | Must | 3

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E1-034 | Letter template management | A screen to upload a template version, record the Legal approval and set it current | A litigation officer | Templates are managed without a developer | Should | 2
RWB-E1-046 | Template and merge field catalog as data | Letter and document templates and their merge fields held as versioned data with the Legal approval record | A litigation officer | A template change is a data release approved by Legal | Must | 3
RWB-E1-052 | Notice generation v1 | Demand, recall and guarantor notices generated from approved templates with case data merged | A litigation officer | Letters are produced without re-keying | Must | 3
RWB-E1-055 | Proof of delivery capture design with WIN | Generated notices sent to WIN for print and post, with the dispatch and proof-of-delivery status written back on the case | A litigation officer | The case shows what was sent and when it arrived | Should | 3

RWB-E1-027 | Decision log writer v1 | A writer that records case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached, with the rule ID and version used | The case workflow module | The first records exist in Epic 1 | Must | 2

RWB-E1-013 | Baseline measures | Cases by route, age and queue, realized recovery, time in stage and TAT per route published as the baseline with definitions agreed with the Tribe | The Tribe lead | Every later epic is measured against the same baseline | Must | 3

RWB-E1-058 | Agent platform set-up [E1a] | The LLM gateway, prompt and policy store, guardrail checker and evaluation suite deployed in the Workbench namespace | An AI product owner | Agents can be built and tested | Must | 5
RWB-E1-059 | Case intake agent in shadow [E1b] | The case intake agent to build a case file summary and flag gaps for Epic 1 cases in shadow mode | An AI product owner | It is scored before anyone sees it | Must | 2
