secs.h: 4. Program requirements met in this epic
secs.t:
The table carries the 77 program requirements this epic meets, of which 75 are live and 2 are removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). Removed requirements keep their IDs and name their later home. The data requirements are read from ACE through the 30 views; the 20 copy, load and tracker tables are gone and no source load job remains.

ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner
REQ-RDF-001 | Recovery data is organized in 14 data products, each with exactly one named system of record, one read path and one named owner. Source data is read from ACE through read-only views and is not copied. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-002 | Account balance, arrears, payments and classification for every account at 90 or more days past due are read from ACE and are current to the previous working day of the ACE batch. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-003 | Collections contact history, promises and case status from EFS are read from ACE, which ingests them, so that the case carries what happened before day 90. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-004 | Collateral records and appraisal values are available on the case without a person looking them up in CCMS or SVAF. ACE ingests them under RWB-ACE-001. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-005 | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). Excel and SharePoint trackers leave system scope. Later home: the Cutover plan lists and retires them. | Removed | Program manager
REQ-RDF-006 | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). No tracker file is loaded. Later home: the Cutover plan retires each local copy with the owner's confirmation and a read-only archive. | Removed | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-007 | The case list reconciles daily to the count of accounts at 90 or more days past due in v_ace_account, which ACE ingests from ALS, with no variance (DL25), and every business key on a Workbench table resolves to an ACE row. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-008 | Data quality checks on source data run in ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001). The Workbench reports reconciliation breaks, referential completeness and its quality measures, each break with a reason visible to the data product owner. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-009 | Every data product carries a freshness stamp from the ACE batch record, and every decision records the freshness of the data it used. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-RDF-010 | Access to each data product is controlled per role through the read-only views, and personal data is masked by role in line with PDPA. | Must | Compliance
REQ-RDF-011 | Every data product has a catalog entry stating its definition, owner, system of record (ACE, ingested from the named source), refresh cycle and retention. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-RDF-012 | Baseline measures for cases by route, age and queue, realized recovery, time in stage and turnaround per route are published, with definitions agreed by the Tribe. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-RDF-013 | Workbench recovery records carry a retention and archive rule by record class; ACE data is retained by ACE. | Should | Compliance
REQ-CWC-001 | Every account at 90 or more days past due that is not excluded carries one recovery case, created by rule from the daily ACE batch. | Must | Business lead
REQ-CWC-002 | Each case carries a case ID in the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN, issued once, never reused, and printed on every letter and document. | Must | Business lead
REQ-CWC-003 | One case covers one customer and one product, with its accounts linked to it. | Must | Business lead
REQ-CWC-004 | Exclusion rules for deceased, fraud, bankruptcy, an active restructure plan and an open dispute are held as data and applied at creation. | Must | Risk
REQ-CWC-005 | The case state model covers stage, status within stage, route and the deviation flags X1 to X7, and a case holds exactly one state at a time. | Must | Business lead
REQ-CWC-006 | Roles, teams, queues, queue membership and capacity are held as versioned reference data and change without a code release. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-CWC-007 | Every new case is placed in a queue and assigned to a person by rule, and no case is allocated by hand as a matter of course. | Must | Team manager
REQ-CWC-008 | Allocation rules read product, region, exposure band, stage, route, deviation flag, customer segment and collateral type, apply first match, and always have a default row. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-CWC-009 | Assignment rules support round robin, lowest load and a named owner for continuity, with a capacity cap and an overflow queue. | Must | Team manager
REQ-CWC-010 | Cases move between queues and roles by transfer rules on stage change, route decision, timer expiry, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, and manual request with a reason code. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-CWC-011 | Service levels per queue and status, warning thresholds and escalation targets are held as data, and a breach raises an event without moving the case. | Must | Team manager
REQ-CWC-012 | Prescription dates are set from the legal periods table at case creation and are visible at all times. | Must | Legal counsel
REQ-CWC-013 | A rule change goes from a validated template load to production with a version stamp and no code release, and rolls back to the previous version by one call. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-CWC-014 | Rule loads are validated for schema, overlapping rows, unreachable rows, a missing default and a set of test cases before they take effect. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-CWC-015 | Unassigned and over-capacity cases are rebalanced daily, and queue counts, ageing and service level breaches are reported. | Must | Team manager
REQ-CWC-016 | Every allocation, assignment, transfer and timer event is logged with the rule ID and the rule version that caused it. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DCM-001 | Every document is stored against its case with type, date, source and extracted fields. | Must | Legal counsel
REQ-DCM-002 | The Workbench document hub is the system of record for recovery documents. No other store holds the authoritative copy. | Must | IT lead
REQ-DCM-003 | Legal document types are held in a write-once container that cannot be altered or deleted. | Must | Legal counsel
REQ-DCM-004 | The document types and their key fields are agreed and signed before the extraction pipeline is built. | Must | Business lead with Legal
REQ-DCM-005 | Inbound documents are classified into one of the agreed types with a confidence score, and anything below the threshold goes to a review queue. | Must | Autonomous Ops
REQ-DCM-006 | Fields are extracted into the index for the agreed document types, in Thai and in English. | Must | Autonomous Ops
REQ-DCM-007 | A classified document attaches to its case without a person doing it. | Must | Autonomous Ops
REQ-DCM-008 | Documents are searchable by case ID, type and date from the case record view. | Must | Case owner
REQ-DCM-009 | Documents arrive from branches, the mailroom, partner file transfer and email through the same intake. | Must | Autonomous Ops
REQ-DCM-010 | Every document carries a retention class, and intake runs a virus scan before the document is stored. | Must | Compliance
REQ-DCM-011 | A document checklist per case type is held as reference data so that a missing document is visible. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DCM-014 | New scope. Document storage is sized, provisioned and costed for the inbound volume and its growth, and the cost belongs to the program's running cost. | Must | Solution architect
REQ-DCM-015 | New scope. Documents are backed up on a stated schedule, and a restore is tested before the first production release and at each subsequent release. | Must | IT lead
REQ-DCM-016 | New scope. A legal hold applied to a case or a document stops deletion and expiry for as long as the hold is in place, overriding the retention class. | Must | Legal counsel with Compliance
REQ-DCM-020 | New scope. The hub carries a records management position signed by Compliance and Legal covering storage, backup, legal hold, discovery and disposal. | Must | Solution architect with Compliance
REQ-DRI-001 | Every decision writes one record holding case and decision, the rule, model, agent and prompt versions, an inputs snapshot, the recommendation, the approval, the actions taken and the outcome. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DRI-002 | The decision log is append only. A record cannot be changed or deleted, and a correction is a new record naming the one it corrects. | Must | Compliance
REQ-DRI-003 | The decision log is hash chained, and the chain integrity is checked every day with a break reported to Compliance the same day. | Must | Compliance
REQ-DRI-004 | Records are written from Epic 1 for case creation, owner assignment, case transfer and document attachment. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DRI-005 | No action proceeds if its decision log entry cannot be written. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DRI-006 | No component calls a system of record directly. Source data is read from the ACE database through the read-only recovery.v_ace_* views, and leaves through paths ACE already has (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). | Must | Solution architect
REQ-DRI-007 | The integration adapters log every outbound file and event, retry on a defined schedule, and place anything that fails after the retry limit in an exception queue with a task for a named owner. | Must | Platform administrator
REQ-DRI-008 | Data from other systems reaches the Workbench only through ACE ingestion and the ACE views. Interfaces that need same-day data are named under DL06 before any is built. | Must | Solution architect
REQ-DRI-009 | The decision log is copied to the data lake copy daily for reporting, with row counts matched. | Must | Data steward and data product owner
REQ-DRI-010 | A parameter catalog and a configuration service hold every threshold, limit and name, versioned, changed without a code release. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-DRI-011 | A reference data service holds every versioned table with its valid from and valid to dates, author and approver. | Must | Reference data administrator
REQ-ACA-001 | Every user signs on through Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-002 | Roles are held as data, and a role change takes effect without a code release. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-003 | The role to permission matrix is held as data and is the only source of what a role may see and do. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-004 | The delegation of authority table is held as reference data and sets every approval limit. | Must | Risk with Credit
REQ-ACA-005 | Personal data is masked by role on every screen and in every agent call. | Must | Compliance
REQ-ACA-006 | Every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is written to the access log. | Must | Compliance
REQ-ACA-007 | Access requested outside the authority matrix is refused and the refusal is recorded. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-008 | A break-glass path exists for an emergency, needs its own approval, and writes to the access log. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-009 | A user sees only the cases and queues their role and scope allow. | Must | Security administrator
REQ-ACA-010 | Agents run under service identities and are subject to the same role checks as people. | Must | Platform administrator
REQ-OCC-001 | Notices are generated from templates approved by Legal, with merge fields from case data and no re-keying. | Must | Legal counsel
REQ-OCC-002 | Letter templates are versioned, and the Legal approval is recorded against the version. | Must | Legal counsel
REQ-OCC-007 | The case record view shows account, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, route, timers, contact history, promises, documents and decisions on one screen. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-001 | One ledger holds every interaction on a case, and no other record is the authoritative history of what happened with the customer. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-002 | Every entry carries the case ID, the event, the timestamp, the actor and the source that produced it. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-003 | Entries carry the channel, who or what was reached, and the outcome, where the interaction had one. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-004 | An offer, a promise, a payment or a hand-over made during an interaction is recorded against that interaction. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-005 | Every action the Workbench takes on a case writes to the ledger as it happens: case creation, allocation, transfer, escalation, document attachment and decisions taken. | Must | Center of excellence
REQ-ILG-006 | The ledger reads back in one ordered sequence, filterable by channel, actor and date range, through one interface. | Must | Case owner
REQ-ILG-007 | The same event arriving twice with the same key produces one entry, and the repeat is counted. | Must | Platform administrator
REQ-ILG-008 | A ledger write that fails raises an incident. An entry is never discarded, because a ledger with silent gaps is trusted and wrong. | Must | Platform administrator
REQ-ILG-014 | Personal data in the ledger is masked by role on the same rules as the case record. | Must | Compliance

The epic releases on time only if the business gives the support below during the build.

Support | From | When
Confirm the count of accounts at 90 days past due by product and month | Data lead | 6 Nov
Confirm the data dictionary sources and owners for each data product | Data steward and data product owner | During the build
Agree the document types and fields the document hub reads | Business lead with Legal | 6 Nov
Approve the wording of the demand, recall and guarantor notice templates | Legal counsel | Before UAT
Provide the allocation rows, caseload caps and service levels as data | Business lead and product owner | 13 Nov
Set retention and masking per data product and document type | Compliance | 13 Nov
Name the Entra ID groups for the Workbench roles | SCB IT security | 6 Nov
Test with the squads during the build and run UAT in the week before release | Business testers | Two to three hours a day, then UAT
Draft Thai names for fields, labels and messages one epic ahead | Business lead with Legal and Compliance | From 5 Nov

Excel and SharePoint trackers are retired through the Cutover plan (U5).

Business testers see each requirement working during the build and confirm it against its scenarios.

SIT runs for one week before the release, and UAT for one week, against the business scripts.

The business lead signs the UAT exit. A requirement that fails has its feature flag switched off and the release goes ahead without it.

The product owner accepts each story against its acceptance criteria.

DL43 is new and open. The other decisions keep their v3 answers, with the wording changed where D-RCV-35 supersedes the COLLINS route or the read and write position.

Decision | Question | Answer the build uses until decided | Owner | Needed by
DL06 | Which interfaces need real-time data, and which take the daily batch? | Option A, a daily batch through COLLINS, is superseded by D-RCV-35: ACE ingests all source data and the Workbench runs no source batch load. Same-day triggers are named under option B: case transferred from EFS, payment received, legal event. | K. Book with K. Pipat | 30 Oct
DL09 | Who tests from the business, and when? | Business testers work with the squads two to three hours a day during the build, then a one-week UAT before each release. | K. Tee with K. Jao | 31 Oct
DL10 | What is the Thai name for each field, label and message? | The business lead drafts per module one epic ahead; Legal and Compliance approve. | Business lead with Legal and Compliance | 5 Nov
DL12 | Which legacy systems are kept, and does any need enhancing? | No legacy enhancement. The read and write wording of option A is superseded by D-RCV-35: source data is read only, through the recovery.v_ace_* views. | K. Tony with K. Book | 7 Nov
DL15 | Are the inventory counts and the growth assumption the right base for sizing? | A: Mortgage 12,256, hire purchase 12,960 and SSME 2,903 accounts; 3,110 new accounts a month; 15 percent growth a year. | Data lead | 6 Nov
DL16 | Does a case enter the Workbench at 90 or 91 days past due? | 90 days past due. The target operating model has the case owner holding the case from day 90. | Business lead | 6 Nov
DL17 | Is a case one per customer per product, one per account, or one per customer? | One per customer per product, with the accounts linked. | Product owner with the solution architect | 6 Nov
DL19 | Which document types and fields does the document hub classify and extract? | B where the bank has one; A until then. | Business lead with Legal | 6 Nov
DL20 | Where do customer facts come from? | The customer facts ACE holds, ingested from SCBPDM and the core bank, read through v_ace_customer. Amended by D-RCV-35. | Solution architect with K. Book | 30 Oct
DL21 | Which systems store the Workbench case identifier? | A for Epics 1 and 2. Each system added later is an interface change. | Solution architect with the IT lead | 6 Nov
DL24 | Which rules does the rules component load in Epic 1? | Allocation, assignment and transfer only. The route decision goes live in a later epic. | Product owner | 30 Oct
DL25 | How large a difference between the case list and the ACE account view is accepted? | Zero; any difference holds the publish. | Data lead | 6 Nov
DL26 | How long is each data product and document type kept, and which fields are masked for which role? | Provide per data product and document type. | Compliance | 13 Nov
DL29 | Which EFS contact outcomes come into the interaction ledger, and how far back? | A named list of outcomes for the case's collection period only. named by the business lead. | Data lead with the business lead | 13 Nov
DL39 | Which roles receive real users at each release? | Administration roles at Epic 1; business roles from the release that gives them a screen, starting with Epic 2. | Business lead | 20 Nov
DL40 | What are the Entra ID group names and the bank IAM entry for the Workbench roles? | One group per role per environment. | SCB IT security | 6 Nov
DL43 | Does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates? | Open. The build assumes the scope is accepted: 14 tables, 12 columns and 80 source fields by 21 November. Until they land, the Section B views and the features that need them stay behind their flags. | ACE team lead | 21 Nov

One owner and a timer on every case, full history on one screen, approval routing, litigation notices generated and approved, letters with proof of delivery, SMS and LINE, and the steering dashboard.

RWB-E2-010 | Stage 2 data products: contracts, plans and treatments | The stage 2 data products (treatments, plans, contracts, guarantees) added to the recovery data store with their systems of record | A data product owner | The settlement, TDR and DIL screens in Epic 3 read from one store | Should | 3

Key | Requirement | What the Workbench does | For | User benefit | Priority | Tests
RWB-E2-001 | EFS hand-over with full history from the COLLINS load | The case created or updated from the EFS data in the COLLINS daily load, with the full contact and promise history | A case owner | The case starts the morning after it reaches 90 days past due | Must | 3
RWB-E2-002 | ACE plan status on the case | The restructure plan status from the ACE common module (created, approved, booked, broken) on the case | A case owner | A case with a live plan is never treated as if it had none | Must | 3
RWB-E2-003 | Customer's other products on the case | The customer's other products and their status on the case, from the customer profile ACE receives through COLLINS | A case owner | I can see the whole relationship before I decide a route | Should | 3
RWB-E2-006 | Credit approval pack for NLEADS | The credit approval pack for an approved plan prepared for submission in NLEADS, with the result recorded on the treatment | A restructure operations officer | A plan reaches credit without re-keying the case facts | Must | 3
RWB-E2-007 | Booking confirmation from the ALS load | The booked terms or settlement matched from the next day's ALS load to the approved treatment, with a task when the booking is missing | A restructure operations officer | Every approved decision is confirmed as booked | Must | 3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Business requirements, program

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench business requirements, program
Version | 4
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Covers | All eight epics, November 2026 to June 2027
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, until the SCB X requirement template is adopted (DL13)
Change | Version 4 re-bases the program requirements on the ACE database under D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5) and ADR-010, which supersedes ADR-005. Sections 1.1, 5 (intro and 5.1 to 5.3), 6.3, 6.5 (NFR-032), 7 and 9 change: section 5.1 states the four-tier read model and its counts, 5.2 is outbound only and 5.3 states the business-key link to ACE; the Workbench runs no inbound source load, reads source data only through the read-only recovery.v_ace_* views, and leaves Excel and SharePoint trackers to the Cutover plan. Requirement IDs are kept. REQ-RDF-005 and 006 are marked removed with their later home, and REQ-RDF-008 is re-worded to the reconciliation duty that stays in the Workbench, leaving 229 of 231 requirements live. DL43 is added as open. Other sections are unchanged.

This document sets the business requirements for the Recovery Workbench across the eight epics: what it must do, for whom, how well, and under which constraints. Each epic has its own document at development detail.

Every recovery case from 90 days past due to close, for Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME.

Decisions D6 to D9 with their sub-decisions, D5 once the restructure program is live, and deviations X1 to X7 after day 90.

Partners, documents, the decision log and the interaction ledger.

The recovery module of ACE, with data through ACE ingestion; the Workbench reads read-only ACE views (D-RCV-35).

Out of scope | Where it is handled
Collections before day 90, decisions D1 to D4 | EFS and the ACE collection module
Dialer and messaging channels | Existing bank channels, reached through the ACE notification path
Core bank booking logic | ALS
COLLINS model development | Data and AI
Restructure affordability and plan calculation | The ACE restructure calculator
Partner systems | Each partner
Changes to bank policy | The policy owners

The Workbench is measured on the 2027 targets below. Each measure is read from the decision log per decision, with the baseline set in Epic 1.

Measure | Today | 2027 target
Recovery rate on NPL | 66.3% (2026 to date) | 73%
Litigation turnaround | 21 days | 6 days
Deed in lieu turnaround | 26 days | 12 days
Restructure turnaround | 23 days | 5 days
Debt sale turnaround | No baseline | 45 days
Manual processes removed | Near zero | 80% of the selected list
Audit findings and fraud cases | 50 | 13
NPA sales cycle | 1,486 days | 1,095 days

Class | Roles
Bank user | 37
Partner user | 7
Customer party | 4
Non-human actor | 6

Every role, its permissions and the release that gives it real users are in the Users, roles and permissions workbook.

19 L1 processes, 84 L2 sub-processes and 247 L3 processes. Processes 01 to 05 run in collections before day 90; the Workbench runs 06 to 19.

L1 | Process | Decision | L2 | L3 | Process owner
01 | Detect and act on signals | D1 | 2 | 6 | Collections, on EFS and ACE
02 | Contact the customer | D2 | 6 | 15 | Collections, on EFS and ACE
03 | Manage promises | D3 | 3 | 6 | Collections, on EFS and ACE
04 | Escalate | D4 | 4 | 10 | Collections, on EFS and ACE
05 | Restructure | D5 | 5 | 15 | Collections, on EFS and ACE
06 | Take over and own the case | D6 entry | 1 | 3 | Recovery Strategy with Risk; the case owner for each case
07 | Route, settle and claim | D6 | 5 | 17 | Recovery Strategy with Risk
08 | Litigate and enforce | D7 | 4 | 16 | Head of Litigation; the enforcement owner after judgment
09 | Dispose assets and sell debt | D8 | 7 | 28 | Head of NPA and Head of Auto Recovery; Head of Asset Liquidity for debt sale
10 | Write off and recover after charge-off | D9 | 3 | 9 | Credit Administration with Risk
11 | Handle customer care and deviations | X1 to X7 | 8 | 31 | Shared operations, with a named handler for each deviation
12 | Manage partners | All | 5 | 13 | Partner and agency manager
13 | Manage documents and correspondence | All | 4 | 14 | Shared operations
14 | Set strategy, policy and decision rules | All | 3 | 12 | Center of excellence
15 | Manage performance, data and AI | All | 8 | 20 | Center of excellence with Model Risk
16 | Manage risk, control and compliance | All | 7 | 14 | Product heads for limits; center of excellence for QA; Shared operations for conduct
17 | Run the decision center | D1 to D9 | 3 | 6 | Center of excellence
18 | Plan capacity and allocate work | D2, D4 | 3 | 6 | Shared operations
19 | Manage payments and reconciliation | D3, D5, D6 | 3 | 6 | Credit Administration

231 business requirements across the platform and stage modules, of which 2 are removed by D-RCV-35 (229 live). Must is needed for the epic to release; Should is planned in the epic; Could is taken if capacity allows.

P1 is the read-only data position for the whole program. ACE ingests every source and holds it; the Workbench reads it only through SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views and holds only Workbench-owned data: the case, its decisions, reference data and the extension tables (D-RCV-35, ADR-010).

The read model has four tiers. Tier 1 is 22 ACE tables that exist today; the recovery data in them is read through 16 Section A views, and the Workbench never alters them. Tier 2 is 14 ACE tables and 12 columns the ACE team adds under RWB-ACE-001 for 80 source fields; the new tables are read through 14 Section B views and the new columns extend v_ace_account, v_ace_customer and v_ace_efs_action. Tier 3 is 4 Workbench extension tables keyed by ACE business keys. Tier 4 is 88 retained Workbench tables. The recovery schema is 92 tables; with the 30 views the dictionary holds 122 sys_objects and 1,366 sys_fields.

Two migrations carry the views, because a view cannot be created over a table that does not exist. Section A ships with RWB-E1-069, the next free sequence after the V0001 baseline. Section B ships when RWB-ACE-001 lands, and until then the features that read the Tier 2 additions stay behind their flags. DL43 is open: the ACE team has yet to accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates. No copy, load or tracker table remains in the recovery schema; source content is read through the views and the trackers are retired through the Cutover plan.

ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner | Epic
REQ-RDF-001 | Recovery data is held in 14 data products, each with exactly one named system of record, ACE (ingested from the named source) or the Workbench, and one named owner. Source data in a data product is read from the ACE database through the read-only recovery.v_ace_* views and is not copied into the Workbench (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-002 | Account balance, arrears, payments and classification for every account at 90 or more days past due are read from ACE through v_ace_account and v_ace_payment, current to the latest completed ACE batch for the previous working day. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-003 | Collections contact history, promises and case status from EFS are read from ACE through v_ace_efs_action and v_ace_efs_assignment, so that the case carries what happened before day 90. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-004 | Collateral records and appraisal values are available on the case without a person looking them up in CCMS or SVAF. ACE ingests them under RWB-ACE-001, and the Workbench reads them through v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail and v_ace_valuation (DL43). The Workbench's acceptance of an appraisal is held in valuation_ext. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-005 | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). Excel and SharePoint trackers leave system scope. Later home: the tracker retirement procedure in the Cutover plan. Was: every recovery team's Excel file, SharePoint list and local file is listed with its owner, fields and update cycle, and each one has a decision to load it or record it as out of scope. | Removed | Program manager | E1
REQ-RDF-006 | Removed by D-RCV-35 (U5). No tracker is loaded into the Workbench. Later home: the Cutover plan, which retires each local copy with the owner's confirmation and a read-only archive. Was: every file with a load decision is loaded, its row counts reconciled, and its local copy retired with the owner's confirmation and a read-only archive kept. | Removed | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-007 | The case list reconciles daily to the count of accounts at 90 or more days past due in v_ace_account, with no variance (DL25), and every business key on a Workbench table resolves to an ACE row. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-008 | Data quality checks on source data run in ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001). The Workbench reports reconciliation breaks, referential completeness and its quality measures, each break with a reason visible to the data product owner. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-009 | Every data product carries a freshness stamp taken from the ACE batch record (v_ace_batch_status), and every decision records the freshness of the data it used. | Must | Center of excellence | E1
REQ-RDF-010 | Access to each data product is controlled per role, and personal data is masked by role in line with PDPA. The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only, and the customer identification number leaves ACE masked. | Must | Compliance | E1
REQ-RDF-011 | Every data product has a catalog entry stating its definition, owner, system of record, refresh cycle and retention, and, for source data, the ACE table and the view it is read through. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E1
REQ-RDF-012 | Baseline measures for cases by route, age and queue, realized recovery, time in stage and turnaround per route are published, with definitions agreed by the Tribe. | Must | Center of excellence | E1
REQ-RDF-013 | Workbench recovery records carry a retention and archive rule by record class; ACE data is retained by ACE. | Should | Compliance | E1
REQ-RDF-014 | Stage 2 data products for contracts, plans and treatments exist before the first treatment goes live. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E2

P2 is outbound only. It provides one adapter pattern for the WIN registered-mail notice file, the data lake and Power BI extract, the decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the data lake, the debt buyer tape and the GL write-off event. It uses the ACE logging path to the SOC, and the transport used by the partner and document channels. It runs no inbound file feed, no file-load adapter and no inbound run record or sign-off: every inbound source lands in ACE through ACE ingestion and is read through the P1 views (D-RCV-35, U1; ADR-010).

ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner | Epic
REQ-DRI-006 | No component calls a system of record directly. Source data lands in the ACE database through ACE ingestion and is read only through the recovery.v_ace_* views; data leaves through paths ACE already has (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). | Must | Solution architect | E1
REQ-DRI-007 | The integration adapters log every outbound file, retry on a defined schedule, and place anything that fails after the retry limit in an exception queue with a task for a named owner. Inbound files belong to ACE ingestion (D-RCV-35). | Must | Platform administrator | E1
REQ-DRI-008 | The Workbench runs no inbound batch or file load. Source data reaches it at the frequency ACE ingests it, and work that depends on a source starts when the ACE batch for that source is complete. Interfaces that need same-day data are named under DL06 before any is built. | Must | Solution architect | E1
REQ-DRI-013 | Case hand-over from EFS is read from ACE through v_ace_efs_assignment once the ACE batch for EFS is complete, and plan status is read from the ACE common module, so a case is current the morning after it changes. | Must | Data steward and data product owner | E2

P3 covers the case and workflow layer, which the Workbench owns. A case links to an ACE customer by person_key and to each account by account_key, with asset_key, payment_code and contact_key used where the case refers to an asset, a payment or a contact point; no link is a foreign key into ACE. Workbench-only facts sit in the extension tables. The case layer never copies a source record and never writes to the ACE schema.

Constraint | What it means
Built on ACE | The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end
Modular monolith | Common, collection and recovery modules, with boundaries checked at build time
Programmatic workflow | Case, stage and task state held in the database and moved by code, in CMMN 1.1 terms. No Temporal
Principle 1 | Every rule, limit, threshold, template, name, queue, role, timer and route is a versioned data row, changed through a validated load without a code release
Data through ACE ingestion | Source data lands in the ACE database through ACE ingestion, including sources ACE does not hold today. The recovery module reads it only through the read-only recovery.v_ace_* views, links to it by ACE business keys and holds no copy, load or staging table (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). No real-time feed today; same-day needs are named under DL06
ACE team dependency | The ACE team owns every ACE table and column the views read, and adds 14 tables, 12 columns and 80 source fields under RWB-ACE-001 by 21 November 2026 for the 30 November release (DL43). Features that read the Tier 2 additions stay behind their feature flags until the additions land
Document hub | The Workbench is the system of record for recovery documents
Monthly releases | One production release at each month end, shared with the collection squad

secs.h: 9. Open decisions that change these requirements
secs.t:
DL43 is the new open decision. The others keep their v3 answers, with the wording changed where D-RCV-35 supersedes the COLLINS route or the read and write position.

Decision | Question | Answer the build uses until decided | Owner | Needed by
DL06 | Which interfaces need real time data, and which take the daily batch? | Option A, daily batch through COLLINS, is superseded by D-RCV-35: ACE ingests all source data, so the Workbench runs no source batch load and reads ACE once its batch is complete. Option B for the named same-day triggers. ACE has no real time feed today. Name the same-day triggers now: case transferred from EFS, payment received, legal event. | K. Book with K. Pipat | 30 Oct
DL10 | What is the Thai name for each field, label and message? | The business lead drafts per module one epic ahead; Legal and Compliance approve. | Business lead with Legal and Compliance | 5 Nov
DL11 | What is the value for each non-functional target, or the owner and date for it? | Use the ACE values where ACE has them; the solution architect proposes the rest; Risk agrees. | Solution architect with Risk | 5 Nov
DL12 | Which legacy systems are kept, and does any need enhancing? | No legacy enhancement, with a list of the systems kept and what the Workbench reads from each. The read and write part of option A is superseded by D-RCV-35: source data is read only, through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, not a direct read of ACE or COLLINS. | K. Tony with K. Book | 7 Nov
DL13 | The SCB X consortium template for AI code generation arrives on 29 October. Are the Epic 1 and Epic 2 requirements rewritten to it before the build? | Remap the Epic 1 requirements by 4 November and use the template from Epic 2. TechX, SCB and Henka agree one template and keep it for every later epic. | K. Tee with TechX and Henka | 30 Oct
DL15 | Are the inventory counts and the growth assumption the right base for sizing? | A: Mortgage 12,256, hire purchase 12,960 and SSME 2,903 accounts; 3,110 new accounts a month; 15 percent growth a year. | Data lead | 6 Nov
DL16 | Does a case enter the Workbench at 90 or 91 days past due? | 90 days past due. The target operating model has the case owner holding the case from day 90. | Business lead | 6 Nov
DL17 | Is a case one per customer per product, one per account, or one per customer? | One per customer per product, with the accounts linked. | Product owner with the solution architect | 6 Nov
DL18 | Which person holds each approval level, with the limit by decision, amount and product, and the substitute for each? | Load the regulation's levels and limits now; add names and substitutes when signed. | Risk with the product heads | 30 Nov
DL20 | Where do customer facts come from? | The customer facts ACE holds, which ACE ingests from SCBPDM and the core bank; the Workbench reads them through v_ace_customer. Amended by D-RCV-35, which removes the COLLINS route. | Solution architect with K. Book | 30 Oct
DL22 | How long may a case stay in each state before it escalates? | Load the values as parameters; escalation runs from the day they are loaded. | Business lead | 13 Nov
DL23 | What is the most cases a person holds, and how is a queue ordered? | Load as parameters. | Product owner | 13 Nov
DL26 | How long is each data product and document type kept, and which fields are masked for which role? | Provide per data product and document type. | Compliance | 13 Nov
DL27 | How are storage, backup, legal hold and e-discovery provided for the document hub? | The ACE storage pattern with a write-once container and the bank backup service. | Solution architect with Compliance | 13 Nov
DL43 | Does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates? The scope is 14 new ACE tables, 12 new columns and 80 source fields. | Open. The build assumes the scope is accepted: 14 new ACE tables, 12 new columns and 80 source fields. Dates to confirm, and the Tier 2 features stay behind their flags until the additions land. | ACE team lead | 21 Nov

S2 | FEAT-TRT-07 Send the offer and start the validity timer | System | Sends the offer to the customer and starts the validity clock. The wait is a timer, not a routed state.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-08 Route the signed offer to operations for booking | System | Moves the case to operations when the customer signs inside the validity period.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-09 Return the case to its prior status on no signature | System | Sends the case back to the status it held in COLLINS when the customer declines or the offer expires.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-10 Book the plan and set the schedule | System | Writes the plan to NLEADS and ALS, sets the payment schedule and starts the plan timers.

S2 | FEAT-TRT-13 Check encumbrance and eligibility before negotiation | System | Runs the encumbrance and title checks early, so a deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-14 Unlock the asset as a non performing asset by rule | System | Applies the auto-unlock rule so the asset moves to the asset list without a person for the cases that qualify.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-15 Capture the collateral inspection in the field | User | Lets the field officer record the inspection, the checklist and the bills against the case.
S2 | FEAT-TRT-16 Set up a deed in lieu buy-back rental | System | Opens the rental record, the auto-debit and the receipt loop where the customer buys back.

Functional specification. SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

| Document title | FSD P1 Recovery data engine |

| Status | In review |

| Date | 15 November 2026 |
| FSD owner | Business analyst, P1 |
| Business owner | Business lead |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5); ADR-010 |

| Module code | Module name | First in |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Recovery data engine | E1 |

**Feature scope.** Read-only ACE source views, the four Workbench extension tables, the data product catalog and data dictionary, freshness from the ACE batch record, case-list reconciliation to ACE, access and retention.

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 28 October 2026 | COLLINS and file loads, load checks, tracker loads, reconciliation to ALS, freshness from the Workbench load |
| 3 | 15 November 2026 | Re-based on the ACE database under D-RCV-35 and ADR-010. The module loads no source data: it reads ACE through the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and owns only the four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext`. Freshness is stamped in `data_product_load` from `ace_batch_run`, read through `v_ace_batch_status` (EV-26 AceDataReady, EV-27 AceDataLate). The case list reconciles to `v_ace_account`, and the same reconciliation set carries REC-03 approved treatments against ACE bookings and REC-04 ACE payments against proceeds. The data dictionary covers the views and the extension tables; systems of record read "ACE (ingested from X)". The load, load-check, tracker and feed-job functions FEAT-RDF-03 to 10 and FEAT-RDF-22 keep their IDs and are marked removed with their later home. JOB-01 and JOB-09 are retired. |

| Document | Type | Relationship |

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** The read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and their grant, the four extension tables, the data dictionary over tables and views, the 14 data products and their systems of record, the freshness stamp from the ACE batch record, the daily reconciliation of the case list to `v_ace_account`, the reconciliation and freshness report, the publish hold, access and masking per data product, the catalog, retention of Workbench records, the case list, baseline measures and the decision log copy to the lake.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces. Removed by D-RCV-35: every inbound source load, staging table and load check (later home ACE ingestion, RWB-ACE-001); the Excel and SharePoint tracker inventory, load and retirement (later home Cutover plan, U5); the legacy feed jobs on ADF and Control-M (later home ACE ingestion; no ADF job remains).

**Dependencies.** FEAT-DRI-01; FEAT-RDF-01; FEAT-RDF-02; FEAT-RDF-11; FEAT-RDF-14; FEAT-CWC-01; RWB-E1-069; RWB-ACE-001; DL43

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Source data is read only through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (D-RCV-35 U4, ADR-010). The module creates no foreign key into a `public` table, because ACE cascades deletes on `account`. It links to a source record by business key (`account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code`, `contact_key`) and never alters an ACE table. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

Recovery source data is held in the ACE database. ACE ingests the core bank (ALS), EFS, SCBPDM and product and branch data today. Under RWB-ACE-001 it adds CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID. The Workbench is a module of ACE (ADR-001). The v2 design copied 121 fields of that data into eleven Workbench tables and ran nine more tables to load them. Two copies of the same account disagree sooner or later. In v3 the module reads ACE through views and holds only the case and its own decisions: **ACE holds the data, the Workbench holds the case, and a view joins them.**

| 4. 88 Workbench tables | Workbench | Case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, debt sale, documents, decision log, reference, outbox, flags, agents |

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date from the ACE batch record, or show their date as stale.
- The ACE schema, with the tables named in the Section A grant, is present in the target environment before V0002 runs. The Section B tables of RWB-ACE-001 are present before V0003 runs.

secs.h: A2.1 Create the recovery tables, extension tables and read-only ACE views

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Creates the 92 recovery tables in the ACE database and the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views over ACE, so the Workbench reads one copy of source data and adds only its own records.

**Problem.** Source data is held in ACE. A Workbench copy of it would disagree with ACE and would be owned by no one who maintains the source.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Views compile and the boundary test passes | 100 percent of pipeline runs | Conformance test in the pipeline | Each release |

**Functional overview.** V0001 creates the recovery tables and the dictionary. V0002 (RWB-E1-069) creates the 16 Section A views over the ACE tables that exist today. V0003 creates the 14 Section B views over the RWB-ACE-001 additions the week they land. The views are owned by a dedicated `ace_view_owner` role that holds SELECT on the ACE tables. The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and nothing else.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a pipeline deployment | Reads the migration set and the dictionary seed |
| 2 | System | Creates the tables, the extension tables and the views, and applies the grant | Runs the conformance test |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the Flyway history; fails the stage and names the statement or the check where a test fails |

secs.h: A2.11 Reconcile the case list to ACE daily

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Compares the case list with the accounts at 90 days past due and the balances in `v_ace_account` every day, checks that every business key on a Workbench table resolves to a view row, reconciles approved treatments to ACE bookings (REC-03) and ACE payments to proceeds (REC-04), and reports the difference.

**Problem.** An account that reaches 90 days past due in ACE and has no case is recovery work nobody does. A business key with no ACE row means a broken link, and there is no foreign key to catch it.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Case list reconciled to ACE with no unexplained variance | 100 percent of days (DL25) | reconciliation_result | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** JOB-04 runs on the ACE batch-complete record for ALS (EV-26), after JOB-02 case creation. It reads `v_ace_account` for the business date in `data_as_of`, takes away the accounts excluded at entry (`case_entry_exclusion`), and compares the result with the open cases and the case list rows by product group.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: AceDataReady for ALS and JOB-02 complete | Reads the tolerance version in force |
| 2 | System | Runs REC-01 count, REC-02 balance and REC-05 business-key resolution; REC-03 and REC-04 run in their owning jobs (JOB-08 and JOB-07) against the same tolerance version | Applies the tolerances |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes reconciliation_result per check and product group; lists the breaks for the data steward; releases or holds the publish (A2.13) |

| Check | ACE side, read through a view | Workbench side | Compared on | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REC-01 | Accounts at 90 days past due or more in v_ace_account, less the accounts excluded at entry | Open recovery cases and the case list rows | Count by product | Zero unexplained |
| REC-02 | Balances in v_ace_account | Balances on the case accounts and the case list rows | Sum by product | Zero |
| REC-03 | Booked plans and settlements in v_ace_account and v_ace_plan for the business date | Approved treatments in treatment, after the booking wait the parameter sets | Count by treatment | Zero after two ACE business dates |
| REC-04 | Payments in v_ace_payment for the business date | Proceeds rows in proceeds, matched by payment_code | Count and amount for the business date | Zero unmatched; every difference listed |
| REC-05 | v_ace_account, v_ace_customer, v_ace_asset and v_ace_payment | Every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code on a Workbench table | Business key, count and amount | Zero orphans; every one listed |

REC-03 and REC-04 are defined here so one rule set covers every reconciliation, but they run inside the job that owns the fact: JOB-08 for approved treatments against bookings, and JOB-07 for payments against proceeds. Each writes its own `reconciliation_result` row with the check ID, business date and product. JOB-04 runs REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 only; REC-03 and REC-04 do not run inside it.

secs.h: A2.12 Publish the daily reconciliation and freshness report

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Produces the daily report of reconciliation results, the freshness of each data product and the data quality measures, for the data steward.

**Problem.** A break or a stale product that nobody sees is a wrong decision waiting to happen.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reconciliation breaks cleared within one day | 100 percent | reconciliation_result and the break list | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** The publish step of JOB-04 writes the data quality extract for the business date. Power BI refreshes from it at 07:30. The source-data checks now run in ACE ingestion and are not reported here.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: the reconciliation step of JOB-04 completes | Reads the measure definitions in force |
| 2 | System | Builds the extract: REC results by product, freshness of the 14 data products from data_product_load, quality measures | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the extract to the data lake; the job monitor records the run |

| Measure | Meaning | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Completeness | Mandatory fields filled on the Workbench tables and in the views the screens read | 99.9 percent |
| Validity | Codes in their lists, including the ACE lists read through v_ace_efs_action_code and v_ace_product | 99.5 percent |
| Timeliness | The ACE batch for the business date is complete when the Workbench reads it | 99 percent of days |
| Accuracy | Reconciliation breaks cleared within one day | 100 percent |
| Uniqueness | One case per customer per product | 100 percent |
| Referential completeness | Every business key on a Workbench table resolves to a v_ace_* row (REC-05) | 100 percent |

**Integration points.** Power BI, Data lake

**Problem.** A case list that does not match ACE sends teams to work the wrong accounts.

secs.h: A2.14 Stamp each data product with its freshness

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Writes the freshness stamp of each data product in `data_product_load` from the ACE batch record, so a decision carries the age of the data it used. Gates the daily data jobs on a complete ACE batch; this gate replaces the daily gate of the retired load checks.

**Problem.** The Workbench no longer loads source data, so it cannot time a load of its own. Without the ACE batch record, it cannot tell today's data from Friday's.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACE batch complete when the Workbench reads it | 99 percent of days | v_ace_batch_status and data_product_load | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** ACE writes one `ace_batch_run` row per source system and business date (RWB-ACE-001). The module reads it through `v_ace_batch_status`. When a source batch completes, EV-26 AceDataReady is raised: the stamp of every data product fed by that source is written, and the data jobs for the business date start. When the cut-off for a product (`data_product.expected_by`) passes before its batch completes, or the batch fails, EV-27 AceDataLate is published and the product is flagged STALE.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a new or changed row in v_ace_batch_status, or a product cut-off | Reads the product-to-source map in force |
| 2 | System | Writes or updates the data_product_load stamp | Raises EV-26 or publishes EV-27 |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Starts JOB-02, JOB-04, JOB-07 and JOB-08 on ALS ready; alerts the data steward on late |

| Data product | Source systems in v_ace_batch_status |
|---|---|
| DP01 Account and arrears | ALS |
| DP02 Customer and party | SCBPDM |
| DP05 Contact and promises | EFS |
| DP06 Collateral and assets | CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS |
| DP07 Legal events and cases | LIT, WIN |
| DP11 Scores and route economics | COLLINS |
| DP13 Money and closure | ALS, GL |
| DP03, DP04, DP08, DP09, DP10, DP12, DP14 | None; Workbench records, current on change |

| data_product_load field | From v_ace_batch_status |
|---|---|
| product_code | The product-to-source map above |
| source_system | source_system |
| business_date | business_date |
| source_extracted_at | started_at (OQ-P1-04) |
| loaded_at | completed_at |
| status | LOADED when is_complete; STALE on EV-27 |
| stale_flagged_at | Time EV-27 was published |
| duplicate_count | Repeat reads of the same COMPLETED row, ignored and counted |

**Integration points.** ACE database (v_ace_batch_status); outbox (EV-26, EV-27)

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-RDF-02; RWB-ACE-001 (v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view; OQ-P1-01, OQ-P1-02)

**Business objective.** Sets who can read each data product and which fields are masked, under the PDPA minimization rule, across the views and the extension tables.

**Problem.** Personal data now comes straight from ACE through the views. There is no load-time tokenization, so the controls are the view, the grant, role masking (E1-037) and the PII access log.

secs.h: A2.16 Maintain the data catalog entry per data product

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Keeps the catalog entry for each data product: definition, owner, system of record, the views and tables behind it, refresh, reconciliation rules and access. The data dictionary covers the views and the extension tables as well as the recovery tables.

**Problem.** A developer must be able to see that `days_past_due` comes from `public.account.delay_days` through `v_ace_account`, and must never go looking in `public`.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Objects and fields in the dictionary | 122 objects and 1,366 fields, matched to the schema | Conformance test; v_data_dictionary | Each release |

**Functional overview.** The dictionary is `sys_objects` (one row per table or view) and `sys_fields` (one row per field), read through `v_data_dictionary`. A view field carries source system "ACE" and its ACE source column as source field. An extension field carries source system "Workbench". The catalog entry joins the dictionary to `data_product`, `data_product_access` and `retention_rule`.

|---|---:|---:|---|
| Recovery tables (Tiers 3 and 4) | 92 | 1,062 | Workbench |
| of which extension tables | 4 | 49 | Workbench |
| Section A views | 16 | 177 | ACE |
| Section B views | 14 | 127 | ACE |
| **Total** | **122** | **1,366** | |

| 1 | Data steward and data product owner | Opens the catalog and maintains the entry for a data product | Checks the role, the capability area and the scope |
| 2 | Data steward and data product owner | Enters or confirms the values | Validates the fields and applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the action | Writes the catalog version and the decision log entry |

secs.h: A2.17 Apply the retention and archive rule to the data store

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Applies the retention class to each Workbench table and archives records past their period. Source data read through the views stays under ACE's retention.

**Problem.** Workbench records kept past their period break PDPA. A Workbench job that tried to archive ACE data would break the boundary rule.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workbench records past retention archived or on legal hold | 100 percent each month | JOB-17 run record | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** The compliance officer loads retention rows by data product and table (`retention_rule`), each versioned and approved. JOB-17 runs monthly on the first Sunday.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compliance and PDPA officer | Opens the retention screen and applies the retention and archive rule to the data store | Checks the role, the capability area and the scope |
| 2 | Compliance and PDPA officer | Enters or confirms the values | Validates the fields and applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the action | Writes the rule version and the decision log entry; JOB-17 applies it |

**Integration points.** ACE database (recovery schema only), archive container

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-RDF-01

secs.h: A2.18 Show the case list with case ID, owner and queue

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Gives every recovery team one list of all 90 plus days past due accounts across Mortgage, HP and SSME, built from the cases and `v_ace_account`.

**Problem.** Teams kept their own lists in spreadsheets. The case list replaces them with one list that is checked against ACE every day.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Case list built and released by 07:30 | 99 percent of days | case_list_row.refreshed_at and publish_status | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** The case list step of JOB-04 runs after AceDataReady for ALS and JOB-03 allocation. It writes one `case_list_row` per case account for the business date. Balance and days past due come from `v_ace_account`; last contact and action code come from `v_ace_efs_action`; case, owner, queue, stage and route come from the case. The link is `account_key`, with no foreign key.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Case owner | Opens the case list with case ID, owner and queue | Checks the role, the capability area and the scope |
| 2 | Case owner | Filters by team, queue and product | Shows the rows for the latest released business date with its freshness |
| 3 | System | Records the action | Writes the PII access log entry where a personal field is shown |

**Integration points.** Workbench, ACE database (v_ace_account, v_ace_efs_action, v_ace_batch_status), Data lake, Power BI

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-RDF-01, FEAT-RDF-14, FEAT-CWC-01

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Orchestrator, tool gateway, guardrails, prompt store, evaluation, autonomy levels.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-AGT-01; FEAT-AGT-03; FEAT-AGT-05; FEAT-AGT-06; FEAT-AGT-07; FEAT-AGT-12; FEAT-CWC-22; FEAT-DCM-09

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P10 | FEAT-AGT-01 | Set up the agent platform with the gateway and prompt store | System | Sets up the agent runtime, the model gateway, the prompt and policy store and the tool gateway. | E1 | A2.1 |

| P10 | FEAT-AGT-03 | Run the case intake agent in shadow | System | Runs the intake agent on 200 cases with its answers recorded and not acted on. | E1 | A2.3 |
| P10 | FEAT-AGT-04 | Evaluate document extraction quality | System | Measures extraction accuracy against the reviewed set, which sets the confidence threshold. | E1 | A2.4 |
| P10 | FEAT-AGT-05 | Run the agent evaluation harness | System | Scores each agent against a fixed set before any autonomy change. | E1 | A2.5 |
| P10 | FEAT-AGT-06 | Publish the agent monitoring dashboard | User | Shows acceptance, override, latency and cost per agent. | E1 | A2.6 |

secs.h: A2.1 Set up the agent platform with the gateway and prompt store

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Sets up the agent runtime, the model gateway, the prompt and policy store and the tool gateway.

**Problem.** Officers gather and check facts by hand before every decision.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent fallback rate | Below 10 percent | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Sets up the agent runtime, the model gateway, the prompt and policy store and the tool gateway.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a load, an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |
| 2 | System | Set up the agent platform with the gateway and prompt store | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed |

**Integration points.** Model gateway, ACE

**Prerequisites.** None

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** The outbound adapters: the WIN registered-mail notice file (INT-14, JOB-10), the reporting extract to the data lake and Power BI (INT-19, JOB-15), the decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the data lake (INT-20, JOB-13), and the debt buyer data tape (INT-25). One outbound pattern: build from Workbench tables and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, send through the outbox (JOB-11), acknowledge, retry, exception queue. Duplicate detection for every consumed event, including EV-26 AceDataReady. Use of the ACE outbound paths for NSS, LINE OA and the PII, audit and SOC logs.

**Out of scope.** Every inbound source load: ALS, SCBPDM, EFS, COLLINS scores, LIT, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, WIN proof of delivery, GL write-off postings, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID land in ACE through ACE's ingestion (RWB-ACE-001) and are read through the views; the batch-complete record and the late-batch alert are P1 (EV-26, EV-27). GL write-off posting is not a Workbench file: the approved write-off raises EV-24 WriteOffApproved, the posting is made in GL, and the posted result is read back through `v_ace_write_off` (INT-16, into ACE). Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-RDF-21; FEAT-RDF-23; RWB-E1-069 (ACE source views, for the data an outbound file reads)

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; source data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded, copied or written (D-RCV-35, ADR-010); P2 has no inbound adapter; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section | Status v3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P2 | FEAT-RDF-21 | Run the integration adapters for outbound files | System | Provides the one pattern every outbound file uses, with checks, retry and an exception queue. v2 name: "for file loads and outbound files"; the file-load half is removed by D-RCV-35. | E1 | A2.1 | Rescoped |
| P2 | FEAT-RDF-23 | Queue and retry a failed interface call | System | Holds an outbound call when the target system is unavailable and retries it on the interface schedule. | E1 | A2.2 | Kept |
| P2 | FEAT-RDF-24 | Raise an interface failure to the exception queue | System | Moves a call that has used its retries to the exception queue and raises a task for the platform team. | E1 | A2.3 | Kept |
| P2 | FEAT-DRI-09 | Run the file adapters for sources outside COLLINS | System | Removed by D-RCV-35 - later home: ACE ingestion. ACE ingests CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, WIN and GL. | E1 | A2.4 | Removed |
| P2 | FEAT-DRI-10 | Run outbound file and SFTP adapters | System | Moves bulk data out by file where the target has no API. v2 name: "Run file and SFTP adapters"; the inbound pickup is removed by D-RCV-35. | E1 | A2.5 | Rescoped |
| P2 | FEAT-DRI-11 | Route every outbound file through the integration adapters | System | Puts every outbound file through one adapter, so retries, logging and throttling are in one place. | E1 | A2.6 | Kept |
| P2 | FEAT-DRI-13 | Detect and ignore a duplicate event | System | Recognizes an event that has already been processed by its key, and records the repeat without acting twice. | E1 | A2.7 | Kept |
Each system is reached by hand or by a one-off file; failures are found late. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench no longer receives files: ACE ingests the sources, and the Workbench only sends.

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale. Freshness comes from the ACE batch record, `v_ace_batch_status`.

secs.h: A2.1 Run the integration adapters for outbound files

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Provides the one pattern every outbound file uses: build from Workbench tables and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, send through the outbox, acknowledge, retry and exception queue. The file-load half of the v2 pattern is removed by D-RCV-35 - later home: ACE ingestion.

**Problem.** Each system is reached by hand or by a one-off file; failures are found late.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|

**Functional overview.** Provides the one pattern every outbound file uses: build from Workbench tables and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, send through the outbox, acknowledge, retry and exception queue. The file-load half of the v2 pattern is removed by D-RCV-35 - later home: ACE ingestion.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Case record, CMMN state, queues, allocation, timers, the rules component.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-ACA-12; FEAT-ACA-15; FEAT-CHO-01; FEAT-CHO-01, FEAT-CWC-04; FEAT-CHO-06; FEAT-CWC-01; FEAT-CWC-02; FEAT-CWC-03

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; source data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010); a link to an ACE record is a business key with no foreign key; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1). The features that read Tier 2 views (`v_ace_batch_status`, `v_ace_party_product`, `v_ace_credit_decision`) stay behind their flags until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale. Freshness comes from the ACE batch record, `v_ace_batch_status`.

The module reads ACE through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views only. A direct read of a `public` table, a copy of a source record or a foreign key into ACE is a defect (Tier Map section 9).

| What P3 needs | View | Key the Workbench holds | Replaces (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Account, days past due, balances, classification, tdr_flag, booked settlement, `data_as_of` | `v_ace_account` | `case_account.account_key`, `case_list_row.account_key`, `case_entry_exclusion.account_key` | `loan_account`, `case_account.account_id` |
| Customer, deceased flag, masked identity number | `v_ace_customer` | `recovery_case.primary_person_key`, `case_party.person_key` | `party`, `primary_customer_id`, `case_party.party_id` |
| Borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles | `v_ace_ca_relation` | `account_key` + `person_key` | `party` roles from the load |
| Phone, email, address | `v_ace_contact` | `contact_key` (`contact_type:key`) | `contact_point` |
| Collateral and asset | `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_asset` | `account_key` | `collateral`, `account_collateral` |
| Collections contact and promise history | `v_ace_efs_action` | `account_key` | `collections_history` |
| Restructure plan status | `v_ace_plan` | plan reference | ACE common module read |
| Customer's other products | `v_ace_party_product` (Tier 2) | `person_key` | `party_product` |
| NLEADS credit result | `v_ace_credit_decision` (Tier 2) | treatment reference | `treatment.nleads_ref`, `credit_result`, `credit_result_reason`, `credit_result_at` |
| Batch business date and completion | `v_ace_batch_status` (Tier 2) | none | `load_run`, COLLINS LoadCompleted |
| Workbench flags about an ACE record | `recovery.party_ext`, `recovery.account_ext` | `person_key`, `account_key` | `party.fraud_flag` and Workbench columns on the copy tables |

**Trigger.** When the ACE batch record for ALS reaches status `COMPLETED` for the expected business date, EV-26 AceDataReady is raised and JOB-02 case creation, JOB-04 reconciliation, JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation start for that business date. If the cut-off passes first, EV-27 AceDataLate is raised. No P3 job reads a file or loads a row. JOB-01 and JOB-09 are retired.

**Case list.** SCR-02 and every queue view read the case, queue and owner from Workbench tables and the account columns (account number, days past due, balance, data as of) from `v_ace_account` by `case_list_row.account_key`. Reconciliation of the case list to `v_ace_account` is `reconciliation_result` (JOB-04); a business key with no ACE row is listed by REC-05.

**Links.** Each link is a `varchar(255)` business key with no foreign key, because ACE deletes on `account` cascade. Referential integrity is checked by the read model and by REC-05, not by the database.

secs.h: A2.52 Accept a queue placement from a model or an agent

secs.t:
**Business objective.** A caller that is not the allocation engine may place a case on a queue. The queue's own allocation, caseload and permission rules still apply, and the placement is logged with the caller and the model version. Disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists.

**Problem.** Cases are run from team spreadsheets; ownership and deadlines are agreed by email.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cases inside the service level | Set with DL22 | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** A caller that is not the allocation engine may place a case on a queue. The queue's own allocation, caseload and permission rules still apply, and the placement is logged with the caller and the model version. Disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: the ACE batch-complete record (EV-26), an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |
| 2 | System | Accept a queue placement from a model or an agent | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed |

**Integration points.** Workbench

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-CWC-04

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Store, index, OCR, classification, extraction, review queue, retention, custody.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-CWC-23; FEAT-DCM-01; FEAT-DCM-02; FEAT-DCM-07; FEAT-DCM-07, FEAT-DCM-03; FEAT-DCM-08; FEAT-DCM-09; FEAT-DCM-10

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-01 | Store documents with a write-once container for legal types | System | Holds every case document in blob storage, with legal types written to a container that cannot be overwritten. | E1 | A2.1 |

| P5 | FEAT-DCM-05 | Search documents within a case | User | Finds any document on the case by type, date or extracted field, in seconds. | E1 | A2.5 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-06 | Search documents across cases | User | Searches the whole document index across cases, for audit, legal and recovery questions. | E1 | A2.6 |

| P5 | FEAT-DCM-09 | Extract fields from the six document types | System | Pulls the agreed fields out of each typed document and writes them into the index with a confidence score. | E1 | A2.9 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-10 | Send a low-confidence extraction to the review queue | System | Routes any extraction below the confidence threshold to a person instead of writing it to the case. | E1 | A2.10 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-11 | Check a low-confidence extraction | User | Lets a person confirm or correct the extracted fields, which also feeds the extraction evaluation. | E1 | A2.11 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-12 | Attach an OCR-read document to its case automatically | System | Matches a read document to its case and attaches it with no person involved. | E1 | A2.12 |

| P5 | FEAT-DCM-17 | Apply retention classes to stored documents | Admin | Sets the retention class on each document type and applies it through the document life. | E1 | A2.17 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-18 | Virus scan every document on intake | System | Scans every inbound document before it is stored, and quarantines anything that fails. | E1 | A2.18 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-19 | Keep the Workbench document hub as the system of record for documents | System | Writes the document to the Workbench document hub as the record and holds only the index and the working copy in the Workbench. | E1 | A2.19 |
| P5 | FEAT-DCM-20 | Version a document and keep its history | System | Keeps every version of a document with the date and the source, so a superseded version is still readable. | E1 | A2.20 |

secs.h: A2.1 Store documents with a write-once container for legal types

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Holds every case document in blob storage, with legal types written to a container that cannot be overwritten.

**Problem.** Documents are in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fields extracted without review | Rising each month | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Holds every case document in blob storage, with legal types written to a container that cannot be overwritten.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |

**Business objective.** Routes any extraction below the confidence threshold to a person instead of writing it to the case.

**Problem.** Documents are in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fields extracted without review | Rising each month | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Routes any extraction below the confidence threshold to a person instead of writing it to the case.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a load, an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |
| 2 | System | Send a low-confidence extraction to the review queue | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed |

**Integration points.** Workbench

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-DCM-09

| REQ-DCM-009 | Documents arrive from branches, the mailroom, partner file transfer and email through the same intake. | Must | E1 |
| REQ-DCM-010 | Every document carries a retention class, and intake runs a virus scan before the document is stored. | Must | E1 |

| REQ-DCM-015 | New scope. Documents are backed up on a stated schedule, and a restore is tested before the first production release and at each subsequent release. | Must | E1 |
| REQ-DCM-016 | New scope. A legal hold applied to a case or a document stops deletion and expiry for as long as the hold is in place, overriding the retention class. | Must | E1 |

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-ACA-04; FEAT-CHO-06; FEAT-COM-01; FEAT-DCM-06; FEAT-DCM-17; FEAT-DCM-19; FEAT-DRI-15; FEAT-DRI-16

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Recommendation with reasons, approval within delegation, decision log store and writer.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-ACA-06; FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-APD-01, FEAT-DRI-14; FEAT-APD-02; FEAT-CWC-13; FEAT-CWC-23; FEAT-DRI-01; FEAT-DRI-02

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| P7 | FEAT-DRI-05 | Block an action when the decision log write fails | System | Stops the action and raises an incident when the log entry cannot be written. No action proceeds unlogged. | E1 | A2.5 |

| P7 | FEAT-APD-03 | Change a recommendation before approving | User | Lets the approver change the terms within their limit, and records what changed and why. | E2 | A2.17 |

secs.h: A2.1 Store decision log entries append-only and hash-chained

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decisions within the delegation of authority | 100 percent | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Holds every decision entry in a store that cannot be altered, with each record hashed to the one before it.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a load, an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |

| VR-P7-001-3 | A decision input is past its age limit | MSG-P7-006 {input} is {days} days old, past its limit. Refresh it before you decide. |
| BR-P7-001 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | None |

| Role | Use |
|---|---|
