| Internal audit, Compliance and PDPA officer | Also uses |

| AC ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then | Story |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-P7-001-01 | Append only | an entry with chain_seq 1 and final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" is stored for case "RW-2026-000123" | an UPDATE setting final_call to "CASE_TRANSFERRED" and a DELETE of the entry are attempted through the ACE service's database role and again through the schema owner role | all four statements are refused: by the missing grant for the service role, and with "decision_log_entry is append only" from tr_declog_append_only for the schema owner And the entry is unchanged And the refused attempts are written to the ACE audit log with the table, the operation and the entry ID | RWB-E1-008 |

| AC ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then | Story |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-ALT-P7-001-01 | Hash chain | 100 entries are appended | the chain verifier runs from chain_seq 1 to 100 | every entry_hash equals the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form And every prev_hash equals the entry_hash of the entry before it, and the first prev_hash is 64 zeros And the result holds count 100, last chain_seq 100 and that entry's entry_hash | RWB-E1-008 |
| AC-ALT-P7-001-02 | Seven field groups | an entry is appended for decision "D6" on case "RW-2026-000123" with rule "R-UNI-14", rule version "UNI-2026.11", inputs reference "inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a", recommendation, approver "U-6101", approval level "L6", final call "APPROVED", actions and outcome | it is read with GET /decision-log/{entryId} | the response holds inputsRef, ruleId and ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId and approvalLevel, finalCall, actions and outcome And decidedAt, prevHash and entryHash are present | RWB-E1-008 |

| AC ID | Scenario | Given | When | Then | Story |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-EXC-P7-001-01 | A failed append leaves nothing behind | the database connection for the store is closed in the test double | a writer appends an entry inside a transaction that also changes the case owner | DecisionLogUnavailableException is raised And no entry is stored, the case owner is unchanged and chain_seq is not used | RWB-E1-008 |
| AC-EXC-P7-001-02 | Role without the right | A user without the right in the capability area | They try the action | Refused with MSG-P4-002; nothing changes | All |
| AC-EXC-P7-001-03 | Decision cannot be recorded | The decision log store is unavailable | The action is taken | Nothing changes; MSG-P7-003; incident raised | All |

| AC ID | Event | Trigger | How often | What happens | Expected result | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-BG-P7-001-01 | Hash chain check | Schedule | Nightly | Checks the decision log chain | Break reported the same day | The log can be relied on in audit |

**Business objective.** Produces demand, recall and guarantor notices from Legal-approved templates and sends them to WIN.

**Problem.** Why a route was chosen, who approved it and on what figures is spread across emails and files.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decisions within the delegation of authority | 100 percent | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Produces demand, recall and guarantor notices from Legal-approved templates and sends them to WIN.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a load, an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |
| 2 | System | Generate notices from approved templates to WIN | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed |

**Integration points.** WIN, Workbench

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-DRI-15

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Payment and proceeds matching, fees, posting files.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-CWC-23; FEAT-OCC-10; FEAT-PAY-01; FEAT-PAY-04; FEAT-PAY-06; FEAT-PAY-07; FEAT-RDF-11

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Payment, account and write-off data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). A link to an ACE record is a business key with no foreign key. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-01 | Match a payment to a plan installment | System | Matches money received in `v_ace_payment` to the installment it pays and updates the plan position. | E2 | A2.1 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-02 | Hold an unmatched payment on the exception list | System | Puts money that matches no plan, sale or lot on the exception list for the reconciliation agent; a payment in `v_ace_payment` with no proceeds row is a REC-04 break. | E2 | A2.2 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-03 | Match a settlement payment | System | Matches a settlement payment read through `v_ace_payment` to the treatment and closes the money side. | E4 | A2.3 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-04 | Match auction and enforcement proceeds | System | Matches money from an auction, a broker or the LED, read through `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_npa_sale`, to the right case. | E4 | A2.4 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-05 | Calculate fees and charges | System | Works out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data. | E4 | A2.5 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-06 | Post a settlement booking to ALS | System | Writes the agreed settlement terms to ALS and reads the booked position back through `v_ace_account` after the next ACE batch. | E4 | A2.6 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-07 | Post to the general ledger | System | Posts the accounting entries for settlements, sales and write-offs to the ledger. | E4 | A2.7 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-08 | Produce provision inputs | System | Builds the provision inputs Finance needs from the case and asset positions. | E6 | A2.8 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-09 | Run the deed in lieu rental auto-debit | System | Takes the rental by auto-debit, issues the receipt and follows up arrears. | E4 | A2.9 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-10 | Apply proceeds to the case balance | System | Applies every receipt read through `v_ace_payment` to the balance in the order the policy sets. | E4 | A2.10 |
| P8 | FEAT-PAY-11 | Reconcile money movements daily | System | Compares what the Workbench matched to the ALS position read through `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account`, and to the ledger, every day; this is REC-04. | E4 | A2.11 |
Payments are matched to plans and settlements by hand; broken plans are found late.

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale. Freshness comes from the ACE batch record, `v_ace_batch_status`.

The module reads ACE through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views only. A direct read of a `public` table, a copy of a source record or a foreign key into ACE is a defect (Tier Map section 9).

| What P8 needs | View | Key the Workbench holds | Replaces (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Payments and receipts, amount, date and channel | `v_ace_payment` | `proceeds.payment_code` | `account_payment`, the ALS payment load |
| Account balance, classification and booked settlement | `v_ace_account` | `proceeds.account_key` | `loan_account` |
| Write-off posting and GL product | `v_ace_write_off` (Tier 2) | `write_off.write_off_key` | the GL file load |
| Asset sale price and taxes | `v_ace_npa_sale` (Tier 2) | `asset_sale.asset_key` | the AMIS file |
| Batch business date and completion | `v_ace_batch_status` (Tier 2) | none | `load_run`, the ALS load report |
| Workbench state about an ACE account | `recovery.account_ext` | `account_key` | Workbench columns on the copy table |

**Trigger.** JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation start when the ALS batch for the expected business date is `COMPLETED` in `v_ace_batch_status` and EV-26 AceDataReady is raised. If the cut-off passes first, EV-27 AceDataLate is raised. No P8 job reads a file or loads a row.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** D6 route decision with COLLINS return by route and the route agent.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-AGT-01; FEAT-APD-02, FEAT-VAL-07; FEAT-APD-05; FEAT-CWC-11; FEAT-DRI-07; FEAT-RDF-01; FEAT-VAL-01; FEAT-VAL-02

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Appraisal, score and account data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). A link to an ACE record is a business key with no foreign key. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-01 | Order an appraisal when the last one is stale | System | Checks `valuation_ext.age_days` against the limit and raises the order to SVAF with no person involved. | E4 | A2.1 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-02 | Receive the appraisal value from SVAF | System | Reads the value and date from `v_ace_valuation` once ACE has ingested the SVAF result, links it by `asset_key`, and records the valuer in `valuation_ext`. | E4 | A2.2 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-03 | Flag appraisal outliers against market and last value | System | Compares the new value to the market and the previous value and flags the gap for a person. | E4 | A2.3 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-04 | Accept the appraisal value | User | Lets the case owner accept the value, which fixes the band the route decision runs on. | E4 | A2.4 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-05 | Call COLLINS for return by route | System | Reads the expected return on each route from `v_ace_score`, which ACE ingests from COLLINS, and records the answer with its model version. | E4 | A2.5 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-06 | Calculate the payoff and settlement range | System | Works out the payoff from the balances read through `v_ace_account` and the settlement range from the rules, with the floor applied. | E4 | A2.6 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-07 | Score the routes and recommend one with reasons | System | Runs the route agent, which recommends a route and states the reasons and the alternatives. | E4 | A2.7 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-08 | Approve a route inside the limit | User | Lets the case owner approve the recommended route within their delegated limit. | E4 | A2.8 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-09 | Approve a route above the limit at committee | User | Takes the route to the credit committee when it is beyond the case owner's limit. | E4 | A2.9 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-10 | Hold the case and set a review date | User | Lets the owner hold a case where no route is right yet, with a date the hold is reviewed. | E4 | A2.10 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-11 | Reconsider the route after new information | User | Reopens the route decision when a value, a payment or a deviation changes the picture. | E4 | A2.11 |
| S1 | FEAT-VAL-12 | Start the route flow and set its timers | System | Opens the chosen route, creates its tasks and starts its clocks. | E4 | A2.12 |
The route is chosen on officer judgment written up in an account plan.

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale. Freshness comes from the ACE batch record, `v_ace_batch_status`.

The module reads ACE through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views only. A direct read of a `public` table, a copy of a source record or a foreign key into ACE is a defect (Tier Map section 9).

| What S1 needs | View | Key the Workbench holds | Replaces (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SVAF appraisal value, date, type and forced sale value | `v_ace_valuation` (Tier 2) | `valuation_ext.valuation_key` | `valuation` |
| Collateral title, location, insurance and lien rank | `v_ace_collateral_detail` (Tier 2) | `asset_key` | the CCMS collateral copy |
| Expected return by route and model version | `v_ace_score` (Tier 2) | `score_key` | `score` |
| Payoff balance, classification and days past due | `v_ace_account` | `account_key` | `loan_account` |
| Accepted value, stale flag and age | `valuation_ext` | `valuation_key` | `valuation.accepted`, `valuation.stale_flag` |
| Batch business date and completion | `v_ace_batch_status` (Tier 2) | none | `load_run`, the SVAF load report |

**Trigger.** The staleness check runs on EV-26 AceDataReady for the expected business date, or on the case timer where the appraisal has aged since entry. The value is read only after ACE reports the SVAF batch `COMPLETED` in `v_ace_batch_status`. No S1 job reads a file or loads a row.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Treatment record, contracts, booking, plan timers.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-CHO-02; FEAT-CHO-06; FEAT-CHO-07, FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-DCM-12; FEAT-OCC-01, FEAT-TRT-04; FEAT-OCC-07

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Account, payment and EFS data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). A link to an ACE record is a business key with no foreign key. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |

| S2 | FEAT-TRT-07 | Send the offer and start the validity timer | System | Sends the offer to the customer and starts the validity clock. The wait is a timer, not a routed state. | E3 | A2.7 |
| S2 | FEAT-TRT-08 | Route the signed offer to operations for booking | System | Moves the case to operations when the customer signs inside the validity period. | E3 | A2.8 |
| S2 | FEAT-TRT-09 | Return the case to its prior status on no signature | System | Sends the case back to the status it held in COLLINS when the customer declines or the offer expires. | E3 | A2.9 |

| S2 | FEAT-TRT-11 | Detect and handle a broken plan | System | Counts missed payments read through `v_ace_payment` against the break rule and moves the case to the point the rule names. | E3 | A2.11 |
| S2 | FEAT-TRT-12 | Run a deed in lieu to ownership transfer | User | Takes the deed in lieu from offer through inspection, documents and transfer to the asset record. | E3 | A2.12 |

Restructures, settlements and deeds in lieu take 23 to 26 days and are tracked by hand.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** TCG and insurance claims, guarantor notices and pursuit.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-DCM-16; FEAT-GUA-01; FEAT-GUA-02; FEAT-GUA-03; FEAT-GUA-05; FEAT-OCC-01; FEAT-VAL-01

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |

| S3 | FEAT-GUA-01 | Prepare a TCG guarantee claim | System | Assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires. | E4 | A2.1 |

Guarantee and TCG claims are late because deadlines are not tracked.

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale.

secs.h: A2.1 Prepare a TCG guarantee claim

secs.t:
**Business objective.** Assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires.

**Problem.** Guarantee and TCG claims are late because deadlines are not tracked.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claims filed inside the deadline | 100 percent | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly |

**Functional overview.** Assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires.

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | Receives its trigger: a load, an event or a timer | Reads the version of the rules in force |
| 2 | System | Prepare a TCG guarantee claim | Applies the rules |
| 3 | System | Records the result | Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed |

**Integration points.** Workbench, TCG portal

**Prerequisites.** FEAT-DCM-16

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Notices, law firm instruction, hearings, judgment, enforcement.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-AGT-01; FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-CWC-11; FEAT-DCM-02; FEAT-DRI-14; FEAT-DRI-17; FEAT-LIT-04, FEAT-DCM-16; FEAT-LIT-05

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |

| S4 | FEAT-LIT-01 | Issue demand and recall notices | System | Produces and sends the statutory notices by rule, with no person in the path. | E5 | A2.1 |

| S4 | FEAT-LIT-12 | Recommend the next litigation step | System | Proposes the next step with reasons, for the officer or the approver to decide. | E5 | A2.12 |

| S4 | FEAT-LIT-19 | Follow the LED auction ladder | System | Tracks the enforcement auction through the 100, 90, 80 and 70 percent steps of official value. | E5 | A2.19 |
| S4 | FEAT-LIT-20 | Record an enforcement deferral with its reason | User | Lets the enforcement owner defer with a coded reason and a review date. Enforcement after judgment has no owner today. | E5 | A2.20 |

Litigation takes 21 days to file; packs are incomplete and law firm progress is not tracked.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Asset record, holding, floor price, listing, auction rounds, RAMC.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-AST-01; FEAT-AST-05; FEAT-AST-07; FEAT-AST-10; FEAT-AST-11; FEAT-AST-12; FEAT-AST-13

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Asset, sale and valuation data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). The Workbench links to an ACE asset by `asset_key` with no foreign key. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Lot building, data room, buyer terms, award, transfer.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-DBS-01; FEAT-DBS-03; FEAT-DBS-04; FEAT-DBS-06; FEAT-DBS-08; FEAT-DBS-09; FEAT-DBS-11

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** Eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-APD-02; FEAT-CWC-14; FEAT-DBS-09; FEAT-DCM-17; FEAT-DRI-07; FEAT-PAY-01; FEAT-WOF-01; FEAT-WOF-03

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module; data through COLLINS and file loads; every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-01 | Run the monthly eligibility scan on both tracks | System | Scans the portfolio each month against the eligibility rules and proposes the write-off population. | E6 | A2.1 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-02 | Apply the tax criteria | System | Tests each proposed account against the tax criteria and records the result. | E6 | A2.2 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-03 | Prepare the write-off pack | System | Assembles the committee pack from the case facts, the documents and the recovery history. | E6 | A2.3 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-04 | Remove a case from the proposed population | User | Lets the write-off team take a case out of the population before committee, with a reason. | E6 | A2.4 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-05 | Route the population to the committee and schedule it | System | Sends the pack to the committee queue and books it into the monthly meeting. | E6 | A2.5 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-06 | Approve a write-off inside the limit | User | Lets the committee approve within its delegation and records the limit applied. | E6 | A2.6 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-07 | Reject a write-off | User | Lets the committee reject, with a reason that returns the case to recovery. | E6 | A2.7 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-08 | Defer a write-off | User | Lets the committee defer with a review date, and holds the case until then. | E6 | A2.8 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-09 | Post an approved write-off | System | Posts the write-off to ALS and the general ledger and releases the provision. | E6 | A2.9 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-10 | Send provision inputs to Finance | System | Produces the provision file Finance needs from the posted population. | E6 | A2.10 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-11 | Reconcile the approved and posted populations | System | Compares what the committee approved to what was posted, and raises every difference. | E6 | A2.11 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-12 | Work the write-off exception loop | User | Opens the exception path for a case the rules cannot clear. This loop has no owner today. | E6 | A2.12 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-13 | Close the case after the retention period | System | Closes the case once the retention period has run and no action is open. | E6 | A2.13 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-14 | Change the eligibility or tax criteria | Admin | Lets the center of excellence change the criteria as a versioned rule load. | E6 | A2.14 |
| S7 | FEAT-WOF-15 | Record a customer payment after charge-off | System | Takes a payment on a charged-off balance, applies it and records the recovery. | E6 | A2.15 |

Write-off populations are assembled by hand each month.

- The user holds a Workbench role with the right in the capability area of the screen or action.
- The data products the module reads carry today's business date, or show their date as stale.

secs.h: A1.1 Scope of work and deliverables
secs.t:
**In scope.** X1 to X7: screening, pause, handling, return.

**Out of scope.** Collections before day 90 on EFS; booking in the core bank, which the officer does; work owned by other modules, reached through their interfaces.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-AGT-08; FEAT-APD-07; FEAT-CWC-03; FEAT-CWC-12; FEAT-DVF-01; FEAT-DVH-01; FEAT-DVH-02; FEAT-DVH-04

**Constraints.** Built in the ACE service as part of the recovery module. Customer, contact, legal and appraisal data is read from the ACE database through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views and is never loaded or copied (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). Workbench flags about an ACE customer stay in `party_ext`, keyed by `person_key`. Every value a business person may change is a versioned data row (principle 1).

| Module | Feature code | Feature name | Kind | Description | First in | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| S8 | FEAT-DVH-05 | Apply a contact stop for X1 to X3 | System | Stops outbound contact on a disputed, vulnerable or deceased case, and holds it until the stop is lifted. | E2 | A2.5 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVH-06 | Clear a deviation and resume the timers | System | Records the outcome, lifts the stop and resumes the stage clock at the state the case paused in. | E2 | A2.6 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVH-07 | Screen for deviations with the agent at L1 on one segment | System | Runs the deviation screening agent live at autonomy level 1 on one segment, with its flags visible. | E2 | A2.7 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVH-08 | Review a flagged deviation below the confidence threshold | User | Puts a low-confidence flag in front of a person before it changes the case. | E2 | A2.8 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVH-09 | Handle two deviations on one case | System | Holds more than one open deviation on a case, each with its own owner, and resumes only when all are cleared. | E2 | A2.9 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-01 | Run X1 dispute and complaint end to end | User | Takes the dispute from detection through the evidence pack to resolution and the return point. | E7 | A2.10 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-02 | Run X2 vulnerability and hardship end to end | User | Takes the case to the specialist queue with contact limits, through to the hardship decision. | E7 | A2.11 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-03 | Run X3 deceased customer end to end | User | Stops contact, notifies heirs, files the insurance claim and settles the estate position. | E7 | A2.12 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-04 | Run X4 fraud end to end | User | Refers to the fraud team, tracks the investigation and routes the case on the outcome. | E7 | A2.13 |

| S8 | FEAT-DVF-06 | Run X6 lost contact and skip trace end to end | System | Runs the skip trace through the bureau, internal data and agency sources and routes on the result. | E7 | A2.15 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-07 | Run X7 collateral event end to end | User | Files the insurance claim, re-appraises the collateral through `v_ace_valuation` and `valuation_ext`, and returns the case to the route decision. | E7 | A2.16 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-08 | Review an override | User | Puts overrides in front of the review forum, with the reason and the outcome of each. | E7 | A2.17 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-09 | Match a complaint to the preceding contact | User | Links each complaint to the contact that caused it, which is how conduct is measured. | E7 | A2.18 |
| S8 | FEAT-DVF-10 | Handle a contact sent while a block is on | User | Opens the breach path when a message goes out against a contact stop. | E7 | A2.19 |
Complaints, hardship, death, fraud, bankruptcy, lost contact and collateral events are handled case by case with no clock.

**Dependencies.** FEAT-AST-07; FEAT-CWC-23; FEAT-DCM-21; FEAT-OCC-13; FEAT-PAY-01; FEAT-PRM-02; FEAT-PRM-03; FEAT-PRM-05

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Lean BRD, Epic 1

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench lean BRD, Epic 1
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, lean
Release | 30 November 2026
Status | For business scope approval

An account that reaches 90 days past due waits for the weekly manual transfer file at day 91 and is first worked at about day 100. For about ten days the case has no owner and no clock. There is no single case list: each team keeps its own Excel and SharePoint lists, 42 applications hold parts of a case and none owns it, and 650 action codes have no agreed meaning. Documents are kept outside the case, so a gap in a filing set is found on the court date. Approvals are replies to email and cannot be counted.

Baseline | Figure today
Accounts at 90 days past due or more, 30 June 2026 (DL15) | 28,119: Mortgage 12,256, hire purchase 12,960, SSME 2,903
New accounts reaching 90 days past due | 3,110 a month; 15 percent growth a year assumed (DL15)
Mapped recovery steps run in Excel | 40.5 percent
Hand-off points on one case; email hand-offs | 310, of which 191 pass through three or more people; 346
Litigation filings that breach their service level | 30 to 40 percent
Time to resolution | 380 days
Open audit findings and fraud cases in recovery | 50

Epic 1, Foundation 1, releases on 30 November 2026. The bank has one case list for every account at 90 days past due or more, reconciled each day to ALS. Every case has a case ID, a queue, an owner set by rule, timers and a prescription date. Documents are found by case. Every case creation, assignment, transfer and document attachment is in the decision log with the rule version that caused it. The case record view is read only; there are no workflow screens.

Administration and control roles receive real users: center of excellence analyst, data steward and data product owner, internal audit, compliance and PDPA officer, platform administrator, reference data administrator and security administrator. Business roles follow in Epic 2 (DL39). The stories serve data product owners first (10), then product owners, case owners and litigation officers (8 each) and team managers (7).

Mortgage, hire purchase and SSME. Product differences are reference data keyed by product. Source data is read from the ACE database through the 30 read-only recovery.v_ace_* views. The Workbench adds no source data, no staging table and no tracker load; the four extension tables hold only Workbench decisions, keyed by ACE business keys (D-RCV-35, ADR-010).

Module | Capability
P1 Recovery data engine | 14 data products with owners, read from ACE through 30 read-only v_ace_* views. No source load, staging table or tracker load. Freshness from the ACE batch record (v_ace_batch_status). Interaction ledger. Daily reconciliation to the ACE account view.
P2 Integration | One pattern for outbound files with checks, retry and an exception queue. Scheduled jobs with monitoring and run books. Feature flags.
P3 Case and workflow | Case created by rule with case ID. Roles, teams and queues as data. Allocation, assignment and transfer by rule. Service levels, timers, escalation, prescription dates. Daily rebalancing. Read-only case record view with timeline.
P4 Access and administration | Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication. Role to permission matrix as data. Masking by role. Delegation of authority table. Access log and break-glass.
P5 Document hub | Store and index with write-once storage for legal types. One intake from branches, mailroom, partner file transfer and email. OCR, classification into six types, field extraction, review queue. Checklist per case type. Retention class and virus scan.
P6 Communications | Templates and merge fields as versioned data with the Legal approval. Demand, recall and guarantor notices generated.
P7, P9, P10 | Append-only, hash-chained decision log. Baseline measures in Power BI. Case intake and deviation screening agents scored in shadow; no user sees their output.

Excluded from Epic 1 | Where it is done
Queue, transfer and approval screens; hand-over with full EFS history; letter dispatch, SMS and LINE; payment matching; steering dashboard; business users | Epic 2
Deviation screening on live cases | Epic 2; end to end in Epic 7
Settlement and deed in lieu to booking; asset record and listing | Epic 3
The route decision D6 and the 448 routing rules | Epic 4 (DL24)
Litigation with law firms on the partner portal | Epic 5
Debt sale, write-off and the partner panel | Epic 6
Full administration, agent autonomy step-ups, regulatory returns | Epic 8
Excel and SharePoint tracker inventory, load and retirement | Cutover and Go Live Plan (U5; E1-005, E1-010, E1-012 removed)
Collections before 90 days past due (D1 to D4); bank policy changes | Not in the Workbench: EFS and the ACE collection module; the policy owners

An account enters recovery at 90 days past due (DL16). The case is created by rule from the daily case list, which reads v_ace_account.

Accounts that are deceased, under fraud review, bankrupt, on an active restructure plan or in an open dispute are excluded at creation. The exclusion list is reference data owned by Risk.

One case covers one customer and one product, with its accounts linked (DL17).

The case ID has the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN, is issued once, never reused and printed on every letter. Only the Workbench stores it; the account number joins it to other systems (DL21).

secs.h: 3.2 Case status and how a case moves
secs.t:
A case holds one status at a time. Epic 1 builds all eight. In Epic 1 a case moves from New to Assigned; the other moves are used from Epic 2.

Status | Meaning | Moves to
New | Created at 90 days past due with its history; no owner yet | Assigned, when the allocation rule matches
Assigned | Owner and queue set by rule; the stage clock starts | In progress, when the first task starts
In progress | The owner or the Workbench is working a task | A waiting status, when an offer, instruction or approval request goes out
Waiting customer | Offer, notice or request with the customer; validity timer runs | In progress, on reply or timer expiry
Waiting partner | Instruction with a partner; service level timer runs | In progress, on result or timer expiry
Waiting approval | Recommendation with the approver the delegation of authority names | In progress, on decision or escalation
On hold | Paused by a deviation or legal hold; prescription clock keeps running | The status it paused in, or Closed
Closed | Cured, settled, sold, or written off with recovery ended | No further action

A move the model does not define is refused and recorded with its reason. A change of queue or owner changes neither the status nor the clocks.

Every status change writes an event to the decision log and the interaction ledger.

Allocation reads product, region, exposure band, stage, route, deviation flag, segment and collateral type, applies the first matching row and always has a default row.

Assignment uses round robin, lowest load or a named owner, up to the caseload cap (DL23). Cases over the cap go to the overflow queue. A daily job rebalances unassigned and over-cap cases.

Transfer moves a case on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, or a manual request with a reason code.

Each queue and status has a service level and an escalation role (DL22). A breach alerts the escalation role and does not move the case. Prescription dates come from the legal periods table.

Exception | What happens
The case list differs from the ACE account view | The publish is held; tolerance is zero (DL25)
An account fails a reconciliation check | The account carries a reason code for the data product owner
A file fails after the retry limit | Exception queue, with a task for a named owner
A document is unmatched or below the confidence threshold | Review queue; the correction trains the model
The decision log entry cannot be written | The action does not proceed
A ledger write fails | An incident is raised; no entry is discarded
Access outside the authority matrix | Refused and recorded; emergencies use break-glass with approval
An ACE batch is late or missing | The case list waits and shows the last completed business date; the data steward is alerted; no Workbench catch-up load runs

Every rule, limit, threshold, template, name, queue, role, timer and route is a versioned data row, changed by a validated load with no code release (DT02).

A load is checked for schema, overlapping rows, unreachable rows, a missing default row and a set of test cases. A load that fails a check is refused.

Each version carries a valid from date, author and approver, and the previous version is restored by one action. The center of excellence analyst loads; the risk and model risk officer approves. One person may not hold both roles.

A policy owner decides a policy change. The Workbench applies it as a new data version.

Epic 1 loads allocation, assignment and transfer rules only (DL24).

The process architecture has 19 L1 processes, 84 L2 sub-processes and 247 L3 processes. Epic 1 touches these L3 processes.

L3 | L3 process | Today | After Epic 1 | Business owner
06.1.1 | Transfer case and history from EFS | Weekly file at day 91 | Case created by rule at 90 days past due | Recovery Strategy with Risk
06.1.2 | Track prescription deadlines | No date on a shared case record | Set at creation from the legal periods table | Recovery Strategy with Risk; Legal counsel
18.3.2 | Allocate work by rule | By hand from team lists | By rule, rebalanced daily | Shared operations
13.1.1 to 13.1.4 | Read, classify, check and attach documents | Kept outside the case | One intake; attached without a person | Shared operations; Legal
13.2.1 | Generate letters from templates | Typed from case files | Generated from approved templates | Shared operations; Legal counsel
13.3.1 | Apply retention rules | No class per document | Retention class; write-once legal types | Compliance
14.2.2, 14.2.3, 14.2.5 | Write and release rules; manage org, teams and queues | No rule tables; 650 codes | Versioned data with validation and rollback | Center of excellence
15.4.1, 15.4.3 | Reconcile to ALS; fix reconciliation breaks | No single list | Daily, zero tolerance, reason codes | Data steward and data product owner
16.5.1 | Apply PDPA access by role | Set per application | Matrix as data; masking; access log | Compliance
17.2.1 | Record one log entry per decision | In email | Hash-chained decision log | Center of excellence

Personal Data Protection Act: personal data masked by role and every read logged. Retention and masking per data product and document type come from Compliance (DL26); until then every personal field stays masked.

Records retention and legal hold: legal document types are held write-once, and a legal hold stops deletion. Compliance and Legal sign a records management position before the first production release.

Delegation of authority follows Regulation กกค.540031 as amended by กกค.690070, loaded as reference data (DL18).

Built inside ACE as a modular monolith with programmatic workflow; ACE sign-in, access control and audit are reused (DT07 to DT09).

Source data arrives through ACE ingestion. The Workbench reads it through read-only views and holds no load, staging or tracker table (D-RCV-35, ADR-010; DT12 superseded). There is no real-time feed today; same-day needs are named under DL06.

The document hub is the system of record for recovery documents (DT06).

Partner access needs an architecture change with one to three months lead time (DL03). No partner uses Epic 1.

Kanban delivery with a sponsor progress review every two weeks. Build from 2 November, SIT 16 to 20 November, UAT 23 to 27 November. A requirement that fails is switched off by its feature flag and the release goes ahead (DL34 sets the window).

ID | What is needed | From | Needed by | Decision | Decision owner, date
DEP-01, 02 | Recovery module place, merge rules and code owners in ACE | ACE team | 2 Nov | DL05, DL04 | K. Pipat, 29 Oct; K. Book, 29 Oct
DEP-03 | DEV and SIT deployment slots | ACE team | 6 Nov | DL35 | K. Tee, 6 Nov
DEP-05 | Monthly release window | SCB IT | 13 Nov | DL34 | SCB IT, 30 Oct
DEP-14 | ACE batch business date record (ace_batch_run) for account, payment and customer data, in addition to the existing ACE ingestion | ACE team | 21 Nov | D-RCV-35, DL43 | ACE team lead; scope 15 Nov, date under DL43
DEP-15 | ACE additions for CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, WIN, GL, COLLINS, SCBPDM, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID (RWB-ACE-001) | ACE team | 21 Nov | D-RCV-35, DL43 | ACE team lead; scope 15 Nov, date under DL43
DEP-16 | Masked test data in SIT and UAT | Data engineering | 13 Nov | DL26 | Compliance, 13 Nov
DEP-18 | Entra ID groups for the Workbench roles | SCB IT security | 9 Nov | DL40 | SCB IT security, 6 Nov
DEP-20 | Model endpoint and agent platform | Enterprise AI | 16 Nov | DL33 | CTO with Enterprise AI, 30 Oct
DEP-22 | OCR and extraction for the first document types | Autonomous Ops | 16 Nov | DL19 | Business lead with Legal, 6 Nov
DEP-26 | Business testers named | Business lead | 6 Nov | DL09 | K. Tee with K. Jao, 31 Oct

The Workbench reads ACE through the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views. It creates no inbound load, staging table or tracker load. The ACE team adds 14 tables, 12 columns and 80 source fields under RWB-ACE-001; the view grant, the four extension tables and the boundary test are in RWB-E1-069.

DL01 | Who grants access? | The application owner; role owners approve each grant | K. Tee | 28 Oct
DL02 | Who owns the application? | The Tribe lead; the ACE team as technical custodian | K. Tee with K. Bell | 28 Oct
DL15 | Base for sizing? | 28,119 accounts; 3,110 new a month; 15 percent growth | Data lead | 6 Nov
DL16 | Entry at 90 or 91 days past due? | 90 days past due | Business lead | 6 Nov
DL17 | What counts as one case? | One per customer per product | Product owner with the solution architect | 6 Nov

DL25 | Reconciliation tolerance? | Zero | Data lead | 6 Nov
DL27 | Storage, backup, legal hold, e-discovery? | ACE storage with write-once container and bank backup | Solution architect with Compliance | 13 Nov
DL28 | Owner of letter templates? | The document module; Legal approves wording | Product owner | 13 Nov
DL29 | Which EFS contact outcomes enter the ledger? | A named list for the collection period | Data lead with the business lead | 13 Nov
DL39 | Roles with real users per release? | Administration roles at Epic 1 | Business lead | 20 Nov
DL43 | Does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates? | Assume the scope is accepted; dates to confirm, and Tier 2 features stay behind their flags until the additions land | ACE team lead | 21 Nov

Case list reconciled to ALS through v_ace_account | No single case list | Zero variance five business days in a row; no break open beyond one day | 31 Dec 2026 | Data steward and data product owner
ACE batches complete on time, and the case list shows the latest business date | Baseline from the first month live | 99 percent | From 30 Nov 2026 | Data steward and data product owner
New cases assigned by rule | By hand from team lists | 100 percent | 31 Dec 2026 | Team managers
Team Excel and SharePoint lists retired | 40.5 percent of mapped steps in Excel | All retired or out of scope; retired after ten clean days in parallel under the Cutover and Go Live Plan retirement procedure (U5) | 13 Dec 2026 | Program manager

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Lean BRD, Epic 2

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench lean BRD, Epic 2
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, lean
Release | 31 December 2026
Status | For business scope approval

A case reaching 90 days past due arrives from collections by a weekly manual file at day 91 and is first worked at about day 100. Contact history found before day 90 does not travel with it. Hand-offs run by email, and a manager cannot see every case with its owner and age. Approvals are replies to email. Letters go out with no proof of delivery on the case, and payments are not matched to plans, so a broken plan is found late. Epic 1 gives one reconciled case list with no screens for business users.

Baseline | Figure today
Hand-off points on one case; email hand-offs | 310, of which 191 pass through three or more people; 346
Transfers of one litigation case | 58
Contactability | 40 percent
Litigation filings that breach their service level | 30 to 40 percent
Recovery rate on NPL, 2026 to date | 66.3 percent
Litigation, deed in lieu and restructure turnaround | 21, 26 and 23 working days

Epic 2, Foundation 2, releases on 31 December 2026 and completes the foundation. The case arrives the morning after it reaches 90 days past due with its contact and promise history and the customer's other products. Every case has one owner, a timer and one next action. Owners and managers work from queues on screen. Approvals route on the delegation of authority. Litigation notices are generated and approved in the Workbench. Letters go out with proof of delivery, and SMS and LINE with their result on the case. The steering committee reads the same numbers the teams work with.

Business roles receive real users (DL39): case owner, team manager, phone collector, litigation officer, capacity and workforce planner, product heads, Head of Litigation, risk and model risk officer, reporting and BI analyst, and the Tribe lead and squad members.

Module | Capability
P1, P2 Data and integration | Hand-over from EFS through the COLLINS load with full history. ACE plan status and the customer's other products on the case. Credit approval pack for NLEADS; booking confirmed from the next ALS load. Data products for treatments and plans. Queue write for models and agents, behind a flag.

secs.h: 3.2 Case status and how a case moves
secs.t:
The eight statuses from Epic 1 are all in use. Each case also carries a service level state (inside, approaching or past), a deviation flag, a queue and owner, and one next action with owner and due date, produced from the rule that moved the case.

Status | Meaning | Moves to
New | Created at 90 days past due with its history; no owner yet | Assigned, when the allocation rule matches
Assigned | Owner and queue set by rule; the stage clock starts | In progress, when the first task starts
In progress | The owner or the Workbench is working a task | A waiting status, when an offer, instruction or approval request goes out
Waiting customer | Offer, notice or request with the customer; validity timer runs | In progress, on reply or timer expiry
Waiting partner | Instruction with a partner; service level timer runs | In progress, on result or timer expiry
Waiting approval | Recommendation with the approver the delegation of authority names | In progress, on decision or escalation
On hold | Paused by a deviation or legal hold; prescription clock keeps running | The status it paused in, or Closed
Closed | Cured, settled, sold, or written off with recovery ended | No further action

An approval is waiting, approved, approved with changes within the approver's limit, rejected with a coded reason, or escalated. A rejected item returns to the point the route rule names.

A manual transfer or reassignment needs a reason code from the agreed list. The case keeps its status and clocks.

Cases of an owner who leaves, is absent beyond the threshold or is over the cap are reallocated inside the team (DL23).

A model or agent may place a case on a queue under a service identity with the same checks as a person. Its work and rule-allocated work share one queue order.

An approval goes to the approver the delegation of authority names for the decision, product and amount (DL18). Above the limit it is refused and raised to the next approver. A person may not approve a decision they proposed or prepared.

An override needs a coded reason, reported monthly. An unanswered approval escalates at its service level. The limit, rule version and approver are logged.

Demand and recall notices (D7.1) are the first decision approved this way.

Deviation | Handled by | Epic 2 rule
X1 Dispute or complaint | Complaint officer | Contact stop; complaint matched to the contact before it
X2 Vulnerable customer or hardship | Hardship and vulnerability specialist | Contact stop
X3 Deceased customer | Specialist, with Legal for estate claims | Contact stop
X4 Fraud | Fraud investigator | Referred to the fraud team; recovery action held
X5 Bankruptcy or external seizure | Legal counsel | Direct collection stops; claim deadline clock starts
X6 Lost contact | Agent, within policy | A new verified contact point clears it
X7 Collateral event | Agent proposes; a person approves the claim | Routed to its handler

A deviation pauses the stage clock, keeps the prescription clock running and does not replace the status. A code with no owner goes to the team manager and is recorded as unmapped.

A next action past its due date escalates like a service level breach. A case with no next action is reported as an exception.

A booking missing from the next ALS load creates a task. An unmatched payment goes to the exception list; a missed payment raises an event the next day.

Every outbound contact carries a conduct check result; a contact that fails is held.

Consent is held per channel. Withdrawn consent stops that channel; statutory notices continue.

The notice period runs from proof of delivery. Signature is electronic where Legal permits and wet ink where Legal requires.

Every rule, limit, threshold, template, name, queue, role, timer and route is a versioned data row, changed by a validated load with no code release (DT02).

A load is checked for schema, overlapping rows, unreachable rows, a missing default row and a set of test cases. A load that fails a check is refused.

Each version carries a valid from date, author and approver, and the previous version is restored by one action. The center of excellence analyst loads; the risk and model risk officer approves. One person may not hold both roles.

A policy owner decides a policy change. The Workbench applies it as a new data version.

A change to the delegation of authority is versioned, approved and dated; open items keep the version they were decided under.

NFR-051 | Agents run under service identities and are subject to the same role checks as people. | Service identities | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-052 | Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts. | No secrets in code or prompts | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-053 | Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. | Encrypted | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-054 | The build pipeline blocks a change that carries a secret, personal data in code, tests or logs, or an unapproved dependency. | Pipeline checks pass | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-055 | Agent outputs are schema checked against an allowed-action list with a confidence threshold, and fall back to rules when the check fails. | Schema check on every output | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-056 | Penetration testing and a security review are completed before the first production release. | Before the first production release and before the partner portal opens to users outside the bank | SCB IT security with the IT lead | Proposed, DL11

ISO/IEC 25010: Usability: operability. Tested by: UAT scripts in Thai and English.

ID | Requirement | Target | Owner | Status
NFR-057 | Document text is read and extracted in Thai and in English. | Thai and English | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-058 | Customer-facing documents and messages are produced in the customer's language. | Thai by default; English where the customer has chosen English | Legal counsel with Compliance | Proposed, DL10
NFR-059 | Screen labels, validation messages and error messages are available in Thai and in English. | Every screen, label and message in Thai and English | Business lead | Proposed, DL10

ISO/IEC 25010: Usability and compatibility. Tested by: Automated accessibility scan and a manual check on the main screens; browser and device test.

ID | Requirement | Target | Owner | Status
NFR-060 | Screens meet the bank's accessibility standard. | WCAG 2.1 level AA for every screen | Tech leads with the ACE team | Proposed, DL11
NFR-061 | Screens work on the browsers and versions the bank supports. | The current and previous major versions of Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome | IT lead | Proposed, DL11
NFR-062 | The field application captures evidence with no network connection and uploads when it reconnects. | Offline capture | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-063 | Partner-facing screens work on the devices partners actually use. | Desktop browsers as in NFR-061 and tablets for field and auction partners | Partner and agency manager | Proposed, DL11

ISO/IEC 25010: Maintainability: analysability. Tested by: Inject a failure in SIT and confirm the alert reaches the named owner within the target.

ID | Requirement | Target | Owner | Status
NFR-064 | Logs, traces and metrics are produced across the workflow, the decision service and the agents. | Across all three | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-065 | Business measures per decision are produced from the decision log and not from a separate count. | From the log | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-066 | Agent acceptance, override rate, latency and cost are measured and reported. | Measured per agent | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-067 | Every scheduled job has a run book, monitoring and an alert to the operations channel. | Every job | Solution architect | Proposed
NFR-068 | A failing interface, job or agent raises an alert to a named owner within its target. | Alert within 15 minutes to the named owner | Platform administrator | Proposed, DL11

secs.h: 4. Partner access from outside the bank
secs.t:
Item | Requirement
Route | Through the external gateway approved by the architecture team (DL03)
Identity | Partner identities separate from bank identities, with multi-factor authentication
Scope | Each partner user sees only the instructions placed with their firm
Lead time | One to three months from approval of the change
First needed | Valuers, auction vendors and RAMC at Epic 4; law firms and debt buyers at Epic 5; collection agencies at Epic 6
Owner | Architecture team, with the partner and agency manager for onboarding
Test | Penetration test and a load test at 50 partner users online before the portal opens

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Acceptance Criteria Glossary v1.xlsx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Acceptance Criteria Glossary v1

secs.t:
Keywords
Every acceptance criteria line starts with one of these words. The word tells you what the line is for. คำแรกของทุกบรรทัดบอกหน้าที่ของบรรทัดนั้น
Keyword | Reading label | ภาษาไทย | What the line is doing
Given | Setup | สิ่งที่ต้องมีอยู่ก่อน | What is already true before the test starts. It is not an action and nobody does it during the test.
When | Action | การกระทำ | The one action that starts the test. Each scenario has one When.
Then | Result | ผลที่ต้องได้ | What must be true after the action. A scenario can have many Then lines, and every one of them must hold.
Scenario | Scenario | สถานการณ์ทดสอบ | One case to prove. The AC number in the title, such as AC3, is how it is referred to elsewhere.

Sentence frames
The acceptance criteria repeat a small number of sentence patterns. Learn these and most lines read themselves. ประโยคในเกณฑ์ยอมรับใช้รูปแบบซ้ำกันไม่กี่แบบ
English pattern | ภาษาไทย | Example from a story
the system writes {X} | ระบบเขียน {X} | Then the system writes 12 dq_exception rows
the system writes {X} to {Y} | ระบบเขียน {X} ลงใน {Y} | Then the system writes the result to the decision log
the system writes {X} with {Y} | ระบบเขียน {X} พร้อมข้อมูล {Y} | Then the system writes one entry with rule ID "ALLOC-014"
the system writes no {X} | ระบบไม่เขียน {X} | Then the system writes no row
nothing is written | ไม่มีการเขียนข้อมูลใด | Then nothing is written
the system refuses {X} | ระบบไม่รับ {X} | Then the system refuses the load
the system refuses {X} in full | ระบบไม่รับ {X} ทั้งรายการ | Then the system refuses the load in full
refuses {X} with {MSG} | ไม่รับ {X} พร้อมข้อความ {MSG} | Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002
the system stores {X} | ระบบจัดเก็บ {X} | Then the system stores the document on case "RW-2026-000123"
the system raises {X} | ระบบแจ้ง {X} | Then the system raises an incident
the system sends {X} to {Y} | ระบบส่ง {X} ไปยัง {Y} | Then the system sends the file to the interface
the system holds {X} in {Y} | ระบบพัก {X} ไว้ใน {Y} | Then the system holds the 3 records in dq_exception
the system places the case in queue {Q} | ระบบจัดกรณีเข้าคิว {Q} | Then the system places the case in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
the system creates no {X} | ระบบไม่สร้าง {X} | Then the system creates no case for A-5002
the system returns {N} with {MSG} | ระบบคืนค่า {N} พร้อมข้อความ {MSG} | Then the system returns 409 with MSG-GEN-004
the system records {X} | ระบบบันทึก {X} | Then the system records the rollback with the caller and the time
the system publishes {X} | ระบบเผยแพร่ {X} | Then the system publishes the copy
the system retires {X} | ระบบยกเลิกการใช้ {X} | Then the system retires the old copy
the system gives the case to {U} | ระบบมอบกรณีให้ {U} | Then the system gives the case to U-03
the system does not {X} | ระบบไม่ {X} | Then the system does not start
the case moves to {STATE} | กรณีเปลี่ยนไปยังขั้นตอน {STATE} | Then the case moves to "IN_LITIGATION"
the case stays in {STATE} | กรณียังคงอยู่ในขั้นตอน {STATE} | Then the case stays in "NEW"
nothing changes | ไม่มีการเปลี่ยนแปลง | Then nothing changes
{X} is unchanged | {X} ไม่เปลี่ยนแปลง | Then the row counts are unchanged
{X} is in force | {X} มีผลบังคับใช้อยู่ | Given version "DOA-2026.11" is in force
{X} stays in force | {X} ยังคงมีผลบังคับใช้ | Then the version in force stays
{X} holds {N} rows | {X} มี {N} แถว | Then data_product holds 14 rows
{X} shows {Y} | {X} แสดง {Y} | Then the job monitor shows the failed step
the response is {N} | ผลตอบกลับคือ {N} | Then the response is 200
the build fails with "{msg}" | การ build ไม่ผ่าน พร้อมข้อความ "{msg}" | Then the build fails with "no data dictionary entry"
the test fails with "{msg}" | การทดสอบไม่ผ่าน พร้อมข้อความ "{msg}" | Then the test fails with "physical type date expected"
{X} passes | {X} ผ่าน | Then check "REC-08" passes
{X} fails | {X} ไม่ผ่าน | Then the pipeline stage fails
the user sees {X} | ผู้ใช้เห็น {X} | Then the user sees the case list
the officer sees {X} on the screen | เจ้าหน้าที่เห็น {X} บนหน้าจอ | Then the officer sees the queue on the screen
{X} is on the exception list | {X} อยู่ในรายการผิดปกติ | Then the payment is on the exception list
{X} is in the exception queue | {X} อยู่ในคิวรายการผิดปกติ | Then the item is in the exception queue
naming {X} | โดยระบุ {X} | Then the system refuses the load naming "business date"
with reason {R} | พร้อมเหตุผล {R} | Then the entry carries the reason "RULE_GAP"
for business date {D} | สำหรับวันที่ทำการ {D} | Then JOB-15 is rerun for business date 2026-11-27
within {N} seconds | ภายใน {N} วินาที | Then the screen opens within 2 seconds
at least {N} | อย่างน้อย {N} | Then at least 20 feedback entries are counted
at most {N} | ไม่เกิน {N} | Then the export holds at most 10,000 rows
no {X} | ไม่มี {X} | Then no instance is restarted
every {X} | {X} ทุกรายการ | Then every record passes the load checks
each {X} | {X} แต่ละรายการ | Then each row has exactly one owner
the same {X} | {X} เดียวกัน | Then the same call is refused
again | อีกครั้ง | When the pipeline runs again in SIT
{X} is not available | {X} ไม่พร้อมใช้งาน | Given the malware scan is not available
the timer starts | เริ่มนับเวลา | Then the timer starts
the timer ends on {D} | ครบกำหนดในวันที่ {D} | Then the timer ends on 2026-12-15
past its service level | เกินระยะเวลามาตรฐาน | Then the case is past its service level
{X} is approved | {X} ได้รับอนุมัติ | Given the treatment is approved
needs approval at level {L} | ต้องได้รับอนุมัติระดับ {L} | Then the item needs approval at level 3
exactly one {X} | {X} เพียงหนึ่งเดียว | Then each row has exactly one system of record

Words
The words that carry the meaning, in order of how often they appear in the acceptance criteria. คำที่พบบ่อยในเกณฑ์ยอมรับ
English | ภาษาไทย | Kind | What it means here

secs.h: RWB-ACE-001 ACE DB additions for the Recovery Workbench
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-ACE-001 |
| Owner | ACE team |
| Epic | ACE backlog, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | ACE ingestion and schema |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-26 ACE DB additions (ACE team) |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-002 |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U2); DL43 |
| Priority | Must - critical path for the 30 November release |
| Depends on | None. This story is first on the recovery critical path |
| Blocks | RWB-E1-069, RWB-E1-002, RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-018, every Tier 2 feature |
| Status | Ready for the ACE team estimate (DL43) |

As the **ACE team lead**, I want **the tables and columns that the recovery module needs but ACE does not hold added to the ACE database, ingested by the existing ACE ingestion and recorded with a business date**, so that **the recovery module reads one copy of source data through its views, and no recovery load or staging table is built**.

The recovery module reads source data from ACE (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). ACE already holds account, payment, customer, contact, collateral, the collateral asset, collections activity, assignment, bucket history, product, branch and holiday. It does not hold the appraisal, the CCMS collateral detail, the NPA asset and sale, the lawsuit and hearing, the proof of delivery, the GL write-off, the COLLINS score, the SCBPDM product holding, the NLEADS credit decision, the EasyApp signature reference or the Entra group mapping. It also lacks a per-source business date record and 12 columns on account, customer and efs_action.

This story adds exactly that: 14 tables, 12 columns and the batch record. It is the single dependency that unblocks the recovery data engine, and it is why DL43 is the top item on the programme risk log. Every field is listed in appendix A with its source, type and frequency, so the estimate is a table read, not a discovery.

- The ACE schema is at the common migration head (V026 at the time of writing).
- The ACE ingestion framework accepts a new source: a file or API contract, a staging-to-target mapper, a batch record writer and a unique business key per target table.
- The ACE DBA role that owns the schema is available for the migration window.
- The recovery role name and the view-owner role name are agreed with the Workbench environment design.
- Each source owner has confirmed the field list in appendix A: SVAF, CCMS, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS, SCBPDM, NLEADS, EasyApp and the Entra ID administrator.

1. ACE team: applies migration `V027__rwb_ace_001_recovery_source_additions.sql` in DEV. It creates 14 tables and adds 12 columns in one transaction.
2. ACE team: adds one ingestion job per source, each writing its target table and one `ace_batch_run` row per source and business date.
3. ACE team: runs the population check (AC2) against one full file per source, comparing the row count with the trailer.
4. ACE team: runs the ACE regression suite (AC6) and confirms no existing screen, job or report changes.
5. ACE DBA: grants SELECT on the listed tables to the view-owner role, and nothing else (AC4).
6. Recovery squad: creates the Section B views in RWB-E1-069 and reads them.
7. ACE team: repeats steps 1 to 5 in SIT, then PROD in the release window.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source file fails its trailer or checksum | The ingestion writes no row for that source and business date; `ace_batch_run` keeps the previous COMPLETED row as the latest | AC3 |
| X2 | A field in appendix A has no column after the migration | The conformance test fails and names the field ID | AC8 |
| X3 | A source re-sends a business date already loaded | The unique business key rejects the duplicate; the batch record keeps one row for that source and date | AC7 |
| X4 | A new column would change an existing ACE column type | The migration is rejected at review; new columns are additive only | AC1, AC6 |
| X5 | The view-owner role is granted more than SELECT | The grant check fails the security review | AC4 |
| X6 | The migration must be backed out | The down script drops the 14 tables and the 12 columns; no ACE row is touched | AC5 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs nothing from the recovery module; it is the first item on the critical path |
| Negotiable | The field list is fixed by appendix A; the ingestion design is the ACE team's choice |
| Valuable | Removes 14 tables and a load estate from the Workbench, and gives ACE one more complete source set |
| Estimable | 14 tables, 12 columns, 14 ingestion jobs, one grant, one conformance test |
| Small | One migration plus the ingestion jobs; the ACE team sizes it in DL43 |
| Testable | Eight criteria, each one automated test |

```gherkin
Feature: ACE DB additions for the Recovery Workbench

 Scenario: AC1 Tables and columns deployed
 Given the ACE schema at the common migration head
 When the ACE team applies V027__rwb_ace_001_recovery_source_additions.sql in DEV and then in SIT
 Then public holds the 14 new tables of section 11
 Then account holds 7 new columns, customer 3 and efs_action 2
 Then ace_batch_run has a primary key and the unique key (source_system, business_date)
 Then no existing ACE column is renamed, retyped or dropped

 Scenario: AC2 Every Workbench field is populated
 Given one full source file for each source in appendix A
 When ACE ingests each file for business date 2026-11-30
 Then all 80 appendix A fields hold a value or an explicit null
 Then the row count per target table equals the file trailer count

 Scenario: AC3 Business date and completion recorded
 Given the ALS file for 2026-11-30 is ingested and completes at 04:40
 When the recovery module reads v_ace_batch_status
 Then it returns ALS, 2026-11-30, COMPLETED, the record count and the completion time
 Then a failed run for 2026-12-01 leaves 2026-11-30 as the latest COMPLETED row for ALS

 Scenario: AC4 Read grant only
 Given the view-owner role agreed with the Workbench environment design
 When the ACE DBA applies the grant script
 Then the role may select the 14 new tables and no other table
 Then the 12 new columns on account, customer and efs_action are covered by the existing Tier 1 grant
 Then the role may not insert, update, delete or truncate any table

 Scenario: AC5 Reversible
 Given a copy of PROD with the migration applied
 When the down script runs
 Then the 14 tables and the 12 columns are gone
 Then account, payment, customer and efs_action row counts are unchanged

 Scenario: AC6 Existing ACE reads unaffected
 Given the ACE regression suite
 When it runs after the migration
 Then every existing screen, batch job and report passes
 Then the row counts of account, payment, customer and efs_action are unchanged

 Scenario: AC7 Idempotent reload
 Given a source file already ingested for 2026-11-30
 When the same file is ingested again
 Then no duplicate row is created
 Then ace_batch_run holds one row for that source and business date

 Scenario: AC8 Field appendix matches the migration
 Given the 80 rows of appendix A
 When the conformance test compares them with the deployed columns
 Then 80 of 80 resolve to a column of the right type
 Then no appendix row is missing and no extra mapped column exists
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every table carries `source_system`, `business_date` and `loaded_at`; the business date is the source business date, not the ingest date | D-RCV-35 U2; E1-015 |
| BR2 | Every table has a business key with a unique constraint; the Workbench links by that key and never by a generated id | D-RCV-35 U4 |
| BR3 | New columns on existing ACE tables are additive only; no existing column is renamed, retyped or dropped | D-RCV-35 U3 |
| BR4 | The batch record is one row per source and business date, written even when the source delivers zero rows | E1-015; E1-016 |
| BR5 | Selective grant: the view-owner role reads the listed tables and writes nothing | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-02 |
| BR6 | A field is in this story only if the Workbench needs it; a field the Workbench does not read is not added | appendix A |
None on a case. This story changes the ACE schema version (V026 to V027) and the ingestion job set (14 jobs added).

AC7 | Idempotent reload | Given a file already ingested for a business date, when it is ingested again, then no duplicate row exists and one batch row remains.

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

| By epic | E4: 1, E8: 21 |
| Related stories already in the Epic 1 and Epic 2 backlog | 10 |

User and role administration, reference data, rule versions, queue and timer configuration, job and ACE batch monitoring, and the audit log. Epic 1 builds the services and the reference and rule loads by file; these stories add the administration screens and approvals in Epic 8, when full administration is delivered, and partner administration in Epic 4.

Version 3 is re-based on D-RCV-35 and ADR-010. The Workbench loads no source data: the job monitor shows Workbench jobs beside the ACE batch status, the console shows reconciliation breaks, and masking profiles name the columns of the recovery.v_ace_* views. Two stories are rewritten around the read path (RWB-AD-018, RWB-AD-019) and one is a minor edit (RWB-AD-004).

secs.h: RWB-AD-001 Map Entra ID groups to Workbench roles
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic | E8, release 30 June 2027 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration |
| Feature | None |
| Process | All recovery processes |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-022 |
| Decision | DL40 |

**Story.** As a security administrator, I want each Entra ID group mapped to one Workbench role in each environment as a data row, so that a person gets their roles from the group the bank IAM grants, with no code change.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Map Entra ID groups to Workbench roles

 Scenario: AC1 Group gives the role
 Given the group RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN mapped to RW-CASEOWN
 When a member of the group signs in to SIT
 Then the session holds the role RW-CASEOWN

 Scenario: AC2 Unmapped group
 Given a person whose only group has no mapping
 When they sign in
 Then the system refuses they with MSG-P4-001 and the refusal is in the access log

 Scenario: AC3 Mapping change
 Given a new mapping version with a valid from date
 When the date arrives
 Then sessions from that date use the new mapping
```

**Data**

| Entity | Fields | BR Field IDs |
|---|---|---|
| decision_log_entry | id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version and 12 more | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 |
| role | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope | DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-038 |
| v_ace_iam_group | entra_group, role_code, source_system, data_as_of | DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304 |

**Endpoints**

| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| GET | /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions | Rules and parameters R |
| POST | /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions | Rules and parameters C |

**Screen and states**

| Screen | States |
|---|---|
| SCR-43 Roles and access | List; access log |

**Permission checks**

| Capability area | Right | Roles that hold it |
|---|---|---|
| Rules and parameters | R | RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE and 30 more |
| Rules and parameters | C | RW-COE |

**Validation and messages**

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Error | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-004 | Warning | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

**Test cases**

| ID | Covers | Test |
|---|---|---|
| TC-AD-001-01 | AC1 | Group gives the role |
| TC-AD-001-02 | AC2 | Unmapped group |
| TC-AD-001-03 | AC3 | Mapping change |
| TC-AD-001-04 | Access | A role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| TC-AD-001-05 | Principle 5 | A forced decision log write failure stops the action with MSG-P7-003 |

**Guardrails.** No value that a business person may change is written in code. No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. No read of another module's tables; ACE data only through recovery.v_ace_* views.

**Story.** As an application owner, I want the permission matrix of roles against the 14 capability areas loaded as a versioned file, so that a permission changes without a code release and every change has an approver.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Permission matrix as a versioned load

 Scenario: AC1 Load a matrix version
 Given a matrix file with every role and area
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then it passes the checks and waits for the application owner's approval

 Scenario: AC2 Incomplete matrix refused
 Given a file with a role missing
 When it is loaded
 Then the system refuses it in full with the missing role named

 Scenario: AC3 Takes effect on its date
 Given an approved version with a valid from date
 When the date arrives
 Then every endpoint checks against the new version
```

**Story.** As an application owner, I want each role given a scope of own cases, team, region or all as data, so that a person sees only the cases their role allows.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Scope per role
```

**Story.** As a risk and model risk officer, I want the autonomy level of each agent step held as data and changed only with committee approval, so that an agent never acts beyond what the committee approved.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
 Given step D6.3 at level L1
 When the route agent answers
 Then the system shows the answer as a recommendation and a person decides

 Scenario: AC2 Step up recorded
 Given a committee approval for L2
 When the new version takes effect
 Then the change shows the approval reference in the version
```

**Story.** As a Compliance and PDPA officer, I want retention classes by data product and document type, and legal holds that stop expiry, so that nothing is kept longer than its rule and nothing held is lost.

```gherkin
 Given a document past its retention period with no hold
```
