Acceptance criteria
Gherkin per story.
Key | Title | Gherkin
RWB-AD-001 | Map Entra ID groups to Workbench roles | Feature: Map Entra ID groups to Workbench roles   Scenario: AC1 Group gives the role  Given the group RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN mapped to RW-CASEOWN  When a member of the group signs in to SIT  Then the session holds the role RW-CASEOWN   Scenario: AC2 Unmapped group  Given a person whose only group has no mapping  When they sign in  Then the system refuses they with MSG-P4-001 and the refusal is in the access log   Scenario: AC3 Mapping change  Given a new mapping version with a valid from date  When the date arrives  Then sessions from that date use the new mapping
RWB-AD-002 | Permission matrix as a versioned load | Feature: Permission matrix as a versioned load   Scenario: AC1 Load a matrix version  Given a matrix file with every role and area  When the reference data administrator loads it  Then it passes the checks and waits for the application owner's approval   Scenario: AC2 Incomplete matrix refused  Given a file with a role missing  When it is loaded  Then the system refuses it in full with the missing role named   Scenario: AC3 Takes effect on its date  Given an approved version with a valid from date  When the date arrives  Then every endpoint checks against the new version
RWB-AD-003 | Scope per role | Feature: Scope per role   Scenario: AC1 Own scope  Given a case owner with scope Own  When they list cases  Then the system returns only cases they own   Scenario: AC2 Out of scope  Given a case owned by another team  When a case owner with scope Team opens it  Then the system does not find the response and the refusal is logged
RWB-AD-004 | Masking profiles per role | Feature: Masking profiles per role   Scenario: AC1 Masked by default  Given a role with no unmasked rule in the version in force  When it reads a case  Then the identity number shows from v_ace_customer.id_no_masked  And the phone number shows from v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked   Scenario: AC2 Unmask is logged  Given a role allowed to unmask the contact value  When it unmasks the phone number on a case  Then the system fills the field from v_ace_contact.contact_value and writes the read to the PII log  And the identity number is still shown from id_no_masked, never in clear   Scenario: AC3 Profile change  Given a new masking_rule version approved by Compliance  When its valid from date arrives  Then responses use the new version and the access log carries the version in force
RWB-AD-005 | Separation of duty check at sign-in | Feature: Separation of duty check at sign-in   Scenario: AC1 Conflict refused  Given a person in the groups for RW-WRITEOFF and RW-WOCOMM  When they sign in  Then the system refuses the session and an incident goes to the security administrator   Scenario: AC2 Table as data  Given a new separation of duty version  When it is approved  Then the next sign-in checks against it
RWB-AD-006 | Break-glass access | Feature: Break-glass access   Scenario: AC1 Granted with an incident  Given an open incident and a reason of at least 20 characters  When the security administrator approves the request  Then the system grants access for the window and every action is marked break-glass   Scenario: AC2 Refused without an incident  Given no open incident  When the request is made  Then the system refuses it   Scenario: AC3 Ends on its own  Given an active grant  When the window ends  Then the grant ends with no action by anyone
RWB-AD-007 | Access log search and export | Feature: Access log search and export   Scenario: AC1 Search  Given sign-ins and refusals for a week  When I search by person and date  Then the matching entries show with the role and versions in force   Scenario: AC2 Export  Given a search result  When I export it  Then the file carries the same masking as the screen
RWB-AD-008 | Access review list | Feature: Access review list   Scenario: AC1 List produced  Given the review date  When the review opens  Then each role owner receives the holders of their roles   Scenario: AC2 Not confirmed  Given a holder not confirmed by the end of the review  When the review closes  Then the system requests removal through the bank IAM and logged
RWB-AD-009 | Load a list of values version | Feature: Load a list of values version   Scenario: AC1 Valid load  Given a file for LOV-ROUTE with codes and English labels  When I load it  Then it passes the checks and waits for the list owner's approval   Scenario: AC2 Code in use removed  Given a load that removes a code used by open cases  When it is loaded  Then the system refuses it with the count of records using the code
RWB-AD-010 | Approve a reference data load | Feature: Approve a reference data load   Scenario: AC1 Approve  Given a loaded version waiting for me  When I approve it  Then it takes effect from its valid from date and the approval is logged   Scenario: AC2 Maker cannot approve  Given a version I loaded  When I try to approve it  Then I am refused with MSG-P7-002
RWB-AD-011 | Load a rule version | Feature: Load a rule version   Scenario: AC1 Rule rows tested  Given a route set file where every row has a test case ID  When I load it  Then the rule table tests run in SIT and the result is attached to the version   Scenario: AC2 Row without a test  Given a row with no test case ID  When I load it  Then the system refuses the version
RWB-AD-012 | Approve a rule version | Feature: Approve a rule version   Scenario: AC1 Approve  Given a version with every test passed  When I approve it  Then it applies to decisions from its valid from date   Scenario: AC2 Open cases keep their version  Given a case decided under the previous version  When the new version takes effect  Then the decided case keeps the version it was decided under (R-UNI-38)
RWB-AD-013 | Roll back a rule or reference version | Feature: Roll back a rule or reference version   Scenario: AC1 Roll back  Given a version in force that causes a breach  When I load the previous version with an immediate date and the owner approves  Then decisions from that time use the previous version and both changes are logged
RWB-AD-014 | Configure queues | Feature: Configure queues   Scenario: AC1 Queue loaded  Given a queue file  When it is loaded and approved  Then allocation uses the new method and cap from the valid from date   Scenario: AC2 Overflow must exist  Given a queue that names an overflow queue that does not exist  When it is loaded  Then the system refuses the load
RWB-AD-015 | Configure service levels and timers | Feature: Configure service levels and timers   Scenario: AC1 Service level loaded  Given a service level of 10 working days for state LIT_PACK with a warning at 8  When it is approved  Then new timers in that state use the values   Scenario: AC2 Running timers  Given a timer already running  When a new version takes effect  Then the running timer keeps its due date unless the rule says to recompute
RWB-AD-016 | Load the delegation of authority table | Feature: Load the delegation of authority table   Scenario: AC1 Limits loaded  Given limits by decision, level, product and amount  When Risk approves the version  Then approvals check against it from its date   Scenario: AC2 Missing limit  Given a decision with no limit at any level  When it is submitted  Then it goes to the next level up and an incident names the missing limit
RWB-AD-017 | Manage letter and notice templates | Feature: Manage letter and notice templates   Scenario: AC1 Approve  Given a new template version in Thai and English  When Legal approves it  Then notices generated from its date use it   Scenario: AC2 Withdraw  Given a template withdrawn  When a notice of that type is due  Then generation holds and a task goes to the litigation officer (R-LIT-04)
RWB-AD-018 | Interface and job monitor | Feature: Interface and job monitor   Scenario: AC1 Workbench jobs and their ACE date  Given the jobs of the job catalog and the outbound actions for 2026-11-30  When I open the monitor  Then each shows its job ID, business date, status, duration and the result of each check  And each job that reads ACE shows the last complete business date of its source from v_ace_batch_status   Scenario: AC2 Rerun a Workbench job  Given a failed Workbench job  When I rerun it from its run book after the cause is fixed  Then the job runs again and both runs are in the job log   Scenario: AC3 A late ACE batch  Given v_ace_batch_status shows EFS for business date 2026-12-01 with status FAILED  When the dependent job reaches its schedule  Then the job is recorded WAITING and is not rerun  And its data product shows STALE with MSG-P1-001

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v5.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 1 v5

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

These notes follow the 71 stories of Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 v8. Version 4 walked every flow step, and most of those steps were load or job steps. The ACE re-base of 15 November 2026 (D-RCV-35, ADR-010) removed that estate: the Workbench takes no inbound source data, ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads ACE only through the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views. In this version each story carries four notes in place of the old steps.

| Note | What it answers |
|---|---|
| View | Which views or Workbench tables the story reads, and what it takes from each |
| Grant | Which role holds which privilege, and what the story may not do |
| Freshness | Which data product the read belongs to, how its business date and stamp are set, and what a stale product does |
| Boundary | Where the module boundary falls and which rule fails the build when a class crosses it |

The story remains the specification. Where these notes and the story differ, the story governs. Section 13 of each story is its solution plan and section 16 its tests; where version 4 described a Workbench step that the re-base did not change, that section still carries it, and where it described a load or a job, the four notes replace it. RWB-E1-069 owns the view list, the grants and the view conformance test. RWB-ACE-001 owns the 14 Tier 2 tables and the 12 columns that Section B needs, and nothing in the Workbench creates or alters them.

The 16 Section A views ship in V0002 and read the 21 ACE tables that exist today. The 14 Section B views ship in V0003 and read the tables that RWB-ACE-001 adds. Together they hold 304 columns, each with a dictionary row in the 122-object, 1,366-field dictionary of V0001.

| View | ACE source | Fields | Section |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `v_ace_account` | account | 42 | A |
| `v_ace_payment` | payment | 12 | A |
| `v_ace_customer` | customer | 20 | A |
| `v_ace_contact` | phone, email, address | 9 | A |
| `v_ace_ca_relation` | ca_relation | 5 | A |
| `v_ace_aa_relation` | aa_relation | 2 | A |
| `v_ace_collateral` | collateral | 8 | A |
| `v_ace_asset` | asset | 9 | A |
| `v_ace_efs_action` | efs_action | 20 | A |
| `v_ace_efs_action_code` | efs_action_code | 3 | A |
| `v_ace_efs_assignment` | efs_assignment | 9 | A |
| `v_ace_bucket_log` | bucket_log_snapshot | 6 | A |
| `v_ace_product` | product | 5 | A |
| `v_ace_branch` | branch | 4 | A |
| `v_ace_holiday` | bot_holiday | 5 | A |
| `v_ace_plan` | ace_case, cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, tdr_calculation, ai_recommended_plan | 18 | A |
| `v_ace_batch_status` | ace_batch_run | 9 | B |
| `v_ace_valuation` | valuation | 9 | B |
| `v_ace_collateral_detail` | collateral_detail | 12 | B |
| `v_ace_npa_asset` | npa_asset | 12 | B |
| `v_ace_npa_sale` | npa_sale | 11 | B |
| `v_ace_lawsuit` | lawsuit | 13 | B |
| `v_ace_hearing` | hearing | 7 | B |
| `v_ace_pod` | pod_receipt | 10 | B |
| `v_ace_write_off` | gl_write_off | 9 | B |
| `v_ace_score` | collins_score | 10 | B |
| `v_ace_party_product` | party_product | 6 | B |
| `v_ace_credit_decision` | credit_decision | 8 | B |
| `v_ace_esign` | esign_request | 7 | B |
| `v_ace_iam_group` | iam_group | 4 | B |

Two database roles carry the read path. Their names are fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design, and no story invents a third.

| Role | Holds | On what | Set by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ace_view_owner` | USAGE and SELECT | The 21 Section A tables and the 14 Section B tables in `public`; owner of the 30 views | V0002 and V0003 (RWB-E1-069), with the SELECT on the Tier 2 tables granted to it by RWB-ACE-001 |
| `recovery_svc` | USAGE on `recovery` and SELECT on each view | The 30 views only; no privilege of any kind in `public` | V0002 for Section A, V0003 for Section B |
| `recovery_svc` | DML on the Workbench tables | The 92 tables of schema `recovery` | V0001 (RWB-E1-001) |
| `PUBLIC` | Nothing | Nothing | `REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC` in V0002 |

No view takes an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE. A story that changes a Workbench decision writes its own table; a story that appears to change an ACE record writes an extension table keyed by the ACE business key.

A product is fresh when ACE reports its batch for the business date COMPLETE. RWB-E1-015 writes one `data_product_load` row per product per business date from `v_ace_batch_status`, and the `ace_batch_run` record that RWB-ACE-001 adds carries the business date, the status and the record count. A read that finds no COMPLETE batch keeps the last good business date, marks the product stale and raises MSG-P1-001. The Workbench products (DP03, DP04, DP08, DP09, DP10, DP12 and DP14) are stamped from their own last committed write, because no ACE batch produces them.

| Product | Data | Cycle | Expected by |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP01 | Account and arrears | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP02 | Customer and party | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP03 | Case and ownership | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP04 | Treatment and offers | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP05 | Contact and promises | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP06 | Collateral and assets | WEEKLY | MON 08:00 |
| DP07 | Legal events and cases | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP08 | Partner performance | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP09 | Debt sale | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP10 | Documents and extracted fields | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP11 | Scores and route economics | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP12 | Decision log | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |
| DP13 | Money and closure | DAILY | 08:00 |
| DP14 | Reference data | ON_CHANGE | As it changes |

The boundary has four parts, and each one fails loudly.

- **No copy.** The recovery schema holds no ACE source table. The 88 Workbench tables hold Workbench records; the four extension tables hold a Workbench decision about an ACE record; the 30 views are the only read of ACE data.
- **No constraint into `public`.** No foreign key, check or unique constraint in `recovery` names a table or type outside it, because ACE cascades deletes on `account`. A link is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key.
- **No direct read.** Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 fails the build when a recovery class names a `public` table. The allowed objects are the 30 view names in `recovery-modules.yaml`, not a literal list in the test.
- **No write to a view.** `recovery_svc` holds SELECT only; the view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 fails if it finds a write privilege or a privilege in `public`.

secs.h: What this version removes from version 4
secs.t:
| Removed | Why | Where it went |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-E1-003 ALS daily extract load | ACE ingests ALS | ACE ingestion; the Workbench reads `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_payment` |
| RWB-E1-004 EFS extract load | ACE ingests EFS | ACE ingestion; the Workbench reads `v_ace_efs_action` |
| RWB-E1-005 Excel and SharePoint inventory | No tracker estate to inventory | Cutover plan |
| RWB-E1-006 Data quality rules v1 | ACE runs the ingestion checks | ACE ingestion; the daily gate is in RWB-E1-015 |
| RWB-E1-009 CCMS and SVAF loads | ACE ingests CCMS and SVAF | ACE ingestion; `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_valuation` and Section B |
| RWB-E1-010 Excel and SharePoint loads | No tracker estate to load | Cutover plan |
| RWB-E1-012 Retire local copies | No local copy to retire | Cutover plan |
| RWB-E1-051 Legacy feed jobs on ADF and Control-M | No ADF job remains | ACE ingestion |

The job steps that remain are Workbench jobs: allocation, rebalancing, the letter and notice runs, OCR and the agent runs. Every one of them reads its source through a view and writes only a Workbench table. The pipeline steps that remain are migrations, the dictionary conformance test, the view conformance test, the boundary test and the PDPA lint.

secs.h: RWB-E1-001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products
secs.t:
Module: P1 Recovery data engine

**View.** No view. The story creates the 92 tables of Physical Schema v5, `data_product`, `sys_objects` and `sys_fields`; the 30 views arrive next in V0002 and V0003 (RWB-E1-069).

**Grant.** V0001 gives the recovery service role DML on the Workbench tables and nothing on a view; no `GRANT` on `public` and no `GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES`.

**Freshness.** All 14 products: DP01, DP02, DP05, DP07, DP11 and DP13 DAILY by 08:00, DP06 WEEKLY by Monday 08:00, and the Workbench products DP03, DP04, DP08, DP09, DP10, DP12 and DP14 ON_CHANGE as they change. RWB-E1-015 stamps `data_product_load` from `v_ace_batch_status`; a product with no COMPLETE batch keeps its last good business date, is marked stale and raises MSG-P1-001.

**Boundary.** v4 created a 43-table copy schema and seeded 108 objects and 1,256 fields. v5 creates the 92 tables, the four extension tables and the 122-object, 1,366-field dictionary, and leaves every source read to RWB-E1-069. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 fails the build when a recovery class names a `public` table; the only source objects it may name are the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views listed in `recovery-modules.yaml`.

secs.h: RWB-E1-002 Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue
secs.t:
Module: P1 Recovery data engine

**View.** `v_ace_account` for balance and days past due, `v_ace_efs_action` for the last contact, `v_ace_batch_status` for the business date of the ACE batch; `case_account`, `case_list_row` and `recovery_case` come through `CaseQueryApi`.

**Grant.** No change. `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views named above from V0002 (RWB-E1-069) and no privilege in `public`; this story grants nothing and writes no ACE object.

**Freshness.** DP01 Account and arrears, DAILY, expected 08:00. RWB-E1-015 stamps `data_product_load` from `v_ace_batch_status`; a product with no COMPLETE batch keeps its last good business date, is marked stale and raises MSG-P1-001.

**Boundary.** v4 steps 2, 3 and 5 built a `load_run` row, called `LoadRunQuery.completedLoad` and joined `loan_account`. The table is gone: the completeness check is a read of `v_ace_batch_status`, and the join is to `v_ace_account`. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 enforces the view-only read, and the Section B read stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed and V0003 applies (DL43).

secs.h: RWB-E1-007 Integration adapters for outbound files
secs.t:
Module: P2 Integration

**View.** `v_ace_account` for the account key, `v_ace_contact` for the contact key and channel, `v_ace_batch_status` for the date; writes `interface_config`, `outbound_item`, `outbox_event`, `outbox_delivery`, `processed_event`, `debt_sale_account` and `recovery_case`.

**Grant.** No change. `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views named above from V0002 (RWB-E1-069) and no privilege in `public`; this story grants nothing and writes no ACE object.

**Freshness.** DP01 Account and arrears, DAILY, expected 08:00; DP05 Contact and promises, DAILY, expected 08:00. RWB-E1-015 stamps `data_product_load` from `v_ace_batch_status`; a product with no COMPLETE batch keeps its last good business date, is marked stale and raises MSG-P1-001.

**Boundary.** v4 built the inbound file loads INT-10, INT-11 and INT-15 and the outbound interface INT-14. v5 keeps the outbound adapter, the outbox and the contract tests; the inbound loads are gone, and the adapter writes Workbench outbound files only. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 enforces the view-only read, and the Section B read stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed and V0003 applies (DL43).

secs.h: RWB-E1-008 Decision log store v1, append only and hash chained
secs.t:
Module: P7 Decision center and log

**View.** No view. The story owns `decision_log_entry` and reads no ACE source.

**Grant.** No view in this story. `recovery_svc` holds DML on the Workbench tables it uses (V0001) and no privilege in `public`; this story grants nothing and writes no ACE object.

**Freshness.** DP12 Decision log, ON_CHANGE as it changes. A Workbench product is stamped from its last committed write, not from an ACE batch, so no ACE clock makes it stale.

**Boundary.** No change of substance. The entry carries the business keys of the ACE records it names, never a copy of an ACE column. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 fails the build when a recovery class names a `public` table; the only source objects it may name are the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views listed in `recovery-modules.yaml`.

secs.h: RWB-E1-011 Reconciliation and data quality report
secs.t:
Module: P1 Recovery data engine

**View.** `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_plan`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact`, `v_ace_asset` and `v_ace_batch_status` for the reconciliation; writes `reconciliation_result`, `case_list_row` and the case exceptions.

**Grant.** No change. `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views named above from V0002 (RWB-E1-069) and no privilege in `public`; this story grants nothing and writes no ACE object.

**Freshness.** DP01 Account and arrears, DAILY, expected 08:00; DP05 Contact and promises, DAILY, expected 08:00; DP06 Collateral and assets, WEEKLY, expected MON 08:00; DP13 Money and closure, DAILY, expected 08:00. RWB-E1-015 stamps `data_product_load` from `v_ace_batch_status`; a product with no COMPLETE batch keeps its last good business date, is marked stale and raises MSG-P1-001.

**Boundary.** v4 reconciled the load runs and the copy tables after JOB-04. v5 reconciles the Workbench case data against the ACE views and the ACE batch record; there is no load run to reconcile. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. Boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001 enforces the view-only read, and the Section B read stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed and V0003 applies (DL43).

Module: P9 Reporting

**View.** `v_ace_payment` for money collected and `case_account` for the case stock; writes `measure_definition` and `measure_snapshot`.

**Grant.** No change. `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views named above from V0002 (RWB-E1-069) and no privilege in `public`; this story grants nothing and writes no ACE object.

**Freshness.** DP03 Case and ownership, ON_CHANGE as it changes; DP13 Money and closure, DAILY, expected 08:00. RWB-E1-015 stamps `data_product_load` from `v_ace_batch_status`; a product with no COMPLETE batch keeps its last good business date, is marked stale and raises MSG-P1-001.

**Boundary.** v4 read the money measures from the copy tables. v5 reads `v_ace_payment`; the case stock comes from `case_account`. No recovery constraint references `public`; a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key. secs.h: RWB-E1-069 Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

One story per Workbench data product: extract from the legacy Workbench, map the ids to ACE business keys, load, reconcile and cut over.

Version 3 is re-based on D-RCV-35 and ADR-010. No story loads a source record. ACE holds the account, payment, customer, contact, collateral, asset, appraisal, collections, legal, proof-of-delivery, write-off and score data, and the Workbench reads it through the recovery.v_ace_* views. Two stories leave because the data is already in ACE (RWB-DM-001, RWB-DM-002) and four are reduced to their Workbench-only part (RWB-DM-005, RWB-DM-006, RWB-DM-011, RWB-DM-013). Every account link is an account_key and every person link is a person_key, held as a business key with no foreign key into ACE.

---

**Removed by D-RCV-35. The data is already in ACE.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Status | Removed |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1) |
| Why | ACE ingests the ALS account, arrears and balance data and holds the one copy. The Workbench loads none of it, so there is nothing to extract, transform, load or reconcile. |
| Read path instead | v_ace_account for the account, the arrears, the balances, the classification and the ACE business date; v_ace_bucket_log for the monthly bucket history; v_ace_product and v_ace_branch for the product and branch lists |
| Data product | DP01 stays in the catalog with system of record "ACE (ingested from ALS)" and its view list. Only the migration story leaves. |
| Withdrawn IDs | AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04 |
| Later home | None. Any column the Workbench still needs is raised once in RWB-ACE-001. |

**Story.** As a data steward, I want the Workbench case and ownership records migrated from the legacy Workbench with their ACE business keys, so that every open case keeps its owner, its queue and its history from the first day.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Migrate case and ownership

 Scenario: AC1 Extract the Workbench records
 Given the legacy Workbench case, case account, case party and assignment records for the open cases at cutover
 When the migration reads them
 Then each case keeps its case number, its owner, its queue and its stage, each account link carries an account_key and each party link a person_key
 And no account and no customer record is copied from ACE

 Scenario: AC2 Reconcile the business keys
 Given the migrated records
 When the REC-05 step runs
 Then every business key on a migrated record resolves to its view row, account_key and person_key included
 And each orphan is listed for the data steward and the ACE team

 Scenario: AC3 Cut over
 Given ten clean days on the migrated records
 When the data steward signs off
 Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period
 And the migrated records are served from the new schema
```

| Entity | Fields | BR Field IDs |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code and 27 more | DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055 |
| case_account | id, case_id, account_key, is_primary, linked_from, linked_to | DF-CAS-024 to DF-CAS-029 |
| case_party | id, case_id, person_key, party_role, role_from, role_to | DF-CAS-030 to DF-CAS-035 |

No endpoint in this story. The migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity, and its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | None |
| Process | All recovery processes |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069 |
| Decision | DL25 |

**Story.** As a data steward, I want the rules, the approval limits, the lists of values and the letter templates that the Workbench owns migrated as versioned reference data, so that the versions in force at go-live are the ones the business approved.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Migrate reference data

 Scenario: AC1 Extract the Workbench records
 Given the legacy Workbench reference versions, their rows and the lists of values that the Workbench owns
 When the migration reads them
 Then each version keeps its table code, its version number, its valid from date and its approver, and each row its key and its data
 And no list that ACE holds is re-loaded, because the action codes, the products, the branches and the holidays are read from v_ace_efs_action_code, v_ace_product, v_ace_branch and v_ace_holiday

 Scenario: AC2 Reconcile the versions
 Given the migrated reference versions
 When the reference data service validates them
 Then every version in force has its row count, its content hash and its approver
 And every rule row names the test case that proves it

 Scenario: AC3 Cut over
 Given ten clean days on the migrated records
 When the data steward signs off
 Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period
 And the migrated records are served from the new schema
```

| reference_row | id, version_id, row_key, row_data | DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184 |

No endpoint in this story. The migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity, and its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract.

**Screen and states**

No screen in this story.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

How to read the acceptance criteria

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group.

Every user story ends in a set of acceptance criteria. They are the test the build must pass, and they are written to one pattern. Once you know the pattern, every story in the set reads the same way.

ทุกสตอรีจบด้วยเกณฑ์ยอมรับ ซึ่งเป็นสิ่งที่งานพัฒนาต้องผ่าน และเขียนด้วยรูปแบบเดียวกันทั้งหมด เมื่อเข้าใจรูปแบบนี้แล้ว จะอ่านได้ทุกสตอรีในชุดเอกสาร

A scenario has three parts

Each scenario is one case to prove. Every line starts with a word that says what the line is for.

แต่ละสถานการณ์ทดสอบคือหนึ่งกรณีที่ต้องพิสูจน์ ทุกบรรทัดขึ้นต้นด้วยคำที่บอกหน้าที่ของบรรทัดนั้น

Keyword | Reading label | ภาษาไทย | What the line is for
Given | Setup | สิ่งที่ต้องมีอยู่ก่อน | What is already true before the test starts. Nobody does it during the test.
When | Action | การกระทำ | The one action that starts the test. Each scenario has one of these.
Then | Result | ผลที่ต้องได้ | What must be true after the action. There are often several, and every one must hold.

Every line states its own role

A line used to start with And, which meant it took its meaning from the line above. Those are gone. A line that is a second result now starts with Then, and a line that is a second precondition starts with Given. You never have to look upward to know what a line is doing.

เดิมบางบรรทัดขึ้นต้นด้วย And ซึ่งต้องย้อนไปดูบรรทัดก่อนหน้าจึงจะเข้าใจ ตอนนี้ไม่มีแล้ว บรรทัดที่เป็นผลลัพธ์เพิ่มเติมจะขึ้นต้นด้วย Then และบรรทัดที่เป็นเงื่อนไขเพิ่มเติมจะขึ้นต้นด้วย Given จึงไม่ต้องย้อนขึ้นไปอ่านบรรทัดบนอีก

The result says who acts

A result names the actor and leads with the verb. "The load is refused" is now "the system refuses the load". The meaning is the same; the sentence says who does it.

บรรทัดผลลัพธ์จะระบุผู้กระทำและขึ้นต้นด้วยคำกริยา เช่น "The load is refused" เปลี่ยนเป็น "the system refuses the load" ความหมายเหมือนเดิม แต่บอกชัดว่าใครเป็นผู้กระทำ

A worked example

This is AC7 from RWB-E1-001, the story that creates the recovery tables.

ตัวอย่างนี้คือ AC7 ของสตอรี RWB-E1-001

Label | ภาษาไทย | The line | What it is telling you
Setup | สิ่งที่ต้องมีอยู่ก่อน | a catalog load file gives DP06 two systems of record, "CCMS; SVAF" | The file already exists and is wrong in this way. You do not build this; you assume it.
Setup | สิ่งที่ต้องมีอยู่ก่อน | the same file gives DP11 no owner user ID | A second fault in the same file. Both faults are present at once.
Action | การกระทำ | the reference data administrator loads the file | The single action. A person with that role loads it.
Result | ผลที่ต้องได้ | the system refuses the whole file and writes no row | All or nothing. One bad row stops the entire file.
Result | ผลที่ต้องได้ | the system returns MSG-P1-003 once for DP06 and once for DP11 | Two messages, one per fault. Click the code in the hub for its exact wording in Thai and English.
Result | ผลที่ต้องได้ | data_product still holds the rows of the version in force | The previous good data is untouched.

The sentence patterns that repeat

These patterns cover most of the result lines in the set.

รูปแบบประโยคเหล่านี้ครอบคลุมบรรทัดผลลัพธ์ส่วนใหญ่ในชุดเอกสาร

Pattern | ภาษาไทย
the system writes {X} to {Y} | ระบบเขียน {X} ลงใน {Y}
the system writes no {X} | ระบบไม่เขียน {X}
the system refuses {X} with {MSG} | ระบบไม่รับ {X} พร้อมข้อความ {MSG}
the system refuses {X} in full | ระบบไม่รับ {X} ทั้งรายการ
the system stores {X} | ระบบจัดเก็บ {X}
the system raises {X} | ระบบแจ้ง {X}
the system places the case in queue {Q} | ระบบจัดกรณีเข้าคิว {Q}
the system returns {N} with {MSG} | ระบบคืนค่า {N} พร้อมข้อความ {MSG}
the case moves to {STATE} | กรณีเปลี่ยนไปยังขั้นตอน {STATE}
the case stays in {STATE} | กรณียังคงอยู่ในขั้นตอน {STATE}
nothing changes | ไม่มีการเปลี่ยนแปลง
{X} is unchanged | {X} ไม่เปลี่ยนแปลง
{X} is in force | {X} มีผลบังคับใช้อยู่
{X} holds {N} rows | {X} มี {N} แถว
{X} shows {Y} | {X} แสดง {Y}
{X} passes / {X} fails | {X} ผ่าน / {X} ไม่ผ่าน
naming {X} | โดยระบุ {X}
for business date {D} | สำหรับวันที่ทำการ {D}
within {N} seconds | ภายใน {N} วินาที
at least {N} / at most {N} | อย่างน้อย {N} / ไม่เกิน {N}
exactly one {X} | {X} เพียงหนึ่งเดียว
{X} is on the exception list | {X} อยู่ในรายการผิดปกติ

The codes you will see

Codes name a rule, a field or a message. In the project hub, click any code and its full wording opens under the line you are reading.

รหัสต่าง ๆ ใช้อ้างถึงกฎ ฟิลด์ หรือข้อความ ในโปรเจกต์ฮับ สามารถคลิกที่รหัสเพื่อดูเนื้อหาเต็มได้ทันทีใต้บรรทัดที่กำลังอ่าน

Prefix | English | ภาษาไทย
REQ- | Requirement | ข้อกำหนด
BR- | Business rule | กฎทางธุรกิจ
VR- | Validation rule | กฎการตรวจสอบข้อมูล
SC- | System constraint | ข้อจำกัดของระบบ
AC- | Acceptance code, main flow | รหัสเกณฑ์ยอมรับ เส้นทางหลัก
AC-EXC- | Acceptance code, exception flow | รหัสเกณฑ์ยอมรับ กรณีผิดปกติ
AC-BG- | Acceptance code, background event | รหัสเกณฑ์ยอมรับ เหตุการณ์เบื้องหลัง
DF- | Data field | ฟิลด์ข้อมูล
MSG- | Message, written in Thai and English | ข้อความระบบ มีทั้งภาษาไทยและอังกฤษ
LOV- | List of values | รายการค่าที่อนุญาต
DL / DT | Open decision / technical decision | ประเด็นที่ยังไม่ตัดสินใจ / การตัดสินใจทางเทคนิค
RWB- | User story | ยูสเซอร์สตอรี

Where to read more

The project hub opens each story with its acceptance criteria already labelled Setup, Action and Result. The button marked ไทย turns on the Thai meaning of the words in each line.

โปรเจกต์ฮับจะแสดงเกณฑ์ยอมรับของแต่ละสตอรีพร้อมป้ายกำกับ Setup, Action และ Result และปุ่ม ไทย จะเปิดคำแปลของคำศัพท์ในแต่ละบรรทัด

The glossary file holds the words, the sentence patterns and the codes, with Thai for each. Its Thai follows the wording already used in the Workbench message standard, so a word means the same thing on the screen as it does in a story.

ไฟล์อภิธานศัพท์รวบรวมคำศัพท์ รูปแบบประโยค และรหัสต่าง ๆ พร้อมคำแปลภาษาไทย โดยใช้คำตามมาตรฐานข้อความของระบบ เพื่อให้คำเดียวกันมีความหมายตรงกันทั้งบนหน้าจอและในสตอรี

If a line is still unclear, the squad lead should raise it against the story key. The wording is changed once, in the story, so every reader gets the same correction.

หากยังมีบรรทัดที่ไม่ชัดเจน หัวหน้าทีมสามารถแจ้งโดยอ้างอิงรหัสสตอรี เพื่อแก้ไขถ้อยคำที่ต้นทางเพียงครั้งเดียว ผู้อ่านทุกคนจะได้รับฉบับที่แก้ไขแล้วเหมือนกัน

secs.h: RWB-TE-001 Recovery module folder and boundary test
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-001 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 7 (constraint Modular monolith) and section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | DL05 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the recovery module folder and packages in the ACE repository with a build-time boundary test**, so that **no module calls the inside of another module, no recovery code calls a system of record directly, and no recovery code reads an ACE table except through a recovery.v_ace_* view**.

Three teams build in one ACE service. Without a checked boundary, a change in one team's code breaks another's, and a direct call to a core system could bypass ACE ingestion. The skeleton gives each Workbench module one package with a published part and an internal part, and a test in every build refuses a call into another module's internal part, a cross-module table read and a direct system call outside the integration adapters. It meets REQ-DRI-006 and applies DT08, ADR-002, ADR-010 and DL05 (option B from 2 November: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package). Under D-RCV-35 the ACE data a recovery class may name is only the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, listed in the module map; a direct read of a public table, and a foreign key from the recovery schema into public, fail the same build. The measure is the count of boundary violations merged to main, which must stay at zero.

- Access to the ACE repository for the TechX squads (DL36).
- DL05 is applied as option B from 2 November 2026: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package; the ACE team applies the module boundaries for the common and collection modules later.
- The common module's published packages are named in the module map. Until the ACE team names them, the map lists `..common.api..` (assumed; DL05).
- The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` view names are listed in the module map as the only source objects a recovery class may name (RWB-E1-069, Section A and Section B).
- The recovery service identity `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.
- The ACE build runs the unit test phase on every pull request.

1. Squad member: creates the recovery folders and packages for the 19 Workbench modules, each with an `api` package and an `internal` package.
2. Squad member: writes the module map `architecture/recovery-modules.yaml` with each module code, its package and its published packages.
3. Squad member: writes RecoveryBoundaryTest with the rules BR1 to BR8, reading the module map and the view list.
4. Squad member: writes the front end boundary rules for `src/modules/recovery`.
5. Squad member: wires the common module access check for `/api/recovery/v1/**` through RecoveryAccessGuard.
6. Pipeline: on each pull request runs the back end tests, including RecoveryBoundaryTest, and the front end dependency check.
7. Pipeline: fails the build when a rule is broken and prints the rule, the class and the class it depends on.
8. Squad member: fixes the call by going through the other module's `api` package or an application event, and the build passes.
None.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only repository access; every later story builds inside these folders |
| Negotiable | Module names and published packages are in the module map file, not in the test code |
| Valuable | The three teams can change their own module without breaking another |
| Estimable | Folders, one map file, one ArchUnit test class, one front end rule file |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each rule has a test fixture class that breaks it |
None. The former criteria covered development and delivery procedures and have been removed from the story set.

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a code owners entry that maps every recovery folder to the TechX tech leads and the common module to the ACE team, with review by a code owner required before merge**, so that **every change in the recovery module is reviewed by its owners**.

The recovery and collection squads and the ACE team merge into one repository and one monthly release. Without named owners per folder, a change to the recovery module or to the common module can merge without the team that answers for it. The code owners file names the reviewing team per folder and the branch rule on main blocks a merge until that team approves. It supports REQ-DRI-006, because the integration adapter folder, the only place allowed to reach other systems, cannot change without a TechX tech lead, and it applies DL04 option A and DL37. The measure is the share of merged pull requests on recovery folders approved by a code owner, which must be 100 percent.

- The teams exist in the repository host: TechX recovery tech leads and the ACE team. Names assumed until DL37 and DL36 are answered: `@scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads` and `@scb-ace/ace-team`.
- The repository administrator of the ACE team can set the branch rule on main.

1. Squad member: writes `.github/CODEOWNERS` with the entries in BR1 to BR5, ordered so that the most specific path is last.
2. Squad member: adds the code owners validation step to the pull request pipeline.

4. Developer: opens a pull request that changes a recovery folder.
5. Repository host: requests review from the owning team named for each changed path.
6. Pipeline: runs the validation step; an owner that does not exist or a path that matches no file fails the check.
7. Code owner: approves; the merge is allowed once every owning team of the changed paths has approved.

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **server interfaces and front end types generated from the OpenAPI file, with a contract test and an access test per endpoint**, so that **the front end and the service never drift from the specification and no endpoint skips its access check**.

The recovery API has 79 operations specified in one OpenAPI 3.1 file. When server code, front end code and the file are kept by hand, a field renamed on one side breaks a screen in SIT, and an endpoint can ship without the capability check its specification states. Generating both sides from the file and testing every implemented operation against it in each build stops both faults before merge. It meets REQ-DRI-007, where the FSD requires every interface to have a contract test (AC-P2-001-01), and REQ-ACA-003, because each endpoint is tested against the right its specification declares from the permission matrix. The measure is the count of contract defects found in SIT, with a target of zero.

- RWB-TE-001 is done: the recovery folders and the boundary test exist; the generated packages are listed in the module map as shared.
- The API specification is held in the repository at `api/recovery-api.yaml`, base path /api/recovery/v1, with x-module, x-capability and x-first-release on every operation.
- The permission matrix seed (roles.txt, loaded as the role and permission tables by RWB-E1-037) is available to tests.
- The build property `rwb.release` names the release being built: E1 for 30 November 2026.

1. Build: lints the specification with the recovery rule set; a missing operationId, x-capability or error response fails the build.
2. Build: generates the Spring server interfaces and models from the specification.
3. Build: generates the TypeScript types and the typed client for the front end.
4. Build: compiles the service against the generated interfaces and the front end against the generated types.
5. Contract test: lists every operation with x-first-release at or before `rwb.release` and finds its implementing controller method.
6. Contract test: calls each implemented operation with its fixture and validates the request and the response against the specification.
7. Access test: calls each operation as a role whose permission lacks the declared right and expects 403 with messageCode MSG-P4-002.
8. Build: reports passed, failed and pending operations; any failure fails the build.

secs.h: RWB-TE-004 Masked data in SIT and UAT
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-004 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-010, REQ-ACA-005 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 4 (REQ-RDF-010, REQ-ACA-005); Business Requirements Program, section 6.7 (NFR-045) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | DL26 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-069, RWB-E1-037 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **Tribe lead and squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **SIT and UAT to run on ACE data whose personal fields are masked in the recovery.v_ace_* views and by role at the API**, so that **tests run on realistic volumes without exposing customers**.

SIT and UAT must show that allocation, reconciliation and reports work at production volume and with production data shapes, which synthetic data does not prove. NFR-045 allows masked data in user acceptance and forbids production data in development. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench takes no inbound copy, so there is nothing to mask at a load: every personal field in SIT and UAT is read from an ACE view that already masks it, or masked by the role rule of RWB-E1-037 at the API. `v_ace_customer` returns `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` and never the clear identification number; `v_ace_contact` returns `contact_value` and `contact_value_masked`. A verifier proves that no clear personal value sits in schema `recovery`, that the views return the masked columns, and that a role without the permission receives the masked column. Serves REQ-RDF-010 and REQ-ACA-005; decision DL26 sets the masking rules, and ADR-010 removes the token that the load used to write.

- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist, and `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on them and no privilege on `public`.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the masking rules by role are loaded, naming the view field IDs DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value` and DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`.
- RWB-E1-065 is done: the synthetic data set and its `is_personal` scan are available for DEV.
- SIT and UAT read an ACE database at production volume, or the ACE test extract, and the recovery schema is at the same Flyway version as the views.
- The masking rule version in force is held in the masking rules reference table (DL26).
- The platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) starts the verification run; squad members hold RW-TRIBE.

1. Platform administrator: points SIT or UAT at the ACE database and confirms `recovery_svc` is the only recovery database account.
2. MaskedDataVerifier: checks the connection: SELECT on each of the 30 views succeeds and SELECT on a `public` table fails.
3. MaskedDataVerifier: checks that the views return the masked columns: every row of `v_ace_customer` holds `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`, and no column of `v_ace_customer` holds the clear identification number.
4. MaskedDataVerifier: scans every column of schema `recovery` tagged `is_personal` in `sys_fields` and fails on a value that looks personal: a 13-digit number with a valid Thai national ID check digit, a Thai mobile number or an email address.
5. Tester: signs in with each test role and reads a case record; FieldMasker returns `id_no_masked` or `contact_value_masked` unless the masking rule lets the role see the field (RWB-E1-037).
6. Tester: confirms that a clear phone or email appears only for a role whose rule allows DF-ACE-078, and that the identity number is never clear for any role.
7. Access log: records each read of a personal field with the user, role, field and time.

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **a harness that runs each rule row against its test case (the state, the event, the case facts and the expected result)**, so that **a rule change is tested the same way as code before it takes effect**.

The routing logic is 448 rules in ten route sets, held as data (ADR-004). A wrong condition or owner in one row moves every case that reaches it, and the bank has no test that proves a row does what its owner expects. Every rule row already names a test case (`rule_row.test_case_id`). This story runs those test cases on every rule load and in every build, and marks a version failed when any test fails. It meets REQ-CWC-014 and REQ-CWC-013. The measure is that every rule row in force has a passing test with its rule ID.

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with the parameterized schema.
- The rules component evaluates a route set as a decision table with hit policy Unique (ADR-004).
- The rule load template (RWB-E1-029) carries a Tests sheet with one test case per rule row.
- Rule rows exist with a `test_case_id` for each row (DF-REF-015, required).
- The Restructure route set is loaded in SIT with its 37 rows, R-RES-01 to R-RES-37.
- The loader holds RW-COE (Rules and parameters C).

**Work in this order.** A1 to A7 are build actions. The harness runs inside the existing rule-version load and in every build; there is no screen and no new endpoint.

Add `RuleTestCase` and `RuleTestCaseRepository`. | The migration runs clean, and a second row for the same route set, version and test case ID is refused. |
| A2 | Read the Tests sheet into test cases | Write `TestsSheetReader` to read the Tests sheet of the rule template, one test case per rule row, and store each through `RuleTestCaseRepository` with the rule ID, test case ID, from state, event, facts and the three expected values. A row that names a `test_case_id` the sheet does not hold fails the version with MSG-P3-014 naming the rule and the test case. | RES-2026.11 loads 37 rows and 37 test cases with nothing missing; version RES-2026.13 fails naming R-RES-12 and RT-RES-012. |
| A3 | Build the synthetic case file | Write `CaseFileFixtureBuilder` to turn the `facts` of a test into a synthetic case file of codes and numbers only (BR5). Refuse the test when a fact its condition needs has no value. | A test with no `break_count` fails naming `break_count`; a complete test builds a fixture with no customer, account or personal value in it. |
| A4 | Build the harness and the pass rule | Write `RuleTableHarnessImpl` implementing the published `RuleTableHarness` in `recovery.casewf.rules.harness`. Read the version's rule rows through the P4 `RuleTableReader`, evaluate the route set with the test's `from_state` and `event_code` through the shared decision-table evaluator under hit policy Unique, and apply the four-part pass rule: exactly one row hit, that row is the `rule_id` the test names, and its `to_state`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec` equal the expected values. Return one `RuleTestResult` per rule ID. | A changed to state fails R-RES-04 with expected and actual named; two hits fail naming both rule IDs; zero hits fail naming the expected rule. |

Build no new endpoint and change no contract. | A load of RES-2026.11 returns 201 after 37 passes; a version with any failing test returns 422 with each failing rule ID in `Problem.detail`. |

A FAILED version cannot be approved or take effect. Put it behind `rwb.p3.rule-harness`: on in SIT, UAT and PROD; off in DEV only, where the load continues with a warning and the version still stays FAILED. | Running the same version twice leaves 37 results, not 74; a FAILED version is refused at approval and never takes effect. |

**Do not build:** the rule template, schema, overlap, unreachable row and default checks, load and rollback (RWB-E1-029); the change log and approval checklist (RWB-E1-048); the rules and parameters screen SCR-39 in Epic 8. **Hand-off:** the published `RuleTableHarness`, `HarnessResult` and `RuleTestResult` go to P4 and to RWB-E1-048 for the test result on the version; the `ruleTests` task goes into the pipeline for every squad; MSG-P3-014 goes to the message table.

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **every application event and every outbound work request written to an outbox in the same transaction as the change, and delivered to each consumer in order with retry**, so that **no outbound action is lost when a system or a consumer is down, and nothing is sent for a change that did not commit**.

The Workbench modules talk to each other through application events, and outbound work such as a notice for WIN starts from an event in the module that approved it. If the event is sent before the change commits, or is lost when a consumer fails, a notice is never dispatched or a ledger entry is missing, and nobody sees it. The outbox stores each event with the change, a sender delivers it to every consumer at least once in case order, retries on a schedule held as data, and moves a delivery that keeps failing to the exception queue with a task. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (retry on a defined schedule; exception queue with a task for a named owner) and NFR-025 and NFR-026. The measure is the count of outbox deliveries in the exception queue over one day, with a target of zero (FSD P2 A2.1.1).

- RWB-E1-044 (versioned migrations), RWB-E1-027 (decision log writer) and RWB-E1-007 (integration adapters, IdempotencyGuard and the outbound file sender) are done.
- The consumer list is loaded in the configuration service (RWB-E1-042) under rwb.integration.outbox.consumers: consumer name, the event types it takes, its owner role, and whether it holds a case step (for example the consumer "win-dispatch" of the work request WIN_DISPATCH holds the case step, owner role RW-PLATADM; assumed).
- The retry settings are loaded under rwb.integration.outbox.retry: 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes after the previous attempt (assumed; NFR-026, DL11).
- Quartz runs clustered in the ACE service; JOB-11 Outbox sender runs every minute.
- Feature flag `rwb.integration.outbox` is on.

1. Business service (for example notice approval): calls OutboxWriter.publish inside its own transaction with the event type (an event from EV-01 to EV-28, or an outbound work request type such as WIN_DISPATCH), schema version, case ID, payload references, actor and idempotency key.
2. OutboxWriter: writes one outbox_event row with the next case sequence, and one outbox_delivery row per consumer listed for the event type.
3. Database: commits the change, the event and its deliveries together, or none of them.
4. JOB-11 Outbox sender (event step): every minute selects due deliveries with a row lock that skips rows another instance holds, oldest case sequence first, taking only the lowest open sequence per case and consumer.
5. OutboxSender: calls the consumer with the event header (event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time, actor) and payload; each consumer checks the key through IdempotencyGuard (RWB-E1-007) before it acts.
6. OutboxSender: on success marks the delivery DELIVERED; when the delivery had failed before and the consumer holds a case step, raises RETRY_SUCCEEDED for the case (R-UNI-35).
7. OutboxSender: on a failure adds 1 to the attempt count and sets the next attempt from the retry settings; on the first failure of a consumer that holds a case step, raises SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE for the case (R-UNI-33).
8. OutboxSender: when the retries are used, sets the delivery to EXCEPTION, raises task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY for the consumer's owner role on the case and, for a consumer that holds a case step, raises RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED (R-UNI-36), which writes the decision log entry; all in one transaction.
9. Platform administrator: reads exception deliveries (GET /admin/outbox/deliveries) and, once the consumer is fixed, sends one again (POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend).

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the timer check, the morning allocation run and the daily reconciliation run as Quartz jobs with a run book each**, so that **scheduled work runs once, on time and visibly, and a missed run is caught up for its business date**.

The morning allocation must finish by 07:00 so no new case waits for a person (JOB-03), the timer check must find every due timer every 5 minutes (JOB-05), and the reconciliation must compare the case list with the core bank every day (JOB-04). The ACE service runs on more than one instance, so without a shared schedule a job runs twice or not at all, and an outage loses a day's run. Under D-RCV-35 the day opens on the ACE batch-complete record, not on a Workbench load: `v_ace_batch_status` holds one row per source and business date, and a COMPLETED row, or the LoadCompleted event (EV-26) that ACE publishes for it, is what lets the daily jobs start. This story runs the three jobs on the clustered ACE Quartz scheduler with one run per business date, catch-up after an outage and a run book for each. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-011 and REQ-RDF-007. The measure is one successful run per job per business date, and JOB-03 complete by 07:00 (NFR-013).

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with the parameterized schema.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: the job monitor records runs and alerts the operations channel.
- The ACE Quartz scheduler runs with a clustered JDBC job store; its `QRTZ_` tables belong to the ACE common module.
- The ACE batch-complete record is read through `v_ace_batch_status`, one row per source and business date, and ACE publishes LoadCompleted (EV-26) when a source's batch completes; JOB-02 Case creation records its run per business date.
- The job bodies exist: allocation (RWB-E1-020), reconciliation (RWB-E1-011) and timer check (RWB-E1-028).
- `jobs.catch-up.max-dates` = 5 (assumed; DL11) and the 07:00 deadline for JOB-03 (NFR-013) are in the configuration service.

1. Scheduler: on LoadCompleted (EV-26) for business date D, on the daily gate of RWB-E1-015 returning COMPLETE from `v_ace_batch_status` for D, and on completion of JOB-02 for D, fires JOB-03 Morning allocation and JOB-04 Daily reconciliation for D.
2. Scheduler: fires JOB-05 Timer check every 5 minutes on cron `0 0/5 * * * ?` in Asia/Bangkok.
3. Job runner: takes the cluster lock so only one instance runs a job at a time.
4. Job runner: checks the job run log for job and business date; if a successful run exists, records the skip and stops.
5. Job runner: checks the job's dependency (JOB-02 succeeded for D); if not met, records WAITING and stops.
6. Job runner: records the run start through the P1 job monitor, runs the job body, records the end with status SUCCEEDED or FAILED and the counts.
7. Job runner: on service start, for each business date with a COMPLETED ACE batch and no successful run of JOB-03 or JOB-04, runs the job for that date in date order, up to `jobs.catch-up.max-dates` dates.
8. Deadline watcher: at 07:00 checks JOB-03 for the current business date; if it has not succeeded, alerts the operations channel.
9. Platform administrator: reads runs on SCR-44 and reruns a failed run through `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun`.

secs.h: RWB-TE-008 Decision log hash chain check
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-008 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-003 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.7; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.7 and 6.6 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-008, RWB-TE-007 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As an **internal auditor (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **a nightly job that recomputes the whole decision log hash chain, records the result with the last hash, and reports a break to Compliance the same day**, so that **a changed entry is found the day it happens and the log can be relied on in audit**.

The decision log is evidence only while nobody can change an entry unseen. The database refuses updates and deletes (RWB-E1-008), but a change made outside the service, for example by a database administrator, is found only by recomputing the chain. This story runs that check as JOB-14 every night after the decision log copy, records each run with its last hash, and tells Compliance of a break, an incomplete run or an intact chain. It meets REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 and supports control CTL-06. The measure is a daily check with a same-day report: target 100 percent of nights.

- RWB-E1-008 is done: HashChainVerifier, CanonicalEntryForm and ChainBreakNotifier exist.
- RWB-TE-007 is done: jobs run on Quartz in the ACE service with job run records shown by GET /admin/jobs.
- JOB-13 Decision log copy is scheduled nightly at 01:00 (RWB-E1-014).
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.decision.chaincheck.start=02:00, rwb.decision.chaincheck.latest-start=04:00, rwb.decision.chaincheck.batch-size=1000, all Asia/Bangkok (assumed; owner RW-COMPLY).
- The Compliance and PDPA officer group and the platform administrator group are set in the ACE notification path.

1. Quartz: fires JOB-14 at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok for the business date of the previous day.
2. Job (HashChainCheckJob): checks that JOB-13 for the same business date has ended; if not, waits and checks again every 5 minutes until 04:00, then runs and records that JOB-13 had not ended.
3. Job: reads the highest chain_seq at the start and fixes it as the end of the run; entries appended later are checked the next night.
4. Job: calls HashChainVerifier over chain_seq 1 to the end in batches of 1,000, recomputing each entry_hash and checking each prev_hash.
5. Job: counts every entry that fails and keeps the first.
6. Job: writes the job run record with type JOB-14, business date, status and checks: entries checked, last chain_seq, last entry_hash, result, first break chain_seq and entry ID, failing count.
7. Job: sends MSG-P7-007 to Compliance when the chain is intact, or MSG-P7-008 with an incident when it is broken.
8. Job: on an error that stops the run, records status FAILED, alerts the platform administrator and sends MSG-P7-013 to Compliance.
9. Platform administrator: can rerun the job for the business date from the job monitor; a rerun is a new run record.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An entry does not match its hash or its prev_hash | Run result BROKEN; first break and failing count recorded; incident; Compliance told | MSG-P7-008 | AC2, AC7 |
| X2 | The run stops on an error, for example a lost database connection | Status FAILED; platform administrator alerted; Compliance told the check did not complete | MSG-P7-013 | AC3 |
| X3 | The job is rerun for the same business date | A new run record with the same checks; the report says it is a rerun; no second scheduled run starts | MSG-P7-007 or MSG-P7-008 | AC4 |
| X4 | The log is empty | Result INTACT with count 0 and the genesis hash | MSG-P7-007 | AC5 |
| X5 | JOB-13 has not ended at 02:00 | The job waits up to 04:00, then runs and records the late copy | MSG-P7-007 or MSG-P7-008 | AC6 |
| X6 | Entries are appended while the job runs | They are outside this run and are checked the next night | None | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the verifier from RWB-E1-008 and the scheduler from RWB-TE-007 |
| Negotiable | Start times and batch size are parameters |
| Valuable | A changed entry is found by the morning after it is changed |
| Estimable | One Quartz job, one report, no screen |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a load test at the busiest-hour volume, run in SIT before each release, that fails the release stage when a screen request is too slow**, so that **response targets are proven before users feel them**.

About 370 staff and 50 partner users are online in the busiest hour (NFR-002, NFR-003), and every screen must respond in under 2 seconds (NFR-008). A screen that is fast with ten testers can be slow with four hundred users on 23,600 cases. The harness runs the busiest hour on the SIT data set before each release and stops the release stage when a target is missed. It proves the response of the case record view (REQ-OCC-007) and the team manager's case list (REQ-WKM-002) under load. The measure is the 95th percentile response time per screen request in the busiest hour.

- RWB-TE-004 is done: SIT holds at least 23,600 open cases read from the ACE views (NFR-001).
- SIT has named test users for each role in the operation mix (roles.txt key: test users before the release that gives a role real users), with Entra ID groups per DL40.
- An SIT deployment slot is booked for the run (DL35).
- The operation mix file and the pass criteria are loaded in the harness configuration: 410 virtual users at 3 requests a minute each; 95th percentile under 2,000 ms per operation; error rate under 1 percent (assumed; DL11).
- The build under test is deployed to SIT with its feature flags as planned for the release.

1. Release pipeline: starts the SIT performance stage for the build, or a squad member starts it by hand.
2. Harness: takes the SIT run lock; refuses to start when another run holds it.
3. Harness: counts open cases through GET /api/recovery/v1/cases and refuses to start when fewer than 23,600 are found.
4. Harness: signs in the test users for each role in the mix.
5. Harness: ramps to 410 virtual users over 10 minutes, then holds 60 minutes at 3 requests a minute per user, following the weights in the mix file.
6. Harness: records the response time and status of each request; 403 responses on operations the mix marks as refusals count as expected.
7. Harness: computes the 50th, 95th and 99th percentiles, the throughput and the error rate per operation over the 60 steady minutes.
8. Gate: passes when every operation's 95th percentile is under 2,000 ms and the error rate is under 1 percent; otherwise fails the stage.
9. Harness: attaches the report to the release record with the build ID, releases the lock and triggers the restore of the SIT data set.

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a pipeline check that finds personal data in code, test fixtures, log statements and error messages, built from the data dictionary's list of personal fields**, so that **personal data never leaks into code or logs**.

Customer names, identifier masks, dates of birth, contact values and interaction summaries are personal data under PDPA. A log line that prints a customer, or a test fixture copied from a real record, puts that data where masking does not apply: in log stores, in build artifacts and in prompts to coding agents. The lint reads the personal fields from the data dictionary and fails the build when code, fixtures, logs or error messages carry them. Under D-RCV-35 the fields it guards are the columns of the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and the Workbench tables beside them: `v_ace_customer` exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` and no clear identity number, and `v_ace_contact` exposes `contact_value_masked` for display. A log line that carries `contact_value` or `id_no_last4` is a finding in the same way a copied name is. It meets REQ-RDF-010 and REQ-ACA-005 (personal data masked by role, which a log line bypasses) and the target NFR-054. The measure is the count of personal data findings merged to main, which must stay at zero.

- RWB-TE-001 is done: the recovery folders and the pipeline checks exist.
- The data dictionary marks each personal field (the `is_personal` column of the metadata table sys_fields in the schema, and `x-personal-data: true` in the API specification).
- Synthetic test data uses the prefix "SYN-" for every value placed in a personal field (assumed convention of RWB-E1-065).
- The masking helper of the common module is available for the rare log line that must name a record (assumed published as part of the common module's PII logging interface).

1. Build: reads the personal fields from the sys_fields seed, including every `is_personal` column of a `recovery.v_ace_*` view, and from the API specification.
2. Build: generates the lint rule set from the field list: Java getter names, entity class names, view names, JSON property names and TypeScript property names.
3. Lint: scans `src/main` and the front end source for log calls, string building in log calls and exception messages that use a personal field or a whole personal entity.
4. Lint: scans `src/test`, end-to-end tests, SQL seed files and JSON fixtures for literals in personal field positions that do not start with "SYN-", and for values that match a Thai national identifier with a valid check digit, a Thai mobile number or an email address outside the example domains.
5. Lint: checks that each entity with a personal field excludes it from its text form.
6. Lint: compares each finding with the allow list; an entry past its expiry does not excuse the finding.
7. Pipeline: fails the build on any finding and prints the rule, the file, the line and the field, without printing the value found.
None.

As a **platform administrator**, I want **blob containers for documents, with a write-once container for legal types, reached by managed identity**, so that **legal documents cannot be overwritten**.

Audit findings record that evidence for decisions was incomplete or unreliable, and a notice or contract held in a shared folder can be replaced without trace. This story sets up the storage that the document store (RWB-E1-024), the intake (RWB-E1-057) and the malware scan (RWB-E1-041) write to: an intake container, a standard container with version history, a write-once container whose immutability policy refuses any overwrite or delete inside its retention period, and a quarantine container, all reached only by managed identity. It meets REQ-DCM-003 and REQ-DCM-002 and is the storage behind control CTL-12 and the storage pattern recommended under DL27.

- RWB-TE-001 (recovery module folder and boundary test) is done.
- The ACE storage pattern is used (DL27, option A recommended): one storage account per environment in the SCB tenant with a private endpoint.
- The managed identities RWB-DEV-SY-OCR, RWB-SIT-SY-OCR, RWB-UAT-SY-OCR and RWB-PROD-SY-OCR exist, and the ACE service has its own managed identity in each environment.
- The retention period of the write-once policy is assumed at 3,650 days (10 years), matching the class LEGAL10Y, until the bank retention schedule is supplied (DL26).
- The infrastructure pipeline of the ACE repository can apply storage templates to DEV and SIT.

1. Platform administrator: applies the infrastructure template for the environment, which sets the storage account (shared key access off, public network access off, TLS 1.2 minimum, private endpoint) and creates the containers rwb-intake, rwb-docs, rwb-docs-legal and rwb-quarantine.
2. Template: turns on blob versioning and soft delete for rwb-docs, sets the time-based immutability policy on rwb-docs-legal (locked in PROD, unlocked in DEV, SIT and UAT), and assigns roles: the ACE service identity on rwb-intake, rwb-docs and rwb-docs-legal; SY-OCR on rwb-intake, rwb-docs and rwb-quarantine.
3. System: on start, StorageReadinessIndicator checks that the four containers exist and that rwb-docs-legal has its immutability policy; the document hub reports ready only if both hold.
4. Document store (RWB-E1-024): writes each file through BlobStorageAdapter with the managed identity, to rwb-docs-legal for a write-once type and to rwb-docs for any other type, at the name {caseId}/{documentId}/v{docVersion}.
5. Any client: an overwrite or delete of a blob in rwb-docs-legal is refused by the storage service; StorageErrorMapper turns the refusal into WriteOnceViolationException, which the store maps to 409 MSG-P5-002, and the attempt is written to the ACE audit log.
6. Document store: a new version is a new blob at v{n+1}; the earlier blob stays readable.
7. Platform administrator: sees the document hub readiness on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor.
