As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **one client in the recovery module that calls the agent orchestrator, applies the autonomy mode, runs shadow mode and falls back to the rule result**, so that **agents are added to a case step without changing the case flow, and every step records what the agent did**.

A case step that waits on an agent with no limit stops the case, and a step that acts on an unchecked answer breaks the rule that a person decides. The client puts every agent call behind one interface: the rule result always exists, the agent answer is used only as the autonomy mode allows, and the decision log entry records the rule, agent and prompt versions and any fallback (REQ-DRI-001). If the entry cannot be written, the step does not act (REQ-DRI-005). The measure is the agent fallback rate, target below 10 percent per month.

- RWB-TE-007 is done: Quartz jobs and their run books exist, so a job step can call the client.
- RWB-E1-058 is done: AgentOrchestrator, agent_policy and agent_run exist.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 DecisionLogWriter interface writes entries and throws on failure.
- An approved agent_policy row exists for the agent, with autonomy_mode SHADOW or L1 and timeout_seconds 60.
- The calling module runs under its own service identity (for example SY-CASEWF) and has evaluated its rule before it calls the client.

1. Calling step (for example SY-CASEWF): evaluates its rule and builds the rule result (rule ID, rule version, next state).
2. Calling step: calls AgentStepClient.runStep with the agent code, case ID, decision code, step key and rule result.
3. Client: reads the autonomy mode from the agent policy in force; if it is OFF or the flag is off, it skips the agent.
4. Client: calls AgentOrchestrator.run with the idempotency key built from the step key and waits at most timeout_seconds.
5. Client: in SHADOW mode, keeps the rule result as the applied result and records the agent answer only.
6. Client: in L1 mode, keeps the rule result as the applied result and returns the checked agent answer as the recommendation for the person who decides.
7. Client: on a timeout or a guardrail failure, keeps the rule result and marks fallback true with the reason (R-UNI-32).
8. Client: writes one decision log entry through DecisionLogWriter with the rule ID and version, agent version, model version, recommendation and fallback, then links it to the agent run.
9. Calling step: acts on the applied result only after the entry is written.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The agent does not answer within 60 seconds | Rule result applied; fallback true with reason TIMED_OUT; step continues | None to a user | AC2 |
| X2 | The answer fails a guardrail check | Rule result applied; fallback true with the check code | None to a user | AC4 |
| X3 | No approved policy exists for the agent on the business date | No agent call; rule result applied; fallback true with reason NO_POLICY | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | The decision log write fails | The step does not act; the case stays in its state; an incident is raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The same step key arrives twice | One agent run and one decision log entry; the repeat returns the first outcome (R-UNI-40) | None to a user | AC7 |
| X6 | Autonomy mode OFF or flag `rwb.agent.client` off | No agent call; rule result applied; fallback false; no agent run row | None to a user | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right reads agent runs | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-TE-013-09 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the orchestrator (RWB-E1-058), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) and the job pattern (RWB-TE-007); no agent story |
| Negotiable | The mode and timeout per agent are data; the client fixes only the order: rule first, agent second, log before action |
| Valuable | Every agent from RWB-E1-059 onward plugs into case steps through this one interface |
| Estimable | One published interface, one service, one decision log mapping, no screen, no table of its own beyond one link column |
| Small | One developer, under one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a unit or component test with a stubbed orchestrator and a stubbed decision log writer |

```gherkin
Feature: Agent runtime client with fallback

 Background:
 Given agent "INTAKE" has approved policy "P1" with timeout 60 seconds and prompt "PR1"
 Given case "RW-2026-000201" is in route state "NEW" and status "New"
 Given the calling step has rule result rule "R-UNI-32" version "2026.11" with next state "RESUME_STATE"

 Scenario: AC1 Shadow
 Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "SHADOW"
 When the agent answers in 2,000 ms with a valid output
 Then the system stores the agent answer on the agent run and the rule result is the applied result
 Then one decision log entry holds agent version "INTAKE@P1/PR1", the rule ID and version, recommendation null and fallback false in actions
 Then the calling step receives the rule result and no agent output

 Scenario: AC2 No answer
 Given the agent does not answer in 60 seconds
 When the step runs
 Then the system uses the rule result and the step continues to "RESUME_STATE"
 Then the decision log entry holds actions fallback true with reason "TIMED_OUT" and the agent run ID (R-UNI-32)
 Then the agent run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true

 Scenario: AC3 Assisted mode returns the answer as a recommendation
 Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "L1"
 When the agent answers with confidence 0.91
 Then the rule result is the applied result
 Then the outcome returns the agent answer as the recommendation for the person who decides
 Then the decision log entry holds the agent answer in recommendation with confidence 0.91

 Scenario: AC4 A guardrail failure falls back
 Given the agent answer fails check "SCHEMA"
 When the step runs
 Then the system applies the rule result
 Then the decision log entry holds actions fallback true with reason "SCHEMA"

 Scenario: AC5 No approved policy
 Given agent "INTAKE" has no approved policy on 2026-11-30
 When the step runs on 2026-11-30
 Then the system makes no orchestrator call
 Then the system applies the rule result with fallback true and reason "NO_POLICY" in the decision log entry

 Scenario: AC6 The decision log write fails
 Given the decision log writer throws on write
 When the step runs
 Then the calling step does not act and case "RW-2026-000201" stays in "NEW"
 Then the client raises DecisionNotRecordedException carrying MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised (R-UNI-39)
 Then the agent run stays with decision_log_id empty

 Scenario: AC7 A repeated step key
 Given the step with key "CASEWF:RW-2026-000201:ENTRY:2026-11-30" ran once
 When it runs again with the same key
 Then one agent run and one decision log entry exist for the key
 Then the second call returns the first outcome (R-UNI-40)

 Scenario: AC8 Agent switched off
 Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "OFF"
 When the step runs
 Then no orchestrator call and no agent run row are made
 Then the decision log entry holds agent version null and fallback false
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The rule result is computed before the agent is called and is always the applied result in SHADOW and L1 | Agent catalog autonomy levels; agent_policy.autonomy_mode (New) |
| BR2 | If the agent does not answer within agent_policy.timeout_seconds (60, assumed; DL11), the rule result is used and the fallback is recorded on the decision | R-UNI-32 |
| BR3 | A step acts only after its decision log entry is written | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR4 | The decision log entry holds the rule ID, rule version, agent version as "<agent>@<policy>/<prompt>", model version and the recommendation | REQ-DRI-001; decision_log_entry.agent_version |
| BR5 | The idempotency key of the agent run is the step key | R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | The client runs under the identity of the calling module; the orchestrator runs tools as SY-AGENT | REQ-ACA-010 |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE | AGENT_UNAVAILABLE | The agent or the model does not answer inside the timeout (R-UNI-32) | RESUME_STATE, with the rule result applied |
| ANY_ACTIVE | DECISION_LOG_WRITE_FAILED | The entry cannot be written (R-UNI-39) | EXCEPTION_QUEUE, raised by the calling step |

The client does not change a case status itself; the calling step moves the case on the applied result.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-CASEWF and other calling module identities | Call AgentStepClient; write the decision log entry through P7 (Decision log C) |
| SY-AGENT | Runs the agent and its tools (read only) |
| SY-DECLOG | Writes the entry |
| RW-PLATADM, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-DATASTEW, RW-SECADM | Read agent runs and fallbacks through GET /admin/agent-runs (Platform administration R) |

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case | id | Read |
| DF-CAS-007 | recovery_case | route_state | Read |
| DF-REF-002 | rule_row | rule_id | Read (from the rule result passed in) |
| DF-REF-003 | rule_row | rule_version | Read (from the rule result passed in) |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write (through the P7 DecisionLogWriter) |
| DF-AGT-008 | agent_policy | autonomy_mode | Read |
| DF-AGT-012 | agent_policy | timeout_seconds | Read |
| DF-AGT-021 | agent_policy | status | Read |
| DF-AGT-022 | agent_policy | valid_from | Read |
| DF-AGT-036 | agent_run | id | Read |
| DF-AGT-046 | agent_run | status | Read |
| DF-AGT-047 | agent_run | fallback | Read |
| DF-AGT-045 | agent_run | idempotency_key | Read |
| DF-AGT-058 | agent_run | decision_log_id | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/agent/api/` and `.../recovery/agent/client/`, Java packages `recovery.agent.api` (interface and records) and `recovery.agent.client` (implementation).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AgentStepClient | Published interface | The only way another module calls an agent |
| AgentStepClientImpl | Service | Mode check, timed orchestrator call, fallback, decision log write, link to run |
| AutonomyModeResolver | Service | Reads the policy in force for the agent and date |
| DecisionLogMapper | Service | Builds the P7 entry from the request, the rule result and the run |
| AgentRunRepository | Repository | Sets agent_run.decision_log_id |

**Database:** reads agent_policy and agent_run; adds column decision_log_id uuid to agent_run in migration `V10_002__agent_run_decision_link.sql`. No new table.

**Configuration and reference data:** agent_policy rows (RW-COE loads, RW-RISK approves). Feature flag in the ACE flag service.

**Build steps**
1. Write the interface and records in `recovery.agent.api`, with an ArchUnit test that other modules import only this package.
2. Build AutonomyModeResolver with tests for OFF, SHADOW, L1 and no policy (AC5, AC8).
3. Build the timed call with a CompletableFuture and the policy timeout; test with a stub that sleeps 61 seconds on a fake clock (AC2).
4. Build DecisionLogMapper and the write before return; test write failure (AC1, AC3, AC6).
5. Build the idempotent repeat on the step key (AC7) and the guardrail fallback (AC4).

**Feature flag:** `rwb.agent.client`. Off: no agent call; the rule result is applied and logged with agent version null.

**Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass and the boundary test shows other modules depend only on `recovery.agent.api`.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write fails and the step does not act | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right reads agent runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
No screen in this story. A fallback shows in GET /admin/agent-runs (fallback true) and on the decision log entry of the case.

| ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-TE-013-01 | AC1, BR1, BR4 | System | Case RW-2026-000201, mode SHADOW, answer in 2,000 ms |
| TC-TE-013-02 | AC2, BR2 | System | Orchestrator stub silent for 61 seconds |
| TC-TE-013-03 | AC3, BR1 | System | Mode L1, confidence 0.91 |
| TC-TE-013-04 | AC4 | System | Answer fails check SCHEMA |
| TC-TE-013-05 | AC5 | System | No approved policy on 2026-11-30 |
| TC-TE-013-06 | AC6, BR3 | System | Decision log writer throws |
| TC-TE-013-07 | AC7, BR5 | System | Step key CASEWF:RW-2026-000201:ENTRY:2026-11-30 twice |
| TC-TE-013-08 | AC8 | System | Mode OFF |
| TC-TE-013-09 | Access | Access | RW-CASEOWN calls GET /admin/agent-runs; refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| TC-TE-013-10 | Principle 5 | Resilience | Decision log write forced to fail during a step in SHADOW mode; step does not act; MSG-P7-003 |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v5.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

- No business value in code: mode and timeout come from the approved agent policy.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; the inputs snapshot is masked before it is referenced.
- No read of another module's tables; the decision log is written only through the P7 interface.
- The client never applies an agent answer as the case result in SHADOW or L1.

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | BRD section | Feature | L3 process | Rules | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-DRI-001 | Every decision records rule, model, agent and prompt versions | Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 | FEAT-AGT-11 | All recovery processes | R-UNI-32 | TC-TE-013-01, TC-TE-013-02, TC-TE-013-03, TC-TE-013-04 |
| REQ-DRI-005 | No action proceeds if its decision log entry cannot be written | Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 | FEAT-AGT-11 | All recovery processes | R-UNI-39 | TC-TE-013-06, TC-TE-013-10 |
| REQ-ACA-010 | Agents run under service identities with the same role checks | Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 | FEAT-AGT-01 | All recovery processes | R-UNI-40 | TC-TE-013-05, TC-TE-013-07, TC-TE-013-08, TC-TE-013-09 |

- The orchestrator, gateway and guardrail checker (RWB-E1-058).
- Agent answers acted on without a person (autonomy L2 and above, Epic 8, FEAT-AGT-15).
- The case steps that call the client: case intake (RWB-E2-028), deviation screening (RWB-E2-029).

Then when JOB-02 succeeds for 2026-12-03 at 08:10 JOB-03 runs for 2026-12-03   Scenario: AC8 Instance stops part way  Given JOB-04 is running for 2026-12-02 on "ACE-1"  When "ACE-1" stops  Then "ACE-2" runs JOB-04 again for 2026-12-02 within the cluster check-in interval of 20 seconds  Then the run log shows one "FAILED" run on "ACE-1" and one "SUCCEEDED" run on "ACE-2"   Scenario: AC9 Allocation late  Given JOB-03 for 2026-12-02 has not succeeded at 07:00  When the deadline check runs at 07:00  Then an alert with MSG-P3-031 naming JOB-03, 2026-12-02 and 07:00 reaches the operations channel by 07:15
RWB-TE-008 | Decision log hash chain check | Feature: Decision log hash chain check   Background:  Given the environment is SIT with the synthetic decision log  Given JOB-13 for business date 2 December 2026 ended at 01:40 on 3 December 2026   Scenario: AC1 Chain intact  Given the decision log holds 48,210 entries and none has been changed  When JOB-14 runs at 02:00 on 3 December 2026  Then the job run record shows type "JOB-14", business date 2 December 2026, status "COMPLETED" and result "INTACT"  Then its checks hold entries checked 48,210, last chain_seq 48,210 and that entry's entry_hash  Then MSG-P7-007 with the count and the last hash is sent to the Compliance group   Scenario: AC2 Break  Given the actions of the entry with chain_seq 30,005 were changed in the SIT database with the trigger disabled  When JOB-14 runs  Then the run result is "BROKEN" with first break chain_seq 30,005 and its entry ID  Then the system raises an incident and MSG-P7-008 with the entry ID is sent to the Compliance group before 08:00 on 3 December 2026   Scenario: AC3 A run that stops is reported  Given the database connection is closed in the test double after 20,000 entries  When JOB-14 runs  Then the run status is "FAILED" with entries checked 20,000  Then the system alerts the platform administrator group  Then the system sends MSG-P7-013 to the Compliance group with the date of the last complete check, 2 December 2026   Scenario: AC4 A rerun gives a new record and no second scheduled run  Given JOB-14 for business date 2 December 2026 failed at 02:20  When test user "U-9301" holding RW-PLATADM reruns it from the job monitor at 08:30  Then a second run record for business date 2 December 2026 is written with rerun true  Then the system marks the report to Compliance as a rerun  Then while the rerun is running a second start of JOB-14 is refused by the scheduler   Scenario: AC5 An empty log is intact  Given the decision log holds no entry  When JOB-14 runs  Then the result is "INTACT" with entries checked 0 and last hash of 64 zeros   Scenario: AC6 The job waits for the decision log copy  Given JOB-13 for business date 2 December 2026 is still running at 02:00 and ends at 02:25  When JOB-14 fires at 02:00  Then it starts the check at 02:25 and records the JOB-13 end time  Then if JOB-13 has not ended by 04:00 the check starts at 04:00 with the note "JOB-13 not ended"   Scenario: AC7 Several changed entries  Given the entries with chain_seq 12,001 and 40,350 were changed in the SIT database  When JOB-14 runs  Then the first break is chain_seq 12,001 and the failing count is 2  Then one incident and one MSG-P7-008 report name both entry IDs   Scenario: AC8 Entries written during the run  Given the log holds 48,210 entries when JOB-14 starts  Given 37 entries are appended while it runs  When the run ends  Then entries checked is 48,210 and last chain_seq is 48,210  Then the next night's run checks 48,247 entries
RWB-TE-009 | Performance test harness | None. The former criteria covered development and delivery procedures and have been removed from the story set.
RWB-TE-010 | Browser and accessibility tests | None. The former criteria covered development and delivery procedures and have been removed from the story set.
RWB-TE-011 | PDPA lint for code, tests and logs | None. The former criteria covered development and delivery procedures and have been removed from the story set.
RWB-TE-012 | Document storage containers | Feature: Document storage containers   Background:  Given the SIT storage account has containers "rwb-intake", "rwb-docs", "rwb-docs-legal" and "rwb-quarantine"  Given "rwb-docs-legal" has a time-based immutability policy of 3650 days   Scenario: AC1 Write-once  Given court notice "DOC-0701" stored at "rwb-docs-legal/RW-2026-000701/DOC-0701/v1" with hash "H701"  When a client using the ACE service managed identity tries to overwrite it  Then storage refuses the write with "BlobImmutableDueToPolicy"  Then the blob hash is still "H701"  Then the attempt is in the audit log with the identity and the time  Then DocumentStore.replaceContent for "DOC-0701" raises WriteOnceViolationException, shown as 409 with MSG-P5-002   Scenario: AC2 Delete is refused  Given court notice "DOC-0701" in "rwb-docs-legal"  When a client using the ACE service managed identity tries to delete it  Then storage refuses the delete  Then the blob is still readable   Scenario: AC3 A new blob in the write-once container is allowed  Given court notice "DOC-0701" at "v1" in "rwb-docs-legal"  When the ACE service identity writes "rwb-docs-legal/RW-2026-000701/DOC-0701/v2"  Then the write succeeds and both "v1" and "v2" are readable   Scenario: AC4 The standard container keeps earlier versions  Given "rwb-docs/RW-2026-000702/DOC-0702/v1" holds an appraisal report  When the blob is overwritten by the ACE service identity in SIT  Then the previous blob version is still readable through blob versioning  Then a deleted blob can be restored within the 30 days of soft delete   Scenario: AC5 The identities hold only their roles  Given the role assignments applied by the template in SIT  When the assignments are listed  Then the ACE service identity holds Storage Blob Data Contributor on "rwb-intake", "rwb-docs" and "rwb-docs-legal" only  Then "RWB-SIT-SY-OCR" holds Storage Blob Data Contributor on "rwb-intake", "rwb-docs" and "rwb-quarantine" only   Scenario: AC6 Key-based access is refused  Given the storage account has shared key access disabled  When a client calls "rwb-docs" with the account key or with a shared access signature  Then storage refuses the request with "KeyBasedAuthenticationNotPermitted"   Scenario: AC7 An identity with no role is refused  Given managed identity "RWB-SIT-SY-AGENT" has no role on "rwb-docs-legal"  When it tries to read "rwb-docs-legal/RW-2026-000701/DOC-0701/v1"  Then storage refuses with "AuthorizationPermissionMismatch"   Scenario: AC8 Public network access is refused  Given public network access is disabled on the storage account  When a client outside the private endpoint calls the account  Then the system refuses the request   Scenario: AC9 A missing immutability policy stops the document hub  Given the immutability policy is removed from "rwb-docs-legal" in DEV  When the service starts  Then the readiness check reports the document hub as not ready, naming "rwb-docs-legal"  Then an upload through POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents returns 503 with MSG-GEN-006  Then the system writes no document row   Scenario: AC10 Storage does not answer  Given the storage account does not answer within 10 seconds  When BlobStorageAdapter writes a file to "rwb-docs"  Then it raises StorageUnavailableException after 10 seconds  Then the upload endpoint returns 503 with MSG-GEN-006   Scenario: AC11 The quarantine container is closed to user sessions  Given file "Q-0001" in "rwb-quarantine"  When the ACE service tries to read it on behalf of a case owner  Then the system refuses the read  Then only "RWB-SIT-SY-OCR" can write to "rwb-quarantine"   Scenario: AC12 A repeated write of the same file is not an overwrite  Given "rwb-docs-legal/RW-2026-000703/DOC-0703/v1" holds a file with hash "H703"  When BlobStorageAdapter is asked to write the same file with hash "H703" to the same name  Then the system attempts no overwrite and the existing blob reference is returned  Then the same name with a different hash raises WriteOnceViolationException
RWB-TE-013 | Agent runtime client with fallback | Feature: Agent runtime client with fallback   Background:  Given agent "INTAKE" has approved policy "P1" with timeout 60 seconds and prompt "PR1"  Given case "RW-2026-000201" is in route state "NEW" and status "New"  Given the calling step has rule result rule "R-UNI-32" version "2026.11" with next state "RESUME_STATE"   Scenario: AC1 Shadow  Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "SHADOW"  When the agent answers in 2,000 ms with a valid output  Then the system stores the agent answer on the agent run and the rule result is the applied result  Then one decision log entry holds agent version "INTAKE@P1/PR1", the rule ID and version, recommendation null and fallback false in actions  Then the calling step receives the rule result and no agent output   Scenario: AC2 No answer  Given the agent does not answer in 60 seconds  When the step runs  Then the system uses the rule result and the step continues to "RESUME_STATE"  Then the decision log entry holds actions fallback true with reason "TIMED_OUT" and the agent run ID (R-UNI-32)  Then the agent run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true   Scenario: AC3 Assisted mode returns the answer as a recommendation  Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "L1"  When the agent answers with confidence 0.91  Then the rule result is the applied result  Then the outcome returns the agent answer as the recommendation for the person who decides  Then the decision log entry holds the agent answer in recommendation with confidence 0.91   Scenario: AC4 A guardrail failure falls back  Given the agent answer fails check "SCHEMA"  When the step runs  Then the system applies the rule result  Then the decision log entry holds actions fallback true with reason "SCHEMA"   Scenario: AC5 No approved policy  Given agent "INTAKE" has no approved policy on 2026-11-30  When the step runs on 2026-11-30  Then the system makes no orchestrator call  Then the system applies the rule result with fallback true and reason "NO_POLICY" in the decision log entry   Scenario: AC6 The decision log write fails  Given the decision log writer throws on write  When the step runs  Then the calling step does not act and case "RW-2026-000201" stays in "NEW"  Then the client raises DecisionNotRecordedException carrying MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised (R-UNI-39)  Then the agent run stays with decision_log_id empty   Scenario: AC7 A repeated step key  Given the step with key "CASEWF:RW-2026-000201:ENTRY:2026-11-30" ran once  When it runs again with the same key  Then one agent run and one decision log entry exist for the key  Then the second call returns the first outcome (R-UNI-40)   Scenario: AC8 Agent switched off  Given the policy of "INTAKE" has autonomy mode "OFF"  When the step runs  Then no orchestrator call and no agent run row are made  Then the decision log entry holds agent version null and fallback false

Release 30 November 2026. Epic 1 status: confirmed. This version is re-based on decision D-RCV-35 and ADR-010, agreed on 15 November 2026, the ACE re-base: the Workbench takes no inbound source data, ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads ACE only through the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views built by RWB-E1-069, 16 Section A views now and 14 Section B views once RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43). The eight data load, inventory and retirement stories removed by the re-base, RWB-E1-003, RWB-E1-004, RWB-E1-005, RWB-E1-006, RWB-E1-009, RWB-E1-010, RWB-E1-012 and RWB-E1-051, are not in this file. The 11 technical enabler stories for Epic 1 are included.

Each story is written for build: the business rationale, preconditions, the main flow and its exception paths, acceptance criteria in Gherkin, business rules, state transitions, authority, the fields it reads and writes with their BR Field IDs, the contract, the solution plan, messages, screens, test cases and traceability to the business requirements. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and Physical Schema v5, endpoints those in the API Specification, messages those in the Error and Message Standard and requirement IDs those in the Business Requirements. The same stories are also supplied one file per story, to hand to a coding agent with the module specifications.

secs.h: RWB-E1-001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-001 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-01 Create the recovery tables and extension tables in the ACE database; FEAT-RDF-02 Define the 14 data products and their systems of record |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5); ADR-010; DL43 open |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **the 92 recovery tables for the 14 data products created in the ACE database, with a data dictionary that covers those tables and the 30 read-only ACE views, and one system of record and one owner per data product**, so that **every Workbench record has one home and every data product has one accountable owner and one read path**.

The Workbench holds no copy of source data. ACE ingests ALS, SCBPDM, EFS, COLLINS, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID, and the Workbench reads what it needs through the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views (D-RCV-35 U1 and U4, ADR-010). This story creates the 88 Workbench tables, the four extension tables that hold a Workbench decision about an ACE record, the metadata registry that holds the data dictionary as data, and the catalog of the 14 data products DP01 to DP14. Each data product then has exactly one system of record, written "ACE (ingested from X)" for source data, "Recovery Workbench" for Workbench records, or one sentence naming both where the product holds both, and one named owner, as REQ-RDF-001 requires. The measure it serves is "the ACE batch is complete when the Workbench reads it on 99 percent of days", because the dictionary and the catalog are what every later read and every freshness stamp are resolved against.

- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway runs in the ACE pipeline and takes the schema name from the parameter `recoverySchema`.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service accepts a validated load for a table code and calls the handler that the owning module provides.
- The DEV and SIT databases of the ACE service exist and the pipeline service identity may run migrations in the recovery schema.
- The reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) holds Reference data C. The person who queries the dictionary view has read access to the recovery schema in DEV or SIT.
- The catalog load file for the 14 data products is prepared from the seed table in section 13, with an owner user ID for each product in that environment (synthetic test users in DEV and SIT).
- The Section A and Section B views are not created here. RWB-E1-069 ships the 16 Section A views as V0002 after V0001, and the 14 Section B views as V0003 once RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).

1. Pipeline: runs migration `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` in DEV with `recoverySchema = recovery`.
2. Migration: creates the 92 tables (the 88 Workbench tables and the four extension tables), their indexes, the append-only triggers on `decision_log_entry` and `interaction`, and the catalog table `data_product`, in one transaction.
3. Migration: inserts the 14 `data_product` rows, then the 122 `sys_objects` rows and the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows (section 13), and creates the view `v_data_dictionary`.
4. Migration: adds `fk_sys_objects_data_product`; `sys_objects.data_product` is nullable, so the 24 operational objects of OPS, AGT and RPT carry no product.
5. Pipeline: runs the dictionary conformance test, which compares every column of the 92 tables in the recovery schema with `sys_fields` (1,062 fields).
6. Pipeline: repeats steps 1 to 5 in SIT.
7. Reference data administrator: loads the data product catalog file with table code `data_product` through `POST /admin/reference-loads`, naming the owner user ID of each product for the environment.
8. System: `DataProductCatalogHandler.validate` checks the file: 14 products DP01 to DP14, each with one system of record written "ACE (ingested from X)", "Recovery Workbench" or one sentence naming both, one owner role from LOV-ROLE, one owner user ID and one refresh cycle.
9. Data steward: confirms the load as owner of the catalog through the reference data change process (RWB-E1-043).
10. System: `DataProductCatalogHandler.apply` writes the 14 rows in one transaction with the valid from date.
11. Developer or data steward: queries `v_data_dictionary` for entity `v_ace_account` and field `days_past_due`.
12. System: returns field ID DF-ACE-018, data type NUMBER, physical type integer, source system ACE, source field `public.account.delay_days`, data product DP01, system of record "ACE (ingested from ALS)", refresh cycle DAILY and the owner of DP01.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A statement in the migration fails | The transaction rolls back; no table is left half created; the pipeline stage fails with the statement named | None (pipeline log) | AC4 |
| X2 | A table column exists with no sys_fields row, or a sys_fields row has no column or a different physical type | The conformance test fails and names the table, the column and the field ID | None (pipeline log) | AC5 |
| X3 | The migration runs again on a schema where it is already applied | Flyway skips it; no table or row changes | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A catalog row names no system of record, two systems of record, a bare source name such as "CCMS", or no owner user ID | The whole load is refused; no row is written | MSG-P1-003 | AC7, AC11 |
| X5 | The catalog file does not hold exactly the 14 products DP01 to DP14 | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | A catalog row names an owner role or refresh cycle outside its list | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-007 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same catalog file is loaded again | Nothing is written; the load is reported as already done | MSG-P1-011 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Reference data C loads the catalog | 403 Problem response; the refusal is in the access log | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-001-11 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the migration tooling (RWB-E1-044) and the reference load service (RWB-E1-043); every later read, the case list and the data dictionary story (RWB-E1-064) build on this one |
| Negotiable | The catalog values (names, definitions, owners, refresh cycles) are data in a load file; the story fixes the tables and the checks |
| Valuable | Gives every Workbench record one home, every data product one accountable owner and every source read one dictionary entry |
| Estimable | One migration, one view, one conformance test, one reference table handler |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery tables for the 14 data products

 Scenario: AC1 Schema deployed
 Given the migration V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql and the parameter recoverySchema = "recovery"
 When the pipeline applies it in DEV and then in SIT
 Then the recovery schema in each environment holds 92 tables: the 88 Workbench tables and the four extension tables party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext
 Then it holds none of the tables that left the schema: loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, party_product, valuation, score, asset, load_run, dq_exception, dq_rule, source_field_map, source_code_map, interface_run, interface_signoff, tracker_inventory and tracker_row
 Then no constraint in schema recovery references a table in schema public
 Then every link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key: account_key, person_key, asset_key, payment_code and contact_key
 Then the conformance test reports 1,062 of the 1,062 table fields matched by name and physical type
 Then the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views ship separately in RWB-E1-069 and add their 304 fields to the dictionary

 Scenario: AC2 Dictionary published
 Given the data dictionary and the data product seed loaded by the migration, and the catalog loaded for DP01
 When a developer queries v_data_dictionary for entity "v_ace_account" and field "days_past_due"
 Then the row holds field ID "DF-ACE-018", data type "NUMBER", physical type "integer"
 Then source system "ACE", source field "public.account.delay_days"
 Then data product "DP01", system of record "ACE (ingested from ALS)", refresh cycle "DAILY", owner role "RW-DATASTEW" and the owner user ID of DP01
 Then the row for entity "account_ext" and field "dispute_open" holds field ID "DF-EXT-028", data type "BOOLEAN", physical type "boolean", source system "Workbench" and data product "DP01"

 Scenario: AC3 One system of record
 Given a catalog load file with the 14 rows DP01 to DP14, each with one system of record and one owner user ID
 When the reference data administrator loads it with valid from 2026-11-30
 Then data_product holds 14 rows
 Then each row has a definition, exactly one system of record and one owner user ID
 Then DP01 names system of record "ACE (ingested from ALS)" and refresh cycle "DAILY"
 Then DP03 names system of record "Recovery Workbench" and refresh cycle "ON_CHANGE"
 Then DP06 names system of record "ACE (ingested from CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and RPS)", refresh cycle "WEEKLY" and expected by "MON 08:00"

 Scenario: AC4 Failed migration leaves no partial schema
 Given a copy of the migration in which the statement creating table valuation_ext fails
 When the pipeline applies it in DEV
 Then the pipeline stage fails and names the failing statement
 Then the recovery schema holds none of the tables of that migration
 Then the Flyway history has no successful row for version 1.001

 Scenario: AC5 Column without a dictionary entry fails the build
 Given a branch that adds the column account_ext.branch_code with no sys_fields row
 When the conformance test runs in the pipeline
 Then the test fails with "account_ext.branch_code has no data dictionary entry"
 Then a sys_fields row DF-EXT-028 whose column is changed to type text fails the test with "DF-EXT-028 physical type boolean expected, text found"

 Scenario: AC6 Repeated migration has no effect
 Given the migration version 1.001 already applied in SIT
 When the pipeline runs again in SIT
 Then Flyway reports version 1.001 as already applied
 Then the row counts of sys_objects (122) and sys_fields (1,366) are unchanged

 Scenario: AC7 Catalog row with two systems of record is refused
 Given a catalog load file in which DP06 names system of record "ACE (ingested from CCMS); SVAF"
 Given DP11 has no owner user ID
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-003 for DP06 and for DP11
 Then data_product keeps the rows of the version in force

 Scenario: AC8 Catalog with a missing product is refused
 Given a catalog load file with 13 rows and no row for DP09
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-004 naming "DP09"
 Then the system writes no row

 Scenario: AC9 Value outside its list
 Given a catalog load file in which row 4 (DP04) names owner role "DP_OWNER" and row 5 (DP05) names refresh cycle "HOURLY"
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-007 "Row 4: owner_role must be one of the role codes in LOV-ROLE." and "Row 5: refresh_cycle must be one of DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, ON_CHANGE."

 Scenario: AC10 Same catalog file loaded again
 Given the catalog version loaded on 2026-11-30 is in force
 When the reference data administrator loads the same file again
 Then the system writes nothing
 Then the response carries MSG-P1-011 "The data product catalog load for 2026-11-30 is already complete or running. It was not run again."

 Scenario: AC11 Source named on its own is refused
 Given a catalog load file in which DP06 names system of record "CCMS"
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-003 "DP06 must name one system of record, written ACE (ingested from X) or Recovery Workbench, or both where the product holds both, and one named owner."
 Then no row is written and the version in force stays in use
```

| ID | Rule | Source |

| BR1 | Every table column and every view column in the recovery schema has exactly one row in the data dictionary, with its BR Field ID, types, source system and meaning | Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary; sys_fields |

| BR4 | The catalog values are a versioned data load, changed without a code release; a load with an exception is refused in full | Principle 1; DT02; CTL-08 |

| BR6 | Schema names come from parameters; one migration per story; forward only in PROD | RWB-E1-044 |

| BR9 | V0001 seeds the dictionary for the tables and the 30 views before the views exist; the view columns are matched from V0002 onward by the view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 | D-RCV-29 amended; RWB-E1-069 |
None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the Flyway version of the recovery schema (none to 1.001) and the version of the data product catalog (none to the first loaded version).

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and in Physical Schema v5. The 92 tables hold 1,062 fields: 1,013 on the 88 Workbench tables, including the 34 of data_product, sys_objects and sys_fields, and 49 on the four extension tables. The 30 views add 304 fields, so the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields.

Ruled 2026-11-06 as D-RCV-29 and amended by D-RCV-35: the baseline migration seeds the full recovery dictionary, 122 `sys_objects` rows and 1,366 `sys_fields` rows, as held in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql, so the dictionary is complete before the views exist and the conformance test can run. The 108 objects and 1,256 fields of the v4 copy schema are superseded. `delegation_limit` holds no baseline rows; its content is loaded as version DOA-2026.11 through RWB-E1-043 by RWB-E1-038 (D-RCV-34). **Dictionary view** `v_data_dictionary` (read model created by the migration; RWB-E1-064 builds the dictionary endpoint on it)

| Column | From |
|---|---|
| entity, data_product, entity_system_of_record | sys_objects |
| field, field_id, data_type, physical_type, is_mandatory, lov_code, references_object, source_system, source_field, is_personal, late_behavior, interface_id, description | sys_fields |
| product_system_of_record, refresh_cycle, owner_role, owner_user_id | data_product |

The view joins sys_fields to sys_objects on object_name and left joins data_product on product_code where the product is active, and returns active rows only. It reads no ACE table.

**Reference load handler** (published interface of P4 that P1 implements, from RWB-E1-043)

```java
public interface ReferenceTableHandler {
 String tableCode(); // returns "data_product"
 ValidationReport validate(ReferenceLoadFile file); // checks every row, writes nothing
 int apply(UUID loadId, ReferenceLoadFile file, LocalDate validFrom); // writes all rows in one transaction, returns the row count
}
```

The load itself is `POST /admin/reference-loads` (P4, Reference data C) with `table = data_product`, and its response is `ReferenceLoad`. A refused load returns 422 with MSG-P1-003, MSG-P1-004 or MSG-P1-007 in the Problem response; a caller without Reference data C gets 403 with MSG-P4-002. Idempotency: a file whose content hash matches the version in force is reported with MSG-P1-011 and writes nothing.

**Migration**

| Trigger | The ACE pipeline, on each deployment to DEV and SIT |
| Name | `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` with placeholder `${recoverySchema}` |
| Includes | The 92 tables, their indexes and triggers, data_product, the dictionary seed and v_data_dictionary. No `v_ace_*` view: those are V0002 and V0003 in RWB-E1-069 |
| Idempotency | The Flyway version 1.001; a changed checksum on an applied version fails the pipeline |
| Restart | A failed run rolls back; the next run applies the full version again |

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dataengine/catalog`, Java package `recovery.dataengine.catalog`; migration in `src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery`.

**Components**

| DataDictionaryConformanceTest | Test (pipeline) | Compares information_schema.columns with sys_fields in both directions for the 92 tables, ignoring the 7 standard columns |

**Database.** Creates the 92 tables of Physical Schema v5 and nothing else: no loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, party_product, valuation, score, asset, load_run, dq_exception, dq_rule, source_field_map, source_code_map, interface_run, interface_signoff, tracker_inventory or tracker_row. Creates data_product with product_code varchar(25) primary key, product_name varchar(80) not null, definition varchar(400) not null, system_of_record varchar(120) not null, owner_role varchar(20) not null, owner_user_id uuid, refresh_cycle varchar(10) not null with values DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY and ON_CHANGE, expected_by varchar(20), valid_from date not null and the 7 standard columns. Creates v_data_dictionary. Adds fk_sys_objects_data_product; sys_objects.data_product is nullable, so the 98 product objects name DP01 to DP14 and the 24 operational objects of OPS (13), AGT (8) and RPT (3) leave it empty. The 24 placeholder rows of delegation_limit are not seeded. The migration inserts the data_product rows before the sys_objects rows.

secs.h: RWB-E1-002 Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-002 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-18 Show the case list with case ID, owner and queue |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D6 entry; D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-069, RWB-E1-007, RWB-E1-015 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **one case list with case number, account, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due for every account at 90 days past due or more, built from the open cases and the ACE account view on each ACE business date and available in Power BI**, so that **every recovery team works from one list that is dated to the ACE batch it was built from**.

Each recovery team keeps its own list of accounts today, and the lists do not agree with each other or with the source. This story builds one case list each business date from the open cases and `v_ace_account`, with the account number, balance and days past due read live from ACE rather than copied, and publishes it to Power BI. The count is checked daily against ACE by REC-01 in RWB-E1-011, and a business key with no ACE row is listed by REC-05. It meets REQ-RDF-007 and serves the measure "case list built and released by 07:30 on 99 percent of days".

- RWB-E1-018 is done: open cases exist with their linked accounts, and P3 publishes `CaseQueryApi` with `account_key` as the account link.
- RWB-E1-020 is done: JOB-03 morning allocation sets the owner and the queue.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the Section A views exist, including `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_efs_action` and `v_ace_batch_status`. `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the freshness line and the gate stay behind their flags until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- RWB-E1-015 is done: the daily completeness gate holds JOB-04 until the ALS batch for the business date is COMPLETED.
- RWB-E1-007 is done: the outbound file adapter writes files to the data lake (INT-19).
- Parameters are loaded: `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16), `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` 0.00 (assumed, DL25), `caselist.allocation.wait.until` 07:15.
- The reporting and BI analyst (RW-BIANAL) has built the Power BI data set "Case list v1" on the lake file and scheduled its refresh at 07:30.
- JOB-04 runs as the recovery service identity (recovery_svc), which holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.

1. Quartz: JOB-04 Daily reconciliation reaches its case list step after JOB-03 completes for the business date, and only when the daily completeness gate of RWB-E1-015 reports COMPLETE for the sources the case list reads.
2. System: reads the business date and completion time of the ALS batch from `v_ace_batch_status` (source_system ALS, is_complete true).
3. System: reads the open case accounts from `CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts(businessDate)`, each with its `account_key`.
4. System: joins each account_key to `v_ace_account` for the account number (`account_code`), total balance and days past due, for the business date in `data_as_of`.
5. System: reads the latest contact and action code per account_key from `v_ace_efs_action`.
6. System: replaces the case_list_row rows for the business date in one transaction, each with the refresh time and publish status PENDING.
7. System: counts the rows below the entry threshold and records the count on the run for information; the reconciliation itself is REC-01 of RWB-E1-011.
8. RWB-E1-011: the reconciliation step compares the list with `v_ace_account` and sets the publish status of the date to HELD or RELEASED.
9. System: the publish step sends the extract file for the business date to the data lake through the outbound file adapter only when the publish status is RELEASED.
10. Power BI: refreshes the data set at 07:30; the report shows the ten columns, the filters, the refresh time and the ACE business date.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source the case list reads is not COMPLETED at the cut-off | The daily completeness gate of RWB-E1-015 holds the step; no case_list_row is written; the lake keeps the last released list; the data steward and team managers are alerted | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | JOB-03 has not completed by 07:15 | The list is built with the owner and queue as they are; the check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE is NO on the run | None (shown on the report) | AC6 |
| X3 | The step runs again for the same business date | The rows for that date are replaced; no duplicate rows | None | AC7 |
| X4 | `CaseQueryApi` raises an error | The transaction rolls back; the run status is FAILED; the previous rows stay; the platform administrator restarts the step | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC8 |
| X5 | The publish step's transfer to the lake fails after the adapter retries | The run is COMPLETED with check PUBLISHED NO; the transfer goes to the exception queue with a task for the platform administrator | None (R-UNI-34) | AC9 |
| X6 | A case account has no `v_ace_account` row for the business date | The row is written with empty balance and days past due; REC-05 lists the key for the data steward and the ACE team; the case and the link are unchanged | None (REC-05) | AC10 |
| X7 | A role without Platform administration R lists the case list runs | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-002-11 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads cases only through the P3 published interface and accounts only through `v_ace_account`; the Power BI report is built by the BI analyst |
| Negotiable | The entry threshold, the tolerance and the wait time are parameters |
| Valuable | One list for every team, with owner and queue, dated to the ACE batch, replacing the team files |
| Estimable | One batch step, one table, one extract file, one join to the ACE view |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic cases |

```gherkin

secs.h: RWB-E1-007 Integration adapters for outbound files
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-007 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-21 Run the integration adapters for outbound files; FEAT-RDF-23 Queue and retry a failed interface call; FEAT-RDF-24 Raise an interface failure to the exception queue; FEAT-DRI-10 Run outbound file and SFTP adapters; FEAT-DRI-11 Route every outbound file through the integration adapters; FEAT-DRI-13 Detect and ignore a duplicate event |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.2; Business Requirements Program, section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069, RWB-E1-015 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **one adapter pattern for every outbound file, with the data it reads taken from the ACE views, retry on a schedule held as data and an exception queue with a named owner**, so that **every later outbound file follows one pattern and a failed file is found on the day it fails**.

The Workbench loads no source data; ACE ingests every source and the Workbench only sends (D-RCV-35 U1). What remains in P2 is one outbound path for the WIN registered-mail notice file, the reporting extract to the data lake and Power BI, the decision and outcome feed to COLLINS through the lake, and the debt buyer data tape. Each outbound file is built from Workbench tables and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, sent through the outbox, acknowledged, retried on the schedule held in its interface row, and moved to the exception queue with a task for a named owner after the retry limit. It meets REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007 and REQ-DRI-008 and serves the FSD P2 measure "outbound items in the exception queue over one day: zero".

- RWB-E1-001 (recovery schema) is done: interface_config, outbound_item, processed_event, outbox_event and outbox_delivery exist.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the Section A views exist, including `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_account`, so an outbound file can read the addressee and the account. `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view; the readiness check stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- RWB-E1-015 is done: the ACE batch status and the late-batch event exist.
- The interface configuration rows for INT-14, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25 are loaded by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM), version "IF-2026.11", each with direction OUTBOUND.
- The SFTP outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052).
- The recovery service identity (recovery_svc) holds its Entra ID managed identity in each environment and SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` only.
- The Quartz scheduler of the ACE service runs JOB-10 (WIN outbound notices), JOB-11 (outbox sender), JOB-13 (decision log copy) and JOB-15 (reporting extract).

1. Owning module: writes an outbound file request through `OutboundFiles.enqueue`, for example JOB-10 for the daily WIN notice file (INT-14).
2. System: reads the interface configuration row in force, which names the target, the transport, the attempts, the retry intervals and the owner role.
3. System: builds the file from Workbench tables and, where the file needs source data, from the `recovery.v_ace_*` views; the addressee and address come from `v_ace_contact` by `contact_key`.
4. System: checks `v_ace_batch_status` that the ACE batch for the file's business date is COMPLETE; if it is not, the item is held and no file is built.
5. recovery_svc: writes one outbound_item with an idempotency key, in the same transaction as the request, and stores the built file in the document store.
6. Scheduler: JOB-11 runs every minute; the OutboundSender sends each due item over SFTP and marks it SENT, then ACKNOWLEDGED when the acknowledgment file arrives.
7. System: on a transfer failure, the sender raises SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE for each case in the file and schedules the next attempt from the retry intervals.
8. System: after the last allowed attempt fails, the sender sets the item to EXCEPTION, raises OUTBOUND_FAILED for each case and a task for the owner role, and logs MSG-P2-001.
9. System: every consumer of an application event checks the idempotency key through `IdempotencyGuard` before it acts, including EV-26 AceDataReady.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch for the file's business date is not COMPLETE | The file is not built and no outbound_item is written; the request waits for the next window after EV-26; the platform administrator and data steward are alerted | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The outbound transfer fails | The item waits for the next attempt; the cases move to RETRY_QUEUE | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3 |
| X3 | The retry limit is reached | The item moves to the exception queue; a task goes to the owner role; the cases move to EXCEPTION_QUEUE | MSG-P2-001 | AC3 |
| X4 | The same application event arrives twice with the same key | The second event is ignored and the hit is counted (R-UNI-40) | None | AC5 |
| X5 | Two sender instances pick the same item | Only one holds the row lock; the other skips it | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A platform administrator resends an item from the exception queue | The item returns to PENDING with attempt count 0 | MSG-GEN-005 | AC7 |
| X7 | A role without the right lists or resends exception items | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-007-10 |
| X8 | A build reads a public table instead of a view | The statement fails at the database and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | AC1, AC2 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the schema (RWB-E1-001) and the views (RWB-E1-069); the outbound files of later epics reuse it |
| Negotiable | Retry counts, intervals, folders, patterns and owners are interface configuration rows; the story fixes the behaviour |
| Valuable | Every outbound file is built from one source of truth, logged, retried and raised to a named owner from Epic 1 |
| Estimable | Five tables, one outbound adapter, one readiness check, one sender job, one guard, two endpoints |
| Small | One squad, within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

```gherkin
Feature: Integration adapters for outbound files

 Background:
 Given the interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" is in force
 Given interface "INT-14" WIN outbound has direction "OUTBOUND", max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes
 Given interface "INT-14" has owner role "RW-PLATADM"

 Scenario: AC1 One outbound pattern
 Given a developer adds the outbound file "INT-25" debt buyer data tape
 When the build pipeline runs
 Then the system declares the file as an interface configuration row with direction "OUTBOUND" and uses OutboundFileAdapter
 Then the contract test "INT-25" builds the synthetic tape of 120 accounts from debt_sale_account and v_ace_account and passes
 Then the architecture test finds no SFTP or file system call outside the package recovery.integration.adapter
 Then no interface configuration row has direction "INBOUND"

 Scenario: AC2 Outbound file reads ACE only through the views
 Given 85 approved notices for business date 2026-11-10, each with person_key and contact_key
 When JOB-10 builds the WIN file "WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt"
 Then each addressee and address is read from v_ace_contact by contact_key
 Then no statement of the build reads a public table
 Then the outbound item records the ACE business date 2026-11-10 from v_ace_batch_status

 Scenario: AC3 Retry and exception queue
 Given the outbound WIN file "WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt" for 85 notices on 85 cases
 Given the SFTP transfer fails on attempts 1, 2 and 3
 When the outbox sender runs
 Then attempt 2 starts 5 minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 starts 15 minutes after attempt 2
 Then each case in the file moves to route state "RETRY_QUEUE" after attempt 1 (R-UNI-33)
 Then after attempt 3 the item status is "EXCEPTION"
 Then each of the 85 cases moves to route state "EXCEPTION_QUEUE" with a task for role "RW-PLATADM" (R-UNI-34)
 Then the item shows in the exception queue with message MSG-P2-001

 Scenario: AC4 Outbound file held while the ACE batch is not complete
 Given v_ace_batch_status shows the ALS batch for 2026-11-10 with status "FAILED" at 05:20
 Given the WIN notice file for 2026-11-10 is due at 16:00
 When JOB-10 reaches its build step
 Then no file is built and no outbound_item is written
 Then the request is held with the reason "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-07"
 Then the platform administrator receives MSG-P1-001 "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-07. Today's ACE batch has not arrived."
 Then the file is built by the next JOB-10 run after EV-26 for 2026-11-10

 Scenario: AC5 Duplicate application event ignored
 Given consumer "booking-confirmation" processed event key "EV-10:TRT-0001:v1"
 When the same event arrives again with the same key
 Then the consumer does not act
 Then the hit count for that key becomes 2 (R-UNI-40)

 Scenario: AC6 Two senders pick the same item
 Given outbound item "OB-0001" is due
 When two sender threads run at 10:00:00
 Then the system sends the file once
 Then the attempt count is 1

 Scenario: AC7 Resend from the exception queue
 Given outbound item "OB-0002" has status "EXCEPTION" after 3 attempts
 When a platform administrator resends it
 Then the item status is "PENDING" with attempt count 0
 Then the system writes the resend to the ACE audit log with the user and the time
 Then the response carries message MSG-GEN-005
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound file goes through the one adapter; no component calls a target system directly | ADR-010; REQ-DRI-006 |
| BR2 | An outbound file reads ACE only through `recovery.v_ace_*`, by business key, and never writes to ACE | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; BR-P2-001-ACE |
| BR3 | An outbound file is built only when the ACE batch for its business date is COMPLETE in `v_ace_batch_status` | VR-P2-001-1; RWB-E1-015 |
| BR4 | An outbound file is sent again on the intervals in its configuration row; after the last failure a task goes to the owning team | ifspec INT-14; interface_config.max_attempts |
| BR5 | A system that is unavailable queues the action and retries | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35, R-UNI-36 |
| BR6 | An item that fails after the retry limit moves to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR7 | An event with a key already processed by the consumer is ignored and the hit is counted | R-UNI-40; events.txt Rules sheet, Duplicates |
| BR8 | Retry counts, intervals, folders, patterns and owners are data rows, never code | Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR9 | P2 has no inbound adapter: no file is picked up, checked or signed off in the Workbench, and `interface_config` holds outbound rows only | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010 |
| BR10 | An outbound item carries case IDs and business keys, never an address, a name or an identity number; the file itself is held in the document store | CTL-11; Guardrails |
| BR11 | The GL write-off posting and the SOC log leave through ACE paths: the approved write-off is posted in GL and read back through `v_ace_write_off`, and access and security events go to the SOC log through ACE logging (INT-22) | D-RCV-35 U1; FSD P2 A1.5 |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE (route state) | SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE | First failed attempt of an outbound file for the case | RETRY_QUEUE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_SUCCEEDED | A later attempt is sent | RESUME_STATE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED | Attempt count equals max attempts | EXCEPTION_QUEUE |
| ANY_ACTIVE (route state) | DUPLICATE_EVENT | Key already processed | RESUME_STATE |

secs.h: RWB-E1-008 Decision log store v1, append only and hash chained
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-008 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-01 Store decision log entries append-only and hash-chained |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-002, REQ-DRI-003 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.7; Business Requirements Program, section 5.7 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an append-only decision log store holding the seven field groups of every decision, with each entry hashed to the one before it**, so that **every decision from Epic 1 is recorded once, cannot be changed or deleted, and any change to a stored entry is found by recomputing the chain**.

Documentation and audit trail findings (5 of 29 in the audit summary behind CTL-06) show that why a route was chosen, who approved it and on what figures is spread across e-mails and files. This story builds the store that every later decision writes to: one record per decision with inputs, versions, recommendation, approver, final call, actions and outcome; refusal of every update and delete in the database; a single hash chain; and a verifier that finds a break. It meets REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-002 and REQ-DRI-003 and implements ADR-009. The measure is every decision reproducible from the log (NFR-033).

- RWB-E1-001 is done: table decision_log_entry exists with the trigger tr_declog_append_only and the function refuse_change from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql.
- The database role of the ACE service holds INSERT and SELECT on decision_log_entry and no UPDATE or DELETE grant.
- The ACE notification path can send to the Compliance and PDPA officer group, and the ACE incident path is available.

1. Writer (SY-DECLOG, built in RWB-E1-027): calls DecisionLogStore.append with a validated record inside the caller's transaction, as its last statement.
2. Store (DecisionLogStore): takes the chain lock (a PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock on the key "decision_log_chain").
3. Store: reads the chain_seq and entry_hash of the last entry; sets chain_seq to last plus 1 and prev_hash to the last entry_hash, or 64 zeros for the first entry.
4. Store: builds the canonical form of the entry and sets entry_hash to its SHA-256 in lower-case hexadecimal.
5. Store: inserts the row; the caller's transaction commits the action and the entry together and releases the lock.
6. Store: on any failure, raises DecisionLogUnavailableException; the caller's transaction rolls back and the action does not happen.
7. Database: refuses any UPDATE or DELETE on decision_log_entry through tr_declog_append_only; the ACE service writes the refused attempt to the ACE audit and SOC log.
8. Verifier (HashChainVerifier): reads entries in chain_seq order over a range, recomputes each entry_hash and checks each prev_hash against the entry before it.
9. Verifier: returns the result with the count checked, the last chain_seq and its entry_hash; on a break, it names the first entry that fails, raises an incident and sends MSG-P7-008 to Compliance within 15 minutes.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An UPDATE or DELETE is attempted on a stored entry | The database refuses it; the attempt is written to the ACE audit and SOC log | None (database error, logged) | AC1 |
| X2 | A stored entry was changed outside the service, for example in a test environment | The verifier names the first entry whose hash does not match; an incident is raised; Compliance is told within 15 minutes | MSG-P7-008 | AC4 |
| X3 | Two writers append at the same moment | The chain lock orders them; chain_seq values are consecutive and each prev_hash names the entry before | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A decided entry is wrong | A new entry is written that names the corrected entry; the original stays | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The store cannot be written | The append fails, the caller's action rolls back and the caller shows its message | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Decision log R reads an entry | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the table from RWB-E1-001; every later writer depends on it |
| Negotiable | The canonical form and the hash algorithm are fixed by this story; retention follows DL26 |
| Valuable | Every decision from Epic 1 is recorded once and any change to it is found |
| Estimable | One store, one migration, one verifier, two read endpoints |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Decision log store v1, append only and hash chained

 Background:
 Given the environment is DEV with synthetic data
 Given the decision log store is empty

 Scenario: AC1 Append only
 Given an entry with chain_seq 1 and final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" is stored for case "RW-2026-000123"
 When an UPDATE setting final_call to "CASE_TRANSFERRED" and a DELETE of the entry are attempted through the ACE service's database role and again through the schema owner role
 Then the system refuses all four statements : by the missing grant for the service role, and with "decision_log_entry is append only" from tr_declog_append_only for the schema owner
 Then the entry is unchanged
 Then the system writes the refused attempts to the ACE audit log with the table, the operation and the entry ID

 Scenario: AC2 Hash chain
 Given 100 entries are appended
 When the chain verifier runs from chain_seq 1 to 100
 Then every entry_hash equals the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form
 Then every prev_hash equals the entry_hash of the entry before it, and the first prev_hash is 64 zeros
 Then the result holds count 100, last chain_seq 100 and that entry's entry_hash

 Scenario: AC3 Seven field groups
 Given an entry is appended for decision "D6" on case "RW-2026-000123" with rule "R-UNI-14", rule version "UNI-2026.11", inputs reference "inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a", recommendation, approver "U-6101", approval level "L6", final call "APPROVED", actions and outcome
 When it is read with GET /decision-log/{entryId}
 Then the response holds inputsRef, ruleId and ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId and approvalLevel, finalCall, actions and outcome
 Then decidedAt, prevHash and entryHash are present

 Scenario: AC4 Hash chain verified daily
 Given the store holds 10,000 entries
 Given the actions of the entry with chain_seq 7,412 were changed in the DEV database with the trigger disabled
 When the chain verifier runs from chain_seq 1 to 10,000
 Then the result names chain_seq 7,412 and its entry ID as the first break
 Then the system raises an incident and MSG-P7-008 is sent to the Compliance group within 15 minutes of the run start

 Scenario: AC5 Two appends at the same moment form one chain
 Given entries up to chain_seq 50 are stored
 When two writers append one entry each in parallel transactions
 Then the entries get chain_seq 51 and 52
 Then the prev_hash of 52 equals the entry_hash of 51, and the prev_hash of 51 equals the entry_hash of 50

 Scenario: AC6 A correction is a new entry
 Given entry "E-1" records owner "U-6102" by mistake
 When a correction entry is appended with corrects_entry_id "E-1" and the right owner "U-6103"
 Then entry "E-1" is unchanged
 Then GET /decision-log for case "RW-2026-000123" returns both entries in chain order with the correction naming "E-1"

 Scenario: AC7 A failed append leaves nothing behind
 Given the database connection for the store is closed in the test double
 When a writer appends an entry inside a transaction that also changes the case owner
 Then the system raises decisionLogUnavailableException
 Then the system stores no entry , the case owner is unchanged and chain_seq is not used

 Scenario: AC8 Reading an entry needs the Decision log right
 Given test user "U-6104" holds only RW-PHONECOL, whose Decision log letter is "-"
 When the user calls GET /decision-log/{entryId}
 Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
```

**Interfaces inside P7** (package recovery.decision.log):

```

- Package: folder `recovery/decision/log` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.decision.log`.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionCenterAndLogController | Controller | GET /decision-log/{entryId} and GET /decision-log by case |
| DecisionLogStore | Service | Chain lock, chain_seq and prev_hash, canonical form, hash, insert |
| CanonicalEntryForm | Service | Builds the canonical JSON per BR4; one implementation used by the store and the verifier |
| HashChainVerifier | Service | Recomputes a range in chain_seq order in batches of 1,000 and reports the first break |
