secs.h: RWB-E1-011 Reconciliation and data quality report
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-011 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-11 Reconcile the case list to ACE daily; FEAT-RDF-12 Publish the daily reconciliation and data quality report; FEAT-RDF-13 Hold the publish when reconciliation breaks tolerance; FEAT-RPT-05 Reconcile case counts across sources; FEAT-RPT-09 Manage a data quality break |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-007, REQ-RDF-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.1 and 3.8; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 15 Manage performance, data and AI |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U4); ADR-010 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-002, RWB-E1-015, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a daily reconciliation of the case list to `v_ace_account`, of every business key on a Workbench table to its ACE view, and of treatments and payments to their ACE records, with the variance by product and the data quality results in one Power BI report**, so that **everyone sees whether today's case list and its links can be trusted**.

No one can say today whether the recovery teams' lists cover every account at 90 days past due, so missing accounts are found late or not at all. This story runs the five daily reconciliations REC-01 to REC-05 every business date: the account count and the balance by product against `v_ace_account`, approved treatments against `v_ace_plan`, payments against proceeds, and every business key on a Workbench table against the view that holds it. It lists every account or key that breaks, holds the publish of the case list when a product is outside the tolerance, and publishes the result with the data quality measures in one report. It meets REQ-RDF-007 and REQ-RDF-008, applies control CTL-01, and serves the accuracy measure "reconciliation breaks cleared within one day, 100 percent". No reconciliation runs against a source load: the Workbench loads nothing, and the ACE side of every check is a read-only view.

- RWB-E1-002 is done: the case list step builds case_list_row and holds its extract for the publish step.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: the daily completeness gate holds JOB-04 until the sources the reconciliation reads are COMPLETE for the business date, and the freshness stamps exist.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the views exist, including `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_plan`, `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_asset` and `v_ace_contact`.
- Parameters are loaded: `recon.tolerance.pct` 0.00 for REC-01 and REC-02 (assumed, DL25), `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16), `recon.treatment.days` 2 and `recon.payment.days` 1 (assumed, DL25).
- The reporting and BI analyst has built the Power BI report "Reconciliation and data quality" on the lake extracts and scheduled its refresh at 07:30.
- JOB-04 runs as the recovery service identity (recovery_svc), which holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.

1. System: JOB-04 Daily reconciliation runs its reconciliation step after the case list step for the business date, on a COMPLETE gate result for the sources it reads.
2. System: reads the business date and completion time of the ALS batch from `v_ace_batch_status`, and uses that one business date for every check.
3. System: REC-01, for each product group, counts the accounts in `v_ace_account` at or above the entry threshold with `data_as_of` equal to the business date, less the accounts in `case_entry_exclusion` for the date, and counts the case_list_row rows at or above the threshold.
4. System: REC-02, for each product group, sums `v_ace_account.total_balance` and case_list_row.total_balance.
5. System: REC-03 counts approved restructure treatments whose case plan is not booked in `v_ace_plan` after two business days, and sums the offer amount.
6. System: REC-04 matches `v_ace_payment` rows of the business date to proceeds by `payment_code`, and counts and sums what is unmatched after one business day.
7. System: REC-05 resolves every `account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code` and `contact_key` on a Workbench table to its view row, and counts the orphans.
8. System: computes the variance and the variance percent for each check and product group, compares it with the tolerance, and writes one reconciliation_result row per check and product group.
9. System: writes the break list, with account keys, keys and amounts, to the reconciliation extract for the data steward; no dq_exception row is written because that table has left the schema.
10. System: if every REC-01 and REC-02 result is PASS, sets the publish status of the date to RELEASED; if any is BREAK, sets HELD and alerts the data steward, the platform administrator and the team managers.
11. System: writes the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract to the data lake.
12. Power BI: the 07:30 refresh shows each product as green, red or not run, the variance, the break rows, the referential completeness and the quality measures.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product's variance is above the tolerance | Result BREAK; red on the report; case list publish held; break rows listed; alert | MSG-P1-012 | AC2 |
| X2 | The variance equals the tolerance | Result PASS | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The ACE batch for the business date is not COMPLETED | The gate holds JOB-04; no reconciliation runs; the report shows not run with the reason; the publish stays held | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X4 | The reconciliation runs again for the same date after a fix | Results for that date are replaced; the publish is released if every REC-01 and REC-02 result passes | None | AC5 |
| X5 | Two runs for the same date | Results are written once per check, product group and date | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A business key has no ACE row | REC-05 is BREAK with the orphan count; the key is listed for the data steward and the ACE team; no Workbench row changes | None | AC7 |
| X7 | A view returns an error during the run | No result is written for the date; the run is FAILED with the system named; the rerun writes every row | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration R lists the break rows | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-011-07 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the case list of RWB-E1-002, the gate and stamps of RWB-E1-015 and the views of RWB-E1-069; changes no case |
| Negotiable | The tolerance per reconciliation and the waiting periods are parameters; the report layout belongs to the BI analyst |
| Valuable | Teams see each morning whether the list and its links are complete, and a broken list is not published |
| Estimable | One batch step, one table, one hold flag, two extracts |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic data |

```gherkin
Feature: Reconciliation and data quality report

 Background:
 Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and v_ace_batch_status shows ALS COMPLETED for 2026-11-30
 Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct = 0.00 is in force for REC-01 and REC-02

 Scenario: AC1 Variance under limit
 Given the v_ace_account accounts at 90 days past due or more less the exclusions are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903
 Given the case list rows at 90 days past due or more are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903, with equal balance sums
 Given no restructure plan is overdue in v_ace_plan, no payment of the date is unmatched, and every business key resolves to its view
 When the reconciliation step of JOB-04 runs
 Then the system writes fifteen reconciliation_result rows, REC-01 to REC-05 for each of the three product groups, each with variance 0 and result PASS
 Then the system sets the publish status of the case list for 2026-11-30 to RELEASED
 Then the report after the 07:30 refresh shows all three products green

 Scenario: AC2 Variance over limit
 Given v_ace_account holds 2,903 SSME accounts at 90 days past due or more less the exclusions
 Given the case list holds 2,891 SSME rows at 90 days past due or more, a variance of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent
 When the reconciliation step runs
 Then the REC-01 result for SSME is BREAK with variance 12 and variance percent 0.41
 Then the 12 account keys are on the break list for the data steward, with their days past due from v_ace_account
 Then the system sets the case list publish for 2026-11-30 to HELD and the lake keeps the case list of 2026-11-27
 Then the data steward, platform administrator and team manager groups receive MSG-P1-012 "The case list for 2026-11-30 does not reconcile to ACE for SSME: a difference of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent."
 Then the report shows SSME red with the 12 break rows, and MORTGAGE and HIRE_PURCHASE green

 Scenario: AC3 Variance equal to the tolerance
 Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct for REC-01 is changed by a reference load to 0.10 from 2026-11-30
 Given the MORTGAGE variance is 0.10 percent and the SSME variance is 0.11 percent
 When the reconciliation step runs
 Then the MORTGAGE result is PASS and the SSME result is BREAK

 Scenario: AC4 ACE batch not complete
 Given v_ace_batch_status shows no COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-30 at 08:00
 When the DP01 cut-off passes and JOB-04 is triggered
 Then the daily completeness gate holds JOB-04 and the system writes no reconciliation_result for 2026-11-30
 Then the case list publish for 2026-11-30 stays HELD
 Then the report shows every product as not run with the reason "DP01 is from 2026-11-27"

 Scenario: AC5 Rerun after a fix
 Given the SSME result for 2026-11-30 is BREAK and the publish is held
 Given P3 has created the 12 missing cases and the case list step has been rerun
 When the platform administrator restarts the reconciliation step for 2026-11-30
 Then the system replaces the fifteen results for 2026-11-30 and all are PASS
 Then the system sets the publish status of the date to RELEASED and the case list extract is sent to the lake

 Scenario: AC6 Two runs for the same date
 Given two JOB-04 runs for 2026-11-30 start on two nodes
 When both reach the reconciliation step
 Then reconciliation_result holds one row per check and product group, fifteen rows in all
 Then no row is written twice for the same rec_code, business_date and product_group

 Scenario: AC7 Business key without an ACE row
 Given case_party on case "RW-2026-000140" carries person_key "P0099881", which has no row in v_ace_customer
 When the REC-05 step runs
 Then the REC-05 result for the product group of the case is BREAK with 1 orphan
 Then "case_party.person_key P0099881" is on the break list for the data steward and the ACE team
 Then the case and its case_party row are unchanged

 Scenario: AC8 View unavailable during the run
 Given v_ace_account returns an error after the MORTGAGE count is read
 When the reconciliation step runs
 Then the system writes no reconciliation_result for 2026-11-30
 Then the run shows FAILED with MSG-GEN-006 for system "ACE database"
 Then the restart writes all fifteen rows for 2026-11-30
```

1. Write ReconciliationResult, its repository and the index migration; test the replace of one date.
2. Write ReconciliationService for REC-01 and REC-02 with the exclusions; unit test variance 0, the tolerance boundary and a break.
3. Write REC-03 and REC-04 with their waiting-period parameters and the unmatched list.
4. Write ReferentialCheck for the five key families; test each view and the composite `contact_key`.

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the decision log copied to the data lake each night, with a retention rule applied to the copy**, so that **reporting reads the log without touching the live log and nothing in the copy is kept longer than its rule**.

Reporting, audit sampling and model feedback need the full decision history, and queries against the live log slow the write path that every action depends on (ADR-009). A nightly copy that matches the live log on row count and last hash gives Power BI and audit one checked source (REC-08). The copy carries its own retention rule, so the lake does not keep decisions longer than the bank schedule allows. Serves REQ-DRI-009 and REQ-RDF-013; measure: copy matched on count and last hash on 99 percent of days (FSD P1 A2.20.1).

- RWB-E1-008 (decision log store) and RWB-E1-027 (decision log writer) are done, and P7 publishes the DecisionLogExport interface in section 12.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-13 has a run book, and its runs show in the job monitor.
- RWB-E1-017 is done: the retention rule table holds a row for product DP12, table decision_log_entry, record class LAKE_COPY (assumed 120 months; DL26).
- The data lake intake container for INT-19 exists in each environment and the job's service identity SY-DATALOAD can write to it.
- Quartz holds the JOB-13 trigger at 01:00 Asia/Bangkok.

1. Quartz: starts JOB-13 Decision log copy at 01:00 for business date D (the previous calendar day).
2. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: reads the watermark (last copied entry hash and cumulative count) from lake_copy_watermark.
3. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: calls DecisionLogExport.head() and fixes the cut-off: the live count and last entry hash at start.
4. DecisionLogLakeCopyService: calls DecisionLogExport.entriesAfter(watermarkHash, 5000) in chain order until it reaches the cut-off hash.
5. LakeFileWriter: writes the entries to `decision-log/business_date=D/` as Parquet files and writes `_manifest.json` with the row count, first hash, last hash and cumulative count.
6. LakeCopyReconciler: reads the manifest back from the lake and compares the cumulative count and last hash with the cut-off (REC-08, tolerance zero).
7. LakeCopyReconciler: on a match, marks the partition complete, moves the watermark forward and records the checks on the job run.
8. LakeRetentionService: reads the retention rule for DP12 LAKE_COPY and moves each partition older than the rule to the archive tier, recording the partition list, the count and the rule version on the job run.
9. Data steward: reads the run result in GET /admin/jobs and the break, if any, in the morning.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The lake count or last hash differs from the cut-off | Partition not marked complete; watermark not moved; break recorded; data steward alerted; JOB-13 runs again the next night | MSG-P1-019 | AC3 |
| X2 | JOB-13 runs again for a business date already copied | The same chain range is written to the same partition; no duplicate rows | None | AC4 |
| X3 | DecisionLogExport is unavailable or the lake write fails | Job ends Failed; previous copy and watermark kept; alert raised; rerun from the job monitor | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | No decision was written since the last copy | Empty partition with a manifest of zero rows and the unchanged last hash; checks pass | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A second start of JOB-13 while one is running | Second start refused; 409 on a manual rerun | MSG-P2-006 | AC7 |
| X6 | A partition is exactly at its retention age | The partition is kept; only partitions older than the rule move | None | AC8 |

secs.h: RWB-E1-015 Freshness stamp per data product
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-015 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-14 Stamp each data product with its freshness; FEAT-DRI-12 Carry a freshness stamp on every decision input |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-009) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 open |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build, Tier 2 behind a flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43) |

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **every data product to carry the business date, start time, completion time and status of the ACE batch it came from, exposed to every consumer and shown on the case record view, and every daily data job to start only when the sources it reads are complete for the business date**, so that **every decision input states how old it is, stale facts are visible, and no list is built from a half-loaded day**.

The Workbench loads no source data; ACE does (D-RCV-35 U1). A fact on the case can therefore be one day or one week old, and the Workbench cannot time its own load. ACE writes one `ace_batch_run` row per source and business date and the Workbench reads it through `v_ace_batch_status`. A stamp per product and business date, shown on the case record and copied into each decision's inputs snapshot, makes the age of every input visible to the person deciding and to audit. A product whose batch has not completed by its cut-off is flagged stale the same morning. The same reading closes the daily gate that the retired load checks used to provide: no data job for a business date starts until every source it reads is COMPLETED. Serves REQ-RDF-009; measure: the ACE batch is complete when the Workbench reads it on 99 percent of days.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: data_product holds DP01 to DP14 and data_product_load exists.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: `v_ace_batch_status` is created in Section B, over `public.ace_batch_run` owned by the ACE team. Until RWB-ACE-001 lands the feature stays behind its flag (DL43).
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 decision log writer builds an inputs snapshot for each entry.
- The data product catalog is loaded with refresh cycle and expected-by time for each product (08:00 for daily products, MON 08:00 for weekly products; DL11).
- The reader holds Case record R (case roles) or Platform administration R (data steward, platform administrator).
- The recovery service identity (recovery_svc) holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.

1. System: reads `v_ace_batch_status`, one row per source system and business date, for a new or changed COMPLETED row.
2. FreshnessStampService: reads the product-to-source map (section 12) and, in one transaction, writes or updates one data_product_load row for each product the source feeds, with the business date, `source_extracted_at` from `started_at`, `loaded_at` from `completed_at` and status LOADED.
3. System: for a product fed by more than one source, sets the stamp to the oldest business date among its sources and marks it STALE while any of them is late.
4. System: at each product's `expected_by` time, checks that a COMPLETED row exists in `v_ace_batch_status` for the expected business date.
5. System: for a product with no COMPLETED row, marks its latest stamp in use (the previous complete business date) STALE with `stale_flagged_at`, publishes EV-27 AceDataLate and sends the operations alert. No row is written for a business date with no batch, because the stamp needs the source start and completion times.
6. System: on a FAILED batch row, marks the product STALE at once; the stamp for the last complete business date stays the one in use.
7. DailyCompletenessGate: at the cut-off for the day, reads `v_ace_batch_status` for the sources the day's data jobs read; when every one is COMPLETED, returns COMPLETE and lets JOB-04 start; otherwise returns HOLD, names the product and the source, and raises the alert.
8. Consumer (case record view, P3 or P7): calls FreshnessQuery or GET /data-products/freshness and receives business date, source start time, completion time and status per product.
9. Case record view: shows the stamp in the data panel, with MSG-P1-001 when the product is stale.
10. P7 inputs snapshot builder: calls FreshnessQuery.stampsFor() for the products a decision reads and writes each stamp into the snapshot that inputs_ref points to.
11. System: a later COMPLETED batch for the same business date sets status LOADED, records the new `loaded_at`, and starts the daily jobs through EV-26.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No COMPLETED batch for the expected business date by the expected-by time | Product set STALE; EV-27 published; operations alert sent; case record shows the stale warning | MSG-P1-001 | AC2 |
| X2 | The batch row is FAILED | Product set STALE at once; the previous stamp stays in use; no daily job starts | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same COMPLETED batch row is read twice | One data_product_load row; the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40); no second event | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A late batch arrives after the stale flag | Status LOADED with the new completion time; the jobs start for that business date | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A batch completes one minute before the expected-by time | Product not flagged stale | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A weekly product inside its weekly cycle | Product not flagged stale on the days between batches | None | AC8 |
| X7 | One source of a multi-source product is late | The product carries the oldest business date among its sources and is STALE; EV-27 names the late source | MSG-P1-001 | AC11 |
| X8 | A source that the day's jobs do not read is late | The gate still returns COMPLETE; only the products that read that source are STALE | MSG-P1-001 | AC10 |
| X9 | A role without the right reads the stamps | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-015-09 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables (RWB-E1-001), the batch view (RWB-E1-069) and the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) |
| Negotiable | Expected-by times, refresh cycles and the product-to-source map are data rows; the story fixes the stamping, the stale check and the gate |
| Valuable | Every decision and every case record shows the age of its data, and no list is built on an incomplete day |
| Estimable | One table, one service, one listener, one gate, two endpoints, one panel |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a test clock and synthetic batch rows |

secs.h: RWB-E1-016 Access control per data product and catalog entries
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-016 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-15 Set access control per data product for PDPA; FEAT-RDF-16 Maintain the data catalog entry per data product |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-010, REQ-RDF-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-010, REQ-RDF-011) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U4); ADR-010 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-064, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **read access to each data product granted by role, source data reached only through the ACE view grant, personal fields masked by role from `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact`, every read logged, and a catalog entry per product that names its owner, system of record, freshness, views and tables and fields**, so that **personal data is read only by the roles that need it and every product is findable**.

Audit findings record staff sending debtor data outside the bank and users holding access they did not need (CTL-11, CTL-09). Under D-RCV-35 there is no load and no tokenization: source data is reached only through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, so access to a data product is the role's access row plus the database grant on the view, and the identity number is masked inside `v_ace_customer` itself. Access rows held as data limit each role to the products its work needs; masking rules decide which role sees a personal field in clear; and every read of personal data goes to the PII access log. The catalog gives one entry per product so a developer, an analyst or an auditor finds the owner, the source, the freshness rule, the retention, the views behind it and the personal fields without asking. Serves REQ-RDF-010 and REQ-RDF-011.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the 92 tables and the 122 sys_objects and 1,366 sys_fields rows exist, with the four extension tables.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist and the grants are applied. `ace_view_owner` owns the views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables; recovery_svc holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: P4 holds the role to permission matrix and the masking rules, and publishes `FieldMasker` in section 12.
- RWB-E1-064 is done: data_product holds DP01 to DP14 with owner role, system of record and refresh cycle.
- data_product_access version "DPA-2026.11" is loaded and approved: for example RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT read DP02; RW-PHONECOL reads DP01, DP02, DP03 and DP05 and not DP06.
- The masking rules from Compliance may be empty (DL26). Until they load, every personal field is masked for every role.
- The ACE common module PII access logging is available (INT-22).

1. User: opens a data product view, which calls GET /data-products/{productCode}/records?caseId=.
2. DataProductAccessService: checks the capability right Case record R through the ACE access check.
3. DataProductAccessService: checks data_product_access for a row in force for one of the user's roles and the product.
4. DataProductAccessService: calls the P3 case scope interface for the case's account keys and person keys in the user's scope.
5. DataProductRecordService: reads the product rows. A Workbench table is read in the recovery schema; a source product is read from its `recovery.v_ace_*` view by `account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code` or `contact_key`. The read runs as recovery_svc, which has SELECT on the view and nothing on `public`.
6. DataProductRecordService: for each field tagged is_personal in sys_fields, applies `FieldMasker` for the user's roles. The identity number is already masked in the view; the phone, email and address are full in the view because notices and calls need them.
7. DataProductAccessService: writes the read to the PII access log with user, product, case, field names and time; no value is logged.
8. Controller: returns the rows with the product's freshness stamp.
9. User with Platform administration R: calls GET /admin/data-products?product=DP01 and reads the catalog entry with owner, system of record, refresh cycle, retention, the views and tables behind it, the reconciliations and the fields with PDPA tags.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No data_product_access row for the user's roles and the product | 403; no row read; refusal written to the access log | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | An access load names a role code not in the roles table, an unknown product, or two overlapping rows | Load refused in full; previous version stays in force | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; no row read; refusal logged | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | No masking rule is loaded for a personal field | The field is masked for every role | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The PII access log cannot be written | Read refused with 503; no personal data returned | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X6 | An access row has a valid-from date after today | The row is not in force; the read is refused until that date | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | A statement reads a `public.*` table as recovery_svc, or writes a view | The database refuses it; the grant test fails the pipeline if the privilege exists | None (pipeline log) | AC9 |
| X8 | A catalog load marks a `v_ace_*` view as system of record "Workbench" | The load is refused whole; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-003 | AC11 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables and the metadata tables (RWB-E1-001), the views and grants (RWB-E1-069), the P4 masking (RWB-E1-037) and the data product table (RWB-E1-064) |
| Negotiable | Which role reads which product, and which field is masked for whom, are data rows; the story fixes the checks |
| Valuable | Personal data reaches only the roles that need it, source access is enforced by the grant, and every read is logged |
| Estimable | Two endpoints, one read service, one catalog service, calls to three published interfaces |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one API or database test with synthetic parties and roles |

secs.h: RWB-E1-017 Retention and archive rule for the data store
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-017 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-RDF-17 Apply the retention and archive rule to the data store |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-013 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-013) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-043, RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-064 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **a retention rule per data product and table, held as reference data, applied by a job that archives rows past their rule and logs the action**, so that **the store holds what the policy allows and nothing older**.

PDPA and the bank retention schedule limit how long personal data is kept, and today recovery records stay in spreadsheets and systems with no end date. A retention rule per data product and table, loaded as versioned data, lets Compliance set and change periods without a release. A monthly job archives rows past their period to a write-once archive container and removes them from the live store, keeps every row of a case under legal hold, and records what it did. Serves REQ-RDF-013 and the retention requirements NFR-031 and NFR-072.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the recovery tables and sys_objects exist.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service validates and approves versioned loads.
- RWB-E1-064 is done: data_product holds DP01 to DP14.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: a write-once archive container exists in each environment, writable by SY-DATALOAD.
- Retention rule version "RET-2026.11" is loaded and approved: DP05 interaction at 24 months on occurred_at (assumed until Compliance supplies the bank schedule; DL26).
- P3 publishes CaseHoldQuery (section 12), returning the cases with legal_hold = true.
- Quartz holds the JOB-17 trigger for the first Sunday of each month at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok.

1. Reference data administrator: loads a retention rule version through POST /admin/reference-loads with table retention_rule; the owner approves it.
2. RetentionRuleLoader: validates the rows (known product, known table in sys_objects, months between 1 and 600, table not decision_log_entry) and stores the version.
3. Quartz: starts JOB-17 Retention job on the first Sunday of the month.
4. RetentionService: reads the rules in force on the run date.
5. RetentionService: calls CaseHoldQuery.casesOnLegalHold() and excludes every row of those cases.
6. RetentionService: selects, per rule, the rows whose age-basis field is older than the run date minus the retention months.
7. ArchiveWriter: writes the selected rows per table to the archive container with a manifest (row count and SHA-256 per file) and reads the manifest back.
8. RetentionService: after the manifest matches, deletes the archived rows from the live table in one transaction per table and rule, under the purge setting the append-only trigger allows.
9. RetentionService: records on the job run the counts per product and table, the rule version, the archive location and the hold report (case numbers and row counts kept).
10. Compliance officer: reads the run result through GET /admin/jobs and the summary alert (MSG-P1-020).

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A case is on legal hold | Its rows are kept and listed in the hold report | MSG-P1-020 | AC3 |
| X2 | A rule row has months outside 1 to 600 | Load refused in full; previous version stays in force | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The archive write or the manifest check fails | No row deleted; run Failed; alert raised; rerun from the job monitor | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | JOB-17 runs again for the same month | Rows already archived are gone; the rerun archives only rows still past their rule | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A row is exactly at its retention age | The row is kept | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A rule names table decision_log_entry | Load refused in full; the decision log is never archived by this job | MSG-P1-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | A rerun is posted while JOB-17 runs | 409; one run continues | MSG-P2-006 | AC9 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables (RWB-E1-001), the reference data service (RWB-E1-043), the data product table (RWB-E1-064) and the archive container (RWB-TE-012) |
| Negotiable | Periods, tables and age-basis fields are rule rows; the story fixes the archive, purge and hold behavior |
| Valuable | The store keeps no row longer than its rule, and each removal is recorded |
| Estimable | One rule table, one job, one archive writer, one trigger change |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic rows with a test clock |

```gherkin
Feature: Retention and archive rule for the data store

 Background:
 Given retention rule version "RET-2026.11" holds product "DP05", table "interaction", age basis "occurred_at", 24 months
 Given the run date is Sunday 2026-12-06

 Scenario: AC1 Retention rule applied
 Given 1,250 interaction rows with occurred_at before 2024-12-06 and 4,800 rows from 2024-12-06 onward
 When JOB-17 runs
 Then 1,250 rows move to the archive container under "retention/2026-12-06/interaction/"
 Then the 1,250 rows are no longer in the live interaction table
 Then the job run logs count 1,250 for DP05 interaction under rule version "RET-2026.11"

 Scenario: AC2 Rule changed as data
 Given retention rule version "RET-2027.01" changes DP05 interaction to 36 months, approved and valid from 2027-01-01
 Given interaction rows with occurred_at on 2024-01-15 and on 2023-12-20
 When JOB-17 runs on Sunday 2027-01-03
 Then the row from 2024-01-15 stays in the live table
 Then the row from 2023-12-20 moves to the archive container
 Then the job run logs rule version "RET-2027.01"

 Scenario: AC3 Legal hold
 Given case "RW-2024-000311" is marked legal hold and has 40 interaction rows older than 24 months
 When JOB-17 runs
 Then the system keeps its 40 rows in the live table
 Then the hold report lists case "RW-2024-000311" with 40 rows kept
 Then the summary alert to Compliance reads MSG-P1-020 with 1 case on legal hold kept

 Scenario: AC4 A rule with months outside the allowed range
 Given a retention load version "RET-2026.12" with a row for DP05 interaction at 0 months
 When the load is validated
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-002 for field "retention_months" between 1 and 600
 Then version "RET-2026.11" stays in force

 Scenario: AC5 The archive write fails
 Given the archive container refuses writes
 When JOB-17 runs
 Then the system deletes no interaction row
 Then the job run ends "FAILED" with MSG-GEN-006 for system "Archive container"

 Scenario: AC6 A repeat run in the same month
 Given JOB-17 archived 1,250 rows on 2026-12-06
 When JOB-17 is rerun on 2026-12-06
 Then the system archives 0 rows
 Then the archive container still holds one set of the 1,250 rows

 Scenario: AC7 A row exactly at its retention age
 Given an interaction row with occurred_at 2024-12-06T00:00+07:00
 When JOB-17 runs on 2026-12-06
 Then the row stays in the live table

 Scenario: AC8 A rule for the decision log is refused
 Given a retention load version "RET-2026.12" with a row for product "DP12", table "decision_log_entry"
 When the load is validated
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-002 and check "decision_log_entry is not archived by the retention job"

 Scenario: AC9 A rerun while the job is running
 Given JOB-17 is running
 When a platform administrator posts a rerun of JOB-17
 Then the system refuses the rerun with status 409 and MSG-P2-006
```

secs.h: RWB-E1-018 Case ID issuance and case record v1
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-018 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-01 Generate the case ID; FEAT-CWC-02 Create one case per customer and product; FEAT-CWC-03 Hold the case state in the ACE database; FEAT-CWC-04 Apply the entry rule at 90 days past due; FEAT-CWC-05 Apply the exclusion rules as data; FEAT-CWC-20 Expose the workflow admin API; FEAT-CWC-21 Log every workflow event |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-001, REQ-CWC-002, REQ-CWC-003, REQ-CWC-004, REQ-CWC-005, REQ-CWC-016, REQ-CHO-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D6 entry; D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 open |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-042, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build, the batch gate behind a flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43) |

As a **product owner**, I want **every account at 90 days past due or more in the ACE account view that is not excluded placed on one recovery case per customer and product, with a case ID in the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN issued at creation and never reused, a status and its linked accounts read from ACE by business key, created by rule when the ACE ALS batch for the business date is complete**, so that **every team, letter and document refers to one case ID**.

Recovery teams keep their own lists today, so one account can be on several trackers under different references, and some accounts at 90 days past due have no owner at all (control CTL-01 answers this audit finding). Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench loads nothing: ACE ingests the ALS account, the SCBPDM customer and the EFS collections history, and P3 reads them through `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_ca_relation`. This story creates the case by rule when the ALS batch for the business date reaches COMPLETED in `v_ace_batch_status`, blocks excluded accounts with a logged reason, and gives the case an ID that every later document carries. It meets REQ-CWC-001 to REQ-CWC-005 and REQ-CWC-016, and supports reconciliation REC-01 (accounts at 90 days past due against open cases, zero unexplained) and REC-05 (every `account_key`, `person_key` and `primary_person_key` on a P3 table resolves to its ACE view row).

- RWB-E1-001 is done: `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `case_party` and `case_entry_exclusion` exist in the V0001 baseline.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the Section A views exist, including `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_ca_relation`. `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the batch gate stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- RWB-E1-016 is done: the P1 ACE source query is published and returns the view rows by business key.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: parameter `case.entry.dpd` = 90 is in force (DL16).
- The exclusion rows (rule table EXCLUSION) are loaded with reason codes DECEASED, FRAUD, BANKRUPTCY, ACTIVE_PLAN and OPEN_DISPUTE (REQ-CWC-004). Their inputs are read from `v_ace_account.tdr_flag`, `v_ace_customer.deceased_flag`, `recovery.account_ext.dispute_open` and `recovery.party_ext.deceased_override`, `.bankruptcy` and `.fraud_flag`, all by business key.
- The exposure band table is served by the reference data service (RWB-E1-043, LOV-EXPOSURE).
- The ALS batch for the business date is COMPLETED in `v_ace_batch_status`, and RWB-E1-015 has raised AceDataReady (EV-26).
- JOB-02 runs as `recovery_svc`, which holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`. Readers hold Case record R (roles.txt permission matrix).

1. ACE: the ALS batch for business date 2026-12-01 completes, and `v_ace_batch_status` holds the row with status "COMPLETED" and `is_complete` true.
2. RWB-E1-015: raises AceDataReady (EV-26) for source ALS and business date 2026-12-01.
3. CaseCreationJob (JOB-02): starts on AceDataReady and reads the entry threshold parameter `case.entry.dpd`.
4. CaseCreationJob: reads `v_ace_account` for every account with `days_past_due` at or above 90 and `data_as_of` equal to the business date, and skips an account that already has an open `case_account` row (`linked_to` is null).
5. CaseCreationJob: for each account reads `v_ace_ca_relation` for the BORROWER `person_key` and `v_ace_customer` for that key; an account whose borrower key has no `v_ace_customer` row is not grouped and gets no case.
6. EntryRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): evaluates the exclusion rows in force for each account over `v_ace_account.tdr_flag`, `v_ace_customer.deceased_flag`, `account_ext.dispute_open` and `party_ext`; an excluded account gets a `case_entry_exclusion` row with the reason code, rule ID and version, and no case.
7. CaseGrouping: groups the remaining accounts by the borrower `person_key` and the product group read from `v_ace_account.product_category`; an existing open case for the same pair receives a new `case_account` row with the `account_key` instead of a new case.
8. CaseNumberIssuer: takes the next number from the sequence for the entry year and formats RW-2026-000123.
9. CaseCreationService: in one transaction writes `recovery_case` with status NEW, `primary_person_key`, `dpd_at_entry`, `total_outstanding_at_entry` and the exposure band, the `case_account` rows with `account_key` and `is_primary`, the BORROWER `case_party` row with `person_key`, and CaseCreated (EV-01) in the outbox. The primary account is the linked account with the highest `total_balance` on the business date; a tie breaks on the lowest `account_key`.
10. CaseCreationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with decision code "D6", final call "CASE_CREATED", the entry rule version and the ALS business date; a failed write rolls the transaction back.
11. CaseCreationJob: records counts (accounts read, excluded, linked, created, failed) on the job record; JOB-03 starts after it.
12. Case owner: opens the case through GET /cases/{caseId} and its accounts through GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The account matches an exclusion row | No case; `case_entry_exclusion` row with reason code and rule version | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | The borrower already has an open case for the same product group | The account is linked to that case by `account_key`; no new case | None | AC3 |
| X3 | Days past due is 89 in `v_ace_account` | No case; the account is read again on the next complete ALS batch | None | AC7 |
| X4 | JOB-02 runs again for the same business date | No duplicate case, link or number | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The ALS batch for the business date is not COMPLETED | JOB-02 does not start; no case from an incomplete day; it starts when AceDataReady is raised for the date | MSG-P1-001 | AC9 |
| X6 | The decision log write fails | The case is not created and no number is consumed by a visible case; the account is retried in the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC10 |
| X7 | The yearly number range RW-2026-999999 is used | Creation stops for the year's remaining accounts; incident raised | MSG-P3-025 | AC11 |
| X8 | The same borrower has a mortgage and a hire purchase account at 90 days past due | Two cases, one per product group | None | AC12 |
| X9 | A business key on a case or in the intake has no row in `v_ace_account` or `v_ace_customer` | The intake creates no case or party link from the missing row; an existing link is unchanged; REC-05 lists the key for the data steward and the ACE team; the key is read again on the next complete batch | None | AC13 |
| X10 | A role without Case record R reads a case | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC14 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the ACE views (RWB-E1-069), the P1 ACE source query (RWB-E1-016), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) and the parameter service (RWB-E1-042); allocation follows in RWB-E1-020 |
| Negotiable | Threshold, exclusion reasons and exposure bands are data values; the story fixes the behavior |
| Valuable | Gives about 28,100 accounts at 90 days past due one case each at go-live (DL15) |
| Estimable | One job, one numbering service, one entry evaluator, two read endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

**Package.** `recovery/casewf/casecreation`, Java package `recovery.casewf.casecreation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseCreationJob | Job | JOB-02; listens for AceDataReady; checks the ALS batch row for the business date; runs the entry rule per `account_key`; writes job counts |
| EntryRuleEvaluator | Service | Applies the threshold and the exclusion rows over `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `account_ext` and `party_ext`; returns ENTER or EXCLUDE with reason and rule version |
| CaseGrouping | Service | Groups accounts by the BORROWER `person_key` and product group; finds an open case to link to |
| CaseNumberIssuer | Service | Draws from sequence case_no_seq_YYYY and formats RW-YYYY-NNNNNN; refuses above 999999 |
| CaseCreationService | Service | Decision log write, then case, account links, primary flag, party link and outbox event in one transaction |
| AceSourceReader | Repository | Reads `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_ca_relation` and `v_ace_batch_status` by business key; SELECT only |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, account_ext, party_ext |
| CaseAndWorkflowController | Controller | GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, caseNo search on GET /cases |
| CaseStatusCatalog | Service | Reads LOV-CASE-STATUS through the P4 list interface; no Java enum of statuses |
| ExclusionRuleTable | Rule table | Rule rows with rule table EXCLUSION, read through RuleTableReader (P4) |

**Database**

- Writes recovery_case (all columns), case_account (all columns), case_party (all columns), case_entry_exclusion, outbox.
- Reads recovery.account_ext and recovery.party_ext by business key; no copy of an ACE row is written.
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_case_open_customer_product ON recovery_case (primary_person_key, product_group) WHERE closed_date IS NULL`.
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_case_account_open ON case_account (account_key) WHERE linked_to IS NULL`, so an account is on one open case.
- One `case_entry_exclusion` row per `account_key` and business date, which the job and TC-E1-018-02 assert.
- Migration in this story: `V018_1__case_creation.sql` creates the yearly sequences case_no_seq_2026 and case_no_seq_2027 (created ahead by the job each December) and the two partial unique indexes above. The four tables come from V0001 (RWB-E1-001) and no column is added for source data.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameter `case.entry.dpd` = 90 (RWB-E1-042; DL16), owner RW-COE.
- Exclusion rows "EXCL-2026.11" with the five reason codes, loaded by RW-COE through RWB-E1-029.
- LOV-EXPOSURE bands, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-PRODUCT from the reference data service (RWB-E1-043).

**Build steps**

1. CaseNumberIssuer with the yearly sequence and the 999999 limit; unit and integration tests for AC1, AC4, AC11.
2. AceSourceReader over `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_ca_relation` and `v_ace_batch_status`; test the join by `account_key` and `person_key` for AC1, AC13.
3. EntryRuleEvaluator over the threshold parameter, the exclusion rows and the extension flags; tests for AC2, AC6, AC7.
4. CaseGrouping with the open case lookup and the primary account rule; tests for AC3, AC12.
5. CaseCreationService: the case, links, primary flag and outbox row, then the decision log write as the last step in the same transaction; test for AC10.
6. CaseCreationJob on AceDataReady with the batch gate and idempotent skip; tests for AC8, AC9.
7. CaseStatusCatalog reading statuses from the list; test for AC5.
8. Controller endpoints with access check and scope; caseNo search; test for AC14.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.casecreation`. Off: JOB-02 does not create cases. The batch gate reads a Section B view, so the flag is on only after RWB-ACE-001 lands and V0003 creates `v_ace_batch_status` (DL43).

secs.h: RWB-E1-019 Roles, teams and queues as data
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-019 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-06 Hold roles, teams and queues as data; FEAT-ACA-03 Hold roles as data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-006, REQ-ACA-002 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 3.4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-038, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)**, I want **queues, queue membership and capacity, each tied to a team code and a role code, held as versioned reference data loaded from the Excel template**, so that **the organization changes without a code release**.

Team structure and who works which list are held in spreadsheets today, and a change of team needs a change request to IT. This story holds every queue, its team, its role, its method, its cap, its overflow queue and its members as versioned tables QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER, loaded from one template through the reference data service, with an approver and a one-call rollback, and applies the version in force to the queue tables the engines use. It meets REQ-CWC-006 and REQ-ACA-002 and is the input to allocation (RWB-E1-020), to scope by team (RWB-E1-037) and to control CTL-08.

- RWB-E1-043 is done: ReferenceVersionRegistry and ReferenceDataService hold versions of reference tables, and POST /admin/reference-loads calls them; QUEUE is a LOV-REF-TABLE code and QUEUE_MEMBER is added to it (see additions).
- RWB-E1-038 is done: the reference approval pattern is in use for the delegation table.
- The ROLE and TEAM tables have a version in force (RWB-E1-043); TEAM holds "TDR-BKK", "DIL-BKK", "LIT-BKK", "NPA-BKK", "DS-BKK" and "WO-BKK" (assumed codes; owner Shared operations), each with its region code.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver is the table owner for queues, Shared operations, acting through RW-TEAMMGR with Reference data A (assumed grant; DL01).
- Queue member user IDs are Entra ID object IDs of people who hold the queue's role.

1. RW-REFADM: fills the Queues template (sheets QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER) and calls POST /admin/reference-loads once per sheet with valid from 2026-11-30.
2. QueueTableChecks: runs the queue checks on top of the RWB-E1-043 row checks: team code in TEAM, role code in ROLE, method in LOV-ASSIGN, cap range, overflow queue exists and forms no loop, member holds the queue role.
3. ReferenceVersionRegistry (RWB-E1-043): on any failed row refuses the load whole and names every failed row; on a clean file stores the version with status VALIDATED.
4. RW-TEAMMGR: approves through POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
5. QueueVersionApplier: on the valid from date, applies the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER versions in force to the queue and queue_member tables: upsert by queue code keeping the queue ID, replace active member rows, set table_version.
6. CapacityService: answers capacity questions for the allocation engine from the applied version.
7. QueueMembershipQuery: answers the teams and regions of a user for scope by team (RWB-E1-037).
8. RW-REFADM: if the version is wrong, calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback; the previous version is in force again and QueueVersionApplier re-applies it in one transaction.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A queue names a team code not in TEAM | Load refused in full; the row is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | A cap outside 1 to 500 | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X3 | The approver is the author | Approval refused; version stays VALIDATED | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | Rollback with no earlier version | Refused; current version unchanged | MSG-P3-015 | AC7 |
| X5 | The same file is loaded again for the same valid from | The existing load is returned; nothing new is written (RWB-E1-043 idempotency) | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Valid from is in the future | The version waits; the current version stays in force until that date | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A member does not hold the queue's role | Load refused in full; the member row is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC10 |
| X8 | Overflow queues form a loop | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC11 |
| X9 | A required column is empty | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12 |
| X10 | A role without Reference data C loads a file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-019-13 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the reference data service of RWB-E1-043; adds the queue checks, the apply step and two read interfaces |
| Negotiable | Team codes, queues, caps and members are data; the template layout can change with the checks |
| Valuable | A team change takes one load and one approval instead of a release |
| Estimable | One check set, one applier, two read services, one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |


secs.h: RWB-E1-020 Allocation and assignment engine v1
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-020 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-07 Run the allocation rule table; FEAT-CWC-08 Run the assignment engine by load and continuity; FEAT-CWC-09 Send a case to the overflow queue when no rule matches |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 18.3.2 Allocate work to teams, people and partners by rule; 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D6 entry, take over and own the case |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-019, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-056 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **every new recovery case placed in a queue and given an owner by the allocation and assignment rule tables on the morning it arrives**, so that **each case at 90 days past due has one owner from its first day and nobody allocates cases by hand**.

Cases are allocated today from team spreadsheets, and ownership is agreed by email, so a case can wait days with no owner. This story places every new case in a queue and gives it an owner by rule before 07:00 on the morning after case creation, with the rule row and version on a decision log entry. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009 and REQ-CWC-016, and serves the business measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22) and control CTL-03.

- RWB-E1-018 is done: new cases exist with status NEW, product group, region and exposure band.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: queues, queue members and caseload caps are loaded; queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-03 has a run book and appears in the job monitor.
- The allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" is loaded and approved (rule rows with rule table ALLOCATION; DL24). Every row holds row ID, product group, region, exposure band, target queue, valid from, valid to, approver and test case ID.
- Parameters loaded through RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code` = "RWB-EXC" and `allocation.deviation.queue.code` = "DEV-HANDLER" (assumed values; DL23).
- JOB-02 case creation has completed for today's business date after v_ace_batch_status showed the ALS batch COMPLETED.
- The job runs as service identity SY-CASEWF; rules are evaluated as SY-RULES.

1. Quartz: starts JOB-03 Morning allocation after JOB-02 completes for business date 2026-12-01.
2. AllocationJob: selects every case with status NEW whose last allocation date is before the business date.
3. AllocationService: locks the case row and reads deviation_open; a case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue (R-DEV-01).
4. AllocationRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): reads the allocation rows in force on the business date and returns the first row, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case.
5. AssignmentEngine: reads the target queue's method (DF-WRK-006) and cap (DF-WRK-007), counts the open cases of each queue member and picks the owner below the cap by the method.
6. AllocationService: in one transaction sets queue, team, owner, status ASSIGNED, stage clock start and rule version, writes the assignment with reason ALLOCATION, sets the last allocation date and writes CaseAllocated (EV-02) to the outbox.
7. AllocationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with the row ID, table version, queue, owner and inputs; a failed write rolls the allocation back.
8. AllocationJob: after the last case, builds the allocation summary per team (MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012) and sends it to the team manager through the ACE notification path.
9. AllocationJob: records the run result (cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed) on the job record for the monitor.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Every owner in the target queue is at or above the cap | Case goes to the overflow queue of the target queue; status stays NEW; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No allocation row matches the case | Case goes to the exception queue; status stays NEW; rule gap logged; CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03) published | MSG-P3-012 | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails | Allocation rolled back; case stays NEW with no queue change; retried in the next run | MSG-P3-013 | AC6 |
| X4 | Case has deviation_open = true | Case goes to the deviation handler queue; no case owner is chosen | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The run is repeated for the same business date | Cases already allocated for that date are skipped; no second assignment or log entry | None | AC8 |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **cases moved between queues and roles by the transfer rule table on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, or a manual request with a reason**, so that **hand-offs between teams run without email**.

A case changes hands between the TDR, litigation, NPA and debt sale teams by email today, and the case can wait between teams with nobody holding it. This story moves the case by rule when one of eight triggers fires, picks the owner in the receiving queue, ends the old assignment and records the rule and version, and gives the team manager a programmatic transfer with a coded reason before the Epic 2 screens. It meets REQ-CWC-010 and REQ-CWC-016.

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and the queue structure are in use.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers publish TimerDue when a timer other than a service level expires. A service level breach (TimerBreached) never moves the case (R-UNI-30).
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- The transfer rows version "TRF-2026.11" (rule table TRANSFER) are loaded through RWB-E1-029. Each row holds trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order.
- The transfer reason list LOV-TRANSFER-REASON holds R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue (DL23).
- Manual transfer callers hold Queue and allocation U (RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CAPACITY). Hold and release callers hold Case record U (for example RW-LITOFF acting on a Legal instruction).

1. Event source: writes a trigger event to the outbox: CaseStateChanged for a stage change or a route decided (rule event ROUTE_APPROVED), TimerDue, DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared, ApprovalRequested, DocumentStored or PaymentMissed.
2. TransferListener: receives the event once per event ID; a repeated event ID is ignored (R-UNI-40).
3. TransferRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): reads the transfer rows in force and returns the first row, in row order, whose trigger and condition match the case.
4. TransferService: skips an automated transfer when legal_hold is true (R-UNI-20) and logs the skip.
5. TransferService: locks the case by its version, picks the owner in the target queue with AssignmentEngine, and checks the move is allowed from the case status.
6. TransferService: in one transaction ends the open assignment, writes the new assignment (reason TRANSFER), updates queue, team and owner, and writes CaseTransferred (EV-04).
7. TransferService: as the last step before commit, writes the decision log entry with the row ID, version, from and to queue and owner, and the trigger.
8. Team manager: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer with reason code MANUAL, transfer reason R03 and a target owner or queue; steps 5 to 7 run with reason MANUAL.
9. Litigation officer: calls POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold with action place or lift; the case goes to On hold or back to the status it paused in.

secs.h: RWB-E1-022 Sign-on with SSO, MFA and the first roles
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-022 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-01 Sign on through Entra ID with single sign-on; FEAT-ACA-02 Enforce multi-factor authentication; FEAT-ACA-03 Hold roles as data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002, REQ-ACA-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.4; Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-019 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to sign in to the Workbench once through Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and see only the screens and actions my Workbench roles allow**, so that **access is controlled from the first release and nobody holds a Workbench password or a local account**.

Access to recovery data today is granted system by system, and the bank cannot show who could see a case on a given date. This story makes Entra ID group membership the only way to hold a Workbench role: one group per role per environment, granted through the bank IAM, read at each sign-in and turned into a session with roles, scope and the permission matrix version in force. It meets REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002 and REQ-ACA-010 and supports control CTL-09 (access by role and scope). The measure is the access test set in section 16 passing for every role with real users at the release (DL39: administration roles at Epic 1).

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the role and permission tables exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: the 54 role rows are loaded, and each environment's role rows carry that environment's Entra ID group name in role.entra_group, for example RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN in SIT (pattern from the Single sign-on sheet; final names DL40).
- Permission matrix version PM-2026.11 is loaded from the Users, roles and permissions workbook (54 roles against 14 capability areas).
- Separation of duty version SOD-2026.11 is loaded into the role conflict table (new, see section 11) from the Separation of duty sheet.
- The ACE common module sign-in is configured for the Workbench application in Entra ID (INT-21), with the bank conditional access policy that requires a second factor.
- The person was added to the Entra ID group for their role through the bank IAM: the line manager requested it, the role owner approved it and the access administrator carried it out (section 10).

1. Person: opens the Workbench in the ACE front end.
2. ACE common module: redirects to Entra ID; the person signs in with password and second factor; Entra ID returns an OpenID Connect token with the groups claim and the amr claim.
3. Workbench (SessionResolver): checks that the amr claim contains "mfa".
4. Workbench: maps each group in the groups claim to an active role row by role.entra_group; groups with no active role row are ignored.
5. Workbench: checks the resulting role set against the role conflict table version in force.
6. Workbench: resolves the session: user reference, roles, the permission matrix version in force at that time, and the default scope of each role.
7. Workbench: writes the sign-in event through the AccessEventPublisher (ACE audit log and SOC log through INT-22).
8. ACE front end: calls GET /me/session and shows the first screen with one line naming the roles and the scope, for example "Case owner. Scope: own cases.", and a menu holding only screens whose capability area has R for at least one role.
9. Person: calls any endpoint; AccessCheck evaluates the capability area and right the endpoint declares against the session's matrix version and allows or refuses the call.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an endpoint, for example the admin API | Refused with 403; the refusal is written to the access event stream with the area and right | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | The person is in no Workbench group | Session refused with 401; the access request page shows the message and no data | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | The token has no second factor in the amr claim | Session refused with 401; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-005 | AC4 |
| X4 | The groups give a role pair listed in the role conflict table | Session refused; an incident is raised to the security administrator; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | A service identity calls an area its role does not hold | Refused with 403, exactly as for a person | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A group maps to no active role row | The group is ignored; if no other group maps, X2 applies | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X7 | A new matrix version takes effect while a session is open | The open session keeps the version it resolved; the next session uses the new one | None | AC9 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the tables (RWB-E1-001) and the role rows (RWB-E1-019). The decision log write of access events is added in RWB-E1-039 |
| Negotiable | Group names, roles, conflicts and permissions are data. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Every Epic 1 administration user signs in with one bank identity and sees only what the role allows |
| Estimable | One resolver, one access check, one session endpoint, no business screen |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role. The Workbench holds no password and no local account | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); DT07; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR2 | A session is refused unless the token carries a second factor | NFR-049; FEAT-ACA-02 |
| BR3 | No role inherits from another. A person with two roles holds the union of both roles' letters | permission.letters (DF-REF-043) |
| BR4 | A capability area with no letter for any of the session's roles refuses every action in that area | Permission matrix; CTL-09 |
| BR5 | A role pair listed in the role conflict table may not be held in one session | Separation of duty sheet, roles.txt; role conflict table (new) |
| BR6 | A service identity holds a role in the same table and is checked the same way as a person | REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR7 | A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends | Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR8 | Group names, roles, letters and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is written in code | Principle 1; DT02 |
None. This story does not change a case status. It creates a session with the states Resolved and Refused, and the session ends at sign-out or token expiry.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Line manager (bank IAM, level 4) | Requests a Workbench role for a team member in the bank IAM, naming the person, the role and the reason. May not approve the request they raised |
| Role owner (bank IAM, level 2), the head of the unit whose staff hold the role | Approves or rejects each grant of a role they own after checking the separation of duty table |
| Access administrator (bank IAM, level 3), Chief Debt Recovery Management Office (assumed, DL01) | Adds the person to the Entra ID group of the approved role in each environment requested. Approves no grant |
| Application owner (level 1), Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe (assumed, DL02) | Approves the roles table and each group to role mapping |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Maintains the Entra ID groups and the IAM link (DL40); receives the conflict incident in AC6 |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or group mapping version. Approves none |
| RW-CASEOWN and every bank role | Signs in and uses the screens of the role |
| RW-PHONECOL Phone collector | Signs in; refused on Platform administration (AC2) |
| SY-RULES and the other service identities | Act under their managed identity and their own role row |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Read GET /admin/roles (Platform administration R) |

The four administration levels act in the bank IAM, not in the Workbench. If the bank chooses central administration (DL01), level 3 moves to the central IAM team and nothing in this build changes.

**Published interface AccessCheck** (package recovery.access.signin), called by every module's controller through a Spring method interceptor:

```java
AccessDecision check(SessionContext session, CapabilityArea area, Right right);
SessionContext resolve(VerifiedToken token); // throws SessionRefusedException(reasonCode, messageId)
```

**Published interface AccessEventPublisher** (package recovery.access.signin):

```java
void publish(AccessEvent event); // E1: ACE audit and SOC log through INT-22; RWB-E1-039 adds the decision log
```

- Package: folder `recovery/access/signin` in the recovery module; Java package `recovery.access.signin`. Front end: `recovery/access` folder in the ACE front end.
- Components:

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | Controller | GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session; maps refusals to problem responses with messageCode |
| SessionResolver | Service | Checks the amr claim, maps groups to role rows, applies the conflict check, builds SessionContext |
| AccessCheckService | Published interface | Implements AccessCheck: unions the letters of the session's roles in the area and tests the right |
| AccessCheckInterceptor | Service | Reads the capability area and right declared on each endpoint (x-capability) and calls AccessCheck before the handler |
| AccessEventPublisher | Published interface | Writes sign-in and refusal events to the ACE audit and SOC log |
| AccessAndAdministrationRepository | Repository | Reads role, permission and role_conflict rows in force |
| RoleConflict | Entity | Maps the new role_conflict table |
| SessionBanner | React component | Shows the one-line roles and scope from GET /me/session |
| AccessRequestPage | React component | Shows MSG-P4-001 and no data when the session is refused with NO_ROLE |

- Database: reads role (id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group, is_active), permission (role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version, is_active). Creates table role_conflict (id uuid, role_code varchar(20), conflicts_with varchar(30), reason varchar(200), conflict_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, plus the standard columns) with Flyway migration V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql; conflicts_with holds a role code or the class values ANY_BUSINESS_ROLE and ANY_OTHER_ROLE. Index ix_role_entra_group on role (entra_group) where is_active.
- Configuration and reference data: role rows and group names (loaded by RW-REFADM after RWB-E1-019; names DL40); permission matrix PM-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM, approved per RWB-E1-037); role conflict version SOD-2026.11 (loaded by RW-REFADM from the Separation of duty sheet); LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE; scope line wording from labels per DL10. Property `rwb.access.required-amr=mfa`.
- Build steps:
 1. Create the role_conflict migration and entity; load SOD-2026.11 into SIT with six rows from the Separation of duty sheet that name Workbench roles.
 2. Build SessionResolver: amr check, group to role mapping on active rows, conflict check, SessionContext with versions; unit tests for AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8.
 3. Build AccessCheckService with letter union per area; unit tests for every letter and the dash.
 4. Build AccessCheckInterceptor reading the declared area and right; contract test that every operation in api.yaml has one.
 5. Build AccessEventPublisher to the ACE audit and SOC log; refusal reason codes NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT, NO_RIGHT.
 6. Build GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session with problem responses.
 7. Build SessionBanner, menu filtering by capability area and AccessRequestPage.
 8. Hold the resolved versions on the session and test AC9 with two matrix versions.
- Feature flag: `rwb.access.sso-roles`.
- Done when: the tests in section 16 pass, a test user per Epic 1 administration role signs in with MFA in SIT, and the contract test finds no endpoint without a declared capability area.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Sign-in with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor (new) | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in (new) | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

Thai text for each message follows DL10; proposed Thai for the new messages is in the additions file.

No screen in this story. The ACE front end shell shows the session line from GET /me/session at the top of every page and hides menu entries whose capability area the session cannot read. A person with no role sees the access request page with MSG-P4-001 and no data. Epic 1 has no business screens (DL39); RW-CASEOWN test users exist in SIT and UAT only.
