secs.h: RWB-E1-023 Case record view v1, read only
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-023 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-11 Show the case record view read only |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.1, 5.4 and 5.6 |
| L3 process | 06 Take over and own the case |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 open |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-037, RWB-E1-039, RWB-E1-068, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build, the freshness line behind a flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43) |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **one read-only screen per case with the case ID, accounts, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, contact history and documents, read live from the ACE views by business key with the business date of each**, so that **I stop searching files and systems to understand a case**.

A case owner opens EFS, ALS, shared drives and team spreadsheets today to answer one question about a case. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench holds no copy of the account, the customer or the contact point: the screen reads `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key` and `person_key`. The identity number is already masked inside `v_ace_customer` (`id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`) and the contact values are masked at the API by role (RWB-E1-037), so no clear personal value is copied into a Workbench table or a screen cache. This story puts the case, its accounts and arrears, its parties and contacts, its contact history and its documents on SCR-03, each section showing the ACE business date behind it, and writes every view of personal data to the access log. It meets REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005 and REQ-ACA-006.

- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist with `account_key` links on case_account and `person_key` links on case_party.
- RWB-E1-024 is done: the document hub lists documents by case.
- RWB-E1-068 is done: the interaction ledger reads back through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the masking rules by role are in force (DL26) and name the view field IDs.
- RWB-E1-039 is done: access events are published to the access log.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` are Section A views. `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the freshness banner stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- The account, customer and contact views carry the ACE business date: `v_ace_account.data_as_of` and the ALS, SCBPDM and EFS rows in `v_ace_batch_status`.
- `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.
- The user holds a role with Case record R and the case is in the user's scope.
- Personal data access is logged through AccessEventPublisher (RWB-E1-039), which also sends the PII access record to PII Kafka through the ACE common module.

1. Case owner: opens a case from SCR-02 Case list; SCR-03 shows the Loading state.
2. CaseRecordPage: calls GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, GET /cases/{caseId}/parties, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions and GET /cases/{caseId}/documents in parallel.
3. CaseAndWorkflowController: checks Case record R and the scope; out of scope returns 404.
4. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the header from recovery_case and the links from case_account and case_party.
5. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the account facts from `v_ace_account` by `account_key`, the customer facts from `v_ace_customer` by `person_key` and the contact points from `v_ace_contact` by `person_key` and `contact_type`; every row carries the ACE business date from `data_as_of` or from `v_ace_batch_status`.
6. CaseRecordQueryService: reads the collections history from `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key` and the Workbench entries through InteractionLedgerReader (RWB-E1-068), and merges them into one contact history ordered by time, each row carrying its source system.
7. MaskingApplier: fills each personal field from the masked or the clear view column for the caller's role through FieldMasker, and publishes one AC-READ access event with the field IDs read and their masked flags. A read whose event cannot be written returns nothing.
8. DocumentHub (P5): returns the document list for the case through its endpoint.
9. CaseRecordPage: shows the header (case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags), then Accounts, Parties with their contact points, Contact history and Documents, each with its ACE business date (read only state).
10. CaseRecordPage: shows the stale banner with MSG-P1-001 on any section whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE for the latest business date, and no Workbench load or job status anywhere.
11. CaseRecordPage: shows the on hold banner with MSG-P3-004 when the case is on hold.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch behind a section is not COMPLETE for the latest business date | Section shows with its business date and the stale banner | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; nothing shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | The document hub does not answer | Documents section shows the section message; the rest shows | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 |
| X4 | The access event cannot be written | The read is refused; no case data and no personal field shows | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | The role may not see a personal field in clear | The field shows from the masked view column | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The case is on hold | On hold banner with the prescription date | MSG-P3-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The case has no documents and no contact history | Each section shows its empty sentence | MSG-P3-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Case record R opens the view | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-023-11 |
| X9 | A case link holds an `account_key` that `v_ace_account` does not return | The Accounts row shows the key with empty values; REC-05 lists it; the rest shows | None | AC12 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads data other stories write; no write in this story |
| Negotiable | Section order and the masking rules are data and design choices |
| Valuable | One screen answers the case owner's first questions, from the same ACE rows every other module reads |
| Estimable | One page, five read endpoints, one query service, four views |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Case record view v1, read only

 Background:
 Given case owner U-81 owns case RW-2026-000701, a hire purchase case with 2 accounts
 Given the latest ACE batch business date is 2026-12-02 and v_ace_batch_status shows the ALS, SCBPDM and EFS batches COMPLETED for it

 Scenario: AC1 Loads fast
 Given case RW-2026-000701 has 50 documents and 120 contact history entries
 When U-81 opens the case record view
 Then the header, accounts, parties, contact history and the first page of documents show in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile over 50 openings

 Scenario: AC2 Data from ACE
 Given v_ace_account holds days_past_due 97, total_balance THB 206,175.00 and data_as_of 2026-12-02 for account A-7001
 When the view opens
 Then the Accounts section shows 97 days past due and THB 206,175.00 for A-7001
 Then the section shows business date 2026-12-02 read from v_ace_account.data_as_of
 Then the header shows queue "TDR-BKK-CO", owner U-81, status "IN_PROGRESS" and entry date 2026-11-30

 Scenario: AC3 Customer and contacts from ACE
 Given v_ace_customer holds person_key P-7001 with first_name "Anan", last_name "Sukjai", category "RETAIL" and id_no_masked "XXXXXXXXX4821"
 Given v_ace_contact holds a mobile for P-7001 with contact_key "PHONE:88421" and contact_value "0812345678"
 When the view opens
 Then the Parties section shows the borrower with role "BORROWER", category "RETAIL" and business date 2026-12-02
 Then the borrower's contact points show from v_ace_contact with their contact_type and usage_code
 Then the contact history shows the v_ace_efs_action entries with action code, time and promise status

 Scenario: AC4 Stale ACE batch
 Given v_ace_batch_status holds no COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-12-03 and v_ace_account.data_as_of is 2026-12-02
 When U-81 opens the view on 2026-12-03
 Then the Accounts section shows business date 2026-12-02
 Then the stale banner shows MSG-P1-001 for "DP01 Account and arrears" with date 2026-12-02
 Then no Workbench load or job status shows

 Scenario: AC5 Case outside the scope
 Given case RW-2026-000702 belongs to team "LIT-BKK" and U-81 has scope Own
 When U-81 opens case RW-2026-000702
 Then the response is 404 with MSG-P4-003
 Then no case data shows

 Scenario: AC6 Document hub unavailable
 Given the document hub does not answer within 3 seconds
 When U-81 opens the view
 Then the Documents section shows MSG-P3-023 for "Documents"
 Then the header, accounts, parties and contact history show

 Given the access event stream rejects every write
 When U-81 opens the view

 Then no personal field shows

 Given case RW-2026-000703 has no documents and no contact history
 When its owner opens the view

 Scenario: AC11 No copy of the account on the case

 Given the ALS batch for 2026-12-03 holds THB 210,000.00 for A-7001
 When U-81 opens the view on 2026-12-03
 Then the Accounts section shows THB 210,000.00 and business date 2026-12-03
 Then no Workbench table holds the previous balance for the case

 Given case RW-2026-000701 links account_key A-7010
 Given v_ace_account holds no row for A-7010
 When U-81 opens the view
 Then the Accounts section shows A-7010 with empty balance and days past due
 Then the rest of the case shows
 Then REC-05 lists account_key A-7010 for the data steward and the ACE team
```

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every document stored against its case with its type, date, source and extracted fields, legal types held in a write-once container, and every version kept**, so that **I find a document by case ID, type and date, and a legal document cannot be changed after it is stored**.

Recovery documents are held today in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit (FSD P5 A1.3). This story builds the store and the index that every other document story writes to: one document record in the Workbench document hub per file, the file in blob storage, legal types write-once (DT06, ADR-007, control CTL-12). It meets REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003 and REQ-DCM-008. The module measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.1.1), which can only be counted once every document is indexed against its case.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: the tables document and document_field exist in the recovery schema.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake container, rwb-docs (standard), rwb-docs-legal (write-once) and rwb-quarantine exist, reached by managed identity through DocumentStorage.
- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist and the P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns a case by ID.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force with the six types, the write-once flag and the retention class of each type.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the P7 published interface DecisionLogWriter writes an entry inside the caller's transaction.
- Document hub parameters loaded (this story creates the table): INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG; INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25, assumed (DL11). RWB-E1-053 and RWB-E1-057 read the same table.
- The caller is the upload service (RWB-E1-026, user with Documents C) or the intake (RWB-E1-032, SY-OCR). A reader holds Documents R with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.store is on.

1. Caller: calls DocumentStore.store with the case ID, the document type, the source, the file in the intake container, its SHA-256 hash and any extracted fields.
2. DocumentStoreService: gets the case through CaseDirectory.findById and refuses the call if the case does not exist.
3. DocumentStoreService: reads the type row from the document type table version in force: write_once and retention_class.
4. DocumentStoreService: checks the file type by its content signature and the file size against INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB.
5. DocumentStoreService: looks for an active document on the case with the same type and hash; if one exists, returns it and stops.
6. DocumentStoreService: in one transaction, writes the decision log entry (decision code DOCATT, final call STORED) through DecisionLogWriter, inserts the document row with doc_version 1 and state COPY_PENDING, inserts the document_field rows and writes DocumentStored (EV-16) to the outbox.
7. DocumentStoreService: after commit, calls DocumentStorage.store (RWB-TE-012), which writes the file to rwb-docs-legal when write_once is true and to rwb-docs otherwise, at {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1; the service sets storage_ref and state STORED.
8. User with Documents R: opens the document from the case documents screen (SCR-30); GET /documents/{documentId} returns the metadata, the extracted fields and the version list; GET /documents/{documentId}/content returns the file. The ACE common module writes each read to the PII access log.
9. User with Documents U: adds a version with POST /documents/{documentId}/versions; the service inserts a new document row with doc_version n+1 and previous_version_id set to the current row, and marks the earlier row is_active = false. The earlier version stays readable.

- Flyway migration `V1_5_024__document_store.sql`: adds document.previous_version_id uuid null with a foreign key to document(id) and document.content_sha256 char(64) not null; creates document_hub_parameter (id, param_code varchar(40), param_value varchar(200), unit varchar(20), table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (param_code, table_version).

2. Build DocumentHubParameters and DocumentTypeReader with the valid_from and valid_to rule of the type table; unit test the version in force on a boundary date.

5. Call DocumentStorage after commit and build CopyPendingStep; integration test against the SIT storage account with rwb-docs-legal under its immutability policy for AC1, AC2 and AC11.
6. Build addVersion with the latest-version rule and optimistic locking; test AC4, AC9, AC10.
7. Build delete and replaceContent with the write-once refusal and the audit event; test AC2.
8. Build the controller endpoints with the access check and scope; API tests for AC1, AC12 and the access test.

secs.t:

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the first six document types (demand letter, court notice, appraisal report, title deed, settlement agreement, guarantor notice) with their key fields agreed with Legal and NPA and held as versioned reference data**, so that **the OCR pipeline, classification and extraction have one signed target list**.

Classification and extraction cannot be built or measured until the bank fixes which types are read and which fields come out of each (REQ-DCM-004, DL19). Today no signed list exists, so the model would train on a list that may change. This story turns the agreed list into a versioned table that the store (RWB-E1-024), classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053) read, and that changes by a data load without a code release (DT02). The measure it serves is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.3.1).

- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 ACE views are in place, so the source fields that each document type can carry are known.
- The load file "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is prepared by the reference data administrator with the six types, 26 fields and the sign-offs of a legal counsel user and a Head of NPA user.
- LOV-RETENTION holds the codes LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y, assumed until the bank retention schedule arrives (DL26), loaded by the data steward.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds Reference data A (see section 10).
- The P4 endpoint POST /admin/reference-loads exists and calls the P5 ReferenceTableLoader for table code DOCUMENT_TYPE.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.doctypes is on.

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares the list of six types and 26 fields; legal counsel and the Head of NPA review it and sign with a date.
2. Reference data administrator: uploads the file with POST /admin/reference-loads, table DOCUMENT_TYPE, validFrom 2026-11-30.
3. P4 reference load service: passes the rows to DocumentTypeLoader through the ReferenceTableLoader interface.
4. DocumentTypeLoader: validates every row: type code unique, label present, write-once flag present, retention class in LOV-RETENTION, at least one field, both sign-offs with a user ID and a date.
5. DocumentTypeLoader: on any failure refuses the load whole and returns the row errors; the version in force is unchanged.
6. DocumentTypeLoader: on success writes the rows as table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 with status LOADED, not yet in force.
7. Approver: approves with POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; a different person from the loader.
8. DocumentTypeLoader: sets the version APPROVED; from validFrom the readers return it as the version in force; the previous version gets valid_to of the day before.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A row has no Legal or no NPA sign-off, or a sign-off without a date | Load refused in full; version in force unchanged | MSG-P3-027 | AC3 |
| X2 | A row has a retention class not in LOV-RETENTION, or repeats a type code | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same table version is loaded a second time | Refused with 409; the first load is kept | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A new version with a future valid from date | The current version stays in force until that date; open work keeps the version it used | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve their own load | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Reference data C uploads the file | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-025-08 (Access) |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the ACE view list (RWB-E1-069) and the P4 reference load endpoint |
| Negotiable | The type list and fields are data; the bank list replaces the six proposed types under DL19 |
| Valuable | Gives the OCR, classification and extraction stories one signed target |
| Estimable | One table, one loader, one validation set |
| Small | Under one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Document types and fields agreed

 Background:
 Given LOV-RETENTION holds "LEGAL10Y" and "GENERAL05Y"
 Given user "TEST-REFADM-01" holds RW-REFADM
 Given user "TEST-APPROVER-01" holds Reference data A

 Scenario: AC1 Field list signed
 Given the six types and their 26 fields in load file "DOCTYPE-2026.11"

 When "TEST-REFADM-01" loads the file for table "DOCUMENT_TYPE" with valid from 30 November 2026
 Then the load has status "LOADED" with 6 rows
 Then every row holds both sign-off user IDs and both dates

 Scenario: AC2 Reference data
 Given the load from AC1
 When "TEST-APPROVER-01" approves it
 Then the document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is in force from 30 November 2026
 Then it holds DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, APPRAISAL_REPORT, TITLE_DEED, SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT and GUARANTOR_NOTICE
 Then COURT_NOTICE holds the fields court_name, black_case_no, notice_date and hearing_date with retention class "LEGAL10Y" and write_once true
 Then APPRAISAL_REPORT has retention class "GENERAL05Y", write_once false and 4 fields

 When "TEST-REFADM-01" loads it

 Then no row of that file is written and the version in force is unchanged

 When "TEST-REFADM-01" loads a file with version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" again
 Then the system refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P3-027 naming "version already loaded"
 Then the first load is unchanged

 When "TEST-REFADM-01" approves it
 Then the system refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P7-002
 Then the load stays "LOADED"
```

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to upload, see and search the documents of a case from the case record view**, so that **the case file is complete and I find a document by type and date without leaving the case**.

Case owners hold documents in shared drives and email today, so the case file is never complete in one place (FSD P5 A1.3). This story puts the case documents screen SCR-30 on the case record view: upload with a type, a list of every document on the case, a search by type and date, and a checklist placeholder showing which of the six agreed types are present. It meets REQ-DCM-008 (search by case, type and date from the case record view) and REQ-DCM-001 (every document stored against its case with type, date and source). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.4.1), which needs documents on the case first.

- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore stores, versions and reads documents.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force.
- RWB-E1-041 is done: the malware scan runs on every file before storage.
- RWB-E1-045 and RWB-E1-030 are done: product parameters and the queue measures used by the case record view exist.
- Parameters INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB = 25 (assumed, DL11) and INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES = PDF, JPG, PNG are in force.
- The user holds a role with Documents C to upload and Documents R to list, with the case in scope.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.casedocs is on.

1. Case owner: opens case RW-2026-000123 on the case record view (SCR-03) and the Documents tab (SCR-30, state Loading then list).
2. Front end: calls GET /cases/{caseId}/documents and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist and shows the list and the checklist placeholder.
3. Case owner: chooses Upload, picks a file and a document type from the list, and submits; the front end checks the size against INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB before sending and sends an Idempotency-Key.
4. CaseDocumentUploadService: puts the file in the intake container, calls the malware scan (RWB-E1-041) and, if clean, calls DocumentStore.store with source UPLOAD.
5. DocumentStore (RWB-E1-024): writes the decision log entry, the document row and DocumentStored, then copies the file.
6. Front end: on 201 refreshes the list; the new document shows within 5 seconds of submit.
7. Case owner: enters a type and a date range in the search bar; GET /cases/{caseId}/documents with type, dateFrom and dateTo returns only the matching documents, newest first, 20 per page.

As the **case workflow module (SY-CASEWF)**, I want **one writer that validates and records case created, owner assigned, case transferred and document attached, with the rule ID and version used, in the same transaction as the action**, so that **the first decision records exist in Epic 1 and no action proceeds without its record**.

Without one writer, each module would build its own record and some actions would go unrecorded. This story gives every module one published interface that checks each record against the seven field groups, refuses an incomplete record, writes it in the caller's transaction so that a failed write stops the action, ignores a repeated event and publishes DecisionRecorded. It meets REQ-DRI-004 and REQ-DRI-005 and is the automated part of control CTL-06. The measure is decisions with a log entry: target 100 percent, and no action without one (NFR-034).

- RWB-E1-008 is done: the store appends hash-chained entries and holds the columns chain_seq, corrects_entry_id and actor_user_id.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: the writer's failure alert and run book are in the job and service monitoring.
- LOV-DECISION is loaded by RW-DATASTEW with the decision codes, including the access event codes for RWB-E1-039.
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.decision.code.CASE_CREATED=D6, rwb.decision.code.OWNER_ASSIGNED=D6, rwb.decision.code.CASE_TRANSFERRED=D6, rwb.decision.code.DOCUMENT_ATTACHED=D6 (assumed; D6 is the entry and ownership decision; owner RW-DATASTEW).
- The ACE outbox (RWB-TE-006) is available in the same database transaction.

1. Calling module (for example SY-CASEWF in the morning allocation): builds a DecisionLogRecord with the case, the event, the rule ID and version, the inputs reference, the actor and an idempotency key, inside its own transaction.
2. Calling module: calls DecisionLogWriter.write as the last step before commit.
3. Writer (DecisionLogWriterService): checks that a transaction is open; refuses the call if not.
4. Writer: checks the idempotency key; for a key already written, returns the first entry reference and counts the repeat.
5. Writer (DecisionLogRecordValidator): checks the required fields and the version group; refuses an incomplete record with the missing field named.
6. Writer: calls DecisionLogStore.append (RWB-E1-008).
7. Writer: writes the DecisionRecorded event to the outbox in the same transaction.
8. Calling module: commits; the action, the entry and the event are stored together.
9. Writer: on a refused record or a failed append, raises the exception; the caller's transaction rolls back, an incident is raised and the caller shows MSG-P7-003 or its own message.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record misses the version group, the inputs reference, the final call or the case | Refused; the writer logs the error with the missing field; the caller's action rolls back | MSG-P7-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | A record carries a rule ID with no rule version | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC3 |
| X3 | The store cannot be written | The caller's action rolls back; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The same event arrives twice with the same idempotency key | One entry; the repeat is counted | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The writer is called outside a transaction | Refused with IllegalTransactionStateException; nothing is written | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A record carries a decision code not in LOV-DECISION | Refused as X1 | MSG-P7-009 | AC7 |

secs.h: RWB-E1-028 Service levels, timers, escalation and prescription dates
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-028 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-11 Set service levels and stage timers; FEAT-CWC-12 Set and track prescription dates; FEAT-CWC-13 Escalate a breached timer to the named point |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes; 06 Take over and own the case; 08 Litigate and enforce |
| Decision | D7 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-045, RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a service level per queue and status, a timer on every case, a warning to the owner and a breach raised to the named escalation point by rule, and a prescription date set from the legal periods**, so that **no case waits past its limit unseen and no legal claim expires unnoticed**.

Deadlines are tracked in personal diaries today, and audit found litigation not filed for debtors meeting the criteria (CTL-18). This story starts a service level timer each time a case enters a queue and status, warns the owner at the warning point, raises a breach to the escalation role without moving the case, and sets the prescription date at case creation from the legal period for the product. It meets REQ-CWC-011, REQ-CWC-012 and REQ-CWC-016 and serves the measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22).

- RWB-E1-020 is done: CaseAllocated is published when a case gets a queue and owner.
- RWB-E1-045 is done: ProductParameterService serves the SERVICE_LEVEL row for a product group and a case status, with limit, unit, warning percent and escalation role.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: ReferenceDataService serves the LEGAL_PERIOD table in force, and the holiday calendar is read from v_ace_holiday over the ACE Bank of Thailand table bot_holiday.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- SERVICE_LEVEL row, values assumed until the business sets them (DL22): product group HIRE_PURCHASE, status ASSIGNED, limit 5 working days, warning percent 80, escalation role RW-TEAMMGR.
- LEGAL_PERIOD row owned by Legal: HIRE_PURCHASE 2 years from the last payment date (assumed value from the current story; other products loaded by Legal). Parameter `legal.prescription.warn.days` = 180 (assumed) from RWB-E1-042.
- v_ace_holiday marks 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-07 as non-working days (synthetic test values).
- JOB-05 runs every 5 minutes as SY-CASEWF.

1. TimerStarter: on CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged, stops the running SERVICE_LEVEL timer of the case.
2. TimerStarter: reads the service level for the new queue and status and starts a SERVICE_LEVEL timer with started_at, expires_at in working days and warn_at at the warning percentage.
3. PrescriptionService: on CaseCreated, reads the last payment date of each linked account through the P1 interface and the legal period for the product, and sets the earliest result as the prescription date.
4. PrescriptionService: starts a PRESCRIPTION timer with expires_at on the prescription date and warn_at 180 days before; a PRESCRIPTION timer never pauses.
5. TimerCheckJob (JOB-05): every 5 minutes finds RUNNING timers whose warn_at or expires_at has passed.
6. TimerCheckJob: for a passed warn_at, writes the decision log entry and sends MSG-P3-003 to the case owner once.
7. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of a SERVICE_LEVEL timer, writes the decision log entry with rule R-UNI-30, sets the timer EXPIRED with escalation level 1, and publishes TimerBreached with the escalation role; the case keeps its queue and owner.
8. TimerCheckJob: for a passed expires_at of any other timer type, sets it EXPIRED and publishes TimerDue.
9. TimerPauseHandler: on DeviationRaised pauses the SERVICE_LEVEL timer; on DeviationCleared resumes it and moves expires_at and warn_at by the paused time (R-UNI-43).
10. Case owner or team manager: reads the timers through GET /cases/{caseId}/timers and the prescription date through GET /cases/{caseId}.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No SERVICE_LEVEL version is in force on the date | No timer; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC4 |
| X2 | No legal period for the product | Prescription date not set; the case is listed on the exception queue | MSG-P3-026 | AC5 |
| X3 | An account has no last payment date | The contract date is used | None | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-05 did not run for 40 minutes | The next run raises every missed warning and breach once | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The timer check runs again after a breach | The breach is not raised twice | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Decision log write fails at a breach | The timer stays RUNNING and the breach is raised by the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | A deviation is raised on the case | Service level timer paused; prescription timer keeps running | MSG-P3-004 | AC10 |
| X8 | The warning point is 4 of 5 working days | Warning sent once, at the first check after 4 working days have passed | MSG-P3-003 | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R reads the timers | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-028-12 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Listens to case events from RWB-E1-018 and RWB-E1-020; values from RWB-E1-043 and RWB-E1-045 |
| Negotiable | Service levels, the warning point, escalation roles and legal periods are parameters |
| Valuable | Every case and every legal claim carries a visible deadline |
| Estimable | One timer service, one job, one prescription calculator, one read endpoint |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Service levels, timers, escalation and prescription dates

 Background:
 Given the SERVICE_LEVEL row for "HIRE_PURCHASE" and "ASSIGNED" is 5 working days with warning percent 80 and escalation role RW-TEAMMGR
 Given the LEGAL_PERIOD row for "HIRE_PURCHASE" is 2 years from the last payment date
 Given 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-07 are not working days in v_ace_holiday

 Scenario: AC1 Timer starts
 Given hire purchase case RW-2026-000401 is placed in queue "LIT-BKK-OFF" with status "ASSIGNED" at 2026-12-01 09:00
 When the case arrives
 Then a SERVICE_LEVEL timer is RUNNING with expires_at 2026-12-09 09:00 and warn_at 2026-12-08 09:00
 Then GET /cases/{caseId}/timers returns the timer with its due date

 Scenario: AC2 Warning and escalation
 Given the SERVICE_LEVEL timer of case RW-2026-000401 passes warn_at and later expires_at
 When the timer check runs after each point
 Then owner U-31 receives MSG-P3-003 at the warning point
 Then the system raises at expiry the breach to RW-TEAMMGR of team "LIT-BKK" with TimerBreached and escalation level 1
 Then the case keeps queue "LIT-BKK-OFF" and owner U-31
 Then both the warning and the breach have a decision log entry, the breach with rule R-UNI-30

 Scenario: AC3 Prescription date
 Given a new hire purchase case RW-2026-000402 with one account whose last payment date is 2026-03-15
 When the case is created
 Then the prescription date is 2028-03-15
 Then a PRESCRIPTION timer expires on 2028-03-15 with warn_at 2027-09-17
 Then GET /cases/{caseId} shows prescription date 2028-03-15

 Scenario: AC4 No service level for the queue and status
 Given no SERVICE_LEVEL version is in force on 2026-12-01
 When case RW-2026-000403 is placed in queue "NPA-BKK-CO" with status "ASSIGNED" on 2026-12-01
 Then no SERVICE_LEVEL timer starts
 Then the system lists the case on the exception queue with MSG-P3-026 for "service level" and "HIRE_PURCHASE ASSIGNED"

 Scenario: AC5 No legal period for the product
 Given the LEGAL_PERIOD table has no row for "SSME"
 When SSME case RW-2026-000404 is created
 Then the prescription date is empty
 Then the system lists the case on the exception queue with MSG-P3-026 for "legal period" and "SSME"

 Scenario: AC6 No payment ever made
 Given a hire purchase case RW-2026-000405 with an account that has no last payment date and contract date 2025-06-30
 When the case is created
 Then the prescription date is 2027-06-30

 Scenario: AC7 Missed timer check runs
 Given JOB-05 did not run from 10:00 to 10:40 and three timers passed expires_at in that time
 When JOB-05 runs at 10:45
 Then the system raises three breaches , one for each timer

 Scenario: AC8 A breach is raised once
 Given the SERVICE_LEVEL timer of case RW-2026-000406 is EXPIRED with escalation level 1
 When JOB-05 runs again
 Then the system publishes no second TimerBreached for the timer
 Then escalation level stays 1

 Scenario: AC9 Decision log unavailable at a breach
 Given the decision log store is unavailable
 When the SERVICE_LEVEL timer of case RW-2026-000407 passes expires_at
 Then the timer stays RUNNING with escalation level 0
 Then the job record carries MSG-P7-003 for the timer
 Then the system raises the breach by the first run after the store is back

 Scenario: AC10 A deviation pauses the stage clock and not the prescription clock
 Given case RW-2026-000408 has a RUNNING SERVICE_LEVEL timer and a PRESCRIPTION timer
 When DeviationRaised arrives on 2026-12-02 and DeviationCleared on 2026-12-04
 Then the SERVICE_LEVEL timer was PAUSED from 2026-12-02 to 2026-12-04 and its expires_at moved by 2 working days
 Then the PRESCRIPTION timer stayed RUNNING with the same expires_at
 Then the case record shows MSG-P3-004 with the prescription date while the deviation was open

 Scenario: AC11 The warning point on a 5-day service level
 Given a SERVICE_LEVEL timer of 5 working days started on Monday 2026-12-14 at 08:00
 When the timer check runs on Friday 2026-12-18 at 08:05
 Then the system sends the warning MSG-P3-003 once in that run, with end date Monday 2026-12-21
 Then no warning was sent by the run on Friday 2026-12-18 at 07:55
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A SERVICE_LEVEL timer starts each time the case enters a queue or a status, from the SERVICE_LEVEL row for its product group and status | SERVICE_LEVEL table (RWB-E1-045); DL22; VR-P3-011-1 |
| BR2 | The warning is raised at the warning percentage of the service level | SERVICE_LEVEL warning percent, 80 assumed (DL22) |
| BR3 | A breach is raised to the named escalation role. The case does not move | R-UNI-30; REQ-CWC-011; FEAT-CWC-13 |
| BR4 | The prescription date is the earliest of last payment date plus the legal period over the linked accounts; the contract date applies when no payment exists | LEGAL_PERIOD table (RWB-E1-043); REQ-CWC-012 |
| BR5 | The prescription timer never pauses | R-DEV-01; FEAT-DVH-03; Timer.paused description in api.yaml |
| BR6 | A deviation pauses the stage clock; clearing it resumes the clock and recomputes the timers | R-UNI-04, R-UNI-43 |
| BR7 | A legal hold keeps the clocks running and visible | R-UNI-20 |
| BR8 | Service levels count working days from the holiday calendar in v_ace_holiday | v_ace_holiday over public.bot_holiday (RWB-E1-043) |
| BR9 | Each timer start, warning and breach is logged with its rule and version | REQ-CWC-016; Principle 5 |

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Quartz schedule |
| Job name | JOB-05 Timer check |
| Schedule | Every 5 minutes |
| Input | RUNNING timers with warn_at or expires_at before now (index ix_timer_due) |
| Output | Warnings, breaches, expired timers, decision log entries |
| Events published | TimerBreached (EV-19: timerId, caseId, escalateTo); TimerDue (EV-18: timerId, caseId, timerType) |
| Idempotency key | timerId and the point (WARN or EXPIRE); a timer already EXPIRED or already warned is skipped |
| Restart | The next run picks up every missed timer (batch.txt JOB-05) |

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId (uuid) |
| Response | Timer[]: id, caseId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused, status, escalationLevel |

**Published interface**

```java
// P3, package recovery.casewf.timers (published)
public interface TimerService {

}
```

**Components**

- Writes timer (all columns), recovery_case.prescription_date, outbox.
- Reads with index ix_timer_due (expires_at WHERE status = 'RUNNING'); add `ix_timer_warn ON timer (warn_at) WHERE status = 'RUNNING'` in migration `V028_1__timer_warn_index.sql`, plus column timer.warned_at (New) to record the single warning.
- One running SERVICE_LEVEL timer per case: partial unique index `ux_timer_sl_running ON timer (case_id) WHERE timer_type = 'SERVICE_LEVEL' AND status IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED')`.

2. TimerStarter with stop-and-start on each case event; test AC1, AC4.
3. PrescriptionService with the earliest-date rule and the contract date fallback; tests AC3, AC5, AC6.

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an Excel template for the five rule tables, validation on load (schema, overlaps, unreachable rows, missing default, 50 test cases and a dry run), a load with a version, approval, rollback by one call and a change log**, so that **a rule change goes from template to production without a code release**.

Collection and recovery rules live in procedure documents today, and audit found the procedure not followed because the rules were not in the system (CTL-08). This story takes a rule version from one template through checks that refuse a bad table whole, an approval by Risk, a dated start and a one-call rollback, with each step in the change log. It meets REQ-CWC-013, REQ-CWC-014 and REQ-DRI-004, and covers the Epic 1 rule tables named in DL24: entry, exclusion, allocation, assignment and transfer.

- The five rule tables are agreed for Epic 1: ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER (DL24, option A).
- Each table has 50 test cases with expected results, prepared by RW-COE in the template's Tests tab (assumed count from the current story).
- The loader holds RW-COE (Rules and parameters C); the approver holds RW-RISK (Rules and parameters A). One person may not hold both (separation of duty).
- Live cases exist for the dry run (RWB-E1-018).

1. RW-COE: fills the Rules template (tabs Rows and Tests) for table ALLOCATION, version "ALLOC-2026.12", valid from 2026-12-15.
2. RW-COE: calls POST /admin/rule-versions with the file, route set UNIVERSAL_RULES and valid from.
3. RuleLoadValidator: runs the schema check (columns, types, lists), then overlap, unreachable rows and missing default.
4. RuleTestRunner: runs the 50 test cases against the new rows and compares each result with the expected queue or outcome.
5. RuleDryRun: evaluates the new rows against every open case and counts the cases whose result would change, by product and queue.
6. RuleVersionService: on any failed check, refuses the load whole and names every failed row or test case; on success stores the rows with status LOADED and writes the change log entry with author, time, check result and dry run counts.
7. RW-RISK: approves through POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
8. RuleVersionService: on the valid from date the version is in force; new decisions use it and open cases keep the version they were decided under (R-UNI-38).
9. RW-COE: if the version is wrong, calls POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/rollback; the previous version is in force again in one transaction and the change log records the rollback.

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a daily job that assigns unassigned cases and moves the newest cases off owners above the cap by the assignment rules, and queue counts, ageing and service level breaches published to Power BI**, so that **queues stay balanced and every team manager sees the same numbers as the case list**.

Team managers rebalance work by hand today and count queues from spreadsheets that do not match. This story moves cases left in overflow or without an owner each morning, takes owners above the cap back inside it (R-UNI-19), and publishes depth, ageing, owner spread and breaches as one snapshot that reconciles to the case list. It meets REQ-CWC-015 and REQ-RDF-012.

- RWB-E1-020 is done: AssignmentEngine and CapacityService answer for the queue version in force.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: timers are EXPIRED on a service level breach.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- Caseload caps are loaded (DL23). If DL23 is late, rebalancing reports and moves nothing.
- JOB-03 has completed for the business date; JOB-06 runs as SY-CASEWF.
- JOB-15 Reporting extract copies the snapshot to the data lake for Power BI nightly (owner RW-BIANAL).

1. Quartz: starts JOB-06 at 06:30, or when JOB-03 completes for the business date if that is later.
2. RebalanceJob: lists cases in each queue with no owner and status NEW or ASSIGNED, and owners whose open cases exceed their capacity.
3. RebalanceService: for each owner above the cap, selects the newest cases by assignment time until the owner is inside the cap (R-UNI-19).
4. RebalanceService: skips cases with deviation_open or legal_hold true.
5. AssignmentEngine: picks an owner below the cap in the same queue for each selected or unassigned case.
6. RebalanceService: writes the decision log entry, ends the old assignment, writes the new one with reason REBALANCE and publishes CaseTransferred, case by case.
7. QueueMeasureService: at the end of the run, takes one snapshot per queue at one time: depth, unassigned, age in days from the entry date, owner spread and SERVICE_LEVEL timers EXPIRED.
8. QueueMeasureService: checks each queue depth against the case count for the same queue and time, and publishes the snapshot only when every queue matches.
9. JOB-15: copies the snapshot to the data lake; Power BI shows it from the next morning.
10. TimerBreachNotifier: on TimerBreached from JOB-05, sends the team manager MSG-P3-028 with the queue's breach count.

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the queue and owner columns on the case list, with filters by queue, team and status and an export to Excel**, so that **I see my queues and who owns each case without a new screen**.

Today a team manager asks each collector for their list to know who holds which case. With allocation by rule (RWB-E1-020), every case has a queue and an owner; this story shows both on the case list, filters by queue, team and status inside the manager's scope, and exports the filtered list with the export written to the access log for PDPA. It meets REQ-CWC-007 (the result of allocation is visible) and REQ-ACA-009 (a user sees only the cases their scope allows).

- RWB-E1-020 is done: cases carry queue_id, team_code and owner_user_id.
- RWB-E1-039 is done: the access log interface records exports.
- The user holds a role with Case record R; the team manager's default scope is Team (roles.txt).
- Parameter `caselist.export.maxrows` = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) from RWB-E1-042.
- Owner display names come from the ACE user directory in the common module.

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list; the screen shows the Loading state.
2. CaseListPage: calls GET /cases with page 0 and size 50; the service applies the caller's scope.
3. CaseListPage: shows each row with case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date (list state).
4. Team manager: picks queue "DIL-BKK-CO", team "DIL-BKK" and status "ASSIGNED"; the page calls GET /cases with the filters (filtered state).
5. CaseQueryService: returns only cases inside the caller's scope that meet every filter, with the total.
6. Team manager: chooses Export.
7. CaseExportService: checks the row count against the limit, publishes the access event AC-EXPT with user, time, filters and row count, then builds the xlsx with masking by role (FieldMasker, RWB-E1-037).
8. Browser: downloads "Case list 20261202 1.xlsx".

| X6 | Exactly 10,000 rows | Export allowed | None | AC8 |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **documents from the OCR intake attached to their case automatically when the case ID or the account number is read, with unmatched or ambiguous documents held for a person who sees the OCR text and the candidate cases and attaches the document**, so that **no document is filed by hand when the case is clear and none is filed on the wrong case when it is not**.

Scans, partner files and emails arrive without a case link; today a person reads each one and files it. This story matches each classified intake item to one open case by the case ID or the account number in its text and stores it on that case with no person involved (FSD P5 A2.12). An item that matches no case, more than one case, a closed case or no agreed type is held as unmatched, and a person attaches it from the review queue with the OCR text and the candidates in front of them. It meets REQ-DCM-007 and writes the document attached record required from Epic 1 (REQ-DRI-004, RWB-E1-027). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.12.1).

- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore stores a document and writes the DOCATT decision log entry.
- RWB-E1-050 is done: intake items carry predicted_type, classification_confidence, type_candidates, classifier_version and review_reason.
- RWB-E1-053 is done: the extracted fields case_no and account_no are available for an item where they were read.
- Parameters loaded in document_hub_parameter: CASE_NO_PATTERN = "RW-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6}", ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN = "[0-9]{10}" (assumed; DL21) and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD = 0.80.
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns a case by case number and the open cases for an account number.
- A person resolving unmatched items holds Documents C; items with no candidate are visible only to roles with scope ALL.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.autoattach is on.

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs matchStep after the extraction step.
2. MatchStep: selects intake items with ocr_status DONE, match_status PENDING, no document_id and a predicted type (review_reason empty or LOW_CONFIDENCE), locking each row; items with review_reason UNKNOWN_TYPE or MODEL_UNAVAILABLE get match_status NO_TYPE and are held for a person.
3. CaseMatcher: collects case numbers from the extracted field case_no and from the OCR text with CASE_NO_PATTERN, and account numbers from the extracted field account_no and the text with ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN.
4. CaseMatcher: resolves each case number with CaseDirectory.findByCaseNo and each account number with CaseDirectory.findOpenCasesByAccountNo, and returns one of MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT or CASE_CLOSED with the candidates.
5. MatchStep: for MATCHED, calls DocumentStore.store with the case ID, predicted_type, the intake source, the file, its hash and the extracted fields; the store writes the DOCATT entry with the classifier version, the confidence and the match method, the document row and DocumentStored.
6. MatchStep: on the stored document sets classification_confidence, document_type and type_candidates; for review_reason LOW_CONFIDENCE sets review_status PENDING and write_once false, so it is held in rwb-docs and listed on SCR-31 (RWB-E1-054).
7. MatchStep: sets the intake item match_status MATCHED, case_id and document_id; for any other result sets match_status to the result and candidate_case_ids, and the item is held for a person.
8. Reviewer: opens the Unmatched list on SCR-31 (GET /intake-items), opens an item to see the scan, the OCR text and the candidates, picks the case and the type, and attaches it (POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach).
9. ManualAttachService: checks the case is in the reviewer's scope and the type is in force, calls DocumentStore.store with the reviewer as approver on the DOCATT entry, and sets the item match_status MATCHED.

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **a search across all cases in my scope by document type, date range, extracted field and free text, with every search written to the access log**, so that **I find a document in seconds without opening cases one by one, and every look at personal data can be audited**.

Legal, audit and recovery questions span many cases: every appraisal above a value, every notice from one court, every document naming a guarantor. Today each case folder is opened by hand (FSD P5 A2.6). This story searches the document index, the extracted fields and the OCR text across the cases the user may see, masks personal data the role may not see, and logs each search. It meets REQ-DCM-001 (documents found by their type, date and extracted fields) and REQ-ACA-006 (every read of the document store written to the access log), under control CTL-09 and CTL-11.

- RWB-E1-024 is done: documents and extracted fields are in the index.
- RWB-E1-049 is done: OCR text is in document_text.
- RWB-E1-053 is done: extracted fields carry names from the type table and a confidence.
- Masking rules loaded (DL26). Assumed until Compliance provides them: RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and RW-AUDIT see party names in document text unmasked; every other role sees them masked.
- Parameters loaded in document_hub_parameter: SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 1000, SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE = 50, FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS = 3, FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 100 (assumed; DL11).
- The ACE common module writes access events to the PII access log and confirms each write.
- The user holds Documents R. Feature flag rwb.dochub.search is on.

1. Litigation officer: opens Document search from the Documents menu and enters a type, a stored date range, a field condition (field, operator, value) and or a free text term.
2. Front end: calls GET /documents with the criteria.
3. DocumentSearchService: validates the criteria: at least one criterion, date order, free text length, field in the type's field list.
4. DocumentSearchService: checks with the masking policy that the role may search a personal field or free text; refuses otherwise.
5. DocumentSearchService: gets the case IDs in the user's scope through CaseDirectory.caseIdsInScope (all cases for scope ALL).
6. DocumentSearchRepository: queries active documents in those cases by type and stored date, joined to document_field for the field condition and to document_text for the free text, newest first, up to SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS.
7. DocumentSearchService: builds each row: case number, document type, stored date, source, the matched field or a text snippet of 60 characters with the term highlighted and other personal identifiers masked.
8. DocumentSearchService: writes the access event DOCUMENT_SEARCH (user, role, criteria with the free text term as a SHA-256 hash, result count, case IDs returned) through the PII access log and waits for the confirmation.
9. Front end: shows the first page of 50 rows; the user opens a row in DocumentDetailPanel (RWB-E1-024).

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **a screen to upload a template version, have Legal counsel record the approval and set it current**, so that **templates are managed without a developer**.

A template change today needs a person outside Legal to edit a file and send it round, and nothing records which wording was approved. This story gives the litigation officer an upload and Legal counsel an approve and withdraw action on SCR-33 Template approval, with the approver and date held on the version. It serves REQ-OCC-002 and control CTL-14 (every notice from the current Legal-approved version), and removes the developer from template changes.

- RWB-E1-046 is done: the template and merge_field tables, the load checks and the TemplateCatalog interface exist.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: the freshness stamp shows on screens that read data products.
- The merge field catalog is loaded, with codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE" in the synthetic set.
- The uploader holds RW-LITOFF or RW-LEGAL (Documents C); the approver holds RW-LEGAL (Documents A).
- The ACE storage pattern with a write-once container is available for template bodies (DL27).

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-33 Template approval and chooses the template code and language, or a new code.
2. Litigation officer: uploads the DOCX body and enters product group, channel, notice type, signature basis and the merge codes used.
3. System: checks the role (Documents C), the required fields, the file type and size, and every merge code against the catalog (MergeCodeScanner from RWB-E1-046).
4. System: stores the body write-once, creates the next version number in state Draft and shows it in the list.
5. Legal counsel: opens the Draft version, reads the body and the merge codes, enters the valid from date and approves.
6. System: checks the role (Documents A), that the approver is not the uploader (CTL-05), that the version is Draft and that valid from is not before today; sets state Approved with approver and approval time.
7. System: from valid from, TemplateCatalog returns this version as current; earlier Approved versions stay readable on SCR-33.
8. Legal counsel: may withdraw an Approved version with a reason; the system sets state Withdrawn and generation for that code and language holds (R-LIT-04).
9. System: writes every upload, approval and withdrawal to the ACE audit log with the user, the version and the time.

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **a timeline on the case record view with contacts, documents, assignments, transfers and status changes in time order, each with who or which rule caused it**, so that **I see what happened to the case without asking anyone**.

A case that changes owner today arrives with no history except what the last owner remembers. This story adds a timeline panel to SCR-03 that merges the interaction ledger, the documents, the assignments and the decision log entries for the case in time order, and shows the person or the rule and version behind each event, including the coded reason of a manual transfer. It meets REQ-CWC-016 (every workflow event carries its rule ID and version, now visible) and REQ-OCC-007 (contact history and documents on the case view).

- RWB-E1-023 is done: SCR-03 shows the read-only case record.
- RWB-E1-021 is done: transfers write assignments with a transfer reason and a decision log entry.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: decision log entries can be read by case through the P7 interface.
- The P5 document hub lists documents by case.
- The user holds Case record R and the case is in scope.

1. Case owner: opens SCR-03 for case RW-2026-000801 and selects the Timeline panel.
2. TimelinePanel: calls GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline with page 0 and size 50.
3. CaseAndWorkflowController: checks Case record R and the scope.
4. TimelineService: reads interactions and assignments from P3 tables, documents through the P5 interface and decision log entries through the P7 interface, for the case.
5. TimelineService: maps each record to a TimelineItem with time, type, summary, by and reference.
6. TimelineService: sorts by time, then by a fixed type order for equal times, then by record ID, and returns the page with the total.
7. TimelinePanel: shows each item with an icon for its type; "by" shows a person's name, or a rule ID with its version.
8. Case owner: opens a transfer item; the panel shows the transfer reason, the from and to queue and owner, and the rule version.

secs.h: RWB-E1-037 Role to permission matrix as data and PDPA field masking by role
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-037 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-04 Hold the role to permission matrix as data; FEAT-ACA-05 Mask PDPA fields by role; FEAT-ACA-13 Apply joiner, mover and leaver changes to access; FEAT-ACA-14 Scope a user's cases by team and region |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009, REQ-ACA-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.4; Business Requirements Epic 2, section 3.4 (REQ-ACA-011); Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-022, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **product owner**, I want **the mapping of roles to capability areas, the scope of each role and the masking of each personal data field held as versioned tables that every screen and API applies, with the identity number masked inside the ACE view and contact values masked at the API**, so that **a change of rights is a data load with an approver, a person sees only the cases in their scope, and personal data shows unmasked only to roles that need it**.

Audit findings record unsuitable user access to EFS and staff sending debtor data outside the bank. Today rights are set inside each system and cannot be shown for a past date. This story holds the permission matrix (54 roles against 14 capability areas), the masking rules and the scope rule as versioned data, applies scope before permission on every request, and ends access at the next request when a person leaves. Under D-RCV-35 there is no load and no tokenization: ACE ingests the source row once, `v_ace_customer` exposes the identity number as `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only, and `v_ace_contact` exposes the full phone, email and address because notices and calls need them. Masking is therefore applied to view columns, not to a token stored at load. It meets REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011 and puts controls CTL-09, CTL-10 and CTL-11 in place. The measure is rule and limit changes made without a code release: target 100 percent (FSD P4 A2.4).

- RWB-E1-022 is done: sessions resolve roles from Entra ID groups, and AccessCheck runs on every endpoint.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: POST /admin/reference-loads validates and versions a load file.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` exist, and `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on them and no privilege on `public`.
- Permission matrix version PM-2026.11 (from the Users, roles and permissions workbook) is the version in force.
- Masking version MASK-2026.11 is loaded with no unmasked rows in PROD until Compliance supplies the rules (DL26), so every personal field is masked for every role. SIT carries a test version MASK-SIT-01.
- The masking rules name the view field IDs of Physical Schema v5: DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value` and DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`, plus the name, date of birth and customer number fields.
- The P3 queue membership interface from RWB-E1-019 returns the teams and regions of a user.
- Parameters `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM` and `rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY` are in the parameter catalog (RWB-E1-042).

1. Reference data administrator (RW-REFADM): prepares the matrix file from the approved workbook, with the application owner's approval reference in the file header, and calls POST /admin/reference-loads with table "permission" and validFrom.
2. Workbench (PermissionMatrixLoader): validates the file whole: every active role once against all 14 capability areas, letters only from C, R, U, D, A in that order or "-", known role codes; stores the rows with status Loaded and the new matrix_version.
3. Security administrator (RW-SECADM): reviews the difference report against the version in force and calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve.
4. Workbench: checks that the approver holds the role the parameter names for the table and is not the person who loaded it; writes one decision log entry for the approval with decision code AC-VERS and no case; marks the version Approved with its valid from date.
5. Workbench: from the valid from date, every new session resolves the new version (RWB-E1-022 keeps open sessions on their version), and the screens and endpoints of the new letters open with no deployment.
6. Person: requests a list or a record; ScopeService builds the filter from the role's default scope (own, team, region, all) and the person's teams and regions; the owning module applies it in its query.
7. Workbench: AccessCheck tests the right in the capability area on the records inside the scope.
8. Workbench (FieldMasker): for each field tagged as personal data, reads the masking rule in force for the session's roles. When no rule lets a role see the field in clear, the response is filled from the masked view column (`v_ace_customer.id_no_masked`, `v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked`) or the value is masked by the masker where the view holds no masked column. When a rule allows it, the response is filled from the clear view column where ACE exposes one (`v_ace_contact.contact_value`) or from `id_no_last4` for the identity number. There is no token and no detokenization call.
9. Workbench: the clear `customer.identification_number` never leaves ACE. No Workbench column, token store or service returns it, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive.
10. Workbench: writes one access event with the field IDs and their masked flags, never a value, through the access log (RWB-E1-039).
11. Workbench: on each request, compares the session's groups with the groups the ACE common module holds for the person (refreshed at most every 5 minutes, assumed; DL38); if a group has been removed the session ends and the request is refused.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an action, for example a transfer | Refused with 403 before the handler runs; nothing changes; refusal logged | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | A record outside the person's scope is requested | Refused with 404; the record is not returned and the count of excluded records is never shown | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | A matrix file misses a role, repeats a role and area, or holds a letter outside C, R, U, D, A and "-" | The load is refused in full; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | The person who loaded a version tries to approve it | Refused; the version stays Loaded | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X5 | A role other than the table's approver role calls approve | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, AC13 |
| X6 | The decision log write for an approval fails | The version is not approved and stays Loaded | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | A leaver's group is removed while a session is open | The next request after the membership refresh ends the session | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X8 | No masking rule exists for a personal field and role | The field shows from the masked view column, or is masked by the masker where the view holds no masked column | None | AC9 |
| X9 | Two approve calls for the same load arrive at once | One approves; the second returns 409 and writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X10 | A rule asks for the clear identity number | The rule is refused at load; the clearest value a rule can name is `id_no_last4` | MSG-P1-002 | TC-E1-037-13 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the session (RWB-E1-022), the load service (RWB-E1-043), the writer (RWB-E1-027) and the ACE views (RWB-E1-069), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | Letters, scopes and masking positions are data; Compliance sets the masking values under DL26 |
| Valuable | A change of rights takes effect by an approved load, and personal data is masked by default from the view and the API |
| Estimable | One loader, one scope service, one masker, one approval check |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

```gherkin
 Then the system writes the view to the access event stream with the case ID, the field IDs and each field's masked flag

 Scenario: AC3 Denied action
 Given test user "U-2105" holds only RW-CASEOWN, whose Queue and allocation letter is "R"
 When the user calls POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer for case "RW-2026-000123"
 Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002 before the handler runs
 Then the case owner and queue are unchanged
 Then the system writes one refusal event with area "QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION" and right "U"

 Scenario: AC4 A case outside the scope is not returned
 Given test user "U-2105" holds RW-CASEOWN with default scope "OWN" and owns 12 cases
 Given case "RW-2026-000456" belongs to team "MTG-NE" and another owner
 When the user calls GET /cases
 Then 12 cases return and the total is 12
 Then GET /cases/{caseId} for "RW-2026-000456" returns status 404 with message MSG-P4-003

 Scenario: AC5 A matrix file with an error is refused in full
 Given matrix file "PM-2026.13" lists RW-CASEOWN twice for Case record and gives RW-AUDIT the letters "RX" in Reporting
 When test user "U-2101" loads it
 Then the system refuses the load with message MSG-P1-002 naming the duplicate row and the invalid letters
 Then the system stores no row of "PM-2026.13" and "PM-2026.11" stays in force

 Scenario: AC6 The loader cannot approve
 Given load "PM-2026.12" was loaded by test user "U-2101"
 When "U-2101" calls approve on that load
 Then the system refuses the call with message MSG-P7-002 and the load stays "Loaded"

 Scenario: AC7 An approval that cannot be recorded does not take effect
 Given the decision log store is unavailable
 When test user "U-2102" holding RW-SECADM approves load "PM-2026.12"
 Then the call returns status 503 with message MSG-P7-003
 Then the load stays "Loaded" and "PM-2026.11" stays in force

 Scenario: AC8 A leaver loses access at the next request
 Given test user "U-2107" holds RW-TEAMMGR and has an open session since 08:00
 Given the access administrator removes "U-2107" from group "RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR" at 10:00
 When the user calls GET /cases at 10:06, after the 5 minute membership refresh
 Then the system refuses the call with status 401 and message MSG-P4-001
 Then the system ends the session and a new sign-in is refused

 Scenario: AC9 A personal field with no masking rule is masked
 Given no masking rule in "MASK-SIT-01" covers v_ace_customer.date_of_birth (DF-ACE-059) for any role
 When test user "U-2105" holding RW-CASEOWN opens case "RW-2026-000123"
 Then the date of birth shows masked as "XXXX-XX-XX"

 Scenario: AC10 Two approvals of the same load at once
 Given load "PM-2026.12" is "Loaded"
 When two approve calls for it arrive at the same time from "U-2102" and test user "U-2108" holding RW-SECADM
 Then one call approves and one decision log entry is written
 Then the other call returns status 409 with message MSG-GEN-004 and writes nothing

 Scenario: AC11 The clear identity number never leaves ACE
 Given the recovery service identity recovery_svc in SIT
 Given v_ace_customer holds the identity number "1234567890123" for person_key "P-0001"
 When the identity test runs
 Then SELECT on public.customer is refused with permission denied
 Then SELECT on recovery.v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked "XXXXXXXXX0123" and id_no_last4 "0123" and no column holds the clear value
 Then no Workbench table, token store or service returns the clear identity number for any role

 Scenario: AC12 A read of a personal field is audited
 Given test user "U-2109" holds RW-CASEOWN, which may see DF-ACE-078 in clear
 When "U-2109" opens case "RW-2026-000123" and reads the borrower's phone number
 Then one access event is written with the case ID, field ID DF-ACE-078 and the flag "clear"
 Then the event holds no field value

 Scenario: AC13 Only the table's approver role may approve
 Given load "PM-2026.12" is "Loaded"
 When test user "U-2106" holding RW-COE calls approve on that load
 Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
 Then the load stays "Loaded"
```

secs.h: RWB-E1-038 Delegation of authority table as reference data
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-038 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-06 Hold the delegation of authority table as reference data; FEAT-APD-10 Apply the delegation of authority limits |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-004, REQ-APD-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.4; Business Requirements Epic 2, section 3.7 (REQ-APD-010); Business Requirements Program, sections 5.4 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | D6.4 to D6.6, D7.1 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-029, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **the delegation of authority (which approval level may approve which decision, by product, principal amount and second condition) held as a versioned table that the approval router reads**, so that **approval limits change by an approved data load and every approval can be checked against the limit that applied on its date**.

Approval and authority governance is an audit finding, and limits today sit in the bank regulation and in people's heads. This story loads the 95 limits of Regulation 540031 as amended by Regulation 690070 (chapter 2 for problem loans, chapter 3 for assets held for sale) as versioned rows, and gives the approval router one lookup that returns the lowest approval level whose limit covers a decision, with the version used. It meets REQ-ACA-004 and REQ-APD-010 and is the data behind control CTL-04. The measure is decisions within the delegation of authority: target 100 percent (FSD P7 A2.1).

- RWB-E1-043 is done: POST /admin/reference-loads validates and versions a load file.
- RWB-E1-029 is done: the rule load template and rollback by one call exist for versioned tables.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available.
- The delegation_limit table exists (RWB-E1-001).
- LOV-DECISION holds D5, D6.4, D6.5, D6.6, D7.1, D7.4, D7.5, D8.2, D8.3, D8.4, D9.2 and D9.3; LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL holds L1 to L6; LOV-PRODUCT holds MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME and UNSECURED.
- Parameter `rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit=RW-RISK` is in the parameter catalog (RWB-E1-042).
- The holder and substitute of each level are not yet named (DL18); rows load with holder_user_id and substitute_user_id empty in PROD and with named test users in SIT and UAT.

1. Reference data administrator (RW-REFADM): converts the Delegation of authority matrix to the load file: one row per limit and decision code, for MORTGAGE and SSME, amounts converted from THB million to baht.
2. RW-REFADM: calls POST /admin/reference-loads with table "delegation_limit", validFrom and the version name, for example DOA-2026.11.
3. Workbench (DelegationLimitLoader): validates the file whole and stores 218 rows with status Loaded.
4. Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK): reviews the difference report and calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve.
5. Workbench: checks that the approver holds RW-RISK and did not load the file; writes one decision log entry with decision code AC-VERS and no case; sets valid_to on the rows of the previous version to the day before the new valid from; marks the new version Approved.
6. Approval router (RWB-E2-013): calls DelegationOfAuthority.lowestLevel with the decision, the regulation item (one decision code can cover several items, for example D7.5 covers items 2.1.4, 2.1.6 and 2.1.9), the product, the amounts, the conditions and the decision date.
7. Workbench (DelegationLookupService): walks levels L6 to L1 over the rows valid on that date and returns the first level with a row that covers the request, the row IDs and the version.
8. Workbench: where no row covers the request at any level, returns NOT_COVERED and raises an incident to RW-RISK naming the decision and product.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A file repeats a decision, regulation item, product, level and condition, or a level's highest principal limit falls below a lower level's | The load is refused in full; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | A file holds an unknown decision code, level or product, or a required field is empty | The load is refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The person who loaded the version approves it | Refused; the version stays Loaded | MSG-P7-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | A role other than RW-RISK approves | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | The decision log write for the approval fails | The version is not approved | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X6 | A lookup finds no row for the decision and product, for example hire purchase before the chapter 8 limits arrive | NOT_COVERED is returned and an incident is raised to RW-RISK | MSG-P7-010 | AC7 |
| X7 | A lookup date falls on the last day of the old version or the first day of the new one | The version valid on that date is used | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A write-off is for a director, senior executive, major shareholder or related party | Level L1 is returned whatever the amount | None | AC9 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the load service (RWB-E1-043), the rule load template (RWB-E1-029) and the writer (RWB-E1-027) |
| Negotiable | Limits, holders and substitutes are data; names follow DL18 |
| Valuable | Every Epic 2 approval reads its limit from one approved table |
| Estimable | One loader, one lookup, one approval check |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

