secs.h: RWB-E1-039 Access log into the decision log and break-glass admin
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-039 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P4 Access and administration, with P7 Decision center and log |
| Feature | FEAT-ACA-07 Write every access event to the access log; FEAT-ACA-08 Write the access log into the decision log; FEAT-ACA-09 Use break-glass access with an incident reference; FEAT-ACA-10 Review break-glass use; FEAT-ACA-16 Answer an access audit query |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.4; Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 |
| L3 process | 16 Manage risk, control and compliance; 17 Run the decision center |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-008, RWB-E1-022, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM)**, I want **every sign-in, refusal, read of a case record or document and export written to the decision log store, and emergency access taken only under a break-glass grant approved in the bank IAM against an open incident, for a limited time, with every action marked**, so that **every access can be audited from one log and emergency access is controlled and reviewed**.

The bank cannot answer today who read a debtor's record on a given date, and administrators have standing access to production data. This story writes each access event into the append-only, hash-chained decision log, so access and decisions are queried together, and replaces standing access with a break-glass grant that names an incident, ends on its own and marks every action. It meets REQ-ACA-006 and REQ-ACA-008 and supports controls CTL-09 and CTL-11. The measure is reads of the case store and the document store written to the access log: target 100 percent (NFR-042).

- RWB-E1-008 is done: the decision log store is append only and hash chained.
- RWB-E1-022 is done: sessions, AccessCheck and the AccessEventPublisher exist.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer validates and writes entries.
- LOV-DECISION holds the access event codes AC-SIGN, AC-DENY, AC-READ, AC-EXPT, AC-BGON and AC-VERS (loaded by RW-DATASTEW with this story; recorded in the additions file).
- The Entra ID break-glass group for each environment exists, granted only through the bank IAM with an end time (name per DL40; RWB-SIT-BREAKGLASS assumed in SIT).
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours=4, rwb.access.breakglass.incident-pattern=^INC[0-9]{7}$, rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min=20, rwb.access.breakglass.review-days=1 (assumed values; DL38).
- The case store (P3) and the document hub (P5) call AccessEventPublisher on every read they serve.

1. Person: signs in, or reads a case record, a document or a list, or exports a list.
2. Owning module: calls AccessEventPublisher.publish with the event, the case ID where there is one, and the field IDs returned with their masking position, or the filter and row count for a list or export.
3. Workbench (AccessLogWriter): writes one decision log entry with an access event code, the actor, the area, the result and the details in actions, in the same transaction as the read response is built; if the write fails, the read returns nothing.
4. Platform administrator (RW-PLATADM): raises a break-glass request in the bank IAM naming the open incident, the capability area, the scope and the reason; the security administrator approves it there, and the IAM adds the administrator to the break-glass group until the window ends.
5. RW-PLATADM: calls POST /admin/break-glass with the incident reference, the IAM request ID, the area, the right, the scope and the reason.
6. Workbench (BreakGlassService): checks the break-glass group, the incident reference pattern and the reason length; writes an AC-BGON entry; sets the session grant to end at the earlier of the window end and the group end.
7. Workbench: marks every entry written while the grant is active with the grant ID and the incident reference; the ACE front end shows the MSG-P4-004 banner with the end time.
8. Workbench: after the end time, AccessCheck ignores the grant with no action by anyone.
9. Security administrator: reviews each use inside the review window from GET /admin/access-log with event AC-BGON and the entries marked with its incident, and records the review in the bank IAM.
10. Internal audit (RW-AUDIT): asks who read a case over a period through GET /decision-log with caseId, decision AC-READ, from and to.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The access log entry cannot be written | The read or export returns no data; status 503; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X2 | Break-glass is requested by a person not in the break-glass group | Refused with 403; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-007 | AC5 |
| X3 | Break-glass is requested with no incident reference, a reference that fails the pattern, or a reason under 20 characters | Refused with 422 naming the field | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | An action is attempted after the grant has ended | The grant is ignored; the role's own letters apply; a refusal is logged | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X5 | A second activation is sent while a grant is active | With the same Idempotency-Key the first response returns; with a new key the call returns 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X6 | A role without Platform administration R calls an admin endpoint, such as the access log or the roles list | Refused with 403; an AC-DENY entry is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the store (RWB-E1-008), the session (RWB-E1-022) and the writer (RWB-E1-027) |
| Negotiable | The window, the incident pattern and the reason length are parameters (DL38) |
| Valuable | One log answers who saw what and when, and ends standing administrator access |
| Estimable | One writer adapter, one break-glass endpoint, query through existing endpoints |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

secs.h: RWB-E1-040 Document checklist per case type as reference data
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-040 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-16 Hold the document checklist per case type as reference data |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-025, RWB-E1-026 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the required documents per case type and route held as a versioned reference table that the case documents screen, the case list and the review queue read**, so that **a missing document shows on the case without a person checking a list**.

Litigation packs and guarantee claims fail when a required document is missing, and today the gap is found by a person reading a paper list, often at filing (CTL-19, R-LIT-17). This story holds the checklist per case stage and route as data and keeps a completeness flag per case, recomputed whenever a document is stored or the case changes stage. It meets REQ-DCM-011 and gives the pack checks of Epic 4 and Epic 5 (R-LIT-16, R-GUA-07) one checklist source. The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.16.1).

- RWB-E1-024 and RWB-E1-026 are done: documents are stored and GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist returns the placeholder.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: the six document types are in force.
- RWB-E1-043 is done: the reference data service serves versioned tables with valid from and valid to.
- Checklist version CHK-2026.11 loaded and approved, assumed until the bank list is signed (DL19): stage LITIGATION requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT; stage DEED_IN_LIEU requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT.
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns stage_code, route_code and owner of a case; CaseStateChanged (EV-05) is published by P3.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.checklist is on.

1. Reference data administrator: loads the checklist file with POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads, table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST; the owner approves it.
2. ChecklistLoader: validates every row: stage in LOV-STAGE, route in LOV-ROUTE or empty, document type in the type table in force, no duplicate row; refuses the load whole on any error.
3. ChecklistEvaluator: on DocumentStored (EV-16), on CaseStateChanged (EV-05) and when a checklist version takes effect, takes the case's stage and route through CaseDirectory.
4. ChecklistEvaluator: picks the rows of the version in force for that stage, using the rows for the route where they exist and the rows with no route otherwise.
5. ChecklistEvaluator: counts the active documents of each required type on the case and writes case_document_check: checklist version, required count, present count, missing types and complete.
6. Litigation officer: opens the Documents tab (SCR-30); GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist returns each required item marked present or missing.
7. Case owner: sees the number of missing documents for each case on the case list (SCR-02) through DocumentChecklistService.missingCounts.
8. JOB-12 Document intake: the step checklistRefreshStep finds checklist versions whose valid from date has been reached since the last run and recomputes the cases of the stages they change.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case stage has no checklist rows | The checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"; complete is empty | None | AC6 |
| X2 | A checklist load names a document type not in the type table, or a stage not in LOV-STAGE | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X3 | The same DocumentStored event arrives twice | One recompute result; the second is ignored and counted | None | AC8 |
| X4 | A document type is present only as an inactive earlier version | Counted once, through its active version | None | AC9 |
| X5 | A role without Documents R opens the checklist | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-040-10 (Access) |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store, the types and the placeholder endpoint, all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The items per stage and route are data under DL19; the story fixes how they are applied |
| Valuable | Missing documents show on the case and the case list before a pack is built |
| Estimable | One table, one loader, one evaluator, one stored flag |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Document checklist per case type as reference data

 Background:
 Given checklist version "CHK-2026.11" is in force
 Given stage "LITIGATION" requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT
 Given stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT

 Scenario: AC1 Checklist by type
 Given case "RW-2026-000123" at stage "LITIGATION" holds a demand letter and a court notice
 When the litigation officer opens the Documents tab
 Then the checklist shows the 4 items from version "CHK-2026.11" for "LITIGATION"
 Then DEMAND_LETTER and COURT_NOTICE are marked present
 Then TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT are marked missing

 Scenario: AC2 Change as data
 Given version "CHK-2026.12" adds GUARANTOR_NOTICE for "DEED_IN_LIEU" and is approved with valid from 1 December 2026
 When case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" is opened on 1 December 2026
 Then the checklist shows 4 items including GUARANTOR_NOTICE
 Then no code was deployed between 30 November and 1 December 2026

 Scenario: AC3 Completeness flag
 Given case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" holds a title deed and an appraisal report
 When the pack check runs after the appraisal report is stored
 Then case_document_check for the case has complete false, missing count 1 and missing type SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT
 Then the case owner sees "1 missing" for the case on the case list

 Scenario: AC4 The missing document arrives
 Given the case from AC3 with SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT missing
 When a settlement agreement is stored on the case
 Then case_document_check has complete true and missing count 0
 Then the case list shows no missing documents for the case

 Scenario: AC5 Stage change
 Given case "RW-2026-000789" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" with complete true
 When CaseStateChanged moves it to stage "LITIGATION"
 Then the pack check uses the "LITIGATION" rows
 Then case_document_check has complete false with the missing litigation types

 Scenario: AC6 No checklist for the stage
 Given case "RW-2026-000321" at stage "DEBT_SALE" and no rows for "DEBT_SALE"
 When the Documents tab opens
 Then the checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"
 Then case_document_check has complete empty and missing count 0

 Scenario: AC7 Load with an unknown type
 Given a load file for table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" with a row for stage "LITIGATION" and type "POWER_OF_ATTORNEY"
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P3-027 naming the row and "document type not in the type table"
 Then version "CHK-2026.11" stays in force

 Scenario: AC8 The same event twice
 Given DocumentStored for one document on case "RW-2026-000123" is delivered twice with the same event ID
 When the evaluator handles both
 Then the system writes case_document_check once for that event
 Then the system counts the second delivery as a repeat

 Scenario: AC9 Earlier version of a document
 Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds an appraisal report at version 2 with version 1 inactive
 When the pack check runs
 Then APPRAISAL_REPORT counts as present once
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The checklist per case type is held as reference data so a missing document is visible | REQ-DCM-011; FEAT-DCM-16 |
| BR2 | The case type is the case stage, with route rows taking precedence over rows with no route | LOV-STAGE; LOV-ROUTE; checklist table (New) |
| BR3 | A checklist version takes effect on its valid from date, without a deployment | refdata.txt change process; R-UNI-38; DT02 |
| BR4 | Only active documents count, once per type | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR5 | The completeness flag is recomputed on every document stored and every stage change | EV-16; EV-05 |
| BR6 | A repeated event changes nothing | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The checklist is the source the pack checks read in later epics | R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, R-GUA-07, R-GUA-08 |

None. This story does not change a case status. It writes the completeness flag of the case in case_document_check: complete false while a required type is missing, true when every required type is present, empty when the stage has no checklist.

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/checklist`, Java package `recovery.dochub.checklist`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components.**

2. Build ChecklistLoader with validation against LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and the type table; test AC7.
3. Build ChecklistEvaluator with the route precedence and the active-version rule; unit test AC1, AC6 and AC9.
4. Build the two listeners with the repeat check; test AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC8.
5. Build ChecklistRefreshStep; test AC2 on 30 November and 1 December 2026.
6. Extend the checklist endpoint and build DocumentChecklistPanel and MissingDocumentsBadge; component tests and the access test.

secs.h: RWB-E1-041 Retention classes and virus scan on intake
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-041 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-17 Apply retention classes to stored documents; FEAT-DCM-18 Virus scan every document on intake |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-010, REQ-DCM-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence; L2 13.3 Store and retain documents |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-049 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **every uploaded or scanned file checked for malware before it is stored, and a retention class per document type that the store applies and a monthly job acts on**, so that **the store holds only safe files and keeps each document for the time the policy sets, never removing one silently or while a legal hold is in place**.

Files reach the bank from branches, partners and email; one infected file in the store reaches every user who opens it. Documents also have no retention rule today, so nothing shows when a document may be archived (FSD P5 A2.17, A2.18). This story scans every file before storage and quarantines a failed file, holds the retention classes as data, and runs JOB-17 to archive documents past their class or list them for the Compliance review. It meets REQ-DCM-010 and REQ-DCM-016 (legal hold overrides retention), with NFR-028, NFR-072 and NFR-074.

- RWB-E1-024 is done: documents carry retention_class and write_once from the type table.
- RWB-E1-049 is done: document_intake and JOB-12 Document intake exist.
- The quarantine container exists (RWB-TE-012) and the bank malware scanning service is reachable through MalwareScanClient under SY-OCR (assumed: the scanning service of the ACE storage pattern, DL27).
- Retention class table loaded through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads, table RETENTION_CLASS, version RET-2026.11: LEGAL10Y 120 months, end action REVIEW; GENERAL05Y 60 months, end action ARCHIVE (assumed; DL26).
- The P3 published interface CaseDirectory returns legal_hold for a case.
- Feature flags rwb.dochub.malware-scan and rwb.dochub.retention are on.

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs scanStep first, before ocrStep.
2. ScanStep: selects intake items with no scan_result and sends each file to MalwareScanClient.
3. ScanStep: on CLEAN, sets scan_result CLEAN and scanned_at, so ocrStep may read the item; on INFECTED, moves the file to the quarantine container, sets scan_result INFECTED, writes the audit event MALWARE_BLOCKED and alerts the platform administrator; the file is never stored.
4. Upload (RWB-E1-026): calls MalwareScanService.scanNow before DocumentStore.store; INFECTED returns 422 MSG-P5-016; if the scanning service does not answer, the call returns 503 MSG-P5-022 and nothing is kept.
5. DocumentStore (RWB-E1-024): stores clean files with the retention class of the type; legal types go to the write-once container.
6. JOB-17 Retention job: runs on the first Sunday of each month; for each active document computes expiry date = stored date plus period_months of its class.
7. RetentionJob: skips a document whose case has legal_hold true and counts it as held.
8. RetentionJob: for a due document with end action ARCHIVE, writes the decision log entry DOCRET, moves the blob to the archive tier and sets the document state ARCHIVED; for end action REVIEW, adds it to the review list for Compliance and changes nothing.
9. RetentionJob: writes the review list to retention/review/{runDate}.csv in the standard container and the counts (due, archived, listed, held, exceptions) to the job record.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The scan finds malware on an intake file | File quarantined, not stored, audit event, platform administrator alerted | MSG-P5-016 | AC1 |
| X2 | The scanning service does not answer | Intake item stays unscanned and is not read by OCR; retried in the next run; alert after two failed runs; an upload returns 503 and nothing is stored | MSG-P5-022 | AC6 |
| X3 | A due document is on a case with a legal hold | Not archived, not listed; counted as held | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A document carries a class not in the retention table | Listed as an exception RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING; nothing changes | None | AC7 |
| X5 | JOB-17 runs again in the same month | Documents already archived or listed for that month are not acted on again | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A retention class load holds an end action other than ARCHIVE or REVIEW, or a period of 0 months | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The decision log write fails for an archive | The document stays as it is; picked up by the next run; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-041-12 (Principle 5) |
| X8 | A role without Reference data C loads retention classes | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-041-11 (Access) |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-024) and the intake (RWB-E1-049); the upload (RWB-E1-026) calls this scan |
| Negotiable | Retention periods and end actions are data under DL26; the scanning service is reached through an adapter |
| Valuable | No infected file reaches a user; every document has a retention rule from day one |
| Estimable | One job step, one monthly job, one table, one adapter |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Retention classes and virus scan on intake

 Background:
 Given retention class table version "RET-2026.11" is in force
 Given class "LEGAL10Y" has period 120 months and end action "REVIEW"
 Given class "GENERAL05Y" has period 60 months and end action "ARCHIVE"

 Scenario: AC1 Malware blocked
 Given a test file "eicar-0002.pdf" with the EICAR signature as an intake item from a branch scanner
 When JOB-12 runs the scan step
 Then the item has scan_result "INFECTED" and the file is in the quarantine container
 Then no document row exists for the file and the OCR step does not read it

 Scenario: AC2 Retention class

 When the document is stored on case "RW-2026-000123"
 Then the document row carries retention class "LEGAL10Y" and write_once true
 Then the file is in the write-once container

 Scenario: AC3 Expiry with end action archive
 Given an appraisal report of class "GENERAL05Y" stored on 1 November 2021 on case "RW-2026-000123" with no legal hold
 When JOB-17 runs on 6 December 2026
 Then the document has state "ARCHIVED" and its blob is in the archive tier
 Then one decision log entry "DOCRET" names the document, class "GENERAL05Y", version "RET-2026.11" and expiry date 1 November 2026

 Then the document and its blob are unchanged

 Scenario: AC5 Legal hold overrides the class
 Given an appraisal report of class "GENERAL05Y" stored on 1 November 2021 on case "RW-2026-000789" with legal_hold true
 When JOB-17 runs on 6 December 2026
 Then the system does not archiv the document and not listed
 Then the job record counts it as held

 Scenario: AC6 Scanning service unavailable
 Given the scanning service stub returns no answer
 When JOB-12 runs twice with 3 unscanned intake items
 Then the 3 items have no scan_result and the OCR step reads none of them
 Then the system alerts the platform administrator after the second run
 Then an upload during the outage returns 503 with MSG-P5-022 and no document row or blob is written

 Scenario: AC7 Class not in the retention table
 Given a document with retention class "OLD03Y" that is not in version "RET-2026.11"
 When JOB-17 runs
 Then the system lists the document as exception "RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING" in the review list
 Then the document is unchanged

 Scenario: AC8 Second run in the same month
 Given JOB-17 ran on 6 December 2026 and archived 4 documents and listed 9
 When JOB-17 is rerun on 7 December 2026
 Then the system archives no document again, no second "DOCRET" entry is written and the review list still holds 9 rows

 Scenario: AC9 Invalid retention class load
 Given a load file for table "RETENTION_CLASS" with class "TEMP01M" at period 0 months and end action "DELETE"
 When the reference data administrator loads it
 Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P3-027 naming both errors
 Then version "RET-2026.11" stays in force

 Scenario: AC10 Expiry on the run date
 Given an appraisal report of class "GENERAL05Y" stored on 6 December 2021
 When JOB-17 runs on 6 December 2026
 Then the system archives the document , because its expiry date equals the run date
```

2. Build MalwareScanClient against a stub that flags the EICAR signature; test AC1 and the upload call.
3. Build ScanStep with quarantine, audit and the two-failure alert; test AC6.
4. Build RetentionClassLoader with validation; test AC9.
5. Build RetentionJob expiry and hold rules; unit test AC5, AC7 and AC10 on fixed dates.
6. Add archive with the decision log entry and the review list; integration test AC3, AC4 and AC8.
7. Test the access and the decision log failure paths.

**Feature flags.** `rwb.dochub.malware-scan` and `rwb.dochub.retention`. With the scan flag off, intake items stay unscanned and are not read; uploads are refused with 503 and MSG-P5-022. With the retention flag off, JOB-17 lists due documents and archives none.

secs.h: RWB-E1-042 Central configuration service and parameter catalog
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-042 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-22 Hold the parameter catalog and configuration service |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **every environment setting and business parameter read from one configuration service and listed in a parameter catalog with name, type, default, owner, environment and where it is used**, so that **no value is hard-coded and every parameter has an owner**.

Thresholds such as the 90-day entry point are written into code and spreadsheets today, so a change needs a release and nobody can say who owns a value. This story holds every parameter definition in a catalog with an owner and a default, holds business values as approved, dated versions per environment, serves them to every engine at run time, and fails the build when code carries a literal business value or reads a parameter the catalog does not list. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and puts Principle 1 (DT02) into the build pipeline.

- RWB-E1-044 is done: the recovery schema exists in each environment.
- The catalog seed file `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is in the repository, owned by RW-COE, with the Epic 1 entries, including `case.entry.dpd` (default 90; DL16), `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (default 300; DL11) and `caselist.export.maxrows` (default 10000; DL11).
- The ACE secret store holds secrets per environment; the catalog lists them and never holds their values.
- Loaders hold Reference data C (RW-COE, RW-REFADM). Approvers hold Reference data A: the parameter owner, and RW-RISK where a threshold or a limit moves (assumed grant; DL01).
- The build pipeline runs the checks of this story on every pull request (DL37 code owners).

1. Squad member: adds a parameter to `config/parameter-catalog.csv` with key, kind, type, unit, range, default, scope, required, owner role, environments and used by; the pull request is reviewed by the owner.
2. Build: generates the `ParameterKeys` class from the catalog file; code reads a value only through ParameterService with a generated key.
3. Build: runs the magic number check over the recovery packages and the catalog completeness check.
4. Flyway: loads the catalog rows and the default values into parameter_catalog and parameter_value at deployment.
5. RW-COE: loads a new value version through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "PARAMETER", for example `case.entry.dpd` = 91 in PROD valid from 2026-12-10.
6. ParameterLoadChecks: checks key in catalog, type, range, environment and required values; refuses the load whole on any failure.
7. Owner: approves through POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
8. ParameterService: from the valid from date returns the new value; every instance refreshes its cache on ParameterVersionApproved and at the latest after the cache time to live.
9. Engines: read values at run time with the version number, and record the version in their decision log inputs.
10. Any role with Rules and parameters R: reads the catalog and the values in force through GET /admin/parameters.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Code holds a literal business value | Build fails naming the file, the line and the parameter with that default | None (build output) | AC2 |
| X2 | Code reads a key that the catalog does not list | Build fails naming the key | None (build output) | AC3 |
| X3 | A required parameter has no value for the environment at start-up | The service does not start; the health check names the key | MSG-P3-032 | AC4 |
| X4 | A loaded value is outside its range | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | A loaded value has the wrong type | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The approver is the author | Approval refused | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | A secret is asked for through the catalog read | The value is not returned | None | AC9 |
| X8 | Rollback of a value version | The previous version is in force | MSG-P3-015 when none exists | AC10 |
| X10 | A new version is approved before its valid from date | The current value stays until that date; no restart is needed | None | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Rules and parameters R reads the catalog | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-042-12 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the schema and migrations (RWB-E1-044); every later engine reads through it |
| Negotiable | The catalog columns and the build check rules can be tuned; the values are data |

As a **reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)**, I want **products, regions, exposure bands, roles, teams, queues, service levels, document types, templates, delegation of authority and legal periods held as versioned reference data with valid from, valid to, author and approver**, so that **business values change by a data release and not by code, and every engine can say which version it used**.

Today the values that drive allocation, timers and approval limits live in team spreadsheets and in procedure documents, so nobody can say which value applied to a case on a given day. This story gives every reference table a version with a valid from date, an author and a different approver, and serves the version in force to the engines. The holiday calendar is not one of them: ACE holds the Bank of Thailand calendar in `bot_holiday`, and the timer engine reads it through `v_ace_holiday`, so no Workbench list holds holidays and no holiday load is needed. It meets REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006 and supports control CTL-08 (a rule, limit or list changes only through a validated load approved by its owner). The measure is that every value an engine reads carries a table code and a version number in its log line.

- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway migrations run with the schema name taken from a parameter.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: the configuration service serves `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (assumed 300; DL11) and the list of reference table codes.
- The list LOV-REF-TABLE (new, see Additions) is loaded with the 12 table codes in section 8, BR1.
- The reference load endpoint `POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads` (P4) is deployed and calls this story's published interface.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds the approve right in Reference data (assumed RW-RISK; see section 10).
- The business date of the ACE service is set from the ACE batch record for the day (v_ace_batch_status).

1. Reference data administrator: uploads a load file for one table code with a valid from date through `POST /admin/reference-loads`.
2. P4 load handler: passes the file rows, the table code, the valid from date and the caller's user ID to `ReferenceVersionRegistry.recordVersion(...)`.
3. Reference data service: checks the table code, the row schema for that table, the row keys, the valid from date and the author; computes the content hash and the next version number.
4. Reference data service: writes one `reference_version` row with status VALIDATED and one `reference_row` row per file row, in one transaction.
5. Approver: approves the load through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
6. Reference data service: checks that the approver is present, is not the author and holds the approve right; sets status APPROVED, `approver_user_id` and `approved_at`.
7. Reference data service: sets `valid_to` of the version it replaces to the day before the new valid from date.
8. Case service, allocation engine and timer engine: on start and on each cache expiry, call `ReferenceDataService.rows(tableCode, businessDate)` and receive the approved version whose valid from is the latest on or before the business date.
9. Each engine: writes one log line per table read, with the table code, the version number and the business date.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Approval attempted with no approver, or by the author | The version stays VALIDATED and is never served | MSG-P7-002 | AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A row fails the schema or key check for its table | The load is refused in full; no version is written | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The valid from date is before the business date | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same file is loaded twice for the same table and valid from date | No second version; the first load is returned | None | AC7 |
| X5 | Two approvals of the same load arrive at the same time | One succeeds; the other is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | No approved version is in force for a table on the business date | The engine does not start its run and raises an alert to the platform administrator | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The load file is empty | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC10 |

| Valuable | Every later rule, timer and approval reads a dated, approved value instead of a spreadsheet |
| Estimable | Two tables, one registry service, one read service, one cache |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests; no screen |
| Testable | Every criterion below is one automated test against a PostgreSQL test container |

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.refdata` in the recovery module; folder `recovery/casewf/refdata`. Published types in `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReferenceVersionRegistryImpl | Service | Runs the load checks, numbers the version, writes the version and its rows, approves |
| ReferenceDataServiceImpl | Service | Resolves the version in force for a date; serves rows from the cache |
| ReferenceRowCache | Service | In-memory cache keyed by table code and business date; entry time to live from `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` |
| ReferenceTableSchemas | Rule table | Column names, types and key columns per table code, read from the parameter catalog (RWB-E1-042) |
| ReferenceVersionRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_version` |
| ReferenceRowRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_row` |
| ReferenceVersionEntity, ReferenceRowEntity | Entity | JPA mappings of the two tables, with the standard columns |
| ReferenceVersionRegistry, ReferenceDataService | Published interface | The Java interfaces in section 12 |

**Database.** Flyway migration `V<next>__rwb_e1_043_reference_versions.sql` (this story creates both tables; schema from the `${schema}` placeholder):

- `reference_version`: `id uuid PK`, `table_code varchar(30) NOT NULL`, `version_no integer NOT NULL`, `valid_from date NOT NULL`, `valid_to date`, `status varchar(15) NOT NULL`, `author_user_id uuid NOT NULL`, `approver_user_id uuid`, `approved_at timestamptz`, `row_count integer NOT NULL`, `content_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, `load_id uuid NOT NULL`, plus the seven standard columns. Constraints: `UNIQUE (table_code, version_no)`; `UNIQUE (table_code, valid_from, content_hash)`; `CHECK (approver_user_id IS NULL OR approver_user_id <> author_user_id)`; partial unique index on `(table_code, valid_from) WHERE status = 'APPROVED'`.
- `reference_row`: `id uuid PK`, `version_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES reference_version (id)`, `row_key varchar(200) NOT NULL`, `row_data jsonb NOT NULL`, plus the standard columns. `UNIQUE (version_id, row_key)`; index on `version_id`.
- Both tables append only: an update trigger refuses changes to `reference_row`, and to `reference_version` except `status`, `approver_user_id`, `approved_at`, `valid_to` and the standard columns.

**Configuration and reference data.** `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11), loaded by the platform administrator in the configuration service. LOV-REF-TABLE values and the column definitions per table code, loaded by the reference data administrator. The first version of each of the 12 tables is loaded by the reference data administrator before SIT and approved by Risk. The holiday calendar is ACE data read through `v_ace_holiday` and has no version row of its own.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the two entities and repositories; test the constraints in a PostgreSQL test container.
2. Build `ReferenceTableSchemas` from the parameter catalog and the row check (type, required, key uniqueness) with a check result per row and column.
3. Build `recordVersion(...)`: table code check, empty file check, valid from check against the business date, content hash (SHA-256 over the rows sorted by key), idempotent return on the same hash, version numbering, one transaction.
4. Build `approve(...)`: approver present and different from the author, approve right checked through the ACE access check, optimistic lock on `version`, set `valid_to` of the replaced version.
5. Build `versionInForce` and `rows` with `NoVersionInForceException`, and the cache.
6. Build `ReferenceVersionLogger` and call it from the case service, the allocation engine and the timer engine start-up hooks (one line per table; no row content).
7. Wire the P4 load and approve handlers to the published interface; map exceptions to the problem responses in section 12.
8. Write the tests in section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.refdata-versions`. Off: the engines read the reference values loaded before this story.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the 12 tables each have version 1 approved in SIT, the holiday calendar is read from `v_ace_holiday` in SIT, and the boundary test (RWB-TE-001) shows no read of `reference_version` or `reference_row` from outside `recovery.casewf.refdata`.

secs.h: RWB-E1-044 Database migrations versioned with parameterized schema names
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-044 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-24 Run versioned migrations with parameterized schema names |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-014 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Epic 2, section 4; Business Requirements Program, section 5.1 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **every schema change applied by a versioned Flyway migration, one migration per story, forward-only in PROD, with the schema name taken from a parameter**, so that **the database in every environment is the sum of known migrations and nothing else**.

The recovery tables share the ACE database with the collection module, and two squads change it from one repository (DT07, DT08). A column added by hand in one environment makes SIT and UAT test a database that PROD does not have. This story makes every change a numbered, checksummed migration with no schema name written in the file, and fails the pipeline on drift. It supports REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products held in the ACE database) and REQ-RDF-014 (stage 2 tables exist before the first treatment goes live). The measure is zero schema differences between a clean build and each environment at every release.

- The recovery tables are defined in the Logical Data Model and Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql.
- The recovery module folder and boundary test exist (RWB-TE-001).
- Each environment has a database account for migrations and a read-only account for the drift check, held in the key store (NFR-052).
- The schema parameter `RWB_SCHEMA` is set per environment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD). Assumed value `recovery` in every environment, as in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql.
- Deployment slots are booked (DL35).

1. Developer: adds one migration file for the story under `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/`, named `V<number>__<description>.sql`, with the header line `-- Story: <story key>`.
2. Pipeline: runs the migration lint: no literal schema name, no foreign key into `public`, exactly one story key per file, no story key in two files, no undo file.
3. Pipeline: starts a clean PostgreSQL container and applies all migrations with `RWB_SCHEMA` set.
4. Pipeline: runs the drift check: dumps the schema object list of the clean database and of the target environment, and compares them.
5. Deployment: on service start, Flyway applies each pending migration once, in version order, and writes its checksum to the history table.
6. Deployment: Flyway validates the checksums of applied migrations; a changed file stops the start.
7. Platform administrator: reads the migration run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An object in the target environment is not produced by the migrations | The pipeline fails and names each extra or missing object | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X2 | An applied migration file was edited after it ran | Flyway validation fails and the service does not start | MSG-P3-016 | AC4 |
| X3 | A migration contains a literal schema name | The lint fails the build and names the file and line | MSG-P3-016 | AC5 |
| X4 | Two migration files carry the same story key, or one carries none | The lint fails the build | MSG-P3-016 | AC6 |
| X5 | An undo migration or a clean command is used against PROD | Refused; PROD runs forward only | MSG-P3-016 | AC7 |
| X6 | A migration fails part way | The transaction rolls back; the history records the failure; the service does not start | MSG-P3-016 | AC8 |
| X7 | Two service instances start at the same time | One applies the migrations; the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending | None | AC9 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the table definitions in the Logical Data Model; it comes first so every later table is a migration |
| Negotiable | The schema name and the history table name are parameters; the story fixes the process |
| Valuable | Every later story changes the database the same way, and environments stay equal |
| Estimable | Flyway configuration, two pipeline checks and a lint |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in the pipeline against PostgreSQL containers |

```gherkin
Feature: Database migrations versioned with parameterized schema names

 Background:
 Given the schema parameter RWB_SCHEMA is "rwb_case"
 Given the Flyway history table is "flyway_schema_history_recovery"

 Scenario: AC1 Migration applied
 Given migration V12__add_queue_to_case.sql with the header "-- Story: RWB-E1-020"
 When the deployment runs
 Then the migration applies once
 Then its version 12 and its checksum are recorded in "flyway_schema_history_recovery"
 Then a second deployment run applies nothing and changes no object

 Scenario: AC2 Drift detected
 Given a column "note_x" added by hand to table "queue" in SIT
 When the migration check runs
 Then the pipeline fails with MSG-P3-016 naming "rwb_case.queue.note_x"
 Then no deployment to SIT starts

 Scenario: AC3 Schema name as parameter
 Given RWB_SCHEMA set to "rwb_case" in DEV and in SIT
 When the migration V13__create_timer.sql runs in DEV and in SIT
 Then the table "timer" exists in schema "rwb_case" in both environments
 Then the file V13__create_timer.sql is byte for byte the same in both runs

 Scenario: AC4 Applied migration edited
 Given V12__add_queue_to_case.sql applied in SIT with checksum 104553219
 Given the file changed in the repository so its checksum is 88120477
 When the service starts in SIT
 Then Flyway validation fails with MSG-P3-016 naming version 12
 Then the service does not start

 Scenario: AC5 Literal schema name
 Given V14__add_index.sql contains the text "CREATE INDEX ix_a ON recovery.queue (team_code)"
 When the migration lint runs
 Then the build fails with MSG-P3-016 naming V14__add_index.sql line 1

 Scenario: AC6 One migration per story
 Given V15__a.sql and V16__b.sql both carry the header "-- Story: RWB-E1-028"
 When the migration lint runs
 Then the build fails with MSG-P3-016 naming both files and RWB-E1-028

 Scenario: AC7 Forward only in PROD
 Given the PROD configuration
 When a pipeline step calls Flyway clean or an undo migration U12__add_queue_to_case.sql is present
 Then the system refuses the step with MSG-P3-016
 Then no object in PROD changes

 Scenario: AC8 Migration fails part way
 Given V17__add_two_columns.sql whose second statement refers to a table that does not exist
 When the deployment runs in DEV
 Then the system rolls the first statement back
 Then the history records version 17 as failed
 Then the service does not start and the run shows "failed" on the job monitor

 Scenario: AC9 Two instances start together
 Given two service instances in SIT with migration V18__add_column.sql pending
 When both start within one second
 Then the system applies V18 exactly once
 Then both instances start
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every schema change is a versioned migration in the repository; no change is made by hand in any environment | ADR-002; DT08 |
| BR2 | No migration file contains a literal schema name; the schema comes from `RWB_SCHEMA` through the Flyway `${schema}` placeholder and the default schema | Principle 1 |
| BR3 | One migration file per story that changes the database, carrying the story key in its header | DL04 (merge owner per module) |
| BR4 | PROD runs forward only: clean is disabled, undo files are refused, a fix is a new compensating migration | DT11; NFR-027 |
| BR5 | An applied migration is never edited; checksums are validated on every start | DT11 (untested code is not merged) |
| BR6 | The recovery module keeps its own Flyway history table so its versions do not collide with the ACE and collection modules | DT07; DT08 |
| BR7 | The drift check runs before every deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD | CTL-02 (checks before use) |
| BR8 | No migration in the recovery schema declares a foreign key into `public`; an ACE row is held by its business key and ACE cascades deletes on `account`. The lint fails the build and names the file | ADR-010; D-RCV-35 U4 |
None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the migration state of each environment: a migration moves from pending to applied (or failed) in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs deployments and reruns a failed migration job (Platform administration CRUD); reads migration runs on SCR-44 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| Pipeline migration account | Applies migrations with the migration database account from the key store; not a Workbench role |

No business field. The story writes the Flyway history table `flyway_schema_history_recovery`, which is a tool table and is not in the Logical Data Model. It reads the schema object list (`information_schema`) in each environment for the drift check.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs** (P1 endpoint) lists migration runs with `type=MIGRATION`.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `type` = MIGRATION, `status`, `from`, `to` |
| Response | 200 `Job[]`: `id`, `type`, `businessDate`, `status` (APPLIED, FAILED), `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `checks` (version, checksum, drift result) |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Migration job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Service start in each environment, and the pipeline step `migrate` |
| Job name | Not a scheduled job in batch.txt; it runs at deployment |
| Input | The files in `db/migration/recovery`, `RWB_SCHEMA`, the migration account |
| Output | Applied objects in schema `RWB_SCHEMA`; rows in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`; one `Job` record per run through the P1 job monitor |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Migration version. An applied version is never applied again |
| Restart behavior | A failed migration rolls back; after a fix is merged as a new version, the next start applies it |

**Configuration** (Spring Boot properties, values from the configuration service):

```properties
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration/recovery
spring.flyway.schemas=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.default-schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.table=flyway_schema_history_recovery
spring.flyway.placeholders.schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.validate-on-migrate=true
spring.flyway.out-of-order=false
spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true
```

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.migration` (configuration and checks); migration files in `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery`; pipeline scripts in `recovery/build/migration-checks`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RecoveryFlywayConfig | Service | Builds the recovery Flyway instance from the properties above; refuses clean in every profile |
| MigrationRunRecorder | Service | Writes one job record per migration run through the P1 job monitor interface |
| MigrationLint | Job | Build step: refuses literal schema names (pattern on `<identifier>.` before a table name for every name in `sys_objects`), a foreign key into `public`, missing or repeated story keys, and `U*.sql` files |
| SchemaDriftCheck | Job | Pipeline step: applies all migrations to a clean container, lists tables, columns, types, constraints and indexes of `RWB_SCHEMA`, compares with the target environment through the read-only account, reports each difference |
| V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql | RWB-E1-001 baseline | Built from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder and `SET search_path` removed; applied by RWB-E1-001 (D-RCV-28) |

**Database.** No business table changes. Flyway creates `flyway_schema_history_recovery` in `RWB_SCHEMA`. The baseline migration creates the 92 tables of Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql; the 4 extension tables ship inside it as ordinary tables of the recovery schema, and the 30 `v_ace_*` views ship in two later migrations (Section A with RWB-E1-069, Section B after RWB-ACE-001). No migration in the recovery schema declares a foreign key into `public`: an ACE row is held by its business key. The initial seed rows (`lov_value`, `role`, `permission`, `delegation_limit`, `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `data_product`) ship with the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` (D-RCV-28, D-RCV-29); later dictionary changes are reference loads through RWB-E1-043, not migrations.

**Configuration and reference data.** The schema value is the placeholder `${recoverySchema}`, fixed to `recovery` in every environment (D-RCV-28); no per-environment override. Migration and read-only database accounts in the key store, set by the platform administrator.

**Build steps**

Ruled 2026-11-05 as D-RCV-28: recovery Flyway files are named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql` with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order; line 1 is `-- Story: <story key>`; the schema is referenced only as `${recoverySchema}` and is `recovery` in every environment. The RWB-E1-001 baseline is `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql`; RWB-E1-044 ships no production migration file. Former open point: The rule in this story is a single rising number with the placeholder ${schema} fed by RWB_SCHEMA. The other 51 stories that name a migration file use four other rules, 30 of them V<epic>_<story>__<name>.sql with the placeholder ${recoverySchema} as in RWB-E1-001. The lint rule reports and fails the build for a name that breaks the rule.

1. Add Flyway to the recovery module and `RecoveryFlywayConfig` with the properties in section 12; prove start-up applies and records a test migration.
2. Convert Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql into the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder; prove it creates every table in the recovery schema.
3. Build `MigrationLint` and add it to the build; test each refusal with fixture files.
4. Build `SchemaDriftCheck` and add it before each deployment stage; test with a hand-added column.
5. Build `MigrationRunRecorder` and show runs on the job monitor.
6. Prove forward only: clean refused, undo files refused, failed migration rolls back.
7. Prove the lock with two instances starting together.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate`. On in SIT, UAT and PROD: drift fails the deployment. Off in DEV: drift is reported and the deployment continues.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and DEV and SIT show no drift against the baseline.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, lint failure, a refused clean or undo, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads migration runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is new (see Additions). It is shown in the pipeline log and on SCR-44, not to business users.
SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, state Running, Failed or Complete: the platform administrator reads each migration run with its version, checksum and drift result. No new screen in this story.

| TC-E1-044-02 | AC2, BR7 | System | SIT container with a hand-added column |
| TC-E1-044-03 | AC3, BR2 | System | DEV and SIT containers with RWB_SCHEMA = rwb_case |
| TC-E1-044-04 | AC4, BR5 | System | V12 edited after it ran |
| TC-E1-044-05 | AC5, BR2 | System | V14 with a literal schema name |
| TC-E1-044-06 | AC6, BR3 | System | Two files with the same story key |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v5.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

- No business value in code or in a migration. Seed values are reference loads (RWB-E1-043), not migration inserts.

secs.h: RWB-E1-045 Multi-product parameters for Mortgage, HP and SSME
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-045 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-25 Set product parameters without a code change |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-010, REQ-CWC-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.3 and 4; Business Requirements Program, sections 5.3 and 5.7 |
| L3 process | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules |
| Decision | D6 entry |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-042, RWB-E1-043 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **every product-specific value (entry rule, exclusion list, service levels, notice and cure periods, exposure bands) keyed by product in the reference data**, so that **a new product or a product change needs no code change**.

Mortgage, hire purchase and SSME follow different notice periods, service levels and bands, and today each difference is held in a team procedure. If the engines carry these values as constants, every product change waits for a release. This story keys each value by product group in the versioned reference tables of RWB-E1-043 and refuses a load that leaves a product without a required value. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-CWC-011. The measure is that a product is added or changed by a reference load with no deployment.

- RWB-E1-043 is done: versioned reference tables, the registry and the read service.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: the parameter catalog marks each parameter with scope PRODUCT or GLOBAL, required yes or no, type, unit and allowed range (new catalog fields, see Additions).
- Tables PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL have an approved version in force.
- The timer engine (RWB-E1-028), case creation (RWB-E1-018) and the allocation engine (RWB-E1-020) read product values only through `ProductParameterService`.
- The loader holds RW-COE or RW-REFADM (Reference data C); the approver holds the approve right in Reference data.

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares a PRODUCT_PARAMETER load with one row per product group and parameter code, and a SERVICE_LEVEL load with one row per product group and case status.
2. Reference data administrator: loads each file through `POST /admin/reference-loads`.
3. Reference data service: runs the RWB-E1-043 checks, then the product completeness check: every product in the PRODUCT version in force on the valid from date has a row for every catalog parameter with scope PRODUCT and required yes, and a SERVICE_LEVEL row for every status in the parameter `servicelevel.required-statuses`.
4. Reference data service: checks each value against the catalog type and range.
5. Approver: approves the version; it takes effect on its valid from date.
6. Timer engine: when it starts a notice timer for a case, calls `ProductParameterService.get(productGroup, "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS", businessDate)` and sets `expires_at` from the value and its unit.
7. Case creation and allocation: read the entry threshold, the exclusion list and the exposure bands for the case's product group the same way.
8. Each engine: records the PRODUCT_PARAMETER version used in its decision log entry inputs (written by the owning story).

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product has no SERVICE_LEVEL row for a required status | The load is refused in full and the missing product and status are named | MSG-P3-034 | AC3 |
| X2 | A parameter value is outside the catalog range or of the wrong type | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | Two rows for the same product and parameter | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A PRODUCT version removes a product that still has open cases | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X5 | At run time a case's product has no parameter row in force | No timer is set; the case goes to the exception queue; the gap is named | MSG-P3-034 | AC7 |
| X6 | A parameter changes while a timer is running | The running timer keeps its expiry; new timers use the new value from its valid from date | None | AC8 |

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **letter and document templates and their merge fields held as versioned data with the Legal approval record on each version**, so that **a template change is a data release approved by Legal and never a code release**.

Letters and notices are prepared by hand today, so the wording and the facts on a notice depend on who typed it. This story holds every template version, the merge fields it draws from the case and the Legal approval as data rows, so the letter engine (RWB-E1-052) can only use a version Legal approved and can only fill fields the catalog knows. It serves REQ-OCC-001 and REQ-OCC-002 and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent", which needs every notice to come from a known template version (CTL-14).

- RWB-E1-001 and RWB-E1-069 are done: the recovery tables exist and recovery data comes only through the 30 ACE views.
- The template table exists in schema recovery (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql) and the reference data load path of P4 (POST /admin/reference-loads) is live.
- Lists LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-NOTICE are loaded (refdata.txt).
- The merge field catalog load file is prepared by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM), one row per merge field, each naming its BR Field ID in the Logical Data Model.
- The person loading holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). Legal counsel (RW-LEGAL) approves each template version through RWB-E1-034, or through the approval columns of the load file in Epic 1 before that screen is live.

1. Reference data administrator: loads the merge field catalog file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "merge_field" and a valid from date.
2. System: checks every row: merge code unique, BR Field ID present in sys_fields, source entity and field present, required flag set. A row that fails refuses the whole load (refdata change process, step 3).
3. Reference data administrator: loads a template version file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "template", carrying template code, language, product group, channel, notice type, signature basis, the body file reference, the merge codes used and, where Legal has signed, the approver and approval date.
4. System: reads every merge code in the body and in the merge code list and checks each one against the catalog in force. An unknown code refuses the load and names the code (MSG-P6-006).
5. System: assigns the next version number for the template code and language, keeps every earlier version readable and sets state Approved only where the approver and approval date are present, otherwise Draft.
6. System: the published interface TemplateCatalog returns, for a template code, language and date, the current version: the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid from date is on or before that date.
7. Letter engine (RWB-E1-052): asks TemplateCatalog for the current version. If none is Approved, the catalog refuses and names the missing approval (MSG-P6-005).
8. System: writes the load result (rows loaded, rows refused, version numbers) to the reference load record and the ACE audit log.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Generation asks for a template whose versions are all Draft | TemplateCatalog throws TemplateNotApprovedException; nothing is generated | MSG-P6-005 | AC2 |
| X2 | A template uses a merge code that is not in the catalog | The whole load is refused; the unknown code is named | MSG-P6-006 | AC3 |
| X3 | A catalog row names a BR Field ID that is not in the data dictionary | The whole catalog load is refused | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | A template row has no template code, language or body reference | The whole load is refused; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X5 | The same template file is loaded twice | The second load creates no new version | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The only Approved version is withdrawn | TemplateCatalog returns no current version; generation holds | MSG-P6-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | A version has valid from in the future | The earlier Approved version stays current until that date | None | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the recovery tables (RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069) and the P4 reference load path; the screen comes in RWB-E1-034 |
| Negotiable | The merge codes and the templates are data; the story fixes the checks and the selection of the current version |
| Valuable | Every notice from Epic 1 on is traceable to one Legal-approved version |
| Estimable | One new table, one validator, one published interface, two load handlers |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test against synthetic load files |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **a feature flag service with each flag held as data (key, owner, value per environment, removal date) and read by the service and the front end at run time**, so that **a feature can be released switched off and switched on without a deployment, and no flag stays after its removal date without its owner being told**.

Two squads release monthly from one repository, and one squad's unfinished change must not hold the other's release (ADR-008, DT11). A flag held as a data row lets the platform administrator switch a change off in SIT or UAT and let the release go ahead, with every change logged. A weekly report lists flags past their removal date so old code paths are removed. It meets REQ-DRI-010 (configuration changed without a code release).

- RWB-E1-001 (recovery schema) is done.
- The person holds RW-PLATADM in the environment through the Entra ID group, for example RWB-UAT-RW-PLATADM.
- The ACE audit log service of the common module is available.
- The ACE front end loads the recovery module folder (ADR-006).
- Flag `rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column` is created with default off and removal date 2027-01-31 for the tests.

1. Platform administrator: creates a flag with key, description, owner, default value and removal date.
2. System: validates the key pattern `rwb.<module>.<short-name>`, the removal date and the owner, and writes the flag row with every environment set to the default.
3. Service code: calls FeatureFlags.isOn(key) at each request; the value comes from a cache refreshed every 30 seconds (assumed; DL11).
4. Front end: reads GET /feature-flags at page load and hides or shows the component.
5. Platform administrator: switches the flag on for one environment with a reason.
6. System: checks the version, writes the new value and a feature_flag_change row with user, time, old and new value, and writes the ACE audit log entry.
7. Front end: after reload, shows the component; no deployment takes place.
8. Scheduler: the weekly flag report job runs every Monday 08:00 and lists every flag past its removal date with its owner.
9. System: sends the report to each owner and to the RW-PLATADM group by email and logs MSG-P2-003 per flag.

| X6 | Two administrators change the same flag at once | The second change is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X7 | A change to a key that does not exist | Refused | MSG-P2-016 | AC9 |
| X8 | A role without the right changes a flag | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-047-10 |

| Negotiable | Flags, owners, values and dates are data rows; the cache interval is a property |
| Valuable | A failed change is switched off in SIT or UAT and the release goes ahead |
| Estimable | Two tables, one service with a cache, four endpoints, one weekly job, one React hook |
| Small | Within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test |

```gherkin
Feature: Feature flags for module release with a removal date

 Background:
 Given flag "rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column" exists with default off, owner team "P3 squad" and removal date 2027-01-31

 Scenario: AC1 Flag off by default
 Given the flag has no value set for UAT
 When the case list service starts in UAT
 Then FeatureFlags.isOn("rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column") returns false
 Then the system hides the queue column on SCR-02 Case list

 Scenario: AC2 Flag switched on
 Given a platform administrator sets the flag to on in UAT with reason "UAT test of queue column" at 10:15
 When the case list page is reloaded at 10:16
 Then the queue column shows without a deployment
 Then a change row holds environment "UAT", old value off, new value on, the user and the time 10:15
 Then the ACE audit log holds the same change

 Scenario: AC3 Flag expiry
 Given flag "rwb.p5.ocr-intake" has removal date 2026-11-30 and owner team "P5 squad"
 Given today is Monday 2026-12-07
 When the weekly flag report runs at 08:00
 Then the system lists the flag for removal with its owner and 7 days past its removal date
 Then the report carries message MSG-P2-003 for the flag
 Then the system does not list flag "rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column" with removal date 2027-01-31

 Scenario: AC4 Removal date checked at creation
 Given today is 2026-11-16
 When a platform administrator creates flag "rwb.p6.line-dispatch" with removal date 2026-11-10
 Then the system does not creat the flag
 Then the response is 422 with message MSG-GEN-003
 Then a creation with no removal date returns 422 with message MSG-GEN-001

 Scenario: AC5 Change without a reason refused
 When a platform administrator sets the flag to on in SIT with an empty reason
 Then the response is 422 with message MSG-GEN-001
 Then the flag stays off in SIT

 Scenario: AC6 Unknown key in code
 When code calls FeatureFlags.isOn("rwb.casewf.not-defined")
 Then the result is false
 Then a warning with the key and no user data is written to the application log

 Scenario: AC7 Flag store unavailable
 Given the flag is on in UAT and the cache holds the value from 10:20
 When the flag table cannot be read at 10:21
 Then FeatureFlags.isOn returns true from the cache
 Then after a restart with the table still unavailable it returns false

 Scenario: AC8 Two changes at once
 Given two platform administrators read the flag at version 4
 When both send a change with If-Match version 4
 Then the system saves one change with version 5
 Then the system refuses the other with 409 and message MSG-GEN-004

 Then the response is 404 with message MSG-P2-016
```

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the parameter change and rule change checklist (request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify, rollback plan) recorded on every change and reported for audit**, so that **a configuration change is as controlled as a code change**.

Audit found the collection procedure was not followed because rules lived in documents (CTL-08). When rules and limits are data, a wrong row changes every case it touches, so each change needs the same evidence as a code change: who asked, what it affects, the test result, who approved, when it took effect and how to undo it. This story makes the checklist fields required before a version can be approved and gives audit one report of every change. It meets REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-DRI-011. The measure is that every version in force has a complete checklist in the report.

- RWB-E1-043 is done: every reference table version is a row in `reference_version` with author and approver.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the permission matrix gives Rules and parameters R to RW-COE, RW-RISK and RW-AUDIT.
- RWB-E1-011 is done: the daily data quality report lists refused loads.
- Rule versions loaded through `POST /admin/rule-versions` (RWB-E1-029) are recorded in the same registry with table code `RULE_` and the route set, for example `RULE_UNIVERSAL_RULES`.
- The rule table test harness (RWB-TE-005) writes its result to the version for rule tables; the load checks of RWB-E1-043 write it for reference tables.

1. Center of excellence analyst: raises the change request in the bank's request tool and receives its reference, for example CR-2026-0042.
2. Reference data administrator: loads the new version through `POST /admin/reference-loads` (or `POST /admin/rule-versions`) with the request reference, the impact summary and the rollback plan as form fields.
3. Reference data service: stores the checklist fields on the version and records the test result from the load checks or the harness (PASSED or FAILED).
4. Approver: approves through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
5. Reference data service: refuses the approval unless the request reference, impact summary, rollback plan and a PASSED test result are present and the approver is not the author.
6. Reference data administrator: after the valid from date, records the verification through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify`.
7. Internal audit or the center of excellence analyst: reads the report through `GET /admin/change-log` for a period and a table, as JSON or CSV.

| X1 | A version reaches its valid from date with no approver | It is not served; the report shows it as not approved | None | AC2 |
| X2 | Approval with a checklist item missing | Refused; the version stays VALIDATED | MSG-P3-022 | AC3 |
| X3 | Approval of a version whose test result is FAILED | Refused | MSG-P3-022 | AC4 |
| X4 | The report period has no changes | An empty list is returned | None | AC6 |
| X5 | Verification recorded before the valid from date | Refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The report period ends before it starts | Refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC8 |

| Negotiable | The checklist items are fixed by the Engineering Standards; the report columns can change |
| Valuable | Audit can test every configuration change without asking the team |
| Estimable | Six fields, one approval check, one verify call, one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |

```gherkin
 Given user "U-REF-01" holds RW-REFADM, "U-RSK-01" holds the approve right and "U-AUD-01" holds RW-AUDIT

 Given "U-REF-01" loads SERVICE_LEVEL version 4 with impact summary "412 open Mortgage cases in IN_PROGRESS" and rollback plan "Reload version 3"
 Given the load checks pass

 When "U-AUD-01" reads the change log for 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-31
 Then one entry shows table "SERVICE_LEVEL", version 4, request "CR-2026-0042", test result "PASSED", author "U-REF-01", approver "U-RSK-01", approved on 2026-12-02 and valid from 2026-12-10
 Then the entry shows 1 row changed, 0 added and 0 removed against version 3
 Then the approval time is before the valid from date

 Scenario: AC2 Checklist skipped
 Given SERVICE_LEVEL version 5 loaded by "U-REF-01" with valid from 2026-12-15 and never approved
 When the business date reaches 2026-12-15
 Then the reference data service still serves version 4
 Then the change log shows version 5 with status "VALIDATED" and approver empty

 Scenario: AC3 Checklist item missing at approval
 Given HOLIDAY version 2 loaded with no rollback plan
 When "U-RSK-01" approves it
 Then the system refuses the approval with MSG-P3-022 naming "rollback plan"
 Then version 2 stays "VALIDATED"

 Scenario: AC4 Failed test result
 Given rule version "RULE_UNIVERSAL_RULES" version 3 whose harness result is "FAILED" with 2 of 50 tests failing
 When "U-RSK-01" approves it
```
