secs.h: RWB-E1-049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-049 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-07 Run the OCR pipeline on inbound documents |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-006, REQ-DCM-009 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-045 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every inbound scan and upload read by the OCR service into text and layout in Thai and English, stored against the intake item and the document**, so that **classification and extraction can start and an unreadable page is sent back for rescan the same day**.

Scanned documents arrive as images; nothing in them can be classified, extracted or searched until the text is read (FSD P5 A2.7). This story builds the OCR step of the document intake: one intake record per file, the text and layout of every page, a quality check per page and a rescan request when a page cannot be read. It meets REQ-DCM-006 (fields extracted in Thai and English, which needs Thai and English text first) and REQ-DCM-009 (every path ends in the same intake). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.7.1).

- RWB-E1-024 is done: documents are stored and DocumentStored (EV-16) is published.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake and standard containers exist.
- RWB-E1-045 is done: product parameters are held as data.
- Document hub parameters loaded: OCR_MIN_QUALITY = 0.70, OCR_WORKERS = 4, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120, OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 (all assumed, DL11).
- The OCR service run by Autonomous Ops is reachable from SIT through the OcrClient adapter under the service identity SY-OCR.
- An intake item has scan_result CLEAN. The malware scan step is added in RWB-E1-041; until then test data is seeded CLEAN.
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.ocr is on.

1. JOB-12 Document intake: starts every 15 minutes in business hours and runs the OCR step after the intake and scan steps.
2. DocumentStoredListener: for each DocumentStored event with source UPLOAD, creates an intake item with the case ID, the document ID and scan_result CLEAN (the upload was scanned before storage).
3. OcrStep: selects intake items with scan_result CLEAN and ocr_status PENDING, oldest first, locking each row so that no two workers take the same item; runs up to OCR_WORKERS items in parallel.
4. OcrClient: sends the file to the OCR service with the languages Thai and English and receives, per page, the lines, words, positions, language and word confidence.
5. OcrStep: computes the page quality as the mean word confidence of the page; stores the full output as JSON at ocr/{intakeId}.json in the standard container and sets ocr_ref.
6. OcrStep: writes one document_text row per page with the page text and quality, with the document ID where the item is already attached.
7. OcrStep: if every page has quality at or above OCR_MIN_QUALITY, sets ocr_status DONE; otherwise sets ocr_status RESCAN and rescan_pages to the page numbers below the threshold.
8. OcrStep: for an item in RESCAN with a known case, sends MSG-P5-018 to the case owner through the ACE notification path; for an item with no case, sets review_reason RESCAN so the item shows in the document review queue (SCR-31, RWB-E1-054).
9. OcrStep: records the run counts (read, done, rescan, failed) on the job record shown in the job monitor.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A page has quality below OCR_MIN_QUALITY | Item set RESCAN with the page numbers; case owner told, or the item goes to the review queue | MSG-P5-018 | AC3, AC4 |
| X2 | Page quality exactly at OCR_MIN_QUALITY | The page is accepted | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The OCR service does not answer within OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS or returns an error | ocr_attempts increases; the item stays PENDING for the next run; after two failed runs the job raises an alert to the platform administrator (JOB-12) | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The item fails OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS times or the file cannot be opened | ocr_status FAILED; review_reason UNREADABLE_FILE; item in the review queue | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The job runs again over items already DONE | Items are not read again; no second set of text rows | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two workers start on the same item | The row lock lets one worker take it; the other skips it | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A user without the Documents right reads a document holding OCR text | Refused with 403; no text returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-049-10 (Access) |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-E1-024) and the containers (RWB-TE-012); classification (RWB-E1-050) and extraction (RWB-E1-053) build on its output |
| Negotiable | Quality threshold, workers, timeout and attempts are parameters; the OCR service can change behind OcrClient |
| Valuable | Every scan becomes text that the later steps and the search read |
| Estimable | One table pair, one job step, one adapter, one listener |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub

 Background:
 Given OCR_MIN_QUALITY is 0.70, OCR_WORKERS is 4 and OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 3
 Given the OCR service stub in SIT is replaced by the OCR service for AC1 and AC2

 Scenario: AC1 Sample processed
 Given the 180 synthetic sample documents, 30 of each of the six agreed types, in Thai and English, each as a CLEAN intake item
 When JOB-12 Document intake runs
 Then each of the 180 items has ocr_status "DONE" or "RESCAN" and an ocr_ref to its JSON output
 Then each page has a document_text row with the page text and its quality
 Then the text of the sample pages holds Thai and English words, and the languages recorded per item are "th" and "en" where both appear

 Scenario: AC2 Throughput
 Given 500 pages in 125 CLEAN intake items in SIT
 When they are processed by JOB-12 with 4 workers
 Then all 125 items reach "DONE" or "RESCAN" within 60 minutes of the first item starting

 Scenario: AC3 Unreadable page on a known case
 Given an uploaded court notice of 4 pages on case "RW-2026-000123" owned by user "TEST-CO-01"
 Given page 3 has quality 0.41 and the other pages are above 0.70
 When the OCR step runs
 Then the intake item has ocr_status "RESCAN" and rescan_pages "3"
 Then "TEST-CO-01" receives MSG-P5-018 naming page 3, the document and case "RW-2026-000123"

 Scenario: AC4 Unreadable page with no case yet
 Given a mailroom scan of 2 pages with no case and page 1 at quality 0.30
 When the OCR step runs
 Then the intake item has ocr_status "RESCAN", rescan_pages "1" and review_reason "RESCAN"
 Then the system sends no notification

 Scenario: AC5 Quality at the threshold
 Given a scan of 1 page with quality 0.70
 When the OCR step runs
 Then the item has ocr_status "DONE" and no rescan pages

 Scenario: AC6 OCR service unavailable
 Given the OCR service stub returns HTTP 503 for every call
 When JOB-12 runs twice
 Then each pending item has ocr_status "PENDING" and ocr_attempts 2
 Then the job monitor shows the OCR step failed in both runs and an alert is raised to the platform administrator
 Then when the service answers again the next run sets the items "DONE"

 Scenario: AC7 File that cannot be read
 Given a password-protected PDF as a CLEAN intake item
 When the OCR step runs
 Then the item has ocr_status "FAILED" and review_reason "UNREADABLE_FILE"
 Then no document_text row exists for it

 Scenario: AC8 Repeat run
 Given 10 intake items already "DONE" with 25 document_text rows
 When JOB-12 runs again
 Then the OCR service receives no call for those items
 Then they still have 25 document_text rows

 Scenario: AC9 Two workers on one item
 Given one CLEAN pending item and 4 workers starting at the same time
 When the OCR step runs
 Then the OCR service receives exactly one call for the item
 Then the item has one set of document_text rows
```

| ID | Rule | Source |

| BR1 | Every inbound file is read in Thai and English | REQ-DCM-006; FEAT-DCM-07 |
| BR2 | Scans, partner files, emails and uploads go through the same intake item and OCR step | REQ-DCM-009 |

```java
}
```

**Package.** Folder `recovery/dochub/ocr`, Java package `recovery.dochub.ocr`.

**Components.**

|---|---|---|
| DocumentIntakeJob | Job | Spring Batch job behind JOB-12 with ordered steps; this story builds the job and ocrStep |

**Database.**
- Flyway migration `V1_5_049__document_intake.sql` creates document_intake (id, source varchar(12), source_ref varchar(120), received_at timestamptz, file_sha256 char(64), intake_ref varchar(400), scan_result varchar(10), case_id uuid, document_id uuid, ocr_ref varchar(400), ocr_status varchar(12) default 'PENDING', ocr_attempts integer default 0, page_count integer, rescan_pages varchar(200), ocr_quality numeric(5,4), languages varchar(20), ocr_engine_version varchar(40), review_reason varchar(20), plus the standard columns) and document_text (id, intake_id uuid not null, document_id uuid, page_no integer, text_content text, quality numeric(5,4), plus the standard columns).
- Foreign keys document_intake.document_id and document_text.document_id to document(id); document_text.intake_id to document_intake(id).
- Indexes: ix_intake_ocr_pending on document_intake (ocr_status, received_at) where scan_result = 'CLEAN'; unique uk_document_text_page on document_text (intake_id, page_no); ix_document_text_document on document_text (document_id).
- Row selection uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

**Configuration and reference data.**
- Parameters OCR_MIN_QUALITY, OCR_WORKERS, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS in document_hub_parameter, loaded by the reference data administrator.
- Property rwb.dochub.ocr.endpoint, set per environment by the platform administrator.
- Notification template for MSG-P5-018 in the ACE notification path, recovery templates.

**Build steps.**
1. Write the migration and the entities; test the unique page index.
2. Build OcrClient against a stub that returns fixed pages; contract test of the response mapping.
3. Build OcrStep selection with SKIP LOCKED and the worker pool; test AC8 and AC9.
4. Add the quality rule and the status setting; test AC3, AC4 and AC5 on synthetic pages.
5. Add retry, attempts and the FAILED rule; test AC6 and AC7.
6. Build DocumentStoredListener and RescanNotifier; test AC3 end to end.
7. Run the 180 sample documents and the 500-page set in SIT against the OCR service; record the results for AC1 and AC2.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dochub.ocr`. Off: ocrStep is skipped and items stay PENDING.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the 500-page run in SIT finishes within 60 minutes.

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **each scanned document classified into one of the six agreed types with a confidence score, and any document below the threshold sent to the review queue with its top two candidate types**, so that **each document is filed under the right type and checklist item without a person typing it**.

A scan arrives with no type; today a person reads it and files it by hand. Classification reads the OCR text and names the type with a confidence, so the document can be attached, extracted and counted against the case checklist (FSD P5 A2.8). A document the model is unsure of goes to a person, so no document is filed under the wrong type. It meets REQ-DCM-005 and serves the measure fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.8.1).

- RWB-E1-049 is done: intake items carry OCR text and ocr_status.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: document type table DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force.
- Parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD = 0.80 loaded in document_hub_parameter (assumed until the RWB-E1-060 report; DL11). RWB-E1-054 routes to review on the same value.
- Parameters loaded: CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES = 3, CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60 (R-UNI-32), assumed.
- The classifier model endpoint is set under DL33 and reachable through the P10 model gateway in SIT; its model version is known.

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs classifyStep after ocrStep.
2. ClassifyStep: selects intake items with ocr_status DONE, no predicted_type and no document type given (uploads carry their type and are skipped), locking each row.
3. ClassifyStep: takes the text of the first CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES pages and replaces national ID numbers, account numbers and phone numbers with tokens through the ACE PII masking service.
4. ClassifierClient: sends the masked text and the six type codes with their labels from the type table in force; receives a score per type and the model version.
5. ClassifyStep: ranks the scores; writes predicted_type, classification_confidence, the top two candidates in type_candidates and classifier_version.
6. ClassifyStep: if the top score is at or above CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD and the type is in the table in force, marks the item classified with no review_reason; attach (RWB-E1-032) stores it with review_status NOT_NEEDED.
7. ClassifyStep: below the threshold, sets review_reason LOW_CONFIDENCE; attach (RWB-E1-032) stores the document with review_status PENDING and write_once false, so it shows on SCR-31 with MSG-P5-003 and its two candidates (RWB-E1-054). A type outside the table sets review_reason UNKNOWN_TYPE with no predicted type, and attach holds the item for a person.
8. ClassificationEvaluationRunner: on demand, runs the labeled sample, writes the accuracy and the 6 by 6 confusion matrix to evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json in the standard container and to the job record.

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **demand, recall and guarantor notices generated from the Legal-approved template with the case data merged, the party and the notice address read from the ACE views by business key**, so that **letters are produced without re-keying and the address on the notice is the address ACE holds**.

Notices are typed by hand from the core bank screens, so a wrong amount or address on a notice can void the notice period and delay litigation. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench holds no party and no contact point: the name comes from `v_ace_customer` by `person_key`, the notice address and phone come from `v_ace_contact` by the composite `contact_key` (`contact_type:key`), and the outstanding comes from `v_ace_account` by `account_key`. The clear identity number never leaves ACE, so it is never merged. This story merges those values into the current approved template, stores the PDF write-once on the case with the template version in the footer and records the decision. It serves REQ-OCC-001 and control CTL-14, and is the input to dispatch and proof of delivery (RWB-E1-055), where the WIN record is read from `v_ace_pod`. The FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" depends on it.

- RWB-E1-046 is done: TemplateCatalog returns the current Approved version.
- RWB-E1-018 is done: cases exist with `person_key` links on case_party.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer accepts D7.1 entries.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: each data product carries its freshness stamp from the ACE batch.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_account` are Section A views. `v_ace_pod` is a Section B view over `public.pod_receipt`, so the delivery facts stay behind their flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- Templates for DEMAND, RECALL and GUARANTOR_NOTICE are Approved for the product groups in the synthetic set, in language TH.
- The customer, the contact points and the account are in ACE (SCBPDM and ALS ingestion); `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` and no privilege on `public`.
- The caller is `recovery_svc`, or a person through RWB-E2-021 from Epic 2.

1. Caller: calls NoticeApi.generate with case ID, notice type, `person_key` and language.
2. System: reads the case summary (case number, product group, status) through the P3 interface and the party role through `case_party` by `person_key`.
3. System: asks TemplateCatalog for the current LETTER template for the notice type, product group and language on the business date.
4. System: resolves each merge code through the interface that owns its source field: `CASE_NO`, `PRODUCT_GROUP` and `ENTRY_DATE` from P3; `CUSTOMER_NAME` from `v_ace_customer.first_name` and `.last_name` by `person_key`; `POSTAL_ADDRESS` and `PHONE` from `v_ace_contact` by `person_key` and `contact_type`; `TOTAL_OUTSTANDING` from `v_ace_account.total_balance` by the case's primary `account_key`. Each value carries the ACE business date of its view or batch.
5. System: if a required merge value is empty, holds the notice, names the field and raises a task to the case owner; stops.
6. System: renders the DOCX template to PDF and adds the footer: case number, template code, template version and generation date.
7. System: writes the D7.1 decision log entry with rule R-LIT-03, the template code and version and the reference to the merge snapshot. The snapshot holds the merge code, the view column, the business key and the field ID of each value used, never the value.
8. System: stores the PDF in the document hub as a generated, write-once document on the case.
9. System: creates the notice row with `person_key`, `template_id`, notice type, sent type and state Generated, and writes NoticeGenerated to the outbox in the same transaction.
10. System: when the notice is read, takes the sent date, barcode, callback date and delivery status from `v_ace_pod` by `notice_ref`. The Workbench writes no WIN delivery fact of its own.

secs.h: RWB-E1-053 Field extraction for the six types into the index
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-053 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-09 Extract fields from the six document types |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-006, REQ-DCM-001 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-025 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **case owner**, I want **the key fields of each of the six document types extracted and written to the document index with a confidence per field**, so that **documents are searchable by their content**.

Court dates, case numbers, appraisal values and title numbers are typed by hand from paper today, and a document is found only by the person who filed it. This story reads the agreed fields of each classified intake item and each uploaded document into the index with a confidence score, so the case owner and the litigation officer find a document by its content, the attach step finds the case from the extracted case number, and the low-confidence values go to a person. It meets REQ-DCM-006 and REQ-DCM-001 and feeds the module measure "fields extracted without review", which is to rise each month.

- RWB-E1-049 (OCR text per page through OcrOutputReader) and RWB-E1-050 (predicted_type and classification on the intake item) are done.
- RWB-E1-025 is done: DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force with the six types and 26 fields, read through DocumentTypeCatalog. Each entry of field_definitions holds name, data_type, personal, extraction_method (TEMPLATE or MODEL), review_only and an optional pattern (keys recorded in the additions file).
- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore.store writes the fields passed in StoreRequest as document_field rows.
- Rows in document_hub_parameter: EXTRACT_FIELD_THRESHOLD 0.80; EXTRACT_PRECISION_PASS 0.90; EXTRACT_RECALL_PASS 0.90; EXTRACT_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3; EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60; BE_YEAR_OFFSET 543. Values assumed until the RWB-E1-060 report (DL11).
- The labeled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 per type, holds the true value of every field.
- The step runs as SY-OCR (Documents CRU). Feature flag rwb.dochub.extract is on.

1. JOB-12 Document intake: runs extractStep after classifyStep and before matchStep.
2. ExtractStep: selects intake items with ocr_status DONE and extract_status PENDING that are classified with no review_reason, or that carry a document ID with a given type (uploads), locking each row.
3. ExtractStep: reads the field definitions of the type from the version of DocumentTypeCatalog in force, the threshold and the attempts.
4. ExtractStep: reads the page text and layout through OcrOutputReader.
5. FieldExtractor: the extractor named by extraction_method returns a raw value and a confidence per field, with the extractor version.
6. ValueNormalizer: converts each value to its data type: Thai and English dates to ISO dates, Buddhist Era years less BE_YEAR_OFFSET, Thai digits to Arabic digits, amounts to numeric(18,2) baht.
7. ExtractStep: sets each field to state OK, or REVIEW when the confidence is below the threshold, the value cannot be converted, the value fails its pattern, or the field is review_only.
8. ExtractStep: for an item with no document, writes the fields to document_intake.extracted_fields and sets extract_status DONE; matchStep (RWB-E1-032) passes them to DocumentStore.store, which writes the document_field rows and sets review_status PENDING when a field is in REVIEW.
9. ExtractStep: for an item with a document, writes the document_field rows directly, sets document.review_status PENDING when a field is in REVIEW, and writes DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17) to the outbox in the same transaction.
10. Case owner: opens SCR-30 Case documents and sees the fields with their confidence; a document with review_status PENDING shows MSG-P5-003.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field confidence is below the threshold | Field state REVIEW; document review_status PENDING when stored | MSG-P5-003 | AC3, AC5 |
| X2 | The field is review_only in the type table | Field state REVIEW whatever its confidence | MSG-P5-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | A value cannot be converted to its data type | Raw value kept, confidence 0.0000, state REVIEW | MSG-P5-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The extractor does not answer within the timeout on every attempt | extract_status FAILED; review_reason EXTRACTION_FAILED; no fields; item in the review queue | MSG-P5-003 | AC8 |
| X5 | The job runs again over extracted items | Not extracted again; no second set of fields | None | AC9 |
| X6 | Two workers start on the same item | The row lock lets one worker take it; the other skips it | None | AC10 |
| X7 | A new version of an uploaded document is added | New rows for the new version; old rows inactive and readable | None | AC11 |
| X8 | A user reads a document outside their scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC13 |
| X9 | A user without Documents R reads the document | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-053-14 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Adds one step to JOB-12 after the OCR and classification steps of Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | Fields, thresholds, methods, patterns and review-only flags are data |
| Valuable | Ends re-keying of court dates, case numbers and appraisal values from paper |
| Estimable | One job step, an extractor interface with two implementations, a normalizer, an evaluation runner |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each scenario below is one test with synthetic data |

```gherkin
Feature: Field extraction for the six types into the index

 Background:
 Given DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force
 Given COURT_NOTICE lists court_name (text), black_case_no (text, pattern two to four letters, a space, digits, "/" and four digits), notice_date (date) and hearing_date (date)
 Given EXTRACT_FIELD_THRESHOLD is 0.80

 Scenario: AC1 Fields extracted
 Given intake item "IN-0001" classified "COURT_NOTICE" with confidence 0.9400
 Given its OCR text holds court "Civil Court", black case number "Por 1234/2569", notice date "1 December 2569 BE" and hearing date "15 December 2569 BE"
 When extractStep runs
 Then extracted_fields of "IN-0001" holds court_name "Civil Court" 0.9600, black_case_no "Por 1234/2569" 0.9100, notice_date "2026-12-01" 0.9000 and hearing_date "2026-12-15" 0.8800, each with state "OK" and extractor version "EXT-TPL-1.0"
 Then extract_status is "DONE"
 Then when matchStep stores the document on case "RW-2026-000123" the four fields are in the index and review_status is "NOT_NEEDED"

 Scenario: AC2 Precision and recall
 Given the labeled sample of 180 documents and the pass marks precision 0.90 and recall 0.90 per field
 When the extraction evaluation run processes the sample
 Then the report lists precision and recall for each of the 26 fields with the extractor version
 Then the system lists TITLE_DEED area_sq_wa with precision 0.84 as "review-only"
 Then the run writes a proposed DOCTYPE load file with review_only true for area_sq_wa only
 Then the version in force does not change until the proposed version is loaded and approved

 Scenario: AC3 A field below the threshold goes to review
 Given intake item "IN-0002" classified "COURT_NOTICE"
 Given the extractor returns hearing_date with confidence 0.6200
 When extractStep runs
 Then hearing_date has state "REVIEW" and the other three fields state "OK"
 Then when the document is stored its review_status is "PENDING" and SCR-30 shows MSG-P5-003

 Scenario: AC4 A review-only field always goes to review
 Given TITLE_DEED field area_sq_wa has review_only true
 Given the extractor returns area_sq_wa "940" with confidence 0.9900 on item "IN-0003"
 When extractStep runs
 Then area_sq_wa has state "REVIEW"

 Scenario: AC5 Confidence equal to the threshold passes
 Given the extractor returns black_case_no on item "IN-0004" with confidence 0.8000
 When extractStep runs
 Then black_case_no has state "OK"

 Scenario: AC6 A value that cannot be converted goes to review
 Given the OCR text of item "IN-0005" holds hearing date "32 December 2569 BE"
 When extractStep runs
 Then hearing_date keeps the value "32 December 2569 BE" with confidence 0.0000 and state "REVIEW"

 Scenario: AC7 The extracted case number and account number are given to matchStep
 Given intake item "IN-0006" classified "DEMAND_LETTER" whose text holds case "RW-2026-000123" and an account number
 When extractStep runs
 Then extracted_fields holds case_no "RW-2026-000123" and account_no
 Then the system marks account_no personal and is not written to the job record or the logs

 Scenario: AC8 The extractor does not answer
 Given the extractor does not answer within 60 seconds on 3 attempts for item "IN-0007"
 When extractStep runs
 Then extract_status is "FAILED" and review_reason is "EXTRACTION_FAILED"
 Then extracted_fields is empty
```

secs.h: RWB-E1-054 Review queue for low-confidence documents
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-054 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-10 Send a low-confidence extraction to the review queue; FEAT-DCM-11 Check a low-confidence extraction |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-005 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-035, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-032 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **litigation officer**, I want **a queue of documents with low classification or extraction confidence, each correctable in one screen, with the correction fed back to the labeled set**, so that **no document is attached wrongly and the models improve**.

A wrong type or a wrong hearing date on a court notice puts the wrong date on the case and the litigation timers run from it. This story shows in one queue every intake item the pipeline could not type, read or match, and every stored document with a field below its threshold; one officer confirms or corrects the type, the case and the fields on one screen, and each correction is kept as a labeled example for the model evaluations. It meets REQ-DCM-005 and moves the measure "fields extracted without review", because each correction improves the next model version.

- RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053 and RWB-E1-032 are done: intake items carry review_reason (LOW_CONFIDENCE, UNKNOWN_TYPE, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, RESCAN, UNREADABLE_FILE, EXTRACTION_FAILED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED), candidates, candidate cases and extracted fields; stored documents carry review_status PENDING when a field is in REVIEW.
- RWB-E1-024 is done: DocumentStore.store writes the document, its fields and the DOCATT decision log entry.
- RWB-E1-035 shows documents on the case record view.
- Rows in document_hub_parameter: REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED "DOC-SVC" (assumed), REVIEW_DATE_MIN 2000-01-01, REVIEW_DATE_MAX 2100-12-31, REVIEW_PAGE_SIZE 50.
- The officer holds RW-LITOFF (Documents CRU) with team scope. Feature flag rwb.dochub.review is on.

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-31 Document review queue.
2. System: lists, oldest first, the intake items with a review_reason and no case that belong to the officer's review team, the intake items whose candidate cases are in the officer's scope, and the stored documents with review_status PENDING on cases in scope; each row shows the reason, the proposed type, the two candidates, confidence and age.
3. Litigation officer: opens an item; the system shows the file, the OCR text, the type with its candidates, the candidate cases and the fields, with fields in REVIEW marked.
4. Litigation officer: keeps the type or chooses another type from the list in force; a new type re-runs extraction for that type and shows the new fields.
5. Litigation officer: chooses the case from the candidates, or enters a case number that the system looks up through CaseDirectory.
6. Litigation officer: confirms each marked field with Confirm, or enters the value with Correct; the system checks it against the field data type and range.
7. Litigation officer: chooses Attach; the system calls DocumentStore.store with the case, the type and the fields, which writes the document, its fields and the DOCATT decision log entry, and stores a legal type in the write-once container.
8. System: sets the intake item review_outcome ATTACHED and the document review_status CONFIRMED (nothing changed) or CORRECTED (type, case or a value changed), and writes DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17).
9. Litigation officer: for a stored document with a field in REVIEW, confirms or corrects the field and completes the review with POST review.
10. Center of excellence analyst: the model evaluations (RWB-E1-060) read the resolved items through LabeledSetReader.

| X1 | Correct is chosen with an empty value | 422; nothing saved | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The chosen type is not in the type list in force | 422; nothing saved | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | A corrected date is outside the allowed range | 422; nothing saved | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | Attach or complete with a field still in REVIEW | 422; nothing stored | MSG-GEN-001 | AC7 |
| X5 | The chosen case is closed | 422; nothing stored | MSG-P5-005 | AC8 |
| X6 | Another officer saved the same item first | 409; the officer reloads | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same file is already on the chosen case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC11 |
| X8 | Discard without a reason | 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC13 |
| X9 | No item in the officer's queue | Empty state on SCR-31 | None | AC15 |
| X10 | A document outside the officer's scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC16 |
| X11 | The same confirmation is sent twice | Second call returns the saved field; nothing changes | None | AC17 |
| X12 | The user holds Documents R only | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-054-18 |
| X13 | The decision log write fails on attach | Nothing stored; item unchanged; incident raised | MSG-P7-003 | Principle 5 test TC-E1-054-19 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Works on the review items the Epic 1 pipeline steps already produce; stores through RWB-E1-024 |
| Negotiable | The review team, date limits and the type list are data; the layout follows the ACE components (DL31) |

secs.h: RWB-E1-055 Proof of delivery capture design with WIN
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-055 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P6 Communications |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-17 Capture proof of delivery from WIN |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-OCC-003, REQ-ILG-004 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, sections 3.6 and 4; Business Requirements Epic 2, section 4 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | D7.1 |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-052, RWB-E1-054, RWB-E1-028, RWB-E1-066 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **generated notices sent to WIN for print and registered mail, with the dispatch and the proof of delivery written back on the notice**, so that **the case shows what was sent and when it arrived**.

Proof of delivery is chased by phone today, and a notice period counted from the print date can be challenged in court. This story writes the daily WIN notice file (INT-14) and reads back the WIN barcode and the weekly proof of delivery that ACE ingests into `pod_receipt`, through `v_ace_pod` by `notice_ref`. It publishes the delivery so the notice period timer starts from the delivery date (CTL-15). It serves REQ-OCC-003 and REQ-ILG-004 and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent", and fixes the interface contract with WIN that RWB-E2-021 completes. The Workbench writes no WIN delivery fact of its own: ACE holds the proof of delivery, as it holds every other source record (D-RCV-35 U1).

- RWB-E1-052 is done: notices are generated in state Generated with a stored PDF.
- RWB-E1-028 is done: P3 starts a NOTICE_PERIOD timer when it consumes NoticeDelivered.
- RWB-E1-066 is done: the interaction ledger accepts entries through its writer.
- RWB-E1-054 is done: held records reach a review list.
- The integration adapters (P2) send and receive WIN files on the SFTP path agreed with the WIN owner.
- The dispatch-eligible notice states are configured: Generated in Epic 1.
- JOB-10 is listed in the job monitor with its run book (RWB-E1-056).
- v_ace_pod is a Section B view over the ACE table pod_receipt, so the proof of delivery steps stay behind their flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).

1. JOB-10 WIN outbound notices, daily 16:00: selects notices in a dispatch-eligible state with no sent date.
2. System: builds one INT-14 file: ContractNO of the case's primary account, addressee, address read from `v_ace_contact` by `person_key`, notice type, template version and document reference; writes the trailer with the record count.
3. System: hands the file to the integration adapters and marks each notice "file sent" with the file ID.
4. Integration adapters: deliver the WIN acknowledgment, which carries per ContractNO the sent date (DDMMYYYY), Barcode and Sent Type (s2t mapping of INT-14).
5. System: sets notice state Sent with sent_date, barcode and sent_type; writes a LETTER entry to the interaction ledger; publishes NoticeDispatched.
6. System: reads the WIN proof of delivery that ACE ingested into `pod_receipt`, through `v_ace_pod`, for the notice's business date.
7. System: matches each `v_ace_pod` row to a notice by barcode, then by `notice_ref`; sets callback_date and delivery_status from the row, and state Delivered.
8. System: writes the delivery to the interaction ledger and publishes NoticeDelivered with the delivery date; P3 starts the notice period timer from that date.
9. System: each day, compares notices sent to WIN with barcodes returned (REC-05) and lists any notice with no barcode three days after sending for the platform administrator.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | WIN does not acknowledge the file | Notices stay Generated with file sent; the next JOB-10 run sends them again; after the third failure a task goes to the owning team | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4 |
| X2 | The ACE batch for source WIN is not COMPLETE for the business date | No `v_ace_pod` row of that date is read; earlier delivery data stays; the notice data product shows stale | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | A `v_ace_pod` row names an unknown barcode and notice_ref | The row is held on the exception list; the rest are read | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The same `v_ace_pod` row is read twice | One delivery is recorded and the repeat is counted | None | AC7 |
| X5 | JOB-10 runs twice on one day | No notice is written to a second file | None | AC8 |
| X6 | No barcode three days after sending | REC-05 break listed for the platform administrator | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A later `v_ace_pod` row repeats a delivery already recorded | Ignored and counted | None | AC10 |
| X8 | The WIN batch is one business day late | The notice data product shows as stale | MSG-P1-001 | AC11 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses generated notices (RWB-E1-052) and the P3 timer consumer (RWB-E1-028); refused and undeliverable results come in RWB-E2-021 |
| Negotiable | The file layouts are the WIN contract; schedule and eligible states are configuration |
| Valuable | The case shows sent and delivered dates from WIN, not from a phone call |
| Estimable | One outbound job step, two inbound handlers, one daily reconciliation |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against synthetic WIN files |

```gherkin
Feature: Proof of delivery capture design with WIN

 Background:
 Given the dispatch-eligible notice states are "GENERATED"
 Given notice "N-0001" for case "RC-2026-000123" is in state "Generated" with notice type "DEMAND" and primary account contract "CT-77001"

 Scenario: AC1 Dispatched
 Given JOB-10 runs at 16:00 on 2026-11-25
 When WIN acknowledges the file with sent date 26112026, barcode "RR123456789TH" and sent type "NPL" for contract "CT-77001"
 Then notice "N-0001" has state "Sent", sent date 2026-11-26 and barcode "RR123456789TH"
 Then the interaction ledger has an outbound "LETTER" entry for case "RC-2026-000123" on 2026-11-26
 Then the system writes noticeDispatched to the outbox with notice "N-0001", barcode "RR123456789TH" and sent date 2026-11-26
 Then the case record shows MSG-P6-004 "DEMAND was sent for registered mail on 26 November 2026."

 Scenario: AC2 Proof of delivery
 Given notice "N-0001" is "Sent" with barcode "RR123456789TH"
 When v_ace_pod holds a row for 2026-11-30 with barcode "RR123456789TH" and callback_date 2026-11-28
 Then notice "N-0001" has state "Delivered", delivery status "DELIVERED" and callback date 2026-11-28
 Then the system writes noticeDelivered to the outbox with delivered date 2026-11-28
 Then case "RC-2026-000123" has a running "NOTICE_PERIOD" timer started on 2026-11-28

 Scenario: AC3 Interface contract agreed with WIN
 Given the sample INT-15 file "WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1" of 25 records supplied by the WIN owner
 When ACE ingests it and the Workbench reads v_ace_pod
 Then all 25 rows are present in v_ace_pod with 0 refused
 Then v_ace_batch_status holds source "WIN" with feed_version "WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1" for the business date

 Scenario: AC4 File not acknowledged
 Given the WIN file of 2026-11-25 holding "N-0001" is not acknowledged
 When JOB-10 runs on 2026-11-26, 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28 and none is acknowledged
 Then the system sends "N-0001" in each of the three files and stays "Generated"
 Then after the third failure a task is raised to the litigation officer team with MSG-GEN-006 naming "WIN"

 Scenario: AC5 The WIN batch fails its check in ACE
 Given the ACE batch for source "WIN" of 2026-11-30 has status "FAILED" at its record count check
 When the proof of delivery for 2026-11-30 is read
 Then the system reads no v_ace_pod row for that date and no notice changes state
 Then the notice data product shows MSG-P1-001 naming "DP07 Legal" and 2026-11-23

 Scenario: AC6 Unknown reference held
 Given v_ace_pod holds 30 rows for 2026-11-30 and 1 row has barcode "RR000000000TH" and notice_ref "WIN-99999" matching no notice
 When the proof of delivery is read
 Then 29 notices update their delivery fields
 Then the system holds 1 row on the exception list with check "References"

 Scenario: AC7 The same proof of delivery read twice
 Given the v_ace_pod rows for business date 2026-11-30 have been read
 When the same rows are read again
 Then one delivery is recorded per notice and the repeat is counted under rule R-UNI-40
 Then no notice changes state a second time

 Scenario: AC8 Repeated dispatch run
 Given JOB-10 has written notice "N-0001" in the file of 2026-11-25
 When JOB-10 is rerun on 2026-11-25 from the job monitor
 Then the second file does not hold "N-0001"

 Scenario: AC9 Barcode missing after three days
 Given notice "N-0002" was in the file of 2026-11-25 and no barcode has returned
 When the daily reconciliation REC-05 runs on 2026-11-28
 Then the system lists "N-0002" as a break for the platform administrator on SCR-45

 Scenario: AC10 Repeated delivery record
 Given notice "N-0001" is "Delivered" with callback date 2026-11-28
 When v_ace_pod holds a second row with barcode "RR123456789TH" and callback_date 2026-11-28
 Then the notice is unchanged
 Then the system writes no second NoticeDelivered
 Then the system counts the repeat under rule R-UNI-40

 Scenario: AC11 Proof of delivery batch late
 Given the WIN batch due on 2026-11-30 is not COMPLETE on 2026-12-01
 When a litigation officer opens case "RC-2026-000123" on 2026-12-01
 Then the notice section shows MSG-P1-001 naming "DP07 Legal" and 2026-11-23
```

**Job JOB-10 WIN outbound notices**

| Item | Value |

| Trigger | Quartz, daily 16:00 Asia/Bangkok |
| Input | Notices in a dispatch-eligible state with no sent date |

|---|---|

secs.h: RWB-E1-056 Run books and monitoring for every Epic 1 Workbench job
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-056 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | FEAT-DRI-18 Run run books and monitoring for every job |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.2; Business Requirements Program, section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-007, RWB-E1-015, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **a run book for every Workbench job, the agent runtime and the view conformance check (purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps, escalation) and monitoring of each job's last run, status and duration beside the last complete ACE business date per source**, so that **the operations team can restart any Epic 1 job without the developer and can tell a late ACE batch from a failed Workbench job**.

The Workbench loads no source data (D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010). Its scheduled work is the case list chain, the timer check, daily rebalancing, payment matching, booking confirmation, the WIN notice file, the outbox sender, document intake, the decision log copy and its hash chain check, the reporting extract, retention, the agent runtime and the view conformance test. A failed job that only its developer can restart holds the case list and the morning allocation; a late ACE batch looks exactly like a failed Workbench job unless the monitor shows the ACE business date beside it.

This story gives each job a catalog row with an owner and a run book, checks in the pipeline that both exist and that the run books name the ACE batch dependency, the stale marker and AceDataLate, and the view conformance test, and shows each job's last run, status and duration beside the last complete ACE business date per source from `v_ace_batch_status`. No inbound load job is catalogued: ACE ingests every source, ACE monitors its own ingestion, and the Workbench watches only the business date it receives. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (a named owner for every failure).

- RWB-E1-007 is done: JOB-10 and JOB-11 send the outbound files and write the outbox.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: `v_ace_batch_status`, `data_product_load`, the stale marker and EV-27 AceDataLate are in place.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, the grants and the view conformance test CHK-01.
- The Workbench jobs are built or stubbed: JOB-02, JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-05, JOB-06, JOB-07, JOB-08, JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12, JOB-13, JOB-14, JOB-15 and JOB-17, plus the agent runtime service AGT-01 and the view conformance test CHK-01. The catalog row sets `first_release` to "E1".
- The jobs run on the clustered ACE Quartz scheduler and record each run through the P1 job run log (RWB-TE-007). No inbound load job exists.
- The person holds RW-PLATADM through RWB-<env>-RW-PLATADM.
- The Log Analytics workspace of the ACE service receives the application logs.

1. Platform administrator: confirms one `job_catalog` row per job with job ID, name, owner role, schedule, run book path, expected duration and alert threshold. V0004 seeds the 16 Epic 1 rows; later changes are data rows, not code.
2. Squad member (RW-TRIBE): writes the run book at `docs/operations/runbooks/<job ID>.md` with eight sections: purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation.
3. Squad member: names the ACE sources the job reads through `recovery.v_ace_*` and the upstream Workbench job in Dependencies; names the stale marker on `data_product_load` and EV-27 AceDataLate in Failure signs when the job reads ACE; the view conformance run book names CHK-01 and the dictionary load through RWB-E1-043 in Checks and Restart steps.
4. Pipeline: `RunbookCompletenessTest` checks that every Quartz job and every catalog row has a run book with the eight headings, that no run book names an inbound load job, a file arrival, a load rerun or a data quality exception console, and that no run book names a table in schema `public`.
5. Each job: writes a structured event `rwb.job.run` at start and end with job ID, business date, status and duration.
6. Platform administrator: opens the Log Analytics workbook "Recovery jobs" or calls GET /admin/jobs and sees last run, status and duration per job, and the last complete ACE business date per source from `v_ace_batch_status`.
7. Alert rule: a job with status FAILED, or running longer than its alert threshold, emails the owner role and RW-PLATADM with MSG-P2-004.
8. System: when an ACE batch is late or failed, the freshness step marks the product STALE, publishes EV-27 AceDataLate and holds the dependent job; the run book says to wait for the batch and not to rerun the job.
9. Platform administrator: follows the restart steps in the run book and calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun.
10. System: restarts the job from its failed step; the dependent jobs run in the order of the daily timeline.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A job has no catalog row or no run book, or a run book lacks a section | The pipeline fails and names the job and the missing section | MSG-P2-005 | AC4 |
| X2 | A run book names an inbound load job, a file arrival, a load rerun, a data quality exception console or a table in schema public | The pipeline fails and names the run book and the forbidden line | Build log: JOB-02.md names public.account; a run book may name only the Workbench jobs and recovery.v_ace_* | AC1 |
| X3 | A rerun is requested while the job runs | Refused; the running job continues | MSG-P2-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | A job runs past its alert threshold | The owner role and RW-PLATADM are alerted; the job is not stopped | MSG-P2-004 | AC6 |
| X5 | A rerun of a job that already completed for the business date | Refused with 409; the job runs nothing and no business row changes | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X6 | An ACE batch is late or failed | The product is marked STALE, EV-27 is published, the dependent job is recorded WAITING and is not rerun | MSG-P1-001 | AC8 |
| X7 | The view conformance test CHK-01 fails | The merge is blocked; the run book gives the dictionary load through RWB-E1-043 as the fix | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC9 |
| X8 | A role without the right reruns a job | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-056-08 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the outbound jobs of RWB-E1-007, the batch view and stale marker of RWB-E1-015 and the views and conformance test of RWB-E1-069; each job's own story supplies the job |
| Negotiable | Owners, thresholds and paths are catalog rows; the story fixes the eight run book sections and the two checks |
| Valuable | Any Workbench job can be restarted by operations on the day it fails, and a late ACE batch is not mistaken for a Workbench failure |
| Estimable | One seed migration, one pipeline test, one workbook, two alert rules, one endpoint |
| Small | Within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test or pipeline check |

```gherkin
Feature: Run books and monitoring for every Epic 1 Workbench job

 Background:
 Given job_catalog holds 16 rows with first release "E1": JOB-02, JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-05, JOB-06, JOB-07, JOB-08, JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12, JOB-13, JOB-14, JOB-15, JOB-17, AGT-01 and CHK-01

 Then each file has the sections purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation

 Given JOB-02 failed at 05:40 on business date 2026-11-30 at its case creation step, because v_ace_account returned no row for an account at 90 days past due
 When a platform administrator follows the restart steps, confirms in v_ace_batch_status that ALS is COMPLETED for 2026-11-30, and calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun at 06:05

 Then the run records no developer action

 Given a developer adds a Quartz job "JOB-20" with a run book that has no "Escalation" section
 When the pipeline runs
 Then the build fails with message MSG-P2-005 naming job "JOB-20" and section "Escalation"

 Scenario: AC5 Rerun while running refused
 Given JOB-04 started at 06:40 and is running
 When a platform administrator calls POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun for JOB-04 at 06:45

 Then JOB-04 continues its run

 Scenario: AC6 Job running past its threshold
 Given JOB-02 has an alert threshold of 45 minutes (assumed; DL11)
 When JOB-02 has run for 46 minutes on business date 2026-12-01
 Then the data steward group and the platform administrator group receive message MSG-P2-004
 Then the system does not stop JOB-02

 Scenario: AC7 Rerun of a completed job changes nothing
 Given JOB-04 completed for business date 2026-12-01
 When a platform administrator reruns it for the same date
 Then the response is 409 with message MSG-GEN-004
 Then case_list_row still holds one row per case account for 2026-12-01
 Then reconciliation_result still holds one row per product group for 2026-12-01

 Scenario: AC8 A late ACE batch holds the job
 Given v_ace_batch_status shows EFS for business date 2026-12-01 with status "FAILED" at 05:20
 When the freshness step runs
 Then data_product_load marks DP05 Contact and promises "STALE" at 05:20 and EV-27 AceDataLate is published
 Then the case list step of JOB-04 does not start for 2026-12-01 and its run is recorded "WAITING"
 Then the run book for JOB-04 says to wait for the EFS batch and not to rerun JOB-04
 Then when the EFS batch completes at 08:40, the daily gate returns COMPLETE and JOB-04 starts for 2026-12-01

 Scenario: AC9 The view conformance test has a run book
 Given a branch adds column "legacy_bucket" to recovery.v_ace_account with no sys_fields row
 When the pipeline runs CHK-01
 Then CHK-01 fails with "v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry"
 Then the merge is blocked
 Then the run book for CHK-01 gives the fix: load the dictionary row through RWB-E1-043 and rerun CHK-01
```

**Published interface (package recovery.integration.ops.api).**

| Item | Value |

| Story key | RWB-E1-057 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P5 Document hub |
| Feature | FEAT-DCM-13 Take intake from branches and the mailroom; FEAT-DCM-14 Take intake from partner SFTP; FEAT-DCM-15 Take intake from email |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-009, REQ-DCM-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence; 12 Manage partners |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-049, RWB-TE-012, RWB-E1-041 |

As a **case owner**, I want **scans from branch scanners and the mailroom, partner files by SFTP and attachments from the recovery mailboxes to enter the same OCR intake with the source recorded**, so that **every document path ends in the document hub**.

Documents reach recovery today by courier, shared folders and personal email, and an original that goes to the wrong desk is rebuilt for each audit. This story reads the four inbound paths every 15 minutes into the document intake, records where each file came from, refuses files that are not allowed or come from an unknown partner, and leaves every accepted file for the malware scan and OCR steps, so a document received in the morning is on the case the same day. It meets REQ-DCM-009 and puts every inbound file through the virus scan of REQ-DCM-010, and removes email hand-offs of customer documents (CTL-11).

- RWB-E1-049 is done: JOB-12 Document intake runs as the Spring Batch job DocumentIntakeJob with ordered steps, and the table document_intake exists.
- RWB-E1-041 is done: scanStep runs before ocrStep and quarantines infected files.
- RWB-TE-012 is done: the intake and quarantine containers exist and SY-OCR writes to the intake container by managed identity.
- The channels are set per environment by the platform administrator in properties: branch scanner folders by branch code, the mailroom folder, the partner SFTP inbound folder with one subfolder per partner_code, and the recovery mailboxes. The mailboxes are read by the SY-OCR managed identity; the mail service is assumed to be Exchange Online read through Microsoft Graph (no open decision covers it).
- Partner panel rows are loaded (reference table "Partner panel", owner partner and agency manager) and readable through PartnerDirectory.
- Rows in document_hub_parameter: INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES PDF, JPG, PNG; INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB 25; INTAKE_DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS 30; INTAKE_MIN_IMAGE_KB 10; INTAKE_ALERT_AFTER_FAILURES 2. All assumed (DL11).
- Feature flag rwb.dochub.intake is on.

1. Scheduler: JOB-12 Document intake fires every 15 minutes in business hours on one service instance; intakeStep runs first, before scanStep.
2. IntakeStep: lists new files in each branch scanner folder and the mailroom folder, in each partner subfolder of the SFTP inbound folder, and new messages in each recovery mailbox.
3. IntakeStep: for each file or email attachment computes the SHA-256 hash and checks document_intake for the same channel and hash inside the duplicate window.
4. IntakeStep: checks the file type by content and extension, and the size, against the parameters.
5. IntakeStep: for a partner file, reads the partner by the subfolder's partner_code and checks that its panel_status is ACTIVE.
6. IntakeStep: copies an accepted file to the intake container and writes one document_intake row with source, channel code, source reference, file name, size, hash, received time, scanner time (scanner files), partner ID (partner files) or sender address (email), and the run ID; scan_result is left empty for scanStep.
7. IntakeStep: after the commit, moves the scanner or SFTP file to the processed folder, or moves the email to the archive folder; a refused file goes to the rejected folder.
8. IntakeStep: writes the counts per channel and result (taken in, refused by reason, duplicate) to the job record shown on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor.
9. ScanStep, ocrStep, classifyStep, extractStep and matchStep (RWB-E1-041, RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-032) then run on the new rows in the same job.
10. Platform administrator: sees the run on SCR-44 and reruns a failed run when needed.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | File type not allowed | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder; counted as refused; audit event | MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-007 | AC5 |
| X2 | File above the size limit | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder | MSG-P5-017, MSG-P5-007 | AC6 |
| X3 | Partner subfolder code unknown or partner not ACTIVE | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder | MSG-P5-007 | AC7 |
| X4 | Same hash from the same channel inside the window | No new row; file moved to processed; counted as duplicate | None | AC8 |
| X5 | No new file on any channel | Run logged with zero counts | None | AC9 |
| X6 | The intake container does not accept writes | Files left at the channel; run failed; next run takes them | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |
| X7 | Two runs in a row fail on one channel | Alert to the platform administrator | MSG-P5-008 | AC11 |
| X8 | Two service instances are due at once | The job runs once | None | AC12 |
| X9 | Email with no attachment, or only images under 10 KB | Email archived; no intake row | None | AC13 |
| X10 | The move to processed fails after the commit | The file is seen again on the next run and counted as a duplicate | None | AC14 |
| X11 | The time is outside business hours | No run | None | AC15 |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the model gateway, the prompt and policy store, the guardrail checker and the evaluation harness deployed in the recovery module**, so that **every Workbench agent is built, called, checked and scored through one path with its versions recorded**.

Officers gather and check case facts by hand before every decision, and no agent can help until there is one controlled way to call a model. This story gives every later agent the same gateway, the same versioned prompts and policies, the same output checks and the same scoring, so that an agent runs under a service identity (REQ-ACA-010), sees only masked personal data (REQ-ACA-005) and reads every threshold from a versioned row (REQ-DRI-010). The measure is the agent fallback rate, target below 10 percent per month, read from the agent run table.

- RWB-E1-001 (recovery tables) and RWB-E1-069 (read-only ACE views) are done, so synthetic cases and ACE source data exist in DEV and SIT.
- RWB-E1-037 is done: the P4 masking service masks personal fields by role, including for SY-AGENT.
- The service identity SY-AGENT exists with the Entra ID managed identity RWB-DEV-SY-AGENT (and the SIT, UAT and PROD equivalents) and the permissions seeded in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql (Case record R, Documents R, Rules and parameters R, Reference data R, Decision log C).
- The model endpoint INT-23 is reachable on a private endpoint in the SCB tenant. Assumed option B of DL33: the endpoint ACE uses through AAL.
- A person holding RW-COE loads prompts, policies and labeled samples; a person holding RW-RISK approves them.

1. RW-COE: loads a prompt file and a policy file for agent "INTAKE" through POST /admin/agent-configs.
2. System: validates each file, stores it as a new version with status "LOADED" and keeps every earlier version readable.
3. RW-RISK: approves the version through POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve; the version takes effect on its valid from date.
4. Calling step (any module, through RWB-TE-013): asks the orchestrator to run agent "INTAKE" for one case with an idempotency key.
5. System: reads the approved policy and prompt in force, reads the inputs through the tool gateway, masks personal fields through the P4 masking service and calls the model endpoint with the policy timeout.
6. System: runs the guardrail checker on the answer: output schema, allowed tool list and confidence floor.
7. System: writes one agent run row with the agent, policy, prompt and model versions, status, latency, tokens and cost, and publishes AgentRunCompleted.
8. System: returns the checked answer, or a fallback result with its reason, to the calling step.
9. RW-COE: loads a labeled sample through POST /admin/agent-samples and starts the evaluation harness through POST /admin/agent-evaluations.
10. System: runs the agent on every sample row in shadow, scores it against the labels and stores the scores with the policy, prompt and model versions.

| X1 | The model endpoint does not answer within the policy timeout of 60 seconds | Run status TIMED_OUT, fallback true; the caller uses the rule result (R-UNI-32) | None to a user | AC6 |
| X2 | The answer fails its output schema | Run status GUARDRAIL_FAILED, failure counted by check code; fallback true | None to a user | AC3 |
| X3 | The agent asks for a tool that is not on its allowed list | The tool call is refused and logged; run status GUARDRAIL_FAILED; fallback true | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | The answer confidence is below the policy confidence floor | Run status BELOW_FLOOR; fallback true | None to a user | AC10 |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs** (API-P10-001, in api.yaml)
- Request: query agent, from, to (dates, ISO 8601).
- Response: 200, array of AgentRun (id, agent, agentVersion, caseId, outcome, fallback, latencyMs). outcome carries agent_run.status. agentVersion is "<agent>@<policy_version>/<prompt_version>", for example "ECHO@P1/PR1".
- Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 role without Platform administration R (MSG-P4-002); 503 store unavailable.
- Authorization: Platform administration, R, scope applied.
- Idempotency: not applicable (read).

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs** (new, see additions)
- Request: query agent, kind (PROMPT or POLICY), status.
- Response: 200, array of AgentConfigVersion (versionId, agent, kind, version, status, validFrom, validTo, loadedBy, approvedBy, bodyHash).
- Errors: 401, 403, 503. Authorization: Rules and parameters, R.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs** (new)
- Request: multipart/form-data: file (JSON), kind (PROMPT or POLICY), agent, validFrom.
- Response: 201 AgentConfigVersion with status LOADED.
- Errors: 401; 403; 409 version number already exists for the agent and kind; 422 a check fails (MSG-P10-001 with the check text); 503.
- Authorization: Rules and parameters, C. Idempotency: agent, kind and version number are unique; a repeat load of the same version returns 409.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve** (new)
- Request: path versionId (uuid); header If-Match with the row version.
- Response: 200 AgentConfigVersion with status APPROVED.
- Errors: 401; 403; 404 unknown version; 409 approver is the loader (MSG-P7-002), version not LOADED, or row changed (MSG-GEN-004); 503.
- Authorization: Rules and parameters, A. Idempotency: a second approval of an APPROVED version returns 409.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-samples** (new)
- Request: multipart/form-data: file (CSV: subject_type, subject_id, label_key, expected_value), agent, sampleCode.
- Response: 201 AgentSample (sampleCode, sampleVersion, rows).
- Errors: 401; 403; 422 a row fails a check (MSG-P10-001); 503.
- Authorization: Rules and parameters, C. Idempotency: each load creates the next sample version.

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations** (new)
- Request: AgentEvaluationRequest (agent, sampleCode, sampleVersion, approaches; approaches default ["AGENT"]).
- Response: 202 AgentEvaluationRun with status RUNNING.
- Errors: 401; 403; 409 the same evaluation is running (MSG-P10-003); 422 sample empty (MSG-P10-002); 503.
- Authorization: Rules and parameters, C. Idempotency: one RUNNING run per agent, sample and sample version.

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations** (new)
- Request: query agent, from, to. Response: 200, array of AgentEvaluationRun with its AgentEvaluation score rows.
- Errors: 401, 403, 503. Authorization: Rules and parameters, R.

| EvaluationHarness | Service | Runs the agent in shadow on each sample row, scores against labels, writes score rows |

secs.h: RWB-E1-059 Case intake agent in shadow [E1b]
secs.t:
| Item | Value |

| Story key | RWB-E1-059 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-03 Run the case intake agent in shadow |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.4 |

| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-030, RWB-E1-058, RWB-TE-013 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the case intake agent to build a case file summary and flag gaps for every new Epic 1 case in shadow mode**, so that **the agent is scored against the business analysts' review before any case owner sees its output**.

A case owner who takes over a case at day 90 reads every account, document and appraisal to find what is missing before deciding the next step. The intake agent prepares that summary and the list of gaps. In Epic 1 it runs in shadow only: its output is stored, compared with the business analysts' review of the same 200 cases and shown to nobody, so the step to autonomy level 1 in RWB-E2-028 is decided on a measured agreement rate. Inputs are masked before the model call (REQ-ACA-005) and the agent reads data as SY-AGENT (REQ-ACA-010).

- RWB-E1-058 (gateway, policy store, guardrail, evaluation harness) and RWB-TE-013 (client) are done.
- RWB-E1-030 is done, so cases are created and allocated daily and EV-01 CaseCreated is published.
- Approved agent_policy "INTAKE" version "P1" with autonomy_mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, confidence floor 0.80, allowed tools read_case, read_accounts, read_documents, read_valuations, read_contact_points, and output schema "intake-summary-v1".
- Approved agent_prompt "INTAKE" version "PR1".
- The output schema lists the gap types as data: MISSING_DOCUMENT, NO_VALID_APPRAISAL, NO_CONTACT_POINT, STALE_INPUT.
- Labeled sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 is loaded by RW-COE: the business analysts' review of 200 Epic 1 cases, one row per case and gap type with expected value Y or N.

1. SY-CASEWF: creates case "RW-2026-000301" and writes EV-01 CaseCreated to the outbox.
2. System (IntakeShadowListener): receives the event and calls the orchestrator for agent "INTAKE" with key "INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>".
3. System: reads the case, accounts, documents, valuations and contact points through the tool gateway as SY-AGENT, masks personal fields and calls the model.
4. System: checks the answer (schema, tools, floor) and stores the summary and gap flags on the agent run with mode SHADOW.
5. System: publishes EV-28 AgentRunCompleted; no screen and no case field changes.
6. RW-COE: starts the evaluation of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" through POST /admin/agent-evaluations.
7. System: runs the agent in shadow on each of the 200 sample cases and compares each gap flag with the label.
8. System: stores one score row per gap type with the agreement rate, precision, recall and sample size.
9. RW-COE: reads the scores through GET /admin/agent-evaluations.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The agent times out or fails a guardrail on a case | Run stored with status TIMED_OUT or GUARDRAIL_FAILED; counted as a failure type; no retry for that event | None to a user | AC4 |
| X2 | The ACE batch for the day is not COMPLETE | Run proceeds; data_as_of holds the last complete business date and the agent must return gap STALE_INPUT; a run without it fails check SCHEMA_RULE | None to a user | AC5 |
| X3 | The same CaseCreated event arrives twice | One run for the case and business date (R-UNI-40) | None to a user | AC6 |
| X4 | Labels cover fewer cases than the sample | Agreement is computed on labeled cases only; sample size shows the labeled count | None to a user | AC7 |
| X5 | A user endpoint is asked for shadow output | No endpoint returns the output content; GET /admin/agent-runs returns metadata only | None to a user | AC1 |
| X6 | Evaluation started on an empty sample | Refused with 422 | MSG-P10-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right starts or reads evaluations | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-059-09 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the platform (RWB-E1-058) and the client (RWB-TE-013) |
| Negotiable | Gap types, prompt and floor are data rows; the business analysts may add a gap type by a new schema version |
| Valuable | Gives the measured agreement rate that decides whether the case owner gets the summary in Epic 3 |
| Estimable | One listener, one prompt, one output schema, one sample; no screen |
| Small | One developer and one analyst for two weeks |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the model stub with synthetic cases |

```gherkin
Feature: Case intake agent in shadow [E1b]

 Background:
 Given agent "INTAKE" has approved policy "P1" with mode "SHADOW" and prompt "PR1"
 Given the gap types in output schema "intake-summary-v1" are MISSING_DOCUMENT, NO_VALID_APPRAISAL, NO_CONTACT_POINT and STALE_INPUT

 Scenario: AC1 Shadow run
 Given 200 Epic 1 cases created between 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-04
 When the agent runs on each CaseCreated event
 Then 200 agent runs with mode "SHADOW" store a summary and gap flags
 Then no case field, task, queue or decision log entry changes
 Then GET /cases/{caseId} and GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline return no agent output
 Then GET /admin/agent-runs returns the 200 runs without the summary or the gap flags

 Scenario: AC2 Agreement rate
 Given the business analysts' review of the same 200 cases in sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1
 When the comparison runs
 Then one score row per gap type holds the agreement rate, precision, recall and sample size 200
 Then for MISSING_DOCUMENT with 182 agreeing cases the agreement rate is 0.9100
 Then each score row holds policy "P1", prompt "PR1" and the model version

 Scenario: AC3 A new case starts one shadow run
 Given case "RW-2026-000301" is created on 2026-11-30
 When EV-01 CaseCreated is processed
 Then one agent run exists with key "INTAKE:<caseId>:2026-11-30", trigger "CaseCreated" and mode "SHADOW"

 Given the model stub does not answer for case "RW-2026-000302"
 When the agent runs
 Then the run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true
 Then the system makes no second run for that event
 Then the failure count for type "TIMED_OUT" on 2026-11-30 is 1

 Given v_ace_batch_status holds a COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-28 and none for 2026-11-30
 When the agent runs for case "RW-2026-000303"
 Then the run holds data_as_of 2026-11-28
 Then the stored gap flags include STALE_INPUT
 Then an answer without STALE_INPUT fails check "SCHEMA_RULE" with fallback true

 Scenario: AC6 A repeated event has no further effect
 Given EV-01 CaseCreated for case "RW-2026-000301" was processed on 2026-11-30
 When the same event arrives again with the same event ID
 Then one agent run exists for the case and date and the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40)

 Scenario: AC7 Partly labeled sample
 Given sample "INTAKE-S1" version 2 has labels for 180 of 200 cases
 When the comparison runs
 Then each score row holds sample size 180
 Then the system lists the 20 unlabeled cases as unlabeled on the evaluation run

 Scenario: AC8 Empty sample
 Given sample "INTAKE-S3" has no labeled rows for "INTAKE"
 When RW-COE starts the evaluation
 Then the system refuses the request with 422 and MSG-P10-002
```

| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-04 Evaluate document extraction quality |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DCM-005, REQ-DCM-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.9; Business Requirements Program, section 5.5 |
| L3 process | 13 Manage documents and correspondence |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-058 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **field extraction for the six document types scored against the labeled sample for three approaches (OCR template, model, and OCR checked by the model)**, so that **the extraction approach and the confidence threshold for each document type are chosen on measured precision and recall**.

Fields read wrongly from a court notice or a title deed send a case down the wrong step, and fields sent to review without need take officer time. This story measures the three approaches on the same reviewed documents, field by field, and proposes for each document type the approach and the confidence threshold below which a field goes to the review queue. It serves REQ-DCM-006 (fields extracted for the agreed types) and REQ-DCM-005 (confidence score and review queue below the threshold).

- RWB-E1-053 is done: the P5 pipeline (SY-OCR) writes document_field rows with a confidence per field for the six types in LOV-DOC-TYPE (assumed six types; DL19).
- RWB-E1-058 is done: the gateway, the evaluation harness and the sample loader exist.
- Approved agent_policy "EXTRACT" version "P1" (mode SHADOW, allowed tools read_document_content, read_document_fields) and prompt "PR1".
- Labeled sample "EXTRACT-S1" version 1 is loaded: fields confirmed or corrected by a person (document_field.confirmed_by set), at least 30 documents per type. Personal field values are held as SHA-256 hashes.
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C.

1. RW-COE: loads sample "EXTRACT-S1" through POST /admin/agent-samples with one row per document and field.
2. RW-COE: starts the evaluation with approaches OCR_TEMPLATE, MODEL and OCR_AND_MODEL through POST /admin/agent-evaluations.
3. System: for OCR_TEMPLATE, reads the stored document_field values through the P5 interface; makes no model call.
4. System: for MODEL, calls agent "EXTRACT" in shadow on the document content and reads the fields from its answer.
5. System: for OCR_AND_MODEL, passes the OCR fields with the content to agent "EXTRACT" and takes its checked values.
6. System: compares each value with the label and stores true positives, false positives, false negatives, precision and recall per field and approach.
7. System: for each document type, picks the approach with the highest F1 and proposes the confidence threshold for the review queue.
8. RW-COE: reads the result through GET /admin/agent-evaluations and exports it; the solution architect records the choice as a proposed architecture decision after ADR-009.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A document type has fewer than 30 labeled documents | The type is scored and marked "insufficient sample"; no approach is proposed for it | None to a user | AC3 |
| X2 | The model times out or fails a guardrail on a document | The MODEL value counts as empty (false negative); the failure is counted on the run | None to a user | AC4 |
| X3 | Two approaches have the same F1 for a type | The approach with fewer model calls is proposed (OCR_TEMPLATE before OCR_AND_MODEL before MODEL) | None to a user | AC5 |
| X4 | A sample row names a document or field that does not exist | The sample load is refused in full | MSG-P10-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | No approach reaches precision 0.95 on a field at any confidence | The field is proposed as review-only | None to a user | AC7 |
| X6 | Evaluation started while the same one is running | Refused with 409 | MSG-P10-003 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-060-09 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the extraction pipeline (RWB-E1-053) and the harness (RWB-E1-058) |
| Negotiable | Thresholds, sample size floor and the tie order are parameters in the policy row |
| Valuable | Sets the review threshold that decides how many documents an officer checks by hand |
| Estimable | Two scorers and one proposal rule on top of the existing harness |
| Small | Under two weeks with one developer |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a fixture of labeled documents with known counts |

secs.h: RWB-E1-061 Intake agent evaluation and L1 proposal [E2a]
secs.t:
| Item | Value |

| Story key | RWB-E1-061 |

| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-059 |

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the evaluation report of the case intake agent and the proposal to run it at autonomy level 1, built from the stored shadow results**, so that **the risk and model risk officer approves the step to L1 on measured results**.

The step from shadow to L1 puts agent output in front of case owners, so the approver needs the agreement rate, the failure types, the cost and the latency on a stated sample before deciding. This story produces that report from the evaluation run of RWB-E1-059 and holds the L1 proposal as a versioned policy row with its conditions, fallback and measures to watch (REQ-DRI-010), approved and dated like any other reference row (REQ-DRI-011). Nothing goes to L1 until RW-RISK approves the row.

- RWB-E1-059 is done: evaluation run of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 has status DONE with 200 labeled cases.
- Policy "INTAKE" version "P1" (SHADOW) is in force.
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C; RW-RISK holds Rules and parameters A.

1. RW-COE: requests the report for the evaluation run through GET /admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report.
2. System: builds the report from the stored runs and scores: sample size, agreement rate per gap type, failure counts by type, total and per-case cost, median and 95th percentile latency, policy, prompt and model versions.
3. RW-COE: exports the report as CSV and PDF for the steering committee pack.
4. RW-COE: loads policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with autonomy mode L1, the evaluation run ID, the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch through POST /admin/agent-configs.
5. System: checks that the evaluation run is DONE, that its scores meet every stated condition and that the fallback and measures are present; stores the version as LOADED.
6. RW-RISK: approves version "P2" with a valid from date through POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve after the committee agrees.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The report is requested for an evaluation that is still running | Refused with 409 | MSG-P10-008 | AC3 |
| X2 | The L1 proposal has no conditions, no fallback or no measures | Load refused in full | MSG-P10-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The evaluation scores do not meet a stated condition | Load refused, naming the gap type and the score | MSG-P10-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | The sample size is below the minimum of 200 cases | Load refused | MSG-P10-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve the proposal | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-061-08 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads only the stored results of RWB-E1-059 |
| Negotiable | Conditions and measures are values in the proposal row; the story fixes their presence and the check against scores |
| Valuable | Gives the approver one report and one row to approve for the first autonomy step |
| Estimable | One report query, one export, one extra check in the policy loader |
| Small | Three to four days |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a stored evaluation fixture |
