As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the deviation screening agent to propose X1 to X7 with reasons from case data, call notes and documents, in shadow on Epic 1 cases**, so that **the Epic 2 and Epic 3 deviation flags start from an agent with measured precision and recall per deviation type**.

A dispute, a death, a fraud sign or a lost contact found late means contact that should have stopped, or a case worked on the wrong route. The screening agent reads the case, the interaction ledger and the documents at entry and when a document arrives, and proposes deviations with reasons. In Epic 1 the proposals are stored only, scored against the business analysts' review and shown to nobody. The story measures detection from case data, call notes and documents (REQ-DVH-001), the named owner each code would route to (REQ-DVH-003) and the contact that preceded a complaint (REQ-DVH-007).

- RWB-E1-058 and RWB-TE-013 are done.
- Approved agent_policy "SCREENING" version "P1": mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, confidence floor 0.80, allowed tools read_case, read_interactions, read_documents, read_document_fields, and output schema "screening-v1" with codes from LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7).
- Approved prompt "SCREENING" version "PR1".
- Rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are loaded, so the owner role of each code is data.
- Labeled sample "SCREEN-S1" version 1: the business analysts' review of 200 Epic 1 cases, one row per case and code with expected value Y or N.

1. SY-CASEWF or P5: writes EV-01 CaseCreated for a new case, or EV-16 DocumentStored for a document on an open case.
2. System (ScreeningShadowListener): calls the orchestrator for agent "SCREENING" with key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>".
3. System: reads the case, the interaction ledger entries, the documents and their fields as SY-AGENT, masks personal fields and calls the model.
4. System: checks the answer: each proposal has a code in X1 to X7, reasons, source references and a confidence.
5. System: asks the rules component which owner role each proposed code routes to (R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06) and stores it with the proposal.
6. System: marks proposals below the confidence floor as "review"; stores everything on the agent run in mode SHADOW. No deviation record, contact stop or clock change is made.
7. RW-COE: starts the evaluation of "SCREENING" on sample "SCREEN-S1".
8. System: compares proposals at or above the floor with the labels and stores precision and recall per deviation code, with the count of review proposals.

| X1 | The answer has a code outside X1 to X7 | Check SCHEMA fails; run GUARDRAIL_FAILED; fallback true | None to a user | AC8 |
| X2 | A proposal is below the confidence floor 0.80 | Stored with marker "review"; scored separately | None to a user | AC6 |
| X3 | An X1 proposal names no preceding contact while the ledger holds one in the 30 days before | Check SCHEMA_RULE fails for that proposal | None to a user | AC5 |

As a **risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **a dashboard with runs, acceptance, override, fallback, latency, cost and evaluation score per agent and version, and an alert when an agent's daily cost passes its limit**, so that **every agent is watched from its first shadow run**.

An agent in shadow that times out on one case in five, or that spends twice its budget, must be seen in the first week, not at the L1 review. This story copies daily agent run figures to the data lake with the nightly reporting extract, matched by row count (REQ-DRI-009), so the Power BI dashboard reads the copy and not the live tables. A daily check sends an alert when the cost of an agent on a business date is above its policy limit.

- RWB-E1-058 is done: agent_run and agent_policy exist with cost, latency and status per run.
- RWB-E1-014 is done: the nightly copy path to the data lake exists.
- RWB-E1-007 is done: outbound files and the exception queue use the integration adapters.
- JOB-15 Reporting extract runs nightly at 01:30.
- Each approved agent policy holds daily_cost_cap_thb (assumed 2,000 baht for INTAKE and SCREENING; DL33) and alert_role (assumed RW-COE).
- RW-BIANAL builds the Power BI report on the data lake table; RW-RISK and RW-COE hold Reporting R.

1. JOB-15 Reporting extract: at 01:30 calls the P10 step AgentRunExtractStep for the previous business date.
2. System: groups the agent runs of that date by agent, policy version, prompt version and model version: runs, answered, fallback, median and 95th percentile latency, tokens and cost.
3. System: adds the latest DONE evaluation score per agent and version.
4. System: writes the rows to the data lake table agent_run_daily and checks that the row count and the sum of runs match the source.
5. System: compares each agent's cost for the date with daily_cost_cap_thb of its policy; for each breach writes one agent alert and sends MSG-P10-004 through the P6 notification interface to the alert role and to RW-RISK.
6. RW-RISK: opens the Power BI report "Agent monitor v1" and reads each agent by version and date.

secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-064 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-011 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story), section 4 (REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-011) and section 5 (data dictionary sources and owners) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-043, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW)**, I want **all 122 objects and 1,366 fields of the 14 data products typed, sourced and owned, including the 30 ACE views and the four extension tables, with a data contract for the ACE read path that the ACE team confirms**, so that **every read has one published definition and a change to an ACE column reaches the dictionary through one governed load**.

The dictionary is the only place that says what a field is, where it comes from and who owns it. It now covers 122 objects and 1,366 fields: the 92 Workbench tables hold 1,062 fields, 49 of them on the four extension tables, and the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views hold 304 fields, 177 in Section A and 127 in Section B. The Workbench loads no source data (D-RCV-35 U1), so every source is either ACE, whose columns are recorded as `public.table.column` on the view fields where the view reads one column, or the Workbench itself.

V0001 creates `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract` and seeds the 122 objects and 1,366 fields. This story does not create a table or a column. It publishes the governance attributes on every field, records the change history, and takes the ACE team's confirmation of the read contract before it is published. A new ACE column is added to the dictionary by a reference load through RWB-E1-043, never by editing an applied migration; the view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 blocks the merge until the row exists. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (one system of record and one owner per product) and REQ-RDF-011 (catalog entry content). The measure is that 100 percent of the 1,366 fields return a source, an owner, a refresh cycle and a late behavior.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the 92 tables, the 30 view objects in the dictionary, the 122 `sys_objects` rows, the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows, `sys_field_version`, `data_product` and `data_contract`.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist and the view conformance test CHK-01 compares every view column with `sys_fields`.
- The reference data service (RWB-E1-043) accepts a load for table code `sys_fields` and hands approved rows to P1.
- The data steward holds RW-DATASTEW (Reference data U); the reference data administrator holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C).
- The ACE team lead is named as the confirming role for the ACE read contract; the confirmation is stored outside the Workbench as a document reference.
- `v_data_dictionary` returns the 122 objects and 1,366 fields of V0001.

1. Data steward: prepares the governance load for all 1,366 fields with owner role, refresh cycle, late behavior and interface, and checks the source system and source field of each view field against the view definition.
2. Reference data administrator: loads the file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table `sys_fields` and valid from 2026-11-30.
3. DataDictionaryLoader: refuses the whole load if any field is unknown, if a view field's source system is not "ACE", if a Workbench field's source system is not "Workbench", if a view field's source field is not a column of that view and is not one of the 7 derived fields, or if any of the required attributes is empty; otherwise writes the attributes and version 1 of each field to `sys_field_version`.
4. Data steward: records the ACE team lead's confirmation of contract DC-ACE, which lists the 304 ACE fields and the read interfaces V0002 and V0003, with the confirming role, the date and the stored document reference.
5. Data steward: publishes DC-ACE with POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish; the service refuses a contract without a confirmation.
6. DataContractService: sets the contract PUBLISHED. The published version stays in force until a later version is confirmed and published.
7. Developer or analyst: calls GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields and reads a field's type, source system, source field, refresh, owner and behavior when late.
8. Data steward: changes a field definition with PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields/{fieldId}, a reason and an If-Match version; the service writes a new `sys_field_version` row with its date and reason.
9. DataContractService: when a changed field belongs to the published DC-ACE, opens a new DRAFT contract version; the published version stays in force.
10. ACE team and recovery developer: a new ACE column is added to a view by a Flyway migration and to the dictionary by a load through RWB-E1-043; no applied migration is edited, and CHK-01 passes only when both exist.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Publish of a contract without the ACE team's confirmation | 409; contract stays DRAFT | MSG-P1-021 | AC6 |
| X2 | A field change without a reason | 422; no version written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | A dictionary load with an unknown field, a missing attribute, a source system outside ACE and Workbench, or an ACE source field that is not a column of the view and not one of the 7 derived fields | Load refused in full; the dictionary in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | Two stewards change the same field from the same version | The second change is refused with 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X5 | A field of a published contract changes | A new DRAFT contract version; the published version stays in force | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A view column exists with no `sys_fields` row | CHK-01 fails and the merge is blocked | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC4 |
| X7 | A field definition is changed with no If-Match version | 428; no version written | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the tables and seed of RWB-E1-001, the reference load of RWB-E1-043 and the views and conformance test of RWB-E1-069; it publishes the definition every later read uses |
| Negotiable | Owners, refresh cycles, late behavior and contract content are data values; the story fixes the completeness, source and version rules |
| Valuable | Every read has one published definition, and a source change is governed in one place |
| Estimable | No DDL, five endpoints, two services, one loader |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one API test against the seeded metadata tables |

secs.h: RWB-E1-065 Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-065 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-010 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-010); Business Requirements Program, section 6.7 (NFR-045) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069 |
| Status | Ready for build, Section B views behind the RWB-ACE-001 DDL (DL43) |

As a **Tribe lead and squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a sandbox database that stands up the ACE schema and the recovery schema from the same DDL as SIT, with synthetic ACE-shaped source rows and synthetic Workbench rows**, so that **I can build and test every view read before the ACE interfaces are available and without production data**.

SIT reads the real ACE database; DEV has none. Without a local ACE schema the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views cannot compile, so no squad can test a source read, the case list, a notice or a report before SIT is connected. The sandbox applies the ACE schema for the 22 Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables, Physical Schema v5 for the 92 recovery tables and the four extension tables, and V0002 and V0003 for the 30 views. It fills the source tables with synthetic rows and the Workbench tables with synthetic cases across Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME, and the exception shapes the rules must handle.

There is no copy and no load table: `loan_account`, `account_payment`, `party`, `contact_point`, `collateral`, `account_collateral`, `collections_history`, `party_product`, `valuation`, `score`, `asset`, `load_run`, `dq_exception`, `dq_rule`, `source_field_map`, `source_code_map`, `interface_run`, `interface_signoff`, `tracker_inventory` and `tracker_row` do not exist. The generator reads the data dictionary, so a schema change reaches the sandbox with no manual rebuild, and the verifier allows a clear identity number only in the ACE-shaped tables, where ACE itself holds it; the recovery schema sees `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products in one schema) and REQ-RDF-010 (no personal data outside its permitted use).

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 creates the 92 tables, `data_product`, the 122 `sys_objects` rows, the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows and the four extension tables.
- RWB-E1-069 is done: V0002 and V0003 create the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and their grants, and CHK-01 compares them with the dictionary.
- The ACE schema DDL `15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` is in the repository. It holds the 22 Tier 1 tables, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer`, `efs_action` and `iam_user`.
- The RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables is available in DEV (DL43); until it lands, the 14 Section B views and the features that read them stay behind their flags.
- A PostgreSQL 17 database `rwb_sandbox` exists in DEV, reachable from the pipeline.
- The Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE exists and maps to the sandbox read-only database role.
- The role to permission matrix rows (roles.txt, Permissions) are available as a seed file for the sandbox.
- The ACE service can be deployed in DEV against the sandbox database.

1. Pipeline: on a merge to main that changes the ACE schema DDL, a recovery Flyway migration or the dictionary, or on a manual start, runs the sandbox build stage in DEV.
2. Pipeline: creates database `rwb_sandbox_next` and two empty schemas, `public` and `recovery`.
3. Pipeline: applies `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` (22 Tier 1 tables), then the RWB-ACE-001 DDL (14 Tier 2 tables), then V0001 (92 tables and the dictionary), V0002 (16 Section A views) and V0003 (14 Section B views).
4. SandboxGenerator: reads `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `lov_value` to learn every table, column, type and list.
5. SandboxGenerator: seeds the 22 Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables with synthetic rows, including one `ace_batch_run` row per source and business date.
6. SandboxGenerator: creates synthetic cases with seed 20261128: 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME (10 percent of the 30 June 2026 inventory; DL15), with their accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments and interactions, linked by business key to the ACE-shaped rows.
7. SandboxGenerator: adds 10 cases for each exception shape in section 8, BR4.
8. SandboxGenerator: loads the 54 roles, the permission matrix and one named test user per role.
9. SandboxVerifier: checks that the 30 views compile and each returns a row, that every seeded table has rows, that every LOV column holds list values, that every foreign key resolves, that no clear personal value sits in schema `recovery`, and that the boundary accounts exist.
10. Pipeline: renames `rwb_sandbox_next` to `rwb_sandbox`, grants SELECT on schema `recovery` to role `rwb_sandbox_read`, and publishes the build result with the row count per table.
11. Developer or analyst: queries the sandbox with SQL or the export script, or calls the DEV service, without a request to another team.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A table column has no `sys_fields` row | Build fails naming the table and column; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC4 |
| X2 | The reset runs twice for the same commit and seed | The schemas are dropped and recreated; the same seed gives the same rows and counts | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A generated value breaks a constraint | Build fails naming the table and constraint; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC6 |
| X4 | A generated value in schema recovery matches a personal data pattern | Build fails naming the table and column | None (pipeline result) | AC7 |
| X5 | Accounts sit at the 90 days past due boundary | Accounts at 89 and at 90 days past due are both generated | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A second build starts while one runs | The second build waits on the pipeline lock and runs after the first | None | AC9 |
| X7 | The RWB-ACE-001 DDL is not yet in DEV | The build stops before V0003; the 16 Section A views and the Workbench tables are still built and published | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the DDL from RWB-E1-001 and RWB-E1-069 and, for Section B, the Tier 2 DDL of RWB-ACE-001; it publishes the environment every squad tests in |
| Negotiable | Volumes, seed and exception shapes are properties; the story fixes the generator, the checks and the access |
| Valuable | Every squad builds and tests every view read from the first day with no production data |
| Estimable | One generator tool, one verifier, one pipeline stage, one database role |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a pipeline test or a query against the built sandbox |

```gherkin
Feature: Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data

 Background:

 Then 10 accounts in v_ace_account have days_past_due 90 and one open case each

 Scenario: AC9 Two builds at once
 Given a sandbox build is running for commit "a1b2c3d"

 Then the second build waits until the first ends
 Then the sandbox after both holds the data for commit "e4f5a6b"
```

secs.h: RWB-E1-066 Interaction ledger store and writer
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-066 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-ILG-01 Write every Workbench event to the ledger; FEAT-ILG-02 Hold the ledger beside the decision log; FEAT-ILG-05 Raise an incident when the ledger cannot be written |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004, REQ-ILG-008 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004, REQ-ILG-008) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-027 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every contact, letter, promise, payment and hand-over on the case written to one ledger when it is recorded**, so that **the history of the case is never assembled after the fact**.

Today the history of a recovery case is spread across EFS, LIT, letters and team spreadsheets, and an officer rebuilds it by hand before each decision. One append-only ledger per case, written in the same transaction as the action it records, gives one ordered history with no gap. The ledger records what happened with the customer; the decision log records why the system acted; each ledger entry for a decision points to its decision log entry. A ledger write that fails stops the action and raises an incident, so the history never has a silent gap. Serves REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-ILG-008; NFR-070 and NFR-077.

- RWB-E1-018 is done: recovery_case exists with case numbers RW-YYYY-NNNNNN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer and its incident path (incident record and operations alert) exist.
- The interaction table from RWB-E1-001 exists with its append-only trigger tr_interaction_append_only.
- The list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT is loaded by the reference data administrator (values in section 13).
- The caller of the writer holds Case record C: a person through POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions, or a service identity (SY-CASEWF, SY-DATALOAD).

1. Case owner: records a call with POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions (channel CALL, direction OUTBOUND, result RIGHT_PARTY, summary, promise amount and date).
2. P3 interactions handler: checks Case record C and the case scope, opens a transaction and calls InteractionLedgerWriter.append().
3. InteractionLedgerWriter: validates the command (case, event code in LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, occurred time, actor, source, idempotency key).
4. InteractionLedgerWriter: takes a transaction-level advisory lock on the case ID and assigns case_seq as the case's highest case_seq plus 1.
5. InteractionLedgerWriter: inserts the entry with event code, actor type and reference, source system and source reference, channel and direction where they apply, and the decision log entry ID for a decision.
6. P3 handler: commits the action and the entry in one transaction and returns 201 with the Interaction.
7. Other recording paths (EFS history load, ALS payment load, notice dispatch): call append() in their own transactions with source system EFS or WORKBENCH.
8. On a write failure: the transaction rolls back, the caller receives MSG-P1-022, and the writer raises an incident with incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED, the case ID and the cause.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ledger cannot be written | Action and entry roll back; 503 to the caller; incident raised; nothing discarded silently | MSG-P1-022 | AC4 |
| X2 | A required value is missing (event code, occurred time, actor) | 422; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | Two entries for one case at the same moment | Both written with consecutive case_seq; no gap and no repeat | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The case does not exist or is out of scope | 404; nothing written | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | Any change or delete of an entry | Refused by the append-only trigger; a correction is a new entry naming the original | None | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the case record (RWB-E1-018) and the decision log writer with its incident path (RWB-E1-027) |
| Negotiable | Event codes are list values; the story fixes the append-only write, the sequence and the failure behavior |
| Valuable | The case history exists as it happens and is never rebuilt by hand |
| Estimable | One table change, one writer, one published interface |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a writer or API test on synthetic cases |

secs.h: RWB-E1-067 Every Workbench action into the interaction ledger
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-067 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P1 Recovery data engine |
| Feature | FEAT-ILG-01 Write every Workbench event to the ledger; FEAT-ILG-04 Reject a duplicate ledger entry |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.1 (story) and section 4 (REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-007) |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-066 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every action the Workbench takes on my case written to the ledger when it is taken**, so that **I can read the history without assembling it from four systems**.

The Workbench creates, allocates, transfers and escalates cases, attaches documents and records decisions by rule, often with no person involved. If these actions are not in the ledger, the case owner sees the customer contacts but not what the Workbench did between them. Each action already publishes an application event to the outbox in the same transaction as the change (events.txt); a ledger listener turns each event into one entry with its source and actor. Events are delivered at least once, so the listener rejects a repeat by its idempotency key and counts it. Serves REQ-ILG-005, REQ-ILG-002 and REQ-ILG-007.

- RWB-E1-066 is done: InteractionLedgerWriter, the case sequence and LOV-LEDGER-EVENT exist.
- RWB-TE-006 is done: the outbox delivers events at least once, per case in written order, with event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time and actor in the event header, and moves an event to the exception queue after the retry limit.
- The publishing stories exist for EV-01 CaseCreated and EV-02 CaseAllocated (RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-020), EV-04 CaseTransferred (RWB-E1-021), EV-16 DocumentStored (RWB-E1-024), EV-08 DecisionRecorded (RWB-E1-027) and EV-19 TimerBreached.
- The listener runs as service identity SY-CASEWF (Case record C).

1. Publishing module: commits its change and writes the event to the outbox in the same transaction.
2. Outbox: delivers the event to LedgerEventListener, in order per case.
3. LedgerEventListener: checks the schema version is the current or the previous version for the event.
4. LedgerEventMapper: maps the event to a LedgerEntryCommand: EV-01 to CASE_CREATED, EV-02 to CASE_ALLOCATED, EV-04 to CASE_TRANSFERRED, EV-19 to CASE_ESCALATED, EV-16 to DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, EV-08 to DECISION_TAKEN with the decision log entry ID.
5. LedgerEventMapper: sets actor from the event header (user ID or service identity), source system WORKBENCH, source reference as the owning module and event ID, and the event's idempotency key.
6. InteractionLedgerWriter: appends the entry with the next case_seq.
7. LedgerDuplicateService: when the idempotency key already exists, writes no entry and adds 1 to the hit count for that key (R-UNI-40).
8. Outbox: marks the event processed for the ledger consumer.
9. On failure: the outbox retries; after three retries the event goes to the exception queue with owner RW-PLATADM and incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED is raised.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The same event arrives twice with the same key | One entry; the repeat is counted | None | AC3 |
| X2 | An event with a schema version that is neither current nor previous | Not written; moved to the exception queue with owner RW-PLATADM | None (exception queue item) | AC4 |
| X3 | The ledger write fails | Retried three times, then the exception queue and an incident; the event is not discarded | MSG-P1-022 (incident detail) | AC5 |
| X4 | Events for one case arrive in written order | Entries follow that order in case_seq | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The same event reaches two consumer threads at once | One entry; one hit counted | None | AC7 |
| X6 | An event names a case that does not exist | Not written; moved to the exception queue | None (exception queue item) | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the ledger writer (RWB-E1-066) and the outbox (RWB-TE-006); the events come from stories earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The event to entry map is configuration; the story fixes the listener, the duplicate rule and the failure path |
| Valuable | The case owner sees every Workbench action in the case history |
| Estimable | One listener, one mapper, one duplicate table |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion publishes synthetic events and reads the ledger |

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **to read a case's ledger in one ordered sequence, filtered by channel, actor or date range**, so that **I can see what has happened to it before I decide anything**.

A case owner who decides a route, a settlement or a legal step must first know what was said, promised, sent and done on the case. One read interface returns the ledger in order with the source of each entry, filters it by channel, actor and date range, and masks personal content by role on the same rules as the case record. The case record view and every other consumer read through this interface, so there is one ordering and one masking rule for the history. Serves REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-003 and REQ-ILG-014; NFR-070 (one case history read in under 2 seconds at its 2031 size; DL11).

secs.t:

| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-001 (V0001); RWB-ACE-001 for the 14 Section B views (DL43) |

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the recovery module to read ACE source data only through SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, with the database grants and the build-time rule that enforce the boundary**, so that **there is one copy of source data, the Workbench cannot alter or copy it, and a direct read of an ACE table fails in the database and in the build**.

The Workbench takes no inbound source data. ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads it through 30 SELECT-only views: 16 over the ACE tables that exist today, 177 fields, and 14 over the tables RWB-ACE-001 adds, 127 fields. The views are owned by a dedicated role that holds SELECT on the ACE tables; the recovery service role holds SELECT on the views and no privilege on anything in `public`. PUBLIC holds no privilege, and no write is granted on a view. The Workbench keeps its own decisions about an ACE record in four extension tables keyed by the ACE business key, never in a copy of an ACE column.

The boundary is enforced twice: by the catalog, where a direct `public` read is refused, and by boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001, which fails the build when a recovery class names a `public` table. Serves REQ-RDF-002 (account balance, arrears, payments and classification read from ACE through `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_payment`) and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly); applies D-RCV-35 U1 and U4 and ADR-010. The measure is 100 percent of pipeline runs in which every view compiles and the conformance test passes.

- RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the recovery tables, the three helper functions `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value`, the dictionary rows and the view `v_data_dictionary`.
- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway runs in the ACE pipeline and takes the schema name from the parameter `recoverySchema`, fixed to `recovery` in every environment (D-RCV-28).
- The ACE schema in DEV and SIT is at the head that holds the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer` and `efs_action` (ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql).
- The roles `ace_view_owner` and `recovery_svc` exist in DEV and SIT, with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design. The recovery migration account holds the ACE DBA role for the release window, so it can grant on schema `public` and set a view owner (RWB-E1-044).
- The module map of RWB-TE-001 is in the repository, with `recovery-modules.yaml` read by `RecoveryBoundaryTest`.
- For the 14 Section B views only: RWB-ACE-001 is deployed in DEV and SIT and its 14 Tier 2 tables exist (DL43). Until then the features that read a Section B view stay behind their flags.

1. Recovery developer: takes Section A of `15 ACE DB Alignment/Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql` into `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql`: the 16 views, the three helper functions and the grant block. The four extension tables ship in V0001 with RWB-E1-001, which runs first; this story verifies them rather than creating them.
2. Recovery developer: writes no environment name in the file. The schema is `${recoverySchema}` and the two role names come from the Environment and Deployment Design (D-RCV-28; RWB-E1-044).
3. Pipeline: applies V0001 then V0002 in DEV, then in SIT.
4. Pipeline: runs the conformance test: 16 of 16 views compile, no constraint in `recovery` references `public`, every view has dictionary rows, and `recovery_svc` has no privilege in `public` and no write on a view.
5. Recovery developer: adds boundary rule BND-6 to `RecoveryBoundaryTest` in RWB-TE-001 and the 30 view names to `recovery-modules.yaml` as the only allowed source objects.
6. ACE team: applies RWB-ACE-001 with the 14 Tier 2 tables, and its migration grants SELECT on those tables to `ace_view_owner` (DL43).

**Source tables.** Section A reads 21 ACE tables: `account`, `payment`, `customer`, `phone`, `email`, `address`, `ca_relation`, `aa_relation`, `collateral`, `asset`, `efs_action`, `efs_action_code`, `efs_assignment`, `bucket_log_snapshot`, `product`, `branch`, `bot_holiday`, `ace_case`, `cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case`, `tdr_calculation` and `ai_recommended_plan`. **Packages and files.** Migration files in `ace-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery` (RWB-E1-044). Boundary rule in the test source of the recovery module, beside `RecoveryBoundaryTest` (RWB-TE-001). The view definitions are taken verbatim from `15 ACE DB Alignment/Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql`; the four extension tables verbatim from `06 Data/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5.sql`.

| recovery.v_ace_* | Published read interface | The only source read for every module |

**Database.** V0002 creates four tables and 16 views; V0003 creates 14 views. No table in schema `recovery` gains a foreign key into `public`, and no ACE table is altered. The extension tables are:

- `party_ext`: person_key varchar(255) primary key, vulnerable, deceased_override, bankruptcy, fraud_flag boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, state varchar(40), version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at and updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), created_by and updated_by uuid.
- `contact_point_ext`: contact_key varchar(255) primary key, contact_type varchar(10) NOT NULL, consent_given boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, consent_at and verified_at timestamptz, failed_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, source varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'WORKBENCH', is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, and the check `ck_contact_point_ext_type` that contact_type is PHONE, EMAIL or ADDRESS.
- `account_ext`: account_key varchar(255) primary key, dispute_open boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.
- `valuation_ext`: valuation_key varchar(255) primary key, accepted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, accepted_at timestamptz, accepted_by and valuer_partner_id uuid, stale_flag boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, age_days integer, is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.

**Configuration and reference data.** The roles `ace_view_owner` and `recovery_svc` and their names are fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design. The schema is `${recoverySchema}`, fixed to `recovery` (D-RCV-28). The 30-view list is frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and copied into `recovery-modules.yaml`; a change needs the data architect and the recovery tech lead. Section B features keep their own flags.

**Build steps**

1. V0002: the four extension tables, copied from Physical Schema v5 with their primary keys and the contact type check (AC7).
2. V0002: the 16 Section A views, copied from the ACE Source Views file, using the V0001 helper functions (AC1).
3. V0002: the grant block of section 12, with one GRANT and one ALTER VIEW OWNER per view and no `ALL TABLES` grant (AC2).
4. ViewConformanceTest with its four checks and a failing fixture for each (AC1 to AC5).
5. Boundary rule BND-6 in RecoveryBoundaryTest, reading `sourceViews` from the module map, with a fixture class on `public.account` and the same class on `recovery.v_ace_account` (AC8).
6. V0003: the 14 Section B views, copied from the ACE Source Views file, and one SELECT grant per view (AC3).
7. A pipeline stage for V0003 that runs only after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed; before that the stage is skipped and the Section B features stay behind their flags (AC3).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC8, including the access test on `recovery_svc` and a test role with no grant.

**Feature flag.** None for the views; they are the read path, not a feature. Each Section B feature keeps the flag it already has until V0003 is applied.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, SIT holds 30 compiling views and four extension tables, and the pipeline of main shows the conformance test and boundary rule BND-6 in its report.

secs.h: RWB-TE-001 Recovery module folder and boundary test
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-001 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-006 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 7 (constraint Modular monolith) and section 5.2 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | DL05 |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | None |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the recovery module folder and packages in the ACE repository with a build-time boundary test**, so that **no module calls the inside of another module and no recovery code calls a system of record directly**.

Three teams build in one ACE service. Without a checked boundary, a change in one team's code breaks another's, and a direct call to a core system could bypass the COLLINS and file load path. The skeleton gives each Workbench module one package with a published part and an internal part, and a test in every build refuses a call into another module's internal part, a cross-module table read and a direct system call outside the integration adapters. It meets REQ-DRI-006 and applies DT08, ADR-002 and DL05 (option B from 2 November: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package). The measure is the count of boundary violations merged to main, which must stay at zero.

- Access to the ACE repository for the TechX squads (DL36).
- DL05 is applied as option B from 2 November 2026: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package; the ACE team applies the module boundaries for the common and collection modules later.
- The common module's published packages are named in the module map. Until the ACE team names them, the map lists `..common.api..` (assumed; DL05).
- The ACE build runs the unit test phase on every pull request.

1. Squad member: creates the recovery folders and packages for the 19 Workbench modules, each with an `api` package and an `internal` package.
2. Squad member: writes the module map `architecture/recovery-modules.yaml` with each module code, its package and its published packages.
3. Squad member: writes RecoveryBoundaryTest with the rules BR1 to BR5, reading the module map.
4. Squad member: writes the front end boundary rules for `src/modules/recovery`.
5. Squad member: wires the common module access check for `/api/recovery/v1/**` through RecoveryAccessGuard.
6. Pipeline: on each pull request runs the back end tests, including RecoveryBoundaryTest, and the front end dependency check.
7. Pipeline: fails the build when a rule is broken and prints the rule, the class and the class it depends on.

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a code owners entry that maps every recovery folder to the TechX tech leads and the common module to the ACE team, with review by a code owner required before merge**, so that **every change in the recovery module is reviewed by its owners**.

The recovery and collection squads and the ACE team merge into one repository and one monthly release. Without named owners per folder, a change to the recovery module or to the common module can merge without the team that answers for it. The code owners file names the reviewing team per folder and the branch rule on main blocks a merge until that team approves. It supports REQ-DRI-006, because the integration adapter folder, the only place allowed to reach other systems, cannot change without a TechX tech lead, and it applies DL04 option A and DL37. The measure is the share of merged pull requests on recovery folders approved by a code owner, which must be 100 percent.

- RWB-TE-001 is done: the recovery folders and the module map exist.
- The repository host supports a code owners file (GitHub format assumed, as ACE uses GitHub Copilot under DL32).
- The teams exist in the repository host: TechX recovery tech leads and the ACE team. Names assumed until DL37 and DL36 are answered: `@scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads` and `@scb-ace/ace-team`.
- The repository administrator of the ACE team can set the branch rule on main.

1. Squad member: writes `.github/CODEOWNERS` with the entries in BR1 to BR5, ordered so that the most specific path is last.
2. Squad member: adds the code owners validation step to the pull request pipeline.
3. ACE team repository administrator: sets the branch rule on main: one approval from a code owner required, stale approvals dismissed on a new commit.
4. Developer: opens a pull request that changes a recovery folder.
5. Repository host: requests review from the owning team named for each changed path.
6. Pipeline: runs the validation step; an owner that does not exist or a path that matches no file fails the check.
7. Code owner: approves; the merge is allowed once every owning team of the changed paths has approved.

| X6 | The code owners file names an owner that does not exist | The validation step fails the build | Build log: owner not found | AC7 |
| X7 | A squad member who is not a code owner tries to satisfy the review | Merge refused | Repository host: review required from code owners | Access test TC-TE-002-08 |

secs.t:

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **server interfaces and front end types generated from the OpenAPI file, with a contract test and an access test per endpoint**, so that **the front end and the service never drift from the specification and no endpoint skips its access check**.

The recovery API has 79 operations specified in one OpenAPI 3.1 file. When server code, front end code and the file are kept by hand, a field renamed on one side breaks a screen in SIT, and an endpoint can ship without the capability check its specification states. Generating both sides from the file and testing every implemented operation against it in each build stops both faults before merge. It meets REQ-DRI-007, where the FSD requires every interface to have a contract test (AC-P2-001-01), and REQ-ACA-003, because each endpoint is tested against the right its specification declares from the permission matrix. The measure is the count of contract defects found in SIT, with a target of zero.

- RWB-TE-001 is done: the recovery folders and the boundary test exist; the generated packages are listed in the module map as shared.
- The API specification is held in the repository at `api/recovery-api.yaml`, base path /api/recovery/v1, with x-module, x-capability and x-first-release on every operation.
- The permission matrix seed (roles.txt, loaded as the role and permission tables by RWB-E1-037) is available to tests.
- The build property `rwb.release` names the release being built: E1 for 30 November 2026.

1. Build: lints the specification with the recovery rule set; a missing operationId, x-capability or error response fails the build.
2. Build: generates the Spring server interfaces and models from the specification.
3. Build: generates the TypeScript types and the typed client for the front end.
4. Build: compiles the service against the generated interfaces and the front end against the generated types.
5. Contract test: lists every operation with x-first-release at or before `rwb.release` and finds its implementing controller method.
6. Contract test: calls each implemented operation with its fixture and validates the request and the response against the specification.
7. Access test: calls each operation as a role whose permission lacks the declared right and expects 403 with messageCode MSG-P4-002.
8. Build: reports passed, failed and pending operations; any failure fails the build.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response no longer matches the specification | Contract test fails naming the operation and the JSON path | Build log: contract broken | AC2 |
| X2 | The specification breaks a lint rule | Build fails before generation | Build log: lint rule broken | AC3 |
| X3 | An operation returns a status not in its specification | Contract test fails | Build log: undocumented status | AC4 |
| X4 | An operation of the current release has no implementation | Build fails | Build log: operation has no implementation | AC5 |
| X5 | An operation of a later release has no implementation | Listed as pending; build passes | Build log: pending | AC6 |
| X6 | The front end uses a field removed from the specification | Front end type check fails | Build log: type error | AC7 |
| X7 | An operation answers 200 to a role without the declared right | Build fails | Build log: access not enforced | AC8 |
| X8 | A role without the right calls an operation | 403 Problem with MSG-P4-002 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-TE-003-09 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the folders of RWB-TE-001 and the specification file |
| Negotiable | Generator settings are build configuration; the rules tested come from the specification |
| Valuable | Screens and services stay in step with one file; every endpoint enforces its right |
| Estimable | Two generators, one lint rule set, one parameterized test class |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below uses one fixture operation that breaks it |

```gherkin
Feature: Types and contract tests from the API specification

 Background:
 Given the build property rwb.release is "E1"
 Given operation getCasesCaseidTimers is first in E1 with capability Case record R

 Scenario: AC1 Types generated
 Given a change to the OpenAPI file that adds property "warnAt" to schema Timer
 When the build runs
 Then the generated server model and the front end type for Timer both hold "warnAt"
 Then the service and the front end compile against them

 Scenario: AC2 Contract broken
 Given the implementation of getCasesCaseidTimers returns "escalationLevel" as the text "two"
 When the contract tests run
 Then the build fails

 Scenario: AC3 The specification is checked before generation
 Given an operation in the file with no x-capability
 When the build runs
 Then it fails at the lint step naming the operation

 Given the implementation of getCasesCaseidTimers returns 400 for an unknown case
 Given the specification lists 200, 401, 403, 404 and 503 only
```

As a **Tribe lead and squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **masked copies of recovery data loaded into SIT and UAT from the PII service**, so that **tests run on realistic volumes without exposing customers**.

SIT and UAT must show that loads, allocation, reconciliation and reports work at production volume and with production data shapes, which synthetic data does not prove. NFR-045 allows masked copies in user acceptance and forbids production data in development. The bank's PII service produces the masked copy under the Compliance masking rules; this story loads it into SIT and UAT only, refuses any copy that still holds a personal value, and keeps dates, keys and row counts unchanged so counts and reconciliations behave as in production. Serves REQ-RDF-010 and REQ-ACA-005; decision DL26 sets the masking rules.

- RWB-E1-065 is done: the generator's personal data pattern checks and the sys_fields is_personal tags are available to the loader.
- The PII service delivers a masked extract per environment to the SIT or UAT intake container, with a manifest: extract ID, business date, masking rule version, row count per table.
- The masking rule version in force is held in the masking rules reference table (DL26; until Compliance supplies the rules, every is_personal field is replaced by a token).
- The SIT and UAT databases hold the recovery schema at the same Flyway version as the extract.
- The platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) starts the load; squad members hold RW-TRIBE.

1. PII service: writes the masked extract files and the manifest to the intake container of SIT or UAT.
2. Platform administrator: starts the masked copy load in the pipeline for the target environment.
3. MaskedCopyLoader: refuses to run when the target environment is DEV or PROD.
4. MaskedCopyLoader: checks the manifest: extract ID not loaded before, masking rule version equal to the version in force, schema version equal to the target.
5. MaskedCopyLoader: runs the load checks of CTL-02 on each file: business date, structure, control totals (row count per table), keys.
6. MaskingVerifier: scans every column tagged is_personal for values that look personal: a 13-digit number with a valid Thai national ID check digit, a Thai mobile number or an email address.
7. MaskedCopyLoader: loads the files into a staging schema, checks foreign keys resolve, and swaps the staging schema for the live one in one step.
8. MaskedCopyLoader: writes the load report: extract ID, business date, masking rule version, rows per table, check results.
9. Squad member: runs SIT or UAT tests on the masked copy.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A personal column holds a value that looks personal | Load refused in full; previous copy stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | Row count differs from the manifest | Load refused in full; previous copy stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC3 |
| X3 | The target environment is DEV or PROD | Load refused before reading any file | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | The same extract ID is loaded again | Load skipped; report shows the earlier load | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The manifest's masking rule version is not the version in force | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | A second load starts while one runs | Second start refused | MSG-P2-006 | AC7 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the personal data checks from RWB-E1-065 and the PII service extract; no screen |
| Negotiable | Masking rules belong to Compliance (DL26); the story fixes the checks and the load |
| Valuable | SIT and UAT run at production volume with no customer data exposed |
| Estimable | One loader, one verifier, one pipeline stage |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a test extract with a manifest |

```gherkin
Feature: Masked data in SIT and UAT

 Background:
 Given masking rule version "MASK-2026.11" is in force
 Given extract "PII-SIT-20261120" for business date 2026-11-19 has a manifest with masking rule version "MASK-2026.11"
 Given the manifest lists 28,119 case accounts: Mortgage 12,256, Hire purchase 12,960 and SSME 2,903, with row counts per product

 Scenario: AC1 Masked copy
```

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **a harness that runs each rule row against its test case (the state, the event, the case facts and the expected result)**, so that **a rule change is tested the same way as code before it takes effect**.

The routing logic is 448 rules in ten route sets, held as data (ADR-004). A wrong condition or owner in one row moves every case that reaches it, and the bank has no test that proves a row does what its owner expects. Every rule row already names a test case (`rule_row.test_case_id`). This story runs those test cases on every rule load and in every build, and marks a version failed when any test fails. It meets REQ-CWC-014 and REQ-CWC-013. The measure is that every rule row in force has a passing test with its rule ID.

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with the parameterized schema.
- The rules component evaluates a route set as a decision table with hit policy Unique (ADR-004).
- The rule load template (RWB-E1-029) carries a Tests sheet with one test case per rule row.
- Rule rows exist with a `test_case_id` for each row (DF-REF-015, required).
- The Restructure route set is loaded in SIT with its 37 rows, R-RES-01 to R-RES-37.
- The loader holds RW-COE (Rules and parameters C).

1. Center of excellence analyst: loads a rule version through `POST /admin/rule-versions` with the rules and the Tests sheet.
2. P4 load handler: stores the rule rows and calls `RuleTableHarness.run(routeSet, ruleVersion)`.
3. Harness: reads the rule rows of the version and their test cases.
4. Harness: for each test case, builds a synthetic case file from the facts, evaluates the route set for the from state and the event, and gets the rows that hit.
5. Harness: passes the test when exactly one row hits, it is the row named by the test, and its to state, owner role and timer equal the expected values.
6. Harness: returns one result per rule ID; the load handler sets the version state to VALIDATED when every test passes, or FAILED otherwise, and writes the test result for the change log (RWB-E1-048).
7. Build pipeline: runs the same harness as a JUnit dynamic test per rule ID over the rule files in the repository.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A row's to state, owner or timer differs from its test | The test fails; the version is marked FAILED | MSG-P3-014 | AC2 |
| X2 | A rule row has no test case in the Tests sheet | The version is marked FAILED naming the rule | MSG-P3-014 | AC3 |
| X3 | Two rows hit the same test input | The test fails naming both rule IDs | MSG-P3-014 | AC4 |
| X4 | No row hits a test input | The test fails naming the expected rule | MSG-P3-014 | AC5 |
| X5 | A test names a fact the condition does not use, or a fact is missing | The test fails naming the fact | MSG-P3-014 | AC6 |
| X6 | The same version is run twice | The same results; no second result row | None | AC7 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the rule rows and the evaluator; the load endpoint calls it |
| Negotiable | The report format can change; the pass rule is fixed |
| Valuable | A rule change cannot take effect with a row that fails its own test |
| Estimable | One harness service, one test runner, one test case table |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | The harness tests itself with fixture route sets |

```gherkin

 Background:

 Given a Tests sheet with one test case per row

 Then 37 tests run

 When the harness runs
 Then the system marks the version "FAILED" with MSG-P3-014 naming "R-RES-12" and "RT-RES-012"
```

secs.h: RWB-TE-006 Outbox and retry for outbound work
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-TE-006 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P2 Integration |
| Feature | None |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-DRI-007 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 5.2 and section 6.4 |
| L3 process | All recovery processes |
| Decision | None |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-044, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-007 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **every application event and every outbound work request written to an outbox in the same transaction as the change, and delivered to each consumer in order with retry**, so that **no outbound action is lost when a system or a consumer is down, and nothing is sent for a change that did not commit**.

The Workbench modules talk to each other through application events, and outbound work such as a notice for WIN starts from an event in the module that approved it. If the event is sent before the change commits, or is lost when a consumer fails, a notice is never dispatched or a ledger entry is missing, and nobody sees it. The outbox stores each event with the change, a sender delivers it to every consumer at least once in case order, retries on a schedule held as data, and moves a delivery that keeps failing to the exception queue with a task. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (retry on a defined schedule; exception queue with a task for a named owner) and NFR-025 and NFR-026. The measure is the count of outbox deliveries in the exception queue over one day, with a target of zero (FSD P2 A2.1.1).

- RWB-E1-044 (versioned migrations), RWB-E1-027 (decision log writer) and RWB-E1-007 (integration adapters, IdempotencyGuard and the outbound file sender) are done.
- The consumer list is loaded in the configuration service (RWB-E1-042) under rwb.integration.outbox.consumers: consumer name, the event types it takes, its owner role, and whether it holds a case step (for example the consumer "win-dispatch" of the work request WIN_DISPATCH holds the case step, owner role RW-PLATADM; assumed).
- The retry settings are loaded under rwb.integration.outbox.retry: 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes after the previous attempt (assumed; NFR-026, DL11).
- Quartz runs clustered in the ACE service; JOB-11 Outbox sender runs every minute.
- Feature flag `rwb.integration.outbox` is on.

1. Business service (for example notice approval): calls OutboxWriter.publish inside its own transaction with the event type (an event from EV-01 to EV-28, or an outbound work request type such as WIN_DISPATCH), schema version, case ID, payload references, actor and idempotency key.
2. OutboxWriter: writes one outbox_event row with the next case sequence, and one outbox_delivery row per consumer listed for the event type.
3. Database: commits the change, the event and its deliveries together, or none of them.
4. JOB-11 Outbox sender (event step): every minute selects due deliveries with a row lock that skips rows another instance holds, oldest case sequence first, taking only the lowest open sequence per case and consumer.
5. OutboxSender: calls the consumer with the event header (event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time, actor) and payload; each consumer checks the key through IdempotencyGuard (RWB-E1-007) before it acts.
6. OutboxSender: on success marks the delivery DELIVERED; when the delivery had failed before and the consumer holds a case step, raises RETRY_SUCCEEDED for the case (R-UNI-35).
7. OutboxSender: on a failure adds 1 to the attempt count and sets the next attempt from the retry settings; on the first failure of a consumer that holds a case step, raises SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE for the case (R-UNI-33).
8. OutboxSender: when the retries are used, sets the delivery to EXCEPTION, raises task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY for the consumer's owner role on the case and, for a consumer that holds a case step, raises RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED (R-UNI-36), which writes the decision log entry; all in one transaction.
9. Platform administrator: reads exception deliveries (GET /admin/outbox/deliveries) and, once the consumer is fixed, sends one again (POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend).

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The business transaction rolls back | No event and no delivery exist | None | AC3 |
| X2 | A consumer fails once and then succeeds | Delivery DELIVERED on the retry; the case resumes when the consumer holds a case step (R-UNI-35) | None | AC4 |
| X3 | The same idempotency key is published twice | One event exists | None | AC5 |
| X4 | Two service instances run the sender at once | Each delivery is made once | None | AC6 |
| X5 | An earlier event for the same case and consumer is failing | Later events for that case and consumer wait | None | AC7 |
| X6 | One consumer fails and another succeeds on the same event | Each consumer's delivery has its own state | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A platform administrator sends a delivery that is not in EXCEPTION | Refused with 409 | MSG-P2-022 | AC9 |
| X8 | An event with no case fails past its limit | EXCEPTION and an alert to the platform administrator; no task, no case event | MSG-P2-001 | AC10 |
| X9 | The retry settings are changed | The next attempt uses the new delays | None | AC11 |
| X10 | The decision log cannot be written when the limit is reached | Nothing changes; the delivery stays RETRYING and is tried at the next run; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | Principle 5 test TC-TE-006-13 |
| X11 | A role without Platform administration U sends a delivery again | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-TE-006-12 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the migration tool, the decision log writer and the IdempotencyGuard of Epic 1; consumers are listed in configuration |
| Negotiable | Consumers, owners, retry counts and delays are configuration |
| Valuable | No event or outbound request is lost or sent for a change that rolled back |
| Estimable | Two tables, one writer, one sender step, two admin endpoints |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below uses a stub consumer that fails on demand |

```gherkin
Feature: Outbox and retry for outbound work

 Background:
 Given consumer "win-dispatch" takes work request WIN_DISPATCH, holds the case step and has owner role RW-PLATADM
 Given consumers "ledger" and "reporting-feed" take CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred and CaseStateChanged, do not hold the case step and have owner role RW-PLATADM
 Given the retry settings are 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes after the previous attempt
 Given case "RW-2026-000601" has notice "NT-SYN-0601" waiting for approval

 Scenario: AC1 Sent after commit
 Given a notice approved
 When the transaction commits at 14 December 2026 10:00:00
 Then the outbox holds one WIN_DISPATCH request for case "RW-2026-000601" with one delivery for "win-dispatch"
 Then the header holds the event ID, idempotency key "WIN_DISPATCH:NT-SYN-0601", schema version 1, occurred time and actor
 Then the payload holds notice and case references only, with no name, address or identifier
 Then at the 10:01 run the sender delivers it and "win-dispatch" passes the notice to OutboundFiles.enqueue for the day's WIN file
 Then the delivery has status DELIVERED

 Scenario: AC2 Retry limit
 Given a target down for longer than the retry limit
 When "win-dispatch" fails at 10:01, 10:02, 10:07 and 10:22
 Then the system makes no fifth attempt
 Then the item moves to the exception queue: the "win-dispatch" delivery has status EXCEPTION and attempt count 4
 Then the system raises task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY on case "RW-2026-000601" for role RW-PLATADM
 Then event RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED moves the case to EXCEPTION_QUEUE by R-UNI-36 with one decision log entry

 Scenario: AC3 Nothing is sent for a change that did not commit
 Given the notice approval fails after OutboxWriter.publish and the transaction rolls back
 When the sender runs
 Then no event and no delivery exist for "NT-SYN-0601"

 Scenario: AC4 A retry that succeeds
 Given "win-dispatch" fails at 10:01 and the case moves to RETRY_QUEUE by R-UNI-33
 When the attempt at 10:02 succeeds
 Then the system delivers the delivery status with attempt count 2
 Then event RETRY_SUCCEEDED returns the case to the state it paused in by R-UNI-35

 Scenario: AC5 The same event is written once
 Given the approval of "NT-SYN-0601" is submitted twice with idempotency key "WIN_DISPATCH:NT-SYN-0601"
 When both transactions commit
 Then the outbox holds one event with that key
 Then the second transaction receives DuplicateOutboxKeyException and changes nothing

 Scenario: AC6 Two sender instances
 Given 200 due deliveries and two service instances
 When JOB-11 runs on both at 10:01
 Then the system makes each delivery once
 Then the delivery log holds 200 calls

 Scenario: AC7 Order per case and consumer
 Given event CaseTransferred with case sequence 11 and event CaseStateChanged with case sequence 12 for case "RW-2026-000601"
 Given the "ledger" consumer fails on sequence 11
 When the sender runs
 Then the system does not deliver sequence 12 to "ledger" until sequence 11 is DELIVERED

 Scenario: AC8 Consumers are independent
 Given event CaseAllocated for case "RW-2026-000601"
 When "ledger" fails and "reporting-feed" succeeds at 10:01
 Then the system delivers the "reporting-feed" delivery and the "ledger" delivery is RETRYING with next attempt 10:02
 Then the case route state does not change, because "ledger" does not hold the case step

 Scenario: AC9 Sending an exception delivery again
 Given delivery "OBD-SYN-0001" has status EXCEPTION
 When the platform administrator sends it again
 Then the response is 200 with message MSG-GEN-005
 Then the delivery status is PENDING with attempt count 0 and due at the next run
 When the platform administrator sends delivery "OBD-SYN-0002" with status DELIVERED again
 Then the response is 409 with message MSG-P2-022

 Scenario: AC10 An event with no case
 Given an event with no case whose only consumer fails 4 times
 When the retries are used
 Then the delivery status is EXCEPTION
 Then the system sends an alert to the platform administrator within 15 minutes
 Then no task and no case event are raised

 Scenario: AC11 Retry settings come from configuration
 Given the retry delays are changed in the configuration service to 2, 10 and 30 minutes at 09:00
 When "ledger" fails at 10:01
 Then the next attempt is due at 10:03
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An event and its deliveries are written in the same transaction as the change: no event without the change and no change without the event | events.txt Rules, Transactions |
| BR2 | Each event carries an event ID and an idempotency key unique in the outbox; consumers drop a repeat through IdempotencyGuard | events.txt Rules, Duplicates; R-UNI-40 |
| BR3 | Delivery is at least once; each consumer has its own delivery state | events.txt Rules, Delivery |
| BR4 | Events for one case reach each consumer in the order they were written | events.txt Rules, Ordering |
| BR5 | A failed delivery is retried on the schedule; after the last retry it moves to the exception queue with a task for the consumer's owner role | events.txt Rules, Failure; NFR-026; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR6 | For a consumer that holds a case step, the first failure raises SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, a later success RETRY_SUCCEEDED, and the limit RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED | R-UNI-33; R-UNI-35; R-UNI-36 |
| BR7 | Payloads hold references and codes, never personal data; the event carries its schema version | events.txt Rules, Payload and Versioning |
| BR8 | The move to the exception queue for a case does not happen unless its decision log entry is written | R-UNI-39; Principle 5; CTL-06 |
| BR9 | Consumers, owners, retry counts and delays are read from configuration | Principle 1; DL11 |

Case status does not change. For a consumer that holds a case step, the route state changes through the universal rules; each delivery has its own status.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE | SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE | First failed delivery to a consumer that holds the case step | RETRY_QUEUE (R-UNI-33) |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_SUCCEEDED | The retry succeeds | RESUME_STATE (R-UNI-35) |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED | Retries used | EXCEPTION_QUEUE (R-UNI-36) |
| Delivery PENDING or RETRYING | Consumer succeeds | None | Delivery DELIVERED |
| Delivery PENDING | Consumer fails | Retries left | Delivery RETRYING |
| Delivery RETRYING | Consumer fails | No retries left | Delivery EXCEPTION |
| Delivery EXCEPTION | Sent again by the platform administrator | None | Delivery PENDING |

**Published interfaces**

```java
// recovery.integration.api; joins the caller's transaction
UUID OutboxWriter.publish(OutboxEvent event);
// OutboxEvent: eventType (EV-01 to EV-28 names, or a work request type such as WIN_DISPATCH), schemaVersion, caseId (nullable), payload (references only), actorRef, idempotencyKey
// throws DuplicateOutboxKeyException when the key exists
// Implemented by each consumer and listed under its consumer name
ConsumeResult OutboxConsumer.consume(EventHeader header, JsonNode payload); // OK or FAILED(code)
// P3 interfaces used on failure and recovery

UUID TaskApi.raiseTask(UUID caseId, String taskCode, String ownerRole);

boolean IdempotencyGuard.firstTime(String consumer, String idempotencyKey);
```

**Job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | JOB-11 Outbox sender, every minute; this story adds the event step beside the outbound file step of RWB-E1-007 |
| Input | outbox_delivery rows with status PENDING or RETRYING and next_attempt_at at or before now |
| Output | Deliveries DELIVERED, RETRYING or EXCEPTION; case events; tasks; alerts |
| Events published | None of its own; it delivers EV-01 to EV-28 to their consumers |
| Idempotency key | outbox_event.idempotency_key, passed to each consumer in the header |
| Restart | Rows are locked per delivery with skip-locked selection; a delivery in flight when an instance stops is retried at its next attempt time and the consumer drops the repeat by its key |

**Package.** Folder `recovery/integration/outbox`, Java package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.outbox`; OutboxWriter and OutboxConsumer in `recovery.integration.api`.

**Components**

| OutboxEventEntity, OutboxDeliveryEntity | Entity | The two new rows |

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the timer check, the morning allocation run and the daily reconciliation run as Quartz jobs with a run book each**, so that **scheduled work runs once, on time and visibly, and a missed run is caught up for its business date**.

The morning allocation must finish by 07:00 so no new case waits for a person (JOB-03), the timer check must find every due timer every 5 minutes (JOB-05), and the reconciliation must compare the case list with the core bank every day (JOB-04). The ACE service runs on more than one instance, so without a shared schedule a job runs twice or not at all, and an outage loses a day's run. This story runs the three jobs on the clustered ACE Quartz scheduler with one run per business date, catch-up after an outage and a run book for each. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-011 and REQ-RDF-007. The measure is one successful run per job per business date, and JOB-03 complete by 07:00 (NFR-013).

- RWB-E1-044 is done: migrations run with the parameterized schema.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: the job monitor records runs and alerts the operations channel.
- The ACE Quartz scheduler runs with a clustered JDBC job store; its `QRTZ_` tables belong to the ACE common module.
- JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake publishes LoadCompleted (EV-26) with the business date; JOB-02 Case creation records its run per business date.
- The job bodies exist: allocation (RWB-E1-020), reconciliation (RWB-E1-011) and timer check (RWB-E1-028).
- `jobs.catch-up.max-dates` = 5 (assumed; DL11) and the 07:00 deadline for JOB-03 (NFR-013) are in the configuration service.

1. Scheduler: on LoadCompleted for business date D, and on completion of JOB-02 for D, fires JOB-03 Morning allocation and JOB-04 Daily reconciliation for D.
2. Scheduler: fires JOB-05 Timer check every 5 minutes on cron `0 0/5 * * * ?` in Asia/Bangkok.
3. Job runner: takes the cluster lock so only one instance runs a job at a time.
4. Job runner: checks the job run log for job and business date; if a successful run exists, records the skip and stops.
5. Job runner: checks the job's dependency (JOB-02 succeeded for D); if not met, records WAITING and stops.
6. Job runner: records the run start through the P1 job monitor, runs the job body, records the end with status SUCCEEDED or FAILED and the counts.
7. Job runner: on service start, for each business date of a passed COLLINS load with no successful run of JOB-03 or JOB-04, runs the job for that date in date order, up to `jobs.catch-up.max-dates` dates.
8. Deadline watcher: at 07:00 checks JOB-03 for the current business date; if it has not succeeded, alerts the operations channel.
9. Platform administrator: reads runs on SCR-44 and reruns a failed run through `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun`.

As an **internal auditor (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **a nightly job that recomputes the whole decision log hash chain, records the result with the last hash, and reports a break to Compliance the same day**, so that **a changed entry is found the day it happens and the log can be relied on in audit**.

The decision log is evidence only while nobody can change an entry unseen. The database refuses updates and deletes (RWB-E1-008), but a change made outside the service, for example by a database administrator, is found only by recomputing the chain. This story runs that check as JOB-14 every night after the decision log copy, records each run with its last hash, and tells Compliance of a break, an incomplete run or an intact chain. It meets REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 and supports control CTL-06. The measure is a daily check with a same-day report: target 100 percent of nights.

- RWB-E1-008 is done: HashChainVerifier, CanonicalEntryForm and ChainBreakNotifier exist.
- RWB-TE-007 is done: jobs run on Quartz in the ACE service with job run records shown by GET /admin/jobs.
- JOB-13 Decision log copy is scheduled nightly at 01:00 (RWB-E1-014).
- Parameters in the catalog: rwb.decision.chaincheck.start=02:00, rwb.decision.chaincheck.latest-start=04:00, rwb.decision.chaincheck.batch-size=1000, all Asia/Bangkok (assumed; owner RW-COMPLY).
- The Compliance and PDPA officer group and the platform administrator group are set in the ACE notification path.

1. Quartz: fires JOB-14 at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok for the business date of the previous day.
2. Job (HashChainCheckJob): checks that JOB-13 for the same business date has ended; if not, waits and checks again every 5 minutes until 04:00, then runs and records that JOB-13 had not ended.
3. Job: reads the highest chain_seq at the start and fixes it as the end of the run; entries appended later are checked the next night.
4. Job: calls HashChainVerifier over chain_seq 1 to the end in batches of 1,000, recomputing each entry_hash and checking each prev_hash.
5. Job: counts every entry that fails and keeps the first.
6. Job: writes the job run record with type JOB-14, business date, status and checks: entries checked, last chain_seq, last entry_hash, result, first break chain_seq and entry ID, failing count.
7. Job: sends MSG-P7-007 to Compliance when the chain is intact, or MSG-P7-008 with an incident when it is broken.
8. Job: on an error that stops the run, records status FAILED, alerts the platform administrator and sends MSG-P7-013 to Compliance.
9. Platform administrator: can rerun the job for the business date from the job monitor; a rerun is a new run record.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An entry does not match its hash or its prev_hash | Run result BROKEN; first break and failing count recorded; incident; Compliance told | MSG-P7-008 | AC2, AC7 |
| X2 | The run stops on an error, for example a lost database connection | Status FAILED; platform administrator alerted; Compliance told the check did not complete | MSG-P7-013 | AC3 |
| X3 | The job is rerun for the same business date | A new run record with the same checks; the report says it is a rerun; no second scheduled run starts | MSG-P7-007 or MSG-P7-008 | AC4 |
| X4 | The log is empty | Result INTACT with count 0 and the genesis hash | MSG-P7-007 | AC5 |
| X5 | JOB-13 has not ended at 02:00 | The job waits up to 04:00, then runs and records the late copy | MSG-P7-007 or MSG-P7-008 | AC6 |
| X6 | Entries are appended while the job runs | They are outside this run and are checked the next night | None | AC8 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the verifier from RWB-E1-008 and the scheduler from RWB-TE-007 |
| Negotiable | Start times and batch size are parameters |
| Valuable | A changed entry is found by the morning after it is changed |
| Estimable | One Quartz job, one report, no screen |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Decision log hash chain check

 Background:
 Given the environment is SIT with the synthetic decision log
 Given JOB-13 for business date 2 December 2026 ended at 01:40 on 3 December 2026

 Scenario: AC1 Chain intact
 Given the decision log holds 48,210 entries and none has been changed
 When JOB-14 runs at 02:00 on 3 December 2026
 Then the job run record shows type "JOB-14", business date 2 December 2026, status "COMPLETED" and result "INTACT"
 Then its checks hold entries checked 48,210, last chain_seq 48,210 and that entry's entry_hash
 Then MSG-P7-007 with the count and the last hash is sent to the Compliance group

 Scenario: AC2 Break
 Given the actions of the entry with chain_seq 30,005 were changed in the SIT database with the trigger disabled
 When JOB-14 runs
 Then the run result is "BROKEN" with first break chain_seq 30,005 and its entry ID
 Then the system raises an incident and MSG-P7-008 with the entry ID is sent to the Compliance group before 08:00 on 3 December 2026

 Scenario: AC3 A run that stops is reported
 Given the database connection is closed in the test double after 20,000 entries
 When JOB-14 runs
 Then the run status is "FAILED" with entries checked 20,000
 Then the system alerts the platform administrator group
 Then the system sends MSG-P7-013 to the Compliance group with the date of the last complete check, 2 December 2026

 Scenario: AC4 A rerun gives a new record and no second scheduled run
 Given JOB-14 for business date 2 December 2026 failed at 02:20
 When test user "U-9301" holding RW-PLATADM reruns it from the job monitor at 08:30
 Then a second run record for business date 2 December 2026 is written with rerun true
 Then the system marks the report to Compliance as a rerun
 Then while the rerun is running a second start of JOB-14 is refused by the scheduler

 Scenario: AC5 An empty log is intact
 Given the decision log holds no entry
 When JOB-14 runs
 Then the result is "INTACT" with entries checked 0 and last hash of 64 zeros

 Scenario: AC6 The job waits for the decision log copy
 Given JOB-13 for business date 2 December 2026 is still running at 02:00 and ends at 02:25
 When JOB-14 fires at 02:00
 Then it starts the check at 02:25 and records the JOB-13 end time
 Then if JOB-13 has not ended by 04:00 the check starts at 04:00 with the note "JOB-13 not ended"

 Scenario: AC7 Several changed entries
 Given the entries with chain_seq 12,001 and 40,350 were changed in the SIT database
 When JOB-14 runs
 Then the first break is chain_seq 12,001 and the failing count is 2
 Then one incident and one MSG-P7-008 report name both entry IDs

 Scenario: AC8 Entries written during the run
 Given the log holds 48,210 entries when JOB-14 starts
 Given 37 entries are appended while it runs
 When the run ends
 Then entries checked is 48,210 and last chain_seq is 48,210
 Then the next night's run checks 48,247 entries
```
