secs.h: RWB-E2-030 Legal document agent in shadow on Epic 1 data [E3c]
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E2-030 |
| Epic | E3, release 31 January 2027 |
| Module | P10 Agent runtime |
| Feature | FEAT-AGT-09 Run the legal document agent in shadow |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-S4-002 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Program, section 5.11 |
| L3 process | 8.2 Instruct and file |
| Decision | D7.2 |
| Priority | Should |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-058, RWB-E2-025, RWB-E1-061 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the legal document agent to assemble litigation packs and completeness lists in shadow on real Epic 1 cases, scored against the packs the legal officers built**, so that **the agent goes to Epic 5 with a known accuracy per pack item**.

A litigation pack that reaches the law firm with a missing or defective document is returned, and the filing waits. From Epic 5 the legal document agent assembles the pack and checks it against the defect list before the officer verifies it (R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, CTL-19). This story runs the agent in shadow on 50 cases whose packs the officers have already built, scores agreement per checklist item, and records the decision to promote or keep it in shadow as a policy version. It serves REQ-S4-002: a pack assembled and checked against the document checklist, with missing documents named.

- RWB-E1-058 is done: platform, sample loader and evaluation harness.
- RWB-E2-025 is done: court filings, hearing notices, judgments, contracts and mortgage documents are classified and their fields extracted.
- RWB-E1-061 is done: the policy loader checks a promotion proposal against its evaluation.
- The document checklist per case type is loaded as reference data (RWB-E1-040).
- Approved policy "LEGAL_DOC" version "P1": mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, allowed tools read_case, read_legal_actions, read_documents, read_document_fields, read_checklist; output schema "legal-pack-v1".
- Sample "LEGAL-S1" version 1: for 50 Epic 1 litigation cases, the officers' pack, one row per case and checklist item with expected status PRESENT, MISSING or DEFECT.

1. RW-COE: loads sample "LEGAL-S1" and starts the evaluation of "LEGAL_DOC" through POST /admin/agent-evaluations.
2. System: for each sample case, runs the agent in shadow: reads the case, the legal action, the documents with their fields and the checklist for the case type.
3. System: checks the answer: every checklist item has a status, every document ID belongs to the case, and every DEFECT has a reason.
4. System: stores the pack (document IDs per item) and the completeness list on the agent run; nothing is shown to a user and no document, pack or legal action changes.
5. System: scores agreement with the officers' pack per checklist item and stores it with sample size.
6. RW-COE: reads the scores and loads policy version "P2": mode L1 with conditions to promote, or mode SHADOW with a review date to keep shadow.
7. RW-RISK: approves the version; the decision and its date are recorded on the policy row.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The agent names a document that belongs to another case | Check SCHEMA_RULE fails; run GUARDRAIL_FAILED; scored as wrong for every item | None to a user | AC4 |
| X2 | A checklist item has no status in the answer | Check SCHEMA fails | None to a user | AC5 |
| X3 | The document interface is unavailable during a run | Run status TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, fallback true; the case is scored as not run and listed (R-UNI-33) | None to a user | AC6 |
| X4 | Fewer than 50 scored cases | A promotion to L1 is refused; keeping shadow is allowed | MSG-P10-001 | AC7 |
| X5 | Keep shadow without a review date | Load refused | MSG-P10-001 | AC8 |
| X6 | The loader approves their own decision | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC9 |
| X7 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-030-10 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the platform and harness; reads S4 and P5 data through their interfaces; no S4 workflow is needed |
| Negotiable | Checklist items come from reference data; the minimum sample and conditions are policy values |
| Valuable | Gives the item accuracy that decides whether the agent assembles packs in Epic 5 |
| Estimable | One prompt, one output schema, one scorer, one proposal |
| Small | One developer and one litigation officer for review |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on fixture cases with known officer packs |

```gherkin
Feature: Legal document agent in shadow on Epic 1 data [E3c]

 Background:
 Given policy "LEGAL_DOC" version "P1" with mode "SHADOW" and prompt "PR1"
 Given the checklist for case type "MORTGAGE_CIVIL" has 9 items including "LOAN_CONTRACT", "MORTGAGE_DEED" and "DEMAND_NOTICE_PROOF"

 Scenario: AC1 Shadow pack
 Given litigation case "RW-2026-000901" with 14 documents and an open legal action
 When the agent runs
 Then a pack listing document IDs for each of the 9 items and a completeness list with PRESENT, MISSING or DEFECT per item are stored on the agent run
 Then no document, legal action, task or case field changes
 Then no user-facing endpoint returns the pack

 Scenario: AC2 Scored
 Given 50 shadow packs for sample "LEGAL-S1" version 1
 When the evaluation runs
 Then the system stores agreement with the officers' packs per item with sample size 50
 Then for "DEMAND_NOTICE_PROOF" with 46 agreeing cases the agreement rate is 0.9200

 Scenario: AC3 Promotion proposal
 Given the score
 When RW-COE loads policy "LEGAL_DOC" version "P2" with mode "SHADOW", review date 2027-03-15 and the evaluation run ID, and RW-RISK approves it
 Then the system records the decision to keep shadow on version "P2" with the approver and the approval date
 Then the system accepts a proposal with mode "L1" only when every stated condition is met by the evaluation

 Scenario: AC4 A document from another case
 Given the model stub names document "D-7001" of case "RW-2026-000902" in the pack of case "RW-2026-000901"
 When the guardrail runs
 Then the run holds status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" and check "SCHEMA_RULE"

 Scenario: AC5 An item without a status
 Given the answer has no status for item "MORTGAGE_DEED"
 When the guardrail runs
 Then the run holds status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" and check "SCHEMA"

 Scenario: AC6 The document interface is down
 Given the P5 document interface is unavailable for case "RW-2026-000903"
 When the agent runs
 Then the run holds status "TOOL_UNAVAILABLE" and fallback true
 Then the evaluation lists the case as not run and scores 49 cases

 Scenario: AC7 Too few cases to promote
 Given the evaluation scored 49 cases
 When RW-COE loads a proposal with mode "L1"
 Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming check "sample size at least 50"

 Scenario: AC8 Keep shadow without a review date
 When RW-COE loads version "P2" with mode "SHADOW" and no review date
 Then the system refuses the load with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming check "review date present"

 Scenario: AC9 The loader cannot approve
 Given user "coe.user01" loaded version "P2"
 When user "coe.user01" approves it
 Then the system refuses the approval with 409 and MSG-P7-002
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | In SHADOW mode the pack and completeness list are stored only; no pack, document or legal action changes | agent_policy.autonomy_mode (New) |
| BR2 | Checklist items come from the document checklist for the case type | Reference table document checklist; REQ-DCM-011 |
| BR3 | Every item has a status PRESENT, MISSING or DEFECT, and every DEFECT has a reason | R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17; CTL-19 |
| BR4 | A pack may name only documents of the same case | CTL-19; CTL-11 |
| BR5 | Agreement per item = cases where the agent status equals the officer status / scored cases, 4 decimals | agent_evaluation.agreement_rate (New) |
| BR6 | A promotion to L1 needs at least 50 scored cases (assumed); keeping shadow needs a review date | agent_policy.review_date (New) |
| BR7 | The loader and the approver are different people | Separation of duty, center of excellence analyst and risk and model risk officer |

secs.h: Recovery Workbench user stories, Epics 3 to 8
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Epic | Stories | Status |
|---|---|---|
| E3 | 31 | Ready for refinement |
| E4 | 50 | Draft; refined one epic ahead |
| E5 | 26 | Draft; refined one epic ahead |
| E6 | 37 | Draft; refined one epic ahead |
| E7 | 18 | Draft; refined one epic ahead |
| E8 | 19 | Draft; refined one epic ahead |

One story per feature in the Epic 3 to 8 scope. Each carries its acceptance criteria, data, endpoints, screens, permission checks, messages and test cases. The squads size each story when it is refined; dependencies name features until the story keys are set.

Re-based in this version on the ACE database (D-RCV-35, ADR-010, DL43). The Workbench takes no inbound source data: ACE ingests it, and these stories read it through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views. Six stories were rewritten on the read path: RWB-E3-010, RWB-E3-017, RWB-E4-002, RWB-E4-006, RWB-E4-046 and RWB-E4-050. 154 more changed only their data rows, where a Workbench copy table becomes the view that now serves it and a key column becomes the ACE business key (account_key, person_key, asset_key, payment_code). The 21 that name no source entity are unchanged. Every entity in a Data table is a table in Physical Schema v5 or one of the 30 views, and every BR Field ID is one in Logical Data Model v7.

---

secs.h: RWB-E4-001 Order an appraisal when the last one is stale
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic | E4, release 28 February 2027 |
| Module | S1 Valuation and route |
| Feature | FEAT-VAL-01 Order an appraisal when the last one is stale |
| Process | See module |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | FEAT-RDF-06 |
| Decision | None |

**Story.** As a case owner, I want the Workbench to check the appraisal age against the limit and raise the order to SVAF with no person involved, so that the route is chosen on expected return with reasons.

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Order an appraisal when the last one is stale

 Scenario: AC1 Order an appraisal when the last one is stale
 Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
 When its trigger arrives
 Then checks the appraisal age against the limit and raises the order to SVAF with no person involved
 Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

 Scenario: AC2 Not recorded
 Given the decision log cannot be written
 When the action is taken
 Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Data**

| Entity | Fields | BR Field IDs |
|---|---|---|
| v_ace_valuation | valuation_key, asset_key, appraisal_no, appraisal_type, appraised_value, appraisal_date and 3 more | DF-ACE-187 to DF-ACE-195 |
| valuation_ext | valuation_key, accepted, accepted_at, accepted_by, stale_flag, age_days and 8 more | DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049 |
| decision_log_entry | id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version and 12 more | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 |
| rule_row | id, rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 9 more | DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 |

**Endpoints**

| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route | Treatment and offer U |

**Screen and states**

| Screen | States |
|---|---|
| SCR-13 Route decision | Loading; recommendation; overridden; submitted |

**Permission checks**

| Capability area | Right | Roles that hold it |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment and offer | U | RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-GUARANT |

**Validation and messages**

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|

| Process | See module |
| Priority | Must |

| Decision | None |

**Story.** As a case owner, I want the Workbench to tell CCMS to release the security once the settlement has cleared, and record the release against the case, so that restructures and settlements reach booking in days.

The securities are read from v_ace_collateral and the title detail from v_ace_collateral_detail; the cleared balance is read from v_ace_account. The release leaves through the outbound interface to CCMS, ACE holds the release state, and the Workbench records its own request and confirmation: it writes no collateral row (D-RCV-35 U1 and U4; ADR-010).

**Acceptance criteria**


secs.h: RWB-E4-046 Post a settlement booking to ALS
secs.t:
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic | E4, release 28 February 2027 |
| Module | P8 Payments and posting |
| Feature | FEAT-PAY-06 Post a settlement booking to ALS |
| Process | See module |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | FEAT-CHO-08 |
| Decision | None |

**Story.** As the Credit Administration officer, I want the Workbench to send the agreed settlement terms to ALS through the outbound interface ACE carries and read the booked position back from the ACE views, so that every payment and booking is matched to its case.

ALS receives the booking through the outbound interface and the item is tracked in outbound_item. Once ACE has ingested the result, the Workbench reads the account and the payment back from v_ace_account and v_ace_payment. It writes nothing to ALS directly and holds no account or payment copy (D-RCV-35 U1 and U4; ADR-010).

**Acceptance criteria**

```gherkin
Feature: Post a settlement booking to ALS

 Scenario: AC1 Post a settlement booking to ALS
 Given treatment "T-0001" is accepted at a settlement amount of 820000 for account "A-0001"
 When the case owner posts the booking
 Then the Workbench sends the agreed terms to ALS through the outbound interface and tracks the item in outbound_item
 Then it reads the booked position from v_ace_account and the settlement payment from v_ace_payment
 Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

 Scenario: AC2 Not recorded
```

RWB-E4-001 | Order an appraisal when the last one is stale | Feature: Order an appraisal when the last one is stale   Scenario: AC1 Order an appraisal when the last one is stale  Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place  When its trigger arrives  Then checks the appraisal age against the limit and raises the order to SVAF with no person involved  Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version   Scenario: AC2 Not recorded  Given the decision log cannot be written  When the action is taken  Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
RWB-E4-002 | Receive the appraisal value from SVAF | Feature: Receive the appraisal value from SVAF   Scenario: AC1 Receive the appraisal value from SVAF  Given ACE has ingested the SVAF appraisal "AP-0001" for asset "AST-0001" at appraisal date 2026-11-02 and v_ace_valuation holds appraised value 4250000  When the case owner assesses the route  Then the Workbench reads the appraisal number, value, type and date from v_ace_valuation for the asset_key  Then it sets accepted, stale_flag and age_days in valuation_ext against the valuation_key  Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version   Scenario: AC2 Not recorded  Given the decision log cannot be written  When the action is taken  Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003

secs.h: Recovery Workbench user story: allocation and assignment engine v1
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Story key | RWB-E1-020 |
| Epic | E1, release 30 November 2026 |
| Module | P3 Case and workflow |
| Feature | FEAT-CWC-07 Run the allocation rule table; FEAT-CWC-08 Run the assignment engine by load and continuity; FEAT-CWC-09 Send a case to the overflow queue when no rule matches |
| Requirement IDs | REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009, REQ-CWC-016 |
| BRD section | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 3.3; Business Requirements Program, section 5.3 |
| L3 process | 18.3.2 Allocate work to teams, people and partners by rule; 6.1 Take over the case at 90 days past due |
| Decision | D6 entry, take over and own the case |
| Priority | Must |
| Depends on | RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-019, RWB-E1-027, RWB-E1-056 |
| Status | Ready for build |

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **every new recovery case placed in a queue and given an owner by the allocation and assignment rule tables on the morning it arrives**, so that **each case at 90 days past due has one owner from its first day and nobody allocates cases by hand**.

Cases are allocated today from team spreadsheets, and ownership is agreed by email, so a case can wait days with no owner. This story places every new case in a queue and gives it an owner by rule before 07:00 on the morning after case creation, with the rule row and version on a decision log entry. It meets REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008, REQ-CWC-009 and REQ-CWC-016, and serves the business measure "cases inside the service level" (target set with DL22) and control CTL-03.

- RWB-E1-018 is done: new cases exist with status NEW, product group, region and exposure band.
- RWB-E1-019 is done: queues, queue members and caseload caps are loaded; queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN.
- RWB-E1-027 is done: the decision log writer is available through its published interface.
- RWB-E1-056 is done: JOB-03 has a run book and appears in the job monitor.
- The allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" is loaded and approved (rule rows with rule table ALLOCATION; DL24). Every row holds row ID, product group, region, exposure band, target queue, valid from, valid to, approver and test case ID.
- Parameters loaded through RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code` = "RWB-EXC" and `allocation.deviation.queue.code` = "DEV-HANDLER" (assumed values; DL23).
- JOB-02 case creation has completed for today's business date after JOB-01 passed its load checks.
- The job runs as service identity SY-CASEWF; rules are evaluated as SY-RULES.

1. Quartz: starts JOB-03 Morning allocation after JOB-02 completes for business date 2026-12-01.
2. AllocationJob: selects every case with status NEW whose last allocation date is before the business date.
3. AllocationService: locks the case row and reads deviation_open; a case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue (R-DEV-01).
4. AllocationRuleEvaluator (SY-RULES): reads the allocation rows in force on the business date and returns the first row, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case.
5. AssignmentEngine: reads the target queue's method (DF-WRK-006) and cap (DF-WRK-007), counts the open cases of each queue member and picks the owner below the cap by the method.
6. AllocationService: in one transaction sets queue, team, owner, status ASSIGNED, stage clock start and rule version, writes the assignment with reason ALLOCATION, sets the last allocation date and writes CaseAllocated (EV-02) to the outbox.
7. AllocationService: as the last step before commit, calls DecisionLogWriter.write with the row ID, table version, queue, owner and inputs; a failed write rolls the allocation back.
8. AllocationJob: after the last case, builds the allocation summary per team (MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012) and sends it to the team manager through the ACE notification path.
9. AllocationJob: records the run result (cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed) on the job record for the monitor.

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Every owner in the target queue is at or above the cap | Case goes to the overflow queue of the target queue; status stays NEW; counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No allocation row matches the case | Case goes to the exception queue; status stays NEW; rule gap logged; CaseAllocationFailed (EV-03) published | MSG-P3-012 | AC5 |
| X3 | Decision log write fails | Allocation rolled back; case stays NEW with no queue change; retried in the next run | MSG-P3-013 | AC6 |
| X4 | Case has deviation_open = true | Case goes to the deviation handler queue; no case owner is chosen | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The run is repeated for the same business date | Cases already allocated for that date are skipped; no second assignment or log entry | None | AC8 |
| X6 | No case has status NEW | Run completes with zero counts; summary says 0 | MSG-P3-011, MSG-P3-012 with count 0 | AC9 |
| X7 | JOB-02 has not completed for the business date | JOB-03 does not start; job monitor shows it waiting; cases stay NEW | MSG-P1-001 | AC10 |
| X8 | A rerun starts while the first run still holds a case | The case row lock stops the second worker; each case is allocated once | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The overflow queue is not set on a queue whose owners are all at the cap | Case goes to the exception queue with the reason "no overflow queue" | MSG-P3-012 | AC13 |
| X10 | A user without the right reruns JOB-03 | Refused with 403; nothing runs | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-020-14 |

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the case record (RWB-E1-018), the roles, teams and queues table (RWB-E1-019), the decision log writer (RWB-E1-027) and the job monitoring (RWB-E1-056), all earlier in Epic 1 |
| Negotiable | The allocation method per queue, the cap and the queue codes are data values. The story fixes the behavior, not the values |
| Valuable | Ends allocation from spreadsheets for every new case, about 3,110 a month (DL15) |
| Estimable | One rule table, one service, one batch step, no screen |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
Feature: Allocate a new recovery case to a queue and an owner

 Background:
 Given the allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" is in force from 2026-11-30
 Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" belongs to team "MTG-BKK" and role RW-CASEOWN
 Given the queue uses the method "ROUND_ROBIN" with a caseload cap of 150
 Given the queue "MTG-BKK-CO" has the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
 Given the business date is 2026-12-01

 Scenario: AC1 A new case is placed in the queue its row names
 Given a new case RW-2026-000201 with status "NEW", product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and exposure band "B2"
 Given allocation row "ALLOC-014" matches product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and any exposure band, with target queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
 When the morning allocation run starts
 Then the system places the case in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
 Then the case team is "MTG-BKK" and the region is "BKK"

 Scenario: AC2 The owner is chosen by the queue's method
 Given queue "MTG-BKK-CO" holds three case owners U-01, U-02 and U-03 with 120, 95 and 140 open cases
 Given the last owner given a case in the queue was U-02
 When case RW-2026-000201 is placed in the queue
 Then the system gives the case to U-03
 Then the case status becomes "ASSIGNED"
 Then the system writes an assignment record with reason "ALLOCATION" and rule ID "ALLOC-014"

 Scenario: AC3 An owner at the caseload cap is skipped
 Given the last owner given a case was U-02
 Given U-03, the next owner in turn, holds 150 open cases
 Given U-01 holds 120 open cases
 When case RW-2026-000202 is placed in the queue
 Then the system gives the case to U-01, the following owner below the cap

 Scenario: AC4 Every owner is at the cap
 Given U-01, U-02 and U-03 each hold 150 open cases
 When case RW-2026-000203 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
 Then the system places the case in the overflow queue "MTG-BKK-OVF"
 Then the case status stays "NEW" and no owner is set
 Then the team manager of "MTG-BKK" receives the allocation summary with MSG-P3-011 and count 1

 Scenario: AC5 No allocation row matches
 Given a new case RW-2026-000204 with product group "SSME" and region "NE3" that matches no allocation row
 When the morning allocation run starts
 Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC"
 Then the case status stays "NEW"
 Then the system writes a decision log entry with final call "RULE_GAP", product group "SSME" and region "NE3"
 Then the system publishes caseAllocationFailed with reason "NO_ROW_MATCHED"
 Then the allocation summary carries MSG-P3-012 with count 1

 Scenario: AC6 Every allocation is logged
 Given case RW-2026-000205 matches row "ALLOC-014" and owner U-02 is below the cap
 When the case is placed in the queue and given an owner
 Then the system writes one decision log entry with rule ID "ALLOC-014", rule version "ALLOC-2026.11", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", owner U-02 and the inputs used
 Then if the decision log write fails, the allocation is not made, the case stays "NEW" with no queue and the job record carries MSG-P3-013 for the case

 Scenario: AC7 A case with an open deviation is not allocated to a case owner
 Given a new case RW-2026-000206 with deviation_open = true
 When the morning allocation run starts
 Then the system places the case in the deviation handler queue "DEV-HANDLER" named by rule R-DEV-01
 Then the system sets no case owner and the status stays "NEW"

 Scenario: AC8 A repeated run for the same date has no further effect
 Given the morning allocation run for 2026-12-01 has assigned case RW-2026-000201 to U-03
 When the run for 2026-12-01 is started again from the job monitor
 Then case RW-2026-000201 keeps owner U-03 and its one assignment record
 Then the system writes no second decision log entry for the case
 Then the job record shows 1 case skipped as already allocated

 Scenario: AC9 A run with no new cases
 Given no case has status "NEW" on 2026-12-01
 When the morning allocation run starts
 Then the run completes with 0 cases read
 Then the allocation summary for each team shows 0 in overflow and 0 in the exception queue

 Scenario: AC10 The run waits for case creation
 Given JOB-02 has not completed for 2026-12-01 because the COLLINS load was refused
 When 07:00 passes
 Then JOB-03 has not started for 2026-12-01
 Then the job monitor shows JOB-03 waiting on JOB-02 with MSG-P1-001
 Then every NEW case keeps no queue and no owner

 Scenario: AC11 Two runs at the same time allocate each case once
 Given a first run is allocating case RW-2026-000207
 When a rerun for 2026-12-01 reaches the same case at the same time
 Then the rerun skips the locked case
 Then the case has exactly one assignment record and one decision log entry for 2026-12-01

 Scenario: AC12 An owner one case below the cap gets the case
 Given U-03 is next in turn and holds 149 open cases
 When case RW-2026-000208 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
 Then the system gives the case to U-03
 Then U-03 now holds 150 open cases

 Scenario: AC13 A queue with no overflow queue sends the case to the exception queue
 Given queue "HP-CEN-CO" has no overflow queue
 Given every owner in queue "HP-CEN-CO" holds 150 open cases
 When case RW-2026-000209 is placed in queue "HP-CEN-CO"
 Then the system places the case in the exception queue "RWB-EXC" with reason "NO_OVERFLOW_QUEUE"
 Then the case status stays "NEW"
```

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case is allocated by the first row of the allocation table, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case. "Any" in a column matches every value | Allocation table (rule_row, rule table ALLOCATION), DL24; REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR2 | The owner is chosen by the method held on the queue: ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL | queue.assignment_method (DF-WRK-006), LOV-ASSIGN |
| BR3 | An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is skipped. Open cases are cases in the queue owned by the person with status other than CLOSED | queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007); values DL23 |
| BR4 | A case that cannot be given an owner goes to the overflow queue of its queue | queue.overflow_queue_id (DF-WRK-008) |
| BR5 | A case that matches no row goes to the exception queue, and the gap is logged. R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides | R-UNI-41; FEAT-CWC-09 |
| BR6 | A case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue | R-DEV-01 |
| BR7 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | A case is allocated at most once per business date | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule "Duplicates" |
| BR9 | Each allocation records the rule row and the table version | REQ-CWC-016; CTL-03 |

| New | Allocation rule matched | No row matched | New, in the exception queue |
| New | DEVIATION_FLAGGED (R-DEV-01) | deviation_open = true | New, in the deviation handler queue |

**Package.** `src/main/java/.../recovery/casewf/allocation`, Java package `recovery.casewf.allocation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AllocationJob | Job | Quartz job for JOB-03; selects NEW cases, calls AllocationService per case, builds the summary, writes job counts |
| AllocationService | Published interface | Implementation AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation check, rule match, owner choice, decision log write, case update, outbox event |
| AllocationRuleEvaluator | Service | Evaluates the allocation rows returned by RuleTableReader in row order; first match wins |
| AssignmentEngine | Service | Applies ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL with the cap |
| OwnerLoadRepository | Repository | Counts open cases per owner in a queue (ix_case_owner_status) |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | Reads and updates recovery_case, queue, queue_member, assignment |
| AllocationSummaryBuilder | Service | Counts overflow and exception cases per team; fills MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 |
| AllocationRuleTable | Rule table | Rule rows with rule table ALLOCATION, read through RuleTableReader |

**Database**

- Reads: recovery_case (id, case_no, product_group, region_code, exposure_band, deviation_open, status, last_allocation_date), queue (id, queue_code, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap, overflow_queue_id), queue_member (user_id, capacity).
- Writes: recovery_case (status, owner_user_id, queue_id, team_code, stage_clock_start, rule_version, last_allocation_date, version), queue (rr_cursor_user_id), assignment (all columns), outbox.
- Lock: `SELECT ... FROM recovery_case WHERE id = ? AND status = 'NEW' FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; optimistic version column on update.
- Migration in this story: `V020_1__allocation_columns.sql` adds recovery_case.last_allocation_date (date) and queue.rr_cursor_user_id (uuid). queue_member is created by RWB-E1-019.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Allocation table version "ALLOC-2026.11" (rule_row, rule table ALLOCATION), prepared by RW-REFADM, loaded by RW-COE through RWB-E1-029, approved by the Shared operations process owner.
- Queues and members from RWB-E1-019; caps DL23.
- Parameters from RWB-E1-042: `allocation.exception.queue.code`, `allocation.deviation.queue.code`.
- Lists LOV-ASSIGN, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-CASE-STATUS (P4 lov_value).

**Build steps**

1. AllocationRuleEvaluator: given a case snapshot and the rows of a version, return the first matching row or none. Unit tests per BR1 with "any" values.
2. AssignmentEngine: implement the four methods with cap skipping and the round robin cursor. Unit tests for AC2, AC3, AC12 boundary.
3. OwnerLoadRepository: open case count per owner and queue; integration test on PostgreSQL with Testcontainers.
4. AllocationServiceImpl: lock, deviation branch, rule match, overflow and exception branches, then case update, assignment and outbox row in one transaction with the decision log write as its last step.
5. Idempotency: skip when last_allocation_date equals the business date; return SKIPPED.
6. AllocationJob: Quartz job with `@DisallowConcurrentExecution`, dependency on JOB-02 completion, per-case transaction, job counts.
7. AllocationSummaryBuilder and the call to the ACE notification path for each team manager.
8. System tests TC-E1-020-01 to TC-E1-020-15 on the synthetic case set.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.allocation`. Off: JOB-03 does not run and cases stay NEW.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; TC-E1-020-01 and TC-E1-020-08 are in the regression suite; JOB-03 finishes 3,110 synthetic cases inside 15 minutes in SIT (assumed target; DL11).

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-011 | Allocation summary, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-012 | Allocation summary, no row matched | {count} new cases matched no allocation row and are in the exception queue. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Decision log write failed for a case | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |
| MSG-P1-001 | JOB-03 waiting because today's load has not arrived | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reruns the job | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

No new screen in Epic 1. SCR-02 Case list (states Loading; list) shows the queue, the owner and the status of each case after the run. SCR-09 Exception queue (states Loading; list) shows cases placed in "RWB-EXC". The team manager receives the allocation summary after each run. Queue screens come in Epic 2 (SCR-07).

| ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E1-020-01 | AC1, BR1 | System | One case per product group and region in the synthetic set |
| TC-E1-020-02 | AC2, BR2 | System | Three owners with 120, 95 and 140 open cases, round robin |

- No allocation value is written in code. Product groups, regions, bands, queues, methods, caps and queue codes are read from tables and parameters.
- No personal data in the allocation summary, the logs, the events or the test data. Cases are named by case number only.
- The service never reads tables owned by another module. Rule rows come through RuleTableReader (P4); the decision log through DecisionLogWriter (P7).

docs.file: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench ACE Architecture Decision v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

ACE architecture decision

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench ACE architecture decision
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Architecture decision record, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010

The Recovery Workbench is built inside ACE, the bank's collection workbench, as its recovery module. The case workflow runs in code, described in CMMN 1.1 terms, with no workflow engine. ACE ingests the source data, including SVAF, CCMS, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, the COLLINS scores, the SCBPDM product, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID group mapping. The Workbench runs no inbound load: it reads the data through read-only views (ADR-010).

Question | Decision | Status | Decision log
Where is the Workbench built? | Inside ACE: one service, one repository, one front end | Agreed | DT07
How is the code structured? | Modular monolith: common, collection and recovery modules by folder, with boundaries checked at build time | Agreed | DT08
How does the case workflow run? | In code, with case, stage, task and timer state held as rows in the ACE database. No Temporal | Agreed | DT09
Which case language is shared? | CMMN 1.1: case, stage, task, milestone, sentry | Agreed | DT10
How do rules change? | Every rule, limit, timer and route is a versioned data row evaluated by a decision table component | Agreed | DT02
How does data arrive? | ACE ingestion: SVAF, CCMS, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS scores, SCBPDM product, NLEADS, EasyApp and Entra ID group mapping land in the ACE database. No Workbench load. The recovery module reads them through recovery.v_ace_* views | Agreed | D-RCV-35; ADR-010
How is the front end split? | One ACE front end with a recovery module folder | Proposed | DL07
How do squads merge and release? | Trunk based development with feature flags. A flag that is off returns the previous code path | Agreed | DT11

A recovery case starts at 90 days past due, when collection hands it over. ACE already runs sign-in with Entra ID and the bank IAM, access control, audit, PII and SOC logging, a case view and the restructure calculator, and it passed the bank's new application standard and penetration test when it went live in October 2026.

Option | For | Against | Cost and time | Verdict
1. Recovery module of ACE | One case view for staff who work collection and recovery; sign-in, audit and logging reused; no integration between collection and recovery | Squads share one repository and one release | Lowest: no new platform to certify | Chosen
2. Separate recovery application on the ACE pattern | Independent releases | Two case views; sign-in, audit and logging rebuilt; an interface between collection and recovery | New application approval and penetration test | Not chosen
3. Separate application on its own platform | Free choice of technology | All of option 2, plus a second platform for SCB IT to run | Highest | Not chosen

A recovery case lives for months or years and mostly waits on people, partners and courts. 366 of the 448 routing rules move a case to a state that a person or a partner owns. The workflow must change while cases are open, when a Bank of Thailand rule or a policy adds a step, and it must still hold cases that started under the old version.

Criterion | 1. Programmatic in ACE | 2. Temporal for everything | 3. Programmatic cases, Temporal for automation tasks | 4. BPMN engine (Flowable)
Long human waits (weeks to years) | A wait is a row with a state and a due date | Held as a running workflow execution for the life of the case | Cases as rows; Temporal only for short tasks | Held as a process instance
Changing the flow while cases are open | A handler change is an ordinary release; open cases keep their rule version as data | Workflow code must stay deterministic; each change needs a version branch kept for as long as the oldest open case, which for litigation can be ten years | As option 1 for cases; Temporal versioning only for short tasks | Process versions migrate through the engine's migration tools
Reporting and audit | SQL on the case tables; the decision log records each rule version | Case history is in Temporal's event history, outside the case tables | As option 1 | Engine history tables
Running and storage | No new runtime | One more runtime; history grows with every step, and retention clean-up must skip workflows still open | Two models to run and a bridge between them | One more engine to run
Automated chains with other systems | Retry and compensation built with Spring Batch and the outbox | Built in: retries, sagas, resume after failure | Built in for the automated parts | Service tasks in the engine
Skills in the teams | Spring Boot, already used by ACE and TechX | Known to TechX; new to the ACE code base | Both teams know both | New to both
Effort for Epics 1 and 2 | Lowest | Highest | Higher than option 1 | Higher than option 1
Verdict | Chosen | Not chosen | Not now; can be added for a task under a separate decision | Not chosen

Recovery is case management with long human waits. Rows and due dates hold these waits with nothing to replay.

The flow changes often. With rules as data rows, a threshold or a route changes on its effective date without a release, and open cases keep the version they were decided under.

The bank runs no extra runtime, and case reporting stays in SQL.

The ACE team and TechX both build in Spring Boot today.

Temporal suits a self-contained automation task: no human step, a known end within days, called through an API and returning its result to the case. Because the case is described in CMMN terms behind one case interface, such a task can run on Temporal later without changing the case model. Adding it needs its own decision record with the task named.

Case, stage, task, milestone and timer state as rows in the ACE database

Quartz for schedules and timers; Spring Batch for automated chains

A transactional outbox for application events between modules

A decision table component that evaluates the 448 routing rules, hit policy Unique, in 10 route sets

An append-only decision log written before every action; a failed write stops the action

Option | For | Against | Cost and time | Verdict
1. Modular monolith by folder | One deployment and one database; each module owns its tables; boundaries tested at build time | Boundary tests and code owners needed before the squads start (DL37) | Low: folders and checks in the existing service | Chosen
2. Separate services per team | Independent deployment | Network calls between modules, separate databases, more to run and secure | High | Not chosen
3. One code base with no module boundaries | Nothing to set up | One team's change breaks another's; the service becomes hard to change | Low now, high later | Not chosen

Until the ACE team has moved ACE to the modular monolith, TechX builds the recovery module in its own package (DL05). A module reads only its own tables and reaches another module through its published interface or an application event. There is one exception, and it is written down rather than left to judgement: the recovery module reads source data through recovery.v_ace_* views, which read the public ACE tables. It holds no direct read of a public table, no write to it and no foreign key into it, because ACE cascades deletes on account (ADR-010).

Option | For | Against | Cost and time | Verdict
1. ACE ingestion, read through read-only views | One way in, run by the team that already ingests the data; one set of checks; no change to legacy systems; one copy of every record | The Workbench waits for the ACE additions (DL43); the data is as fresh as ACE holds it, end of day for COLLINS | Lowest: no inbound load to build or run | Chosen
2. COLLINS daily batch plus Workbench file loads | The Workbench controls its own load and its own checks | A second copy of every record, kept in step by hand; a load, data quality and tracker estate to build and run | High | Not chosen; superseded by ADR-010
3. Real-time interfaces to each system of record | Same-day data | New interfaces into legacy systems; each one an enhancement request | High | Not chosen
4. Events for every source | Same-day data with loose coupling | Sources do not publish events today | High | Not chosen

Every source in scope arrives through ACE's ingestion. ACE holds account, payment, customer, address, phone, email, relation, collateral, asset, collections action, assignment, bucket, product and branch data today. SVAF appraisals, CCMS collateral detail, AMIS and RPS repossessed and purchased assets, LIT litigation and hearings, WIN proof of delivery, GL write-off postings, the COLLINS scores, the SCBPDM product holding, NLEADS credit decisions, EasyApp signature requests and Entra ID group mapping are added under RWB-ACE-001 (DL43).

The recovery module owns the case and the extension tables; ACE owns the source data. Four tiers: 22 Tier 1 ACE tables read through 16 views; 14 Tier 2 ACE tables and 12 columns, raised in RWB-ACE-001, read through 14 views; 4 Workbench extension tables keyed by ACE business keys; and 88 Workbench tables that stay. The Workbench schema is 92 tables, and the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields in place of 108 and 1,256.

Same-day needs are named under DL06: the case transfer from EFS, a payment received and a legal event. The Workbench no longer meets them with its own feed. They depend on what ACE ingests, and the age of the data is visible on every view.

Two TechX squads and the collection squad release from one repository. Branches merge into main at least once a working day. Unfinished work sits behind a feature flag; a flag that is off returns the previous code path, so a change that fails SIT or UAT is switched off and the release goes ahead. Untested code is not merged. Each squad merges into its own module through code owners, and the ACE team owns the common module and the release decision (DL04).

Area | What follows
Security | Sign-in, the bank IAM, access control, audit, PII and SOC logging come from ACE
Staff | One case view across collection and recovery
Release | One release train with collection; merge ownership and flags matter (DL04)
Data | ACE owns the source data and the Workbench owns the case: 92 tables and 30 views, and 1,366 dictionary fields, in place of 108 tables and 1,256 fields. Source data is read through read-only views, so there is one copy of every record and no inbound load (ADR-010). The Workbench cannot start before the ACE additions land (DL43)
Build | Retry and compensation for automated chains are built in Spring Batch with the outbox
Partners | Partner access from outside the bank needs an architecture change with one to three months of lead time (DL03)

ID | Question | Proposed answer | Owner | Due
DL03 | Who raises the architecture change for partner access from outside the bank | The Workbench team or the ACE team, raised in November | K. Book with the architecture team | 29 October 2026
DL04 | Who merges between squads and decides when a change holds the release | Each squad through code owners; the ACE team for the common module and the release | K. Book | 29 October 2026
DL05 | Who creates the recovery module in ACE | TechX in its own package from 2 November, then the ACE team applies the boundaries | K. Pipat | 29 October 2026
DL06 | Which interfaces need same-day data | Option A (daily batch through COLLINS) superseded by D-RCV-35. Same-day triggers stay named; they depend on what ACE ingests | K. Book with K. Pipat | 30 October 2026
DL07 | How the ACE front end is split | One front end with a recovery folder from 2 November | K. Pipat | 31 October 2026
DL37 | When code owners and the browser test runner are in place | Code owners before 2 November; browser runner before the first SIT run | K. Book | 6 November 2026
DL43 | Does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates | Accept the 14 tables, 12 columns and 80 fields, delivered by 21 November 2026 | ACE team lead | 21 November 2026

Role | Approves | Status
SCB CTO | The decision as a whole | To approve
SCB IT architecture | Sections 2 to 5 | To approve
ACE team lead | Sections 3, 4 and 6 | Agreed
TechX delivery lead | Sections 3, 4 and 6 | Agreed
Henka solution architect | The decision as a whole | Agreed

400 | Bad request | The request is malformed | MSG-GEN-001

403 | Forbidden | The role lacks the right in the capability area | MSG-P4-002
404 | Not found | The record does not exist or is outside the caller's scope | MSG-P4-003
409 | Conflict | The state does not allow the action, the record changed, the approver is above the limit or prepared the decision | MSG-P3-005, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P7-001, MSG-P7-002
413 | Payload too large | The file is above the size limit | MSG-P5-001
415 | Unsupported media type | The file type is not allowed | MSG-P5-001
422 | Unprocessable | A field fails validation | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003
503 | Service unavailable | The decision could not be recorded, or a system of record is down | MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-006

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
 title: Recovery Workbench API
 version: 3.0.0
 description: >-
 Endpoints of the recovery module in the ACE service. Every endpoint checks the role, the capability area, the right and the scope.
 Version 3.0.0, 15 November 2026: re-based on the ACE database under D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5). The Workbench takes no inbound source data; ACE ingests every source and the Workbench reads it only through 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, linked by ACE business keys (account_key, person_key, payment_code, contact_key, asset_key, valuation_key) with no foreign key into ACE.
 This version removes the tracker endpoints, the source load rerun, the data quality exception list and the manual interface retirement sign-off. It adds GET /data/freshness over v_ace_batch_status and re-keys CaseAccount, CaseParty and Proceeds to the ACE business keys.
 (C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

 in: query

 type: string
 description: Add query parameter route (LOV-ROUTE) and sort value serviceLevelDueAt; size 1 to 200; response header X-Data-As-Of. Case items
 add ageDays (integer), serviceLevelDueAt (date-time) and serviceLevelState (string). Add query parameter breached (boolean). Query values
 product, stage and status are checked against LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-STAGE and LOV-CASE-STATUS; a value outside its list returns 422 with MSG-GEN-007.
 Case items add prescriptionClockStatus (RUNNING, EXPIRED, NONE). Case items add nextAction (string), nextActionOwner (string), nextActionDueDate
 (date) and nextActionOverdue (boolean).

 description: Success

 schemas:
 Case:
 type: object
 description: One recovery case per customer per product, from 90 days past due to close.
 properties:
 id:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: Record identifier of the case
 readOnly: true
 caseNo:
 type: string
 maxLength: 18
 description: Case number RW-YYYY-NNNNNN, issued at creation and never reused
 productGroup:
 type: string
 maxLength: 15
 x-list-of-values: LOV-PRODUCT
 description: Mortgage, hire purchase, SSME or unsecured
 primaryPersonKey:
 type: string
 description: The ACE person_key of the borrower the case is opened for; held as a business key with no foreign key into ACE
 status:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - NEW
 - ASSIGNED
 - IN_PROGRESS
 - WAITING_CUSTOMER
 - WAITING_PARTNER
 - WAITING_APPROVAL
 - ON_HOLD
 - CLOSED
 description: 'Case status: new, assigned, in progress, waiting customer, waiting partner, waiting approval, on hold, closed'
 stageCode:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - RESTRUCTURE
 - SETTLEMENT
 - DEED_IN_LIEU
 - GUARANTEE_CLAIM
 - LITIGATION
 - ASSET_DISPOSAL
 - DEBT_SALE
 - WRITE_OFF
 - DEVIATIONS
 description: The stage the case is on
 routeState:
 type: string
 maxLength: 60
 description: The routing state from the rule set, for example FIRM_INSTRUCTED
 routeCode:
 type: string
 maxLength: 4
 enum:
 - R1
 - R2
 - R3
 - R4
 - R5
 - R6
 - R7
 - R8
 description: The approved route R1 to R8
 ownerUserId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The case owner
 queueId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The queue the case is in
 teamCode:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 description: The owning team, used by scope rules
 regionCode:
 type: string
 maxLength: 10
 description: The owning region, used by scope rules
 entryDate:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: The date the case entered recovery
 dpdAtEntry:
 type: integer
 description: Days past due on the entry date
 exposureBand:
 type: string
 maxLength: 10
 description: Exposure band set from the outstanding balance at entry
 totalOutstandingAtEntry:
 type: number
 description: Total outstanding across linked accounts at entry, in baht
 prescriptionDate:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: The earliest date a legal claim on the case expires
 stageClockStart:
 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When the current state started, for the service level
 deviationOpen:
 type: boolean
 description: True while any deviation X1 to X7 is open
 legalHold:
 type: boolean
 description: True while a legal hold stops normal routing
 ruleVersion:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 description: The rule version the current state was entered under
 closedDate:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: The date the case closed
 closureReason:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - CURED
 - SETTLED
 - REALIZED
 - SOLD
 - WRITTEN_OFF
 - INSURANCE_SETTLED
 - MERGED
 - CANCELED
 description: Cured, settled, realized, sold, written off, insurance settled, merged, canceled
 planRef:
 type: string
 maxLength: 30
 description: Reference of the ACE restructure plan on the case
 planStatus:
 type: string
 maxLength: 10
 enum:
 - CREATED
 - APPROVED
 - BOOKED
 - BROKEN
 description: 'ACE plan status: created, approved, booked or broken'
 planStatusAsOf:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: Date of the plan status in ACE
 nextActionText:
 type: string
 maxLength: 1000
 description: The next action, copied from action_text of the rule that moved the case
 nextActionOwnerRole:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 description: Owner role of the next action, from owner_role of the rule
 nextActionDueDate:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: Due date from the rule's timer_spec or the service levels and timers table
 nextActionRuleId:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 description: Rule ID that set the next action
 nextActionWaiting:
 type: boolean
 description: True when the next action waits on a customer, party or partner
 lastAllocationDate:
 type: string
 format: date
 description: Business date of the last allocation run that decided the case
 statusBeforeHold:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - NEW
 - ASSIGNED
 - IN_PROGRESS
 - WAITING_CUSTOMER
 - WAITING_PARTNER
 - WAITING_APPROVAL
 - ON_HOLD
 - CLOSED
 description: The case status when a legal hold was placed, restored when it is lifted
 required:
 - id
 - caseNo
 - productGroup
 - primaryPersonKey
 - status
 - entryDate
 - dpdAtEntry
 - totalOutstandingAtEntry
 - deviationOpen
 - legalHold
 - nextActionWaiting
 CaseAccount:
 type: object
 description: Links each ACE account to the case it is recovered under. The link is an ACE business key read from v_ace_account, not a foreign key.
 properties:
 id:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: Record identifier of the case account link
 readOnly: true

 type: string

 type: string
 maxLength: 255

 type: boolean

 type: string

 type: string
 format: date

 required:
 - id
 - caseId
 - accountKey
 - isPrimary
 - linkedFrom

 maxLength: 20

 - GUARANTOR
 - AUTHORIZED_SIGNATORY
 - HEIR

 type: string
 format: date
 description: Date the role starts
 roleTo:
 type: string
 format: date

 - caseId
 - personKey
 - partyRole
 - roleFrom

 type: object
 description: A deviation X1 to X7 raised on a case.

 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: Record identifier of the deviation
 readOnly: true

 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The recovery_case this record belongs to

 type: string
 maxLength: 3

 - X2

 - X4
 - X5
 - X6
 - X7
 description: X1 to X7

 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When it was raised
 raisedBy:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - SCREENING_AGENT
 - RULE
 - OFFICER
 - CUSTOMER_CONTACT
 description: Screening agent, rule, officer, customer contact
 pausedState:
 type: string
 maxLength: 60
 description: The routing state the case was in when paused

 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The named handler
 contactStop:
 type: boolean
 description: True when customer contact is stopped
 clearedAt:
 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When it cleared
 outcome:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - RETURNED
 - RE_ROUTED
 - CASE_ENDED
 description: Returned, re-routed, case ended
 required:
 - id
 - caseId
 - deviationCode
 - raisedAt
 - raisedBy
 - pausedState
 - contactStop
 Assignment:
 type: object
 description: Who holds a case or a task and from when.
 properties:
 id:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: Record identifier of the assignment
 readOnly: true
 caseId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The recovery_case this record belongs to
 taskId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The task this record belongs to
 assigneeUserId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The person or service identity assigned
 assignedAt:
 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When assigned
 endedAt:
 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When the assignment ended
 reason:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - ALLOCATION
 - TRANSFER
 - REBALANCE
 - MANUAL
 - ESCALATION
 description: Allocation, transfer, rebalance, manual, escalation
 ruleId:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 description: The rule that made the assignment
 queueId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The queue the assignment placed the case in
 transferReasonCode:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - R01
 - R02
 - R03
 - R04
 - R05
 - R06
 description: Coded reason for a manual transfer or move
 required:
 - id
 - caseId
 - assigneeUserId
 - assignedAt
 - reason
 Task:
 type: object
 description: 'A unit of work on a case: a CMMN human, customer, partner or decision task.'
 properties:
 id:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: Record identifier of the task
 readOnly: true
 caseId:
 type: string
 format: uuid
 description: The recovery_case this record belongs to

 type: string
 maxLength: 60
 description: The task in the case model, for example VERIFY_PACK
 elementType:
 type: string
 maxLength: 20
 enum:
 - HUMAN_TASK
 - CUSTOMER_TASK
 - PARTNER_TASK
 - DECISION_TASK
 - STAGE_ENTRY
 - MILESTONE
 - EVENT_LISTENER
 description: Human, customer, partner or decision task, milestone, event listener
 discretion:
 type: string
 maxLength: 15
 enum:
 - AUTOMATIC
 - DISCRETIONARY
 - REQUIRED
 description: Automatic, discretionary, required
 status:
 type: string
 maxLength: 15
 enum:
 - OPEN
 - IN_PROGRESS
 - DONE
 - CANCELED
 description: Open, in progress, done, canceled

 type: string
 maxLength: 20

 type: string
 format: date-time
 description: When the task is due

 type: string
 format: date-time

 type: string
 maxLength: 40

 - caseId

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v2.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v2

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| ID | Decision | Status | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-001 | Build the Workbench as a module of ACE | Accepted | 27 October 2026 |
| ADR-002 | Structure ACE as a modular monolith with common, collection and recovery modules | Accepted | 27 October 2026 |
| ADR-003 | Run the case workflow in code, in CMMN 1.1 terms, with no workflow engine | Accepted | 27 October 2026 |
| ADR-004 | Hold every rule as versioned data and evaluate it with a decision table component | Accepted | 20 October 2026 |
| ADR-005 | Take data through COLLINS and file loads, and call no system of record directly | Superseded by ADR-010 | 27 October 2026 |
| ADR-006 | One ACE front end with a recovery module folder | Proposed | 28 October 2026 |
| ADR-007 | Build the document hub in the Workbench as the system of record for recovery documents | Accepted | 26 October 2026 |
| ADR-008 | Trunk based development with feature flags | Accepted | 27 October 2026 |
| ADR-009 | An append-only, hash-chained decision log that blocks an action it cannot record | Proposed | 28 October 2026 |
| ADR-010 | Read source data from the ACE database through read-only views | Accepted | 15 November 2026 |

---

secs.h: ADR-001 Build the Workbench as a module of ACE
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 27 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB IT, the ACE team, TechX and Henka
- Decision log: DT07

Recovery needs a case system from day 90 to close. ACE is the bank's collection engine and already runs sign-in, access control, audit and personal data logging, a case view and the restructure calculator. Building recovery as a separate application would give staff who work both collection and recovery two systems and two case views, and the bank two platforms to run.

- One case view for collection and recovery staff
- Reuse of what ACE already runs in production
- No integration cost between collection and recovery
- One platform for SCB IT to operate and secure

1. A module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end
2. A separate recovery application on the ACE infrastructure pattern
3. A separate recovery application on its own platform
Option 1. The Workbench is the recovery module of ACE.

- Good: sign-in, the bank IAM, access control, audit, PII and SOC logging come from ACE.
- Good: one case view across collection and recovery.
- Good: recovery takes ACE's data position, which is now an asset rather than a constraint: one copy of the source data, ingested by ACE and read through read-only views (ADR-010).
- Bad: the recovery and collection squads share one repository and one release, so merge ownership and release discipline matter (ADR-008, DL04).

---

secs.h: ADR-002 Structure ACE as a modular monolith
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 27 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB IT, the ACE team, TechX and Henka
- Decision log: DT08; module creation DL05

Three teams build in one service: the ACE team, the collection squad and the TechX recovery squads. Without boundaries, a change in one team's code breaks another's, and the service becomes hard to change.

- Squads can change their own module without coordinating every change
- One deployable service
- Boundaries that are checked, not agreed

1. Modular monolith: common, collection and recovery modules by folder, boundaries checked at build time
2. Separate services per team
3. One codebase with no module boundaries
Option 1. Each module owns its tables and is reached only through its published interface or an application event. A boundary test fails the build on any violation.

- Good: one deployment and one database, with clear ownership of code and tables.
- Good: a recovery component the collection module needs can move to the common module by agreement.
- Bad: the boundary test and code owners must be in place before the squads start (DL37).

---

secs.h: ADR-003 Run the case workflow in code, with no workflow engine
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 27 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB IT, the ACE team, TechX and Henka
- Decision log: DT09, DT10

A recovery case lives for months or years and mostly waits on people, partners and courts. 366 of the 448 routing rules move a case to a state that a person or a partner owns. The case model has 10 stages, 30 milestones, 150 tasks, 53 event listeners and 448 sentries. The question is whether a workflow engine such as Temporal holds the case, or the case is held as data and moved by code.

- Long human waits, which a workflow engine holds poorly
- Cases that outlive several releases, so in-flight versioning matters
- One case language shared with the collection module
- Skills the ACE team and TechX already have

1. Case state as rows in the ACE database, moved by code, timers on Quartz, automated chains on Spring Batch with an outbox
2. Temporal, with one workflow execution per case
3. A commercial case management engine

Option 1. The case is modeled in CMMN 1.1 terms. Case, stage, task and timer state are rows. A wait of weeks is a row with a state and a stored due date. Temporal is not used; adding it later for a self-contained automation task needs its own decision record.

- Good: no extra runtime for SCB to operate; a change to a handler is an ordinary release; state does not replay.
- Good: case terms mean the same in both modules.
- Bad: retry and compensation for automated chains are built with Spring Batch and an outbox.

---

secs.h: ADR-004 Hold every rule as versioned data
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 20 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB core team with Henka
- Decision log: DT02; Epic 1 rule scope DL24

Thresholds, limits, routes, timers and templates change often. If they are written in code, every change needs a release, and the business waits a month to move a number. ACE has rule based logic in code and no rules engine.

- A business change without a code release
- An audit trail of which rule version decided each case
- Open cases kept on the version they were decided under

1. Rules as versioned rows, evaluated by a decision table component in the recovery module
2. A commercial or open source rules engine
3. Rules in Java code

Option 1. Every rule, limit, threshold, template, name, queue, role, timer and route is a data row with a version, valid from and valid to dates, an approver and a test case, changed through a validated load. Each route set is a decision table with hit policy Unique. Code holds the behavior; data holds the choices.

- Good: a threshold moves on its effective date with no release, and rolls back the same way.
- Good: the decision log records the rule ID and version for every move.
- Bad: the evaluator, the load checks and the rule table tests are built by the squads.

---

secs.h: ADR-005 Take data through COLLINS and file loads
secs.t:
Superseded by ADR-010 on 15 November 2026. The Workbench no longer loads source data: ACE ingests it, and the recovery module reads it through read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views. This section is kept as the record of what was decided on 27 October 2026.

- Status: Superseded by ADR-010
- Date: 27 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB IT and the ACE team
- Decision log: DT12; real-time needs DL06; legacy scope DL12

The Workbench needs account, customer, collections, litigation, collateral, valuation and asset data. ACE takes its data through COLLINS by end of day batch. Collateral, appraisals and assets are not in COLLINS today.

- One way in for data, with checks
- No new direct interfaces to legacy systems
- A known age for every input to a decision

1. COLLINS daily batch, plus file loads for sources COLLINS does not carry
2. Direct real-time interfaces to each system of record
3. Events for every source

Option 1. No component calls a system of record directly. Each load is checked for business date, structure, control totals, keys and references, and is refused whole if it fails. Every loaded record carries its business date.

- Good: one path in, one set of checks, no legacy enhancement.
- Bad: decisions use end of day data, and collateral, appraisals and assets arrive weekly or monthly. Same-day needs are named under DL06.

---

secs.h: ADR-006 One ACE front end with a recovery module folder
secs.t:
- Status: Proposed
- Date: 28 October 2026
- Deciders: the ACE team
- Decision log: DL07
ACE has one React front end. The recovery screens can live in a module folder of that front end, or the front end can be split into a workspace of modules.

- Squads work from 2 November
- One look and one sign-in for staff
- Types generated from the back end

1. One ACE front end with a recovery module folder
2. A workspace of front end modules with NX
3. A separate recovery front end
Option 1 from 2 November. A move to option 2 is the ACE team's choice and does not change the recovery screens.

- Good: no wait for a front end restructure.
- Bad: code owners per folder are needed to keep squads out of each other's screens (DL37).

---

secs.h: ADR-007 Build the document hub in the Workbench
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 26 October 2026
- Deciders: CTO
- Decision log: DT06; storage pattern DL27; document types DL19
Recovery runs on documents: contracts, notices, proofs of delivery, court papers, appraisals and titles. The choice was to index documents held in another store or to hold them in the Workbench.

- Documents found by case, type and date without manual filing
- Legal documents that cannot be altered
- Custody of originals tracked

1. A document hub built in the Workbench as the system of record
2. An index over an existing document store
Option 1. Documents are stored in Blob storage with a write-once container for legal types, indexed by case, type, date and extracted fields, with retention classes and custody tracking.

- Good: one place for every recovery document, linked to its case.
- Bad: storage, backup, legal hold and e-discovery are in scope (DL27).

---

secs.h: ADR-008 Trunk based development with feature flags
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 27 October 2026
- Deciders: SCB IT, the ACE team, TechX and Henka
- Decision log: DT11; merge owner DL04
Two squads release monthly from one repository. One squad's unfinished or failed change must not hold the other's release.

1. Trunk based development with short branches and feature flags
2. Long-lived squad branches merged before each release
Option 1. Branches merge into main at least once a working day. Unfinished work is behind a flag. A flag that is off returns the previous code path. Untested code is not merged.

- Good: a change that fails SIT or UAT is switched off and the release goes ahead.
- Bad: flags must be listed, owned and removed after release.

---

secs.h: ADR-009 An append-only decision log that blocks an action it cannot record
secs.t:
- Status: Proposed
- Date: 28 October 2026
- Deciders: the solution architect with Risk and Internal Audit
Every recovery decision must be traceable for audit, testing and learning: the inputs, the rule and model versions, the recommendation, the approver, the actions and the outcome.

1. An append-only, hash-chained log in the ACE database, written before the action, with a failed write blocking the action
2. Application logs searched after the event
Option 1. A correction is a further entry naming the original. Analysis reads a copy in the data lake, not the live log.

- Good: an auditor can test that every action carries a rule version and an approver.
- Bad: the decision log write is in the path of every action and must be fast and available. Retention is set by Compliance (DL26).

---

secs.h: ADR-010 Read source data from the ACE database through read-only views
secs.t:
- Status: Accepted
- Date: 15 November 2026
- Deciders: the recovery tech lead with the data architect; the ACE team lead for RWB-ACE-001 and DL43
- Decision log: D-RCV-35 (U1 to U4); supersedes ADR-005

The design built a second copy of account, customer, payment, party, contact, collateral, valuation, asset, collections, product and score data in the recovery schema, and filled it with eleven copy tables and nine load tables. ACE already ingests those records and owns them. Two copies of one account row disagree over time, and the Workbench maintains the copy that nothing else reads. The question is where source data lives and how the recovery module reaches it.

- One copy of source data, held by the team that already ingests it
- No inbound interface or second load estate for the Workbench to build and run
- A boundary the database enforces, not only code review
- Case history that a change in a source system cannot delete

1. Read source data from the ACE database through `recovery.v_ace_*` views, SELECT only
2. Keep the copy tables in the recovery schema and load them (ADR-005)
3. Read the ACE `public` tables directly from the recovery module

Option 1. The recovery module reads source data from the ACE database through `recovery.v_ace_*` views. It does not load, copy or transform source data. The views are SELECT only and owned by a dedicated role that holds SELECT on the ACE tables; the recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and on nothing else, so a direct read of a `public` table fails in the catalog.

- 30 views in two migrations: 16 over ACE tables that exist today, shipped with RWB-E1-069 as the next free sequence after the V0001 baseline; 14 over the Tier 2 additions, shipped the week RWB-ACE-001 lands. Until then the features that need them stay behind their flags.
- The ACE team owns every table and column the views read, raised once in RWB-ACE-001. The Workbench owns only its four extension tables, keyed by ACE business keys.
- No foreign key from a `recovery` table into `public`, because ACE uses ON DELETE CASCADE on `account`. A link to a source record is a business-key column with no foreign key.

- Good: one copy of source data. There is no Workbench copy to reconcile, correct or retire.
- Good: no inbound load, data quality or tracker estate to build and run; 20 tables leave the schema.
- Good: the view list is the contract between the two teams, so a change to a source column is an ACE change with a named owner.
- Bad: the Workbench cannot start before the ACE additions land (DL43).
- Bad: there is no tokenization at load, so masking moves into the views and to E1-037 at the API, and every read of personal data is audited.
- Bad: a view that reads a changed ACE column breaks at deploy, so the view conformance test runs in the pipeline.

Field | Meaning
entry_id, case_id | The entry and its case
decision_code | D1 to D9, a sub-decision or a deviation
rule_id, rule_version | The rule that fired and its version
model_version, agent_version, prompt_version | Where a model or agent took part

secs.h: 3. Tracing an action end to end
secs.t:
Every request carries a trace ID from the front end through the service, the outbox and the outbound file.

The decision log entry stores the trace ID.

The interaction ledger entry stores the decision log entry ID where a decision caused it.

Outbound files carry the case number and the entry ID, so a notice in WIN can be traced to its decision.

Internal audit searches by case, rule, approver or date on the decision log query screen and exports with masking.

The decision log, the interaction ledger and the access log accept inserts only. Migrations cannot update or delete their rows.

A daily job checks the hash chain and reports a break to Compliance the same day.

A correction is a new entry that names the entry it corrects; the original stays.

A failed write to the decision log stops the action; a failed write to the ledger raises an incident.

Record | Retention
Decision log | Set by Compliance (DL26); proposed as the life of the case plus the bank records period
Interaction ledger | Set by Compliance, separately from the decision log (DL26)
Access log | Per the bank retention schedule (DL26)
Application logs | 90 days in Log Analytics, then archived

Clear national ID or passport numbers.

Personal fields in application logs, traces or agent prompts.

Secrets, tokens or keys.

Structure | arc42 runtime view

Quartz in the ACE service holds the schedules in ACE's existing qrtz_* tables, shared with ACE; one run per job across service instances. The Workbench creates no new qrtz_ table.

Spring Batch runs the Workbench jobs and the outbound files in chunks with restart from the last chunk. It runs no inbound load. Its step records go to ACE's existing Spring Batch batch_* tables, shared with ACE; no new batch_ table is created (ACE Data Tier Map rows 23 and 24).

Every job writes its run to the job monitor with business date, rows, checks and result.

Schedules and thresholds are configuration; changing them needs no release.

The data jobs start on the ACE batch-complete record, read through recovery.v_ace_batch_status (EV-26 AceDataReady). No job waits on a file, and no data job starts on a fixed clock time.

19 jobs are listed. JOB-01 and JOB-09 are retired under D-RCV-35 and keep their rows; the other 17 run on Quartz and Spring Batch. The data jobs start on the ACE batch-complete record, not on a load.

JOB-09 | File loads | Retired - D-RCV-35 | Not run; ACE ingestion replaces it and reports its own status through v_ace_batch_status | ACE team
JOB-10 | WIN outbound notices | Daily 16:00 | Retry; exception queue | Platform administrator
JOB-11 | Outbox sender | Every minute | Exception queue after the retry limit | Platform administrator
JOB-12 | Document intake | Every 15 minutes in business hours | Next run; alert after two failures | Platform administrator
JOB-13 | Decision log copy | Nightly 01:00 | Rerun the next night | Data steward

The data jobs start from the ACE batch record, not from a fixed time. ACE ingests each source and writes a completion record; the Workbench reads recovery.v_ace_batch_status and starts the chain when the record for the business date shows COMPLETED: JOB-02 case creation, then JOB-04 reconciliation, JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation, then JOB-03 allocation by 07:00. JOB-16 write-off scan runs on the same record on its scheduled day. If a source is not complete at the Workbench cut-off, the data products show their last complete business date, AceDataLate goes to the data steward, and the chain starts when the record arrives. No job reads a file, and no job retries a load.

A missed run is processed when the service starts.

A failed job alerts its owner within 15 minutes.

A rerun from the job monitor is logged with who ran it.

No job processes the same business date twice; repeats are ignored.

An ACE batch that is late raises AceDataLate; the data jobs start when its record arrives and use the business date it carries.
Working days come from the bank holiday calendar held as reference data. Monthly jobs on a holiday run the next working day.
