Recovery Workbench

Document management design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench document management design
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 building block and runtime views, C4 component view

Element | Design
System of record | The document hub in the recovery module is the system of record for recovery documents (DT06)
Storage | Blob storage; a write-once container for legal document types (DL27)
Index | document, document_field and document_custody tables in the ACE database
Intake | Branch scanners, the mailroom, partner SFTP and uploads, recovery mailboxes, the field app and generated documents enter one intake
Reading | OCR for Thai and English, classification by the intake agent, extraction of key fields with a confidence per field
Review | Fields below the confidence floor go to the document review queue
Versions | Every change is a new version; legal documents cannot be overwritten
Originals | Physical originals tracked with holder, location and due-back date
Retention | A retention class per document type; a legal hold overrides it (DL26)

Source | How it arrives | Recorded as
Branch scanner | Scanner folder picked up by the intake job | Scan, branch and scan time
Mailroom | Scanner folder | Scan, mailroom
Partner | Partner portal upload, or SFTP until external access (DL03) | Partner, firm ID
Recovery mailbox | Attachment taken from the mailbox; the email is archived | Email, sender
Field app | Photos and bills synced with location and time | Upload, field collector
Generated | Notices and agreements produced from templates | Generated, template version
Upload by staff | Case documents screen | Upload, user

Each file is scanned for malware before storage. A failed scan rejects the file and logs it.

The file is stored in Blob storage; legal types go to the write-once container.

OCR produces text and layout. A page below the quality threshold is flagged for rescan.

The intake agent classifies the type and matches the document to the case by case number, account or name.

Key fields are extracted with a confidence per field. Fields below the floor go to the review queue (MSG-P5-003).

The document appears on the case with its type, source, fields and review status.

Type | Fields extracted | Retention class | Arrives as
Demand letter | Debtor name, account number, amount demanded, due date, sent date | Legal, write-once | Generated; scan of signed copy
Court notice | Court, case number, hearing date, parties | Legal, write-once | Law firm upload; scan
Appraisal report | Valuer, valuation date, market value, forced sale value, title number | Collateral | Valuer upload; SVAF
Title deed | Title number, land office, area in rai-ngan-wa, owner, encumbrances | Legal, write-once | Scan of the original
Settlement agreement | Parties, accounts, settlement amount, installments, signature date | Legal, write-once | Generated; e-signature or scan
Guarantor notice | Guarantor name, amount, sent date, delivery date | Legal, write-once | Generated; proof of delivery from WIN

Further types are added as reference data with their fields and retention class, after Legal and the business sign the field list (DL19).

A changed document is stored as a new version with a reason; earlier versions stay readable.

Legal types cannot be changed or deleted in their retention period (MSG-P5-002).

A document produced for court carries its origin, intake date, version history and read history (NFR-076).

Event | What is recorded
Original received | Holder Vault, location, received date
Sent out | Holder (branch, post, lawyer, court, land office), date out, due-back date
Returned | Date back, condition
Overdue | Task to document services; MSG-P5-004 on the case

Documents are found by case, type, date and extracted field. Masked fields are not searchable.

Opening a document checks the Documents capability area and the case scope.

Every open and download is written to the access log.

Each type carries a retention class; the period is set by Compliance (DL26).

A legal hold on a case or document stops expiry for as long as it is in place.

At the end of retention the document is disposed of or extended by a recorded decision, never silently.

e-Discovery returns every document for a named population with metadata and versions.

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL19 | Document types and fields | The six types above
DL26 | Retention per type | Proposed classes; hold overrides
DL27 | Storage, backup, legal hold and e-discovery | ACE storage pattern with a write-once container and the bank backup

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Environment and deployment design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench environment and deployment design
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Change | D-RCV-35 (ADR-010): no inbound load. Spring Batch runs automated chains on the ACE Quartz and Spring Batch tables; two-migration rule for the ACE views and the view conformance test; stale data from ace_batch_run lateness; no load containers, inbound file folders or file shares; DL43 is a deployment dependency (sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8)
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 deployment view, with C4 deployment and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoints

Element | Design | Status
Where it runs | The ACE service on the shared ACE AKS clusters in the SCB Azure tenant, Southeast Asia region | Agreed
Source data | Read from the ACE database through read-only recovery.v_ace_* views. The Workbench runs no inbound load and receives no source file | Agreed; D-RCV-35
Deployment dependency | RWB-ACE-001, the ACE tables and columns the Section B views read, is a deployment dependency, not a parallel workstream. DL43 must be accepted by 21 November 2026 and the additions must land in each environment before the release that switches on a Section B feature | Blocking; DL43
Environments | DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD on one pattern, built from code | Agreed
Deployment slots | Four in DEV and two in SIT planned, so squads test in parallel; one of each available today | Open, DL35
Repository | One ACE repository with common, collection and recovery modules | Agreed
Module set-up | TechX builds in its own package from 2 November; the ACE team applies the module boundaries | Assumed, DL05
Branching | Trunk based, with short branches merged into main at least once a working day | Agreed
Merge owner | Each squad merges into its own module through code owners; the ACE team owns the common module and the release decision | Assumed, DL04
Feature flags | Every unfinished or cross-squad change is behind a flag held as configuration per environment | Agreed
Release | One production release at each month end, shared with the collection squad | Agreed; window DL34

Environment | Purpose | Data | Deployed | Who uses it
DEV | Build and developer testing | Synthetic only | On every merge into main | Squads
SIT | System and integration testing against the SCB test systems | Masked copies from the PII service | On a release tag | QA with SCB IT
UAT | Business acceptance | Masked copies from the PII service | In the week before each release | Business testers
PROD | Live service | Live | In the monthly change window | Bank staff and partners

No production data reaches DEV. Each environment holds its own configuration, feature flag values, secrets and Entra ID groups. Every environment holds the ACE schema the views read; in DEV and in the pipeline test database it is the ACE schema with synthetic rows, so the views compile and return data.

Component | What it is | Shared with ACE
Service | The ACE Spring Boot service with the recovery module, in the ACE namespace | Yes
Front end | The ACE React front end with the recovery module folder | Yes
Database | PostgreSQL flexible server, zone redundant: the ACE database, with the recovery schema owned by the service. The recovery module reads ACE tables only through the recovery.v_ace_* views | Same server and database; own schema
Document storage | Blob storage with a write-once container for legal document types. No load container, no inbound file folder and no file share: the Workbench receives no source files | New containers
Secrets | Key Vault, reached by managed identity. No secret in code, configuration or prompts | Yes
Ingress | Internal application gateway with web application firewall for staff; the external gateway for partners (DL03) | Yes
Network | Private endpoints to storage and the database | Yes
Scheduler | Quartz for timers and scheduled jobs; Spring Batch for automated chains (case creation, reconciliation, payment matching, allocation, write-off scan) and outbound files, with restart from the last chunk. No Spring Batch job loads source data. Both share ACE's existing Quartz (qrtz_*) and Spring Batch (batch_job_*, batch_step_*) tables; the Workbench adds no qrtz_ or batch tables | Yes; same Quartz and Spring Batch tables
Source loads | None. No load container, no inbound file folder, no file share, no staging table and no load job. ACE ingests every source and records each batch in ace_batch_run; the Workbench reads the batch record through v_ace_batch_status | ACE ingestion
Identity | Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication; managed identities for services | Yes
ACE read role | recovery_svc, the recovery service role: SELECT on recovery.v_ace_* only, no direct public read, no write. ace_view_owner: a NOLOGIN ACE role that owns the views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables they read. PUBLIC is revoked. These are the names the ACE Source Views v1 grants use | ace_view_owner is an ACE role
Logs | Log Analytics for logs, traces and metrics; PII Kafka and the SOC log | Yes
Model endpoint | Private endpoint in the SCB tenant | Open, DL33

Gate | Checks
1 Build and unit tests | The service builds and every unit and rule table test passes
2 Lint | Code style and the naming rules
3 Secret scan | No credential, key or token in the code
4 PDPA lint | No personal data in code, tests or log statements
5 Container scan | No known vulnerability above the bank threshold in the image
6 Module boundary | No call or table read across a module boundary; the recovery module reads ACE only through recovery.v_ace_* views (TE-001)
7 Integration and contract tests | Modules work with the database and the generated types; the view conformance test passes against the ACE schema (section 5)
8 AI first-pass review | Bugs, security, PDPA and style, with a summary on the pull request
9 Human approval | One named reviewer, and the code owner where another module is touched

Step | When | Approved by
Deploy to DEV | On every merge into main | Pipeline
Deploy to SIT | On a release tag | Tech lead
SIT exit | After one week of SIT | QA lead with SCB IT
Deploy to UAT | In the week before the release | QA lead
UAT exit | After the business scripts are signed | Business lead
ACE dependency gate | RWB-ACE-001 accepted and landed in the environment (DL43) before the release that turns on a Section B view | ACE team lead and release owner
Deploy to PROD | In the monthly change window | Release owner in the ACE team with the application owner
Rollback | Switch the feature flag off first; redeploy the previous tag if a flag does not cover the fault | Release owner

Every schema change is a versioned migration script in the recovery module, run by the pipeline in each environment in order.

V0001 is the baseline of the recovery schema (D-RCV-28). No recovery migration creates or alters a table in the ACE public schema; the ACE tables and columns change only through the ACE team's own migrations (RWB-ACE-001).

Two-migration rule. A view cannot be created over a table that does not exist, so the ACE views ship in two migrations. Section A, the 16 Tier 1 views over the ACE tables that exist today, with the grants and the revoke from PUBLIC, ships with RWB-E1-069 as the next free sequence after V0001.

Section B, the 14 Tier 2 views over the tables and columns the ACE team adds, ships as a later sequence in the week RWB-ACE-001 lands in each environment. Until then the features that read the Section B views stay behind their feature flags, switched off.

The Section A migration also creates or confirms the two database roles. ace_view_owner is a NOLOGIN ACE role that owns the 16 views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables they read. recovery_svc is the recovery service identity: USAGE on schema recovery and SELECT on the 16 views, and nothing else. PUBLIC is revoked. A direct read of a public table or any write fails in the catalog, not only in code review.

The pipeline runs the view conformance test after the migrations in every environment: every v_ace_* view compiles; no constraint in schema recovery references a public table; recovery_svc cannot select a public table directly and cannot insert, update or delete on any public or recovery table. A failure stops the deployment, so an ACE column change that breaks a view is found before release.

In DEV and the pipeline test database the ACE schema runs first, then V0001, then Section A, then Section B once the ACE additions are present.

Schema names are parameters, so the same script runs in every environment.

A migration that changes data shape runs behind a feature flag until both code paths are no longer needed.

Reference data, rules, limits and lists of values load through the validated load, not through migrations.

The decision log and the interaction ledger are append only; migrations never update or delete their rows.

Rule | Detail
What a flag does | Chooses between the new code path and the previous one. Off returns the previous path
Where it is held | As configuration for each environment. Changing a value needs no code release
What it records | Name, owner, story key, value in each environment, and the release in which it is removed
At release | A change that fails SIT or UAT has its flag switched off and the release goes ahead without it
Removal | The old path and the flag are removed in the release after the flag is switched on in production

Item | Design | Status
Availability | 99.9% in business hours | Proposed, DL11
Recovery point and time | Set by SCB IT for the ACE service | Open, DL11
Database | Zone-redundant PostgreSQL with point-in-time restore | ACE pattern

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v2.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v2

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Error handling and resilience standard

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench error handling and resilience standard
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 crosscutting concepts

Every failure is caught at the boundary where it happens and is given a category and a message code.

No failure is silent: it reaches a person, a queue or an alert with a named owner.

A decision that cannot be recorded is not taken.

Outbound work is never lost: it waits in the outbox and retries.

A user sees what happened and what to do, in Thai and English, from the error and message standard.

An agent or model failure never stops a case: the rule result is used.

Category | Example | Caught where | What happens | User sees | Owner
Validation | A required field is empty | Request validation | Request refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-001 next to the field | The user
Access | Role lacks the right | Permission check | 403 or 404 | MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003 | The user's manager
State conflict | Move not allowed from the current state | Workflow | 409 | MSG-P3-005 | The user
Concurrent change | Record changed by someone else | Version check | 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | The user
Decision log | Log write fails | Decision log writer | Action stopped; incident | MSG-P7-003 | Platform administrator
Load | Control total fails | Load checks | Load refused; previous load kept; product marked stale | MSG-P1-001 on affected screens | Data steward
Outbound | WIN file transfer fails | Outbox sender | Retry, then exception queue | Task to the owner | Platform administrator
Agent | No answer in 60 seconds | Agent runtime client | Rule result used; fallback recorded | Nothing changes for the user | Risk and model risk officer
Platform | Database unavailable | Service | 503; health check fails | Service unavailable page | SCB IT

Item | Policy
Outbound files and messages | Retry at 1, 5 and 15 minutes, then the exception queue (three retries, NFR-026 proposed)
Inbound loads | Check each hour until the load window closes; then the previous load stays in use
Agent calls | No retry inside the step; the rule result is used
Idempotency | Every retried action carries its idempotency key so a repeat has no effect

A stale data product shows its business date and a warning on every screen that uses it.

An outbound action waiting in the outbox shows as pending on the case timeline.

A case in the exception queue shows the reason and the owner of the fix.

During an outage the front end shows the service unavailable page and keeps unsent form input in the browser.

Event | Recovery
Failed load | Rerun from the job monitor after the source is fixed
Exception queue item | Fixed by its owner and resent; the resend is logged
Decision log chain break | Compliance and internal audit investigate; no entry is changed
Bad rule version | Previous version reloaded with an immediate date
Bad release | Feature flag off; previous tag redeployed if a flag does not cover it

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v3.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v3

secs.h: Recovery Workbench event and messaging design
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Document title | Recovery Workbench event and messaging design |
| Version | 3 |
| Status | In review |
| Date | 15 November 2026 |
| Owner | Solution architect |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 |

The Workbench publishes and consumes events inside the ACE service. Each event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the change that raises it, and delivered to its consumers at least once. There is no external event bus today. Source data arrives in ACE through ACE's own ingestion, and the Workbench learns that a source is ready by reading the ACE batch record, `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` (D-RCV-35, U1). EV-26 and EV-27 are raised from that record; every other event is raised by a Workbench change. If a same-day feed is approved under DL06, the same events are published to it without changing their payloads.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Ordering | Events for one case are processed in the order they were written, by a sequence per case in the outbox |
| Delivery | At least once; consumers are idempotent |
| Duplicates | Each event carries an event ID and an idempotency key; a repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40) |
| Transactions | The event is written in the same transaction as the change; no event without the change and no change without the event. EV-26 and EV-27 are exempt: they are raised from the ACE batch record, not from a Workbench change |
| Payload | References and codes; no personal data |
| Versioning | An event carries its schema version; consumers accept the current and previous version |
| Failure | A consumer failure retries; after the limit the event goes to the exception queue with its owner |

| ID | Event | Direction | Owning module | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EV-01 | CaseCreated | Published | Case and workflow | Allocation, ledger, reporting |
| EV-02 | CaseAllocated | Published | Case and workflow | Ledger, reporting |
| EV-03 | CaseAllocationFailed | Published | Case and workflow | Exception queue |
| EV-04 | CaseTransferred | Published | Case and workflow | Ledger, timers |
| EV-05 | CaseStateChanged | Published | Case and workflow | Timers, reporting |
| EV-06 | DeviationRaised | Published | Deviation handling | Timers, communications (contact stop) |
| EV-07 | DeviationCleared | Published | Deviation handling | Timers, communications |
| EV-08 | DecisionRecorded | Published | Decision center and log | Ledger, reporting |
| EV-09 | ApprovalRequested | Published | Decision center and log | Approval queue, notifications |
| EV-10 | TreatmentApproved | Published | TDR, settlement and deed in lieu | Communications, booking confirmation |
| EV-11 | TreatmentBooked | Published | Payments and posting | Case and workflow |
| EV-12 | PaymentMissed | Published | Payments and posting | Case and workflow (transfer rule) |
| EV-13 | NoticeGenerated | Published | Communications | Approval queue |
| EV-14 | NoticeDispatched | Published | Communications | Ledger |
| EV-15 | NoticeDelivered | Published | Communications | Timers (notice period) |
| EV-16 | DocumentStored | Published | Document hub | Intake agent, checklist |
| EV-17 | DocumentFieldsExtracted | Published | Document hub | Review queue, case |
| EV-18 | TimerDue | Published | Case and workflow | Rules component |
| EV-19 | TimerBreached | Published | Case and workflow | Notifications |
| EV-20 | InstructionIssued | Published | Partner management | Partner portal |
| EV-21 | PartnerResultSubmitted | Consumed | Partner portal | Case and workflow |
| EV-22 | AssetTakenOn | Published | Assets and auction | Timers (holding age) |
| EV-23 | LotAwarded | Published | Debt sale | Case and workflow (R-UNI-47) |
| EV-24 | WriteOffApproved | Published | Write-off and recovery | Posting |
| EV-25 | ProceedsMatched | Published | Payments and posting | Case and workflow |
| EV-26 | AceDataReady | Consumed | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_batch_status` | Case creation (JOB-02), reconciliation (JOB-04), payment matching (JOB-07), booking confirmation (JOB-08), write-off scan (JOB-16) |
| EV-27 | AceDataLate | Published | Recovery data engine, from `v_ace_batch_status` | Alerts, stale marker, data steward |
| EV-28 | AgentRunCompleted | Published | Agent runtime | Decision center, monitoring |

EV-26 and EV-27 are not raised by a Workbench change. They come from the ACE batch record, one row per source system and business date, which the ACE team adds in RWB-ACE-001.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Read path | `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` |
| Grain | One row per `source_system` and `business_date` |
| Fields | `source_system`, `business_date`, `status`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `record_count` |
| Ready | `status` is `COMPLETED` for the business date the Workbench expects |
| Late | That business date is still not complete at the Workbench cut-off for the source; the cut-off is configuration |
| Raised | EV-26 when the record completes; EV-27 when the cut-off passes first |
| Consumer action | Start the data jobs for that business date. No job reads a file and no job loads a row |

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| EV-26 AceDataReady | eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status, completedAt |
| EV-27 AceDataLate | eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status, completedAt |

The payload keeps the event naming convention. Each field maps one to one to the view column: `sourceSystem` is `source_system`, `businessDate` is `business_date`, `status` is `status`, and `completedAt` is `completed_at`.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5.pptx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Information Flow v5

secs.t:
COLLECTIONS AND RECOVERY TRANSFORMATION
Recovery Workbench: information flow
Henka Group, 15 November 2026
(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

secs.h: Slide 2. How information reaches the Workbench
secs.t:
2
Into ACE (ACE team), daily
Core bank (ALS)
EFS
SCBPDM
LIT
COLLINS models
NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID, on change
Into ACE (ACE team), less often
CCMS and SVAF, weekly
AMIS, monthly
RPS and WIN, weekly
GL, monthly
ACE ingestion
ACE team. Lands each source in ACE tables at the end of its business day
ACE checks
ACE ingestion checks each feed, takes it whole or not at all and records it in ace_batch_run
ACE
ACE database: source data in Tier 1 and Tier 2 ACE tables, and everything the Workbench writes
30 recovery.v_ace_* views, SELECT only: the only read path out of ACE source data
Recovery Workbench module: reads those views only; case, rules, decision log, document hub, partner portal
People and partners write directly through the screens and the partner portal
Out of the Workbench
Core bank: bookings made by the officer
WIN: notices for registered mail
NSS and LINE OA: messages
Power BI and COLLINS: daily batch to the data lake
Partners: instructions
Debt buyers: data tape
Bank log services: audit, PII and SOC events
The Workbench loads no source data: ACE ingests it and the Workbench reads views. Source data is end of day or older; what people enter is current.

secs.h: Slide 3. Integration patterns and the ones the Workbench uses
secs.t:
3
Pattern | Available at the bank | Used by the Workbench
Real time | REST, SOAP, MQ, HTTPS | Not used for data from other systems in Epics 1 and 2. Same-day candidates stay open under DL06
Event | Kafka | PII Kafka for personal data access logging. ACE batch status reaches the Workbench as AceDataReady and AceDataLate
Batch | File, SFTP, Azure Data Factory, Control-M, COLLINS | ACE ingestion, owned by the ACE team, for every inbound source. The Workbench runs no inbound load and reads 30 views
Manual | Excel file | Trackers leave system scope and retire through the Cutover plan. Data no system holds is entered on the case
Direct entry | Workbench screens and the partner portal | Everything the Workbench is the system of record for
The Workbench calls no system of record directly. Data comes in through ACE ingestion and is read through recovery.v_ace_* views; it leaves through ACE paths that already exist.

secs.h: Slide 4. Information that comes in daily through ACE
secs.t:
4
ID | Information | Source, ACE table | How often | Read through
I01 | Loan accounts: balances, interest, fees, days past due, bucket, classification, restructure flag | ALS, account | Daily, end of day | v_ace_account
I02 | Payments posted to each account | ALS, payment | Daily, end of day | v_ace_payment
I03 | Customer profile, identifiers and contact details | SCBPDM, customer and contacts | Daily, end of day | v_ace_customer, v_ace_contact
I04 | Collections history: contacts, action codes, promises | EFS, efs_action | Daily, end of day | v_ace_efs_action
I05 | Scores, expected return by route, sale price and sale success estimates, restructure scheme suggestions | COLLINS, collins_score | Daily; monthly for some models | v_ace_score
I06 | Litigation status and lawsuit numbers | LIT, lawsuit | Daily, end of day | v_ace_lawsuit
ACE ingests each source after the business day closes, into Tier 1 tables or the Tier 2 tables and columns in RWB-ACE-001. The Workbench reads the views the next morning, so a payment made today is seen tomorrow. Data products: I01 DP01; I02 DP01, DP13; I03 DP02; I04 DP05; I05 DP11; I06 DP07.

secs.h: Slide 5. Information that comes in weekly or monthly, or is entered
secs.t:
5
ID | Information | From | Path and how often | Read through; data product
I07 | Collateral records | CCMS | ACE ingestion to collateral_detail, weekly | v_ace_collateral; DP06
I08 | Appraisals | SVAF | ACE ingestion to valuation, weekly | v_ace_valuation; DP06
I09 | Assets held and asset sales | AMIS | ACE ingestion to npa_asset and npa_sale, monthly | v_ace_npa_asset, v_ace_npa_sale; DP06
I10 | Repossessed vehicles and stock | RPS | ACE ingestion to npa_asset, weekly | v_ace_npa_asset; DP06
I11 | Registered letters and proof of delivery | WIN | ACE ingestion to pod_receipt, weekly | v_ace_pod; DP07
I12 | Write-off postings | GL | ACE ingestion to gl_write_off, monthly | v_ace_write_off; DP13
I13 | Partner results: court dates, enforcement steps, appraisal reports, sale results | Partners | Partner portal in the Workbench, as entered | Entered in the Workbench; DP06, DP07, DP08
I14 | Documents | Scans, uploads, email, partners | Document hub, as received | Entered in the Workbench; DP10
I15 | Thai Credit Guarantee quota and claim deadlines | Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation | Entered by the guarantee officer, as received | Entered in the Workbench; DP04
I16 | Users and the roles they hold | Entra ID and the bank IAM | ACE sign-in; groups through ACE ingestion to iam_group | v_ace_iam_group; DP14

secs.h: Slide 6. Information that leaves the Workbench
secs.t:
6
ID | Information | To | Path | How often
O01 | Restructure, settlement and write-off bookings | Core bank (ALS) | The officer books in the core bank. The Workbench confirms the booking from ACE on the next business date | As approved
O02 | Demand, recall and sale notices for registered mail | WIN | File from the Workbench | Daily
O03 | SMS and LINE messages to customers | NSS and LINE OA | The ACE notification path | As sent
O04 | Case, queue, decision and outcome data for reporting | Power BI | Daily batch to the data lake | Daily
O05 | Decisions and outcomes for model learning | COLLINS | Daily batch to the data lake | Daily
O06 | Instructions to partners | Partners | Partner portal | As sent
O07 | Debt sale data tape | Debt buyers | File, through the data room for the lot | Per lot
O08 | Audit, personal data access and security events | Bank log services | The ACE audit, PII Kafka and SOC logs | As they happen

secs.h: Slide 7. How fresh each decision's inputs are
secs.t:
7
Decision | Inputs it uses | How fresh, per ace_batch_run | What that means
D6 entry | Account, arrears, customer, collections history | End of day | A case enters the morning after ACE shows it at 90 days past due
D5 restructure | Account, payments, restructure calculation, scheme suggestion | End of day | The offer is built on yesterday's balance. The officer confirms the figure in the core bank before booking
D6 route | Account, collateral value, scores, contact history | End of day; collateral weekly | An appraisal older than its age limit holds the route decision until replaced
D7 legal | Litigation status, notices and proof of delivery | End of day; proof of delivery weekly | A notice period starts from the delivery date, which can arrive up to a week late
D8 disposal | Asset, appraisal, price and sale success estimates | Monthly for assets; weekly for appraisals | The floor price uses the latest appraisal and the latest model estimate
D9 write-off | Balance, recoveries, GL posting | End of day; GL monthly | The posting is confirmed against the GL data in ACE each month

secs.h: Slide 8. When information does not arrive
secs.t:
8
What happens | What the Workbench does | Who is told | What the user sees
An ACE source is late | Raises AceDataLate at the source cut-off and marks the data product stale. The previous ACE business date stays in use | Data steward, platform administrator, ACE team | The age of the data on every screen that uses it
ACE refuses a feed | Reads the last complete business date from ace_batch_run. The previous ACE data stays in use | Data steward, ACE team | The same, with the product marked stale
A weekly or monthly source is late | Raises AceDataLate and marks the data product stale one business day after the ACE batch was due | ACE team, data steward | The age of the data on the case
A decision input is older than its age limit | Holds the decision. The task names the input and its age | Case owner | Which input is out of date and how to refresh it
A score is missing for an account | Shows the route decision without the score. The decision log records the missing input | Case owner, Risk and model risk officer | No score, and the reason
A booking is not seen on the next ACE business date | Raises a task to the officer who recorded the booking. The case stays in its waiting state | Officer, team manager | The booking marked as not confirmed
An outbound file is not acknowledged | Sends it again. After the third failure, raises a task to the owning team. A notice timer starts only on confirmed dispatch | Owning team, platform administrator | The notice marked as not sent

secs.h: Slide 9. The checks ACE data passes
secs.t:
9
Check | What it tests | If it fails
Business date | ACE ingestion: the feed is for the expected business date and is not a repeat of one already taken | ACE refuses the feed
Structure | Every expected field is present with the expected type and length | ACE refuses the feed
Control totals | Record count and balance totals match the totals the source sends | ACE refuses the feed
Keys | Every record has its business key, and no key appears twice | ACE refuses the feed
View conformance | Workbench build: every v_ace_* view compiles, nothing references public and the role cannot write | The build fails and nothing deploys
Batch complete | ace_batch_run shows the source complete for the expected business date by its cut-off | AceDataLate; the data product is marked stale
Reconciliation | Case accounts reconcile to v_ace_account; every business key resolves | Alert the data steward
ACE ingestion records each feed's business date, record count and result in ace_batch_run. Each view carries the business date, so a decision can show the age of every input.

secs.h: Slide 10. Where same-day information would change the result
secs.t:
10
Information | What a day's delay can cause | How the Workbench works without it
A payment | A customer who paid this morning is contacted this afternoon | Staff check the core bank for today's payments before a call or a letter
A complaint or dispute | Contact continues while a complaint is open | Raised on the case by the person who receives it. Contact stops at once
A death or bankruptcy notice | Collection action against an estate or a debtor under protection | Raised on the case by the officer. Contact and legal steps stop at once
A promise kept or broken | The next step is a day late | The next step runs on the next ACE business date
A court date change | A hearing prepared for the wrong date | The law firm records the new date in the partner portal
Assumed: ACE end of day data for all Epic 1 and Epic 2 work (D-RCV-35), with events added later for named same-day triggers. Which interfaces need real-time data stays open under DL06.

secs.h: Slide 11. Gaps and the assumptions taken
secs.t:
11
What is open | Assumption the flow takes | Decision
Which interfaces need real-time data | ACE end of day data for every source; events added later for named triggers | DL06; D-RCV-35
Whether any legacy system is enhanced | None. The Workbench reads ACE through views and writes through ACE paths only | D-RCV-35, was DL12
Which systems carry the case identifier | The Workbench only. The account number is the join | DL21
The difference accepted between an ACE feed and its source | Zero. ACE refuses a feed that does not reconcile; cases reconcile to v_ace_account | DL25
How much EFS history ACE holds | The contact outcomes the business lead names, for the collection period only | DL29
Who builds SMS and LINE dispatch | A bank-wide service where one exists; the Workbench squads otherwise | DL30
How partners reach the partner portal from outside the bank | The architecture change is raised in November. Law firms first need the console at Epic 5 | DL03
Whether the ACE team accepts RWB-ACE-001 and its dates | Tier 2 tables needed by 21 November; until then the Tier 2 views and their features stay behind flags | DL43, open

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Document title | Recovery Workbench interface specifications |
| Version | 3 |
| Status | In review |
| Date | 15 November 2026 |
| Owner | Solution architect |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 |

The Workbench loads no source data. ACE ingests every inbound source named here, and the recovery module reads the result through the read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views. The inbound field maps below are the ACE ingestion specification: they say what ACE must deliver for the Workbench read path, not what the Workbench copies. The ACE team owns the inbound interfaces and the tables behind them, raised once in RWB-ACE-001. The Workbench owns the outbound interfaces and the case.

No component calls a system of record directly. Data arrives in ACE through ACE's own ingestion, the Workbench reads it through 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, and outbound data leaves through the paths ACE already has. There is no inbound run, sign-off or data quality gate inside the Workbench; those move to the ACE ingestion story.

| ID | System | Direction | Owner | Approach | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_account` | Daily, end of day |
| INT-02 | Core bank (ALS) | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_payment` | Daily, end of day |
| INT-04 | SCBPDM | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` | Daily, end of day |
| INT-07 | EFS | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_efs_action` | Daily, end of day |
| INT-08 | COLLINS models | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_score` | Daily; monthly for some models |
| INT-09 | LIT | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_lawsuit` and `v_ace_hearing` | Daily, end of day |
| INT-10 | CCMS | In, into ACE | ACE team | ACE ingestion, read through `v_ace_collateral` and `v_ace_collateral_detail` | Weekly |

These checks run in ACE, not in the Workbench. They are the ingestion contract for every inbound interface above and are owned by the ACE team in RWB-ACE-001. The Workbench runs none of them: it reads the result from `v_ace_batch_status` and never sees a refused feed.

| Check | What it tests | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Business date | The feed is for the expected business date and is not a repeat | ACE refuses the feed |
| Structure | Every expected field is present with the expected type and length | ACE refuses the feed |
| Control totals | Record count and balance totals match the totals the source sends | ACE refuses the feed |
| Keys | Every record has its key, and no key appears twice | ACE refuses the feed |
| References | Each account, customer or asset matches a record ACE holds | ACE holds the row and reports it in its exception list |
| Lists of values | Each coded value is in its list of values | ACE holds the row and reports it in its exception list |
| Movement | Changes against the previous business date are within the expected range | ACE loads and alerts the data steward |

| Check | What it tests | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Layout | Every field matches the agreed file specification and template version | Do not send; raise to the platform administrator |
| Control totals | The header count and amount totals match the rows in the file | Do not send; raise to the platform administrator |
| Acknowledgement | The receiving system confirms the file | Hold the case step and send again |

Checks every outbound file passes
Applied to every outbound file. The inbound checks are the ACE ingestion contract, owned by the ACE team in RWB-ACE-001; the Workbench reads completion from v_ace_batch_status and runs no inbound check.
Check | What it tests | If it fails
Layout | Every field matches the agreed file specification and template version | Do not send; raise to the platform administrator
Control totals | The header count and amount totals match the rows in the file | Do not send; raise to the platform administrator
Acknowledgement | The receiving system confirms the file | Hold the case step and send again

Key
What each term means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Approach | ACE ingestion | ACE receives the COLLINS feed or the file and lands it in its own tables; the Workbench loads nothing and reads the result through a v_ace_* view
Standard | OpenAPI 3.1 | Request and response interfaces
Standard | AsyncAPI 3.0 | Event interfaces
Standard | File specification | Layout, control totals, business date and checks
Column | Owner of the fix | Who is told and acts when the interface fails
Direction | In, into ACE | ACE ingests the source; the Workbench reads it through a read-only v_ace_* view
Trigger | ACE batch complete | The per-source record in v_ace_batch_status for the business date
Owner | ACE team | Owns the inbound source interface, the ACE tables behind it and the ingestion checks

Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 runtime view

Kind | Examples | Channel | Proof
Statutory notice | Demand, recall, statutory sale notice, guarantor notice | Registered mail through WIN | Proof of delivery from WIN
Customer letter | Offer, settlement terms, restructure terms | Registered or ordinary mail; e-signature link | Delivery record; signed copy
Message | Reminder, offer ending, payment received | SMS through NSS; LINE OA | Delivery receipt from the channel

A rule raises the notice (R-LIT-03 for demand and recall).

The Workbench checks the contact stop and the consented channel. A stop holds the notice (R-LIT-05).

It fills the current template version approved by Legal for the type, product and language.

The litigation officer approves the notice where the template requires approval.

The notice goes to WIN in the daily outbound file through the outbox.

WIN returns the barcode, then the proof of delivery in the weekly file.

The delivery date starts the notice period (R-LIT-07). No proof within the window marks the notice unserved (R-LIT-08).

Item | Design
Held as | Template rows with code, version, language, product group, body and Legal approval
Merge fields | From a catalog held as data; a template may use only catalog fields
Approval | Legal counsel approves each version; Compliance approves customer wording
Withdrawal | A withdrawn template holds generation (R-LIT-04)
Language | Thai by default; English where the customer chose English (DL10)

No message goes to a channel without consent; statutory notices continue when consent is withdrawn (R-UNI-10).

A contact stop for a complaint, death or legal hold stops messages and letters except statutory notices where the law requires them.

Contact times and frequency follow the Debt Collection Act and bank policy, held as reference data.

Every message sent is written to the interaction ledger.

Item | Volume
Registered letters | About 1,900 a month
Proofs of delivery | About 1,900 a month
Messages | Set by the contact strategy; sized on the ACE notification path

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided

Element | Design
What it is | A decision table evaluator inside the recovery module of ACE. No external rules engine
What it holds | 448 routing rules in ten route sets, the allocation table, thresholds, limits and timers, all as versioned data rows
Table form | DMN 1.4 decision tables: inputs, conditions, output, hit policy FIRST in row order

Testing | Every row names its test case. The rule table harness runs every row before a version can be approved
Approval | The process owner approves; Risk approves where a limit or threshold moves
Deployment | A version takes effect from its valid from date. No code release
Rollback | The previous version is loaded again with an immediate date
Record | Every evaluation that changes a case writes the rule ID, the version and the inputs to the decision log

Route set | Rules | Decision
Restructure | 37 | D5, D6
Settlement | 27 | D6.4
Deed in lieu | 37 | D6.4
Guarantee claim | 32 | D6.5, D6.6
Litigation | 79 | D7
Asset disposal | 72 | D8.1 to D8.3
Debt sale | 41 | D8.4
Write-off | 51 | D9
Deviations | 22 | X1 to X7
Universal rules | 50 | All
Total | 448

secs.h: 3. The structure of a rule row
secs.t:
Column | Meaning | Example
Rule ID | Unique, never reused | R-SET-05
Route set | The stage the rule belongs to | SETTLEMENT
From state | The case state the rule listens in, or ANY_ACTIVE | OFFER_PREPARED
Event | The event that fires the rule | OFFER_PREPARED
Condition | A FEEL expression over case file items; blank means any | offer_amount < floor_amount
Action | What the Workbench does | Route the offer to the approver with the gap to the floor
To state | The state the case moves to | AWAITING_APPROVAL
Owner | Who owns the next state | Approver by delegation of authority
Timer | The clock the next state carries, from the service level table | 5 working days
Test case ID | The test the row must pass | TC-R-SET-05
Valid from and to | When the row applies | 30 Nov 2026
Version | The route set version the row belongs to | SETTLEMENT-2026.11

An event reaches a case: a load, a screen action, a partner result, a timer or another module.

The evaluator reads the version of the route set in force for the case. A case keeps the version it was decided under (R-UNI-38).

It selects the rows whose from state matches the case state, or ANY_ACTIVE, and whose event matches.

It tests the conditions in row order. The first row that holds fires (hit policy FIRST).

If no row holds, the case goes to the exception queue and the gap is logged (R-UNI-41).

The decision log entry is written first. If the write fails, nothing changes (R-UNI-39).

The action runs: the state moves, tasks and timers are set, outbound work goes to the outbox.

Step | Who | What happens
Prepare | Center of excellence analyst | Writes or changes rows in the route set workbook, with a test case per row
Load | Reference data administrator | Loads the file; structure, references, states and lists are checked; a failed check refuses the file whole
Test | Rule table harness | Runs every row against its test case in SIT and attaches the result to the version
Review | Process owner | Reads the change report: rows added, changed and removed, with the test result
Approve | Process owner; Risk where a limit moves | Approves with a valid from date. The maker cannot approve
In force | Workbench | New decisions use the version from its date; decided cases keep their version
Roll back | Reference data administrator with the owner | Loads the previous version with an immediate date

Every rule has a unique ID.

Every from state and to state exists in the route set.

Every state that is not an end state has a rule out.

No two rules share the same from state, event and condition.

Every rule names its owner and its action.

Every route set has at least one end state.

Every row has a test case and the test passes.

Item | Target
One evaluation | Under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile (NFR-011, proposed under DL11)
Evaluations a month | About 12 for each open case, about 320,000 a month by the end of 2027
Caching | The route set version in force is cached in memory and refreshed when a version takes effect

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL22 | Service levels per case state | Placeholders loaded; escalation from the day values are supplied
DL23 | Caseload caps and queue rules | Placeholders loaded
DL24 | Which rules are loaded in Epic 1 | Allocation, transfer, timers and the universal rules

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v3.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Security and access design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench security and access design
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Change | D-RCV-35 (ADR-010): the Workbench reads ACE through read-only recovery.v_ace_* views and runs no load. No tokenization at load and no load service identity; the view owner and the read-only ACE grant are added (sections 1, 2, 5, 7 to 11)
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 crosscutting concepts, with C4 component views and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoints

Concern | Design | Status
Sign-in | Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication through the ACE front end; OpenID Connect with the authorization code flow and PKCE | ACE pattern
Identity to role | Entra ID group membership, granted through bank IAM, maps to Workbench roles held as data | Agreed; groups DL40
Permission check | Every endpoint checks the role, the capability area, the right and the scope before it runs | Designed
Scope | Own cases, team, region or all, applied as a filter on every query | Designed
Approval limits | The delegation of authority table checked before an approval is accepted | Designed; limits DL18
Masking | Personal fields masked in the response at the API unless the role may see them (E1-037). The national ID is never read in clear: v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked and id_no_last4 only. Every read of a personal field is audited | Designed; rules DL26
Sessions | Token lifetime, inactivity timeout and break-glass window set by SCB IT security | Open, DL38
Partners | Separate partner identities through the external gateway, limited to the cases placed with the firm | Open, DL03
Service identities | Managed identities with credentials in Key Vault; one identity per non-human actor. No data load identity: ACE ingests every source | ACE pattern
ACE data access | Read only. The recovery service role holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views and nothing else; the views are owned by ace_view_owner, which reads the public ACE tables. No direct public read, no write, PUBLIC revoked | Designed; D-RCV-35, RWB-E1-069
Logging | Access log in the Workbench, ACE audit log, PII log through PII Kafka, security events to the SOC log | ACE pattern

The Workbench is a module of the ACE service. It reuses the ACE sign-in, access check, audit, PII logging and SOC logging. The recovery module adds its roles, permissions, scope rules, masking rules and approval limits as data, and checks them on every request. The Workbench loads, copies and transforms no source data. ACE ingests every source into the ACE database, and the recovery module reads it only through SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views (D-RCV-35, ADR-010).

Actor | How it reaches the Workbench | Identity
Bank staff | ACE front end on the bank network, through the internal application gateway with web application firewall | Entra ID user with multi-factor authentication
Partners | Partner portal through the external gateway, once external access is approved (DL03) | Partner identity, separate from bank identities
Customers | No sign-in. Offers and listings reach them through SCB Easy, LINE OA, SMS, branches and HOME.SCB | Bank channel identity
Non-human actors | Service to service inside the ACE namespace; outbound through the outbox | Managed identity
Agents | Through the tool gateway only | Managed identity per agent, limited by the autonomy level

The person opens the ACE front end. The front end redirects to Entra ID with the authorization code flow and PKCE.

Entra ID applies multi-factor authentication and the bank conditional access policies.

The front end receives the tokens. The ID token names the person; the access token carries the group claims for the ACE application.

On the first request the service resolves the groups to Workbench roles, the scope and the masking profile, and writes the session start to the access log.

A person with no Workbench role is refused with MSG-P4-001. A person whose groups hold a conflicting role pair is refused and an incident is raised.

Rule | Value used until DL38 is decided | Set by
Access token lifetime | The ACE value | SCB IT security
Inactivity timeout | 15 minutes, with a warning at 13 minutes | SCB IT security
Maximum session length | One working day | SCB IT security
Group change | Takes effect at the next request; a removed role ends the session | Workbench
Concurrent sessions | One active session per person per device | Workbench
Break-glass window | Four hours, then the grant ends with no action by anyone | SCB IT security

Every endpoint declares the capability area and the right it needs. The check runs in the service before any data is read, using the role permissions in force for the request date.

Step | What is checked | Refused with
1 | The session is valid and the person holds at least one Workbench role | HTTP 401; MSG-P4-001
2 | One of the person's roles holds the right (C, R, U, D or A) in the capability area the endpoint declares | HTTP 403; MSG-P4-002
3 | The record is inside the person's scope: own cases, team, region or all | HTTP 404; MSG-P4-003
4 | For an approval: the person's approval level and the delegation of authority limit for the decision, product and amount | HTTP 409; MSG-P7-001
5 | For an approval: the person did not prepare or propose the decision | HTTP 409; MSG-P7-002
6 | The response is masked by the person's masking profile before it leaves the service | Not refused; fields masked

Scope is applied in the query, so a record outside the scope is never read. A refusal returns 404 for records outside the scope, so the response does not reveal that the record exists.

The permission matrix, the scope per role and the masking rules are versioned data. A change is a validated load with a valid from date and needs no code release.

Control | Design
National ID | ACE holds the national ID or passport number (customer.identification_number). The Workbench never reads it in clear: v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked, with only the last four digits shown, and id_no_last4. Nothing is tokenized at load, because there is no load; role masking at the API (E1-037) replaces the former id_no_token
Tokenization | None at load. There is no Workbench load to tokenize, so there is no id_no_token column and no token vault in the source path. Masking is applied in v_ace_customer (id_no_masked, id_no_last4) and by E1-037 at the API
Masking | Name, address, phone, email and account numbers are masked at the API by the masking profile of the role (E1-037). v_ace_contact returns the full phone, email and address, because notices and calls need them, so the API mask is the control. The profile is a data row per role and field
Unmasking | A role allowed to unmask a field does so per record; each unmask is written to the PII log
Audit of reads | Every read of a personal field, including each read through v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact, is written to the PII log through PII Kafka. The control is the read-only grant, E1-037 masking and the audit log together; the mask in a view is not a PDPA control on its own
Exports | Exports carry the masking of the person who runs them. A debt sale data tape passes the masking check before the data room opens
Test data | Synthetic only in DEV. Masked copies from the PII service in SIT and UAT
Logs and prompts | No personal data in application logs, test fixtures or agent prompts. The PDPA lint gate checks code before merge
Retention | Each data product and document type carries a retention class (DL26). Expiry is held while a legal hold is in place

Partner users reach the partner portal through the external gateway once the architecture team approves external access (DL03).

Each partner user has a partner identity, separate from bank identities, with multi-factor authentication.

The partner and agency manager requests partner users; the role owner approves. Accounts end when the firm's contract ends.

A partner user sees only the instructions placed with their firm. Scope is the firm, set on the instruction.

Partner uploads pass a file type check and a malware scan before they reach the document hub.

Until external access is in place, partners keep their current channels and bank staff record partner results.

Item | Design
Managed identities | One per non-human actor: case workflow, rules component, OCR pipeline, decision log writer, agent platform
Load identity | None. The Workbench runs no inbound load, so it holds no source load identity, no file share credential and no staging account. ACE ingestion uses its own identity and writes the ACE tables
Secrets | Key Vault, reached by managed identity. No secret in code, configuration or prompts. The secret scan gate checks every merge
Database | The service connects with its managed identity. The recovery schema is still owned by the service; people do not hold write access in production. No recovery migration creates or alters a table in the ACE public schema
Read-only ACE access | The recovery service role (recovery_svc) holds USAGE on schema recovery and SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only. It holds no SELECT on any public ACE table and no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on any ACE table or view, so a direct public read or a write fails in the database catalog, not only in code review. This is the read-only ACE service identity of the Admin and Access Model v5
View owner | The v_ace_* views are owned by ace_view_owner, a NOLOGIN ACE role that holds SELECT on the public ACE tables the views read and writes neither schema. It is not a Workbench role and nobody signs in as it. A view runs with its owner's privileges, so any row-level security ACE adds later is applied inside the view
PUBLIC | All privileges on the recovery tables and views are revoked from PUBLIC. A role reads a view only through an explicit grant
Grant check | The view conformance test in RWB-E1-069 runs in the pipeline and fails the build if recovery_svc can select a public table or write any table, if a v_ace_* view does not compile, or if a constraint in schema recovery references a public table
Agents | An agent reaches a system only through the tool gateway. The gateway holds the permissions; the agent holds none
Network | Private endpoints to storage and the database. No public endpoint on the service

Record | Holds | Read by
Access log | Sign-ins, refusals, grants, removals, break-glass use and the versions in force. Append only | Application owner, security administrator, Compliance, internal audit
Decision log | Every decision with inputs, rule version, recommendation, approver and action. Append only and hash chained | Internal audit, Risk, center of excellence
ACE audit log | Every change made through the service | Security administrator, internal audit
PII log | Every read and unmask of a personal field, including reads through v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact, through PII Kafka | Compliance, internal audit
SOC log | Security events: repeated refusals, conflict refusals, break-glass, failed sign-ins | SCB security operations

Threat | Example | Control
Spoofing | A stolen password used to sign in | Multi-factor authentication; conditional access; SOC alert on unusual sign-in
Tampering | A decision or legal document changed after the fact | Append-only, hash-chained decision log; write-once container for legal documents; no write grant on any ACE table or view
Repudiation | An approver denies approving | Decision log entry with the approver identity, level and time
Information disclosure | Customer data read outside the role or sent outside the bank | Scope filter; masking (E1-037); national ID masked in v_ace_customer; SELECT on recovery.v_ace_* only, no direct public read; PII log; no personal data in exports beyond the role
Denial of service | A partner floods the portal | External gateway rate limits; web application firewall
Elevation of privilege | A person grants themselves a business role | Separation of duty at grant and at sign-in; access review every six months (DL38)

Test | Passes when | Signed by
Sign-in per role | Each role in the release signs in and shows the right roles, scope and masking | Role owner
Endpoint permissions | An automated test calls every endpoint with a role that lacks the right and receives 403 | QA lead
Scope | A role reads a record outside its scope and receives 404 | QA lead
Masking | Three roles read the same case and see the fields their profiles allow | Compliance
Read-only ACE grant | The view conformance test passes: recovery_svc reads every v_ace_* view, cannot select a public table and cannot insert, update or delete on any table | Tech lead
Approval limit | An approval above the limit routes to the next level | Risk
Container and secret scans | No vulnerability above the bank threshold; no secret in code | Tech lead
Penetration test | Before the partner portal opens to users outside the bank | SCB IT security

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL01 | Whether access is granted centrally or by the application owner | Application owner administration
DL03 | How partners reach the partner portal from outside the bank | Partners keep current channels until external access is approved
DL26 | Retention and masking per data product and document type | Masking profiles as proposed in the data classification
DL38 | Session, inactivity and break-glass timers | The values in 3.2
DL40 | Entra ID groups for the Workbench roles | One group per role per environment
DL43 | Whether the ACE team accepts the RWB-ACE-001 scope and dates, by 21 November 2026 | Section A views and grants only; Section B features stay behind flags
