secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Target architecture, all eight epics

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench target architecture
Version | 5
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42, with C4 context and container views and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoints

The Recovery Workbench owns every recovery case from 90 days past due to close for Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME. It is the recovery module of ACE.

Goal | What it means
One case record from day 90 to close | Every recovery case is held once, with one owner, one clock and one history, in the same application as collection
Change without a release | Every rule, limit, threshold, template, queue, role, timer and route is a versioned data row
Every decision traceable | Each decision is logged once with its inputs, the rule and model versions, the approver and the outcome
Safe use of AI | Agents prepare and recommend through one runtime, start in shadow and fall back to the rules when they do not answer
Monthly releases | One production release at each month end, shared with the collection squad, from November 2026 to June 2027

Constraint | What it means | Status
Built on ACE | The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end | Taken
Modular monolith | Common, collection and recovery modules by folder, with boundaries checked at build time | Taken
Programmatic workflow | Case, stage and task state held in the database and moved by code. No Temporal | Taken
CMMN 1.1 | Case, stage, milestone, task, sentry, event listener and case file item mean the same in both modules | Taken
Data through ACE | Source data lands in the ACE database through ACE ingestion. The recovery module reads it through 30 read-only views and holds no copy | Taken; D-RCV-35, ADR-010; ACE additions DL43
ACE technology | Spring Boot, React on Vite, PostgreSQL, Entra ID, the bank IAM, PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs | Taken
Document hub built here | The Workbench holds recovery documents as their system of record | Taken; storage pattern DL27
No legacy enhancement | The Workbench reads source data through ACE and writes through ACE only | Taken; D-RCV-35 (supersedes DL12 option A)

No component calls a system of record directly. Source data lands in the ACE database through ACE ingestion, and the recovery module reads it through recovery.v_ace_* views. Work for other systems leaves through paths ACE already has.

Actor or system | What passes | How
Bank staff | Case owners, officers, approvers, committees, control functions | Workbench screens in the ACE front end, signed in through Entra ID
Partners | Law firms, agencies, valuers, auction vendors, debt buyers, RAMC | Partner portal, once partner access from outside the bank is in place (DL03)
Customers | Borrowers, guarantors, heirs, bidders | Existing bank channels only: SCB Easy, LINE OA, SMS, branches, HOME.SCB
COLLINS | Account, customer, collections history, litigation status, scores | ACE ingestion, daily batch into the ACE database
CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, SCBPDM, NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID | Collateral detail, appraisals, assets, litigation, registered mail, write-off postings, product holding, credit decisions, signature requests, group mapping | ACE ingestion into the ACE database. No Workbench load
Core bank (ALS) | Bookings for restructures, settlements and write-offs | Made by the officer; confirmed in ACE on the next business date
NSS and LINE OA | SMS and LINE messages | The ACE notification path
Power BI and the data lake | Reporting and model learning | Daily batch out
Enterprise AI platform | The model endpoint the agents call | Private endpoint in the SCB tenant (DL33)

| Principle
1 | Everything that a business person may want to change is a versioned data row, changed through a validated load without a code release
2 | One service, one repository, one front end. A module calls another only through its published interface or an application event
3 | Each module owns its tables. No module reads another module's tables directly; the recovery module reads ACE source data only through its own read-only views
4 | No component calls a system of record directly. ACE ingests the source data and the recovery module reads it through read-only views; outbound work leaves through existing ACE paths
5 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed
6 | An agent reaches a system only through the tool gateway and holds no credential. When it does not answer, the rule result is used
7 | Personal data is masked in the views and at the API unless the role is allowed to see it. No personal data in code, tests, logs or prompts
8 | Every value read from ACE carries its business date, so every decision can show the age of its inputs

Module | Built by | Holds
Common | ACE team | Sign-in and access checks, audit and PII logging, the shared case view, shared entities (customer, account, product, collateral, asset), shared tasks such as the restructure calculator, the notification path
Collection | Collection squad | Phone, field, FCR and restructure work, as split under DL14
Recovery | TechX recovery squads | Recovery stages, tasks and screens, the rules component, the decision center and log, the document hub, the partner portal, the read-only ACE views and the extension tables

A module calls another only through its published interface or an application event.

Each module owns its tables; another module reads them only through the owning module's interface.

The recovery module reads ACE source data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: no direct read of a public table, no write and no foreign key into ACE (ADR-010).

A boundary test runs in every build and fails it on any violation.

A recovery component the collection module also needs moves to the common module by agreement with the ACE team.

| Module | Where it lives | What it owns | First in
P1 | Recovery data engine | Recovery | Read-only ACE source views, the extension tables, reconciliation to the ACE account list, freshness from the ACE batch record | E1
P2 | Integration | Common and recovery | Outbound files and adapters, the ACE integration paths | E1
P3 | Case and workflow | Recovery, with the common case view | Case record, CMMN state, queues, allocation, timers, the rules component | E1 core, E2 screens
P4 | Access and administration | Common, with recovery roles as data | Roles, permissions, scope, masking, delegation of authority table, access log | E1; E2 partners; E8 full administration
P5 | Document hub | Recovery | Store, index, OCR, classification, extraction, review queue, retention, custody | E1 store and OCR; E2 generation
P6 | Communications | Common path, recovery templates | Letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery | E1 notices; E2 dispatch; E4 self-service
P7 | Decision center and log | Recovery | Recommendation with reasons, approval within delegation, decision log store and writer | E1 log; E2 routing; E3 center
P8 | Payments and posting | Recovery | Payment and proceeds matching, fees, posting files | E2 matching; E4
P9 | Reporting | Recovery, with Power BI | Baseline measures, steering dashboard, operational and regulatory reports | E1 baseline; E2 dashboard
P10 | Agent runtime | Recovery, calling the Enterprise AI platform | Orchestrator, tool gateway, guardrails, prompt store, evaluation, autonomy levels | E1 shadow; E2 L1

| Module | What it owns | First in
S1 | Valuation and route | D6 route decision with COLLINS return by route and the route agent | E4
S2 | TDR, settlement and deed in lieu | Treatment record, contracts, booking, plan timers | E2 foundations; E3
S3 | Guarantees and guarantors | TCG and insurance claims, guarantor notices and pursuit | E4
S4 | Litigation and enforcement | Notices, law firm instruction, hearings, judgment, enforcement | E2 notices; E5
S5 | Assets and auction | Asset record, holding, floor price, listing, auction rounds, RAMC | E3; E4
S6 | Debt sale | Lot building, data room, buyer terms, award, transfer | E5 data; E6 screens
S7 | Write-off and recovery | Eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off | E6
S8 | Deviation handling | X1 to X7: screening, pause, handling, return | E2 screening; E7
S9 | Partner management | Panel, allocation, fees, scorecards, conduct | E6 panel; E7 scoring

Step | What happens
Event arrives | An ACE refresh, a screen action, a partner result, a timer or another module
Rules evaluated | The rules component finds the rule for the state and the event
Decision logged | Rule version, inputs and approver written. A failed write stops here
Action taken | Next state, tasks, owner, queue, documents or notices
Timer set | The next due date is stored for the scheduler
Work queued | Work for other systems goes to an outbox with retry

Case, stage and task state are rows in the ACE database. A wait of weeks is a row with a state and a stored due date. Timers run on Quartz. Automated chains to other systems run on Spring Batch with an outbox, retry and an exception queue. No workflow engine is used.

Case model, CMMN 1.1 | Count
Stages | 10
Milestones | 30
Tasks | 150
Event listeners | 53
Sentries (rules) | 448
Case file items | 12

What | How it works
Rules as rows | Each route set is a decision table: from state, event and condition in; action, next state, owner and timer out. Each row has an ID, a version, valid from and valid to dates, an approver and a test case
Hit policy Unique | For one state and one event in a route set, at most one condition holds, so one rule fires
Evaluator | A decision table evaluator in the recovery module reads the rows in force and returns the action. ACE has no rules engine today
Loading a change | A new version is loaded, checked against the schema and the completeness checks, and refused whole if any check fails
Open cases | A case keeps the rule version it was decided under. New decisions use the version in force on the day
Universal rules | Rules that apply in every state, such as a cure, a hold or a death, are evaluated before the route rules
Epic 1 | Allocation, assignment and transfer rules only. The route decision follows in Epic 4 (DL24)

Part | What it does
Orchestrator | Runs the decision steps and applies the autonomy level
Tool gateway | The only way an agent reaches a system. No agent holds a credential
Guardrail checker | Checks every output against its schema, the allowed actions and a confidence floor
Prompt and policy store | Versioned, so a run can be reproduced
Evaluation harness | Labeled sets scored before a result is used
Model endpoint | On the approved endpoint in the SCB tenant (DL33)

Level | The agent | A person
L0 | Nothing. The rule decides | Everything
L1 | Recommends, with its reasons | Decides. Every decision starts here after a shadow run
L2 | Acts inside a narrow band | Reviews a sample and the exceptions
L3 | Acts across the decision | Reviews by exception
L4 | Acts and closes | Monitors the measures

Agents run in shadow first. A decision moves up one level on evidence and drops one level on a guardrail breach. When an agent does not answer in time, the rule result is used and the case still routes.

Environment | Data | Deployed | Notes
DEV | Synthetic data | On every merge into main | Four slots planned, one available (DL35)
SIT | Masked data | On a release tag | Two slots planned, one available (DL35)
UAT | Masked data | In the week before each release | Shared with the collection squad
PROD | Live data | In the monthly change window (DL34) | ACE namespace on the shared ACE AKS clusters

Nine pipeline gates run before every merge: build and unit tests, lint, secret scan, PDPA lint, container scan, module boundary, integration and contract tests, AI first-pass review, and human approval. A change that fails SIT or UAT has its feature flag switched off and the release goes ahead without it.
The Workbench holds no source data. ACE holds it, and the Workbench reads it through 30 read-only views.

Tier | Owner | What it holds | Count
1 | ACE team, read only | ACE tables that exist today, read through a view and never altered | 22 tables, 16 views
2 | ACE team | New ACE tables and columns for source data that ACE does not hold | 14 tables, 12 columns, 14 views
3 | Workbench | 1:1 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys | 4 tables
4 | Workbench | Case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, debt sale, documents, decision log, reference, outbox, flags, agents | 88 tables
Removed | - | Source copies, load machinery and the 6 columns the ACE story absorbs | 20 tables, 243 fields

The Workbench schema is 92 tables: 4 extension tables and 88 retained tables. With the 30 views, the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields, in place of 108 tables and 1,256 fields. Tier 1 views ship with RWB-E1-069; the Tier 2 views ship when RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).

The tier table above is the normative data tier diagram for this document. Slide 11 of the Recovery Workbench Target Architecture v5 deck draws the same four tiers and the single read path.

The elements that hold the Workbench's own data:

Element | What it holds
ACE database (PostgreSQL) | Case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, disposal and money records; reference data; the decision log and the interaction ledger. ACE also holds the source data the Workbench reads, written by ACE ingestion
Blob storage, write-once container | Documents. Legal document types cannot be overwritten
14 data products | Each with one system of record, one read path and one freshness
92 tables, 30 views, 1,366 fields | In the bank TSD section T3 form, with seven standard columns on every entity. 122 dictionary objects: 92 tables and 30 views
Decision log | Append only, hash chained, one entry per decision
Out to the data lake | Case, queue, decision and outcome data by daily batch for Power BI and COLLINS

Control | How it works
Sign-in | Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication
Roles | 54 roles held as data, granted by Entra ID group membership through the bank IAM
Permissions | A matrix of roles against 14 capability areas, held as versioned data, checked on every endpoint
Scope | Own cases, team, region or all, set per role
Masking | Personal data masked in the views and at the API unless the role is allowed to see it
Approval limits | The delegation of authority table as reference data, checked before an approval is accepted
Logs | Access to personal data through PII Kafka; security events to the SOC log; every decision to the decision log
Break-glass | Emergency access with a reason and a review window
Partners | Their own identities, scoped to the cases placed with them (DL03)

Epic | Release | Added
E1 | 30 Nov 2026 | P1 read-only ACE views for Tier 1 (RWB-E1-069) and the extension tables, reconciliation and freshness; P3 case record, state model and rules component with allocation rules; P4 sign-in and roles; P5 document store and OCR; P6 notice generation; P7 decision log store; P9 baseline; P10 agent runtime in shadow; Tier 2 after RWB-ACE-001: the Tier 2 views ship when the ACE additions land (DL43)
E2 | 31 Dec 2026 | P3 queue and transfer screens; P4 partner identities; P5 document generation; P6 dispatch and proof of delivery; P7 approval routing; P8 matching skeleton; P9 steering dashboard; S2 treatment record; S4 notice approval; S8 deviation screening
E3 | 31 Jan 2027 | S2 settlement and deed in lieu to booking; S5 asset record, floor price and listing; P7 decision center
E4 | 28 Feb 2027 | S1 route decision with COLLINS and the route agent; S3 guarantee and TCG claims; S5 auction rounds and RAMC; P6 customer self-service; P8 posting
E5 | 31 Mar 2027 | S4 litigation end to end with law firms through the partner portal; S6 lot data and data room
E6 | 30 Apr 2027 | S6 debt sale screens and award; S7 write-off and committee; S9 partner panel, allocation and fees
E7 | 31 May 2027 | S8 deviations end to end; S9 partner scoring, conduct and the field app
E8 | 30 Jun 2027 | P4 full administration; conduct checks; autonomy step-ups; regulatory returns; hardening

Quality | Target or position | Status
Availability | 99.9% in business hours | Proposed, DL11
Screen response | Under 2 seconds | Proposed, DL11
Agent response | Within 60 seconds; after that the rule result is used | Proposed, DL11
Recovery point and time | Set by SCB IT | Open, DL11
Volume | About 23,600 open cases at go-live and 26,500 at the end of 2027; about 410 concurrent users | Sized; bank confirms under DL15
Retention and masking | Per data product and document type | Open, DL26
Data freshness | End of day for ACE data; the view reports the ACE batch date. Tier 2 sources arrive at the frequency ACE ingests them | Taken; DL06 for same-day needs, DL43 for the ACE additions
Auditability | Every decision reproducible from the log with its rule version and approver | Designed
Resilience | An agent or model outage falls back to rules. A source that has not refreshed shows its age on the view and through the data product freshness stamp | Designed

Risk | Effect | Answer
Data arrives a day late | End of day data for decisions that need today's position | Officers confirm payoff figures in the core; same-day triggers named under DL06
A source is not ingested by ACE | That source reopens U1 for it and needs a Workbench staging table and a load | Each source confirmed with the ACE team under DL43; the gap list names them one by one
RWB-ACE-001 lands late | The Tier 2 views, and the features that read them, cannot ship on their planned release | Tier 2 features stay behind their feature flags until RWB-ACE-001 lands; Tier 1 views ship with RWB-E1-069; scope and dates confirmed under DL43
Two squads, one repository | One squad's change holds the other's release | Feature flags, code owners and the module boundary test (DL04, DL37)
Rules component is new to ACE | ACE has rule based logic and no engine | A decision table evaluator in the recovery module, tested rule by rule against its test case
Volume grows faster than forecast | Reads, storage and queues sized too small | Sized at 15 percent inflow growth a year from the 30 June 2026 inventory; reviewed each quarter (DL15)
Partner access from outside | One to three months of lead time | Change raised in November; law firms first needed at Epic 5 (DL03)

Decision | What is needed
DL03 | How partners reach the partner portal from outside the bank
DL05 | Who creates the recovery module in ACE
DL06 | Which interfaces need real-time data
DL07 | How the front end is split into modules
DL11 | Non-functional target values
DL12 | Which legacy systems are kept
DL21 | Which systems carry the case identifier
DL27 | Storage, backup, legal hold and e-discovery for the document hub
DL33 | The model endpoint the agents call
DL35 | Further ACE deployment slots
DL43 | Whether the ACE team accepts the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates (needed by 21 November 2026)

Customers | Borrowers, guarantors, heirs, bidders | Existing bank channels only: SCB Easy, LINE OA, SMS, branches, HOME.SCB
COLLINS | Account, customer, collections history, litigation status, scores | ACE ingestion, daily batch into the ACE database
CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, SCBPDM, NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID | Collateral detail, appraisals, assets, litigation, registered mail, write-off postings, product holding, credit decisions, signature requests, group mapping | ACE ingestion into the ACE database. No Workbench load
Core bank (ALS) | Bookings for restructures, settlements and write-offs | Made by the officer; confirmed in ACE on the next business date
NSS and LINE OA | SMS and LINE messages | The ACE notification path
Power BI and the data lake | Reporting and model learning | Daily batch out
Enterprise AI platform | The model endpoint the agents call | Private endpoint in the SCB tenant (DL33)

6
Module | Built by | Holds
Common | ACE team | Sign-in and access checks, audit and PII logging, the shared case view, shared entities (customer, account, product, collateral, asset), shared tasks such as the restructure calculator, the notification path

Recovery | TechX recovery squads | Recovery stages, tasks and screens, the rules component, the decision center and log, the document hub, the partner portal, the read-only ACE views and the extension tables
Boundary rules
A module calls another only through its published interface or an application event
Each module owns its tables; another module reads them only through the owning module's interface
A boundary test runs in every build and fails it on any violation
A recovery component the collection module also needs moves to the common module by agreement with the ACE team
The recovery module reads ACE source data only through recovery.v_ace_* views: no direct public read, no write and no foreign key into ACE

secs.h: Slide 9. How the case workflow runs
secs.t:
9
Event arrives
An ACE refresh, a screen action, a partner result, a timer or another module
Rules evaluated
The rules component finds the rule for the state and the event
Decision logged
Rule version, inputs and approver written. A failed write stops here
Action taken
Next state, tasks, owner, queue, documents or notices
Timer set
The next due date is stored for the scheduler
Work queued
Work for other systems goes to an outbox with retry
Case model, CMMN 1.1 | Count
Stages | 10
Milestones | 30
Tasks | 150
Event listeners | 53
Sentries (rules) | 448
Case file items | 12
No workflow engine
Case, stage and task state are rows in the ACE database. A wait of weeks is a row with a state and a stored due date. Timers run on Quartz; automated chains to other systems run on Spring Batch with an outbox, retry and an exception queue.

10
What | How it works
Rules as rows | Each route set is a decision table: from state, event and condition in; action, next state, owner and timer out. Each row has an ID, a version, valid from and valid to dates, an approver and a test case
Hit policy Unique | For one state and one event in a route set, at most one condition holds, so one rule fires
Evaluator | A decision table evaluator in the recovery module reads the rows in force and returns the action. ACE has no rules engine today
Loading a change | A new version is loaded, checked against the schema and the completeness checks, and refused whole if any check fails
Open cases | A case keeps the rule version it was decided under. New decisions use the version in force on the day
Universal rules | Rules that apply in every state, such as a cure, a hold or a death, are evaluated before the route rules
Epic 1 | Allocation, assignment and transfer rules only. The route decision follows in Epic 4 (DL24)

secs.h: Slide 11. Data architecture: four tiers, one read path
secs.t:
11
ACE ingestion
ALS, EFS, COLLINS (today); SVAF, CCMS, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS scores, SCBPDM, NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID
ACE database
Tier 1: 22 tables. Tier 2: 14 tables and 12 columns
30 read-only views
recovery.v_ace_* - SELECT only, no write, no foreign key
Recovery module
Tier 3: 4 extension tables. Tier 4: 88 Workbench tables
Tier 1 - ACE tables that exist today
ACE team, read only. 22 tables, 16 views. Read through a view, never altered
Tier 3 - recovery extension tables
Workbench. 4 tables, 1:1, keyed by ACE business keys
Tier 2 - new ACE tables and columns
ACE team. 14 tables, 12 columns, 14 views. Raised once in RWB-ACE-001 (DL43)
Tier 4 - Workbench tables that stay
Workbench. 88 tables: case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, debt sale, documents, decision log, reference, outbox, flags, agents
Removed from the schema
20 tables, 243 fields: source copies, load machinery and the 6 columns the ACE story absorbs
92 Workbench tables, 30 views, 122 dictionary objects and 1,366 dictionary fields. Tier 1 views ship with RWB-E1-069; the Tier 2 views ship when RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43). No foreign key into ACE: a link to a source record is a business key.

12
Control | How it works
Sign-in | Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor authentication
Roles | 54 roles held as data, granted by Entra ID group membership through the bank IAM
Permissions | A matrix of roles against 14 capability areas, held as versioned data, checked on every endpoint
Scope | Own cases, team, region or all, set per role
Masking | Personal data masked in the views and at the API unless the role is allowed to see it
Approval limits | The delegation of authority table as reference data, checked before an approval is accepted
Logs | Access to personal data through PII Kafka; security events to the SOC log; every decision to the decision log
Break-glass | Emergency access with a reason and a review window
Partners | Their own identities, scoped to the cases placed with them (DL03)

13
Part | What it does
Orchestrator | Runs the decision steps and applies the autonomy level
Tool gateway | The only way an agent reaches a system. No agent holds a credential
Guardrail checker | Checks every output against its schema, the allowed actions and a confidence floor
Prompt and policy store | Versioned, so a run can be reproduced
Evaluation harness | Labeled sets scored before a result is used
Model endpoint | On the approved endpoint in the SCB tenant (DL33)
Level | The agent | A person
L0 | Nothing. The rule decides | Everything
L1 | Recommends, with its reasons | Decides. Every decision starts here after a shadow run
L2 | Acts inside a narrow band | Reviews a sample and the exceptions
L3 | Acts across the decision | Reviews by exception
L4 | Acts and closes | Monitors the measures
Agents run in shadow first. A decision moves up one level on evidence and drops one level on a guardrail breach.

secs.h: Slide 14. Environments and the release path
secs.t:
14
Environment | Data | Deployed | Notes
DEV | Synthetic data | On every merge into main | Four slots planned, one available (DL35)
SIT | Masked data | On a release tag | Two slots planned, one available (DL35)
UAT | Masked data | In the week before each release | Shared with the collection squad
PROD | Live data | In the monthly change window (DL34) | ACE namespace on the shared ACE AKS clusters
Nine pipeline gates before every merge: build and unit tests, lint, secret scan, PDPA lint, container scan, module boundary, integration and contract tests, AI first-pass review, and human approval. A change that fails SIT or UAT has its feature flag switched off and the release goes ahead without it.

secs.h: Recovery Workbench P1 Recovery data engine
secs.t:
Technical specification. SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Document title | TSD P1 Recovery data engine |
| Document ID | P1-RWB-TSD-v3 |
| Version | 3 |
| Status | In review |
| Date | 15 November 2026 |
| TSD owner | Solution architect |
| Build squad | TechX recovery squads |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5), ADR-010 |

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 28 October 2026 | Module specification with COLLINS and file loads, load checks, data quality rules, tracker inventory and the freshness stamp |
| 3 | 15 November 2026 | D-RCV-35: the Workbench loads no source data (U1). T3 is re-drawn around the 30 read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views, the 4 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys (U3), and freshness read from `v_ace_batch_status`. The 11 source copies, the 9 load, data quality and tracker tables, and the inbound interfaces leave the module. API-P1-003 to API-P1-008 are retired |

| Document | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine | FSD | Pair |
| Recovery Workbench Target Architecture | Architecture | Parent |
| Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7 | Data | Source of T3 and the 1,366 dictionary fields |
| Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v5 | Data | Source of the T3 physical types, the extension tables and the views |
| Recovery Workbench ACE Data Tier Map v1 | Data | Frozen table-and-column map, tiers 1 to 4 and the removals |
| Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql | Data | The 30 view definitions, the helper functions, the grants and the conformance test |
| Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1 | Governance | Decision record for this version |
| Recovery Workbench API Specification | API | Source of appendix T-A |

| Capability | Verdict | Owning document | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound source data (ALS, SCBPDM, UDP, AAL, EFS, COLLINS, LIT, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, WIN, GL, NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID) | REUSE | ACE ingestion, RWB-ACE-001 (ACE team) | ACE lands every source row. The Workbench runs no load, no file check, no data quality rule and no sign-off |
| Read path into ACE source data | REUSE | RWB-E1-069, this document | 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views. No direct `public` read and no write |
| Freshness and the intake trigger | NEW | This document | The stamp is built from `v_ace_batch_status`; ACE owns the batch record |
| Scheduler and batch | REUSE | ACE pattern: Quartz and Spring Batch | No new `qrtz_` or `batch_` table; jobs trigger on the ACE batch-complete record |
| Reconciliation of the case list | NEW | This document | Case list to `v_ace_account` by product group |
| Data dictionary held as data | NEW | This document | 92 tables and 30 views, 1,366 fields |
| Outbox and retry | REUSE | Error Handling and Resilience Standard | Through P2 |
| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P1 Recovery data engine is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers the read model over the ACE views, the four extension tables, freshness, reconciliation, the data dictionary and the publication of the case list. It no longer covers a source load.

The boundary rule frames the module. ACE ingests every source row. The recovery module reads ACE only through `recovery.v_ace_*` SELECT-only views, adds only its own tables and columns, and writes nothing to `public`. There is no foreign key from a Workbench table into ACE, because ACE uses `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `account` and a cascade would delete recovery history. A link to a source record is a business key: `account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code`, `contact_key` or `valuation_key`.

P1 reaches other modules only through their published interfaces. It reaches ACE only through the views in T3.1.1.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| RecoveryDataEngineController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| RecoveryDataEngineService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| RecoveryDataEngineRepository | Reads and writes the module's own tables; never a `public` table |
| AceViewReader | The only component in the module that queries `recovery.v_ace_*`; returns read-only records with `data_as_of` |
| FreshnessMonitor | Reads `v_ace_batch_status`, writes the `data_product_load` stamp and publishes AceDataReady or AceDataLate |
| ReconciliationService | Reconciles the case list to `v_ace_account` by product group and writes `reconciliation_result` |
| DictionaryService | Maintains `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `sys_field_version` and serves the dictionary screens |
| ExtensionWriter | Writes `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext`; one row per ACE business key, no copy of ACE data |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns; each triggers on an ACE batch-complete record, not on a fixed clock |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

The load adapter, the data quality rule engine and the tracker loader of version 2 are removed with their tables. Their checks are now ACE ingestion checks (RWB-ACE-001) or reconciliation rules REC-01 to REC-09.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| is_active | boolean | The active or inactive status of the record |
| state | varchar(40) | Record lifecycle state |
| version | integer | Optimistic lock version |
| created_at | timestamptz | When the record was created |
| created_by | uuid | Who or which service identity created it |
| updated_at | timestamptz | When the record last changed |
| updated_by | uuid | Who or which service identity last changed it |

The 30 ACE views are read-only and carry no standard record columns; their columns are the ACE data as the Workbench reads it. Every Workbench table and every extension table carries the seven columns above.

The module's model has three parts:

1. The 30 ACE source views. P1 does not own them; it is the only way P1 reads ACE.
2. The four extension tables. P1 owns them; each is 1:1 with an ACE record, keyed by its business key.
3. The Workbench metadata and operations tables that stay. P1 owns them; they hold the dictionary, the data products, the freshness stamp, reconciliation, retention and the case list snapshot.

secs.h: T3.1.1 ACE source views, the only read path
secs.t:
One view per ACE object family, so a developer is told which view to read and cannot wander into `public`. Section A holds 16 views over tables ACE has today and ships with RWB-E1-069 as V0002. Section B holds 14 views over the RWB-ACE-001 additions and ships as V0003 once the ACE change lands; until then the features that need them stay behind their flags.

Every view is owned by `ace_view_owner`, which holds SELECT on the ACE tables it reads. The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and on nothing else in `public`.

| # | View | Section | ACE object or objects read | Key the Workbench links on | What the Workbench reads it for |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `v_ace_account` | A, plus B columns | `account`, `product`, `branch` | `account_key` | Account, balances, arrears, days past due, classification, restructure flag, `data_as_of` |
| 2 | `v_ace_payment` | A | `payment`, `account` | `payment_code` | Payments posted to an account, for proceeds matching |
| 3 | `v_ace_customer` | A, plus B columns | `customer` | `person_key` | Party identity, masked to the last four, and vulnerability inputs |
| 4 | `v_ace_contact` | A | `phone`, `email`, `address` (union) | `contact_key` (`contact_type:key`) | Contact point, consent basis, notice address |
| 5 | `v_ace_ca_relation` | A | `ca_relation` | `person_key` and `account_key` | Borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles |
| 6 | `v_ace_aa_relation` | A | `aa_relation` | `parent_account_key`, `child_account_key` | Parent and child accounts of a grouped facility |
| 7 | `v_ace_collateral` | A | `collateral`, `asset` | `asset_key` | Collateral link, value and type |
| 8 | `v_ace_asset` | A | `asset` | `asset_key` | The collateral asset record |
| 9 | `v_ace_efs_action` | A, plus B columns | `efs_action` | `efs_record_key` | Collections history, contact result and promise |
| 10 | `v_ace_efs_action_code` | A | `efs_action_code` | `action_code` | Action code list, 1,106 values |
| 11 | `v_ace_efs_assignment` | A | `efs_assignment` | `account_key` | Assignment and hand-over history |
| 12 | `v_ace_bucket_log` | A | `bucket_log_snapshot`, `account` | `account_key` | Monthly bucket history |
| 13 | `v_ace_product` | A | `product` | `product_code` | Product and product group lists |
| 14 | `v_ace_branch` | A | `branch` | `branch_code` | Branch and region lists |
| 15 | `v_ace_holiday` | A | `bot_holiday` | `holiday_date` | Service level and legal-day calendar |
| 16 | `v_ace_plan` | A | `ace_case`, `cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case`, `tdr_calculation`, `ai_recommended_plan`, `account` | `plan_ref` | Plan reference, status, booking and approval dates, published calculation |
| 17 | `v_ace_batch_status` | B | `ace_batch_run` | `source_system` and `business_date` | Freshness, record count and the intake trigger |
| 18 | `v_ace_valuation` | B | `valuation` | `valuation_key` | SVAF appraisal number, values and date |
| 19 | `v_ace_collateral_detail` | B | `collateral_detail` | `asset_key` | Title deed, plot, area, location, insurance and lien rank |
| 20 | `v_ace_npa_asset` | B | `npa_asset` | `asset_key` | NPA asset, transfer in, book value and auction price |
| 21 | `v_ace_npa_sale` | B | `npa_sale` | `npa_sale_key` | NPA sale contract, taxes, fees and incentive |
| 22 | `v_ace_lawsuit` | B | `lawsuit` | `lawsuit_key` | Court case numbers, claim, judgment and status |
| 23 | `v_ace_hearing` | B | `hearing` | `hearing_key` | Hearing date, type and next date |
| 24 | `v_ace_pod` | B | `pod_receipt` | `pod_key` | Proof of delivery for a notice |
| 25 | `v_ace_write_off` | B | `gl_write_off` | `write_off_key` | GL write-off posting, cost centre and GL product |
| 26 | `v_ace_score` | B | `collins_score` | `score_key` | COLLINS score, estimate and route |
| 27 | `v_ace_party_product` | B | `party_product` | `person_key` and `account_key` | Customer product holding |
| 28 | `v_ace_credit_decision` | B | `credit_decision` | `credit_decision_key` | NLEADS credit result, reason and decision date |
| 29 | `v_ace_esign` | B | `esign_request` | `esign_key` | EasyApp signature request and status |
| 30 | `v_ace_iam_group` | B | `iam_group` | `entra_group` | Group-to-role mapping used at sign-in |

Two rules apply to every view:

- A view field is named for the Workbench, not for ACE. The ACE name appears only in the view definition and the STTM. `account.delay_days` becomes `days_past_due`; `payment.pay_date` becomes `payment_date` through `ace_to_date`; `customer.person_key` becomes `cif_no` and `person_key`.
- A view casts and masks; it does not decide. `ace_to_date` returns NULL on an unrecognised text date. `ace_to_boolean` turns Y/N into boolean. `v_ace_customer` exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only; the clear identity number never leaves ACE. `v_ace_contact.contact_value` is in full because notices and calls need it, and display masking is E1-037 at the API.

Section B adds 12 columns to views that already exist, through `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` in V0003: `v_ace_account` gains `business_unit`, `principal_outstanding`, `interest_outstanding`, `fees_outstanding`, `daily_bucket`, `settlement_booked_date` and `settlement_booked_amount`; `v_ace_customer` gains `party_type`, `id_type` and `segment`; `v_ace_efs_action` gains `contact_result` and `action_contact_status`. A feature that reads one of the 12 stays behind its flag until V0003 is applied.

The full field list of every view, with types and BR field IDs DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-304, is in Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7. The view definition is the contract: a change to a column a view reads is a change to that contract.

Each extension table holds Workbench decisions about an ACE record and never a copy of it. The row exists only while the Workbench has something to say about the ACE record; a missing row means the defaults (no flag set, no consent recorded, no acceptance). No existing ACE table is altered.

**party_ext** (NEW). Workbench flags about an ACE customer, keyed by `person_key`. A 1:1 table.

No relationship in this table is a foreign key into ACE. The 14 re-keyed foreign keys of the retained tables are listed in the Tier Map section 5 and are owned by the module that holds the table.
No case state machine of its own; the module acts on events from P3 and writes through the decision log.

P1 owns no inbound interface. Every inbound interface in Interface Specifications v3 is owned by ACE ingestion, and P1 reads the ACE database through the views in T3.1.1. A P1 job is triggered by an ACE batch-complete record, never by an inbound file.

| ID | System | Direction | Approach | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| INT-01, INT-02, INT-04, INT-05, INT-06, INT-07, INT-08, INT-09, INT-10, INT-11, INT-12, INT-13, INT-15, INT-16 | Source systems | In, into ACE | ACE ingestion (ACE team). P1 reads the matching `v_ace_*` view and never the source | Per the source cycle in Interface Specifications v3 |
| None | ACE database | In | `recovery.v_ace_*` SELECT-only views, through `ace_view_owner` | As each ACE batch completes |
| INT-19 | Data lake and Power BI | Out | P1 builds the case list snapshot; P2 sends the file | Daily |

The freshness web service is the only P1 screen an operator uses: it shows the last complete ACE business date per selected source from `v_ace_batch_status`, and the STALE reason for each data product.
Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices.

| Event | Direction |
|---|---|
| AceDataReady | Published: the ACE batch for a source completed and the data product is LOADED |
| AceDataLate | Published: the ACE batch is incomplete, late or failed and the data product is STALE |

`AceDataReady` replaces `LoadCompleted` and `AceDataLate` replaces `LoadRefused` from version 2. The named and numbered event catalogue is in Event and Messaging Design v3 (EV-26, EV-27).

| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P10 Agent runtime is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: orchestrator, tool gateway, guardrails, prompt store, evaluation, autonomy levels. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces and other systems only through COLLINS, file loads and the ACE paths.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| AgentRuntimeController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| AgentRuntimeService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| AgentRuntimeRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| 3 | 15 November 2026 | D-RCV-35: the Workbench loads no source data (U1). P2 becomes outbound only. Inbound interfaces INT-01 to INT-16 are re-owned by ACE ingestion (ACE team) and the Workbench reads them through `recovery.v_ace_*` views. The inbound file adapter, `interface_run` and `interface_signoff` are removed; `interface_config` is kept for outbound interfaces only; `party_product` is replaced by the ACE Tier 2 view `v_ace_party_product`; `efs_ledger_outcome` stays as in Physical Schema v5. API-P2-013 and API-P2-014 are retired |

| Document | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration | FSD | Pair |
| Recovery Workbench Target Architecture | Architecture | Parent |

| Capability | Verdict | Owning document | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound source data (ALS, SCBPDM, UDP, AAL, EFS, COLLINS models, LIT, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS, RPS, WIN proof of delivery, GL, NLEADS, EasyApp) | REUSE | ACE ingestion, RWB-ACE-001 (ACE team) | ACE lands the data; the Workbench runs no inbound load, file check, run record or sign-off |
| Read path into ACE data | REUSE | RWB-E1-069, TSD P1 | SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views; P2 reads them and never a `public` table |
| Sign-in, access check, audit, PII and SOC logging | REUSE | ACE common module | Called through the published interface |
| Notification path for SMS and LINE | REUSE | ACE common module | INT-17 and INT-18 |
| Scheduler and batch | REUSE | ACE pattern: Quartz and Spring Batch | Jobs in the Batch and Scheduling Design; no new `qrtz_` or `batch_` table |
| Outbound file adapter | NEW | This document, RWB-E1-007 | Outbound files only |
| Outbox and retry | NEW | Error Handling and Resilience Standard | Built in P2 for the recovery module |
| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P2 does not own the read path, but it reads through it and must keep to its rules (Tier Map section 1):

| Rule | What it means for P2 |
|---|---|
| One read surface | P2 reads source data only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views. A direct `public.*` read in P2 code or SQL is a defect and fails the TE-001 boundary test |
| No write | The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and nothing else in `public`; P2 never writes to an ACE table |
| No foreign key into ACE | P2 links to source records by business key (`person_key`, `account_key`), never by a UUID foreign key, because ACE cascades deletes on `account` |
| Freshness | The business date of each source comes from `v_ace_batch_status`. The recovery data engine (P1) stamps `data_product_load` and publishes EV-27 AceDataLate; P2 does not check inbound files |
| Two migrations | Tier 1 views ship with RWB-E1-069 (V0002). Tier 2 views, including `v_ace_party_product` and `v_ace_credit_decision`, ship with V0003 once RWB-ACE-001 lands; the P2 features that read them stay behind their flags until then |

Views P2 reads:

| View | Tier | Read by | For |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_ace_plan` | 1 | API-P2-010 | ACE restructure plan status |
| `v_ace_efs_action_code` | 1 | `efs_ledger_outcome` maintenance | Valid EFS action codes |
| `v_ace_efs_action` | 1 | Interaction ledger build (P6), filtered by `efs_ledger_outcome` | Which EFS actions enter the ledger and on which channel |
| `v_ace_party_product` | 2 | API-P2-011 | Other products the case's borrowers hold |
| `v_ace_credit_decision` | 2 | API-P2-012 | NLEADS credit result shown with the credit pack |
| `v_ace_batch_status` | 2 | Job catalog screen | Last complete ACE business date per source, for display only |

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| IntegrationController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| IntegrationService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| OutboundFileAdapter | Builds each outbound file from its `interface_config` version, runs the outbound file checks (layout, control totals), sends it by SFTP, records the acknowledgement and holds the waiting case steps until it arrives |
| OutboxRelay | Reads `outbox_event` rows committed with the change, creates one `outbox_delivery` per consumer, delivers with the retry intervals and raises a RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task on the last failure |
| IntegrationRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| AceViewReader | Read-only access to the `v_ace_*` views listed in T1.1; no other ACE access |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns: the outbound file runs, the data lake publish and the outbox relay |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call to queue outbound work; no table is read across modules |

| outbound_item | PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION, ACKNOWLEDGED | Sent on the next run; a failed send or failed outbound check moves to RETRY at the `retry_intervals_min` of its `interface_config` version; after `max_attempts` (three for INT-14 and INT-25) it moves to EXCEPTION and a task goes to `owner_role`; the waiting case steps resume on ACKNOWLEDGED |
| outbox_delivery | PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED, EXCEPTION | One delivery per event and consumer; a repeat is dropped through `processed_event`; the last failure raises a RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task |

A resend from the exception queue (API-P2-002, API-P2-004) sets PENDING and attempt count 0.

Owners and approaches follow Interface Specifications v3 and the Integration Inventory v3. Every inbound row is owned by ACE ingestion; P2 builds only the Workbench-owned outbound rows.

Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices. Entra ID single sign-on through the ACE front end; each endpoint declares its capability area and right; scope filters every query; masking applies to personal fields; service identities for jobs and agents. P3 Case and workflow is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: case record, CMMN state, queues, allocation, timers, the rules component. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces, and it reads ACE source data only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| CaseAndWorkflowController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| CaseAndWorkflowService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Column | Type | Meaning |

| is_active | boolean | The active or inactive status of the record |
| state | varchar(40) | Record lifecycle state |
| version | integer | Optimistic lock version |
| created_at | timestamptz | When the record was created |
| created_by | uuid | Who or which service identity created it |
| updated_at | timestamptz | When the record last changed |
| updated_by | uuid | Who or which service identity last changed it |

The case is Workbench-owned. The account and the party are ACE records: the case links to them by business key and reads their attributes from `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_customer`. A link carries no foreign key, because ACE cascades deletes on `account` and a cascade would delete case history.

| NFR-003 | The system supports the peak number of partner users signed on at once across 73 agencies, 11 to 12 law firms, 4 auction vendors and 35 buyers. | About 50 partner users online in the busiest hour, of about 320 named users | Proposed from the volume forecast |
| NFR-004 | The document store holds the annual inbound document volume with its growth rate. | About 860,000 documents in 2027, rising with 15 percent inflow growth a year | Proposed from the volume forecast |
| NFR-005 | The restructure path carries the monthly case volume reaching the Workbench. | About 3,000 restructure accounts a month reach the bank's restructure process today | Proposed |
| NFR-006 | The deed in lieu path carries its target monthly volume. | 1,000 cases a month in 2027, from 685 today | Proposed |
| NFR-007 | The decision log holds one record for every decision on every case for the full retention period without degrading query time. | About 36 GB for the decision log and the interaction ledger by the end of 2031; a single case history query under 2 seconds at that size | Proposed, DL11 |
| NFR-069 | The document hub holds the full recovery document estate as a system of record, including every version and every held document, with storage sized for growth. | About 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031, with every version and held document | Proposed, DL11 |
| NFR-070 | The interaction ledger holds every interaction on every open and closed case within its retention period, and reads a single case history inside the user wait. | One case history reads in under 2 seconds with the ledger at its 2031 size | Proposed, DL11 |
| NFR-008 | A screen responds within its target under normal load. | Under 2 seconds | Proposed |
| NFR-009 | The case record view loads for a case with 50 documents. | Under 2 seconds | Proposed |
| NFR-010 | An agent returns an answer within its target, after which the rule result is used and the case still routes. | Under 60 seconds | Proposed |
| NFR-011 | A rule evaluation at a routing decision completes inside the user's wait. | Under 300 milliseconds per rule evaluation at the 95th percentile | Proposed, DL11 |
| NFR-012 | A search across cases and documents returns within its target. | Under 3 seconds for a search across cases; under 5 seconds across documents | Proposed, DL11 |

secs.t:
Technical specification. SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Document | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration | FSD | Pair |
| Recovery Workbench Target Architecture | Architecture | Parent |
| Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary | Data | Source of T3 |
| Recovery Workbench API Specification | API | Source of appendix T-A |

| Capability | Verdict | Owning document | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign-in, access check, audit, PII and SOC logging | REUSE | ACE common module | Called through the published interface |
| Scheduler and batch | REUSE | ACE pattern: Quartz and Spring Batch | Jobs in the Batch and Scheduling Design |
| Outbox and retry | REUSE | Error Handling and Resilience Standard | Through P2 |
| Rules evaluation | NEW | Rules Engine Design | Decision table evaluator |

P4 Access and administration is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: roles, permissions, scope, masking, delegation of authority table, access log. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces and other systems only through COLLINS, file loads and the ACE paths.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| AccessAndAdministrationService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| AccessAndAdministrationRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P5 Document hub is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: store, index, OCR, classification, extraction, review queue, retention, custody. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces and other systems only through COLLINS, file loads and the ACE paths.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| DocumentHubController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| DocumentHubService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| DocumentHubRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Scheduler and batch | REUSE | ACE pattern: Quartz and Spring Batch | Jobs in the Batch and Scheduling Design |
| Outbox and retry | REUSE | Error Handling and Resilience Standard | Through P2 |
| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P6 Communications is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces and other systems only through COLLINS, file loads and the ACE paths.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| CommunicationsController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| CommunicationsService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| CommunicationsRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

P7 Decision center and log is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: recommendation with reasons, approval within delegation, decision log store and writer. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces and other systems only through COLLINS, file loads and the ACE paths.

| DecisionCenterAndLogController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |

| DecisionCenterAndLogRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |

secs.t:

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| 3 | 15 November 2026 | D-RCV-35: `proceeds.account_payment_id` becomes `payment_code`, read from `v_ace_payment`; the GL write-off is read from `v_ace_write_off`; INT-02 and INT-16 are owned by ACE ingestion; the SY-DATALOAD actor is removed |

| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

P8 Payments and posting is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: payment and proceeds matching, fees, posting files. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces, and it reads payments and GL postings only through `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_write_off`.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| PaymentsAndPostingController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| PaymentsAndPostingService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| PaymentsAndPostingRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| is_active | boolean | The active or inactive status of the record |
| state | varchar(40) | Record lifecycle state |
| version | integer | Optimistic lock version |
| created_at | timestamptz | When the record was created |
| created_by | uuid | Who or which service identity created it |
| updated_at | timestamptz | When the record last changed |
| updated_by | uuid | Who or which service identity last changed it |

The proceeds record is Workbench-owned. The payment it matches is an ACE record: the link is `payment_code`, the business key of `v_ace_payment`, with no foreign key. A payment that ACE has not yet ingested cannot be matched; the proceeds row waits in UNMATCHED and shows the last ACE business date.

| INT-16 | GL | In, into ACE | ACE ingestion (ACE team); the Workbench reads `v_ace_write_off` | Monthly |

| NFR-051 | Agents run under service identities and are subject to the same role checks as people. | Service identities | Proposed |
| NFR-052 | Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts. | No secrets in code or prompts | Proposed |
| NFR-053 | Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. | Encrypted | Proposed |
| NFR-054 | The build pipeline blocks a change that carries a secret, personal data in code, tests or logs, or an unapproved dependency. | Pipeline checks pass | Proposed |
| NFR-055 | Agent outputs are schema checked against an allowed-action list with a confidence threshold, and fall back to rules when the check fails. | Schema check on every output | Proposed |
| NFR-056 | Penetration testing and a security review are completed before the first production release. | Before the first production release and before the partner portal opens to users outside the bank | Proposed, DL11 |

S1 Valuation and route is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: the D6 route decision with COLLINS return by route and the route agent. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces, and it reads appraisals and scores only through `recovery.v_ace_valuation` and `recovery.v_ace_score`.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| ValuationAndRouteController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| ValuationAndRouteService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| ValuationAndRouteRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| is_active | boolean | The active or inactive status of the record |
| state | varchar(40) | Record lifecycle state |
| version | integer | Optimistic lock version |
| created_at | timestamptz | When the record was created |
| created_by | uuid | Who or which service identity created it |
| updated_at | timestamptz | When the record last changed |
| updated_by | uuid | Who or which service identity last changed it |

The appraisal and the score are ACE records. S1 reads them and holds only its own decision about an appraisal. It has no valuation table and no score table, and it writes nothing to ACE.

**v_ace_valuation** (ACE, read-only; Section B). An SVAF appraisal as ingested into ACE and read through the view. Key: `valuation_key`. 9 fields.

| BR Field ID | Field | Data type | Physical type | Required | List | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-ACE-187 | valuation_key | TEXT | varchar(255) | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.valuation_key` |
| DF-ACE-188 | asset_key | TEXT | varchar(255) | No | None | ACE `valuation.asset_key` |
| DF-ACE-189 | appraisal_no | TEXT | varchar(20) | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.appraisal_no` |
| DF-ACE-190 | appraisal_type | LOV | varchar(15) | Yes | LOV-APPRAISAL | ACE `valuation.appraisal_type` |
| DF-ACE-191 | appraised_value | NUMBER | numeric(18,2) | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.appraised_value` |
| DF-ACE-192 | forced_sale_value | NUMBER | numeric(18,2) | No | None | ACE `valuation.forced_sale_value` |
| DF-ACE-193 | appraisal_date | DATE | date | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.appraisal_date` |
| DF-ACE-194 | source_system | TEXT | varchar(20) | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.source_system` (SVAF) |
| DF-ACE-195 | data_as_of | DATE | date | Yes | None | ACE `valuation.business_date` |

The view is Section B because ACE holds no appraisal today; it is created the week RWB-ACE-001 lands. Until then the valuation screens and the D6 route rule stay behind their flag. `accepted`, `stale_flag`, `age_days` and the valuer are Workbench decisions and are not in ACE.

**v_ace_score** (ACE, read-only; Section B). A COLLINS score, estimate and route as ingested into ACE. Key: `score_key`. 10 fields.

| BR Field ID | Field | Data type | Physical type | Required | List | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-ACE-270 | score_key | TEXT | varchar(255) | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.score_key` |
| DF-ACE-271 | account_key | TEXT | varchar(255) | No | None | ACE `collins_score.account_key` |
| DF-ACE-272 | model_code | TEXT | varchar(30) | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.model_code` |
| DF-ACE-273 | model_version | TEXT | varchar(20) | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.model_version` |
| DF-ACE-274 | score_value | NUMBER | numeric(12,4) | No | None | ACE `collins_score.score_value` |
| DF-ACE-275 | estimate_value | NUMBER | numeric(18,2) | No | None | ACE `collins_score.estimate_value` |
| DF-ACE-276 | route_code | LOV | varchar(4) | No | LOV-ROUTE | ACE `collins_score.route_code` |
| DF-ACE-277 | scored_at | DATE | timestamptz | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.scored_at` |
| DF-ACE-278 | source_system | TEXT | varchar(20) | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.source_system` (COLLINS) |
| DF-ACE-279 | data_as_of | DATE | date | Yes | None | ACE `collins_score.business_date` |

The view is Section B. The route decision is recorded on the case (`recovery_case.route_code`, `route_state`), not on the score: the score is an input, the decision is Workbench-owned.

**valuation_ext** (NEW). The Workbench decision about an ACE appraisal. Key: `valuation_key`. A 1:1 table with `v_ace_valuation`.

| BR Field ID | Field | Data type | Physical type | Required | List | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-EXT-036 | valuation_key | TEXT | varchar(255) | Yes | None | ACE `v_ace_valuation.valuation_key` |
| DF-EXT-037 | accepted | BOOLEAN | boolean | Yes | None | Workbench |
| DF-EXT-038 | accepted_at | DATE | timestamptz | No | None | Workbench |
| DF-EXT-039 | accepted_by | CROSS_REF | uuid | No | None | Workbench |
| DF-EXT-040 | valuer_partner_id | CROSS_REF | uuid | No | None | Workbench |
| DF-EXT-041 | stale_flag | BOOLEAN | boolean | Yes | None | Workbench |
| DF-EXT-042 | age_days | NUMBER | integer | No | None | Workbench |

Plus the seven standard record columns, DF-EXT-043 to DF-EXT-049. A missing row means the appraisal is not accepted and is judged stale by its date alone.

The version 2 tables `valuation` and `score` leave Physical Schema v5. Their field IDs DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027 and DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027 are retired and not reused.

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| LOV-APPRAISAL | MARKET, OFFICIAL, FORCED_SALE, DESKTOP, AGENT_ESTIMATE |
| LOV-ROUTE | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8 |

| From | Field | To | Cardinality |
|---|---|---|---|
| valuation_ext | valuation_key | v_ace_valuation | One to one; business key, no foreign key |
| valuation_ext | valuer_partner_id | partner | Many to 0 or 1 |
| v_ace_valuation | asset_key | v_ace_asset | Many to 0 or 1; business key, no foreign key |
| v_ace_score | account_key | v_ace_account | Many to 0 or 1; business key, no foreign key |

No relationship here is a foreign key into ACE. A score or an appraisal that ACE has not ingested has no row to read, and the screen shows the last ACE business date rather than an empty value.

secs.t:

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Document | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction | FSD | Pair |
| Recovery Workbench Target Architecture | Architecture | Parent |

| Recovery Workbench API Specification | API | Source of appendix T-A |

| Capability | Verdict | Owning document | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign-in, access check, audit, PII and SOC logging | REUSE | ACE common module | Called through the published interface |

| Outbox and retry | REUSE | Error Handling and Resilience Standard | Through P2 |
| Rules evaluation | REUSE | Rules Engine Design | Through the rules component |

S5 Assets and auction is part of the recovery module in the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end. It covers: asset record, holding, floor price, listing, auction rounds, RAMC. It reaches other modules only through their published interfaces, and it reads assets and NPA sales only through `recovery.v_ace_npa_asset`, `recovery.v_ace_npa_sale` and `recovery.v_ace_asset`.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| AssetsAndAuctionController | REST endpoints in appendix T-A; validation; maps errors to problem responses |
| AssetsAndAuctionService | Business logic; calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change |
| AssetsAndAuctionRepository | Reads and writes the module's tables only |
| Jobs | Quartz and Spring Batch jobs the module owns |
| Published interface | Java interface other modules call; no table is read across modules |

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| is_active | boolean | The active or inactive status of the record |
| state | varchar(40) | Record lifecycle state |
| version | integer | Optimistic lock version |
| created_at | timestamptz | When the record was created |
| created_by | uuid | Who or which service identity created it |
| updated_at | timestamptz | When the record last changed |
| updated_by | uuid | Who or which service identity last changed it |

The held asset and its sale are ACE records. S5 reads them and owns the work that follows: the holding decision, the listing, the auction rounds and the sale record. There is no Workbench asset table, and nothing is written to ACE.

**v_ace_npa_asset** (ACE, read-only; Section B). An NPA asset from AMIS (property) and RPS (vehicles), as ingested into ACE. Key: `asset_key`. 12 fields.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Workflow Engine Design v2.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Workflow Engine Design v2

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Workflow engine design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench workflow engine design
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | CMMN 1.1, arc42 runtime view

Element | Design
Model | CMMN 1.1 case model: 10 stages, 30 milestones, 150 tasks, 53 event listeners, 448 sentries, 12 case file items
Runtime | Programmatic workflow in the recovery module of ACE. Case, stage and task state are rows in the ACE database; code moves them (DT09)
Sentries | Each sentry is one routing rule, evaluated by the rules component
Timers | Every due date is stored on the timer table; a Quartz job checks due timers every five minutes
Outbound work | Written to an outbox in the same transaction and sent with retry
Changes to the model | Route set versions as data; cases in flight keep the version they were decided under

Element | Count | How it is held
Case | 1 per customer per product | recovery_case
Stage | 10 | stage_code on the case; LOV-STAGE
Milestone | 30 | Reached state recorded on the case timeline
Task | 150 | task, with assignment and timer
Event listener | 53 | Rules that fire on an event in any state
Sentry | 448 | rule_row
Case file item | 12 | The data products the sentries read

Step | What happens
Event arrives | A load, a screen action, a partner result, a timer or another module
Rules evaluated | The rules component finds the rule for the state and the event
Decision logged | Rule version, inputs and approver written. A failed write stops here
Action taken | Next state, tasks, owner, queue, documents or notices
Timer set | The next due date is stored for the scheduler
Work queued | Work for other systems goes to an outbox with retry

Timer | Set by | What happens when it ends
Stage clock | Entry to a state, from the service level table (DL22) | Warning at the warning point; escalation at the end (R-UNI-30)
Prescription clock | Case entry, from the claim type | Warning forces a litigation review (R-UNI-31). Never paused by a deviation
Notice period | Delivery date on the proof of delivery | Pack assembly opens (R-LIT-15)
Offer validity | Offer sent | The offer lapses and the case returns to the owner
Partner service level | Instruction issued | Breach raised and re-selection (R-LIT-28)
Claim deadline | Default conditions met for a guarantee | Warning to the guarantee officer (R-GUA-01)
Holding age | Asset take-on | Provision steps and re-appraisal (R-DIS-06, R-DIS-09)

Timers count working days from the bank holiday calendar held as reference data. A deviation pauses the stage clock; the prescription clock keeps running.

secs.h: 5. A case in flight when the model changes
secs.t:
A new route set version takes effect from its valid from date.

Cases already decided keep the version they were decided under for that decision.

The next event on a case is evaluated against the version in force on the event date.

A state removed from the model is mapped to its replacement in the version's migration table; cases in it are moved by a logged correction (R-UNI-24).

A timer already running keeps its due date unless the new version says to recompute it.

The change report lists the cases affected before the version is approved.

Case | Handling
Two events on one case at once | One transaction per case; the second waits on the row lock and is evaluated after
The same event twice | Idempotency key per event; the repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40)
Decision log write fails | Nothing changes; incident raised (R-UNI-39)
Outbound system down | Outbox retry; exception queue after the limit (R-UNI-33, R-UNI-36)
Service restart | Quartz jobs resume; missed timers are processed on start

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL16 | Entry at 90 or 91 days past due | 90 days past due
DL17 | What counts as one case | One case per customer per product
DL22 | Service level per case state | Placeholders loaded

Workbench: 88 tables

8
Rule | What it means
Held as metadata | Each entity is an object and each field a field definition, as in the bank TSD section T3. A field or a list value is added by a versioned load
Standard columns | Every record carries is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at and updated_by
One system of record | Each entity names the system whose value is correct. Source data is read from ACE through a view and never written by the Workbench
Reference data is versioned | Rules, limits, lists of values, roles and templates carry a version, a valid from date and the approver
Personal data is protected | Identification numbers never leave ACE in clear. Every field marked as personal data is masked unless the role is allowed to see it, and every read is audited
The decision log is append only | Entries are never changed. Each entry carries the hash of the one before it
Every value has its age | Each ACE row carries the business date of its batch, so a screen and a decision can show how old an input is
The account number is the join | The case identifier stays in the Workbench. Other systems are matched on the ACE account_key

G4 | The Thai Credit Guarantee quota is not available in ACE. | The guarantee officer records the quota and the claim deadline on the case. The deadline drives a timer. | DL06
G5 | The full loan history since the account opened is not available. | The model holds what COLLINS carries. Routing does not need history before collections started. | DL12
G6 | How much EFS contact history ACE keeps. | The outcomes the business lead names, for the period in collections, are read through v_ace_efs_action. Nothing is copied. | DL29
G7 | Where customer facts come from. | ACE ingests them from SCBPDM and the core bank; the Workbench reads v_ace_customer. DL20 is amended. | DL20, D-RCV-35
G8 | What counts as one case. | One case per customer per product, with the accounts linked through case account. | DL17

secs.t:
10
Gap | What is missing | Assumption the model takes | Decision

G10 | Thai names for fields, labels and list values. | Each list value of a closed list carries an English and a Thai label. Thai labels are filled as they are approved. | DL10
G11 | Retention and masking per data product. | Every field marked as personal data is masked for every role except those the masking rules name. Identification numbers never leave ACE in clear. Retention follows the bank schedule once read. | DL26

G13 | GL write-off postings are not in ACE today. | ACE ingests the GL file; gl_write_off is Tier 2 in RWB-ACE-001, read through v_ace_write_off and matched to the write-off decision. | DL43, DL12

Gaps and the assumptions taken
Where the data needed is not available today or waits on a bank decision. The model is built on the assumption shown. The ACE gaps section lists what the ACE team adds under RWB-ACE-001.
Gap | What is missing | Assumption the model takes | What it affects | Decision
G1 | ACE holds no appraisal and no title deed detail today. | ACE ingests SVAF and CCMS; valuation and collateral_detail are Tier 2 in RWB-ACE-001. Until they land, DP06 stays behind its feature flag. An appraisal past its age limit is flagged on the case and blocks the route decision until it is replaced. | DP06; D6 route, D8 floor price | DL43, DL06, DL12
G2 | ACE holds the collateral asset, not the repossessed or purchased asset. | ACE ingests AMIS and RPS; npa_asset and npa_sale are Tier 2 in RWB-ACE-001. Until they land, the NPA screens stay behind their feature flag. | DP06; D8 disposal | DL43, DL06, DL12
G3 | Debt sale data is not available in ACE. | Debt sale lots are built and held in the Workbench. Past lots are migrated once from the bank's debt sale files. | DP09; D8.4 debt sale | None
G4 | The Thai Credit Guarantee quota is not available in ACE. | The guarantee officer records the quota and the claim deadline on the case. The deadline drives a timer. | DP04; D6.5 guarantee claim | DL06
G5 | The full loan history since the account opened is not available. | The model holds the ACE account at its current state and the monthly bucket snapshot. Routing does not need history before collections started. | DP01 | DL12
G6 | How much EFS contact history ACE keeps, and for how long. | The contact outcomes the business lead names, for the period the account was in collections, are read through v_ace_efs_action. Nothing is copied into the Workbench. | DP05; D6 entry, X6 | DL29
G7 | Where customer facts come from. | ACE ingests them from SCBPDM and the core bank batch; the Workbench reads v_ace_customer. DL20 is amended by D-RCV-35. | DP02 | DL20, D-RCV-35
G8 | What counts as one case. | One case per customer per product, with the accounts linked through case account. | DP03; every entity linked to the case | DL17
G9 | Systems that carry the case identifier. | The Workbench only. The ACE account_key joins the case to ACE and to other systems. | DP03; all inbound and outbound flows | DL21
G10 | Thai names for fields, labels and list values. | Each list value carries an English and a Thai label. Thai labels are filled as they are approved. | DP14 lists of values; every screen | DL10
G11 | Retention and masking per data product. | Every field marked as personal data is masked for every role except those the masking rules name. Identification numbers never leave ACE in clear; contact values are full in v_ace_contact because notices need them, and display masking is E1-037. Retention follows the bank schedule once received. | All data products | DL26
G12 | Difference accepted between a view and its ACE source. | Zero. ACE ingestion refuses a batch that does not reconcile to its control totals, and the Workbench reconciles the case list to v_ace_account and the money movements to v_ace_payment and v_ace_write_off every day (REC-01 to REC-05). | All loaded data products | DL25
G13 | GL write-off postings are not in ACE today. | ACE ingests the GL file; gl_write_off is Tier 2 in RWB-ACE-001, read through v_ace_write_off and matched to the write-off decision. | DP13; D9 | DL43, DL12
G14 | Work orders and operational status held in Salesforce are not available. | Not modeled. NPA work orders are raised as tasks on the case. | DP06; D8 | DL12
