Key
What each term and value means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Term | Subject area | A group of entities about one business subject
Term | Data product | A set of entities with one system of record, one way into the Workbench and one freshness, published for use by decisions, screens and reports
Term | Entity | A thing the model holds a record of: a Workbench table, an extension table or an ACE source view
Term | System of record | The system whose value is correct when two systems differ
Value | Held in the Workbench | The Workbench is the system of record and writes the data itself
Value | ACE end of day | ACE ingests the source at the end of the business day; the Workbench reads the result through a v_ace_* view the next morning
Value | Reuse ACE | The entity exists in ACE and is read through a v_ace_* view as it is
Value | Extend ACE | The entity exists in ACE and the Workbench adds fields or states in its own table or extension table
Value | New | The entity is added in the recovery module
Value | Many to one | Every record refers to exactly one record of the other entity
Value | Many to zero or one | A record may refer to one record of the other entity or to none
Standard | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 | Requirements for data and information
Standard | Bank TSD section T3 | Metadata-driven data model: objects, fields and records, standard columns, lists of values and relationships
Term | ACE source view | A SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* view over ACE source tables. The only read path from the recovery module into ACE
Term | Extension table | A Workbench 1:1 table keyed by an ACE business key. Holds Workbench flags and decisions about an ACE record, never a copy of it
Term | Business key | The ACE key a Workbench table stores to link to a view, for example account_key or person_key. No foreign key is created
Value | ACE (ingested from X) | ACE is the system of record; the named source lands in ACE through ACE ingestion, not through a Workbench load

DF-EXT-036 | valuation_ext | valuation_key | Indirect identifier | Confidential | Shown within the role's scope; masked in UAT | ACE appraisal key the decision belongs to

Handling rule by classification
What each classification means for storage, screens, logs, prompts, test data and export.
Classification | Where | Rule
Restricted | Stored | ACE source fields stored in ACE only; Workbench Restricted fields encrypted at rest. Identification numbers never leave ACE in clear
Restricted | On screen | Masked unless the role is allowed to see the field for cases in its scope
Restricted | In logs | Never written to application logs. Every read of a v_ace_* personal field is logged through PII Kafka
Restricted | In agent prompts | Removed or masked before a prompt is built
Restricted | In test data | Synthetic in DEV. Masked copies in SIT and UAT
Restricted | Export | Blocked except through an approved extract, logged with the requester
Restricted | Debt sale tape | Only the fields the sale terms allow, after the award
Confidential | Stored | Encrypted at rest and in transit
Confidential | On screen | Shown within the role's scope. Indirect identifiers masked in UAT
Confidential | In agent prompts | Only the fields the agent's step needs
Confidential | Export | Within the role's scope, logged
Internal | Stored | Encrypted at rest and in transit
Internal | On screen | By permission
All | Retention | Set per data product and document type by Compliance (DL26). A legal hold overrides retention
All | Data subject request | Access, correction or erasure routed to Compliance inside the statutory period; automated processing on the case is held (R-UNI-11)
Restricted | In ACE | customer.identification_number is never exposed in clear. v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked (last four) and id_no_last4 only
Restricted | Contact values | phone.phone_number, email.email and address.address are full in v_ace_contact because notices and calls need them. Display masking is E1-037 at the API, and every read is audited
Restricted | Every ACE read | The recovery identity holds SELECT only on recovery.v_ace_* and on nothing else. A read of a personal field is audited; a direct public read fails in the catalog

Who sees personal data unmasked
Proposed until Compliance issues the masking rules (DL26). Held as data, so a change needs no release.
Role | Scope | Direct identifiers | Sensitive flags
Case owner | Own cases | Unmasked | Masked unless the case has the deviation
Team manager | Team | Unmasked | Masked
Restructuring, litigation, enforcement, guarantee, sale, NPA and debt sale officers | Team | Unmasked | Masked
Hardship and vulnerability specialist, complaint officer, fraud investigator | Cases with their deviation | Unmasked | Unmasked
Legal counsel | All | Unmasked | Unmasked
Phone and field collectors | Own cases | Name and contact points only | Masked
Credit Administration and the write-off team | All | Unmasked | Masked
Compliance and PDPA officer | All | Unmasked | Unmasked
Internal audit | All | Unmasked, read only, logged | Unmasked, read only, logged
Center of excellence, reporting and BI, data steward, Risk | All | Masked | Masked
Platform, security and reference data administrators | All | Masked | Masked
Partner users | Placed cases | Name, contact points and what the instruction needs | Masked
Agents | As the step needs | Removed or masked | Removed or masked
ACE service identity | All | SELECT only on v_ace_* views; every read audited | Same; never shown on a screen

Key
What each category and class means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Category | Direct identifier | Identifies a person on its own: name, identity number, date of birth, contact point, free text about them
Category | Sensitive | May reveal health, death or insolvency. Handled as sensitive data under PDPA section 26
Category | Indirect identifier | Identifies a person when joined to other data: account, contract, case, lawsuit, title deed
Category | Customer data | Data about an identified customer: profile, debt, case, assets or contacts
Category | Staff identifier | Identifies a bank employee or a partner user
Category | Not personal | Reference, configuration, partner company or asset data
Class | Restricted | Highest protection: masked or never exposed in clear, never in logs or prompts
Class | Confidential | Customer data shown within scope, encrypted
Class | Internal | Bank internal data shown by permission
Standard | Thai PDPA | Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562
Category | ACE contact value | A phone number, email address or postal address read through v_ace_contact. Full value where a notice or a call needs it; masked for display at E1-037
Class | Read audit | Every read of a personal field on a v_ace_* view is written to the access log through PII Kafka

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Data migration approach

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench data migration approach
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Henka word rules
Decision | D-RCV-35: ACE holds the source data; the Workbench migrates only its own case state, documents, decisions and reference data

What | Data product | Scope | History | How | When
Case and ownership state | DP03 | Open cases: status, stage, route, owner, queue, tasks, timers and deviations | Current position | Spreadsheet extract, re-keyed to person_key and account_key | E1
Recovery team spreadsheets | DP03, DP04 | The Excel and SharePoint lists of open recovery work | Open items only | File extract, then retired through the Cutover plan (U5) | E1
Treatment records | DP04 | Restructures, settlements and deeds agreed but not yet booked, with their approvals | Open only | Spreadsheet extract; the plan itself is read from v_ace_plan | E2
Documents | DP10 | Documents for open cases in shared drives and the mailroom | Open cases only; originals tracked | Bulk intake through OCR | E1 and E2
Decision log | DP12 | Decisions taken outside the Workbench on the open cases, with their rule and model version | Open cases only | Spreadsheet extract | E1
Partners and open instructions | DP08 | Panel firms and their open work | Open instructions | Partner master load | E4 to E6
Reference data | DP14 | Rules, approval limits, lists of values, roles and letter templates | Current versions | Validated load, versioned | E1

These data products are already in ACE. Nothing of them moves into the recovery schema: the Workbench reads them through the view named beside each one and holds only its own decisions about them, in party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext.

Already in ACE | Read through
Account, arrears, balances, bucket and classification | v_ace_account
Payments and proceeds | v_ace_payment
Customer, identity and relations | v_ace_customer, v_ace_ca_relation
Phone, email and address | v_ace_contact
Collateral, assets and appraisals | v_ace_collateral, v_ace_asset, v_ace_valuation, v_ace_npa_asset, v_ace_npa_sale
Collections history from EFS | v_ace_efs_action
Lawsuits, hearings and proof of delivery | v_ace_lawsuit, v_ace_hearing, v_ace_pod
Write-offs and GL postings | v_ace_write_off
Scores and route economics | v_ace_score

ACE holds the source data. The Workbench runs no load of accounts, payments, customer, contact, collateral or collections history, and migrates none of it.

Only open work and the history a decision needs move; closed history stays in its source.

Every migrated record carries its source and migration date.

Each migration reconciles to its source before cutover, and the case list reconciles to v_ace_account.

Spreadsheets are retired with a read-only archive once their content is on the case.

A link to a source record is a business key, never a copy of the record.

State today | On the Workbench
Account at 90 days past due with no recovery action | New case, allocated by rule; the account is read from v_ace_account
In restructure or settlement | Case with the treatment record and its status; the plan is read from v_ace_plan
In litigation | Case in the litigation stage, linked to v_ace_lawsuit and v_ace_hearing; the Workbench keeps the instruction
Asset held | Case linked by asset_key to v_ace_asset and v_ace_npa_asset where the case is open
In a partner's hands | Case with an open partner instruction

Six of the fourteen migration stories change. The other eight, DM-003, DM-004, DM-007, DM-008, DM-009, DM-010, DM-012 and DM-014, keep their scope, with their sources re-worded to ACE where a read replaces a load.

Story | New scope
RWB-DM-001 Migrate account and arrears | Out of scope. The data is in ACE and is read through v_ace_account.
RWB-DM-002 Migrate customer and party | Out of scope. The data is in ACE and is read through v_ace_customer, v_ace_ca_relation and v_ace_contact.
RWB-DM-005 Migrate contact and promises | Reduced to the Workbench part. EFS history is read through v_ace_efs_action; only the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS move.
RWB-DM-006 Migrate collateral and assets | Reduced to the Workbench part. Collateral, appraisals, NPA assets and sales are read through v_ace_collateral, v_ace_valuation, v_ace_asset, v_ace_npa_asset and v_ace_npa_sale; only listings, case asset links and sale instructions move.
RWB-DM-011 Migrate scores and route economics | Reduced to the Workbench part. COLLINS scores are read through v_ace_score; only the expected-return and sale-estimate records the Workbench calculates move.
RWB-DM-013 Migrate money and closure | Reduced to the Workbench part. Payments and GL postings are read through v_ace_payment and v_ace_write_off; only proceeds matching and closure records move.

Each team runs its spreadsheet and the Workbench side by side for two weeks after its first release. The data steward reconciles daily. The spreadsheet retires when the business lead signs ten clean days.

Counts and balances per data product reconcile to the source within the tolerance under DL25. Breaks are listed for the data steward and cleared before cutover.

The cut-over check is the case list. Every case_list_row.account_key must resolve to a row in v_ace_account for the cut-over business date, and the count of open cases by product and bucket must agree with the view. A key that does not resolve is either a closed account or a key error; both are cleared before go-live, and the result is recorded against reconciliation rule REC-05. No case starts on the Workbench until this check passes.

Decision | What is needed
DL12 | Which legacy systems are kept, and what the Workbench reads from each. Option A is superseded by D-RCV-35: the read path is the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, not a direct read of ACE or COLLINS
DL29 | Closed: EFS contact history is read through v_ace_efs_action, so no migration decision is needed
DL43 | Open with the ACE team lead, needed by 2026-11-21: the ACE team accepts the RWB-ACE-001 scope and dates (14 new ACE tables, 12 new columns). The Tier 2 reads this approach names depend on it

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Data Ownership and Stewardship v3.xlsx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Data Ownership and Stewardship v3

secs.t:
Who owns each data product
14 data products, each with one business owner, one steward and one system of record. ACE owns the source data; the Workbench owns the case. The tier column says which, and RWB-ACE-001 is the only route to a new field in Tier 1 or Tier 2.
ID | Data product | What it holds | Business owner | Data steward | System of record | System of record owner | Who may change it | How a change is requested | Freshness | Tier
DP01 | Account and arrears | Loan accounts with balances, interest, fees, days past due, bucket, classification, restructure flag and payments | Product heads | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (account and payment, ingested from ALS) | Core banking owner | The ACE team only; the Workbench reads the view | Raise it with the ACE team; a new field is a change to RWB-ACE-001 | End of day in ACE; read as of the ACE business date | 1
DP02 | Customer and party | Customers, guarantors, co-borrowers and heirs, identity numbers masked in the view, contact points, consent and flags for vulnerability, death and bankruptcy | Compliance and PDPA officer | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (customer, ca_relation and contact views) | Data and analytics owner | The ACE team only; Workbench flags live in the extension tables | Raise it with the ACE team; a new field is a change to RWB-ACE-001 | End of day in ACE; read as of the ACE business date | 1 and 3
DP03 | Case and ownership | The case, its accounts and parties, status, stage, route, owner, queue, tasks, timers and deviations | Business lead | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench | Application owner (DL02) | Users with the right in the permission matrix, through Workbench screens | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP04 | Treatment and offers | Restructures, settlements, deeds in lieu, buy-backs and guarantee claims, with terms, approval level and outcome | Product heads | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench; restructure plans read from v_ace_plan | Application owner with the ACE team | Users with the right in the permission matrix for the Workbench record; the ACE team for the plan | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP05 | Contact and promises | Every contact, letter, promise and hand-over on the case, in order, including the collections history from EFS | Business lead | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (efs_action) and the Workbench for its own interactions | Collections system owner; application owner | The ACE team for EFS history; users for Workbench interactions | Raise it with the ACE team for EFS history; Workbench fields go to the product owner | End of day in ACE for EFS history; as it changes here | 1 and 4
DP06 | Collateral and assets | Collateral, appraisals, assets held after repossession or transfer, listings and sale results | Head of NPA | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (collateral, asset, valuation, npa_asset and npa_sale) | Collateral, valuation, NPA and repossession system owners | The ACE team only; the Workbench decides in valuation_ext | Raise it with the ACE team; a new field is a change to RWB-ACE-001 | Weekly or monthly in ACE, as each source ingests | 1 and 2
DP07 | Legal events and cases | Notices and proof of delivery, lawsuits, court case numbers, hearings, judgments and enforcement | Head of Litigation | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (lawsuit and hearing) and the Workbench for instructions | Legal systems owner; application owner | The ACE team for court records; users for instructions | Raise it with the ACE team for court records; Workbench fields go to the product owner | End of day in ACE for LIT status | 2 and 4
DP08 | Partner performance | Partners on the panel, work placed with each, results, fees and scorecards | Partner and agency manager | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench | Application owner (DL02) | Users with the right in the permission matrix, through Workbench screens | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP09 | Debt sale | Debt sale lots, the accounts in each lot, buyers, prices, approval and put-backs | Head of Asset Liquidity | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench | Application owner (DL02) | Users with the right in the permission matrix, through Workbench screens | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP10 | Documents and extracted fields | Documents against the case, the fields read from them, retention class and custody of originals | Legal counsel | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench document hub | Application owner (DL02) | The document hub; legal documents are write-once | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP11 | Scores and route economics | Risk scores, expected return by route, estimated sale price and sale success rate, restructure scheme suggestions | Risk and model risk officer | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (collins_score) and the Workbench for route economics | Data and analytics owner | The ACE team for scores; the product owner for route economics | Raise it with the ACE team for scores; Workbench changes go to the product owner | End of day in ACE for scores; monthly for some models | 2 and 4
DP12 | Decision log | One entry per decision with the rule, model and agent versions, inputs, recommendation, approval, actions and outcome | Risk and model risk officer | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench | Application owner (DL02) | No one; append only. Corrections are new entries | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | As it changes | 4
DP13 | Money and closure | Payments and proceeds matched to the case, write-off postings and recovery after charge-off | Finance and CFO delegate | Data steward and data product owner | ACE (payment and gl_write_off) and the Workbench for matching | Core banking and finance systems owners | The ACE team only; the Workbench matches proceeds to the case | Raise it with the ACE team; a new field is a change to RWB-ACE-001 | End of day in ACE for payments; monthly for GL | 1, 2 and 4
DP14 | Reference data | Rules, approval limits, lists of values, roles, permissions and letter templates, each versioned | Center of excellence | Data steward and data product owner | Recovery Workbench | Application owner (DL02) | Reference data administrator, after approval by the list owner; Risk where a limit moves | Raise the change with the business owner; the product owner adds it to the backlog or the reference data administrator loads it | By versioned load | 4

Who owns which tier
ACE owns the source data, the Workbench owns the case. RWB-ACE-001 is the only route to a new field in Tier 1 or Tier 2; a Workbench request never alters an ACE table.
Tier | What it holds | Owner | Who may add a field | Route for a new field | Workbench access
1 | 22 ACE tables that exist today, read through 16 views | ACE team | The ACE team, under ACE change control | No new ACE object: the view maps a column ACE already holds. If ACE holds nothing, the field is Tier 2 | SELECT through recovery.v_ace_* only
2 | 14 new tables and 12 new columns for source data that ACE does not hold, read through 14 views | ACE team | The ACE team, under ACE change control | RWB-ACE-001, with a field row in the ACE Field Gap List. The views ship the week it lands | SELECT once the view exists; the feature stays behind its flag until then
3 | 4 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys: party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext | Workbench data steward | The Workbench data steward, with the business owner | Workbench backlog. The table holds a decision about an ACE record and never a copy of one | Read and write by the recovery module
4 | 88 Workbench tables: case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, debt sale, documents, decision log, reference, outbox, flags and agents | Workbench data steward | The Workbench data steward, with the business owner | Workbench backlog; the product owner approves, and the change is versioned in the data dictionary | Read and write by the recovery module
A screen that needs a new source field follows the Tier 2 route even when the screen is a Workbench screen. The Workbench never alters an ACE table and never adds a column to one.

Data roles
What each data role does.
Role | Accountable for
Business owner | Decides what the data means, who may use it and the quality it must meet. Approves definition changes in the Workbench and sponsors an RWB-ACE-001 change for a source field
Data steward | Keeps definitions, read mappings, quality checks and the exception list. The Workbench data steward owns Tier 3 and Tier 4; the ACE data steward owns the ingestion checks for Tier 1 and Tier 2
System of record owner | Owns the source system and its fields. The ACE team lead holds this for Tier 1 and Tier 2; the Workbench application owner holds it for Tier 3 and Tier 4. Confirms the read mapping
Application owner | Owns the Workbench as the system of record for the data it creates
Reference data administrator | Loads lists, rules and limits after the owner approves, in the Workbench only
Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the classification, masking and retention for personal data
ACE team lead | Owns the Tier 1 and Tier 2 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 scope and dates, and the SELECT grant the views need. Approves every change to an ACE table or column the views read
ACE data steward | Keeps the identity match M1 to M5, the ingestion checks and the per-source business date that v_ace_batch_status reports

How a data change is requested
Every change to a data product follows these steps.
Step | Stage | What happens
1 | Request | The requester raises the change with the business owner, with the reason and the date it is needed
2 | Assess | The data steward assesses the effect on the read mapping, the checks, the reports and the models; the ACE team assesses it too where a Tier 1 or Tier 2 field moves
3 | Approve | The business owner approves. Compliance approves where personal data changes; Risk where a limit or a model input changes
4 | Make | A Tier 1 or Tier 2 change is made by the ACE team, through RWB-ACE-001 for a new field; a Tier 3 or Tier 4 change goes to the Workbench backlog; a list or limit change is a validated load
5 | Test | The change runs through the ACE ingestion checks and the view conformance test in SIT
6 | Release | In the monthly release, or as a validated reference load with a valid from date
7 | Record | The data dictionary and the mapping are updated with the version

What the steward measures
Measured for every data product each day.
Measure | Meaning | Where it is checked
Completeness | Every mandatory field is filled | ACE ingestion checks
Accuracy | Balances reconcile to the core bank within the tolerance (DL25) | Daily reconciliation
Timeliness | The data product carries the expected business date | v_ace_batch_status
Validity | Every coded value is in its list | ACE ingestion checks
Uniqueness | One case per customer per product (DL17) | ACE identity match M1 to M5
View conformance | Every v_ace_* view compiles and no recovery table reads public.* | Build pipeline
Freshness stamp | The ACE business date is visible on the case screen | Screen check

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3

secs.t:
Load checks, retired to ACE ingestion
98 load checks, retired. Every one tested an inbound Workbench load that no longer exists: business date, structure, control total, keys, references, lists of values and movement. Each row is kept with its ID and marked moved to the ACE team; the ACE ingestion checks that replace it are in RWB-ACE-001.
ID | Interface | Source | Data product | Check | What it tests | Tolerance | If it fails | Owner | Status
DQ-001 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | Business date | The load is for the expected business date and is not a repeat | None | Refuse the load | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)
DQ-002 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | Structure | Every field present with its type and length | None | Refuse the load | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)
DQ-003 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | Control total | Record count and balance total match the trailer | Zero | Refuse the load | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)
DQ-004 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | Keys | Every record has its key; no key twice | None | Refuse the load | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)
DQ-005 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | References | Each account, customer or asset can be matched | Up to 0.5 percent held | Hold the records; refuse above the tolerance | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)
DQ-006 | INT-01 | Core bank (ALS) | DP01 | Lists of values | Each code maps to its list | Up to 0.5 percent held | Hold the records; refuse above the tolerance | Data steward | Moved to ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001)

Reconciliations
Nine reconciliations. Each compares ACE, read through a v_ace_* view, with the case list or the Workbench record it feeds. None is a load check: the Workbench does not load source data.
ID | Source side | Workbench side | Compared on | Tolerance | When | Break goes to
REC-01 | Accounts at 90 days past due or more in recovery.v_ace_account, less the accounts excluded at entry | Open recovery cases and the case list rows | Count by product | Zero unexplained | Daily | Break list to the data steward
REC-02 | Balances in recovery.v_ace_account | Balances on the case accounts and the case list rows | Sum by product | Zero | Daily | Break list to the data steward
REC-03 | Approved treatments whose plan is booked in recovery.v_ace_plan | Treatments approved in the Workbench | Count and amount | Zero after two days | Daily | Task to the officer
REC-04 | Payments in recovery.v_ace_payment | Proceeds matched to cases | Count and amount | Unmatched held on the exception list | Daily | Reconciliation agent; Credit Administration
REC-05 | Every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code on a Workbench table | The matching row in v_ace_account, v_ace_customer, v_ace_asset and v_ace_payment | Business key, count and amount | Zero orphans; every one listed | Daily | Data steward; the ACE team where the row is missing in ACE
REC-06 | Write-offs approved in the Workbench | Postings in recovery.v_ace_write_off | Count and amount | Zero | Monthly | Credit Administration
REC-07 | Assets taken on in the Workbench | Assets in recovery.v_ace_npa_asset | Count | Zero | Weekly | Head of NPA
REC-08 | Decision log copy | Live decision log | Count and last hash | Zero | Nightly | Data steward
REC-09 | Notices sent to WIN | Barcodes returned in recovery.v_ace_pod | Count | Zero after three days | Daily | Platform administrator

Data quality measures
Reported daily on the data quality console. The retired load checks are not counted here; freshness is read from the ACE batch, not from a Workbench load.
Measure | Meaning | Target
Completeness | Mandatory fields filled on the Workbench tables and in the views the screens read | 99.9 percent
Validity | Codes in their lists, including the ACE code lists read through v_ace_efs_action_code and v_ace_product | 99.5 percent
Timeliness | The ACE batch for the business date is complete when the Workbench reads it | 99 percent of days
Accuracy | Reconciliation breaks cleared within one day | 100 percent
Uniqueness | One case per customer per product | 100 percent
Referential completeness | Every business key on a Workbench table resolves to a v_ace_* row (REC-05) | 100 percent

secs.h: The ACE boundary and the references between data products
secs.t:
122 objects: 88 Workbench tables, 4 extension tables and 30 ACE source views, with 104 references. The 14 data products hold 97 of them; OPS, AGT and RPT hold the other 25. The views are external and read only, and their boxes are dashed. The 18 business-key links carry no foreign key into ACE; the other 86 references are ordinary foreign keys inside the recovery schema.

These are the only way the recovery module reads ACE. Each is a SELECT-only view over one ACE object family, owned by ace_view_owner ; the recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and on nothing else in public . They have no primary key and no foreign key, and the Workbench links to them by business key. Section A ships with RWB-E1-069; Section B ships the week RWB-ACE-001 lands.

View | Tier | ACE objects read | Data product | What it gives the Workbench
v_ace_account | 1 | public.account, public.product, public.branch | DP01 | Read-only view over the ACE account: balances, arrears, days past due, classification, restructure flag and the ACE business date. Replaces the former loan account copy.
v_ace_payment | 1 | public.payment, public.account | DP01 | Read-only view over the ACE payment: amount, capital, interest and expense split, channel and payment date. Replaces the former account payment copy.
v_ace_customer | 1 | public.customer | DP02 | Read-only view over the ACE customer: name, identity masked to the last four, date of birth, status and profile. Replaces the former customer copy.
v_ace_contact | 1 | public.phone, public.email, public.address | DP02 | Read-only view over ACE phone, email and address, unioned behind a contact_type discriminator. Replaces the former contact point copy; values in full because notices need them.
v_ace_ca_relation | 1 | public.ca_relation | DP02 | Read-only view over the ACE borrower, guarantor and co-borrower relation, with the guarantee amount.
v_ace_aa_relation | 1 | public.aa_relation | DP01 | Read-only view over the ACE parent and child account link.
v_ace_collateral | 1 | public.collateral, public.asset | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE collateral link: collateral number, asset, account, value and type. Replaces the former collateral copy.
v_ace_asset | 1 | public.asset | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE asset: the collateral asset, its type and its address. Replaces the former asset copy.
v_ace_efs_action | 1 | public.efs_action | DP05 | Read-only view over the ACE collections action: action code, contact result, promise and outcome. Replaces the former collections history copy.
v_ace_efs_action_code | 1 | public.efs_action_code | DP14 | Read-only view over the ACE action code list: 1,106 values, with the English name and category.
v_ace_efs_assignment | 1 | public.efs_assignment | DP05 | Read-only view over the ACE assignment and hand-over history, with the balance at each hand-over.
v_ace_bucket_log | 1 | public.bucket_log_snapshot, public.account | DP01 | Read-only view over the ACE monthly bucket snapshot: bucket, past due amount and month start.
v_ace_product | 1 | public.product | DP14 | Read-only view over the ACE product list: code, name, type and category. Source of the product and product code lists.
v_ace_branch | 1 | public.branch | DP14 | Read-only view over the ACE branch list: code, name, address and phone. Source of the branch, business unit and region values.
v_ace_holiday | 1 | public.bot_holiday | DP14 | Read-only view over the ACE holiday calendar, used for service levels and legal days.
v_ace_plan | 1 | public.ace_case, public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, public.account, public.tdr_calculation, public.ai_recommended_plan | DP04 | Read-only view over the ACE restructure plan: reference, status, booking, approval and the published calculation.
v_ace_batch_status | 2 | public.ace_batch_run | OPS | Read-only view over the ACE batch record: source, business date, completion, row count and checksum. Drives the Workbench freshness stamp.
v_ace_valuation | 2 | public.valuation | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE appraisal: number, type, appraised and forced sale value, date. Replaces the former valuation copy.
v_ace_collateral_detail | 2 | public.collateral_detail | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE collateral detail: title deed, plot, area, province, district, insurance and lien rank. Replaces the former collateral link copy.
v_ace_npa_asset | 2 | public.npa_asset | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE NPA asset: transfer in, book value, auction price and repossession dates.
v_ace_npa_sale | 2 | public.npa_sale | DP06 | Read-only view over the ACE NPA sale: contract, sale price, taxes, fees and incentive.
v_ace_lawsuit | 2 | public.lawsuit | DP07 | Read-only view over the ACE lawsuit: court case numbers, claim, filing, judgment and status.
v_ace_hearing | 2 | public.hearing | DP07 | Read-only view over the ACE hearing: date, type and next date.
v_ace_pod | 2 | public.pod_receipt | DP07 | Read-only view over the ACE proof of delivery: notice reference, barcode, sent date and delivery status.
v_ace_write_off | 2 | public.gl_write_off | DP13 | Read-only view over the ACE write-off posting: amount, posted date, responsibility and cost centre.
v_ace_score | 2 | public.collins_score | DP11 | Read-only view over the ACE score: model, version, score, estimate and route. Replaces the former score copy.
v_ace_party_product | 2 | public.party_product | DP02 | Read-only view over the ACE customer product holding: product type and status. Replaces the former product holding copy.
v_ace_credit_decision | 2 | public.credit_decision | DP04 | Read-only view over the ACE credit decision: NLEADS reference, result, reason and decision date.
v_ace_esign | 2 | public.esign_request | DP10 | Read-only view over the ACE e-signature request: external reference, requested date and status. The signed file stays in the Workbench document hub.

Every view box is dashed: it is external to the recovery schema and read only. The fields are the view columns named for the Workbench, not the ACE column names. A field marked B is one of the 12 Tier 2 columns that V0003 adds to an existing view through CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW: seven on v_ace_account, three on v_ace_customer and two on v_ace_efs_action.

The page uses the IDEF1X key notation for entities and keys, and adds a notation for the ACE boundary.

Symbol | Meaning
Square-cornered box | A Workbench table. Its key does not depend on any other entity
Name above the box | The entity name as it is held in the physical schema
Line inside the box | Above the line is the primary key. Below it are the other attributes
(PK) | The primary key of the entity
(AK1) | An alternate key: unique on its own or together with the other AK1 attributes
(FK) | A foreign key inside the recovery schema
(BK) | A business key. The column holds an ACE business key and carries no foreign key
Dashed box with an ACE view name | An ACE source view. External to the recovery schema, read only, no primary key and no foreign key
Orange left edge | A Workbench extension table, 1:1 with an ACE record and keyed by its business key
Dashed grey box | An entity outside the recovery schema, shown with its key and its fields
Label on a reference | The kind: foreign key, business key, or business key on a 1:1 extension
A view box lists the view columns as the Workbench names them. The ACE name appears only in the view definition and the STTM. A blue-purple view box is never written and never the parent of a foreign key.

Entity | Business name | Subject area | Data product | What it is | System of record | ACE | Fields | Personal data fields

case_party | Case party | Case | DP03 | The role each party plays on a case. | Workbench | New | 6
deviation | Deviation | Case | DP03 | A deviation X1 to X7 raised on a case. | Workbench | New | 10
queue | Queue | Work management | DP03 | A queue of work belonging to one team and one role. | Workbench | Extend ACE work queue | 10
assignment | Assignment | Work management | DP03 | Who holds a case or a task and from when. | Workbench | Reuse ACE Assignee | 10
task | Task | Work management | DP03 | A unit of work on a case: a CMMN human, customer, partner or decision task. | Workbench | New | 10
timer | Timer | Work management | DP03 | A running clock on a case: a service level, a legal period or an offer validity. | Workbench | New | 14

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Party and customer master data design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench party and customer master data design
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, bank TSD section T3
Decision | D-RCV-35: ACE holds the source data, the Workbench reads it through recovery.v_ace_* views

Element | Design
Golden source | The ACE database. ACE ingests the customer, contact and account facts from SCBPDM and the core bank (DL20, as amended by D-RCV-35). The Workbench loads nothing.
Key | The ACE person_key. cif_no in v_ace_customer carries the same customer number, so a CIF match is a person_key match.
In the Workbench | No local party table and no local contact_point table. A party is the ACE customer and its ca_relation rows, read through v_ace_customer, v_ace_ca_relation and v_ace_contact, plus one recovery.party_ext row for the Workbench flags.
Identity matching | Run in ACE ingestion under M1 to M5. The Workbench consumes the surviving person_key and never re-masters, re-matches or merges a person.
Partners | Partner master held in the Workbench; one row per firm, keyed by partner_code. A partner firm is a Workbench record, not an ACE customer.
Duplicates | Decided before the row reaches the Workbench. A suspected duplicate is raised with the ACE data steward; the Workbench has no merge function.
Identity number | identification_number stays in ACE in clear. v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked and id_no_last4; no token is created at load because there is no load.

Party | Identified by | Source
Borrower | person_key, with cif_no from v_ace_customer; the account link from v_ace_ca_relation | ACE, ingested from SCBPDM and the core bank
Co-borrower and guarantor | person_key through v_ace_ca_relation, with relation_type, amount_of_guarantee and date_of_guarantee | ACE, ingested from SCBPDM and the core bank
Heir and estate representative | Named on the case in the document and decision log; linked as a case party by person_key only where ACE holds the person | Workbench documents; ACE where the person is a customer
Juristic person | person_key, with id_type and the masked registration number from v_ace_customer | ACE, ingested from SCBPDM
Partner firm | partner_code; tax ID | Workbench partner master

No row in this table creates a person. A party that ACE does not hold is not a party in the Workbench: an heir or an estate representative is named in the case documents and the decision log, and is linked as a case party only when ACE holds them as a customer. The Workbench never adds a person to the customer master to make a case work.

M1 to M5 are ACE ingestion rules. They run before a customer row reaches the Workbench, and the outcome is a single person_key. The Workbench does not match, merge or re-master a person: it reads the key and links its own records to it. A duplicate that survives into the Workbench is raised with the ACE data steward and corrected in ACE, not in the recovery schema.

M1 - CIF equal. ACE treats the records as one customer and publishes one person_key. The Workbench reads that key.

M2 - Identity type and number equal. ACE treats the records as one customer, using identification_number as it holds it. The Workbench sees the masked value only.

M3 - Name and date of birth equal, with no CIF and no identity number. ACE raises a possible duplicate and the ACE data steward decides. It is never an automatic merge, and the Workbench never merges.

M4 - Company registration number equal. ACE treats the records as one juristic person.

M5 - Partner tax ID equal. ACE treats the records as one firm; the partner and agency manager confirms the panel entry in the Workbench partner master.

Attribute | Wins
Name, identity, date of birth | ACE, ingested from SCBPDM. Read from v_ace_customer; no Workbench copy and no override
Contact points | ACE phone, email and address, read through v_ace_contact. All three are shown; the most recently verified is preferred, and the verification is held in contact_point_ext
Vulnerable, deceased, bankruptcy, fraud | recovery.party_ext, set in the Workbench by the handler with the evidence document. deceased_override wins over the ACE deceased flag, and the ACE value is shown beside it
Consent | recovery.contact_point_ext, recorded against contact_key and contact_type. ACE holds no consent column

The clear identity number never leaves ACE, and no token is created in its place. The view is the only read path, and the grant on the view, E1-037 and the audit log are the control.

Value | Where it lives | What the Workbench sees
identification_number | public.customer, in clear | id_no_masked, all but the last four replaced, and id_no_last4, both from v_ace_customer. No Workbench table holds the clear value
id_no_token | Removed | There is no tokenization at load because there is no load. E1-037 role masking replaces the token as the display control
phone_number, email, address | public.phone, email and address, in clear | contact_value in v_ace_contact, in full, for notices and calls; contact_value_masked for display. Every read is audited
Masking control | The SELECT grant on v_ace_customer, E1-037 at the API, the audit log | The view mask alone is not the control; the ACE DB Alignment Change Register records this as risk R5

A Workbench column, report extract or lake table never carries identification_number. Where a report needs an identifier it uses id_no_masked; where a case must prove identity it cites the document in the document hub.

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL20 | Source of customer facts | ACE, which ingests them from SCBPDM and the core bank. Closed by D-RCV-35
DL43 | Does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and dates? | Open. If the scope and dates are accepted, party_type, id_type and segment appear in v_ace_customer when RWB-ACE-001 lands; until then they read blank and the rest of the design is unaffected

Match rules
M1 to M5 run in ACE ingestion, before a customer row reaches the Workbench.
Rule | Condition | Result | Action
M1 | CIF number equal | Same ACE customer | Automatic in ACE; the Workbench reads one person_key
M2 | Identity type and number equal | Same ACE customer | Automatic in ACE; the number is masked in the view
M3 | Name and date of birth equal, no CIF or identity number | Possible duplicate | ACE data steward decides; the Workbench never merges
M4 | Company registration number equal | Same juristic person | Automatic in ACE
M5 | Partner tax ID equal | Same firm | Automatic in ACE; the partner manager confirms the panel entry
M1 to M5 run in ACE ingestion. The Workbench never re-matches, merges or re-masters a person: it reads the person_key that ACE publishes in v_ace_customer. A suspected duplicate is raised with the ACE data steward.

-- Recovery Workbench physical schema, PostgreSQL
-- SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026. Version 5.
-- (C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd
-- 92 tables and 30 views in the recovery module of the ACE database, the metadata registry of bank TSD section T3, and seed reference data.
-- Source data is read from the ACE database through recovery.v_ace_* views (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). No inbound load table, no source copy.
-- Flyway split: V0001 tables and dictionary, V0002 Tier 1 views, V0003 Tier 2 views once RWB-ACE-001 lands.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS recovery;
SET search_path TO recovery;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;


-- Recovery case: One recovery case per customer per product, from 90 days past due to close.
CREATE TABLE recovery_case (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 case_no varchar(18) NOT NULL,
 product_group varchar(15) NOT NULL,
 primary_person_key varchar(255),
 status varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NEW',
 stage_code varchar(20),
 route_state varchar(60),
 route_code varchar(4),

 queue_id uuid,
 team_code varchar(20),
 region_code varchar(10),
 entry_date date NOT NULL,
 dpd_at_entry integer NOT NULL,
 exposure_band varchar(10),
 total_outstanding_at_entry numeric(18,2) NOT NULL,
 prescription_date date,
 stage_clock_start timestamptz,
 deviation_open boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
 legal_hold boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
 rule_version varchar(20),
 closed_date date,
 closure_reason varchar(20),
 plan_ref varchar(30),
 plan_status varchar(10),
 plan_status_as_of date,
 next_action_text varchar(1000),
 next_action_owner_role varchar(20),
 next_action_due_date date,
 next_action_rule_id varchar(20),
 next_action_waiting boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
 last_allocation_date date,
 status_before_hold varchar(20),
 is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
 state varchar(40),
 version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 created_by uuid,
 updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 updated_by uuid,
 CONSTRAINT uk_recovery_case UNIQUE (case_no)
);

-- Case account: Links each loan account to the case it is recovered under.
CREATE TABLE case_account (

 state varchar(40),

 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 created_by uuid,
 updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 updated_by uuid
);

-- Case party: The role each party plays on a case.
CREATE TABLE case_party (

-- Deviation: A deviation X1 to X7 raised on a case.
CREATE TABLE deviation (

 created_by uuid,

 updated_by uuid
);

-- Queue: A queue of work belonging to one team and one role.
CREATE TABLE queue (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

);

-- Assignment: Who holds a case or a task and from when.
CREATE TABLE assignment (

 updated_by uuid

-- Task: A unit of work on a case: a CMMN human, customer, partner or decision task.
CREATE TABLE task (

-- Treatment: A resolution put to the customer or carried out on the case, with its terms and outcome.
CREATE TABLE treatment (

CREATE TABLE guarantee_claim (

-- Legal action: A notice, lawsuit, appeal, enforcement or bankruptcy action on a case.
CREATE TABLE legal_action (

CREATE TABLE notice (

-- Hearing: A court hearing on a legal action.
CREATE TABLE hearing (

-- Partner: An outside firm the bank places work with.
CREATE TABLE partner (

CREATE TABLE debt_sale_account (

-- References between tables

-- v_data_dictionary: the data dictionary as one row per field, joining the metadata tables to
-- the data product catalog so a developer can ask where a field comes from and who owns it.
CREATE VIEW v_data_dictionary AS
SELECT o.object_name AS entity,
 f.field_name AS field,
 f.field_id,
 f.data_type,
 f.physical_type,
 f.is_mandatory,
 f.lov_code,
 f.references_object,
 f.source_system,
 f.source_field,
 f.is_personal,
 o.data_product,
 p.refresh_cycle,
 f.owner_role,
 p.owner_user_id,
 f.late_behavior,
 f.interface_id,
 f.description
FROM sys_fields f
JOIN sys_objects o ON o.object_name = f.object_name
LEFT JOIN data_product p ON p.product_code = o.data_product AND p.is_active
WHERE f.is_active AND o.is_active;

COMMENT ON VIEW v_data_dictionary IS 'The data dictionary as one row per field, with its data product, refresh cycle and owner.';

-- The decision log and the interaction ledger are append only
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION refuse_change() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
 RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append only: % refused', TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER tr_declog_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON decision_log_entry FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_change();
CREATE TRIGGER tr_interaction_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON interaction FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_change();

-- Helper functions. Immutable, no side effects, safe in a view definition.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- ACE stores some dates as text. Accept ISO, YYYYMMDD and DD/MM/YYYY; return NULL on anything else
-- so a dirty source row can never break a Workbench read.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_date(p_text text)
RETURNS date
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE
 WHEN p_text IS NULL OR btrim(p_text) = '' THEN NULL
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN btrim(p_text)::date
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{8}$' THEN to_date(btrim(p_text), 'YYYYMMDD')
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN to_date(btrim(p_text), 'DD/MM/YYYY')
 ELSE NULL
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_date(text) IS
 'Converts an ACE text date to date. Returns NULL rather than failing on an unrecognised value.';

-- ACE holds Y/N flags as text.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_boolean(p_text text)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE upper(btrim(coalesce(p_text, '')))
 WHEN 'Y' THEN true
 WHEN 'YES' THEN true
 WHEN 'TRUE' THEN true
 WHEN '1' THEN true
 WHEN 'N' THEN false
 WHEN 'NO' THEN false
 WHEN 'FALSE' THEN false
 WHEN '0' THEN false
 ELSE NULL
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_boolean(text) IS
 'Converts an ACE Y/N text flag to boolean. Returns NULL rather than failing.';

-- PDPA masking for display values. Keeps the last four characters.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_mask_value(p_value text)
RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE
 WHEN p_value IS NULL OR btrim(p_value) = '' THEN NULL
 WHEN position('@' in p_value) > 1
 THEN left(p_value, 1) || '***' || substring(p_value from position('@' in p_value))
 WHEN length(p_value) <= 4 THEN repeat('*', length(p_value))
 ELSE repeat('*', length(p_value) - 4) || right(p_value, 4)
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_mask_value(text) IS
 'PDPA display mask. Keeps the last four characters, or the first character and the domain of an email address.';

-- A1. Loan account. The Workbench account row, with product, branch and the ACE batch date.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_account
AS
SELECT
 a.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 a.account_code::varchar(255) AS account_code,
 a.account_name::varchar(255) AS account_name,
 a.account_status::varchar(255) AS account_status,
 a.account_status_date AS account_status_date,
 a.contract_number::varchar(255) AS contract_no,
 a.contract_date AS contract_date,
 a.product_key::varchar(255) AS product_key,
 p.product_type::varchar(255) AS product_type,
 p.product_category::varchar(255) AS product_category,
 p.product_category_efs::varchar(255) AS product_category_efs,
 a.current_branch::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 b.branch_name::varchar(255) AS branch_name,
 a.oc_code::varchar(255) AS oc_code,
 a.company_code::varchar(255) AS company_code,
 a.collection_officer::varchar(255) AS collection_officer,
 a.collection_phase::varchar(255) AS collection_phase,
 a.delay_days AS days_past_due,
 a.loan_classification::varchar(255) AS classification,
 a.total_balance AS total_balance,
 a.accounting_balance AS accounting_balance,
 a.past_due_amount AS past_due_amount,
 a.total_interest_fin_charge AS total_interest_fin_charge,
 a.collections_fee AS collections_fee,
 a.interest_rate::numeric(7,4) AS interest_rate,
 a.last_payment_date AS last_payment_date,
 a.last_payment_amount AS last_payment_amount,
 a.next_installment_date AS next_installment_date,
 a.next_installment_amount AS next_installment_amount,
 a.last_tdr_date AS last_tdr_date,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(a.is_restructured) AS tdr_flag,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(a.is_rescheduled) AS rescheduled_flag,
 a.number_reschedules AS number_reschedules,
 a.tdr_aging AS tdr_aging,
 a.principle_not_reduce::varchar(255) AS principle_not_reduce,
 a.core_banking_system_date AS data_as_of,
 a.days_since_last_contact AS days_since_last_contact,
 a.days_since_last_collection_activity AS days_since_last_collection_activity,
 a.rm_name::varchar(255) AS relationship_manager,
 a.rm_phone_number::varchar(255) AS relationship_manager_phone,
 a.special_memo::varchar(255) AS special_memo,
 a.expiry_date AS expiry_date
FROM public.account a
LEFT JOIN public.product p ON p.product_key = a.product_key
LEFT JOIN public.branch b ON b.oc_code = a.current_branch;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_account IS
 'ACE account as the Workbench reads it. delay_days maps to days_past_due; core_banking_system_date is the data_as_of.';

-- A2. Payment. pay_date is text in ACE; the view casts it and never fails on a bad value.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_payment
AS
SELECT
 p.pay_key::varchar(255) AS payment_code,
 p.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 recovery.ace_to_date(p.pay_date) AS payment_date,
 p.total_amount AS payment_amount,
 p.capital_amount::varchar(255) AS capital_amount,
 p.payinterest::varchar(255) AS interest_amount,
 p.payexpenses::varchar(255) AS expense_amount,
 p.paycommission::varchar(255) AS commission_amount,
 p.pay_type::varchar(255) AS payment_channel,
 p.description::varchar(255) AS description,
 p.comments::varchar(255) AS comments,
 a.core_banking_system_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.payment p
LEFT JOIN public.account a ON a.account_key = p.account_key;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_payment IS
 'ACE payment as the Workbench reads it. pay_date is varchar in ACE, cast to date by ace_to_date.';

-- A3. Customer. The identity number is never exposed in clear: last four only.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_customer
AS
SELECT
 c.person_key::varchar(255) AS cif_no,
 c.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 c.first_name::varchar(255) AS first_name,
 c.surname::varchar(255) AS last_name,
 c.birth_date AS date_of_birth,
 c.deceased_date AS deceased_date,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(c.is_deceased) AS deceased_flag,
 c.gender::varchar(255) AS gender,
 c.nationality::varchar(255) AS nationality,
 c.marital_status::varchar(255) AS marital_status,
 c.occupation::varchar(255) AS occupation,
 c.spouse_name::varchar(255) AS spouse_name,
 c.status::varchar(255) AS customer_status,
 c.category::varchar(255) AS category,
 c.country_of_residence::varchar(255) AS country_of_residence,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(c.is_staff) AS is_staff,
 c.branch::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 c.vat_number::varchar(255) AS vat_number,
 recovery.ace_mask_value(c.identification_number) AS id_no_masked,
 right(coalesce(c.identification_number, ''), 4) AS id_no_last4
FROM public.customer c;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_customer IS
 'ACE customer as the Workbench reads it. identification_number is masked in the view; the clear value is never exposed.';

-- A4. Contact points. Phone, email and address in one view, with a type and a display mask.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_contact
AS
SELECT
 'PHONE'::varchar(10) AS contact_type,
 ('PHONE:' || ph.phone_key)::varchar(255) AS contact_key,
 ph.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 ph.phone_number::varchar(256) AS contact_value,
 recovery.ace_mask_value(ph.phone_number) AS contact_value_masked,
 ph.contact_usage::varchar(255) AS usage_code,
 NULL::varchar(255) AS city,
 NULL::varchar(20) AS post_code,
 NULL::varchar(255) AS country
FROM public.phone ph
UNION ALL
SELECT
 'EMAIL'::varchar(10),
 ('EMAIL:' || em.email_key)::varchar(255),
 em.person_key::varchar(255),
 em.email::varchar(256),
 recovery.ace_mask_value(em.email),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 NULL::varchar(20),
 NULL::varchar(255)
FROM public.email em
UNION ALL
SELECT
 'ADDRESS'::varchar(10),
 ('ADDRESS:' || ad.address_key)::varchar(255),
 ad.person_key::varchar(255),
 ad.address::varchar(256),
 recovery.ace_mask_value(ad.address),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 ad.city::varchar(255),
 ad.zip_code::varchar(20),
 ad.country::varchar(255)
FROM public.address ad;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_contact IS
 'ACE phone, email and address as one contact-point view. contact_value is the full value notices and calls need; contact_value_masked is for display (E1-037).';

-- A5. Customer to account relations. Borrower, guarantor, co-borrower and related roles.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_ca_relation
AS
SELECT
 r.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 r.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 r.relation_type::varchar(255) AS relation_type,
 r.amount_of_guarantee AS amount_of_guarantee,
 r.date_of_guarantee AS date_of_guarantee
FROM public.ca_relation r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_ca_relation IS
 'ACE customer-account relation: who is borrower, guarantor or co-borrower on which account.';

-- A6. Account to account relations. Parent and child accounts for grouped facilities.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_aa_relation
AS
SELECT
 r.parent_account_key::varchar(255) AS parent_account_key,
 r.child_account_key::varchar(255) AS child_account_key
FROM public.aa_relation r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_aa_relation IS
 'ACE account-account relation, used to group a facility with its sub-accounts.';

-- A7. Collateral. The ACE collateral link with the asset it points at.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral
AS
SELECT
 col.asset_key::varchar(255) AS collateral_no,
 col.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 col.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 col.collateral_value AS collateral_value,
 col.register_date AS register_date,
 col.in_active AS in_active,
 ast.asset_type::varchar(255) AS collateral_type,
 ast.description::varchar(1000) AS description
FROM public.collateral col
LEFT JOIN public.asset ast ON ast.asset_key = col.asset_key;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral IS
 'ACE collateral and the asset behind it. One row per account-collateral-asset link.';

-- A8. Asset. The collateral asset record.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_asset
AS
SELECT
 ast.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_ref,
 ast.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 ast.asset_type::varchar(255) AS asset_type,
 ast.description::varchar(1000) AS description,
 ast.address::varchar(255) AS address,
 ast.town::varchar(255) AS town,
 ast.zipcode::varchar(255) AS post_code,
 ast.county::varchar(255) AS county,
 ast.country::varchar(255) AS country
FROM public.asset ast;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_asset IS
 'ACE asset as the Workbench reads it, for collateral and for a held asset.';

-- A9. Collections activity. The EFS action log ACE already ingests.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action
AS
SELECT
 e.action_id::varchar(255) AS efs_record_key,
 e.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 e.customer_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 e.action_code::varchar(255) AS action_code,
 e.action_code_name::varchar(255) AS action_code_name,
 e.action_date AS action_date,
 e.action_timestamp AS contact_at,
 e.user_code::varchar(255) AS user_code,
 e.comments::varchar(2000) AS comments,
 e.is_call AS is_call,
 e.is_rpc AS is_rpc,
 e.is_ptp AS is_ptp,
 e.promise_status::varchar(100) AS promise_status,
 e.promise_eval_status::varchar(100) AS promise_eval_status,
 e.settlement_due_date AS promise_date,
 e.settle_total_amount AS promise_amount,
 e.collection_phase::varchar(100) AS collection_phase,
 e.act_date_bucket AS act_date_bucket,
 e.act_date_past_due_days AS act_date_past_due_days,
 e.last_tdr_date AS last_tdr_date
FROM public.efs_action e;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action IS
 'ACE EFS action log. Replaces the collections_history copy; action_timestamp maps to contact_at.';

-- A10. Action code reference. The list of values behind the collections action code.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action_code
AS
SELECT
 c.action_code::varchar(255) AS action_code,
 c.description::varchar(255) AS action_name,
 c.category::varchar(100) AS category
FROM public.efs_action_code c;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action_code IS
 'ACE EFS action code reference. The loaded LIST-ACTION-CODE list (1,106 values) reads this.';

-- A11. Assignment history. Which officer or agency held the account, and when.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_assignment
AS
SELECT
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.assignment_scheme::varchar(255) AS assignment_scheme,
 s.assignee_code::varchar(255) AS assignee_code,
 s.assignee_name::varchar(255) AS assignee_name,
 s.assignment_start_date AS assignment_start_date,
 s.assignment_end_date AS assignment_end_date,
 s.assignment_start_total_balance AS assignment_start_total_balance,
 s.assignment_end_total_balance AS assignment_end_total_balance,
 s.distribution_area::varchar(255) AS distribution_area
FROM public.efs_assignment s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_assignment IS
 'ACE assignment history, used for hand-over and agency performance.';

-- A12. Monthly bucket history. The daily bucket is an ACE-new column (RWB-ACE-001).
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_bucket_log
AS
SELECT
 a.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 b.snapshot_year AS snapshot_year,
 b.snapshot_month AS snapshot_month,
 b.bucket AS bucket,
 b.past_due_amount AS past_due_amount,
 make_date(b.snapshot_year, b.snapshot_month, 1) AS snapshot_month_start
FROM public.bucket_log_snapshot b
JOIN public.account a ON a.id = b.account_id;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_bucket_log IS
 'ACE monthly bucket snapshot, keyed by account_key. bucket is the month-end bucket, not the daily bucket.';

-- A13. Product reference.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_product
AS
SELECT
 p.product_key::varchar(255) AS product_code,
 p.description::varchar(255) AS product_name,
 p.product_type::varchar(255) AS product_type,
 p.product_category::varchar(255) AS product_category,
 p.product_category_efs::varchar(255) AS product_category_efs
FROM public.product p;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_product IS
 'ACE product reference, used for the product and product group lists of values.';

-- A14. Branch reference.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_branch
AS
SELECT
 br.oc_code::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 br.branch_name::varchar(255) AS branch_name,
 br.address::varchar(255) AS address,
 br.phone::varchar(255) AS phone
FROM public.branch br;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_branch IS
 'ACE branch reference, used for the branch and region lists of values.';

-- A15. Bank of Thailand holidays. Replaces the Workbench HOLIDAY reference list.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_holiday
AS
SELECT
 h.holiday_date AS holiday_date,
 h.holiday_year AS holiday_year,
 h.holiday_description::varchar(255) AS holiday_name,
 h.holiday_description_thai::varchar(255) AS holiday_name_thai,
 h.holiday_weekday::varchar(20) AS holiday_weekday
FROM public.bot_holiday h;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_holiday IS
 'ACE Bank of Thailand holiday calendar. E1-043 and E1-045 read this instead of a Workbench list.';

-- A16. Restructure plan. The ACE case plus its TDR calculation and recommended plan.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_plan
AS
SELECT
 ac.case_business_id::varchar(255) AS plan_ref,
 ac.id AS ace_case_id,
 ac.current_station_name::varchar(255) AS plan_status,
 ac.created_timestamp AS plan_created_at,
 tc.id AS tdr_calculation_id,
 tc.published_timestamp AS plan_published_at,
 tdr.associated_account_id AS associated_account_id,
 acc.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 tdr.plan_setup_completed_timestamp AS booked_at,
 tdr.approval_completed_timestamp AS approved_at,
 tdr.submitted_for_approval_timestamp AS submitted_at,
 tdr.closed_timestamp AS closed_at,
 tdr.closed_reason::varchar(255) AS closed_reason,
 tdr.ca_approved_timestamp AS ca_approved_at,
 rec.months AS installments,
 rec.installment AS recommended_installment,
 rec.package_type::varchar(255) AS recommended_package,
 coalesce(tdr.approval_completed_timestamp, tdr.submitted_for_approval_timestamp, ac.created_timestamp)
 AS plan_status_as_of
FROM public.ace_case ac
LEFT JOIN public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case tdr ON tdr.id = ac.id
LEFT JOIN public.account acc ON acc.id = tdr.associated_account_id
LEFT JOIN public.tdr_calculation tc ON tc.case_id = tdr.id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
 SELECT r.months, r.installment, r.package_type
 FROM public.ai_recommended_plan r
 WHERE r.case_id = tdr.id
 ORDER BY r.rank
 LIMIT 1
) rec ON true;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_plan IS
 'ACE restructure case, its TDR calculation and the top-ranked recommended plan. Replaces the plan fields the Workbench used to copy.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Section B - Tier 2 views. These depend on RWB-ACE-001 and are applied only when the ACE
-- change is live. Until then the dependent Workbench features stay behind their flags.
-- Proposed migration: the next free sequence after RWB-ACE-001 is deployed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- B1. Batch completion and business date per source. The Workbench freshness stamp reads this.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status
AS
SELECT
 r.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 r.business_date AS business_date,
 r.started_at AS started_at,
 r.completed_at AS completed_at,
 r.status::varchar(12) AS status,
 r.record_count AS record_count,
 r.checksum::varchar(64) AS checksum,
 r.feed_version::varchar(20) AS feed_version,
 (r.status = 'COMPLETED') AS is_complete
FROM public.ace_batch_run r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status IS
 'Per-source ACE batch completion and business date. The Workbench freshness stamp (E1-015) reads this.';

-- B2. Valuation. SVAF appraisals, held in ACE after RWB-ACE-001.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_valuation
AS
SELECT
 v.valuation_key::varchar(255) AS valuation_key,
 v.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 v.appraisal_no::varchar(20) AS appraisal_no,
 v.appraisal_type::varchar(15) AS appraisal_type,
 v.appraised_value AS appraised_value,
 v.forced_sale_value AS forced_sale_value,
 v.appraisal_date AS appraisal_date,
 v.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 v.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.valuation v;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_valuation IS
 'SVAF appraisal as ingested into ACE. Accepted, stale and valuer fields stay in recovery.valuation_ext.';

-- B3. Collateral detail from CCMS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral_detail
AS
SELECT
 d.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 d.title_doc_no::varchar(40) AS title_doc_no,
 d.plot_no::varchar(20) AS plot_no,
 d.area_text::varchar(20) AS area_text,
 d.province::varchar(40) AS province,
 d.district::varchar(60) AS district,
 d.subdistrict::varchar(60) AS subdistrict,
 d.insured_value AS insured_value,
 d.insurance_expiry AS insurance_expiry,
 d.lien_rank AS lien_rank,
 d.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 d.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.collateral_detail d;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral_detail IS
 'CCMS collateral detail as ingested into ACE: title deed, plot, area, location, insurance and lien rank.';

-- B4. NPA asset from AMIS and RPS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_asset
AS
SELECT
 n.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_ref,
 n.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 n.asset_code::varchar(20) AS asset_code,
 n.transfer_in_type::varchar(20) AS transfer_in_type,
 n.from_segment::varchar(20) AS from_segment,
 n.transfer_in_date AS transfer_in_date,
 n.book_value AS book_value,
 n.auction_purchase_price AS auction_purchase_price,
 n.repossessed_date AS repossessed_date,
 n.stock_date AS stock_date,
 n.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 n.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.npa_asset n;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_asset IS
 'NPA asset from AMIS (property) and RPS (vehicles), as ingested into ACE.';

-- B5. NPA asset sale from AMIS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_sale
AS
SELECT
 s.npa_sale_key::varchar(255) AS npa_sale_key,
 s.npa_asset_key::varchar(255) AS npa_asset_key,
 s.contract_date AS contract_date,
 s.sale_date AS sale_date,
 s.sale_price AS sale_price,
 s.transfer_fee AS transfer_fee,
 s.specific_business_tax AS specific_business_tax,
 s.corporate_income_tax AS corporate_income_tax,
 s.incentive_amount AS incentive_amount,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.npa_sale s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_sale IS
 'NPA sale contract and its taxes and fees, from AMIS, as ingested into ACE.';

-- B6. Lawsuit from LIT.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_lawsuit
AS
SELECT
 l.lawsuit_key::varchar(255) AS lawsuit_key,
 l.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 l.lawsuit_no::varchar(30) AS lawsuit_no,
 l.black_case_no::varchar(30) AS black_case_no,
 l.red_case_no::varchar(30) AS red_case_no,
 l.court_name::varchar(120) AS court_name,
 l.claim_amount AS claim_amount,
 l.filed_date AS filed_date,
 l.judgment_date AS judgment_date,
 l.judgment_amount AS judgment_amount,
 l.lit_status::varchar(200) AS lit_status,
 l.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 l.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.lawsuit l;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_lawsuit IS
 'LIT lawsuit as ingested into ACE: case numbers, court, claim, judgment and status.';

-- B7. Hearing from LIT.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_hearing
AS
SELECT
 h.hearing_key::varchar(255) AS hearing_key,
 h.lawsuit_key::varchar(255) AS lawsuit_key,
 h.hearing_date AS hearing_date,
 h.hearing_type::varchar(20) AS hearing_type,
 h.next_date AS next_date,
 h.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 h.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.hearing h;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_hearing IS
 'LIT court hearing as ingested into ACE.';

-- B8. Proof of delivery from WIN.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_pod
AS
SELECT
 w.pod_key::varchar(255) AS pod_key,
 w.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 w.notice_ref::varchar(60) AS notice_ref,
 w.sent_date AS sent_date,
 w.barcode::varchar(40) AS barcode,
 w.callback_date AS callback_date,
 w.delivery_status::varchar(15) AS delivery_status,
 w.sent_type::varchar(10) AS sent_type,
 w.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 w.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.pod_receipt w;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_pod IS
 'WIN proof of delivery as ingested into ACE. The notice itself stays in recovery.notice.';

-- B9. Write-off from GL.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_write_off
AS
SELECT
 g.write_off_key::varchar(255) AS write_off_key,
 g.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 g.amount AS amount,
 g.posted_date AS posted_date,
 g.responsibility_center::varchar(10) AS responsibility_center,
 g.cost_center::varchar(10) AS cost_center,
 g.gl_product::varchar(10) AS gl_product,
 g.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 g.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.gl_write_off g;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_write_off IS
 'GL write-off posting as ingested into ACE. The write-off decision stays in recovery.write_off.';

-- B10. COLLINS score.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_score
AS
SELECT
 s.score_key::varchar(255) AS score_key,
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.model_code::varchar(30) AS model_code,
 s.model_version::varchar(20) AS model_version,
 s.score_value AS score_value,
 s.estimate_value AS estimate_value,
 s.route_code::varchar(4) AS route_code,
 s.scored_at AS scored_at,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.collins_score s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_score IS
 'COLLINS score and route estimate as ingested into ACE, if ACE does not already hold it.';

-- B11. Party product from SCBPDM.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_party_product
AS
SELECT
 pp.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 pp.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_no,
 pp.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 pp.product_type::varchar(20) AS product_type,
 pp.product_status::varchar(15) AS product_status,
 pp.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.party_product pp;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_party_product IS
 'SCBPDM customer product holding as ingested into ACE. Replaces the Workbench party_product copy.';

-- B12. NLEADS credit decision.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_credit_decision
AS
SELECT
 d.credit_decision_key::varchar(255) AS credit_decision_key,
 d.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 d.nleads_ref::varchar(30) AS nleads_ref,
 d.credit_result::varchar(10) AS credit_result,
 d.credit_result_reason::varchar(1000) AS credit_result_reason,
 d.decided_at AS decided_at,
 d.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 d.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.credit_decision d;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_credit_decision IS
 'NLEADS credit approval as ingested into ACE. Replaces the four credit fields the Workbench used to record by hand.';

-- B13. EasyApp signature request.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_esign
AS
SELECT
 s.esign_key::varchar(255) AS esign_key,
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.external_ref::varchar(60) AS external_ref,
 s.requested_at AS requested_at,
 s.status::varchar(20) AS status,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.esign_request s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_esign IS
 'EasyApp signature request as ingested into ACE. The Workbench document still owns the signed file.';

-- B14. Entra ID group to role mapping.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_iam_group
AS
SELECT
 g.entra_group::varchar(120) AS entra_group,
 g.role_code::varchar(20) AS role_code,
 g.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 g.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.iam_group g;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_iam_group IS
 'Entra ID group to Workbench role mapping as ingested into ACE. ACE performs the sign-in, so it owns the mapping.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Grants. The recovery service identity may read the views and nothing else.
-- Replace :recovery_role and :ace_view_owner with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- CREATE ROLE :ace_view_owner NOLOGIN;
-- CREATE ROLE :recovery_role NOLOGIN;
-- GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO :ace_view_owner;
-- GRANT SELECT ON public.account, public.payment, public.customer, public.phone, public.email,
-- public.address, public.ca_relation, public.aa_relation, public.collateral, public.asset,
-- public.efs_action, public.efs_action_code, public.efs_assignment, public.bucket_log_snapshot,
-- public.product, public.branch, public.bot_holiday, public.ace_case,
-- public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, public.tdr_calculation, public.ai_recommended_plan
-- TO :ace_view_owner;
-- ALTER VIEW recovery.v_ace_account OWNER TO :ace_view_owner; -- and every other v_ace_* view
-- GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO :recovery_role;
-- GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery TO :recovery_role;
-- REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC;
-- No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on any table, and no SELECT on a public table
-- is granted to :recovery_role.

-- Conformance test (added to RWB-E1-069 AC4 as a repeatable check):
-- 1. Every view in recovery whose name starts with v_ace_ compiles.
-- 2. No constraint in schema recovery references a table outside schema recovery.
-- 3. select * from recovery.v_ace_account where days_past_due > 90 returns rows in SIT.
-- 4. The recovery role cannot select a public table directly, and cannot insert, update or delete
-- on any public or recovery table.

How reference data changes
Every change to a Workbench reference list or table is a validated load with a version. None needs a code release. Lists read from ACE are not loaded.
Step | Stage | What happens
1 | Request | The owner of the list or table raises the change with the reason and the date it should take effect
2 | Prepare | The reference data administrator prepares the new version as a load file, with a test case for each changed row
3 | Validate | The load runs against the schema and the completeness checks in SIT. A load with an exception is refused whole
4 | Approve | The owner approves. Risk also approves where a limit or a threshold moves
5 | Load | The new version loads into production with its valid from date. No code release
6 | In force | New decisions use the new version from its date. Open cases keep the version they were decided under
7 | Roll back | A breach returns the previous version through the same load
8 | ACE-sourced lists | A list read from ACE through a v_ace_* view is not loaded and not versioned in the Workbench. A change to its values comes from the ACE batch; the Workbench reads the new values on the next request.

Key
What each term means.
Item | Term | Meaning
Kind | Closed list | A fixed set of codes held in the Workbench
Kind | Source list | Values that come from ACE through a view or from a versioned Workbench table, not a fixed list held in this workbook
Column | Code | The value stored in the field
Column | Valid from | The date the value comes into force
Standard | Bank TSD section T3.2 | Closed lists of values
Value | Read from ACE | Values come from a recovery.v_ace_* view on every request. The Workbench does not load or store them
Term | Source view | The recovery.v_ace_* view that supplies or confirms a list of values
Value | Closed list with a source view | A closed list held in the Workbench whose codes mirror an ACE list. The view confirms the codes on each release; the values do not change on the read
