fact_case_daily | One row per open case per day | case, date, product, stage, route, owner, team, queue | open flag, days in state, breached flag, balance | recovery_case, timer, v_ace_account | Read through v_ace_account; nightly
fact_decision | One row per decision log entry | case, date, decision, rule, approver, agent | count, override flag, fallback flag, amount | decision_log_entry | Nightly from the Workbench
fact_treatment | One row per treatment | case, date, product, treatment type, status | offer amount, approved amount, booked amount, days to book | treatment, v_ace_plan | Read through v_ace_plan; nightly
fact_legal | One row per legal action | case, date, firm, court, status | days to file, days to judgment, court fees | legal_action, v_ace_lawsuit, v_ace_hearing | Read through v_ace_lawsuit and v_ace_hearing; nightly
fact_asset | One row per asset per month | asset, month, type, region, status | book value, holding cost, list price, sale price, days held | v_ace_asset, v_ace_npa_asset, listing, asset_sale | Read through v_ace_asset and v_ace_npa_asset; nightly
fact_lot | One row per lot | lot, buyer, date | balance, reserve, price, put-backs | debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account | Nightly from the Workbench
fact_recovery | One row per receipt | case, date, route, product, source | amount, principal resolved | proceeds, write_off, v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off | Read through v_ace_payment and v_ace_write_off; nightly
fact_partner | One row per instruction | partner, case, date, type | days to complete, breached flag, fee | partner_instruction | Nightly from the Workbench
fact_flow | One row per bucket per month | month, product, bucket | opening balance, forward flow balance, flow rate | v_ace_bucket_log | Read through v_ace_bucket_log; monthly

Dimensions
Shared by every fact table.
Table | Holds
dim_date | Calendar with bank holidays and business days
dim_product | Mortgage, hire purchase, SSME and the product codes
dim_route | Routes from LOV-ROUTE
dim_stage | Stages from LOV-STAGE
dim_org | Team, region, queue and owner, with history
dim_partner | Partner firm and type
dim_rule | Rule and version
dim_decision | D1 to D9 and sub-decisions

Measure definitions
Each management measure, its formula and the fact table it reads.
Measure | Formula | From
Recovery rate | Sum of amount / sum of principal resolved | fact_recovery
Turnaround to book | Median days to book | fact_treatment
Litigation turnaround | Median days to file | fact_legal
NPA sales cycle | Median days held at sale | fact_asset
Cases inside the service level | Open cases not breached / open cases | fact_case_daily
Recommendations accepted | Decisions without override / decisions with a recommendation | fact_decision
Agent fallback rate | Fallbacks / agent steps | fact_decision
Flow rate by bucket | Forward flow balance / opening balance | fact_flow
Loss on NPL sale | 1 - price / balance sold | fact_lot
Partner service level met | Instructions not breached / instructions | fact_partner

Rule | Detail
No load-time transform | The Workbench does not transform source data at load. There is no load. A rename or a type cast happens in the recovery.v_ace_* view.
Name mapping | The view field is named for the Workbench. The ACE column name appears only in the view definition and the ACE mapping tab of the LDM.
Type casts | payment.pay_date is varchar in ACE and becomes date through recovery.ace_to_date, which returns NULL rather than failing. account.is_restructured and customer.is_deceased are Y/N text and become boolean through recovery.ace_to_boolean.
Masking | customer.identification_number is never exposed in clear. v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked and id_no_last4. Phone, email and address are exposed in full because notices need them; display masking is E1-037 at the API.
Business date | The business date is read from recovery.v_ace_batch_status, one row per source and business date, written by ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001). No row carries a Workbench load date.
Codes | Source codes map to Workbench lists in the view or in the list load, not in a load-time map table. LOV-ACTION-CODE reads v_ace_efs_action_code.
Amounts | Amounts are numeric(18,2) in baht. ACE numeric(38,2) columns are cast in the view where the Workbench column is narrower.
New fields | A field ACE does not hold is raised once in RWB-ACE-001 and then read from its view. It never becomes a Workbench column.
Links | A Workbench link to a source record is a business key (varchar 255) with no foreign key. The 14 re-keyed links are listed in the Tier Map.
Status | Ready means the field is in an ACE table today. Waiting on RWB-ACE-001 means the field is in the ACE story and the dependent feature stays behind its flag.

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Accessibility standard

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench accessibility standard
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | WCAG 2.2 level AA
Every Workbench and partner portal screen meets WCAG 2.2 level AA. The design system components meet it by construction; each screen is checked before release.

Area | Rule | WCAG
Contrast | Text 4.5 to 1 against its background; large text and controls 3 to 1. The design tokens meet this | 1.4.3, 1.4.11
Color | Status shown by text and badge, never by color alone | 1.4.1
Keyboard | Every action reachable and usable by keyboard, in a logical order, with no trap | 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3
Focus | A visible 2 px focus ring on every control; focus never hidden behind sticky headers | 2.4.7, 2.4.11
Target size | Click targets at least 24 by 24 px | 2.5.8
Labels | Every field has a visible label tied to it; required fields marked in text | 1.3.1, 3.3.2
Errors | Errors named in text next to the field and summarized at the top; focus moves to the summary | 3.3.1, 3.3.3
Headings | One screen title; panels use headings in order | 1.3.1, 2.4.6
Tables | Header cells marked; sortable columns announce their state | 1.3.1
Dialogs | Focus moves into the dialog and returns on close; Escape closes | 2.4.3
Timing | Session timeout warns two minutes before and lets the user extend | 2.2.1
Zoom | Usable at 200 percent zoom and at 320 px width without loss | 1.4.4, 1.4.10
Language | Page language set; Thai text marked lang=th | 3.1.1, 3.1.2
Status messages | Toasts and banners announced to screen readers | 4.1.3
Dragging | No action needs dragging | 2.5.7
Help | Help in the same place on every screen | 3.2.6
Authentication | Sign-in through Entra ID with no cognitive test | 3.3.8

Check | When | Who
Automated scan of every screen | Every pull request that changes a screen | Pipeline (RWB-TE-010)
Keyboard walk-through | Before SIT exit | QA engineer
Screen reader check of the main screens | Before the first release of each screen | QA engineer
Zoom and narrow width | Before SIT exit | QA engineer

A screen with an open level A or AA failure does not pass the definition of done.

How labels are written
Applies to every screen and message.
Rule | Detail
Case | Sentence case for every label, heading and button
Buttons | A verb for what happens: Approve, Transfer, Record result
Field labels | The business term from the glossary, with the unit in brackets: Offer amount (THB)
Help text | One sentence that says what to enter or why; no repetition of the label
Dates | d MMM yyyy in English; d MMM yyyy in the Buddhist Era in Thai
Numbers | Thousands separators; amounts in THB with no decimals unless the field is a rate
Thai length | Layouts allow Thai labels to run 30 percent longer than English
Terms | Use the glossary term; never the synonyms the glossary lists as not to use
Messages | From the error and message standard; never written on a screen by hand

Glossary terms for labels
The business glossary terms the labels use.
Term | Thai | Meaning | Field | Do not use
Recovery case | กรณีติดตามหนี้ | One case per customer per product, from 90 days past due to close, with its accounts linked | recovery_case | Ticket, file, job
Case number | เลขที่กรณี | The identifier issued when a case is created, in the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN, never reused | recovery_case.case_no | Case ID in other systems
Case owner | ผู้รับผิดชอบกรณี | The person who holds the case from day 90 to close and answers for its outcome | recovery_case.owner_user_id; role RW-CASEOWN | Collector, handler
Case status | สถานะกรณี | One of New, Assigned, In progress, Waiting customer, Waiting partner, Waiting approval, On hold, Closed | recovery_case.status; LOV-CASE-STATUS | Stage, step

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Error and Message Standard v3.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Error and Message Standard v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Error and message standard

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench error and message standard
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Thai text | Proposed. The business lead drafts per module one epic ahead; Legal and Compliance approve (DL10)

Every message says what happened and what to do next, in that order, in the fewest words that are clear. A message names the thing on the screen and never the code behind it.

Type | When it is used | Pattern | Example
Error | The action did not happen | What is wrong. What to do. | Enter the reason for the transfer.
Warning | The action can happen, but something needs attention | What is at risk. By when. | The claim on this case expires on 4 March 2027. File before then.
Confirmation | The action happened | What happened. What follows. | Approved. The case moves to Offer with customer.
Information | A state the user should know | The state, and the date or owner it depends on | This case is on hold for a complaint.

Write to the user as you. Write the system as the case, the record or the Workbench, never as I or we.

Use the names in the business glossary. A field is called what the screen calls it.

No codes, stack traces, table names or rule IDs on screen. The message ID and the rule ID go to the log.

No blame and no apology. State the fact.

Put a date, an amount or a name in the message when the user needs it to act.

One message per problem. Field errors show next to the field; a summary at the top lists them when there is more than one.

English and Thai carry the same meaning and the same placeholders. The Thai text uses กรุณา for a request and no ending particle.

Dates show as 4 March 2027 in English and 4 มีนาคม 2570 in Thai. Amounts show in baht with thousands separators.

Item | Rule
ID | MSG, the module code and a number, for example MSG-P3-011. GEN for messages every module uses
Where it is held | In the message table as reference data, with the English and Thai text and a version. A wording change is a data load, not a code release
Placeholders | Names in braces, for example {date}. Each placeholder is filled from the record, formatted for the language
Rule link | Each message names the rule or validation that raises it, so a test can check both
Language | The user's language setting picks the text. Customer-facing letters and messages follow the customer's language
Approval | Legal and Compliance approve customer-facing wording. The product owner approves screen wording

163 messages that the platform and stage modules and the Epic 1 and Epic 2 stories use. A new story adds its messages to this table in the same form.

States every screen handles
The wording comes from the error and message standard.
State | How it shows
Loading | Skeleton rows while data arrives; no spinner over the whole page
Empty | A plain sentence saying there is nothing to show, and the action to take if one applies
Read only | Fields shown without edit controls; the reason is shown when the role cannot change them
On hold | A banner with the deviation or legal hold and the prescription date
Stale input | A warning with the age of the data (MSG-P7-006, MSG-P1-001)
Error | The message from the error and message standard next to the field or at the top

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

Each agent runs through the orchestrator and the tool gateway, at the autonomy level the strategy and model committee approves. If it does not answer in 60 seconds or fails a guardrail, the rule result is used.

| Does | Classifies inbound documents and checks extracted fields against the case |

| Output | Document type, fields with confidence |
| May decide alone | Document type and fields above the confidence floor |
| Escalates | Below the confidence floor, outside the band, or a guardrail failure: to the owner's queue with reasons |

An event reaches the case: a load, a screen action, a partner result or a timer.

The rules component finds the step and reads its autonomy level from the reference data.

The agent runtime module calls the orchestrator with only the fields the step needs.

The agent calls tools through the tool gateway. The gateway checks each call against the agent's allowed actions.

The guardrail checker tests the output against its schema, the allowed actions and the confidence floor.

At L1 the output is shown to the person as a recommendation with reasons. At L2 and above the agent acts inside its band.

The decision log writer records the inputs, the versions, the output, the decision and the approver. A failed write stops the action.

If the agent does not answer in 60 seconds, or a guardrail fails, the rule result is used and the fallback is recorded.

Guardrail | What it does
Tool gateway | The only way an agent reaches data or acts. The gateway holds the permissions; the agent holds no credential
Allowed actions | Each agent has a list of the actions it may propose or take at its autonomy level
Schema check | Every output is checked against its schema before it is used
Confidence floor | An output below the floor goes to a person; the rule result is used meanwhile
Fallback | If the agent does not answer within 60 seconds, the rule result is used and the fallback is recorded
No personal data in prompts beyond need | Each agent receives only the fields its step needs; the PDPA lint checks prompts
Versioned prompts and policies | Each run records the prompt, policy, model and agent versions, so it can be reproduced
Decision log | Every agent proposal and action is written to the decision log on the same terms as a person's

Step | What the agent does | Measured before the next step
Shadow | The agent runs beside the rule; its output is logged and not shown | Agreement with the rule and with people's decisions on a labeled set
L1 recommend | The output is shown as a recommendation; a person decides every case | Acceptance rate, override reasons, outcome against the rule
L2 act in a band | The agent acts inside a narrow band; a person reviews a sample and the exceptions | Sample error rate, exception rate, outcome measures
L3 act across the decision | The agent acts across the decision; people review by exception | Outcome measures by route and product; complaints
L4 act and close | The agent acts and closes; people monitor the measures | Outcome measures; model risk review

Level | What the agent does | What a person does
L0 | Nothing. The rule decides | Everything
L1 | Recommends, with its reasons | Decides. Every decision starts here after a shadow run
L2 | Acts inside a narrow band | Reviews a sample and the exceptions
L3 | Acts across the decision | Reviews by exception
L4 | Acts and closes | Monitors the measures

Who | Accountable for
Strategy and model committee | Approves each autonomy step on the measured results, and agent changes
Model Risk | Validates models and agents before use and at each step-up, under the bank model risk standard
Center of excellence | Owns prompts, policies and evaluation sets; proposes changes
Enterprise AI team | Runs the agent platform, the model endpoint and the evaluation harness
Risk and model risk officer | Monitors acceptance, overrides, fallbacks and drift each month
Internal audit | Reads the decision log for agent decisions

Measure | Meaning | Reviewed
Acceptance rate | Recommendations approved without override | Monthly
Override reasons | Coded reasons when a person departs from the recommendation | Monthly
Fallback rate | Steps where the rule result was used because the agent did not answer or a guardrail failed | Weekly
Latency | Time from call to answer at the 95th percentile | Weekly
Cost | Model cost per decision | Monthly
Outcome | Recovery, turnaround and loss for agent-advised decisions against rule-only decisions | Quarterly

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL33 | The model endpoint the agents call and where it is hosted | A private endpoint in the SCB tenant
DL11 | Agent response target | 60 seconds, then the rule result is used
DL26 | Which personal fields each agent may receive | Only the fields the step needs; masked otherwise

secs.h: Recovery Workbench: AI assisted development approach
secs.t: SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026. Version 1.

The Recovery Workbench is built with AI in two parts. In both, a person owns the result.

| Part | What AI does | What a person owns |
|---|---|---|
| AI assisted delivery | Drafts stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, test cases, UAT scripts, Thai message drafts, release notes and status packs | The analysts, QA and the product owner correct, decide and sign each one |
| AI assisted engineering | Proposes the plan for a story, writes the tests and the code, reviews pull requests first | Developers conduct the agent and read every line. Tech leads approve plans. Reviewers approve merges |

Seven working rules apply to both parts.

1. The person who merges a change owns it, whoever or whatever wrote it.
2. The agent works from files: the standards file, the story file and the plan file. Anything the agent needs is in one of the three.
3. The tests and the acceptance criteria exist before the code is generated.
4. Every line that reaches production is read by a person.
5. An AI error found by a reviewer is written into the standards file, so the agent is told not to repeat it.
6. No personal data or production data goes into a prompt, a test or a log.
7. The unit of work is one story. Work is merged at least once a working day.

| Step | What happens | Who | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Story file | AI drafts the story file from the requirement, the routing rules and the data model. The analyst corrects it and owns it | Analyst | Definition of ready |
| 2 Plan | The agent reads the story file and the standards file and writes the plan file. The tech lead approves it before any code is written | Developer with the agent; tech lead | Plan approved |
| 3 Tests | The agent writes failing tests from the acceptance criteria. The developer checks that each test asserts its criterion | Developer with the agent | Every criterion has a test |
| 4 Build | The agent writes the code in DEV with synthetic data, in small commits | Developer with the agent | Tests pass |
| 5 AI review | The review agent checks the pull request and writes a summary on it | Review agent | Summary on the pull request |
| 6 Human review and merge | The reviewer works through the review checklist and approves. The author merges behind a feature flag if the work is not finished | Reviewer; author | Nine pipeline checks pass |
| 7 Test | QA runs SIT. Business testers test during the build and in the UAT week. AI drafts the UAT scripts from the acceptance criteria | QA; business testers | SIT exit; UAT exit |
| 8 Learn | AI errors found in steps 5 to 7 go into the standards file. The weekly measures in section 10 are published | Tech lead | Standards file updated |

The standards file is `AGENTS.md` in the root of the ACE repository, with a section for the recovery module. The agent reads it before every task. The solution architect owns it with the tech leads, and it changes by pull request like code.

- The Workbench is the recovery module of the ACE service: one service, one repository, one front end.
- Back end: Spring Boot (Java), Spring JPA, Spring Batch, Spring Security with method security, Quartz. Front end: React on Vite with Radix and TanStack Query. Database: PostgreSQL.
- Domain driven design, RESTful API, front end types generated from the back end.
- Cases are modeled in CMMN 1.1 terms: case, stage, milestone, task, sentry, event listener, case file item.

1. Put recovery code in the recovery module folder only. Change the common or collection module only where the story file names it.
2. Read every threshold, limit, timer, queue, role, template and route from its versioned reference table. Never write one as a literal in code.
3. Put a Spring Security method check on every endpoint, naming the capability area and the operation.
4. Write a decision record entry for every change to a case and every decision, with the rule ID and version used.
5. Use the names in the business glossary for classes, fields, tables and endpoints.
6. Return each validation message from the message table by its rule ID.
7. Make database changes by migration script only, one script per story.
8. Use Spring Batch and Quartz for scheduled work.
9. Use the synthetic data generator for test data.
10. Write the test before the code. A change with no test is not complete.

1. Commit a credential, key or token.
2. Call or read the inside of another module.
3. Call a system of record directly. Data arrives through COLLINS and leaves through the integration adapters.
4. Add a workflow engine, a rules engine or any new dependency.
5. Disable, skip or weaken a test.
6. Change a migration script that is already merged.
7. Put personal data in code, test fixtures, prompts or log lines.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench AI Decision Governance v2.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench AI Decision Governance v2

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

AI decision governance

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench aI decision governance
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | arc42 crosscutting concepts

A model or agent decides alone only at the autonomy level the strategy and model committee has approved for that step.

Every automated or advised decision is recorded with its inputs, versions, reasons and outcome.

Every decision can be explained to the customer, the business, audit and the regulator.

Any decision can be challenged and reversed by a person with the authority for it.

If the AI does not answer or fails a guardrail, the rule result is used.

What is recorded | Where
Inputs used, by reference with their business date | Decision log
Rule, model, agent and prompt versions | Decision log
Recommendation and reasons | Decision log
Autonomy level of the step | Decision log
Who decided, or that the agent decided within its band | Decision log
Override and its coded reason | Decision log

Audience | What they receive | How
Case owner | The recommendation with its top reasons and the expected return by route | Decision screen
Customer | The outcome and the main reasons in plain words, on request or where a letter requires it | Letter or contact center
Audit and regulator | The full entry with versions and inputs | Decision log query and export

Review | Who | How often
Sample of agent-decided cases at L2 and above | Conduct and QA officer | Monthly
Acceptance, overrides and fallbacks | Risk and model risk officer | Monthly
Outcomes against rule-only decisions | Center of excellence | Quarterly
Autonomy step-ups | Strategy and model committee | On request with results

A customer complaint about a decision raises X1 and pauses the stage clock.

The complaint officer reviews the decision log entry.

If the decision is wrong, a person with the authority records a correcting decision that names the original (R-UNI-24).

If the cause is the agent or the rule, the center of excellence raises a change; Risk may lower the autonomy level at once.

Lowering an autonomy level is a reference data change that takes effect immediately.

Level | What the agent does | What a person does
L0 | Nothing. The rule decides | Everything
L1 | Recommends, with its reasons | Decides. Every decision starts here after a shadow run
L2 | Acts inside a narrow band | Reviews a sample and the exceptions
L3 | Acts across the decision | Reviews by exception
L4 | Acts and closes | Monitors the measures

secs.h: 3. Changing a model without a release
secs.t:
Model Risk validates the new version under the bank standard.

COLLINS publishes the new version's output with its version in the load.

The model version in force for each decision step is reference data; the center of excellence loads the change and Risk approves it.

Decisions from the valid from date use the new version; earlier decisions keep theirs.

Champion and challenger runs are set by the same table, with a share of cases per version.

Reached only through the agent platform's tool gateway; no Workbench code calls it directly.

A private endpoint in the SCB tenant (DL33).

Prompts carry only the fields the step needs; no clear identifiers.

Prompt, policy and model versions are recorded on each run.

docs.name: Recovery Workbench Defect Management Process v2

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Defect management process

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench defect management process
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Henka word rules

Severity | Meaning | Example | Fix by
1 Critical | A decision is wrong, data is lost or exposed, or the service is down | Approval accepted above the limit; personal data shown unmasked | Same day; release blocked
2 High | A main path does not work and there is no workaround | Allocation does not run | Before the release
3 Medium | A path fails with a workaround | Filter returns extra rows | Agreed date
4 Low | Cosmetic or wording | Label misaligned | Backlog

Raise: anyone raises the defect on the board with steps, expected and actual result, environment and story key.

Grade: the QA engineer sets severity; the product owner confirms severity 1 and 2.

Assign: the tech lead of the owning module assigns it the same day.

Fix: the developer fixes it with a test that fails before and passes after.

Retest: the QA engineer retests in the environment where it was found.

Close: closed when the retest passes; reopened if it returns.

No personal data in a defect record or screenshot.

A defect found in UAT is also added to the regression suite.

A severity 1 or 2 defect open at the go decision stops the release unless its flag is off.

Rule defects are fixed by a new rule version, not by code.

Measure | Meaning
Defects found in UAT | Defects per release found after SIT
Age of open defects | Days open by severity
Reopen rate | Share of fixed defects reopened

secs.h: 4. When a story fails a definition
secs.t:
Case | What happens
Not ready when it is due to be pulled | The story stays in refinement. The next ready story in priority order is pulled instead
A decision blocks it | The story is built on the recommended answer in the decision log and the assumption is stated in the story
Not done at the epic cut | The story moves to the next epic with its flag off. It is not split to claim part of it as done
Fails SIT or UAT | Its flag is switched off and the release goes ahead without it. A defect story is raised
A defect traced to AI-written code | It is tagged, and the standards file is updated before the fix merges

Restore | Restore the database and documents to a point in time | Within the ACE recovery objectives (DL11) | Before E1
Security | Container and dependency scans; access tests per role; penetration test | No finding above the bank threshold | Each release; penetration before the partner portal opens
Accessibility | Automated scan and keyboard checks | No level A or AA failure | Each screen
SIT at production sizing where the ACE team provides it; masked data scaled to the target volume. Results are recorded against the release.

Test | Who
Load, stress, volume, batch | QA engineers with the ACE team
Resilience and restore | SCB IT with the ACE team
Security | SCB IT security
Accessibility | QA engineers
Recovery point and time objectives come from SCB IT under DL11.

How the suite grows
Each release adds its cases; a defect found in UAT adds a case.
Release | Adds
E1 | Epic 1 story main paths and access tests; every rule row loaded in Epic 1; view conformance, ACE batch freshness, the boundary rule and the ACE read grant
E2 | Adds queues, approvals, notices, deviations screening
E3 | Adds settlement, deed in lieu, asset record and listing
E4 | Adds the route decision, guarantees, auctions, RAMC, self-service
E5 | Adds litigation end to end and the data room
E6 | Adds debt sale, write-off and the partner panel
E7 | Adds deviations end to end and partner scoring
E8 | Adds full administration and the autonomy step-ups

Rules for the suite
Applies to every release.
Rule | Detail
Run | Automated in SIT on every release tag; the rule harness on every commit
Pass | Every case passes before the SIT exit
Add | A UAT or production defect adds a case before it is closed
Remove | A case is removed only with its feature, with the product owner's approval

Test cases from the stories
1284 live cases from the Epic 1 and Epic 2 stories, the enabler stories, the ACE team story and the administration stories, each traced to a story and an acceptance criterion, with its Given, When and expected result taken from that criterion; 98 cases from the nine stories removed by D-RCV-35 are kept in place, marked Parked with their later home, and excluded from the regression suite.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
docs.name: Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Test data plan

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench test data plan
Version | 3
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119
Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43

Every environment below SIT is seeded from the ACE schema and the recovery schema. No environment holds a copy of a source table or a load table, because neither exists under D-RCV-35 (U1). SIT and UAT read source data through the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; the Workbench schema holds no copy of a source row.

Environment | Data | Source | Personal data
DEV | Synthetic ACE-shaped rows and synthetic Workbench rows, rebuilt from the DDL and the data dictionary | RWB-E1-065 SandboxGenerator, seed 20261128 | None
SIT | Masked copy of the ACE tables, ingested by ACE from the SIT sources, plus scripted cases | ACE ingestion; PII service (RWB-TE-004) | Masked
UAT | Masked ACE copy plus scripted cases | PII service; testers | Masked
Performance | Masked ACE copy scaled to the 2027 volume | PII service with scaling | Masked

The sandbox is the only test data set below SIT. RWB-E1-065 builds it from the same DDL as SIT: ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql for the 22 Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables, then V0001 for the 92 recovery tables and the four extension tables, V0002 for the 16 Section A views and V0003 for the 14 Section B views. It seeds rows by reading sys_objects, sys_fields and lov_value, so a schema change reaches the sandbox with no generator edit.

Object group | What is seeded
Tier 1 ACE tables (22) | One or more rows in account, payment, customer, phone, email, address, ca_relation, aa_relation, collateral, asset, efs_action, efs_action_code, efs_assignment, bucket_log_snapshot, product, branch, bot_holiday, iam_user, ace_case, cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, tdr_calculation and ai_recommended_plan. 184,500 account rows carry the ALS business shape; 28,140 of them sit at 90 days past due or more, with accounts at 89 and at 90.
Tier 2 ACE tables (14) | ace_batch_run holds one row per source and business date, with COMPLETED, FAILED and LATE rows; valuation, collateral_detail, npa_asset, npa_sale, lawsuit, hearing, pod_receipt, gl_write_off, collins_score, party_product, credit_decision, esign_request and iam_group each hold rows for every Workbench read. The 12 new columns on account, customer and efs_action are filled. Behind DL43: until the DDL lands, the Section B views and their features stay behind their flags.
Recovery tables (92) | 2,812 cases with seed 20261128: 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME, plus 10 cases for each exception shape; their accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments, interactions and documents are linked by business key.
Extension tables (4) | party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext, 49 columns in all, one row per ACE business key where a Workbench decision exists.
Views (30) | The 16 Section A and 14 Section B recovery.v_ace_* views; each returns at least one row; each has one sys_objects row and one sys_fields row per column.
Removed tables (20) | None. loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, party_product, valuation, score, asset, load_run, dq_exception, dq_rule, source_field_map, source_code_map, interface_run, interface_signoff, tracker_inventory and tracker_row do not exist in schema recovery and are neither seeded nor read.

There is no copy table and no load table in the sandbox. A test that needs a source value reads it through its view; the expected value comes from the ACE-shaped row, not from a Workbench copy.

Test | Data
Allocation | Cases for every product group, region and exposure band; owners at and below the capacity limit and one owner above it.
Routing rules | One case per rule row in its from state, with its condition true and false.
Case list | v_ace_account at 89 and at 90 days past due; 21 entry exclusions; 37 case accounts below the threshold; v_ace_batch_status with COMPLETED and missing rows.
Reconciliation | Variances at zero, below and above recon.tolerance.pct; a person_key with no v_ace_customer row; a payment in v_ace_payment with no proceeds.
Freshness | One ace_batch_run row per source and business date, with COMPLETED, FAILED, LATE and duplicate rows; a weekly source between its batches.
Views and dictionary | One row per view; a view column with no sys_fields row; a recovery constraint that points at public; a role with no grant.
Approvals | Decisions at each level and amount boundary of the delegation table.
Deviations | Cases with each of X1 to X7.
Documents | The labeled sample of 180 documents across the six types.
Batch and job runs | JOB-02, JOB-03 and JOB-04 held by the daily gate, failed at a step and rerun; no inbound file and no file arrival.
Partners | A firm of each partner type with instructions in every status.

Masking follows RWB-E1-037. The rules, the masking version and the masking position are data; Compliance sets them and approves each version.

No production data in DEV. The sandbox is synthetic and is rebuilt from the seed and the DDL.

The ACE-shaped tables hold clear values where ACE holds them, because ACE is the system of record; the sandbox verifier allows a clear identity number only there.

recovery.v_ace_customer exposes id_no_masked (DF-ACE-073) and id_no_last4 (DF-ACE-074) only. The clear identification number never leaves ACE, and there is no token and no token store.

recovery.v_ace_contact exposes contact_value and contact_value_masked (DF-ACE-078, DF-ACE-079). Phone, email and address are clear in the view because notices and calls need them; display masking is applied at the API.

Masking is applied by role under RWB-E1-037 with masking version MASK-SIT-01; a personal field with no masking rule is masked.

No clear personal value is written to schema recovery. The sandbox verifier fails the build and names the table and column when one appears.

Masked data never leaves SIT and UAT. Defect records and screenshots carry no personal data.

The PDPA lint (RWB-TE-011) checks fixtures, code and logs in the pipeline. Test data is refreshed before each release and destroyed when the environment is rebuilt.

Item | Owner
Synthetic seed and fixtures | QA engineers with the recovery squad
ACE-shaped seed and batch rows | Data engineering with the ACE team
Masked copies | Data engineering
Document sample | Autonomous Ops team
Approval of masking rules and masked copies | Compliance
View, dictionary and grant fixtures | Recovery squad

Item | Count
Tier 1 ACE tables | 22
Tier 2 ACE tables | 14
Recovery tables | 92
Extension tables | 4
recovery.v_ace_* views | 30 (16 Section A, 14 Section B)
Dictionary objects | 122
Dictionary fields | 1,366 (304 on the views, 49 on the extension tables)
Removed tables | 0 seeded, 0 read; 20 do not exist
Cases in the sandbox | 2,812 plus 10 for each exception shape

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Test strategy

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench test strategy
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119

Level | What it covers | Who | Where | When | Exit
Unit | Every service method and rule evaluation | Developer | DEV and the pipeline | Every commit | 80 percent line coverage on new code
Rule table | Each rule row against its test case | Developer with the analyst | Pipeline | Every commit and every rule version | Every row passes
Integration | Modules with a real PostgreSQL database | Developer | Pipeline | Every pull request | All pass
API contract | Requests and responses against the OpenAPI file | Developer | Pipeline | Every pull request | All pass
System | Stories end to end against the SCB test systems | QA engineer | SIT | Rolling, then the SIT week | Every test case for the release passes; no open severity 1 or 2
Regression | The regression suite | QA engineer | SIT | Each release | All pass
Non-functional | Performance, resilience, security | QA with SCB IT | SIT | Before each release | Targets in the NFR specification
Accessibility | Automated scan and keyboard checks | QA engineer | SIT | Each screen | No level A or AA failure
User acceptance | Business scripts | Business testers | UAT | UAT week | Scripts signed by the business lead

Environment | Data | Use
DEV | Synthetic only | Developer and rule tests
SIT | Masked copies from the PII service | System, regression, non-functional
UAT | Masked copies | Business acceptance

Gate | Entry | Exit
SIT | Release tag built; stories done in DEV; test data loaded | Every test case passes; no open severity 1 or 2; severity 3 with an agreed fix date
UAT | SIT exit met; scripts walked through with the testers | Scripts signed by the business lead; open defects accepted or behind a flag
Release | SIT and UAT exits | Go decision by the release owner
Synthetic in DEV; masked copies in SIT and UAT; no production data below production. The test data plan sets the data each test needs.

Who | Tests
Developers | Unit, rule table, integration, contract
QA engineers | System, regression, accessibility, non-functional with SCB IT
Business testers | During the build with the squads; UAT scripts
SCB IT security | Penetration test before the partner portal opens
Role owners | Access tests per role
Every test case names its story and acceptance criterion or its rule ID. The requirements traceability matrix links requirement, feature, story, specification section and test.
Defects follow the defect management process: severity, owner, fix and retest. A release goes with no open severity 1 or 2 defect.

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Personal data protection design

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench personal data protection design
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Thai Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562

Category | Examples | Classification
Direct identifier | Name, tokenized national ID, date of birth, contact points, interaction summaries, extracted document fields | Restricted
Sensitive | Vulnerable, deceased and bankruptcy flags | Restricted
Indirect identifier | Account, contract, case, lawsuit and title deed numbers | Confidential
Customer data | Balances, arrears, treatments, legal actions, assets | Confidential
Staff identifier | Users who act on cases; partner users | Internal

The field-level inventory is the data classification and personal data inventory workbook.

Processing | Basis, proposed | Section
Recovering the debt under the loan contract | Contract | 24(3)
Statutory notices, regulatory reporting, court filings | Legal obligation | 24(6)
Sensitive flags: death, bankruptcy, vulnerability | Establishment, exercise or defense of legal claims; explicit consent where it applies | 26(4)
Contact on optional channels such as LINE | Consent | 19
Fraud prevention and monitoring | Legitimate interest | 24(5)
Staff and partner user data | Employment and contract; legitimate interest | 24

Compliance confirms the bases (DL26).

Consent state is held per contact point and channel (contact_point.consent_status).

Withdrawal removes the channel from the contact plan at once; statutory notices continue (R-UNI-10).

Consent comes from the bank's consent records through COLLINS; the Workbench does not collect new consent.

National ID and passport numbers are tokenized at load; the clear value is not stored.

Each role has a masking profile; fields are masked unless the role may see them.

Each screen and each agent receives only the fields it needs.

Debt sale tapes carry only the fields the sale terms allow and pass a masking check.

Access by role, capability area and scope; out of scope records are not returned.

Every read of a personal field is logged through PII Kafka.

Access is reviewed every six months by the role owners.
Retention is set per data product and document type in the records retention and archiving schedule. A legal hold overrides retention. Expired data is disposed of by a recorded decision.

Right | Path | Time
Access | Request through the bank's PDPA process; Compliance retrieves the case data | Within 30 days
Correction | Corrected in the system of record; the next load updates the Workbench | Within 30 days
Erasure or restriction | Assessed against the legal claims exemption; automated processing held while assessed (R-UNI-11) | Within 30 days
Objection | Assessed by Compliance | Within 30 days

Recipient | What | Safeguard
Law firms, agencies, valuers, auction vendors | The data the instruction needs | Contract with data protection terms; firm scope in the partner portal
Debt buyers and AMCs | Masked data tape before award; full data after transfer | Non-disclosure agreement; masking check
Courts and the Legal Execution Department | Filings | Legal obligation
Cross-border | None planned; data stays in the SCB Azure tenant, Southeast Asia | Bank position to confirm
A suspected breach is an incident to SCB security operations. Compliance assesses it and notifies the regulator within 72 hours where the Act requires, and the people affected where the risk is high.

Decision | What is needed | Answer used until decided
DL26 | Retention and masking | Proposed classes and profiles
DL33 | Model endpoint location | Inside the SCB tenant; no cross-border transfer

Records retention and archiving

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench records retention and archiving
Version | 1
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Thai PDPA, bank records policy

Periods are proposed until Compliance issues the bank retention schedule for recovery records (DL26). Each period is a reference data value and changes by load.

Record | Data product | Retention | Archive | Reason
Case record and case history | DP03 | 10 years after the case closes | Archive after 2 years closed | Legal claims and audit
Account, payments and money | DP01, DP13 | 10 years after the case closes | Archive after 2 years closed | Accounting and tax records
Customer and party | DP02 | 10 years after the last case closes | Archive after 2 years closed | Legal claims
Treatments and offers | DP04 | 10 years after the treatment ends | Archive after 2 years | Contract evidence
Contact and interaction ledger | DP05 | 5 years after the case closes | Archive after 1 year closed | Conduct review
Collateral and assets | DP06 | 10 years after disposal | Archive after 2 years | Legal claims
Legal actions and notices | DP07 | 10 years after the legal action ends | Archive after 2 years | Legal claims
Partner performance | DP08 | 5 years | Archive after 1 year | Contract management
Debt sale | DP09 | 10 years after transfer | Archive after 2 years | Legal claims
Legal documents | DP10 | 10 years after the case closes; write-once | Archive after 2 years closed | Legal claims
Other documents | DP10 | 5 years after the case closes | Archive after 1 year closed | Operations
Scores | DP11 | 2 years | Delete | Model monitoring
Decision log | DP12 | 10 years after the case closes | Copy kept in the data lake | Audit and regulatory
Reference data versions | DP14 | 10 years after superseded | Archive | Audit: which rule applied
Access log | None | Per the bank security standard | Archive | Security and audit
Application logs | None | 90 days | Archive for 1 year | Operations

Stage | Where | Access
Active | ACE database and document storage | By role and scope
Archived | Archive tier of storage; database partitions detached to the archive | Compliance and internal audit on request
Destroyed | Removed from every store and backup cycle | None; the disposal decision is kept

The retention job lists records past their period each month.

Records under a legal hold or with an open case, claim or dispute are excluded.

Compliance reviews the list and approves disposal or an extension; the decision is recorded.

Approved records are destroyed and a disposal certificate is kept with counts by type.

Legal counsel places a hold on a case, a party or a document with a reference.

A hold stops archiving and destruction for as long as it is in place.

Lifting a hold is recorded; retention resumes from the original dates.

docs.name: Recovery Workbench Benefit Tracking Plan v2

secs.t:
Benefits and how each is tracked
8 benefits with baseline, target, source, who publishes and how often. Baselines are agreed with the owners before the first release that moves them.
ID | Benefit | Baseline | 2027 target | Source of the number | Published by | How often | First moved by
BEN-01 | Recovery rate on NPL | 66.3% (2026 to date) | 73% | Monthly recovery report; decision log from Epic 3 | Finance publishes; Chief Debt Recovery Management Office owns | Monthly | E3
BEN-02 | Litigation turnaround | 21 days | 6 days | Decision log: route approved to filed | Reporting and BI analyst | Monthly | E5
BEN-03 | Deed in lieu turnaround | 26 days | 12 days | Decision log: route approved to title transferred | Reporting and BI analyst | Monthly | E3
BEN-04 | Restructure turnaround | 23 days | 5 days | Decision log: route approved to booked | Reporting and BI analyst | Monthly | E3
BEN-05 | Debt sale turnaround | No baseline | 45 days | Decision log: lot approved to transfer | Reporting and BI analyst | Per lot | E6
BEN-06 | Manual processes removed | Near zero | 80% of the selected list | Process architecture: L3 processes automated | Business lead | Quarterly | E2
BEN-07 | Audit findings and fraud cases | 50 | 13 | Audit and fraud records | Internal audit | Quarterly | E2
BEN-08 | NPA sales cycle | 1,486 days | 1,095 days | Asset records: take-on to sale | Head of NPA | Quarterly | E3

How benefits are tracked
Applies to every benefit.
Step | Detail
1 | The owner agrees the baseline and its source before the release that moves the benefit
2 | The number is read from the decision log or the source named, never counted by hand
3 | Published on the steering dashboard at the frequency shown
4 | Reviewed four weeks after each release at the benefit check gate (G6)
5 | A benefit off track goes to the sponsor review with its cause

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Cutover and go-live plan

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench cutover and go-live plan
Version | 2
Date | 15 November 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Structure | Henka word rules

Each monthly release goes live in the change window agreed with SCB IT (DL34). The first release, 30 November 2026, also starts the case list. The Workbench runs no load: ACE ingests every source and the release reads the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views (D-RCV-35, ADR-010). The release is ready when the ACE batch is ready, so the checks in section 6 are release gates.

When | Step | Who
Friday before | Go decision on the SIT and UAT exits; flags for unfinished work confirmed off | Release owner with the product owner and application owner
Release day minus 1 | Reference data, rules and templates for the release loaded with their valid from date | Reference data administrator
Release day | Deploy the tag to production in the change window | ACE team
Release day | Smoke test: sign-in per role, case list, one decision, one notice | QA engineers with business testers
Next morning | ACE batch for the business date checked in v_ace_batch_status, then the case list reconciled to the ACE account view | Data steward
First week | Floor support for the teams that receive real users | Business analysts, business lead
Four weeks after | Benefit check (G6) | Product owner
Each release is rehearsed in UAT: the deploy, the reference data load, the smoke test and the rollback. The first release is rehearsed twice.

Switch the feature flags for the release off.

If a flag does not cover the fault, redeploy the previous tag.

Reload the previous reference data versions if they changed.

Decisions taken under the new release stay in the decision log; corrections are new entries.

No ACE data is rolled back with the Workbench: the views read the ACE batch for the business date, and a wrong batch is corrected in ACE.
The release owner in the ACE team decides with the product owner and the application owner. A severity 1 or 2 defect open without a flag stops the release.

The check runs on the release day before the smoke test, and again on the first morning after the release. A failed check holds the part of the release that reads ACE; the Workbench features that read no ACE data go ahead behind their flags.

Check | Passes when | Who confirms
ACE additions | RWB-ACE-001 is applied in PROD and the 14 tables and 12 columns are present | ACE team lead
Batch complete | ace_batch_run holds a COMPLETED row for each recovery source and the business date, and v_ace_batch_status returns it | ACE ingestion owner
Grant in place | The view-owner role selects the 21 listed ACE tables and no other; the recovery role reads recovery.v_ace_* only and writes no ACE table | ACE DBA with SCB IT security
Views resolve | 16 Section A and 14 Section B views compile, and the conformance test resolves the 80 appendix fields | Data steward
Case list runs | JOB-02 starts on AceDataReady for the ALS business date and creates no case from an incomplete batch | QA lead with the data steward
Fallback agreed | If a check fails, the case list holds, the data screens stay behind their flags, and the ACE team names the recovery date | Release owner with the product owner

Item | Plan
Case list | Built from the ACE account view on the first COMPLETED ALS batch for the business date; reconciled to v_ace_account before it is shown
ACE views | 16 Section A views live on the day; the 14 Section B views and the 12 new ACE columns need RWB-ACE-001 (DL43, due 21 November)
Spreadsheets | Retired team by team under the procedure in section 8; each team keeps a read-only archive
Access | Administration roles only; business roles from Epic 2 (DL39)
Documents | Store and OCR live; bulk intake of open-case documents starts

The 20 Excel and SharePoint trackers, 14 marked LOAD and 6 marked RETIRE in the inventory, are retired in this release, team by team. Six teams own them: TDR, DIL, LIT, NPA, DEBT_SALE and WRITE_OFF. None is loaded into the Workbench. RWB-E1-005, RWB-E1-010 and RWB-E1-012 are removed under D-RCV-35, so the Workbench provides no inventory, no load and no retirement screen: the procedure below is run by the teams and recorded in one report.

Step | What happens | Who
1 | The team manager works from the case list for two working days after the last tracker file of the team is signed off | Team manager
2 | The team manager makes each tracker read-only or moves it to the read-only archive, and records the archive location | Team manager
3 | The team manager confirms the retirement of each tracker, with the archive location and the date | Team manager
4 | The data steward records the fields of each tracker that no data product carries, for the later epic that picks them up | Data steward
5 | The Tribe lead reads the six-team report: trackers, retired, outstanding and the confirming manager for each team | Tribe lead
6 | The report is filed with the release checklist on 26 November 2026; a team with an outstanding tracker is named with its tracker codes | Tribe lead with the business lead

Decision | What is needed
DL12 | Which legacy systems are kept
DL34 | The release window
DL43 | Whether the ACE team accepts RWB-ACE-001 and its 21 November date

Engineering practices

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench engineering practices
Version | 3
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Applies to | The two TechX recovery squads, the collection squad and the ACE team, working in one ACE service

Practice | Position | Status
Where code lives | One ACE service, one repository, one front end. Recovery code is in the recovery module. | Agreed
Structure | Modular monolith: common, collection and recovery modules by folder, with boundaries checked at build time. | Agreed
Workflow | Programmatic, in CMMN 1.1 terms. Conditions and actions are versioned data rows. No Temporal. | Agreed
Branching | Trunk based. Short-lived branches merged into main at least once a working day. | Agreed
Merge owner | Each squad merges into its own module through code owners. The ACE team owns the common module and the release decision. | Assumed, DL04
Code review | AI first-pass review, then one named human reviewer. A change in another module's folder needs that module's code owner. | Proposed
Tests | No untested code is merged. Tests are written from the acceptance criteria before the code. | Agreed
Feature flags | Every unfinished or cross-squad change is behind a flag. A flag that is off returns the previous code path. | Agreed
Pipeline gates | Nine checks before merge, deploy to DEV on merge, SIT on tag, UAT and production by the monthly release. | Proposed, Sprint 0
Release | One production release a month, shared with the collection squad: one week of SIT, one week of UAT, business testing during the build. | Agreed; dates DL34

Agreed: agreed by SCB IT, the ACE team, TechX and Henka. Proposed: the practice the squads use from 2 November unless the ACE team or SCB IT changes it. Assumed: the position used until the bank decides, with the decision log entry that holds the question.

The Recovery Workbench is built inside the ACE service. There is one service, one repository and one front end. The service is split into modules by folder.

Module | Built by | Holds
Common | ACE team | The case view shared by both modules, sign-in and access checks, audit and PII logging, the shared entities (customer, account, product, collateral, asset) and shared tasks such as the TDR calculator
Collection | Collection squad | Phone, field, FCR and TDR work, as split under DL14
Recovery | The two TechX recovery squads | Recovery case stages, tasks and screens; litigation, debt sale, NPA and write-off; the document hub; the decision record; the recovery data products

A recovery component that the collection module also needs moves to the common module by agreement with the ACE team. Until the ACE team has moved ACE to the modular monolith, TechX builds in its own package (DL05).

A module calls another module only through that module's published interface or through an application event. It never calls the inside of another module.

Each module owns its tables. Another module reads them only through the owning module's interface.

A module boundary test runs in the build and fails it on any violation.

Front end types are generated from the back end by code. They are not written by hand or by an AI tool.

Names follow the business glossary, so one concept has one name in the model, the code and the conversation.

Layer | Technology, as ACE runs it today
Back end | Spring Boot (Java) with Spring JPA, Spring Batch, Spring Security with method security and OAuth, Spring Session, Spring Cloud Azure, Spring Data REST, Spring HATEOAS and Quartz
Front end | React on Vite with Radix and TanStack Query
Database | PostgreSQL
Data in | COLLINS on Databricks by ETL batch: UDP, SCBPDM, core bank batch, EFS and AAL. No real time feed today
Identity and logs | Entra ID, the bank IAM, PII Kafka, audit log and SOC log
Design patterns | Domain driven design, RESTful API, end-to-end type safety and validation
Hosting | ACE namespace on the shared ACE AKS clusters

A recovery case is modeled in CMMN 1.1 terms: case, stage, milestone, task, sentry, event listener and case file item. The collection module uses the same terms.

The case, its stages and its tasks are held in the database and moved by code. No workflow engine is used.

The condition a sentry tests and the action it takes are rows in a versioned table. Code holds the behavior; data holds the choices. A change to a threshold, a timer or a route is a data load, not a code release.

The recovery module owns its case data and its specific actions. The common case view shows the case, its stages, tasks and history, and passes common actions such as view, assign and start stage to the recovery module.

Timers and scheduled work run on Quartz and Spring Batch. A long wait, such as a court date, is a stored due date that the scheduler checks.

Temporal is not used. Adding it later for a self-contained automation task is a separate architecture decision with its own decision record.

Main is the only long-lived branch. It can be released at any time.

Each change starts on a short branch from main. The branch name starts with the Jira story key.

A branch is merged into main at least once a working day. Work that is not finished is merged behind a feature flag.

The author brings main into the branch before opening a pull request.

No fork and merge, and no long-lived feature or squad branches.

A production fix is made on a branch from the release tag and merged back into main the same day.

Rule | Detail
Size | One story, or one part of a story that can be tested on its own
Description | The story key, the acceptance criteria covered and the AI first-pass review summary
Checks | Every pipeline check in section 7 passes before a person reviews
Approval | One named reviewer from the owning squad. A change in another module's folder also needs that module's code owner
Who merges | The author merges after approval, into their own module. A change in the common module is merged by the ACE team
Code owners | A code owners file maps each module folder to its owners: recovery to the TechX tech leads, collection to the collection squad, common to the ACE team
Conflicts | A conflict between squads is settled by the two tech leads the same day. The ACE team decides if they do not agree

Merge owner between the recovery and collection squads: the position above is assumed until the decision is taken (DL04).

Every line that reaches production is read by a person. An AI review runs first and a human reviewer decides.

The reviewer checks | Fails when
Acceptance criteria | A criterion in the story has no test or no code that meets it
Tests | New behavior has no test, or a test checks nothing
Principle 1 | A threshold, limit, timer, queue, role, template or route is written in code instead of read from a versioned table
Personal data | Personal data appears in code, test data, fixtures or log lines
Access | An endpoint has no permission check, or the check is made in the front end only
Module boundaries | Code reads another module's tables or calls inside another module
Names | A class, field or endpoint uses a name that is not in the business glossary
Logging | A decision or a change to a case is not written to the decision record

A review is completed the same working day it is requested.

An error the AI tool makes that a reviewer finds is added to the repository standards file (AGENTS.md), so the tool is told not to repeat it.

Only the coding tool approved by the CTO and SCB IT is used on SCB code (DL32). No personal data or production data goes into a prompt.

Level | What it covers | Written by | Runs
Unit | Every service method and every rule evaluation | Developer | Every commit
Rule table | Each rule row against its test case ID: the event, the condition and the expected action | Developer with the analyst | Every commit
Integration | A module with a real PostgreSQL database | Developer | Every pull request
API contract | Requests and responses against the generated types | Developer | Every pull request
Module boundary | No call or table read across a module boundary | ACE team, once | Every pull request
Browser | The main path and the exception paths of each screen | QA | Every merge, once the browser test runner is in the pipeline
SIT | The release against the SCB test systems | QA with SCB IT | One week before each release
UAT | The release against the business scripts | Business testers | During the build and in the week before each release

The test and the acceptance criteria are written before the code is generated.

Code with no test is not merged into main, with or without a feature flag.

A failing test blocks the merge. A test that fails at random is fixed or removed the same day by its author.

DEV uses synthetic data only. UAT uses masked data from the PII service. No production data reaches DEV.

Gate | Checks | Blocks
1 Build and unit tests | The service builds and every unit and rule table test passes | Merge
2 Lint | Code style and the naming rules | Merge
3 Secret scan | No credential, key or token in the code | Merge
4 PDPA lint | No personal data in code, tests or log statements | Merge
5 Container scan | No known vulnerability above the bank threshold in the image | Merge
6 Module boundary | No call or table read across a module boundary | Merge
7 Integration and contract tests | Modules work with the database and the generated types | Merge
8 AI first-pass review | Bugs, security, PDPA and style, with a summary on the pull request | Merge
9 Human approval | One named reviewer, and the code owner where another module is touched | Merge

Step | When | Approved by
Deploy to DEV | On every merge into main | Pipeline
Deploy to SIT | On a release tag | Tech lead
Deploy to UAT | After SIT exit, in the week before the release | QA lead with SCB IT
Deploy to production | In the monthly change window | Release owner with the application owner
Rollback | Switch the feature flag off first; redeploy the previous tag if a flag does not cover the fault | Release owner
Penetration test | Before the first production release of the recovery module, and when the security design changes | SCB IT security

ACE has four deployment slots planned in DEV and two in SIT, so squads can test in parallel. One slot in each is available today; the rest are being provisioned (DL35).

A feature flag chooses between two code paths. When the flag is off, the service runs the previous code path, the same result as reverting the change. When it is on, the new path runs. A flag does not switch a feature off for users while leaving broken code running.

Rule | Detail
When a flag is required | Any change merged before it is finished; any change another squad depends on; any change in the common module that alters behavior
What a flag records | Name, owner, story key, value in each environment, and the release in which it is removed
Where a flag is held | As configuration for each environment. Changing a value needs no code release
Testing | Both paths keep their tests while the flag exists
At release | A change that fails SIT or UAT has its flag switched off and the release goes ahead without it
Removal | The old path and the flag are removed in the release after the flag is switched on in production

One production release a month, at the end of each epic, shared by the recovery and collection squads. The window is agreed with SCB IT (DL34).

Development is continuous. Business testers work with the squads during the build (DL09), so UAT confirms work the business has already seen.

SIT takes one week and UAT takes one week before each release.

The release owner in the ACE team makes the go decision on the SIT and UAT exit, with the product owner and the application owner.

A squad that is not ready does not hold the release. Its flags stay off.

Practice | Owner | Follows it

Branching and merging into the recovery module | TechX tech leads | TechX recovery squads
Merging into the common module and the release decision | ACE team (assumed, DL04) | All squads

Decision log | Needed | Owner | By | Position used until answered

DL05 | Whether the bank or TechX creates the Workbench module | K. Pipat | 29 Oct | TechX builds in its own package from 2 November; the ACE team applies the boundaries

How to use it

Take the next item in order whose dependencies are done. Work in progress per squad stays within the board limit. An item on the critical path is taken before any other item. An item that will miss its release stays behind its flag and moves to the next release. The two squads agree the split at the daily board; the product owner settles a disagreement the same day.

The critical path starts outside the squads. RWB-ACE-001, the ACE team's 14 tables, 12 columns and read grant, is due on 21 November under DL43 and gates RWB-E1-069, the 30 read-only views. RWB-E1-069 gates RWB-E1-018 and RWB-E1-002, the case record and the case list. From RWB-E1-020 the chain runs RWB-E1-028, RWB-E1-030, RWB-E1-059, RWB-E1-061 and RWB-E1-063, then RWB-E2-031, RWB-E2-028 and RWB-E2-029: 13 items end to end. docs.name: Recovery Workbench Ways of Working and Governance v3

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench

Ways of working and governance

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 28 October 2026

Item | Detail
Document | Recovery Workbench ways of working and governance
Version | 2
Date | 28 October 2026
Prepared by | Henka Group
Applies to | The TechX recovery squads, Autonomous Ops, Enterprise AI, the ACE team for shared items, the product owner, the business lead and the sponsors

No more than three planning or review meetings a week for a squad member, and none longer than 30 minutes

The sponsor review and the steering committee look back at finished work and are outside that limit

Work flows on a Kanban board with limits on work in progress per column and a written pull policy

The monthly release is the only date the business sees. What slips moves to the next epic; the date does not move

Planning happens daily at the board. There is no sprint commitment and no velocity target

When | Meeting | Length | Who attends | What it covers
Daily | Board review | 15 minutes, each morning | Each squad: tech lead, developers, analyst, QA | Blockers and the oldest item on the board. What is pulled next
Daily | Help needed | As raised, the same day | Product owner with the person blocked | Who removes each blocker and by when. A blocker needing the bank goes to its owner the same day
Weekly | Delivery review | 30 minutes | Product owner, tech leads, analysts, QA lead, ACE team | The four flow numbers, what broke between modules, changes to the definitions of ready and done
Weekly | Decision review | 30 minutes | Product owner with the owners of open decisions | Each open decision against its date. Overdue decisions go to the sponsor review or the steering committee
Weekly | Design review for the next epic | 30 minutes | Analysts, solution architect, business lead | Progress of the next epic's design, one epic ahead of the build
Weekly | Progress update | Written | Product owner to the business unit heads | Finished work, the next release, open decisions and risks
Two-weekly | Sponsor progress review | 45 minutes | Sponsors, product owner, business lead | A look back at finished work. No commitment is made
Monthly | Epic design sign-off | 45 minutes | Business lead, product owner, Risk where limits move | The next epic's design is signed before its build starts
Monthly | Release go decision | 30 minutes | Release owner in the ACE team, product owner, application owner | Go or no-go on the SIT and UAT exits. Flags stay off for work that is not ready
Monthly | Epic demo | 60 minutes | Squads, business users, sponsors | The released work, shown on the system
Monthly | Steering committee | 60 minutes | Sponsors, CTO delegate, product owner, Henka | Decisions above the project: scope, budget, overdue decisions, risks

Forum | What it decides | Chair
Squad board review | What is pulled next, who helps whom | Tech lead
Delivery review | Changes to the board, the limits and the definitions of ready and done | Product owner
Decision review | Whether an overdue decision goes to the sponsor review or the steering committee | Product owner
Epic design sign-off | The next epic's design and scope | Business lead
Release go decision | Whether the release goes, and which flags stay off | Release owner, ACE team
Sponsor progress review | Priorities between the next epics' scope items | Sponsor
Steering committee | Scope, budget, decisions the project cannot take, risks | Sponsor

Step | What happens
1 Raise | Anyone raises a question the build cannot answer. The product owner adds it to the decision log with an ID
2 Frame | The analyst writes the question, the options, a recommendation, what it blocks and what happens if it is late
3 Assign | The product owner names one owner and a date needed. Decision owners are bank roles
4 Build on the recommendation | The squads build on the recommended answer and mark it as an assumption in the story
5 Decide | The owner decides within five working days of the date needed, or the decision goes to the next review
6 Record | The decision moves to Decisions taken with the date, who took it and what it means for the build
7 Apply | Documents and stories built on the assumption are updated. An architecture decision also gets a decision record

The decision log holds every open decision with its question, options, recommendation, owner, date needed and what it blocks, and every decision taken. Its days-left column counts down to the date needed and shows an overdue decision in red.

Role | What they own
Product owner | Owns the backlog order, the decision log and the weekly reviews
Business lead | Owns the business design, UAT and the epic design sign-off
Solution architect | Owns the architecture, the decision records and the standards file with the tech leads
Tech leads | Own their module, its merges and its board
QA lead | Owns the definition of done, the test levels and the SIT exit
Release owner, ACE team | Owns the release decision for the shared ACE service
Application owner | Signs access reviews and accepts each release (DL02)
Decision owners | Answer the open decisions named to them by the date needed

Issue | Goes to | Answered within
Within a squad | Tech lead | Same day
Between squads or with the ACE team | Tech leads together; the ACE team decides if they do not agree | Same day
Needs a bank answer | Decision owner, through the decision log | Five working days
Overdue decision or cross-unit issue | Sponsor progress review | Next review
Scope, budget or a decision above the project | Steering committee | Next meeting

Measure | Definition
Cycle time | Working days from pulled to done, per story
Throughput | Stories done per week
Blocked time | Working days a story waits on something outside the squad
Work in progress | Stories in progress against the limit per column
Decisions overdue | Open decisions past their date
Defects found in UAT | Defects per release found after SIT

If cycle time rises while throughput falls, the limits on work in progress are wrong and are changed at the next delivery review. Velocity is not used as a measure.

Column | A story enters when | Leaves when
Ready | It meets the definition of ready | A developer pulls it
Plan | A developer pulls it | The tech lead approves the plan
Build | The plan is approved | The pull request is opened with its tests
Review | The pull request is opened | The pipeline passes and the reviewer approves
Done | It meets the definition of done | The epic is released

Each column carries a limit on work in progress set at the delivery review. A story that waits on something outside the squad is marked blocked, and its blocked time is counted.

secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

Every asset in the document set at its current version, who reads it and the file that holds it. Functional and technical specifications are one file per module, in the two specification archives. The ACE DB alignment section carries the controlling change for the 15 November 2026 re-base, recorded as D-RCV-35.

Read by: Sponsors, product owner, decision owners.

| # | Document | What it is | Standard | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Admin and access model | Whether access is granted centrally or by the application owner, who the application owner is, and the authority levels. | NIST RBAC | Recovery Workbench Admin and Access Model v5.docx |
| 2 | Decision log | Every open decision with the question, the options, the owner, the date needed and what it blocks. | Henka excel rules | Recovery Workbench Decision Log v9.xlsx |
| 131 | Specification rulings, RWB-E1-001 | The four source conflicts found in RWB-E1-001 and the ruling on each, re-based on Physical Schema v5 and D-RCV-35: the counts and the systems of record move to ACE, the rulings are unchanged. | Henka word rules | Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Specification Rulings v2.md |
| 132 | Pre-build rulings, RWB-E1-001 | The same four conflicts ruled as a best-answer set before anything is built, with the paste-ready seed, view SQL and edit schedule held in the specification rulings. | Henka word rules | Recovery Workbench RWB-E1-001 Pre-Build Rulings v2.md |

Read by: Program manager, sponsors, SCB IT.

| # | Document | What it is | Standard | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 40 | Release plan | The eight epics across eight months, what each release contains, and the gates between them. | Henka slide rules | Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4.pptx, Recovery Workbench Release Plan v4.xlsx |

COLLECTIONS AND RECOVERY TRANSFORMATION
Recovery Workbench
Executive presentation for the CEO. Henka Group, 28 October 2026
(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

2
One case, one owner, one record
Every account from 90 days past due to close is held once, with its owner, its clocks and its history
Decisions prepared, people decide
Rules and agents gather the facts and recommend; people approve within their authority
Evidence by design
Every decision is recorded with its reasons and approver; audit reads the log
Benefit | Today | 2027 target
Recovery rate on NPL | 66.3% (2026 to date) | 73%
Litigation turnaround | 21 days | 6 days
Deed in lieu turnaround | 26 days | 12 days
Restructure turnaround | 23 days | 5 days
Debt sale turnaround | No baseline | 45 days

3
Measure | Value | Note
Accounts at 90 days past due, active inventory | 28,119 | 30 June 2026
New accounts reaching 90 days past due a month | 3,110 | Average of the last 12 months
% recovery of NPL, January to June 2026 | 64.0% | Against a 2026 target of 68%
Flow rate, bucket 3, June 2026 | 29.0% | Against a target of 24.4%
Audit findings and fraud cases | 50 | Approval and authority the largest group

4

secs.h: 4. How a case moves from day 90 to close
secs.t:
A case passes through six stages. It can return to the route decision at any stage, on a cure, a payment, a deviation or an override.

Stage | What it produces
Receive the case | One owner, the history from collections, running deadlines and a deviation screen
Choose the route | An approved route with the expected return of each option and the reasons
Resolve with the customer | A settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor agreement, booked and reconciled
Enforce | A judgment enforced, a settlement before judgment, or proceeds matched to the case
Realize the asset | Cash from the asset or the debt: auction, RAMC, buy-back, rental or debt sale
Close | The balance written off and posted, recovery after charge-off, the case closed

A deviation such as a complaint, a death, fraud or lost contact pauses the stage at any point and returns the case when it clears.

Every decision follows five steps: gather and check the information, decide by a rule, a model or an agent, make the outcome final or send it to the approver, act in the systems, and log the decision once. The approver is set by the bank approval authority regulation and the delegation of authority table.

Who carries out the step, from day 90 to close | L3 processes | Share
Automated | 38 | 52%
AI prepares, a person decides | 17 | 23%
A person decides | 7 | 10%
Partner | 9 | 12%
Manual | 2 | 3%
Total | 73 | 100%

Element | What it means
ACE | The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end. It reuses ACE sign-in, access control, audit and logging.
COLLINS | Account, customer, collections history, litigation status and scores arrive by daily batch through COLLINS.
Case model | Stages, milestones, tasks and timers in CMMN 1.1 terms, the standard shared with the collection module.
