secs.h: Slide 2. What the Recovery Workbench is
secs.t:
2
The Recovery Workbench is the system that owns every recovery case from 90 days past due to close, for Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME. It is built as the recovery module of ACE, the bank's collection engine, so collection and recovery work in one application with one case view.
From day 90 to close
One case per customer and product, with one owner, one clock and one history
Mortgage, Hire Purchase, SSME
Every route: restructure, settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale and write-off
Built on ACE
One service, one repository and one front end, with data through COLLINS

3
Work is spread across systems
Collections and recovery staff use 42 applications. A case's facts are held in the core bank, EFS, LIT, CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and the document stores, and no screen shows them together.
Cases are run from spreadsheets
Teams keep their own case lists in Excel and SharePoint, build account plans by hand and approve by email. Hand-overs between teams are manual.
Decisions are not recorded in one place
Why a route was chosen, who approved it and on what figures is spread across emails and files. Audit findings and fraud cases number 50.
Cases take too long
Turnaround is 21 days for litigation, 23 days for a restructure and 26 days for a deed in lieu. The NPA sales cycle is 1,486 days.

4
Area | Today | With the Workbench
Case list | Each team's Excel and SharePoint list | One case list for every account at 90 days past due or more, reconciled to the core bank
Ownership | Agreed between teams by email | One owner per case by rule, with transfers recorded and a clock on every state
Choosing the route | Officer judgment, written up in an account plan | Expected return of each route from COLLINS, a recommendation with reasons, approved within the delegation of authority
Approvals | Email and paper | Routed to the right approval level, with the limit checked and the decision logged
Documents | Folders, shared drives and couriers | One document hub per case, with types read and fields extracted, and custody of originals tracked
Partners | Email and spreadsheets | Instructions, results and fees through a partner portal, with a scorecard per partner
Rules and limits | In procedures and people's heads | Versioned data rows, changed by a validated load without a code release
Evidence | Rebuilt for each audit | One decision log entry per decision, append only

secs.h: Slide 5. How a case moves from day 90 to close
secs.t:
5
Receive the case
Choose the route
Resolve with the customer
Enforce
Realize the asset
Close
Stage | What it produces
Receive the case | One owner, the history from collections, running deadlines and a deviation screen
Choose the route | An approved route with the expected return of each option and the reasons
Resolve with the customer | A settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim or guarantor agreement, booked and reconciled
Enforce | A judgment enforced, a settlement before judgment, or proceeds matched to the case
Realize the asset | Cash from the asset or the debt: auction, RAMC, buy-back, rental or debt sale
Close | The balance written off and posted, recovery after charge-off, the case closed
A deviation such as a complaint, a death, fraud or lost contact pauses the stage at any point and returns the case when it clears.

6
Information
Gather and check the facts
Decide
A rule, a model or an agent
Outcome
Final, or sent to the approver
Act
Carry it out in the systems
Log
Record it once
Who carries out the step, from day 90 to close | L3 processes | Share
Automated | 38 | 52%
AI prepares, a person decides | 17 | 23%
A person decides | 7 | 10%
Partner | 9 | 12%
Manual | 2 | 3%
Total | 73 | 100%

The Recovery Workbench is the system that owns every recovery case from 90 days past due to close, for Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME. It is built as the recovery module of ACE, the bank's collection engine, so collection and recovery work in one application with one case view.
From day 90 to close
One case per customer and product, with one owner, one clock and one history
Mortgage, Hire Purchase, SSME
Every route: restructure, settlement, deed in lieu, guarantee claim, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale and write-off
Built on ACE
One service, one repository and one front end, with data through COLLINS

secs.h: Slide 3. Where the work happens in ACE
secs.t:
3
Module | Built by | What it holds
Common | ACE team | Sign-in and access checks, audit and PII logging, the shared case view, shared entities (customer, account, product, collateral, asset), shared tasks such as the restructure calculator, the notification path
Collection | Collection squad | Phone, field, FCR and restructure work, as split under DL14
Recovery | TechX recovery squads | Recovery stages, tasks and screens, the rules component, the decision center and log, the document hub, the partner portal, the recovery data loads
One service, one repository, one front end. Each squad merges into its own module folder; the ACE team owns the common module and the release decision.

4
Epic | Release | Theme | What the business gets
E1 | 30 Nov 2026 | Foundation 1 | One case list for every account at 90 days past due or more, reconciled to the core bank. Documents found by case. Decision log store. Read-only case record view
E2 | 31 Dec 2026 | Foundation 2 | One owner and a timer on every case, full history on one screen, approval routing, litigation notices generated and approved, steering dashboard
E3 | 31 Jan 2027 | Settle, deed in lieu, assets | Settlements and deeds in lieu end to end to booking. Asset record, floor price and listing on HOME.SCB
E4 | 28 Feb 2027 | Route decision | The route recommended with reasons and approved within the delegation of authority for every new case. Guarantee and TCG claims. Auction rounds and RAMC transfer
E5 | 31 Mar 2027 | Litigation | Litigation instructed and tracked end to end, law firms through the partner portal. Debt sale lot data and the buyer data room
E6 | 30 Apr 2027 | Debt sale and write-off | Debt sale screens and award, write-off committee, partner panel, allocation and fees
E7 | 31 May 2027 | Deviations and partners | Deviations X1 to X7 end to end. Partner scoring, conduct and the field app
E8 | 30 Jun 2027 | Administration and hardening | Full administration, conduct checks, autonomy step-ups, regulatory returns, hardening

5
Epic | Release | Stories | Points | Content
E1 | 30 Nov 2026 | 67 | 374 | P1 loads and checks for COLLINS, CCMS and SVAF; P3 case record, state model and rules component with allocation rules; P4 sign-in and roles; P5 document store and OCR; P6 notice generation; P7 decision log store; P9 baseline; P10 agent runtime in shadow
E2 | 31 Dec 2026 | 32 | 199 | P3 queue and transfer screens; P4 partner identities; P5 document generation; P6 dispatch and proof of delivery; P7 approval routing; P8 matching skeleton; P9 steering dashboard; S2 treatment record; S4 notice approval; S8 deviation screening
13 technical enabler stories run alongside, and three agent stories carry into Epic 3. Environments, pipelines and secrets are on the Sprint 0 checklist.

6
 | Rule
1 | No more than three planning or review meetings a week for a squad member, and none longer than 30 minutes
2 | The sponsor review and the steering committee look back at finished work and are outside that limit
3 | Work flows on a Kanban board with limits on work in progress per column and a written pull policy
4 | The monthly release is the only date the business sees. What slips moves to the next epic; the date does not move
5 | Planning happens daily at the board. There is no sprint commitment and no velocity target

7
Cadence | Forum | Length | Who | What it covers
Daily | Board review | 15 minutes, each morning | Each squad: tech lead, developers, analyst, QA | Blockers and the oldest item on the board. What is pulled next
Daily | Help needed | As raised, the same day | Product owner with the person blocked | Who removes each blocker and by when. A blocker needing the bank goes to its owner the same day
Weekly | Delivery review | 30 minutes | Product owner, tech leads, analysts, QA lead, ACE team | The four flow numbers, what broke between modules, changes to the definitions of ready and done
Weekly | Decision review | 30 minutes | Product owner with the owners of open decisions | Each open decision against its date. Overdue decisions go to the sponsor review or the steering committee
Weekly | Design review for the next epic | 30 minutes | Analysts, solution architect, business lead | Progress of the next epic's design, one epic ahead of the build
Weekly | Progress update | Written | Product owner to the business unit heads | Finished work, the next release, open decisions and risks
Two-weekly | Sponsor progress review | 45 minutes | Sponsors, product owner, business lead | A look back at finished work. No commitment is made
Monthly | Epic design sign-off | 45 minutes | Business lead, product owner, Risk where limits move | The next epic's design is signed before its build starts
Monthly | Release go decision | 30 minutes | Release owner in the ACE team, product owner, application owner | Go or no-go on the SIT and UAT exits. Flags stay off for work that is not ready
Monthly | Epic demo | 60 minutes | Squads, business users, sponsors | The released work, shown on the system
Monthly | Steering committee | 60 minutes | Sponsors, CTO delegate, product owner, Henka | Decisions above the project: scope, budget, overdue decisions, risks

8
Ready
Definition of ready met
Plan
Files, tests and migrations named
Merge
Nine pipeline gates and a reviewer
Done
Definition of done met
SIT and UAT
One week each before the release
Release
Month end, flags off for unfinished work
Gate | Who checks
Ready | Analyst with the tech lead and QA
Merge | Named reviewer; code owner where another module is touched
Done | Product owner
SIT exit | QA lead with SCB IT
UAT exit | Business lead
Release | Release owner in the ACE team with the application owner

secs.h: Slide 9. When the build needs an answer
secs.t:
9
Step | What happens
1 Raise | Anyone raises a question the build cannot answer. The product owner adds it to the decision log with an ID
2 Frame | The analyst writes the question, the options, a recommendation, what it blocks and what happens if it is late
3 Assign | The product owner names one owner and a date needed. Decision owners are bank roles
4 Build on the recommendation | The squads build on the recommended answer and mark it as an assumption in the story
5 Decide | The owner decides within five working days of the date needed, or the decision goes to the next review
6 Record | The decision moves to Decisions taken with the date, who took it and what it means for the build
7 Apply | Documents and stories built on the assumption are updated. An architecture decision also gets a decision record
Issue | Who resolves it | By when
Within a squad | Tech lead | Same day
Between squads or with the ACE team | Tech leads together; the ACE team decides if they do not agree | Same day
Needs a bank answer | Decision owner, through the decision log | Five working days

secs.h: Slide 10. The first month: build team
secs.t:
10
Role | 2 to 6 Nov | 9 to 13 Nov | 16 to 20 Nov | 23 to 27 Nov
Product owner | Confirm the backlog order; chase decisions due this week (DL04, DL05, DL13, DL24, DL32 to DL34, DL36) | Sponsor review on 13 Nov; Epic 2 design pack drafted | Epic 2 design signed by 20 Nov; SIT scope confirmed | UAT; go decision on 27 Nov; release on 29 Nov
Business analysts | Window 1 stories ready; rule rows with test case IDs | Window 2 stories ready; Epic 2 stories refined | Answer SIT questions; Epic 2 stories ready | UAT scripts walked through with the testers
Tech leads | Recovery module folder, boundary test and code owners (RWB-TE-001, RWB-TE-002); first items pulled | Board limits held; merges daily | Release scope closed; SIT defects triaged | Fixes for UAT; flags off for unfinished work
Developers | Access to DEV; schema and migrations (RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-044); file adapter pattern | Case record, allocation, decision log writer, document store | Finish and fix in SIT | Fix UAT defects; nothing new merged into the release
QA engineers | Synthetic data (RWB-E1-065); rule table harness (RWB-TE-005) | Automated tests per story; contract tests | SIT for Epic 1 | UAT support; regression

secs.h: Slide 11. The first month: business and platform
secs.t:

Business testers | Named and given DEV access (DL09) | Test with the squads as stories finish | UAT scripts prepared | UAT and sign-off

docs.file: Recovery Workbench ACE Data Tier Map v1.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench ACE Data Tier Map v1

secs.h: Recovery Workbench ACE data tier map
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | Recovery Workbench ACE Data Tier Map v1 |
| Purpose | The frozen table-and-column map that every Wave 1 to Wave 5 edit reads: what the Workbench takes from ACE, what the ACE team adds, what the Workbench owns, and what leaves the schema |
| Status | Frozen input. Changes need the data architect and the recovery tech lead, and a new version of this file |
| Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1 to U5) |
| Companions | Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1.md; Recovery Workbench ACE Field Gap List v1.xlsx; Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql; ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql |
| Counts fixed here | 108 tables to 92 tables, 30 views, 122 dictionary objects, 1,366 dictionary fields |

The Workbench never loads source data. Every source record lands in the ACE database through ACE's own ingestion. The recovery module reads it through one surface only:

- `recovery.v_ace_*` views, `SELECT` only, owned by the recovery module and by a dedicated `ace_view_owner` role that holds `SELECT` on the ACE tables.
- The recovery service identity holds `SELECT` on the views and on nothing else, so a direct read of a `public` table fails in the catalog, not only in code review.
- No foreign key from a `recovery` table into a `public` table, because ACE uses `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `account` and a cascade would delete Workbench case history.
- Workbench links to source records are business-key columns (`varchar(255)`), not UUID foreign keys.
- The recovery schema never writes to `public`.

Two migrations, because a view cannot be created over a table that does not exist yet:

| Migration | Contains | Ships |
|---|---|---|
| Section A | 16 views over ACE tables that exist today, 177 fields | With RWB-E1-069, the next free sequence after the V0001 baseline |
| Section B | 14 views over the Tier 2 additions, 127 fields | The week RWB-ACE-001 lands; until then the dependent features stay behind their flags |

secs.h: 2. Tier 1 - ACE tables that exist today, read through a view and never altered
secs.t:
| # | ACE table | View | Used for | Note |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `account` | `v_ace_account` | Account, arrears, balances, classification, restructure flag, batch date | `delay_days` becomes `days_past_due`; `core_banking_system_date` becomes `data_as_of` |
| 2 | `payment` | `v_ace_payment` | Payments, proceeds matching | `pay_date` is `varchar`, cast by `ace_to_date` |
| 3 | `customer` | `v_ace_customer` | Party, identity, vulnerability inputs | `identification_number` is masked in the view |
| 4 | `phone` | `v_ace_contact` | Contact point, notice and call inputs | Union with email and address, `contact_type` discriminator |
| 5 | `email` | `v_ace_contact` | Contact point | Same view |
| 6 | `address` | `v_ace_contact` | Contact point, notice address | Same view |
| 7 | `ca_relation` | `v_ace_ca_relation` | Borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles | |
| 8 | `aa_relation` | `v_ace_aa_relation` | Parent and child accounts | |
| 9 | `collateral` | `v_ace_collateral` | Collateral link and value | |
| 10 | `asset` | `v_ace_asset` | Collateral asset and held asset | |
| 11 | `efs_action` | `v_ace_efs_action` | Collections history and interaction | Replaces `collections_history` |
| 12 | `efs_action_code` | `v_ace_efs_action_code` | Action code list of values | 1,106 values, loaded list |
| 13 | `efs_assignment` | `v_ace_efs_assignment` | Assignment and hand-over history | |
| 14 | `bucket_log_snapshot` | `v_ace_bucket_log` | Monthly bucket history | The daily bucket is a Tier 2 column |
| 15 | `product` | `v_ace_product` | Product and product group lists | |
| 16 | `branch` | `v_ace_branch` | Branch and region lists | |
| 17 | `bot_holiday` | `v_ace_holiday` | Service level and legal-day calendar | E1-043 and E1-045 use this instead of a Workbench list |
| 18 | `iam_user` | none | Sign-on identity, read by the ACE common module | Not read by the recovery module |
| 19 | `ace_case` | `v_ace_plan` | Restructure plan reference and status | E2-002 already reads ACE |
| 20 | `cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case` | `v_ace_plan` | Plan booking, approval and closure dates | |
| 21 | `tdr_calculation` | `v_ace_plan` | Published calculation version | |
| 22 | `ai_recommended_plan` | `v_ace_plan` | Recommended installments and package | |
| 23 | Quartz tables `qrtz_*` | none | Scheduler state, shared with ACE | No new `qrtz_` table is created |
| 24 | Spring Batch tables `batch_*` | none | Step execution, shared with ACE | The per-source completion record is `ace_batch_run`, Tier 2 |

Tier 1 tables are never altered by the Workbench. Where ACE already holds a column with a different name or type, the view maps it. Where ACE holds nothing, the field is Tier 2.

secs.h: 3. Tier 2 - new ACE tables and columns, owned by the ACE team
secs.t:
The ACE team owns these. The Workbench raises them once, in RWB-ACE-001, with the field appendix. The count is 80 field mappings to 14 new tables and 12 new columns; 79 distinct columns, because `efs_action.contact_result` serves two LDM fields.

| # | ACE object | Kind | Columns | Source | Why ACE does not have it |
|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `ace_batch_run` | new table | 9 | all | A per-source business date and completion record; the Workbench freshness stamp and the intake trigger read it |
| 2 | `valuation` | new table | 11 | SVAF | ACE holds no appraisal |
| 3 | `collateral_detail` | new table | 15 | CCMS | Title deed, plot, area, province, district, subdistrict, insured value, insurance expiry, lien rank |
| 4 | `npa_asset` | new table | 14 | AMIS, RPS | ACE holds the collateral asset, not the repossessed or purchased asset |
| 5 | `npa_sale` | new table | 13 | AMIS | Sale contract, taxes, fees and incentive |
| 6 | `lawsuit` | new table | 15 | LIT | Court case numbers, claim, judgment and status |
| 7 | `hearing` | new table | 9 | LIT | Hearing date, type and next date |
| 8 | `pod_receipt` | new table | 12 | WIN | Proof of delivery for a notice |
| 9 | `gl_write_off` | new table | 11 | GL | Write-off posting, cost centre and GL product |
| 10 | `collins_score` | new table | 12 | COLLINS | Score, estimate and route, if ACE does not already hold it |
| 11 | `party_product` | new table | 7 | SCBPDM | Customer product holding |
| 12 | `credit_decision` | new table | 10 | NLEADS | Credit result, reason and decision date for a treatment |
| 13 | `esign_request` | new table | 9 | EasyApp | Signature reference and status; the signed file stays in the Workbench document hub |
| 14 | `iam_group` | new table | 7 | Entra ID | Group-to-role mapping; ACE performs the sign-in |
| 15 | `account` | 7 new columns | 7 | ALS | `business_unit`, `principal_outstanding`, `interest_outstanding`, `fees_outstanding`, `daily_bucket`, `settlement_booked_date`, `settlement_booked_amount` |
| 16 | `customer` | 3 new columns | 3 | SCBPDM | `party_type`, `id_type`, `segment` |
| 17 | `efs_action` | 2 new columns | 2 | EFS | `contact_result`, `action_contact_status` |

Every Tier 2 table carries `source_system`, `business_date` and `loaded_at`, so the Workbench can always say where a row came from and how old it is. Every Tier 2 table has an ACE business key with a unique constraint, because the Workbench links to it by key.

Full list with type, nullability, source field and LDM field ID: **Recovery Workbench ACE Field Gap List v1.xlsx**, sheet `ACE additions`.

secs.h: 4. Tier 3 - recovery extension tables, Workbench-owned, keyed by ACE business keys
secs.t:
One-to-one tables. They hold Workbench decisions about an ACE record and never a copy of it. They carry the seven standard record columns.

| Table | Key | Columns | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery.party_ext` | `person_key varchar(255)` | `vulnerable`, `deceased_override`, `bankruptcy`, `fraud_flag` | Workbench flags about an ACE customer |
| `recovery.contact_point_ext` | `contact_key varchar(255)` + `contact_type` | `consent_given`, `consent_at`, `verified_at`, `failed_count`, `source` | Consent and contact quality for a phone, email or address |
| `recovery.account_ext` | `account_key varchar(255)` | `dispute_open` | Workbench state about an ACE account |
| `recovery.valuation_ext` | `valuation_key varchar(255)` | `accepted`, `accepted_at`, `accepted_by`, `valuer_partner_id`, `stale_flag`, `age_days` | The Workbench's decision about an ACE appraisal |

secs.h: 5. Tier 4 - recovery Workbench tables that stay
secs.t:
88 Workbench-owned tables keep their purpose. Their links to source data change from UUID foreign keys to business-key columns.

The 14 surviving foreign keys into a source record become:

| Table | Old column | New column | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | `primary_customer_id` | `primary_person_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `case_account` | `account_id` | `account_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `case_party` | `party_id` | `person_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `notice` | `party_id` | `person_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `listing` | `asset_id` | `asset_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `asset_sale` | `asset_id` | `asset_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `debt_sale_account` | `account_id` | `account_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `interaction` | `party_id` | `person_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `interaction` | `contact_point_id` | `contact_key` (composite: contact_type:key) | `varchar(255)` |
| `document` | `party_id` | `person_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `proceeds` | `account_payment_id` | `payment_code` | `varchar(255)` |
| `case_list_row` | `account_id` | `account_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `case_entry_exclusion` | `account_id` | `account_key` | `varchar(255)` |
| `signature_request` | `party_id` | `person_key` | `varchar(255)` |

No foreign key is created on any of these columns. Referential integrity is checked by the read model and by reconciliation rule REC-05, not by the database.

| Object | Fields | Reason | Where its content goes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `loan_account` | 24 | Copy of ALS data | `v_ace_account` |
| `account_payment` | 7 | Copy of ALS data | `v_ace_payment` |
| `party` | 13 | Copy of SCBPDM data | `v_ace_customer` plus `party_ext` |
| `contact_point` | 8 | Copy of SCBPDM data | `v_ace_contact` plus `contact_point_ext` |
| `collateral` | 13 | Copy of CCMS data | `v_ace_collateral` and `v_ace_collateral_detail` |
| `account_collateral` | 4 | Copy of CCMS data | `v_ace_collateral`, `collateral_detail.lien_rank` |
| `collections_history` | 10 | Copy of EFS data | `v_ace_efs_action` |
| `party_product` | 6 | Copy of SCBPDM data | `v_ace_party_product` |
| `valuation` | 12 | Moves to ACE | `v_ace_valuation` plus `valuation_ext` |
| `score` | 9 | Moves to ACE | `v_ace_score` |
| `asset` | 15 | ACE already holds the asset | `v_ace_asset` and `v_ace_npa_asset` |
| `load_run` | 20 | No inbound load | ACE batch record |
| `dq_exception` | 11 | No inbound load | ACE ingestion checks; REC-01 to REC-05 for reconciliation |
| `dq_rule` | 12 | No inbound load | ACE ingestion checks |
| `source_field_map` | 11 | No inbound load | STTM v4 and the ACE field appendix |
| `source_code_map` | 8 | No inbound load | ACE ingestion; LOV values from ACE |
| `interface_run` | 12 | Inbound runs leave; outbound runs stay | `outbound_item` and `outbox_delivery` |
| `interface_signoff` | 7 | Inbound runs leave | ACE team sign-off in RWB-ACE-001 |
| `tracker_inventory` | 26 | Excel and SharePoint trackers leave scope | Cutover plan |
| `tracker_row` | 9 | Excel and SharePoint trackers leave scope | Cutover plan |

20 tables and 237 fields leave, plus 6 columns on retained tables (`treatment` 4, `signature_request` 1, `role` 1) that the six fields moved to ACE, 243 fields in all. `interface_config` stays for outbound interfaces only. `data_product_load` stays as the freshness stamp, sourced from `ace_batch_run`. `reconciliation_result` stays and reconciles the case list to `v_ace_account`.

Three examples that every downstream document repeats:

| LDM field | Physical today | Source | Read path v5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loan_account.days_past_due` | `loan_account.days_past_due` | ALS `DELAY_DAYS` | `v_ace_account.days_past_due` from `public.account.delay_days` |
| `account_payment.payment_date` | `account_payment.payment_date date` | ALS `Payment_Date` | `v_ace_payment.payment_date` from `recovery.ace_to_date(public.payment.pay_date)` |
| `party.cif_no` | `party.cif_no` | SCBPDM `CIF` | `v_ace_customer.cif_no` from `public.customer.person_key` |

Two type rules the views enforce:

- Text dates in ACE (`payment.pay_date`) become `date` through `recovery.ace_to_date`, which returns NULL rather than failing on an unrecognised value.
- Y/N text flags in ACE (`account.is_restructured`, `customer.is_deceased`) become `boolean` through `recovery.ace_to_boolean`.

One masking rule:

- `customer.identification_number` is exposed as `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only. The full value never leaves ACE. Phone, email and address are exposed in full because notices and calls need them; display masking is E1-037 at the API, and every read is audited.

| Item | v4 today | v5 target | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Workbench tables | 108 | 92 | 108 - 20 removed + 4 extension |
| Views | 0 | 30 | 16 Tier 1 + 14 Tier 2 |
| Dictionary objects (`sys_objects`) | 108 | 122 | 92 tables + 30 views |
| Dictionary fields (`sys_fields`) | 1,256 | 1,366 | 1,256 - 243 removed + 49 extension + 304 view |
| Foreign keys into `public.*` | 0 | 0 | The boundary rule forbids them |
| UUID foreign keys into a source copy | 23 | 0 | 14 re-keyed, 9 leave with their table |

The exact figures are re-derived from the LDM v7 and the Physical Schema v5 pair; if any of them moves, the register and D-RCV-35 are amended in the same pass.

1. A Workbench table never holds a column that ACE already holds. If the screen needs it, it reads the view.
2. A Workbench table never holds a copy of a source record. A snapshot taken at case entry is allowed and is named `_at_entry`.
3. A link to a source record is a business key with no foreign key.
4. A new source field is either already in ACE (map it) or goes into RWB-ACE-001 (ask the ACE team). It never becomes a Workbench column.
5. A view field is named for the Workbench, not for ACE. The ACE name appears only in the view definition and the STTM.
6. `recovery.v_ace_*` is the only read path. A direct `public.*` read in a story, spec or query is a defect.

docs.file: Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1.md
docs.name: Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1

secs.h: Recovery Workbench ACE DB alignment change register
secs.t:
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.

(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1 |
| Purpose | The decision record and the edit plan for re-basing the Workbench on the ACE database: no inbound source loads, read-only views, ACE-owned additions, Workbench-owned extension tables |
| Status | Signed off on 15 November 2026 (U1 to U5, 30 views, all 133 fields through ACE). Wave 1 delivered: STTM v4, LDM v7, Physical Schema v5, RWB-ACE-001 |
| Decisions | U1 to U5, recorded as D-RCV-35 |
| Decision owner | Recovery tech lead with the data architect; ACE team lead for RWB-ACE-001 and DL43 |
| Scope | 82 files, 332 existing stories, 2 new stories, 133 source fields |
| Frozen inputs produced with this register | ACE Data Tier Map v1.md, ACE Field Gap List v1.xlsx, ACE Source Views v1.sql, ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql, ACE Schema Extract v1.csv, ACE DB Alignment Tracker v1.xlsx |
| Sources examined | ACE-data-schema_20261104.xlsx (62 tables, 547 columns); Physical Schema v4.sql (108 tables, 1,256 fields); LDM and Data Dictionary v6.xlsx (133 external fields); STTM v3.xlsx; Conceptual Data Model v5.xlsx; Decision Log v8.xlsx; ADR v1.md; all six story workbooks; TSD P1 v2 |

The Workbench design today builds a separate recovery schema inside the ACE database and fills it with copies of source data. Eleven copy tables hold 121 fields of loan, payment, party, contact, collateral, valuation, asset, collections, product and score data. Nine more tables run the load: `load_run`, `dq_exception`, `dq_rule`, `source_field_map`, `source_code_map`, `interface_run`, `interface_signoff`, `tracker_inventory` and `tracker_row`, 116 fields. JOB-01 and JOB-09 move the data from the COLLINS staging feeds and the file loads.

The bank already runs ACE. ACE ingests account, payment, customer, address, phone, email, ca_relation, collateral, asset, efs_action, efs_assignment, bucket_log_snapshot, product and branch today, and it has case, SLA, holiday, audit, Quartz and Spring Batch tables. The Workbench is a module of ACE (ADR-001). Two copies of the same account row, one in ACE and one in the recovery schema, is a defect in waiting: they disagree, and the Workbench owns the one nobody else maintains.

The documents half-anticipate the change. The LDM has an ACE column, the Conceptual Data Model has an In ACE today column, CDM slide 7 and the TSD P1 model mark `loan_account` and `account_payment` as Reuse ACE and `party` and `collateral` as Extend. The physical schema, the STTM, the interface specifications, the jobs and the stories still build the copies.

This register finishes the move. The Workbench stops handling source data. It reads ACE through views, and it adds only new tables and columns.

| # | Decision | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | No inbound source loads in the Workbench. All source data lands in the ACE DB through ACE's ingestion, including SVAF and CCMS, which ACE does not hold today. The Workbench only reads the ACE DB. | Deletes the load machinery and the inbound half of the interface estate. 20 tables leave the schema. |
| U2 | The ACE team owns the new ACE tables and columns for source data. One new story, RWB-ACE-001, lists every new table and column the Workbench needs. | Adds 14 tables and 12 columns to the ACE team's backlog, with an 80-row field appendix. |
| U3 | Workbench-owned fields that ACE lacks go into extension tables in the recovery schema. They are 1:1 tables keyed by ACE business keys. Existing ACE tables are never altered by the Workbench. | Adds 4 extension tables. Keeps the Workbench out of ACE's DDL. |
| U4 | Read path is read-only views. `recovery.v_ace_*` SELECT-only views sit over ACE tables and map names and types. There are no FK constraints into ACE tables, because ACE uses ON DELETE CASCADE on account. Boundary rule: the recovery module may read ACE only through these views. | Adds 30 views and the grant they need. Re-keys 14 foreign keys to business keys. |
| U5 | Excel and SharePoint trackers are removed from system scope. Retirement is handled in the Cutover plan. | Removes 2 tables and 3 stories from scope; adds a retirement procedure to Cutover. |

secs.h: 2.1 Assumption to confirm at the gate
secs.t:
AMIS and RPS (NPA assets), LIT (legal), WIN proof-of-delivery inbound, GL write-off inbound and COLLINS scores follow the same route as SVAF and CCMS: ACE ingests them, and they appear in RWB-ACE-001. That is the assumption this register is built on. If any one of them is not ingested by ACE, its fields leave the ACE story and become a Workbench staging problem again, which reopens U1 for that source.

At sign-off the bank also routed the last three sources through ACE rather than recording them by hand:

| Field | Source | ACE object added |
|---|---|---|
| `treatment.nleads_ref`, `credit_result`, `credit_result_reason`, `credit_result_at` | NLEADS | `credit_decision` (4 fields) |
| `signature_request.external_ref` | EasyApp | `esign_request` (1 field) |
| `role.entra_group` | Entra ID | `iam_group` (1 field) |

That takes the ACE story to 80 fields and leaves no external field entered by hand. The ACE team lead confirms the whole list at the gate, together with DL43.

One line: **ACE holds the data, the Workbench holds the case, and a view joins them.**

| Tier | Owner | What it holds | Count |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | ACE team, read only | ACE tables that exist today, read through a view and never altered | 22 tables, 16 views |
| 2 | ACE team | New ACE tables and columns for source data that ACE does not hold | 14 tables, 12 columns, 14 views |
| 3 | Workbench | 1:1 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys | 4 tables |
| 4 | Workbench | Case, workflow, treatment, legal, partner, debt sale, documents, decision log, reference, outbox, flags, agents | 88 tables |
| Removed | - | Source copies, load machinery and the 6 columns the ACE story absorbs | 20 tables, 243 fields |

The full table-and-column map is **Recovery Workbench ACE Data Tier Map v1.md**. The field-level list is **Recovery Workbench ACE Field Gap List v1.xlsx**. The view definitions that compile are **Recovery Workbench ACE Source Views v1.sql**.

secs.h: 3.1 Tier 2 - what the ACE team is asked to add
secs.t:
| Object | Kind | Columns | Source | Fields the Workbench reads |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `ace_batch_run` | new table | 9 | all | 0 (drives freshness) |
| `valuation` | new table | 11 | SVAF | 5 |
| `collateral_detail` | new table | 15 | CCMS | 9 |
| `npa_asset` | new table | 14 | AMIS, RPS | 8 |
| `npa_sale` | new table | 13 | AMIS | 7 |
| `lawsuit` | new table | 15 | LIT | 9 |
| `hearing` | new table | 9 | LIT | 3 |
| `pod_receipt` | new table | 12 | WIN | 5 |
| `gl_write_off` | new table | 11 | GL | 5 |
| `collins_score` | new table | 12 | COLLINS | 6 |
| `party_product` | new table | 7 | SCBPDM | 4 |
| `credit_decision` | new table | 10 | NLEADS | 4 |
| `esign_request` | new table | 9 | EasyApp | 1 |
| `iam_group` | new table | 7 | Entra ID | 1 |
| `account` | 7 new columns | 7 | ALS | 7 |
| `customer` | 3 new columns | 3 | SCBPDM | 3 |
| `efs_action` | 2 new columns | 2 | EFS | 2 |
| **Total** | 14 tables, 12 columns | **166** | | **80** |

Every new table carries `source_system`, `business_date` and `loaded_at`, a business key with a unique constraint, and a primary key. The Workbench links to the business key only.

secs.h: 3.2 The read path and the two-migration rule
secs.t:
A view cannot be created over a table that does not exist. The views therefore ship in two parts:

- **Section A**, 16 views, 177 fields, over ACE tables that exist today. Ships with RWB-E1-069 as the next free sequence after the V0001 baseline.
- **Section B**, 14 views, 127 fields, over the Tier 2 additions. Ships the week RWB-ACE-001 lands. Until then the features that need them stay behind their flags.

This is the one place where the plan's estimate and the design differ: the plan said about 10 views, and the frozen list is 30. The reason is the boundary rule itself: one view per ACE object family, so a developer can be told which view to read and cannot wander into `public`. Merging them would save 15 objects and make the grant and the conformance test coarser. The recommendation is 26.

| Field | Treatment |
|---|---|
| `customer.identification_number` | Never exposed in clear. `v_ace_customer` returns `id_no_masked` (last four) and `id_no_last4`. |
| `phone.phone_number`, `email.email`, `address.address` | Full value in `v_ace_contact`, because notices and calls need it. Display masking is E1-037 at the API. Every read is audited. |
| Tokenization at load | Removed. There is no load. E1-037 role masking replaces `id_no_token`. |

The LDM v6 holds 133 fields with an external source. Every one is resolved:

| Disposition | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| ACE reuse | 52 | Already in an ACE table. Named in the view; no new column. |
| ACE new | 80 | Not in ACE. RWB-ACE-001 asks the ACE team. |
| Recovery extension | 1 | `party.fraud_flag` becomes `recovery.party_ext.fraud_flag`. |
| Workbench | 0 | No external field is entered by hand. |
| **Total** | **133** | |

Distinct ACE columns for the 80 ACE-new fields: 79, because `efs_action.contact_result` serves both `interaction.contact_result` and `collections_history.contact_result`.

The carried examples, repeated in the LDM v7 and STTM v4:

| LDM field | Source | Read path v5 |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_account.days_past_due` | ALS `DELAY_DAYS` | `v_ace_account.days_past_due` from `public.account.delay_days` |
| `account_payment.payment_date` | ALS `Payment_Date` | `v_ace_payment.payment_date` from `recovery.ace_to_date(public.payment.pay_date)`; `pay_date` is varchar |
| `party.cif_no` | SCBPDM `CIF` | `v_ace_customer.cif_no` from `public.customer.person_key` |
| `collections_history.contact_at` | EFS | `v_ace_efs_action.contact_at` from `public.efs_action.action_timestamp` |

| Group | Tables | Fields |
|---|---|---:|
| Source copies | `loan_account`, `account_payment`, `party`, `contact_point`, `collateral`, `account_collateral`, `collections_history`, `party_product`, `valuation`, `score`, `asset` | 121 |
| Load machinery | `load_run`, `dq_exception`, `dq_rule`, `source_field_map`, `source_code_map`, `interface_run`, `interface_signoff`, `tracker_inventory`, `tracker_row` | 116 |
| Columns on retained tables | `treatment` 4, `signature_request` 1, `role` 1 - read from ACE now | 6 |
| **Total** | **20 tables** | **243** |

Kept and re-pointed:

- `interface_config` stays for outbound interfaces only.
- `data_product_load` stays as the freshness stamp and is sourced from `ace_batch_run`.
- `reconciliation_result` stays and reconciles the case list to `v_ace_account`.

The plan says 23 foreign keys across 14 tables are re-pointed. The schema says something slightly different, and the difference matters to the edit:

- 23 foreign key constraints reference the 11 source-copy tables.
- They span 20 tables, not 14.
- 9 of them are on tables that leave with the copy (`account_payment`, `account_collateral` twice, `valuation` twice, `asset`, `score`, `party_product`, `contact_point`).
- The other 14 sit on 13 retained tables and are re-keyed to business keys with no foreign key.

The 14 are listed in the Tier Map section 5. One of them, `interaction.contact_point_id`, becomes `contact_key` holding a composite `contact_type:key`, because a contact point is now one of three ACE objects and the key must be unambiguous on its own.

> D-RCV-35 ruled: the Recovery Workbench takes no inbound source data. All source data lands in the ACE database through ACE's ingestion (U1); the ACE team owns the new ACE tables and columns, raised once in RWB-ACE-001 (U2); Workbench-only fields go into 1:1 extension tables keyed by ACE business keys and no existing ACE table is altered by the Workbench (U3); the recovery module reads ACE only through SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views, with no foreign key into ACE because ACE cascades deletes on `account` (U4); Excel and SharePoint trackers leave system scope and are retired through the Cutover plan (U5). This supersedes DT12, DL06 option A and DL12 option A, amends DL20 to name ACE as the route for customer facts, and amends D-RCV-29 because the sys_objects and sys_fields counts change.

- **Supersedes** DT12 (data through COLLINS), DL06 option A (daily batch through COLLINS for all Epic 1 and Epic 2 data), DL12 option A (read and write through ACE and COLLINS only).
- **Amends** DL20 (source of customer facts) to say the facts come from ACE, which ingests them from SCBPDM and the core bank.
- **Amends** D-RCV-29: the baseline dictionary becomes 122 `sys_objects` rows and 1,366 `sys_fields` rows instead of 108 and 1,256.

> **ADR-010 Read source data from the ACE database through read-only views.** Status: accepted. Supersedes ADR-005. The recovery module reads source data from the ACE database through `recovery.v_ace_*` views. It does not load, copy or transform source data. The ACE team owns every table and column the views read; the Workbench owns only its extension tables. Consequences: one copy of source data; the Workbench cannot start before the ACE additions land (DL43); no tokenization at load, so masking moves to the views and to E1-037; the load, DQ and tracker estate leaves scope. ADR-001 consequence updated: recovery takes ACE's data position, which is now an asset rather than a constraint.

secs.h: 6.3 ACE Architecture Decision v2 to v3
secs.t:
| Section | Edit |
|---|---|
| 1 How does data arrive | SVAF, CCMS, AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS scores and SCBPDM party product arrive through ACE ingestion, not through a Workbench load. |
| 4 A module reads only its own tables | Exception: the recovery module reads `recovery.v_ace_*` views, which read public ACE tables. No direct public read, no write. |
| 5 Data | The recovery module owns the case and the extension tables; ACE owns source data. |
| 7 Data | The entity list loses the copy tables and gains the views and extension tables. |

- **DL43** (new, open): does the ACE team accept the RWB-ACE-001 scope and its dates? Owner: ACE team lead. Needed by: 2026-11-21 for a 30 November release. Blocks: E1-069, E1-002, E1-016, E1-018, the whole recovery data engine.
- **Rulings v2**: mark the copy-table counts (44 tables, 533 fields, 108/1,256) superseded by D-RCV-35. Ruling R4 (definitions) holds; the systems of record are re-worded "ACE (ingested from X)".
- **Admin and Access Model v5**: remove the SY-DATALOAD actor; add the read-only ACE service identity.

The rule for every row: a new version in the home folder, the old version stays until sign-off, one writer per file, and an edit log returned to this register.

159 stories are touched. The per-story list with entities today, the ACE action and a status column is the tracker's `Stories` sheet.

The named lists and the automated scan do not agree in every family. The scan is the list of record, because it reads the Entities column and the Gherkin of all 332 stories rather than a sample. The differences:

| Item | Plan | Reconciled | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Epic 1 removals | 9 | 8 | The plan's own list names eight: E1-003, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 051. |

None of these changes the intent. Each is a bookkeeping correction so the Wave 3 agents edit the right files.

**RWB-ACE-001 - ACE DB additions for the Recovery Workbench** (owner: ACE team). It carries:

- The 14 new tables and 12 new columns, per source, with type, nullability, key and reference.
- The field appendix: 80 rows from the gap list, each with field ID, source field, type, frequency and the Workbench view that reads it.
- The batch business-date record `ace_batch_run` and its population rules.
- The SELECT grant for the recovery role on the listed tables.
- Acceptance criteria on population, on freshness, on not breaking the existing ACE reads, and on the migration being reversible.
- The date the Workbench needs it: 2026-11-21 for a 30 November release.

**RWB-E1-069 - Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule** (owner: recovery squad). It carries:

- The 16 Section A views (over ACE tables that exist today), and the 14 Section B views (over the RWB-ACE-001 additions) as a second migration: 30 in all, per section 3.2.
- The 4 extension tables.
- The grant to the recovery service identity and the revoke from PUBLIC.
- TE-001 extended so the boundary test allows only `recovery.v_ace_*`.
- A view conformance test that fails the build if a recovery constraint references `public`, if a view does not compile, or if the recovery role can write.

One writer per output file. Every agent reads the same frozen inputs and never edits a file another agent owns. Each returns a short edit log: sections changed, IDs removed or added, open questions. The log is appended to this register.

secs.h: 10.1 What was run for this register
secs.t:
The ACE schema was generated from the workbook into PostgreSQL 17 and the views were compiled against it:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| ACE schema loads | 62 tables, 547 columns, 58 composite foreign keys, 60 primary keys, 22 unique constraints, 31 indexes |
| Section A views compile against the ACE schema on their own | 16 of 16 |
| Section B views compile after the Tier 2 probe | 14 of 14 |
| `v_ace_account.days_past_due` reads `account.delay_days` | 95 on the smoke row |
| `v_ace_payment.payment_date` casts `20261130` | 2026-11-30 |
| `v_ace_customer.id_no_masked` | `*********0123` from `1234567890123` |
| `v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked` | `******5678` from `0812345678` |
| Physical Schema v4 loads as written | **No** - see DEF-01 to DEF-03 |

- Physical Schema v5 in a PostgreSQL 17 container that first runs the ACE schema, then V0001, then the Section A views.
- Every `v_ace_*` view compiles; no constraint in `recovery` references `public.*`; `v_data_dictionary` returns `days_past_due` sourced from `public.account.delay_days`.
- `sys_objects` and `sys_fields` counts match LDM v7 exactly.
- The recovery role cannot select a public table directly, and cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on any table.

- Cross-document grep: no remaining `loan_account`, `account_payment`, `collections_history`, `party` as a table, `load_run`, `tracker_`, `JOB-01` or inbound `INT-0x` load wording, except in superseded text and this register.
- Every story's Entities column resolves to a Physical Schema v5 table or a `v_ace_*` view.
- Every removed story or test case has a row in this register's appendix.
- Every REQ-RDF in the RTM points at a live story or test.
- RWB-ACE-001 rows equal STTM v4 gap-sheet rows, 1:1.

secs.h: 11. Defects found while writing this register
secs.t:
| ID | Where | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEF-01 | Physical Schema v4.sql | No `data_product` seed rows, although D-RCV-29 and rulings R1 and R4 require 14. The file does not load: the first `sys_objects` insert fails the foreign key. | v5 seeds 14 rows before `sys_objects`, definitions from CDM v6. |
| DEF-02 | Physical Schema v4.sql | `data_product.refresh_cycle` is `varchar(10)`, but its comment and the LDM use "On change" and "By versioned load". | Widen to `varchar(30)` in v5. |
| DEF-03 | Physical Schema v4.sql | 33 `sys_objects` rows carry OPS, AGT or RPT and `data_product` is NOT NULL. Ruling R1 is not applied to v4. | Apply R1 in v5: nullable, 33 rows NULL, FK created. |
| DEF-04 | ACE workbook | `ace_case_accounts` and `batch_job_execution_params` carry no primary key. | No Workbench change; recorded so the conformance test does not assume one. |
| DEF-05 | Physical Schema v5 | 42 fields on retained tables still carry a source system and source field from the copy design (hearing, legal_action, notice, write_off, asset_sale, proceeds, dp_treatment, interaction, decision_log_entry, debt_sale_account, treatment, recovery_case). They mirror a Tier 1 or Tier 2 column and should either be dropped and read from the view, or declared a Workbench snapshot. | Wave 2 cleanup, one story at a time: the owning story drops the column and reads the view, or states why the snapshot is kept. Recorded, not blocking: the schema, the views and the dictionary counts are consistent. |
| DEF-06 | Physical Schema v5 | `case_list_row` was UNIQUE (business_date) and `case_entry_exclusion` was UNIQUE (business_date), which allow one row per day in the whole table rather than one per case account. | Fixed in v5: `case_list_row` is UNIQUE (business_date, case_id, account_no) and `case_entry_exclusion` is UNIQUE (business_date, account_key). Found by RWB-E1-002 and RWB-E1-018 while they were re-based. |
| DEF-07 | Physical Schema v5 | `dp_treatment` was UNIQUE (business_date) and `dp_guarantee_claim` was UNIQUE (business_date), which allow one stage-2 snapshot row per day in the whole table rather than one per treatment or claim. | Fixed in v5: `dp_treatment` is UNIQUE (business_date, treatment_id) and `dp_guarantee_claim` is UNIQUE (business_date, guarantee_claim_id). Found while RWB-E2-006 was checked against `v_ace_credit_decision`. |

DEF-01 to DEF-03 are pre-existing and would have blocked the build at V0001. They are fixed in Physical Schema v5 as part of Wave 1, not by a separate change.

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The ACE team does not accept RWB-ACE-001 or cannot deliver by 21 November | Medium | The 30 November release moves; E1-002, E1-016, E1-018 and the data engine cannot start | DL43 raised on the day of sign-off; a fallback scope of Tier 1 views plus the case list is costed but not recommended |
| R2 | A source is not ingested by ACE after all (AMIS, RPS, LIT, WIN, GL, COLLINS, NLEADS, EasyApp, Entra ID) | Medium | That source reopens U1 and needs a staging table and load in the Workbench | Confirm each source in DL43; the gap list names them one by one |
| R3 | ACE changes a column the views read | Low | A view breaks at deploy | The conformance test runs in the pipeline; the ACE team treats the view list as a contract |
| R4 | The dictionary count changes again after LDM v7 | Medium | D-RCV-29 and E1-001 AC1 disagree | The Wave 1 verify agent re-derives both counts from the same pair before either is signed |
| R5 | Masking in the view is read as a PDPA control on its own | Low | Audit finding | The register states the control is the grant plus E1-037 plus the audit log; Data Classification v4 repeats it |

secs.t:
Recovery Workbench ACE DB alignment tracker v1
SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026.
What this workbook is
The working tracker for the ACE alignment. It holds the per-document edit list, the per-story disposition and the
governance actions. The narrative case for the change is in Recovery Workbench ACE DB Alignment Change Register v1.md.
Status values
Not started - no new-version file exists yet
Drafted - the new-version file exists and the edit log is appended to the register
In review - the data architect or the ACE team lead is reading it
Approved - signed off; the old version may be retired at the next index update
Superseded - the document is replaced by a different document, not a new version
One writer per file
Each row has one owner agent. An agent writes only its own new-version file and returns an edit log. No agent edits a
file another agent owns. Frozen inputs: the change register, the ACE schema dump, the Tier Map, LDM v7 and Physical Schema v5.

U2 | The ACE team owns the new ACE tables and columns | One new story, RWB-ACE-001, lists every new table and column with its field appendix. | Agreed | ACE team lead | Critical path for 30 November.

-- Recovery Workbench ACE source views
-- SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 15 November 2026. Version 1.
-- (C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd
--
-- Purpose: the only read path from the recovery module into the ACE database (D-RCV-35, U4).
-- Boundary rule: the recovery module reads ACE only through recovery.v_ace_* views. No direct
-- table read, no foreign key into a public.* table, no write.
--
-- Two migrations, because a view cannot be created over a table that does not exist yet:
-- Section A Tier 1 views over ACE tables that exist today. Ships with RWB-E1-069 as the next
-- free sequence after the V0001 baseline (D-RCV-28).
-- Section B Tier 2 views over the tables and columns owned by the ACE team (RWB-ACE-001).
-- Ships as a later sequence the week the ACE change lands; until then the Workbench
-- features that need them stay behind their feature flag.
--
-- Grants: SELECT only, and only on the views. The views are owned by a dedicated ACE role
-- (ace_view_owner) that holds SELECT on the ACE tables. The recovery service identity holds SELECT
-- on recovery.v_ace_* and on nothing else, so a direct read of a public table fails at the database,
-- not only in code review. This is the boundary rule, enforced by the catalog.
-- Trade-off recorded for the security review: a view owned by a definer role runs with that role's
-- privileges, so any row-level security ACE adds later must be applied inside the view.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS recovery;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Helper functions. Immutable, no side effects, safe in a view definition.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- ACE stores some dates as text. Accept ISO, YYYYMMDD and DD/MM/YYYY; return NULL on anything else
-- so a dirty source row can never break a Workbench read.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_date(p_text text)
RETURNS date
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE
 WHEN p_text IS NULL OR btrim(p_text) = '' THEN NULL
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN btrim(p_text)::date
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{8}$' THEN to_date(btrim(p_text), 'YYYYMMDD')
 WHEN btrim(p_text) ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN to_date(btrim(p_text), 'DD/MM/YYYY')
 ELSE NULL
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_date(text) IS
 'Converts an ACE text date to date. Returns NULL rather than failing on an unrecognised value.';

-- ACE holds Y/N flags as text.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_boolean(p_text text)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE upper(btrim(coalesce(p_text, '')))
 WHEN 'Y' THEN true
 WHEN 'YES' THEN true
 WHEN 'TRUE' THEN true
 WHEN '1' THEN true
 WHEN 'N' THEN false
 WHEN 'NO' THEN false
 WHEN 'FALSE' THEN false
 WHEN '0' THEN false
 ELSE NULL
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_to_boolean(text) IS
 'Converts an ACE Y/N text flag to boolean. Returns NULL rather than failing.';

-- PDPA masking for display values. Keeps the last four characters.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION recovery.ace_mask_value(p_value text)
RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
 SELECT CASE
 WHEN p_value IS NULL OR btrim(p_value) = '' THEN NULL
 WHEN position('@' in p_value) > 1
 THEN left(p_value, 1) || '***' || substring(p_value from position('@' in p_value))
 WHEN length(p_value) <= 4 THEN repeat('*', length(p_value))
 ELSE repeat('*', length(p_value) - 4) || right(p_value, 4)
 END
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION recovery.ace_mask_value(text) IS
 'PDPA display mask. Keeps the last four characters, or the first character and the domain of an email address.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Section A - Tier 1 views over ACE tables that exist today.
-- Proposed migration: V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql (next free sequence at merge).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- A1. Loan account. The Workbench account row, with product, branch and the ACE batch date.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_account
AS
SELECT
 a.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 a.account_code::varchar(255) AS account_code,
 a.account_name::varchar(255) AS account_name,
 a.account_status::varchar(255) AS account_status,
 a.account_status_date AS account_status_date,
 a.contract_number::varchar(255) AS contract_no,
 a.contract_date AS contract_date,
 a.product_key::varchar(255) AS product_key,
 p.product_type::varchar(255) AS product_type,
 p.product_category::varchar(255) AS product_category,
 p.product_category_efs::varchar(255) AS product_category_efs,
 a.current_branch::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 b.branch_name::varchar(255) AS branch_name,
 a.oc_code::varchar(255) AS oc_code,
 a.company_code::varchar(255) AS company_code,
 a.collection_officer::varchar(255) AS collection_officer,
 a.collection_phase::varchar(255) AS collection_phase,
 a.delay_days AS days_past_due,
 a.loan_classification::varchar(255) AS classification,
 a.total_balance AS total_balance,
 a.accounting_balance AS accounting_balance,
 a.past_due_amount AS past_due_amount,
 a.total_interest_fin_charge AS total_interest_fin_charge,
 a.collections_fee AS collections_fee,
 a.interest_rate::numeric(7,4) AS interest_rate,
 a.last_payment_date AS last_payment_date,
 a.last_payment_amount AS last_payment_amount,
 a.next_installment_date AS next_installment_date,
 a.next_installment_amount AS next_installment_amount,
 a.last_tdr_date AS last_tdr_date,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(a.is_restructured) AS tdr_flag,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(a.is_rescheduled) AS rescheduled_flag,
 a.number_reschedules AS number_reschedules,
 a.tdr_aging AS tdr_aging,
 a.principle_not_reduce::varchar(255) AS principle_not_reduce,
 a.core_banking_system_date AS data_as_of,
 a.days_since_last_contact AS days_since_last_contact,
 a.days_since_last_collection_activity AS days_since_last_collection_activity,
 a.rm_name::varchar(255) AS relationship_manager,
 a.rm_phone_number::varchar(255) AS relationship_manager_phone,
 a.special_memo::varchar(255) AS special_memo,
 a.expiry_date AS expiry_date
FROM public.account a
LEFT JOIN public.product p ON p.product_key = a.product_key
LEFT JOIN public.branch b ON b.oc_code = a.current_branch;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_account IS
 'ACE account as the Workbench reads it. delay_days maps to days_past_due; core_banking_system_date is the data_as_of.';

-- A2. Payment. pay_date is text in ACE; the view casts it and never fails on a bad value.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_payment
AS
SELECT
 p.pay_key::varchar(255) AS payment_code,
 p.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 recovery.ace_to_date(p.pay_date) AS payment_date,
 p.total_amount AS payment_amount,
 p.capital_amount::varchar(255) AS capital_amount,
 p.payinterest::varchar(255) AS interest_amount,
 p.payexpenses::varchar(255) AS expense_amount,
 p.paycommission::varchar(255) AS commission_amount,
 p.pay_type::varchar(255) AS payment_channel,
 p.description::varchar(255) AS description,
 p.comments::varchar(255) AS comments,
 a.core_banking_system_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.payment p
LEFT JOIN public.account a ON a.account_key = p.account_key;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_payment IS
 'ACE payment as the Workbench reads it. pay_date is varchar in ACE, cast to date by ace_to_date.';

-- A3. Customer. The identity number is never exposed in clear: last four only.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_customer
AS
SELECT
 c.person_key::varchar(255) AS cif_no,
 c.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 c.first_name::varchar(255) AS first_name,
 c.surname::varchar(255) AS last_name,
 c.birth_date AS date_of_birth,
 c.deceased_date AS deceased_date,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(c.is_deceased) AS deceased_flag,
 c.gender::varchar(255) AS gender,
 c.nationality::varchar(255) AS nationality,
 c.marital_status::varchar(255) AS marital_status,
 c.occupation::varchar(255) AS occupation,
 c.spouse_name::varchar(255) AS spouse_name,
 c.status::varchar(255) AS customer_status,
 c.category::varchar(255) AS category,
 c.country_of_residence::varchar(255) AS country_of_residence,
 recovery.ace_to_boolean(c.is_staff) AS is_staff,
 c.branch::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 c.vat_number::varchar(255) AS vat_number,
 recovery.ace_mask_value(c.identification_number) AS id_no_masked,
 right(coalesce(c.identification_number, ''), 4) AS id_no_last4
FROM public.customer c;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_customer IS
 'ACE customer as the Workbench reads it. identification_number is masked in the view; the clear value is never exposed.';

-- A4. Contact points. Phone, email and address in one view, with a type and a display mask.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_contact
AS
SELECT
 'PHONE'::varchar(10) AS contact_type,
 ('PHONE:' || ph.phone_key)::varchar(255) AS contact_key,
 ph.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 ph.phone_number::varchar(256) AS contact_value,
 recovery.ace_mask_value(ph.phone_number) AS contact_value_masked,
 ph.contact_usage::varchar(255) AS usage_code,
 NULL::varchar(255) AS city,
 NULL::varchar(20) AS post_code,
 NULL::varchar(255) AS country
FROM public.phone ph
UNION ALL
SELECT
 'EMAIL'::varchar(10),
 ('EMAIL:' || em.email_key)::varchar(255),
 em.person_key::varchar(255),
 em.email::varchar(256),
 recovery.ace_mask_value(em.email),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 NULL::varchar(20),
 NULL::varchar(255)
FROM public.email em
UNION ALL
SELECT
 'ADDRESS'::varchar(10),
 ('ADDRESS:' || ad.address_key)::varchar(255),
 ad.person_key::varchar(255),
 ad.address::varchar(256),
 recovery.ace_mask_value(ad.address),
 NULL::varchar(255),
 ad.city::varchar(255),
 ad.zip_code::varchar(20),
 ad.country::varchar(255)
FROM public.address ad;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_contact IS
 'ACE phone, email and address as one contact-point view. contact_value is the full value notices and calls need; contact_value_masked is for display (E1-037).';

-- A5. Customer to account relations. Borrower, guarantor, co-borrower and related roles.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_ca_relation
AS
SELECT
 r.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 r.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 r.relation_type::varchar(255) AS relation_type,
 r.amount_of_guarantee AS amount_of_guarantee,
 r.date_of_guarantee AS date_of_guarantee
FROM public.ca_relation r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_ca_relation IS
 'ACE customer-account relation: who is borrower, guarantor or co-borrower on which account.';

-- A6. Account to account relations. Parent and child accounts for grouped facilities.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_aa_relation
AS
SELECT
 r.parent_account_key::varchar(255) AS parent_account_key,
 r.child_account_key::varchar(255) AS child_account_key
FROM public.aa_relation r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_aa_relation IS
 'ACE account-account relation, used to group a facility with its sub-accounts.';

-- A7. Collateral. The ACE collateral link with the asset it points at.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral
AS
SELECT
 col.asset_key::varchar(255) AS collateral_no,
 col.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 col.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 col.collateral_value AS collateral_value,
 col.register_date AS register_date,
 col.in_active AS in_active,
 ast.asset_type::varchar(255) AS collateral_type,
 ast.description::varchar(1000) AS description
FROM public.collateral col
LEFT JOIN public.asset ast ON ast.asset_key = col.asset_key;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral IS
 'ACE collateral and the asset behind it. One row per account-collateral-asset link.';

-- A8. Asset. The collateral asset record.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_asset
AS
SELECT
 ast.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_ref,
 ast.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 ast.asset_type::varchar(255) AS asset_type,
 ast.description::varchar(1000) AS description,
 ast.address::varchar(255) AS address,
 ast.town::varchar(255) AS town,
 ast.zipcode::varchar(255) AS post_code,
 ast.county::varchar(255) AS county,
 ast.country::varchar(255) AS country
FROM public.asset ast;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_asset IS
 'ACE asset as the Workbench reads it, for collateral and for a held asset.';

-- A9. Collections activity. The EFS action log ACE already ingests.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action
AS
SELECT
 e.action_id::varchar(255) AS efs_record_key,
 e.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 e.customer_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 e.action_code::varchar(255) AS action_code,
 e.action_code_name::varchar(255) AS action_code_name,
 e.action_date AS action_date,
 e.action_timestamp AS contact_at,
 e.user_code::varchar(255) AS user_code,
 e.comments::varchar(2000) AS comments,
 e.is_call AS is_call,
 e.is_rpc AS is_rpc,
 e.is_ptp AS is_ptp,
 e.promise_status::varchar(100) AS promise_status,
 e.promise_eval_status::varchar(100) AS promise_eval_status,
 e.settlement_due_date AS promise_date,
 e.settle_total_amount AS promise_amount,
 e.collection_phase::varchar(100) AS collection_phase,
 e.act_date_bucket AS act_date_bucket,
 e.act_date_past_due_days AS act_date_past_due_days,
 e.last_tdr_date AS last_tdr_date
FROM public.efs_action e;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action IS
 'ACE EFS action log. Replaces the collections_history copy; action_timestamp maps to contact_at.';

-- A10. Action code reference. The list of values behind the collections action code.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action_code
AS
SELECT
 c.action_code::varchar(255) AS action_code,
 c.description::varchar(255) AS action_name,
 c.category::varchar(100) AS category
FROM public.efs_action_code c;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_action_code IS
 'ACE EFS action code reference. The loaded LIST-ACTION-CODE list (1,106 values) reads this.';

-- A11. Assignment history. Which officer or agency held the account, and when.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_assignment
AS
SELECT
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.assignment_scheme::varchar(255) AS assignment_scheme,
 s.assignee_code::varchar(255) AS assignee_code,
 s.assignee_name::varchar(255) AS assignee_name,
 s.assignment_start_date AS assignment_start_date,
 s.assignment_end_date AS assignment_end_date,
 s.assignment_start_total_balance AS assignment_start_total_balance,
 s.assignment_end_total_balance AS assignment_end_total_balance,
 s.distribution_area::varchar(255) AS distribution_area
FROM public.efs_assignment s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_efs_assignment IS
 'ACE assignment history, used for hand-over and agency performance.';

-- A12. Monthly bucket history. The daily bucket is an ACE-new column (RWB-ACE-001).
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_bucket_log
AS
SELECT
 a.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 b.snapshot_year AS snapshot_year,
 b.snapshot_month AS snapshot_month,
 b.bucket AS bucket,
 b.past_due_amount AS past_due_amount,
 make_date(b.snapshot_year, b.snapshot_month, 1) AS snapshot_month_start
FROM public.bucket_log_snapshot b
JOIN public.account a ON a.id = b.account_id;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_bucket_log IS
 'ACE monthly bucket snapshot, keyed by account_key. bucket is the month-end bucket, not the daily bucket.';

-- A13. Product reference.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_product
AS
SELECT
 p.product_key::varchar(255) AS product_code,
 p.description::varchar(255) AS product_name,
 p.product_type::varchar(255) AS product_type,
 p.product_category::varchar(255) AS product_category,
 p.product_category_efs::varchar(255) AS product_category_efs
FROM public.product p;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_product IS
 'ACE product reference, used for the product and product group lists of values.';

-- A14. Branch reference.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_branch
AS
SELECT
 br.oc_code::varchar(255) AS branch_code,
 br.branch_name::varchar(255) AS branch_name,
 br.address::varchar(255) AS address,
 br.phone::varchar(255) AS phone
FROM public.branch br;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_branch IS
 'ACE branch reference, used for the branch and region lists of values.';

-- A15. Bank of Thailand holidays. Replaces the Workbench HOLIDAY reference list.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_holiday
AS
SELECT
 h.holiday_date AS holiday_date,
 h.holiday_year AS holiday_year,
 h.holiday_description::varchar(255) AS holiday_name,
 h.holiday_description_thai::varchar(255) AS holiday_name_thai,
 h.holiday_weekday::varchar(20) AS holiday_weekday
FROM public.bot_holiday h;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_holiday IS
 'ACE Bank of Thailand holiday calendar. E1-043 and E1-045 read this instead of a Workbench list.';

-- A16. Restructure plan. The ACE case plus its TDR calculation and recommended plan.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_plan
AS
SELECT
 ac.case_business_id::varchar(255) AS plan_ref,
 ac.id AS ace_case_id,
 ac.current_station_name::varchar(255) AS plan_status,
 ac.created_timestamp AS plan_created_at,
 tc.id AS tdr_calculation_id,
 tc.published_timestamp AS plan_published_at,
 tdr.associated_account_id AS associated_account_id,
 acc.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 tdr.plan_setup_completed_timestamp AS booked_at,
 tdr.approval_completed_timestamp AS approved_at,
 tdr.submitted_for_approval_timestamp AS submitted_at,
 tdr.closed_timestamp AS closed_at,
 tdr.closed_reason::varchar(255) AS closed_reason,
 tdr.ca_approved_timestamp AS ca_approved_at,
 rec.months AS installments,
 rec.installment AS recommended_installment,
 rec.package_type::varchar(255) AS recommended_package,
 coalesce(tdr.approval_completed_timestamp, tdr.submitted_for_approval_timestamp, ac.created_timestamp)
 AS plan_status_as_of
FROM public.ace_case ac
LEFT JOIN public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case tdr ON tdr.id = ac.id
LEFT JOIN public.account acc ON acc.id = tdr.associated_account_id
LEFT JOIN public.tdr_calculation tc ON tc.case_id = tdr.id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
 SELECT r.months, r.installment, r.package_type
 FROM public.ai_recommended_plan r
 WHERE r.case_id = tdr.id
 ORDER BY r.rank
 LIMIT 1
) rec ON true;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_plan IS
 'ACE restructure case, its TDR calculation and the top-ranked recommended plan. Replaces the plan fields the Workbench used to copy.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Section B - Tier 2 views. These depend on RWB-ACE-001 and are applied only when the ACE
-- change is live. Until then the dependent Workbench features stay behind their flags.
-- Proposed migration: the next free sequence after RWB-ACE-001 is deployed.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- B1. Batch completion and business date per source. The Workbench freshness stamp reads this.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status
AS
SELECT
 r.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 r.business_date AS business_date,
 r.started_at AS started_at,
 r.completed_at AS completed_at,
 r.status::varchar(12) AS status,
 r.record_count AS record_count,
 r.checksum::varchar(64) AS checksum,
 r.feed_version::varchar(20) AS feed_version,
 (r.status = 'COMPLETED') AS is_complete
FROM public.ace_batch_run r;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status IS
 'Per-source ACE batch completion and business date. The Workbench freshness stamp (E1-015) reads this.';

-- B2. Valuation. SVAF appraisals, held in ACE after RWB-ACE-001.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_valuation
AS
SELECT
 v.valuation_key::varchar(255) AS valuation_key,
 v.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 v.appraisal_no::varchar(20) AS appraisal_no,
 v.appraisal_type::varchar(15) AS appraisal_type,
 v.appraised_value AS appraised_value,
 v.forced_sale_value AS forced_sale_value,
 v.appraisal_date AS appraisal_date,
 v.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 v.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.valuation v;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_valuation IS
 'SVAF appraisal as ingested into ACE. Accepted, stale and valuer fields stay in recovery.valuation_ext.';

-- B3. Collateral detail from CCMS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral_detail
AS
SELECT
 d.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 d.title_doc_no::varchar(40) AS title_doc_no,
 d.plot_no::varchar(20) AS plot_no,
 d.area_text::varchar(20) AS area_text,
 d.province::varchar(40) AS province,
 d.district::varchar(60) AS district,
 d.subdistrict::varchar(60) AS subdistrict,
 d.insured_value AS insured_value,
 d.insurance_expiry AS insurance_expiry,
 d.lien_rank AS lien_rank,
 d.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 d.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.collateral_detail d;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_collateral_detail IS
 'CCMS collateral detail as ingested into ACE: title deed, plot, area, location, insurance and lien rank.';

-- B4. NPA asset from AMIS and RPS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_asset
AS
SELECT
 n.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_ref,
 n.asset_key::varchar(255) AS asset_key,
 n.asset_code::varchar(20) AS asset_code,
 n.transfer_in_type::varchar(20) AS transfer_in_type,
 n.from_segment::varchar(20) AS from_segment,
 n.transfer_in_date AS transfer_in_date,
 n.book_value AS book_value,
 n.auction_purchase_price AS auction_purchase_price,
 n.repossessed_date AS repossessed_date,
 n.stock_date AS stock_date,
 n.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 n.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.npa_asset n;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_asset IS
 'NPA asset from AMIS (property) and RPS (vehicles), as ingested into ACE.';

-- B5. NPA asset sale from AMIS.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_sale
AS
SELECT
 s.npa_sale_key::varchar(255) AS npa_sale_key,
 s.npa_asset_key::varchar(255) AS npa_asset_key,
 s.contract_date AS contract_date,
 s.sale_date AS sale_date,
 s.sale_price AS sale_price,
 s.transfer_fee AS transfer_fee,
 s.specific_business_tax AS specific_business_tax,
 s.corporate_income_tax AS corporate_income_tax,
 s.incentive_amount AS incentive_amount,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.npa_sale s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_npa_sale IS
 'NPA sale contract and its taxes and fees, from AMIS, as ingested into ACE.';

-- B6. Lawsuit from LIT.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_lawsuit
AS
SELECT
 l.lawsuit_key::varchar(255) AS lawsuit_key,
 l.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 l.lawsuit_no::varchar(30) AS lawsuit_no,
 l.black_case_no::varchar(30) AS black_case_no,
 l.red_case_no::varchar(30) AS red_case_no,
 l.court_name::varchar(120) AS court_name,
 l.claim_amount AS claim_amount,
 l.filed_date AS filed_date,
 l.judgment_date AS judgment_date,
 l.judgment_amount AS judgment_amount,
 l.lit_status::varchar(200) AS lit_status,
 l.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 l.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.lawsuit l;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_lawsuit IS
 'LIT lawsuit as ingested into ACE: case numbers, court, claim, judgment and status.';

-- B7. Hearing from LIT.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_hearing
AS
SELECT
 h.hearing_key::varchar(255) AS hearing_key,
 h.lawsuit_key::varchar(255) AS lawsuit_key,
 h.hearing_date AS hearing_date,
 h.hearing_type::varchar(20) AS hearing_type,
 h.next_date AS next_date,
 h.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 h.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.hearing h;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_hearing IS
 'LIT court hearing as ingested into ACE.';

-- B8. Proof of delivery from WIN.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_pod
AS
SELECT
 w.pod_key::varchar(255) AS pod_key,
 w.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 w.notice_ref::varchar(60) AS notice_ref,
 w.sent_date AS sent_date,
 w.barcode::varchar(40) AS barcode,
 w.callback_date AS callback_date,
 w.delivery_status::varchar(15) AS delivery_status,
 w.sent_type::varchar(10) AS sent_type,
 w.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 w.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.pod_receipt w;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_pod IS
 'WIN proof of delivery as ingested into ACE. The notice itself stays in recovery.notice.';

-- B9. Write-off from GL.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_write_off
AS
SELECT
 g.write_off_key::varchar(255) AS write_off_key,
 g.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 g.amount AS amount,
 g.posted_date AS posted_date,
 g.responsibility_center::varchar(10) AS responsibility_center,
 g.cost_center::varchar(10) AS cost_center,
 g.gl_product::varchar(10) AS gl_product,
 g.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 g.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.gl_write_off g;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_write_off IS
 'GL write-off posting as ingested into ACE. The write-off decision stays in recovery.write_off.';

-- B10. COLLINS score.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_score
AS
SELECT
 s.score_key::varchar(255) AS score_key,
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.model_code::varchar(30) AS model_code,
 s.model_version::varchar(20) AS model_version,
 s.score_value AS score_value,
 s.estimate_value AS estimate_value,
 s.route_code::varchar(4) AS route_code,
 s.scored_at AS scored_at,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.collins_score s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_score IS
 'COLLINS score and route estimate as ingested into ACE, if ACE does not already hold it.';

-- B11. Party product from SCBPDM.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_party_product
AS
SELECT
 pp.person_key::varchar(255) AS person_key,
 pp.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_no,
 pp.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 pp.product_type::varchar(20) AS product_type,
 pp.product_status::varchar(15) AS product_status,
 pp.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.party_product pp;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_party_product IS
 'SCBPDM customer product holding as ingested into ACE. Replaces the Workbench party_product copy.';

-- B12. NLEADS credit decision.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_credit_decision
AS
SELECT
 d.credit_decision_key::varchar(255) AS credit_decision_key,
 d.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 d.nleads_ref::varchar(30) AS nleads_ref,
 d.credit_result::varchar(10) AS credit_result,
 d.credit_result_reason::varchar(1000) AS credit_result_reason,
 d.decided_at AS decided_at,
 d.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 d.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.credit_decision d;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_credit_decision IS
 'NLEADS credit approval as ingested into ACE. Replaces the four credit fields the Workbench used to record by hand.';

-- B13. EasyApp signature request.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_esign
AS
SELECT
 s.esign_key::varchar(255) AS esign_key,
 s.account_key::varchar(255) AS account_key,
 s.external_ref::varchar(60) AS external_ref,
 s.requested_at AS requested_at,
 s.status::varchar(20) AS status,
 s.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 s.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.esign_request s;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_esign IS
 'EasyApp signature request as ingested into ACE. The Workbench document still owns the signed file.';

-- B14. Entra ID group to role mapping.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW recovery.v_ace_iam_group
AS
SELECT
 g.entra_group::varchar(120) AS entra_group,
 g.role_code::varchar(20) AS role_code,
 g.source_system::varchar(20) AS source_system,
 g.business_date AS data_as_of
FROM public.iam_group g;

COMMENT ON VIEW recovery.v_ace_iam_group IS
 'Entra ID group to Workbench role mapping as ingested into ACE. ACE performs the sign-in, so it owns the mapping.';

-- CREATE ROLE :recovery_role NOLOGIN;

-- REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC;
-- No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on any table, and no SELECT on a public table
-- is granted to :recovery_role.

-- 1. Every view in recovery whose name starts with v_ace_ compiles.
-- 2. No constraint in schema recovery references a table outside schema recovery.
