REQ-DRI-013.t: Case hand-over from EFS arrives in the COLLINS daily load, and plan status is read from the ACE common module, so a case is current the morning after it changes. — Must — Data steward and data product owner

REQ-ACA-011.t: Joiner, mover and leaver changes reach the Workbench so that access matches the current organization. — Must — Security administrator

REQ-ACA-012.t: Partner users reach the Workbench only through the external gateway, with multi-factor authentication, scoped to their own cases. — Must — Security administrator

REQ-CHO-001.t: A case transferred from collections reaches the Workbench on the day of transfer, with its full contact and promise history read from ACE through the EFS views. Case transferred from EFS is a named same-day trigger under DL06. — Must — Business lead — E2

REQ-CHO-002.t: A change to a restructure plan status in ACE is visible on the case through the ACE common module. — Must — Data steward and data product owner — E2

REQ-CHO-003.t: Customer, product and account facts reach the case from ACE, which ingests them from SCBPDM and the core bank, read through v_ace_customer, v_ace_party_product and v_ace_account (DL20 as amended by D-RCV-35). — Must — Solution architect — E2

REQ-CHO-004.t: The hand-over point is one agreed number of days past due, used by every rule and every report. — Must — Risk with the ACE team — E2

REQ-CHO-005.t: The Workbench is the system of record for case state after hand-over. — Must — Solution architect — E2

REQ-CHO-006.t: A treatment record exists for every offer made to a customer, holding its type, terms, approval and outcome. — Must — Business lead — E2

REQ-CHO-007.t: Plan timers run from the treatment record, and a missed payment raises an event. — Must — Business lead — E2

REQ-CHO-008.t: A plan submitted for credit approval and terms booked in the core system are recorded on the case, and the booking is confirmed from the next business date's ACE account data in v_ace_account. — Must — Data steward and data product owner — E2

REQ-CHO-009.t: Payments received, read from ACE through v_ace_payment, are matched to the plan, the settlement or the fee they belong to by the ACE payment_code, and anything unmatched goes to an exception list. — Must — Autonomous Ops — E2

REQ-CHO-010.t: A duplicate case for the same customer and product, by ACE person_key and product, merges into the earlier case, carrying its documents and decision log. — Should — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-001.t: A case owner sees their own queue with ageing and service level state. — Must — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-002.t: A team manager sees every queue in their team, filters by status, product and ageing, and exports the view. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-003.t: A case is transferred or reassigned manually only with a reason code from the agreed list. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-004.t: A case that breaches its service level is visible to the named escalation role without the case moving. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-005.t: Timers, escalation state and the deviation flag are visible on the case record view. — Must — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-006.t: Queue counts, ageing and breaches are reported daily and reconcile to the case list. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-007.t: An owner who leaves, is absent beyond the threshold or breaches the caseload cap has their cases reallocated inside the team, keeping the state and the clocks. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-008.t: Queue and transfer history is visible on the case so that a reader sees where the case has been. — Must — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-009.t: A steering dashboard reports volume, ageing, route mix, turnaround and recovery against the baseline. — Must — Tribe lead — E2

REQ-WKM-011.t: Work allocated to a partner is visible in the same queue view as internal work. — Should — Partner and agency manager — E2

REQ-WKM-012.t: Every open case carries one next action: what has to happen, who owns it and the date it is due. — Must — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-013.t: The next action is produced from the rule that moved the case, taking the action, the owner of the next state and the timer that rule already carries. It is not entered by hand as a matter of course. — Must — Center of excellence — E2

REQ-WKM-014.t: The next action is visible to whoever picks the case up, on the case record and in every queue view, without opening the history. — Must — Case owner — E2

REQ-WKM-015.t: A next action that passes its due date raises the same escalation as any other service level breach, and the case does not move. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-WKM-016.t: A case with no next action is reported as an exception, because a case nobody owes anything on is the state this program exists to remove. — Must — Team manager — E2

REQ-APD-001.t: A decision that needs approval is routed to the approver named by the delegation of authority table for that decision, product and amount. — Must — Risk with Credit

REQ-APD-002.t: An approver sees the recommendation, the reasons behind it, the inputs used and the limit that applies, on one screen. — Must — Business lead

REQ-APD-003.t: An approver can accept, change, reject or return the item with a question, and each outcome is recorded. — Must — Business lead

REQ-APD-004.t: A request above the approver's limit is refused and raised to the next approver in the matrix, with no silent approval. — Must — Risk

REQ-APD-005.t: An override of a recommendation needs a coded reason, and the reason is reported monthly. — Must — Center of excellence

REQ-APD-006.t: Demand and recall notices are approved through this path as the first use of approval routing. — Must — Legal counsel

REQ-APD-007.t: An approval that is not answered inside its service level escalates to the named role. — Must — Team manager

REQ-APD-008.t: A committee decision is recorded against the item with the members present and the decision taken. — Must — Business lead

REQ-APD-009.t: The limit, the rule version and the approver are written to the decision log with every approval. — Must — Center of excellence

REQ-APD-010.t: A change to the delegation of authority table is versioned, approved and dated, and open items keep the version they were decided under. — Must — Risk — E2

REQ-APD-011.t: Approval routing works with no person available in a role, by escalating rather than stalling. — Should — Team manager

REQ-DVH-001.t: Deviations X1 to X7 are detected by rule from case data, call notes, documents and external flags. — Must — Center of excellence

REQ-DVH-002.t: A deviation pauses the stage clock, keeps the prescription clock running, and does not replace the case state. — Must — Business lead

REQ-DVH-003.t: Each deviation code routes to its named owner, and a code with no owner routes to the team manager and is recorded as unmapped. — Must — Center of excellence

REQ-DVH-004.t: Contact stops apply automatically for a dispute or complaint, a vulnerable or hardship case, and a deceased customer. — Must — Compliance

REQ-DVH-005.t: A resolved deviation returns the case to the state it paused in, or to the route decision where the outcome changes the route. — Must — Case owner

REQ-DVH-006.t: A deviation flag is visible on the case record view and in every queue view. — Must — Case owner

REQ-DVH-007.t: A complaint is matched to the contact that preceded it. — Must — Conduct and QA officer

REQ-DVH-009.t: A bankruptcy or external seizure stops direct collection and starts the claim deadline clock. — Must — Legal counsel

REQ-DVH-010.t: A fraud flag refers the case to the fraud team and holds recovery action until it is confirmed or cleared. — Must — Fraud

REQ-OCC-003.t: Letters are dispatched for print and post, and proof of delivery returns to the case. — Must — Autonomous Ops

REQ-OCC-004.t: Messages are sent by SMS and LINE through the bank's channel platforms, with the result recorded on the case. — Must — Autonomous Ops

REQ-OCC-005.t: Every outbound contact carries a conduct check result, and a contact that fails the check is held. — Must — Conduct and QA officer

REQ-OCC-006.t: A customer who withdraws consent for a channel stops receiving on that channel, and statutory notices continue. — Must — Compliance

REQ-OCC-008.t: The case record view carries a history timeline showing every state change, transfer, contact, document and decision in order. — Must — Case owner

REQ-OCC-009.t: A customer signs an agreement electronically where Legal permits it, and by wet ink where Legal requires it. — Must — Legal counsel

REQ-OCC-010.t: A new verified contact point updates the contact data and clears a lost contact deviation. — Must — Case owner

REQ-ILG-009.t: Contact outcomes from collections reach the ledger, so that contactability found before day 90 is not lost at hand-over. — Must — The data lead with the business lead

REQ-ILG-010.t: Letters, messages and calls dispatched by the Workbench write their result to the ledger, including proof of delivery where it returns. — Must — Autonomous Ops

REQ-ILG-011.t: A hand-over to or from a partner writes to the ledger, naming who held the case, who holds it now, and when. — Must — Partner and agency manager

REQ-ILG-012.t: The case record view shows the ledger as an ordered timeline. — Must — Case owner

REQ-ILG-013.t: Ledger entries carry their own retention class, set independently of the decision log. — Must — Compliance

NFR-032.t: Under D-RCV-35 (U5), retired local files and Excel and SharePoint trackers are handled through the Cutover and Go Live Plan, which keeps each as a read-only archive at a recorded location. The Workbench loads and holds no tracker. — Archive location recorded per file in the Cutover and Go Live Plan — Solution architect — Proposed

REQ-WKM-010.t: A capacity view shows inflow by product, bucket and region against available capacity. — Could — Capacity and workforce planner — E7

REQ-ACA-013.t: Full administration screens for roles, permissions and delegation are available to the security administrator. — Should — Security administrator — E8

REQ-OCC-011.t: Customer self-service for an offer, a signature, a payment and a dispute is available on the bank's digital channels. — Should — Business lead — E4

REQ-S1-001.t: An appraisal older than the policy limit triggers a new valuation order without a person asking for it. — Must — Sale officer — E4

REQ-S1-002.t: A valuation that is an outlier against the market and the last value is flagged before it is accepted. — Must — Sale officer — E4

REQ-S1-003.t: The expected return by route is available for every case at the route decision. — Must — Center of excellence — E4

REQ-S1-004.t: The payoff amount and the settlement range are calculated by rule from current balances. — Must — Center of excellence — E4

REQ-S1-005.t: The route recommendation names the option, the reasons, the confidence and the alternatives considered. — Must — Business lead — E4

REQ-S1-006.t: The route decision is approved inside the delegation of authority, and above the limit it reaches the committee. — Must — Credit approval committee — E4

REQ-S1-007.t: A route decision starts the route flow and sets its timers in the same step. — Must — Business lead — E4

REQ-S1-008.t: A change in the exposure band, the valuation or the classification after a route decision triggers a fresh decision. — Should — Case owner — E4

REQ-S2-001.t: A restructure proposed in the collections system reaches the restructuring officer with the case, and the case does not leave the Workbench. — Must — Restructuring officer — E3

REQ-S2-002.t: An offer to a customer carries a validity period, and expiry returns the case to the status it came from. — Must — Restructuring officer — E3

REQ-S2-003.t: A signed offer routes to operations for booking, and an unsigned or declined offer returns the case to its prior status. — Must — Restructuring officer — E3

REQ-S2-004.t: Settlement terms are negotiated inside a rule-set range, and anything outside the range needs approval. — Must — Product head — E3

REQ-S2-005.t: Deed in lieu readiness, including the encumbrance check and an early valuation, is established before negotiation starts. — Must — Sale officer — E3

REQ-S2-006.t: The credit application, contract and mortgage documents for a deed in lieu are generated from templates. — Must — Legal counsel — E3

REQ-S2-007.t: An asset accepted under a deed in lieu is unlocked as a non performing asset by rule, with exceptions summarized for the approver. — Must — NPA and asset manager — E3

REQ-S2-008.t: Booked terms, settled accounts and released collateral are posted to their systems of record without re-keying. — Must — Credit Administration — E3

REQ-S2-009.t: A broken plan raises an event and returns the case to a decision rather than leaving it in a plan state. — Must — Case owner — E3

REQ-S2-010.t: Buyback rental, auto-debit, receipts and arrears follow-up run without a person for a standard arrangement. — Should — NPA and asset manager — E3

REQ-S3-001.t: A guarantee claim is prepared from case data and submitted inside the guarantor's deadline. — Must — Guarantee officer — E4

REQ-S3-002.t: Claim status, payment and any shortfall are recorded on the case. — Must — Guarantee officer — E4

REQ-S3-003.t: A guarantee payment that clears the balance closes the case and records the subrogation position. — Must — Guarantee officer — E4

REQ-S3-004.t: Guarantor and co-borrower notices are generated by rule and sent on the same path as customer notices. — Must — Case owner — E4

REQ-S3-005.t: A guarantor who answers a demand enters the same treatment paths as a borrower. — Must — Case owner — E4

REQ-S3-006.t: A rejected or reduced claim raises a reason and routes the residual to the next decision. — Must — Guarantee officer — E4

REQ-S3-007.t: Claims are filtered for eligibility before submission so that ineligible claims are not filed. — Should — Guarantee officer — E4

REQ-S4-001.t: Demand and recall notices are generated by rule, approved, dispatched, and their notice periods are timed. — Must — Legal counsel — E5

REQ-S4-002.t: A litigation pack is assembled and checked against the document checklist, and missing documents are requested. — Must — Litigation officer — E5

REQ-S4-003.t: The litigation officer verifies the pack against the defect list before filing is approved. — Must — Litigation officer — E5

REQ-S4-004.t: A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E5

REQ-S4-005.t: Court state, hearing dates, deadlines and fees are tracked on the case without a person reading an email. — Must — Litigation officer — E5

REQ-S4-006.t: Settlement before judgment, an appeal and fee payment each need approval inside the delegation. — Must — Head of Litigation — E5

REQ-S4-007.t: Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement. — Must — Enforcement owner — E5

REQ-S4-008.t: A deferred enforcement step carries a coded reason and a review date. — Must — Enforcement owner — E5

REQ-S4-009.t: Prescription warnings force a litigation review ahead of every other open action on the case. — Must — Litigation officer — E5

REQ-S4-010.t: Proceeds from enforcement are matched to the case and posted. — Must — Credit Administration — E5

REQ-S5-001.t: Every repossessed or surrendered asset is recorded with its source, date taken in, holding cost and provision step. — Must — NPA and asset manager — E3

REQ-S5-002.t: The non performing asset stock balance has one named owner and is reported monthly. — Must — Head of NPA — E3

REQ-S5-003.t: Holding age drives re-appraisal and the provision step by rule. — Must — NPA and asset manager — E3

REQ-S5-004.t: A start price and a floor price are proposed for every asset, and the floor is approved by the named role. — Must — Head of NPA — E3

REQ-S5-005.t: Listings are published to the bank's channel and the auction portal from one action. — Must — Sale officer — E3

REQ-S5-006.t: Auction rounds run down the price ladder to the floor, and a round with no bid re-lists by rule. — Must — Sale officer — E4

REQ-S5-007.t: A price below the floor needs a second signature. — Must — Head of NPA — E4

REQ-S5-008.t: Title transfer is prepared and recorded for vehicles and for property. — Must — Sale officer — E4

REQ-S5-009.t: Proceeds are applied to the case and any residual routes to the next decision or closes the case. — Must — Credit Administration — E4

REQ-S5-010.t: A transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval. — Must — Head of NPA — E4

REQ-S6-001.t: Accounts eligible for sale are selected by rule against the policy cap. — Must — Debt sale officer — E5

REQ-S6-002.t: Lots are built with an estimated price, and the reserve price is approved before the lot is offered. — Must — Head of Asset Liquidity — E5

REQ-S6-003.t: The data room holds a masked data tape, and no unmasked personal data leaves the bank. — Must — Compliance — E5

REQ-S6-004.t: Buyers pass a know your customer, licensing and eligibility check before they bid. — Must — Debt sale officer — E6

REQ-S6-005.t: A buyer who fails the check is given a remediation window and is removed from the panel if it is not met. — Must — Head of Asset Liquidity — E6

REQ-S6-006.t: The award of a lot is approved and recorded with the price achieved against the reserve. — Must — Head of Asset Liquidity — E6

REQ-S6-007.t: An account awarded in a lot stops every other open action on its case the same day. — Must — Debt sale officer — E6

REQ-S6-008.t: Data transfer, derecognition and the general ledger posting follow the award without re-keying. — Must — Credit Administration — E6

REQ-S6-009.t: A put-back claim from a buyer is reviewed against the sale terms and either accepted or refused with a reason. — Must — Debt sale officer — E6

REQ-S7-002.t: The committee pack is prepared from case and provision data with no manual assembly. — Must — E6

REQ-S7-003.t: The committee decision to approve, reject or defer is recorded against each account. — Must — E6

REQ-S7-004.t: The write-off exception loop has one named owner and a time limit. — Must — E6

REQ-S7-005.t: Approved write-offs post to the core system and the general ledger, the provision is released, and completeness is published. — Must — Credit Administration — E6

REQ-S7-006.t: Post charge-off treatment is set by rule, including placement with an agency. — Must — Credit Administration — E6

REQ-S7-007.t: Recoveries after charge-off are matched to the account, with income and agency fees recorded. — Must — Credit Administration — E6

REQ-S7-008.t: A case closes after its retention period, and reopening a closed case needs a written rule, a reason and an approver. — Must — Compliance — E6

REQ-DVH-008.t: A death stops all contact, notifies the heirs and the estate, and starts the insurance claim path. — Must — Legal counsel — E3

REQ-DVH-011.t: The full deviation flows with their approvers, contact stops and return points run end to end. — Must — Center of excellence — E7

REQ-S8-001.t: Each of X1 to X7 runs end to end with its own flow, approver, contact rules and return point. — Must — Center of excellence — E7

REQ-S8-002.t: A hardship or vulnerability case follows the contact limits set for it and reaches a hardship or relief decision. — Must — Hardship and vulnerability specialist — E7

REQ-S8-003.t: A complaint is resolved inside its service level and the case returns to the same decision with its timers resumed. — Must — Complaint officer — E7

REQ-S8-004.t: A lost contact case runs skip tracing and returns to a decision whether or not contact is restored. — Must — Case owner — E7

REQ-S8-005.t: A collateral event triggers an insurance claim and a re-appraisal before the next decision. — Must — NPA and asset manager — E7

REQ-S8-006.t: Override and deviation patterns are reviewed monthly by the center of excellence. — Must — Center of excellence — E7

REQ-S8-007.t: A data subject request holds automated processing on the case and routes to Compliance inside the statutory period. — Must — Compliance — E7

REQ-S9-001.t: Every partner type is managed on the same six points: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E6

REQ-S9-002.t: Each partner type has one named owner. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E6

REQ-S9-003.t: Work is allocated to partners by measured return against a scorecard, not by a fixed share. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E6

REQ-S9-004.t: Fees are calculated from the contracted schedule and paid against recorded results. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E6

REQ-S9-005.t: A partner that misses its service level is chased once and then has the work recalled. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E7

REQ-S9-006.t: A partner panel exit, a declared conflict of interest, insolvency or an upheld conduct breach recalls every open case held by that partner. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E7

REQ-S9-007.t: Partner performance, conduct and complaint data are reported to the partner review forum. — Must — Partner and agency manager — E7

REQ-S9-008.t: Partners exchange data through the partner portal and the external gateway, and not by email. — Must — IT lead — E6

REQ-S9-009.t: Field work and its evidence reach the case through the field application. — Should — Partner and agency manager — E7

NFR-001.t: The case store holds one case per customer and product for every account at 90 or more days past due across Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME. — About 23,600 open cases at go-live and 26,500 at the end of 2027, from 3,110 new accounts at 90 days past due a month. Confirmed under DL15 — Risk with the data product owner — Proposed from the volume forecast

NFR-002.t: The system supports the peak number of staff users signed on at once. — About 370 staff online in the busiest hour, of 914 named users — Business lead — Proposed from the volume forecast

NFR-003.t: The system supports the peak number of partner users signed on at once across 73 agencies, 11 to 12 law firms, 4 auction vendors and 35 buyers. — About 50 partner users online in the busiest hour, of about 320 named users — Partner and agency manager — Proposed from the volume forecast

NFR-004.t: The document store holds the annual inbound document volume with its growth rate. — About 860,000 documents in 2027, rising with 15 percent inflow growth a year — Legal with Autonomous Ops — Proposed from the volume forecast

NFR-005.t: The restructure path carries the monthly case volume reaching the Workbench. — About 3,000 restructure accounts a month reach the bank's restructure process today — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-006.t: The deed in lieu path carries its target monthly volume. — 1,000 cases a month in 2027, from 685 today — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-007.t: The decision log holds one record for every decision on every case for the full retention period without degrading query time. — About 36 GB for the decision log and the interaction ledger by the end of 2031; a single case history query under 2 seconds at that size — Compliance with the solution architect — Proposed, DL11

NFR-069.t: The document hub holds the full recovery document estate as a system of record, including every version and every held document, with storage sized for growth. — About 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031, with every version and held document — Solution architect with Compliance — Proposed, DL11

NFR-070.t: The interaction ledger holds every interaction on every open and closed case within its retention period, and reads a single case history inside the user wait. — One case history reads in under 2 seconds with the ledger at its 2031 size — Data lead with the solution architect — Proposed, DL11

NFR-008.t: A screen responds within its target under normal load. — Under 2 seconds — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-009.t: The case record view loads for a case with 50 documents. — Under 2 seconds — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-010.t: An agent returns an answer within its target, after which the rule result is used and the case still routes. — Under 60 seconds — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-011.t: A rule evaluation at a routing decision completes inside the user's wait. — Under 300 milliseconds per rule evaluation at the 95th percentile — Solution architect — Proposed, DL11

NFR-012.t: A search across cases and documents returns within its target. — Under 3 seconds for a search across cases; under 5 seconds across documents — Business lead — Proposed, DL11

NFR-016.t: The document intake pipeline processes its throughput in the test environment. — 500 pages per hour — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-017.t: Document classification is correct on the labeled sample, and anything below the confidence threshold goes to a review queue. — 90 percent correct — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-019.t: The daily rebalancing job completes before the working day starts. — Complete by 07:00 — Team manager — Proposed, DL11

NFR-013.t: Under D-RCV-35 (U1 and U4) and ADR-010, the Workbench reads source data only through the recovery.v_ace_* views, and every case list and decision states the business date and load time of the ACE source batches behind it. — Case list available by 07:00 on the latest completed ACE batch — Solution architect — Proposed, DL43

NFR-014.t: Freshness is read from recovery.v_ace_batch_status, one row per source and business date; a missing, failed or late batch is visible on the case list and alerts the data steward. — Start of day, on the ACE business date (target unchanged) — Solution architect — Proposed, DL43

NFR-015.t: The Workbench holds no load window: a late ACE batch delays the case list and raises an alert rather than starting a Workbench load, catch-up job or staging table. — Visible as soon as the ACE batch completes; no Workbench lag; same-day needs under DL06 — Solution architect — Proposed, DL43

NFR-018.t: The case list reconciles to the ACE account view daily. — No unexplained variance; tolerance under DL25 (target unchanged) — Solution architect — Proposed, DL25

NFR-020.t: The Workbench is available during business hours. — 99.9 percent in business hours — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-021.t: Availability outside business hours, when batch, dispatch and partner exchange run. — 99.5 percent outside business hours, excluding the change window — IT lead — Proposed, DL11

NFR-022.t: Recovery point objective: the maximum data loss the business accepts. — IT lead with Operational Risk — DL11

NFR-023.t: Recovery time objective: the maximum time to restore service. — IT lead with Operational Risk — DL11

NFR-024.t: An agent or model outage falls back to the rule result, and the case still routes. — Fallback always on — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-025.t: A system of record outage queues the outbound action and retries on a schedule, and does not lose it. — Queue and retry — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-026.t: An interface failure after the retry limit moves the item to an exception queue with a task for a named owner. — Three retries per item, then the exception queue — Platform administrator — Proposed, DL11

NFR-027.t: A production release rolls back by redeploying the previous tag. — Rollback by previous tag — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-071.t: Documents in the hub are backed up on a stated schedule, and a restore is tested before the first production release and at each release after it. — IT lead — DL27

NFR-028.t: Every document type carries a retention class, and the class sets how long the document is kept. — Compliance with Legal — DL26

NFR-030.t: The decision log is retained for the period the regulator and internal audit require. — Compliance — DL26

NFR-031.t: Case records carry a retention and archive rule by record class, and a case closes after its retention period. — Compliance — DL26

NFR-072.t: A legal hold stops deletion and expiry for the case or document it covers, for as long as it is in place, overriding the retention class. — Hold overrides retention — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-073.t: An electronic discovery request is answered with every document for a named population, its metadata, its version history and the date each version was created. — Not set as a response time — Legal counsel — Open, DL26

NFR-074.t: A document reaching the end of its retention period is disposed of or extended by a recorded decision, and is never removed silently. — Recorded decision on every disposal — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-075.t: Interaction ledger entries carry their own retention period, set independently of the decision log. — Compliance — DL26

NFR-033.t: Every decision is reproducible from the log, including the rule, model, agent and prompt versions and the inputs used. — Every decision reproducible — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-034.t: Every action carries the rule version applied and the approver who allowed it. — Every action — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-035.t: The decision log hash chain is checked daily, and a break is reported to Compliance the same day. — Daily check, same-day report — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-036.t: An audit or regulatory request is answered inside its deadline with the decision history and the supporting documents. — Inside the deadline set by the requester — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-037.t: Quality assurance reaches first-time-right on case packs and write-off returns. — 90 percent — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-038.t: Every outbound contact carries a conduct check result, and a contact without one is held. — Every contact — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-076.t: A document produced from the hub carries its origin, the date it entered the hub, whether it has been altered since, and who has read it, to the standard a court applies. — Every document produced — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-077.t: A failed write to the interaction ledger raises an incident, and no entry is discarded. — No silent gaps — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-078.t: A model or agent write to a queue is logged with the model or agent version, on the same terms as a decision taken by a person. — Every write — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-039.t: Party identifiers are masked at rest in the case store, and on every screen and every agent call, by role. — Masked at rest and in use — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-040.t: Each screen and each agent receives only the personal data it needs. — Data minimization per screen and per agent — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-041.t: The debt sale data tape is masked before it reaches the data room. — Masked tape — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-042.t: Every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is logged. — Every read — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-043.t: A data subject access, correction or erasure request is answered inside the statutory period. — Statutory period, Not set as a working service level — Compliance — Open, DL26

NFR-044.t: Consent state per channel is held and applied, and statutory notices continue when consent is withdrawn. — Applied on every send — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-045.t: No production data is used in the development environment, and the user acceptance environment uses masked copies. — Synthetic in development, masked in user acceptance — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-046.t: Workbench data stays in the bank's own cloud tenancy in the agreed region. — SCB Azure, Southeast Asia — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-047.t: Every data product and every document type carries a data classification, and the classification sets its handling. — Classification scheme to be applied — Compliance with Security — Open, DL26

NFR-048.t: The approved large language model endpoint is reached over a private endpoint inside the bank's tenancy. — Private endpoint — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-049.t: Staff authenticate with single sign-on and multi-factor authentication. — Entra ID single sign-on with multi-factor — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-050.t: Partner accounts authenticate with multi-factor and are scoped to their own cases. — Multi-factor, scoped — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-051.t: Agents run under service identities and are subject to the same role checks as people. — Service identities — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-052.t: Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts. — No secrets in code or prompts — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-053.t: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. — Encrypted — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-054.t: The build pipeline blocks a change that carries a secret, personal data in code, tests or logs, or an unapproved dependency. — Pipeline checks pass — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-055.t: Agent outputs are schema checked against an allowed-action list with a confidence threshold, and fall back to rules when the check fails. — Schema check on every output — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-056.t: Penetration testing and a security review are completed before the first production release. — Before the first production release and before the partner portal opens to users outside the bank — SCB IT security with the IT lead — Proposed, DL11

NFR-057.t: Document text is read and extracted in Thai and in English. — Thai and English — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-058.t: Customer-facing documents and messages are produced in the customer's language. — Thai by default; English where the customer has chosen English — Legal counsel with Compliance — Proposed, DL10

NFR-059.t: Screen labels, validation messages and error messages are available in Thai and in English. — Every screen, label and message in Thai and English — Business lead — Proposed, DL10

NFR-060.t: Screens meet the bank's accessibility standard. — WCAG 2.1 level AA for every screen — Tech leads with the ACE team — Proposed, DL11

NFR-061.t: Screens work on the browsers and versions the bank supports. — The current and previous major versions of Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome — IT lead — Proposed, DL11

NFR-062.t: The field application captures evidence with no network connection and uploads when it reconnects. — Offline capture — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-063.t: Partner-facing screens work on the devices partners actually use. — Desktop browsers as in NFR-061 and tablets for field and auction partners — Partner and agency manager — Proposed, DL11

NFR-064.t: Logs, traces and metrics are produced across the workflow, the decision service and the agents. — Across all three — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-065.t: Business measures per decision are produced from the decision log and not from a separate count. — From the log — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-066.t: Agent acceptance, override rate, latency and cost are measured and reported. — Measured per agent — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-067.t: Every scheduled job has a run book, monitoring and an alert to the operations channel. — Every job — Solution architect — Proposed

NFR-068.t: A failing interface, job or agent raises an alert to a named owner within its target. — Alert within 15 minutes to the named owner — Platform administrator — Proposed, DL11

AC-ALT-P1-001-02.t: Section B views after RWB-ACE-001 — RWB-ACE-001 is deployed in SIT and public.ace_batch_run, public.valuation and the other 12 new ACE tables exist — the pipeline applies V0003 — the 14 Section B views compile with 127 fields And sys_objects holds 122 rows, 92 tables and 30 views, and sys_fields holds 1,366 rows And the features behind the Section B flag can be switched on

AC-ALT-P1-001-03.t: Extension row written, ACE untouched — person_key "P0000123" exists in v_ace_customer and has no party_ext row — a fraud specialist confirms fraud on the case and the Workbench writes party_ext with fraud_flag true — party_ext holds one row for "P0000123" with fraud_flag true and the seven standard columns And public.customer for "P0000123" is unchanged And no foreign key links party_ext to...

AC-ALT-P1-001-04.t: Type rules in the view — ACE payment "PAY-0001" carries pay_date "20261130" and account "ACC0000017" carries is_restructured "Y" — the developer reads v_ace_payment and v_ace_account — payment_date is the date 2026-11-30 And tdr_flag is true And a pay_date "31-11-2026" returns payment_date NULL without an error

AC-EXC-P1-001-01.t: Failed migration leaves no partial schema — a copy of V0001 in which the statement creating table valuation_ext fails — the pipeline applies it in DEV — the pipeline stage fails and names the failing statement And the recovery schema holds none of the tables of that migration And the Flyway history has no successful row for V0001

AC-EXC-P1-001-02.t: Column without a dictionary entry fails the build — a branch that adds the column account_ext.branch_code with no sys_fields row — the conformance test runs in the pipeline — the test fails with "account_ext.branch_code has no data dictionary entry" And a sys_fields row DF-EXT-028 whose column is changed to type text fails the test with "DF-EXT-028 physical type boolean expected, text found"

AC-EXC-P1-001-03.t: Repeated migration has no effect — V0001 and V0002 already applied in SIT — the pipeline runs again in SIT — Flyway reports both versions as already applied And the row counts of sys_objects (122) and sys_fields (1,366) are unchanged

AC-EXC-P1-001-04.t: Foreign key into ACE fails the build — a branch that adds a foreign key from case_account.account_key to public.account — the conformance test runs in the pipeline — the test fails with "fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema" And the merge is blocked

AC-EXC-P1-001-05.t: Recovery identity cannot read ACE directly or write a view — the recovery service identity in SIT — it runs SELECT on public.account, and INSERT on recovery.v_ace_account — both statements are refused with permission denied And the conformance test step 4 passes

CTL-40.t: 16.2 — Control conduct — Payments from staff accounts to customer loans are flagged for review — Detective

CTL-39.t: 16.2 — Control conduct — A sample of contacts, notices and decisions is checked each month against the conduct rules — Detective

CTL-13.t: 13.4 — Control document custody — Each original document has a holder and a due-back date; overdue originals raise a task — Detective

CTL-25.t: 6.1 — Take over the case at 90 days past due — Interest is reduced under the restructure terms once the customer has paid as agreed — Detective

CTL-23.t: 7.3 — Negotiate settlement or deed in lieu — A settlement below the floor goes for approval with the gap shown — Preventive

CTL-24.t: 7.3 — Negotiate settlement or deed in lieu — A payoff figure older than its limit is refreshed before an offer is sent — Preventive

CTL-21.t: 11.4 — X3 Deceased customer — A death raises X3, stops contact and routes the case to the specialist and Legal — Preventive

CTL-20.t: 7.4 — Claim guarantees — Each guarantee has a claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met — Preventive

CTL-33.t: 10.1 — Assess write-off — Only cases meeting the eligibility rule and the tax criteria version enter the write-off population; cases with open deviations are held out — Preventive

CTL-22.t: 11.6 — X5 Bankruptcy or external seizure — A bankruptcy stops enforcement, starts the claim deadline and ends bad debt follow-up where the rule applies — Preventive

CTL-34.t: 10.3 — Recover after charge-off — Follow-up on written-off debt ends when the bank's criteria are met, and the case is handed to the right unit — Detective

CTL-27.t: 9.2 — Hold and manage assets — An asset is priced only on an appraisal inside its age limit; Stage 3 collateral is revalued on schedule — Preventive

CTL-30.t: 9.1 — Take assets onto the books — An asset whose title has transferred is taken onto the books and moved to sale without delay — Detective

CTL-29.t: 9.4 — Sell assets by Dutch auction — Every asset ready to sell is listed on HOME.SCB and the app with the approved price and details — Detective

CTL-28.t: 9.4 — Sell assets by Dutch auction — The floor price is within the approver's limit as a share of fair market value — Preventive

CTL-42.t: 16.7 — Handle data subject requests — A data subject request holds automated processing on the case and reaches Compliance within the statutory period — Preventive

CTL-43.t: 16.5 — Control access and data protection — Every read of ACE source data goes through recovery.v_ace_*; the view-owner role holds SELECT on the listed ACE tables and nothing else; the recovery role has no privilege on an ACE table and cannot write a view — Preventive

CTL-44.t: 16.4 — Answer audit and regulatory requests — Every recovery.v_ace_* view exists with the columns and types the dictionary and the data contract publish: 30 views, 122 objects and 1,366 fields — Detective
